items.headline: Keon Coleman caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams.
items.analysis: Coleman was largely erased by the lockdown corner play of the Rams but had a receiving line also heavily influenced by a ground-heavy game plan from a Bills team that attempted only 19 passes in almost 70 minutes of football. It was quite the letdown fantasy performance for managers looking to take advantage of the absences of both DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer. Coleman is a borderline FLEX play in Week 6 against the Raiders, pending the status of Moore.

items.name: Khalil Shakir
items.headline: Khalil Shakir caught all three targets for 80 yards in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams.
items.analysis: Shakir’s modest target total was primarily a product of a ground-heavy approach from the Bills, who were playing without both DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer. His quiet fantasy outing was quickly remedied through a 57-yard, catch-and-run reception on the team’s second possession of overtime to set up the game-winning, Tyler Bass field goal. Shakir remains a shaky fantasy bet ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders.

items.name: James Cook
items.headline: James Cook rushed 25 times for 111 yards and two touchdowns in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams, adding seven yards on one reception.
items.analysis: Cook’s elite rushing line was overshadowed by two fumbles, the second of which was a lost fumble on the team’s first possession of overtime, placing the Rams in position to complete the comeback and steal away the victory. A blocked field goal on what would have been the game-winning kick breathed new life into the Bills, who demonstrated confidence in their lead back by throwing him right back out there on the following possession to eventually win the game. The 26 touches go down as a season high for the veteran back, who found paint for the fourth consecutive game in the thrilling overtime win. Cook remains a top-tier RB1 for fantasy purposes ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders in Las Vegas.

items.name: Josh Allen
items.headline: Josh Allen completed 12-of-19 passes for 210 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Bills’ 37-34, Week 5 win over the Rams, adding 121 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries.
items.analysis: The two teams mustered only 20 combined points in the first half as they felt each other out. There were only two punts after the break between the two sides, who combined for seven touchdowns on nine combined possessions including five straight touchdowns in the fourth quarter to send the game to overtime. Allen and the Bills took the ball first in the extra frame and quickly found themselves deep in enemy territory following a 57-yard, catch-and-run pass to Khalil Shakir. A James Cook fumble on the next play appeared to shatter Allen’s chances of earning his first career win in overtime, but a blocked 48-yard field goal attempt from Harrison Mevis gave the ball back to the Bills with a chance to win. Two Josh Allen scrambles set up a game-winning, 45-yard field goal for Tyler Bass. Allen ended with the second most yards on the ground of his career as the Bills moved to 4-1 with the wild win. Allen remains the top overall quarterback in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders on the road.

items.name: Max Klare
items.headline: Rams declared WR CJ Daniels, QB Ty Simpson, TE Max Klare, DE Larrell Murchison, and OL Bill Murray inactive for Week 5 against the Bills.
items.analysis: Klare had been active from Week 2 through Week 4 but retreats to the inactives list with Colby Parkinson returning from a one-game absence. Puka Nacua’s absence Week 2 and Week 3 could have also played a role in Klare’s game-day status during that period, with the Rams now set to face the Bills with just three active tight ends after going through multiple games with either four or five active.

items.name: DJ Moore
items.headline: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) is inactive for Week 5 against the Rams.
items.analysis: Moore’s absence leaves only Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir, Greg Dortch, and Skyler Bell as healthy wide receivers on the active roster with Joshua Palmer also sidelined. Expect heavy snap rates for Coleman and Shakir alongside tight end Dalton Kincaid, with the possibility the team elevates their 12-personnel rates through the inclusion of Dawson Knox. Also inactive for the Bills are WR Joshua Palmer, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL Ed Oliver DL, Landon Jackson, and NCB Dee Alford.

items.name: Audric Estime
items.headline: Browns signed RB Audric Estime from the Vikings’ practice squad.
items.analysis: Estime’s signing comes as Quinshon Judkins is dealing with an ankle injury he suffered in Week 5. Estime, who is only 23 years old, already feels like an NFL journeyman as he now heads to his fifth team in three seasons after brief stints with the Broncos, Eagles, Saints, and Vikings. The former fifth-round pick has rushed for 508 yards and three touchdowns in his career and rushed for 76-310-2 as a rookie with the Broncos. Estime could see snaps in Week 6 against the Ravens if Judkins is unable to play, but we wouldn’t expect to see anything close to a meaningful workload at this time.

items.name: Jonathon Cooper
items.headline: Broncos EDGE Jonathon Cooper was granted permission to travel to the team’s away games this season.
items.analysis: Cooper, who is facing felony assault charges and domestic violence and harassment charges, appeared in court on Monday and is currently on the commissioner’s exempt list. With his pretrial set for February 19th and his new trial date set for March 2nd, it’s possible Cooper could be removed from the exempt list now that his trial is set for after the season. Cooper has not played a game for the Broncos this season.

items.name: JuJu Smith-Schuster
items.headline: Vikings worked out WR JuJu Smith-Schuster on Monday.
items.analysis: Smith-Schuster was released by the Giants in training camp, and last worked out for the Jets in September. The 29-year-old receiver caught 33 passes for 345 yards and one touchdown last season, but wouldn’t be anything more than a depth signing if he were to sign with the Vikings or another team this season.

items.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
items.headline: Seahawks listed Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
items.analysis: With the Seahawks preparing to face the Broncos on a short week, it would be a bit more concerning if JSN were listed as a DNP. The team listing him as limited on the first day of the week is encouraging after he clearly battled through an ankle injury in Week 5’s loss to the 49ers. Smith-Njigba still topped 100 receiving yards for the fourth time this season and made several big plays despite being in visible pain. We’ll continue to update his practice status throughout the week, but as long as he’s active come Thursday, JSN should be in your fantasy lineups.

items.name: Talanoa Hufanga
items.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) did not practice on Monday.
items.analysis: It was an estimated session, but one that probably bodes pretty prescient since Hufanga left Week 5’s game with the ankle injury and was ruled out. Riley Moss (ribs) was listed as limited and would appear to have a chance to come back after being ruled out for Week 5.

items.name: Fernando Mendoza
items.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Kirk Cousins is the starter “but if Fernando [Mendoza]'s number is called we have confidence in him.”
items.analysis: No real surprise after Mendoza’s mop-up appearance in Week 5. It doesn’t appear that he’s taken a major step towards unseating Cousins — who has played well — just yet. But it remains a reasonable bet to happen in the near future.

items.name: Jermaine Eluemunor
items.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) is “day to day.”
items.analysis: It wouldn’t be surprising if he missed some practice time this week. Marcus Mbow would get snaps in Week 6 if Eluemunor were not able to go.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said he’s “hopeful” he will receive offensive reinforcements in Week 6 when asked about Saquon Barkley’s (hamstring) status.
items.analysis: Sirianni was asked about both Barkley and DeVonta Smith, who is also dealing with a hamstring injury. Sirianni didn’t commit to either player practicing this week, but we’ll see how things look on Wednesday when the Eagles release their first injury report. Philly suddenly finds itself in desperate need of help at running back after Tank Bigsby (core) was placed on IR last week and Will Shipley (foot) was diagnosed with a partial tear in his plantar fascia that’s expected to sideline him for several weeks. If Barkley is unable to play in Week 6, Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue would be next in line to lead the Eagles’ banged up backfield.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has “a shot” to return for Week 6’s game against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Smith hasn’t been seen on the practice field since Week 3 ended, so to say the practice week matters would perhaps be underselling it. Expect Smith to play if he practices at all, though, as the veteran often has suited up with little practice time in the past.

items.name: Jared Wayne
items.headline: Texans waived WR Jared Wayne.
items.analysis: He had four catches on 12 targets and it felt worse than that. Wayne will likely resurface on the Texans practice squad upon clearing waivers.

items.name: Jared Wayne
items.headline: Texans released WR Jared Wayne.
items.analysis: He had four catches on 12 targets and it felt worse than that. Wayne will likely resurface on the Texans practice squad upon clearing waivers.

items.name: Deebo Samuel
items.headline: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Deebo Samuel will miss “at least a couple of weeks” with the hamstring injury he suffered in Week 5’s win over the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Shanahan confirming this will be a multi-week absence isn’t surprising, but we still aren’t clear on just how much time he could miss. We’ll likely get a more specific timeline in the days ahead, but it sounds like we can safely assume Samuel will miss Week 6’s game against the Commanders and Week 7’s game against the Falcons. Jacob Cowing and Brandin Cooks could both be in line to see more work in the weeks ahead, with Cooks perhaps being the favorite to get the first crack at replacing Samuel. Cooks’ 11 routes run in the second half of Sunday’s game led all 49ers, including Mike Evans, and he found the end zone on a seven-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to put the Niners ahead with just over 11 minutes left in regulation.

items.name: Ben Skowronek
items.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Ben Skowronek (leg) has been ruled out for Week 6.
items.analysis: We weren’t exactly worried about Skowronek siphoning many targets away, but with him out of the pecking order entirely Germie Bernard should be a wheels-up WR3 for Week 6 now that both Skowronek and Roman Wilson have been ruled out.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) is “definitely doing better” after missing Week 5’s game against the Falcons.
items.analysis: While this is good news for Jackson, Minter also said he wasn’t sure if Jackson would be back on the practice field on Wednesday. It was reported earlier on Monday that there was “some hope” that Jackson would play in Week 6 after he was “closer than people realized” to playing in Week 5 against the Falcons. This is shaping up to be another week where we are forced to monitor Jackson’s practice status up until Friday, when the team releases its final injury report. The Ravens are 4-1 and set to face a 3-2 Browns team in a pivotal AFC North matchup. If Jackson is unable to start, Tyler Huntley would make his second start of the season.

items.name: Tyler Shough
items.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore, asked directly if Tyler Shough’s non-throwing hand is broken, said “it got banged two weeks ago and he’s just wearing some protective layers there.”
items.analysis: So, probably, then. The hand hasn’t really been a contributing factor to New Orleans’ decline so much as the Saints offensive line has just been in the blender for two weeks against Atlanta and Minnesota’s fronts, but it sure looks like Shough is managing through something and we should probably break ties against him in the rankings.

items.name: Michael Penix
items.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports there’s “optimism” that Michael Penix (ribs) will be able to play in Week 6 against the Bears.
items.analysis: Penix said after Sunday’s loss that he didn’t believe his injury would be long-term. He was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa in overtime because of his injury, but he also added that he likely would have gone back on the field had the Falcons received the ball to start the extra quarter. Instead, Penix said his pain worsened the longer he sat, which was why he ultimately didn’t go back in. Penix’s status will be one to monitor throughout the week. If he can’t start in Week 6, Tagovailoa would be in line to start his first game of the season.

items.name: Malik Willis
items.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Malik “is our quarterback.”
items.analysis: “Malik needs to be better, but that’s not the headline -- we all need to be better ... everything in the pass game has to be better.. It’s the receivers, it’s the tight ends, it’s the protection,” Hafley continued. Willis is by all statistical measures one of the weakest quarterbacks in the league with his arm, but at least he’s skimping some superflex QB2 value with his legs. There’s not much reason for the Dolphins to bench him either way, as they have nobody they pressingly need to evaluate. Willis should return after the Week 6 bye.

items.name: Jaylen Warren
items.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said “there’s a number you’d like to continue to give [Jaylen Warren],” even after Rico Dowdle (toe) returns.
items.analysis: “He’s produced, so it’s been heavy. It’d be great to get Rico back this week, too. ... Having him as a one-two punch was the vision of this offense, but Jaylen’s crushing it right now. He’s been awesome for us,” McCarthy continued. That’s a very telling “but.” Warren has to be regarded as the chair of a committee at this point rather than in a backfield split, and Dowdle probably doesn’t belong in the FLEX conversation coming off his injury until we see a good workload for him.

items.name: Quinshon Judkins
items.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Quinshon Judkins is considered day-to-day with an ankle injury.
items.analysis: Monken was spotted in a walking boot after Sunday’s loss to the Jets, but Monken said his RB1 will have a chance to play in Week 6 against the Ravens. Judkins rushed 14 times for 44 yards last week and has a rushing line of 73-221-1 for the season, along with 18 receptions for 102 additional yards. Judkins’ practice status will be one to monitor throughout the week. If he’s not able to play, Raheim Sanders would likely handle the early-down work, with Jaleel McLaughlin mixing in as well.

items.name: Dre Greenlaw
items.headline: 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw has been suspended for one game after being ejected from Week 5’s game against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: This was the exact outcome we expected after Greenlaw was ejected from Sunday’s game for headbutting Seahawks LB Ernest Jones on the sideline during a scuffle. Greenlaw, who was wearing a helmet, hit a helmet-less Jones and was immediately ejected and will now be suspended for one game without pay. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Greenlaw will appeal his suspension, but for now, he will miss Week 6’s game against the Commanders and be in line to return in Week 7 when the Niners visit the Falcons.

items.name: Taylor Moton
items.headline: Panthers designated OT Taylor Moton (blood clots) for return.
items.analysis: Moton was placed on the reserve/non-football injury list entering camp after it was revealed that he was dealing with blood clots in his lungs. The 32-year-old tackle now has 21 days to be activated from IR or be ruled out for the season, but we would expect him to be activated in the coming weeks. Moton earned a PFF offensive grade of 80.5 last season and allowed just three sacks and 22 pressures. In addition to Moton, the Panthers also designated DL Tershawn Wharton (neck) for return.

items.name: Tom Kennedy
items.headline: Tom Kennedy (knee) suffered a significant MCL injury that is expected to require season-ending surgery.
items.analysis: The 30-year-old culture tonesetter has mostly only turned to fantasy relevancy when injuries piled up. The Lions had to use Amon-Ra St. Brown on returns after his injury and will likely seek a new returner off the practice circuit this week.

items.name: Fernando Mendoza
items.headline: Fernando Mendoza completed 6-of-8 passes for 48 yards in relief of Kirk Cousins in Las Vegas’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots.
items.analysis: This doesn’t necessarily mean that Mendoza is going to take the reins this week; we expect Cousins to continue starting even if Raiders coach Klint Kubiak didn’t affirmatively get ahead of the situation in Sunday’s post-game. But Mendoza looked reasonable and this will obviously be something that will bubble up eventually. No. 1 overall picks don’t typically stay on benches too long.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said “there’s a chance” A.J. Brown (ankle) will practice this week.
items.analysis: Brown has been rehabbing from a high-ankle sprain he suffered in the season-opener. It was reported on Sunday that Brown was walking without a limp, and last week NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that “the hope is” Brown will play in Week 6 against the Jets. The team has not opened his return window, which they will need to do in order for him to practice this week. Once that happens, the focus will then move to his practice status and whether or not he can log a full practice or two before the weekend. We would expect Brown’s 21-day return window in the next 24 hours if the team really believes there’s a chance he could return this week.

items.name: David Montgomery
items.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said David Montgomery will be week-to-week with the groin injury he suffered in Week 5 against the Titans.
items.analysis: Ryans said Woody Marks “will carry the load” for the team while Montgomery is sidelined. It’s been a tough start to the season for Montgomery, who scored three times in Week 1 but has been locked out of the end zone ever since while averaging a career-low 3.5 yards per touch. Marks has been slightly more efficient than Montgomery this season, but the Texans’ running game as a whole has left much to be desired. Marks’ expected workload makes him worth a waiver wire claim where available, but fantasy managers shouldn’t expect anything more than RB3 levels of production at this time. The Texans will take on the Jaguars in London in Week 6.

items.name: Javon Hargrave
items.headline: Packers DT Javon Hargrave suffered a torn Achilles in Week 5’s win over the Bears, ending his season.
items.analysis: It was reported after Sunday’s game that the Packers believed Hargrave suffered a torn Achilles, so this news doesn’t come as a surprise. The 33-year-old lineman will now miss the remainder of the season and look to rehab in hopes of being back in time for training camp next season. Hargrave signed a two-year, $23 million contract with the Packers this offseason and has totaled six tackles in four games played.

items.name: Carson Schwesinger
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Browns LB Carson Schwesinger is dealing with a Grade 1 ankle sprain.
items.analysis: Schwesinger has not been ruled out for Week 6’s game against the Ravens, and attempted to play through the injury at one point. With a big AFC North matchup on tap for this week, it wouldn’t be surprising if the Browns gave Schwesinger every opportunity to play. His practice status will be one to keep an eye on throughout the week. The 2025 Defensive Rookie of the Year has totaled 43 tackles, one sack, and one forced fumble this season.

items.name: Will Shipley
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Eagles RB Will Shipley (foot) suffered “a partial tear of his plantar fascia” in Week 5’s loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: The Eagles’ running backs room continues to take hits. After losing Tank Bigsby (core) last week to a multi-week injury, the team is now preparing to be without Shipley for multiple weeks. Saquon Barkley, who missed Week 5 with a hamstring injury, could be back as early as Week 6 against the Panthers, but if he’s unable to play, the Eagles could be looking at Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue as their top two backs. Shipley totaled 13 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown on six touches before going down yesterday.

items.name: Caleb Williams
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said “all signs point” to Caleb Williams (hamstring) returning in Week 6 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Head coach Ben Johnson said on Sunday that Williams would be “close” to suiting up for Week 6, and he reportedly had a good workout before Week 5’s game against the Packers. Williams has missed the last three games with the hamstring injury he suffered in Week 2, but the Bears have managed to go 2-1 over that span. Williams logged one limited practice last week, after being a DNP on Wednesday and Thursday. If he can get on the practice field multiple days this week, it would be a good sign for his availability for next week’s game against the Falcons.

items.name: Teagan Quitoriano
items.headline: Cardinals TE Teagan Quitoriano caught 2-of-2 targets for 15 yards and two touchdowns in Arizona’s Week 5 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: ( The Aristocrats voice ) The Lions defense! Quitoriano, Arizona’s No. 2 tight end, remains outside of the fantasy TE2 discussion. These were his first touchdowns since the 2022 season, doubling his career total to four.

items.name: Oronde Gadsden II
items.headline: Oronde Gadsden failed to haul in his only target in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Gadsden had another disappointing outing for the Chargers and his fantasy managers on Sunday. He’s now been held without a catch in two of his last three games and has yet to exceed 36 receiving yards in any game this season. Playing in one of the worst offenses in the league certainly doesn’t help things, but Gadsden can’t be trusted by fantasy managers at this point and won’t be on the fantasy radar in Week 6 when the Chargers visit the Chiefs.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports there is “some hope” Lamar Jackson (ankle) will play in Week 6 against the Browns.
items.analysis: According to Rapoport, Jackson was “closer than people realized” to playing in Week 5 against the Falcons, which is an encouraging sign as the Ravens enter a pivotal matchup against the Browns. Jackson’s injury didn’t appear too severe when it initially happened in the second quarter of Week 4’s win over the Titans, so it’s not too surprising to hear that he nearly suited up for Sunday night’s game. That said, Jackson’s injuries have lingered in the past, so we’ll be monitoring his status throughout the week. If he’s not able to go, Tyler Huntley would make a second straight start for the Ravens, who currently lead the AFC North with a 4-1 record.

items.name: Deebo Samuel
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will have an MRI on Monday.
items.analysis: The MRI will help determine the severity of Samuel’s injury, but the 30-year-old receiver is likely looking at a multi-week absence after he was quickly ruled out of Sunday’s game. Samuel has caught 16 passes for 206 yards and three touchdowns this season for the Niners while adding another 78 yards on nine carries. He seems unlikely to play in Week 6 against the Commanders, which means we could see an increased role for either Jacob Cowing or Brandin Cooks, who scored in Week 5’s win over the Seahawks.

items.name: Roman Wilson
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Steelers WR Roman Wilson is expected to miss a “couplf of weeks” after suffering a finger injury in Week 5 against the Colts.
items.analysis: According to Fowler, Wilson is seeking a second opinion on his injury. He was initially diagnosed with a dislocated finger, but given today’s report, it sounds like this may be more severe than initially expected. Wilson entered Week 5 with back-to-back 60-plus-yard games and had been targeted six times in each of his first four games. Rookie Germie Bernard, who caught 6-of-9 targets for 80 yards in Week 5’s win over the Colts, will be worth a claim on waivers this week and profiles as a WR4/FLEX option in PPR leagues for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.

items.name: Roman Wilson
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Steelers WR Roman Wilson is expected to miss a “couple of weeks” after suffering a finger injury in Week 5 against the Colts.
items.analysis: According to Fowler, Wilson is seeking a second opinion on his injury. He was initially diagnosed with a dislocated finger, but given today’s report, it sounds like this may be more severe than initially expected. Wilson entered Week 5 with back-to-back 60-plus-yard games and had been targeted six times in each of his first four games. Rookie Germie Bernard, who caught 6-of-9 targets for 80 yards in Week 5’s win over the Colts, will be worth a claim on waivers this week and profiles as a WR4/FLEX option in PPR leagues for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.

items.name: Michael Penix
items.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) said he doesn’t believe his injury will be a long-term issue.
items.analysis: Penix will undergo an MRI on Monday to confirm the severity of his injury, but it doesn’t sound like he’s at risk of missing much time. Penix exited in the fourth quarter of Sunday night’s game against the Ravens and was forced to stay on the sideline in overtime to watch Tua Tagovailoa throw the game-losing interception shortly after the Ravens scored the go-ahead touchdown. Penix threw for 240 yards and a touchdown and has been solid in his three games since returning from injury. If he’s not able to start in Week 6, Tagovailoa would presumably draw the start at home against the Bears.

items.name: Mark Andrews
items.headline: Mark Andrews caught 4-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons.
items.analysis: Andrews dropped a would-be touchdown on the team’s opening possession on a ball that went through his hands in the end zone. He would then fumble on the following possession, which Jessie Bates returned for a touchdown to force the Ravens into catch-up mode for the remainder of the game. Luckily for him, late heroics from Tyler Huntley and Derrick Henry had the team escaping with a victory. Andrews has not looked great to start the 2026 season, having not eclipsed 50 yards through five games. He’ll remain a shaky fantasy start in Week 6 when the Ravens host the Browns.

items.name: Zay Flowers
items.headline: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-9 targets for 53 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons, adding 13 yards on one carry.
items.analysis: Flowers was largely confined to short area work with Tyler Huntley under center and also saw a 26-yard reception erased from his ledger due to a 29-yard pass interference penalty on the play. It was a weird situation in which the penalty yardage was greater than his reception. Fantasy managers might be forced to continue waiting on the return of Lamar Jackson after it was reported this week that the All Pro starter could be forced to miss another week. Flowers is a locked-in WR2 against the Browns in Week 6 with Huntley under center and an elite WR1 should Jackson return.

items.name: Rashod Bateman
items.headline: Rashod Bateman caught 5-of-6 targets for 62 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons.
items.analysis: Bateman had a relatively quiet game until notching 38 yards on three receptions on the team’s final possession of regulation, helping to spur an improbable comeback victory in overtime. The team took the ball with just over two minutes remaining down by eight, eventually driving the field and tacking on a two-point conversion to send the game to extra time. Bateman remains a shaky FLEX option for as long as Zay Flowers remains healthy. He won’t be worth starting in most leagues in a Week 6 meeting with the Browns.

items.name: Derrick Henry
items.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 24 times for 102 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons, adding 18 yards and a touchdown on one reception.
items.analysis: Henry also tacked on a successful two-point conversion to further pad his counting stats. The King erupted for 59 yards in the first half before being largely held in check for the final two quarters with the Ravens playing from behind. He would watch from the sidelines for the duration of the team’s final possession in the two-minute drill but came on the field to tie the game with a two-point conversion on a direct snap. The Falcons were no match for Henry in the extra frame, with the bruising back tacking on an additional 32 yards on the ground on the team’s lone overtime possession. Henry continues to turn back the clock while notching his eighth touchdown in five appearances, having scored in every game to start the season. He remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Browns.

items.name: Tyler Huntley
items.headline: Tyler Huntley completed 24-of-32 passes for 201 yards and two touchdowns in the Ravens’ 30-23, Week 5 win over the Falcons, adding 20 yards and a touchdown on six carries.
items.analysis: Huntley was in command of the offense throughout, showing poise and pocket presence in the face of one of the most stout defensive fronts in the league. The Ravens marched the field on the opening possession but a dropped touchdown from tight end Mark Andrews forced them to settle for a field goal. Their next possession resulted in an Andrews fumble that was returned for a touchdown, forcing the Ravens to play from behind for the remainder of the game. Down by eight with just over two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, Huntley took the ball and led the team to a touchdown and successful two-point conversion to force overtime. He would then lead an opening possession touchdown drive in the extra frame, with the team escaping with an unlikely comeback victory on a game-sealing interception. Huntley could be tasked with another start in Week 6 against the Browns after late-week reports indicated that Lamar Jackson could be headed for another absence. Huntley will be a middling QB2, should he start.

items.name: Kyle Pitts
items.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 5-of-6 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
items.analysis: Pitts remained largely confined to short area work with his game-long reception going for only 13 yards. A second quarter touchdown from five yards out gave the veteran tight end his first trip to paint through five games and his five receptions doubled that of his previous four appearances. Pitts remains a difficult weekly start for as long as Drake London and Bijan Robinson remain healthy. A Week 6 meeting with the Bears in Atlanta should see him remain in the TE2 ranks.

items.name: Jahan Dotson
items.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 54 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
items.analysis: Dotson’s 54 yards finished second on the team behind alpha Drake London but his four targets finished behind London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson. His status as the starting wide receiver opposite London likely means little in the wake of modest volume games that continue to stack up. He can safely be left on, or returned to, the waiver wire.

items.name: Drake London
items.headline: Drake London caught 7-of-11 targets for 118 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
items.analysis: London started slow along with the rest of an Atlanta offense that gained just 37 total yards on their first three possessions before a 78-yard scoring drive to end the half. He would add six receptions after the break to push his season average to 127 yards per game in games started by Michael Penix. Penix departed late in the fourth quarter with a ribs injury, suddenly making London’s fantasy managers skittish after the veteran receiver managed a meager 80 total yards in two games without Penix to begin the season. Fantasy managers will want to monitor Atlanta’s starting quarterback’s status in the coming days ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Bears, where London will be a WR1 with Penix or an upside WR3 in his absence.

items.name: Bijan Robinson
items.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 17 times for 86 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens, adding 32 yards on four receptions.
items.analysis: Robinson suffered through poor offensive efficiency in the first half, finally breaking loose for a 38-yard carry on the team’s first possession of the third quarter. Although the receiving production and yardage total were enough to salvage a usable fantasy week, it was only the second time in five games in which Robinson failed to find the end zone. Robinson remains an elite fantasy RB1 ahead of a Week 6 showdown against the Bears in Atlanta.

items.name: Tua Tagovailoa
items.headline: Tua Tagovailoa completed 2-of-3 passes for 34 yards and an interception in the Falcons’ 30-23, Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
items.analysis: Tagovailoa came on in relief of the injured Michael Penix late in the fourth quarter and would be charged with leading the Falcons to a potential game-tying drive in overtime after the Ravens took the ball and scored a touchdown to start the extra period. He completed one pass at the end of the fourth quarter, one in overtime, and then threw a game-ending interception to send the Falcons to a 2-3 record ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Bears. Fantasy managers of Penix will want to track his status closely in the coming days.

items.name: Michael Penix
items.headline: Falcons QB Michael Penix (ribs) is questionable to return to Week 5 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Penix took the full brunt of a brutal hit to the midsection late in the fourth quarter of Week 5 against the Ravens. He would leave for one play due to the medical timeout, return for one play, and then retreat to the sideline. Tua Tagovailoa came on in relief in overtime, with the team designating Penix questionable to return with an injury to his ribs. Penix completed 19-of-32 passes for 240 yards and one touchdown prior to departing, adding eight yards on two carries. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his practice status in the coming days ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Bears.

items.name: Devin White
items.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said LB Devin White “is probably going to need surgery” after fracturing his forearm in Week 5 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: The Lions’ backup linebacker is expected to miss some time. The Lions will also be without WR Tom Kennedy, who serves as the team’s top returner, for a while. Kennedy suffered a “sprain,” seemingly in his knee, during a return.

items.name: Javon Hargrave
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Packers DT Javon Hargrave is believed to have suffered an Achilles tendon rupture in Week 5 against the Bears.
items.analysis: He was injured in Week 5’s win over the Bears. Hargrave has one year remaining on his contract. He faces a tough recovery late in his career. This is the second Achilles tendon rupture for the Packers’ defense in as many weeks, with LB Edgerrin Cooper suffering the same injury in Week 4 against the Buccaneers. Hargrave will ultimately require surgery and be placed on injured reserve.

items.name: Tyler Allgeier
items.headline: Tyler Allgeier rushed three times for seven yards in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Allgeier was a non-factor, even with the Cardinals pulling Jeremiyah Love in the fourth quarter. Allgeier did not log a carry in the first quarter. He is nothing more than a bench stash moving forward. The Cardinals face the Rams in Week 6.

items.name: Jeremiyah Love
items.headline: Jeremiyah Love rushed 12 times for 22 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Love played extensively early in the game. He was the only Cardinals running back to record a carry in the first quarter. The Lions began running up the score in the second quarter, and Love was seemingly simply phased out as Jacoby Brissett repeatedly fired passes downfield. Later, in the fourth quarter, the camera suddenly showed Love standing on the sideline without his helmet. A reporter chimed in to say that Love had not received attention from the training staff, but noted that Love told her he is still managing the ankle injury he suffered in training camp. Reports also indicated that he tweaked his other ankle last week. Love’s weekly floor is sinking as his production becomes increasingly touchdown-dependent. That said, he should be in fantasy lineups as an RB2/3 against the Rams next week.

items.name: Trey McBride
items.headline: Trey McBride caught 9-of-10 targets for 66 yards and one touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: McBride looked like his normal, dominant self, carving up defenders on out routes and in-breakers. Unfortunately, hearts were also broken when Jacoby Brissett fired a touchdown pass right past McBride, running wide open inside the Lions’ five-yard line, to backup TE Teagan Quitoriano, also running wide open in the back of the end zone. Fortunately, McBride was able to haul in a juggling, falling and contested touchdown catch late in the fourth quarter to boost his final stat line. McBride is an elite TE1 against the Rams next week.

items.name: Kendrick Bourne
items.headline: Kendrick Bourne caught 5-of-8 targets for 70 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Bourne looks like a viable FLEX starter for those in need. His 70 receiving yards were a team high, and his eight targets trailed only Trey McBride (10). The journeyman receiver delivered two 20-plus-yard gains via post routes, the first coming on the Cardinals’ first drive and the second on the seventh. Jacoby Brissett tried to force another downfield shot to Bourne on the latter drive, but it didn’t work out. Bourne is running high-value routes in the center of the field, playing for a garbage-time team with a cannon-armed quarterback. The results could be volatile at times, but he is worth starting in the FLEX against the Rams next week.

items.name: Michael Wilson
items.headline: Michael Wilson caught 4-of-7 targets for 30 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions, adding one pass for seven yards.
items.analysis: Wilson almost scored a passing touchdown via an end-around trick play on the Cardinals’ opening drive, but his receiver, Jacoby Brissett, was stopped two yards shy of the end zone. Heartbreak struck again two drives later, when Wilson only got one foot in bounds along the sideline on a would-be 19-yard catch. Brissett went right back to him on the following play, but the contested pass edged past Wilson’s outstretched hands. Wilson tacked on a couple of short gains before snagging a 17-yard pass on the Cardinals’ ninth drive, and he nearly bagged a 47-yard touchdown down the left sideline on the 10th drive, but his coverage defender effectively contested it, resulting in an incompletion. Wilson should handle a WR2-level workload against the Rams in Week 6.

items.name: Jacoby Brissett
items.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 29-of-47 passes for 292 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in the Cardinals’ 21-45, Week 5 loss to the Lions.
items.analysis: Brissett also rushed twice for 19 yards and nearly scored on a trick play via a seven-yard reception. He was stopped at the Lions’ two-yard line. Brissett guided the Cardinals to a 14-play scoring drive on their first possession, which he capped off with a two-yard touchdown strike to backup TE Teagan Quitoriano. The bottom dropped out after that. The Cardinals racked up five straight drives ending a punt, with Brissett only managing to break the dreary streak by throwing an interception. Brissett managed to salvage his box score with another Quitoriano score, and a juggling touchdown catch secured by Trey McBride. Brissett also coaxed a few big plays out of fellow backup TE Elijah Higgins. Apparently, the veteran quarterback is ready to target more towering pass catchers with Marvin Harrison Jr. now a Texan. Brissett is a borderline QB1/2 with a shaky floor in Week 6 against the Rams. Coach Mike LaFleur said post-game that he is not considering a quarterback change.

items.name: Jermaine Eluemunor
items.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports Giants RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) is feeling better post-game, but the team will have to see how he feels as the week progresses.
items.analysis: According to Raanan, Eluemunor felt his calf pop and left today’s game against the Commanders. Fortunately, he was able to walk around on his own, which is a good sign. The Giants went to Marcus Mbow at right tackle in Eluemunor’s absence.

items.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
items.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals, adding five receptions for 56 yards.
items.analysis: Gibbs scored twice today, bringing his career touchdown total up to 57, breaking the NFL record set by former Lions RB Barry Sanders for the most touchdowns scored by a player under 25 years old. The exceptionally talented player gets a boost from his sharp coaching staff, who continue to maximize Gibbs’ strengths. OC Drew Petzing dialed up a trick-play screen pass for Gibbs after the two-minute warning, in which Gibbs took the handoff, pitched it to Amon-Ra St. Brown, who pitched it back to Jared Goff, who then chucked it back to Gibbs with three offensive linemen in front of him on the left side of the field. An 18-yard gain ensued. Gibbs later produced a season-long 22-yard run. Although he scored two touchdowns today, he could have had a third. On the Lions’ ninth drive, Gibbs got two chances from the one-yard line on the ninth drive before the coaching staff greenlit a successful QB sneak for Goff. The Lions are on bye in Week 6, but he returns to the top of the running back ranks against the Packers in Week 7.

items.name: Rachaad White
items.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 18 yards in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie against the Giants, adding one reception for two additional yards.
items.analysis: White continued to serve as the RB2 behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt and led the backfield with 11 snaps on third down. While his role remained largely the same, even with Austin Ekeler active, White offered nothing of fantasy value in this one. He saw only one target on the afternoon, and could continue to have his fantasy upside limited as long as Jayden Daniels is scrambling away from pressure rather than dumping it off to his checkdown options. Fantasy managers should avoid White in Week 6 against the 49ers.

items.name: Chig Okonkwo
items.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 4-of-6 targets for 60 yards in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie with the Giants.
items.analysis: Okonkwo caught two passes on the Commander’s opening and immediately topped his previous best game of the season. He hauled in passes of 11 and 23 yards on back-to-back catches before Jacory Croskey-Merritt ended the drive with a 33-yard touchdown run. Okonkwo would come up with a 25-yard reception later in the second quarter on a drive that ended with a Drew Stevens field goal, but was targeted just one time in the second half. It was an overall nice outing for Okonkwo, but fantasy managers shouldn’t rush to add him to their lineups. He’ll be a boom-or-bust streaming option in Week 6 against the Niners.

items.name: George Kittle
items.headline: George Kittle caught 5-of-6 targets for 24 yards in the 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
items.analysis: After three straight big weeks, Kittle finally came back down to earth in Sunday’s win over the Seahawks. His longest reception came on a 13-yard gain in the third quarter, but proved inconsequential after Deebo Samuel lost a fumble on the following play to end the drive. Kittle has been targeted 19 times over the last three weeks and has gone for 70-plus yards in three of his last four games. He should be primed for a bounce-back next week when the Niners play host to the Commanders on Monday night.

items.name: Sam LaPorta
items.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 5-of-5 targets for 88 yards and one touchdown in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: LaPorta got involved on the Lions’ third drive, making a clutch 12-yard grab on 4th-and-3 while suffering what the officials deemed an unnecessarily rough hit by LB Mack Wilson at the end of the play. He chipped in two catch-and-run plays on the following drive. The first being an 11-yard play that was controversially ruled down in front of the sticks. Coach Dan Campbell called his number on the next play, resulting in an effortless 38-yard touchdown down the right side of the field. LaPorta tacked on an eight-yard catch and a 19-yard catch in the second half as the Lions cruised to a blowout win. He goes on bye next week but returns to the TE1 ranks in Week 7 against the Packers.

items.name: AJ Barner
items.headline: AJ Barner caught 3-of-5 targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers.
items.analysis: Barner continues to be a non-factor in the Seahawks’ passing game. Outside of a Week 3 game against the Commanders in which he went for 5-69-0 on nine targets, Barner has totaled 53 yards in his other four games combined and has yet to find the end zone this season. Barner won’t be on the streaming radar in Week 6, even with four teams on bye.

items.name: Isaac TeSlaa
items.headline: Isaac TeSlaa caught 0-of-2 targets in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Jared Goff gave TeSlaa two chances to contribute today. The first was a 3rd-and-13 pass on the Lions’ second drive, just beyond the sticks, in which TeSlaa went aerial and fully horizontal, trying to make the diving catch. The pass, unfortunately, fell incomplete. Goff went back to him on the fifth drive, firing a pass — just a touch too high — to the second-year wide receiver who was wide open on a crossing route, racing across the back of the end zone. TeSlaa leapt for it and got a hand on it, but he couldn’t come down with it. TeSlaa takes his goose egg into the Lions’ Week 6 bye. With any luck, it hatches into a FLEX-relevant stat line against the Packers in Week 7, though he remains a boom-bust pass catcher.

items.name: George Holani
items.headline: George Holani rushed four times for seven yards in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers, adding four receptions for 24 additional yards.
items.analysis: Holani put the ball on the turf twice in this one, but it was his fumble with 13 seconds left in the first half that proved to be one of the more costly mistakes of the game. With the Seahawks simply looking to get to halftime, Holani took a handoff from Sam Darnold for what should have been the final play of regulation. Instead, the third-year back had the ball knocked out and into his own end zone, which resulted in a Niners touchdown after it was recovered by DT Gracen Halton for the score. Holani hasn’t emerged as the late-round value fantasy managers hoped for this offseason and is fully off the fantasy radar for Week 6 against the Broncos.

items.name: Jameson Williams
items.headline: Jameson Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 47 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: The Lions’ speedster only caught two passes today, but he made them count. Williams’ first catch was a nine-yard, fourth-down touchdown on the Lions’ fifth drive. He nearly hauled in a 25-yarder via a play-action target on the sixth drive, but Cardinals CB Max Melton batted it away. He was open for an explosive gain on the next drive, but Jared Goff checked down to Sam LaPorta about 10 yards beneath Williams. A few plays later, Williams dusted his coverage defender for a 39-yard score from bunch formation, hauling in the touchdown pass in stride in the end zone. Goff later gave him another touchdown chance on a downfield throw targeted inside the Cardinals’ five-yard line, but Williams couldn’t secure it. He’ll now take a week off with the Lions’ Week 6 bye, but return as a WR2 against the Packers in Week 7.

items.name: Will Campbell
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Patriots OT Will Campbell is believed to have suffered a knee sprain and will likely miss some time.
items.analysis: Campbell will undergo an MRI tomorrow to fully assess the injury, but it seems likely that Drake Maye will be playing without his left tackle for a few weeks. They face the Jets, Bears and Dolphins over the next three weeks. Keeping Jets rookie EDGE David Bailey at bay could prove challenging.

items.name: Emanuel Wilson
items.headline: Emanuel Wilson rushed 20 times for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers, adding two receptions for 11 additional yards.
items.analysis: Wilson again led the Seahawks in rushing sans Jadarian Price. He handled all but four of the team’s running back carries in this one and found the end zone on a two-yard plunge in the first quarter to tie the game at 7-7. Wilson coughed up a key fumble in the second quarter that gave the Niners the ball on Seattle’s 11-yard line. On the following play, the Seahawks would allow an 11-yard touchdown run to Christian McCaffrey to put the Niners back out in front. Assuming Zach Charbonnet (Achilles) is at least one more game away from returning, Wilson will be on the RB2 radar in Week 6 when the Seahawks take on the Broncos on Thursday night.

items.name: Christian McCaffrey
items.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed 11 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks, adding three receptions for 15 additional yards.
items.analysis: McCaffrey’s lone touchdown came on an 11-yard touchdown run immediately after the 49ers had recovered a fumble by Emanuel Wilson. He hasn’t had the gaudy yardage totals we’re accustomed to seeing, but fantasy managers won’t be mad at this performance. While McCaffrey has yet to rush for 100 yards in a game this season, he’s gone for 80-plus yards from scrimmage in three of five games and has scored in four straight. He continues to be the only fantasy-relevant running back on the Niners and is set up to smash in Week 6 against the Commanders on Monday Night Football.

items.name: Zach Charbonnet
items.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said he does not plan to play Zach Charbonnet (knee) in Week 6 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: The Seahawks face the Broncos in Week 6’s Thursday Night Football game. Late last week, Macdonald acknowledged that the short turnaround time would make it difficult to ramp up Charbonnet as planned. The Seahawks are set to scale back the intensity at practice this week, which runs counter to the rehab plan. The Seahawks face the Chiefs in Week 7’s Sunday Night Football game. That seems like a plausible return date at this point.

items.name: Mike Washington Jr.
items.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had one rush for five yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots, adding one catch for five yards.
items.analysis: It was odd usage for Washington, who had at least five carries in three of four games headed into Week 5. Even Ashton Jeanty being limited with his ankle and foot injuries did nothing to bolster Washington’s involvement in the Vegas offense. In fact, Dylan Laube was the team’s clear No. 2 back behind Jeanty on Sunday. Laube had four carries and three receptions and punched in a short touchdown in the second half of the blowout loss. It raises serious questions about what Washington’s workload might look like if Jeanty misses time this season.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: Mike Evans caught 7-of-10 targets for 113 yards and one touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Evans’ only touchdown of the game came on a two-yard pass from Brock Purdy in the first quarter to give the Niners an early 7-0 lead. Evans came up big on multiple occasions in this one, hauling in three catches of 20-plus yards, including back-to-back receptions of 23 and 28 yards that helped set up a seven-yard touchdown to Brandin Cooks. Evans then caught a pass in the end zone on the next play to convert a two-point try and put the Niners up 29-26. This was Evans’ best day as a Niner. He set season-highs in receptions, targets, and receiving yards, and has now found the end zone three times on the year. With Deebo Samuel (hamstring) potentially set to miss some time, Evans could very easily see more days like today. He will be a fringe WR1/WR2 next week against a porous Commanders secondary.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 6-of-11 targets for 69 yards in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Lions coach Dan Campbell tasked St. Brown with punt return duties (2/36) after Tom Kennedy got hurt. While St. Brown looked great weaving through traffic, his first return nearly ended in a lost fumble, but a teammate dove on the loose ball, bailing him out after it was punched out of St. Brown possession. St. Brown nearly had a 43-yard touchdown on a sideline play-action shot on the Lions’ seventh drive, but he couldn’t quite get his hands on it. He almost bagged short scores via out routes on the Lions’ eighth and ninth drives, but his coverage defender effectively challenged the pass on the first and the pass was just out of his reach on the second. He had a nice 36-yard catch-and-run on the eighth drive and nearly nabbed another explosive gain on the sixth drive, but Sam LaPorta accidentally knocked him down 11 yards downfield after St. Brown leapt over a downed Cardinals defender. He had another fumble recovered by a teammate after snagging a pass on a crosser. The Lions’ stud wide receiver will be an elite WR1 against the Packers following the Lions’ Week 6 bye.

items.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
items.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 5-of-8 targets for 102 yards and one touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers, adding one rush for 16 additional yards.
items.analysis: JSN appeared to be playing through a bit of an ankle injury in this one, but he looked perfectly fine when he turned what would have been a short two-yard reception upfield for a 16-yard touchdown in the third quarter. In the fourth quarter, as the Seahawks were attempting a comeback, JSN hauled in a 35-yard reception, evading multiple defenders to get the Seahawks to the 50-yard line. A few plays later, he would drop a wide-open pass that may have set the Seahawks up for a game-winning field goal opportunity, but JSN did his part to keep the Seahawks in what proved to be a sloppy game for the offense as a whole. He’s gone for 100-plus yards in four of his first five games of the season and will look for his fifth 100-yard game on Thursday night when the Seahawks visit the Broncos.

items.name: Jared Goff
items.headline: Jared Goff completed 19-of-30 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in the Lions’ 45-21, Week 5 win over the Cardinals, adding one rush for a one-yard touchdown.
items.analysis: Sacks and a few errant throws under pressure derailed the Lions’ first three drives. Goff got things back on track after that, guiding the offense to seven straight scoring drives, including six touchdowns. He even punched in a one-yard rushing touchdown via a quarterback sneak, marking his first rushing score since 2023. Goff could have boosted his passing yards total with a likely explosive gain by targeting an open Jameson Williams on the first drive after halftime, but he instead checked down to Sam LaPorta in the flats for an eight-yard pickup. The Lions are on bye in Week 6, but Goff will be a locked-in QB1 against the Packers in Week 7.

items.name: Kyle Williams
items.headline: Kyle Williams caught all three of his targets for 91 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Williams caught a beautifully thrown 49-yard score from Drake Maye, who had four touchdown passes to go along with 376 yards through the air in the blowout victory. Williams ran a route on 19 of the team’s 42 drop backs with Mack Hollins on injured reserve. He also came down with a long grab in the second half that put the Pats in position to take a four-score lead. A.J. Brown’s eventual return to the New England offense — as soon as this week against the Jets — will further limit Williams’ snaps and routes. He won’t be playable in most formats going forward.

items.name: Marquez Valdes-Scantling
items.headline: Marquez Valdes-Scantling caught 2-of-3 targets for 22 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Valdes-Scantling finished second in receiving yards for the Chargers against the Broncos. That’s not great. The veteran wideout is going to get some opportunities because of the injuries, but that shouldn’t equate to a chance to help a fantasy roster. He’ll face the Chiefs in Week 6.

items.name: Sam Darnold
items.headline: Sam Darnold completed 18-of-29 passes for 195 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Seahawks’ 32-29, Week 5 loss to the 49ers.
items.analysis: It was a rough outing for Darnold, who was picked off on his first pass attempt of the day and absorbed a season-high five sacks. His lone touchdown pass came on a 16-yard pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Darnold completed a short two-yard pass to JSN, who turned it upfield for the score to give the Seahawks the 23-21 lead with just over five minutes left in the third quarter. On the Seahawks’ final drive of the game, Darnold found JSN for a 35-yard completion, but three straight incompletions, including an uncharacteristic drop by JSN, put the Seahawks in a fourth-and-10 situation that they were unable to convert after Cooper Kupp came up a yard short on his second reception of the night. Darnold has now thrown seven touchdowns and six interceptions in his last three games since returning from injury, and now faces a short week to get ready for the Broncos on Thursday night. He profiles as a mid-to-low-end QB2 in what could be a tough road matchup.

items.name: Tre' Harris
items.headline: Tre Harris caught 2-of-4 targets for 16 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Harris was a complete non-factor even against the depleted Broncos’ secondary. The second-year wideout was the top target with Ladd McConkey and Quinton Johnston unavailable, and that extra attention didn’t help. Harris will try and bounce back in Week 6 against the Chiefs.

items.name: Brock Purdy
items.headline: Brock Purdy completed 19-of-29 passes for 189 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the 49ers’ 32-29, Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Purdy and the 49ers made the most of several short fields in this one. After an interception by Sam Darnold on the Seahawks’ first drive of the game, Purdy led a short 18-yard drive that he capped with a two-yard touchdown pass to Mike Evans to give the Niners an early lead. Purdy would orchestrate a long scoring drive in the fourth quarter, completing seven passes for 89 yards, with his final completion resulting in a seven-yard touchdown to Brandin Cooks. The Seahawks became the first team to sack Purdy this season, bringing him down three times in the backfield in the second half, but Purdy was able to evade pressure for the entire second half. Purdy and the Niners get a juicy Week 6 matchup next Monday against the Commanders, where he will profile as a solid QB1.

items.name: Charlie Kolar
items.headline: Charlie Kolar caught 3-of-4 targets for 37 yards with a lost fumble in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Kolar tied for the team lead in catches, and finished with the most receiving yards. Unfortunately, 19 of those came on the first play, and were followed by a fumble. Oronde Gadsden didn’t catch his only target and Hayden Rucci had just one catch — for a touchdown, to be fair — so Kolar sadly appears to be the one “reliable” receiving target for the Chargers’ tight end room. That doesn’t mean he’s a great fantasy play for Week 6 against the Chiefs, however. On the contrary.

items.name: Courtland Sutton
items.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-3 targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
items.analysis: It’s the first touchdown for Sutton on the season, and it tied the game at 17-17. The 31-year-old was unable to find room versus the Chargers’ secondary, and for the fifth-straight week, Sutton was held under 50 yards. His size could give the smaller Seahawks’ defensive backs trouble, but he’s essentially a touchdown-dependent FLEX for Week 6 against Seattle.

items.name: Jaylen Waddle
items.headline: Jaylen Waddle got 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers while adding a nine-yard rush.

items.name: Jaylen Waddle
items.headline: Jaylen Waddle caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers while adding a nine-yard rush.
items.analysis: Give some credit to the Chargers’ defense, but this was an ugly game for both passing attacks. Waddle has his second dud in three weeks, and doesn’t appear to have great chemistry with Bo Nix thus far. No one really does, to be fair, as no receiver caught more than four passes for Denver. Waddle is a volatile WR2, and that volatility becomes more, well, volatile for Week 6 against the Seahawks.

items.name: Evan Engram
items.headline: Evan Engram caught all four targets for 55 yards in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
items.analysis: Engram did a large portion of his damage on a busted coverage that allowed him to pick up 34 yards and come just short of a receiving score. The 55 yards are a season high, and it’s encouraging to see more involvement after being a non-factor in the previous two weeks. Engram will hope to build on this effort in Week 6 against the Seahawks, but fantasy managers shouldn’t bet on it.

items.name: Keaton Mitchell
items.headline: Keaton Mitchell rushed 6 times for 11 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos while adding three receptions for 18 yards.
items.analysis: The only positive here was that Mitchell was somewhat involved in the pass game, but it was all of the check-down variety. The injuries to the Los Angeles offensive line just won’t open many holes right now, and even if Mitchell has looked more spry than Omarion Hampton, there’s more risk than reward having him in a lineup right now.

items.name: Omarion Hampton
items.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 14 times for 33 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Webster’s defines plodding as whatever this was. Hampton picked up a literal third of his yards on one 11-yard carry, and while much of the blame goes to the sheer lack of bodies on the offensive line, it was still mightily unimpressive. Hampton is at best a dart-throw FLEX for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

items.name: Kimani Vidal
items.headline: Kimani Vidal rushed eight times for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Vidal showed off his potential to be a big-play back on a 42-yard touchdown that gave the Chargers a 17-0 lead. The 25-year-old did nothing outside of that carry, but in a game where offense was limited — limited is putting it nicely — it stood out. Vidal was more effective than Omarion Hampton (33 yards on 14 carries) and Keaton Mitchell (11 on six) but still seems likely to be behind both for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

items.name: RJ Harvey
items.headline: RJ Harvey picked up seven yards on three carries in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
items.analysis: Harvey was a non-factor in this one, and a week after his big receiving game, he was held without a catch with just one target. The second-year tailback was clearly the backup to JK Dobbins, and was unable to make the most of his limited opportunities. He’s off the radar for Week 6 versus the Seahawks on Thursday.

items.name: Pierre Strong
items.headline: Pierre Strong rushed five times for seven yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears, adding three receptions for 11 yards.
items.analysis: Making his Packers debut, 27-year-old journeyman Strong slid into Chris Brooks’ (ankle, injured reserve) vacated role. Although it’s a potential concern for MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson — any new face in this makeshift backfield would be — it appears to be a bigger issue for Johnson, as Strong was playing ahead of him until garbage time. Ominous for Johnson managers, though Strong has little shot at carving out 12-team league value of his own.

items.name: J.K. Dobbins
items.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
items.analysis: Dobbins was the most effective offensive player for both teams, which isn’t quite the compliment you’d think it is. The 27-year-old was the bellcow for the Broncos, however, and he was able to keep the chains moving enough to give Denver the victory over the winless Chargers. Dobbins will likely find the sledding tougher in Week 6 when the Broncos face the Seahawks on Thursday Night Football.

items.name: Justin Herbert
items.headline: Justin Herbert completed 14-of-24 passes for 121 yards with a touchdown and interceptions while rushing for 54 yards and losing a fumble in the Chargers’ 23-17, Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Herbert was without his top wideouts, his top offensive lineman, and the fact he was able to put up even this type of statline is somewhat impressive, if you squint very hard. The 28-year-old quarterback was constantly under pressure, and was at his best when he was able to escape the pocket and use his underrated wheels. That being said, he could have had more turnovers than this, and his interception was an inexcusable throw right into the hands of the Broncos’ defender. Even if Herbert gets his weapons back, fantasy managers should be looking elsewhere in Week 6 in standard leagues fora touch matchup against the Chiefs.

items.name: Justin Herbert
items.headline: Justin Herbert completed 14-of-24 passes for 121 yards with a touchdown and interception while rushing for 54 yards and losing a fumble in the Chargers’ 23-17, Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
items.analysis: Herbert was without his top wideouts, his top offensive lineman, and the fact he was able to put up even this type of statline is somewhat impressive, if you squint very hard. The 28-year-old quarterback was constantly under pressure, and was at his best when he was able to escape the pocket and use his underrated wheels. That being said, he could have had more turnovers than this, and his interception was an inexcusable throw right into the hands of the Broncos’ defender. Even if Herbert gets his weapons back, fantasy managers should be looking elsewhere in Week 6 in standard leagues fora touch matchup against the Chiefs.

items.name: Bo Nix
items.headline: Bo Nix completed 16-of-127 passes for 123 yards with a touchdown in the Broncos’ 23-17, Week 5 win over the Chargers.
items.analysis: Nix also added 10 yards on the ground on his four carries. He once again wasn’t able to get the ball downfield, with a long passing gain of 34 yards on a busted coverage. He was at least able to find Courtland Sutton for a short touchdown, but this was an ugly day for both signal-callers. Nix is no more than a QB2 for a matchup against the tough Seattle defense in Week 6, and it’s worth noting that game takes place Thursday night.

items.name: Kaleb Johnson
items.headline: Kaleb Johnson rushed seven times for 26 yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears.
items.analysis: Even with Chris Brooks (ankle) on injured reserve, Johnson remain mired in a three-man committee, as veteran journeyman Pierre Strong slid seamlessly into Brooks’ vacated “role.” In fact, it was worse than that, as Johnson could also only watch as MarShawn Lloyd and Strong formed an early 1-2 punch. Johnson wasn’t really involved before garbage time. Before that, Lloyd had the advantage in short-yardage situations, notching the first two rushing touchdowns of his star-crossed career. Yet to handle more than eight carries in a game, it just isn’t happening for Johnson in 12-team league fantasy. He’s a distant FLEX bet ahead of Week 6 against the Cowboys.

items.name: Kalif Raymond
items.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 3-of-4 targets for six yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers.
items.analysis: Raymond’s fast start to the season has now been erased to the tune of just five catches for 12 yards over the past two weeks. Even with Caleb Williams (hamstring) looking likely to return for Week 6 against the Falcons, Raymond’s brief moment in the 2026 fantasy sun has come and gone.

items.name: Roschon Johnson
items.headline: Roschon Johnson rushed five times for six yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers, adding five receptions for 34 yards.
items.analysis: Filling in for Kyle Monangai (toe), Johnson helped close out a blowout loss. Pro Football Focus charted him as playing the final 13 snaps over D’Andre Swift, goosing his touch totals with No. 3 QB Case Keenum under center. Johnson would perhaps be worth a desperation PPR flier if Monangai remains sidelined for Week 6 against the Falcons and Caleb Williams (hamstring) returns, but “desperation” would be the operative word there.

items.name: Mason Taylor
items.headline: Mason Taylor caught 3-of-3 targets for 24 yards in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns.
items.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 2, Taylor caught the second most balls on the team as Kenyon Sadiq departed with a third quarter concussion. Those are awful developments for Sadiq managers, but almost certainly not enough to create TE2 value for Taylor, even if Sadiq misses Week 6 against the Patriots.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: Ravens declared QB Lamar Jackson, OLB Trey Hendrickson, C Cam Jurgens, G Andrew Vorhees, WR Elijah Sarratt, and DT Aeneas Peebles inactive for Week 5 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Jackson had already been ruled out earlier in the week and reportedly could be looking at a multi-game absence due to an ankle injury suffered before halftime in Week 4. Tyler Huntley will start under center for the Ravens as they look to subdue the momentum of the Falcons, who have won both games started by Michael Penix. Wide receiver Zay Flowers is officially active for Sunday Night Football.

items.name: Isaiah Davis
items.headline: Isaiah Davis rushed two times for eight yards in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns, adding a nine-yard reception.
items.analysis: Davis at least touched the ball after his Week 4 doughnut, but Pro Football Focus charted him as getting out-snapped 60-10 by fill-in No. 2 Braelon Allen. Decisive, to say the least. Even if Breece Hall (quad) is forced to miss his third straight game in Week 6, Davis hasn’t shown enough to warrant a 12-team league looksee.

items.name: Za'Darius Smith
items.headline: Falcons declared DE Za’Darius Smith, LB Christian Harris, QB Cooper Rush, QB Jack Strand, OL Ethan Onianwa, DB Malcolm DeWalt IV, and DB Robert Longerbeam inactive for Week 5 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: The Falcons remain one of the healthier teams in the league as they enter Week 5 with no major injuries amongst skill position players. They’ll look to maintain the momentum under starting quarterback Michael Penix, who has won his first two starts of the season, against the stingy Ravens on Sunday Night Football.

items.name: David Montgomery
items.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said David Montgomery (groin) may miss “some time.”
items.analysis: It sounds like Montgomery is in danger of missing both the Jaguars and Giants games before Houston’s Week 8 bye, assuming this is just a mild injury. Woody Marks will take over as Houston’s lead back for the time being and could be in for sizable role given how no other back received a snap or touch once Montgomery went down in Week 5.

items.name: Deebo Samuel
items.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 5’s game against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: That didn’t take long. Just moments after leaving the game, it was announced that Samuel had suffered a hamstring injury and would not return to the field. Shortly after being ruled out, Samuel was shown walking gingerly to the locker room with trainers. His day ends with a 2-21-0 line on three targets. Samuel also had two carries for four yards and a lost fumble, which came on the play he was injured on.

items.name: Isaiah Williams
items.headline: Isaiah Williams caught 1-of-2 targets for 16 yards in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns, adding a three-yard rush.
items.analysis: Fill-in No. 2 wideout Williams is stuck on just four catches in three games during Adonai Mitchell’s surprisingly lengthy absence with a finger injury. The fact that Mitchell was not placed on I.R. suggests the Jets were not expecting more than a three-game absence, so Mitchell could be back as soon as Week 6 against the Patriots. Either way, Williams has not shown enough to earn a spot on 12-team league benches.

items.name: Deebo Samuel
items.headline: Deebo Samuel exited in the third quarter of Week 5’s game against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Samuel went down after being tripped up on a run play and remained down for an extended period of time after the play. It was hard to tell exactly what happened on the play, but Samuel was able to make his way to the sideline and could be seen sitting on the bench while being evaluated by trainers. We will provide an update on his status when we receive one.

items.name: Raheim Sanders
items.headline: Raheim Sanders rushed three times for 12 yards in the Browns’ Week 5 loss to the Jets, adding a one-yard reception.
items.analysis: Sanders also lost a few snaps to Jaleel McLaughlin. 4-5 touches have been Sanders’ weekly norm, but that could change for Week 6 against the Ravens after Quinshon Judkins was spotted with his right foot in a boot following today’s contest. There have not been any indications Judkins is dealing with something serious, but it’s a situation worth monitoring ahead of Tuesday evening’s waiver wire run.

items.name: Isaiah Bond
items.headline: Isaiah Bond caught 3-of-7 targets for 74 yards in the Browns’ Week 5 loss to the Jets.
items.analysis: With KC Concepcion lost to a first quarter concussion, second-year pro Bond was the next man up. His 74 yards were the second most of his career after he entered today with just 12 yards all season under new head coach Todd Monken. He notched gains of 20, 24 and 30 yards, which will undoubtedly catch the attention of the coach and quarterback. So will the shaky hands Bond displayed on a number of other targets. Bond is at best the No. 4 weapon when this offense is at full health, and Concepcion could easily be cleared for Week 6 against the Ravens. Bond is not worth a 12-team league flier at this time.

items.name: Harold Fannin
items.headline: Harold Fannin caught 1-of-4 targets for four yards in the Browns’ Week 5 loss to the Jets.
items.analysis: Fannin’s worst game of the season came in rainy New Jersey conditions. That obviously held down the Browns’ passing-game production, but it’s confusing they weren’t drawing up more manufactured, chain-moving looks for their YAC-focused tight end. Fannin established a 2026 ceiling the past two weeks, but today’s effort reminds of just how low his floor can be with Deshaun Watson under center and more target competition in the skill corps.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston caught 3-of-7 targets for 47 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 5 loss to the Jets.
items.analysis: Boston’s score was his third in five games as a pro. This one was a 29-yard strike down the left sideline where Boston won a 1-on-1 matchup with CB Brandon Stephens. Boston’s yardage totals are not popping off the page in this limited offense, but his play-making ability has been. He has also reached at least 40 yards all five times out, giving him a non-zero floor. The rookie second-rounder continues to press his WR3 case heading into Week 6 against the Ravens.

items.name: Quinshon Judkins
items.headline: Quinshon Judkins rushed 14 times for 44 yards in the Browns’ Week 5 loss to the Jets, adding three receptions for six yards.
items.analysis: Not a great day in the rain, one that got worse when Judkins was spotted in the Browns’ locker room after the fact with his right foot in a walking boot. Boots are frequently precautionary, but they are always noteworthy. Also noteworthy is that Judkins finished the game without an injury announcement. Hopefully he’s just managing a little something ahead of Week 6 against the Ravens. If not, the Browns’ backfield is a mess behind Judkins, with Raheim Sanders and Jaleel McLaughlin the next backs up.

items.name: Colston Loveland
items.headline: Colston Loveland caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers.
items.analysis: Everyone’s favorite breakout tight end is now sitting on an unseemly 110 yards receiving through five games played. It’s an inconceivable outcome after Loveland’s stretch-run and postseason dominance last season, but now very much a trend. Loveland’s “rates,” while good, just haven’t been good enough, and he is not compensating with the off-the-charts efficiency he would need to produce on that kind of usage, a la a Dalton Kincaid-type. It’s hard to throw in the TE1 towel since Loveland has only finished one game alongside QB Caleb Williams, but Williams’ likely Week 6 return against the Falcons could be something of a “last stand.” If Loveland can’t get it going with Williams back in the lineup, we might have to accept Loveland’s TE2 fate.

items.name: Rome Odunze
items.headline: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-9 targets for 40 yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers, also losing a fumble.
items.analysis: Although the Bears were already losing 31-7, Odunze’s fourth quarter giveaway was an ill-advised decision on a fourth down catch-and-run where he had already secured a new set of downs. Odunze seemed to be extending the ball forward. Unnecessary. Like every Bears pass catcher, Odunze is treading fantasy water waiting for the return of Caleb Williams (hamstring). It appears that will be Week 6 against the Falcons, but Odunze’s returns have been uneven enough that not even Williams’ re-insertion under center will be enough to get Odunze above the mid-range WR3 ranks.

items.name: Luther Burden
items.headline: Luther Burden III caught 4-of-6 targets for 47 yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers.
items.analysis: Burden “led” the Bears in receiving, but the fact that 47 yards was the team’s high-water mark tells you all you need to know about their offensive effectiveness this afternoon.
