Today was actually the first time in three games without Caleb Williams that Burden finished under 60 yards receiving, but he is still in dire need of his starting quarterback’s return. It appears that will be Week 6 against the Falcons, keeping Burden in the low-end WR2 mix despite his lack of spiked weeks through the season’s first five contests.

items.name: D'Andre Swift
items.headline: D’Andre Swift rushed nine times for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers, adding four receptions for 30 yards.
items.analysis: Swift was the only Bear to find the end zone in a throwaway performance where Tyson Bagent was benched for the fourth quarter. It was still a disappointing statline with Kyle Monangai (toe) on the shelf, but there just wasn’t much Swift could do with Bagent failing to threaten the Packers’ defense and the Bears’ D struggling mightily. Swift also lost a ton of passing-game work and targets to fill-in No. 2 RB Roschon Johnson. That’s a potentially disturbing development heading into Week 6 against the Falcons, with or without Monangai in the lineup. Thankfully, Caleb Williams (hamstring) should be back, shoring up Swift’s value in the RB10-14 range.

items.name: Greg Dulcich
items.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 4-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
items.analysis: Dulcich also added a two-point conversion to his total. It was a low-efficiency passing offense for the Dolphins once again, leading to Dulcich averaging under 10 yards per reception. The 26-year-old tight end is a fantasy TE3 as the Dolphins head into a Week 6 bye.

items.name: Tyler Shough
items.headline: Tyler Shough completed 16-of-25 passes for 96 yards and two interceptions in the Saints’ 23-13, Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
items.analysis: Shough had been coasting on extreme play volume over the first month of the fantasy season. Brian Flores and the Vikings’ hyper-aggressive defense had no issues shutting down that approach. The Saints had five drives in the first half. Only one lasted longer than three plays. Of their four second-half drives, two ended with interceptions. A fumbled kickoff coming out of the break didn’t help the team’s play volume either. Shough has ultimately been a better fantasy quarterback than a real-life passer this year and the Vikings’ defense exposed that truth for the better part of four quarters. He will look to rebound against a far worse Giants unit in Week 6.

items.name: Kevin Coleman
items.headline: Kevin Coleman caught 3-of-7 targets for 30 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
items.analysis: Coleman was heavily involved in the Dolphins’ second-half gameplan, seeing the second-most targets among Miami pass-catchers on the day. He scored on a Malik Willis red zone pass in the fourth quarter and was tackled at the one-yard line on a reception towards the end of the game. Coleman is a fifth-round rookie and unlikely to see this much volume moving forward but is an intriguing deep-league stash in case Malik Washington were to suffer an injury.

items.name: Tucker Kraft
items.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 5-of-5 targets for 64 yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears.
items.analysis: The five-catch effort was Kraft’s second straight after previously having zero. His 54 yards were almost his most since Week 1. His 46-yard reception in the third quarter was his longest of the season. All of that is good, though it was still somewhat disappointing amidst a 367-yard Jordan Love outburst where Christian Watson and Matthew Golden both eased by 100 yards. Kraft is averaging a pedestrian six targets. He’s going to need both more looks and big plays to remain a higher-end TE1. It will nevertheless be impossible to bench him for Week 6 against the Cowboys’ shaky defense.

items.name: Chris Bell
items.headline: Chris Bell caught neither of his two targets in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding one carry for 26 yards.
items.analysis: Bell was targeted just twice on the day, catching neither target. He did see a carry on an end-around play, rushing for 26 yards on his sole touch of the game. He has ramped up to a starting receiver’s workload of snaps, ranking second among Dolphins receivers with 41 snaps. Though Bell is the field more, he is yet to be a key part of the Dolphins offense and will see less opportunities once Caleb Douglas (ankle) returns. Bell is best left on fantasy benches when the Dolphins come out of their Week 6 bye.

items.name: Chris Olave
items.headline: Chris Olave caught 4-of-6 targets for 46 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
items.analysis: Olave was averaging over 120 yards per game before today’s contest. The Saints’ extreme play volume and tilt to toward passing the ball turned his great role into elite fantasy production. That finally came to a halt with Brian Flore’s defense shutting down Tyler Shough. The second-year passer completed just 16 throws for 96 yards. Shough and the entire passing attack should improve drastically versus the Giants next week. Fantasy managers can keep treating Olave as a WR1 despite this speed bump.

items.name: Matthew Golden
items.headline: Matthew Golden caught 6-of-7 targets for 123 yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears.
items.analysis: Golden’s 123 yards were his third new career high in just five games this season. In other words, his breakout year remains ongoing. Golden’s long gain was a soaring 50-yard deep shot over the middle of the field where the wideout had to go up and get it. Golden also contributed a 36-yard reception. Routinely contributing 40-plus yard grabs while also doing some nice compiling, Golden has become not only a WR2 option, but a safe one at that. That will definitely include for Week 6 vs. the Cowboys’ leaky defense.

items.name: Terry McLaurin
items.headline: Terry McLaurin caught 4-of-4 targets for 62 yards in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie with the Giants.
items.analysis: It was reported before the game that McLaurin would not be a full go after he was limited in practice all week with a hamstring injury. While McLaurin would finish the game with the third-most snaps played by any Commanders receiver, his 28 routes run were tied for the most of any player on the team. McLaurin converted all four of his targets into receptions on Sunday, with his biggest gain coming on a 22-yard reception in overtime that looked to be the start of an eventual game-winning drive for Washington. McLaurin’s 62 receiving yards led all of Washington’s pass-catchers in this one, and he has now totaled 50 or more yards in three straight games. If Stefon Diggs, who missed this week’s game (hamstring) is able to suit up next week against the 49ers, McLaurin will profile as a fringe WR2/WR3.

items.name: Malik Washington
items.headline: Malik Washington caught 6-of-8 targets for 43 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding one carry for 19 yards.
items.analysis: Washington was the most involved Dolphins receiver, leading the team in targets and receiving yards. He started things off with an 18-yard rush and saw a steady peppering of low-depth targets. Though he led all Dolphins skill-position players in snaps, Washington doesn’t see many scoring opportunities in the Miami offense. After a Week 6 bye, The 25-year-old is a volume-based FLEX play Week 7 against the Jets.

items.name: Cam Skattebo
items.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 13 times for 59 yards in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders, adding two receptions for 12 additional yards.
items.analysis: Skattebo rushed for just 12 yards on six carries in the first half as he and the Giants struggled on the ground for most of the day. He would come up with a few big runs in the second half, one of which resulted in a 19-yard gain in overtime as the Giants were attempting to drive into position for a game-winning field goal. Unfortunately for Skattebo, disaster struck later on the drive when he lost a fumble on the Commanders’ 24-yard line, which was recovered by Washington and ended any hopes of a Giants’ victory. Poor late-game clock management by the Commanders made Skattebo’s fumble a little less costly, as the two sides would end Sunday’s game in a tie, but it’s impossible to overstate how big a 4-1 start to the season would be for the Giants, who are playing in a struggling NFC East. Skattebo hasn’t rushed for more than 81 yards in any game this season and has only one touchdown to his name. His reliable volume continues to put him in fringe RB1/RB2 territory, but it’s been a disappointing start for the second-year back. He’ll look to turn things around next week against the Saints.

items.name: Devaughn Vele
items.headline: Devaughn Vele caught 4-of-6 targets for 26 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
items.analysis: Tyler Shough managed a dismal 96 passing yards in this game, so there simply wasn’t enough production for any New Orleans wideout to post usable fantasy numbers. Vele still tied Chris Olave for a team-high in targets. He has at least four catches and six targets in every game this year. Even after a quiet Week 5, Vele remains a solid WR4 option headed into a Week 6 date with the Giants.

items.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
items.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 11 times for 82 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie with the Giants.
items.analysis: Croskey-Merritt’s 82 rushing yards set a new season high. Nearly half of his yards came in the first quarter when “Bill” broke free for a 33-yard touchdown to give the Commanders a 7-0 lead on their opening drive. On the final play of the third quarter, Croskey-Merritt would rip off a 22-yard run on a drive that eventually ended on a 26-yard touchdown run by Jayden Daniels. JCM continues to be the unquestioned leader in Washington’s backfield, but he remains a touchdown-dependent fantasy option due to his lack of receiving upside. He’ll be a boom-or-bust RB2 in next week’s game against the 49ers.

items.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
items.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merrit rushed 11 times for 82 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie with the Giants.

items.name: MarShawn Lloyd
items.headline: MarShawn Lloyd rushed 10 times for 31 yards and a two touchdowns in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears, adding a six-yard reception.
items.analysis: Although he notched a receiving score in Week 2, these were the first two rushing touchdowns of Lloyd’s career. Awesome stuff, though a player who was averaging 2.7 yards per carry coming into this afternoon saw that number sit at just 3.1 against the Bears. The Pack also got journeyman Pierre Strong involved in their increasingly frustrating backfield committee. Strong was mostly just absorbing Chris Brooks’ (ankle, injured reserve) lost work, but that of course means Lloyd wasn’t seeing a bigger workload. Although the scores are nice, Lloyd is still lacking an RB2 profile heading into Week 6. He will be a low-upside FLEX vs. the Cowboys.

items.name: Dre Greenlaw
items.headline: Dre Greenlaw was ejected in the second quarter of the 49ers Week 5 game against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: A hit on Sam Darnold as he was scrambling toward the sidelines sparked a sideline scuffle between the Niners and Seahawks. In the middle of that scuffle were Greenlaw and Seahawks LB Ernest Jones. Jones, who was not wearing a helmet, was head-butted by Greenlaw, which immediately resulted in his ejection. This will certainly result in a hefty fine for Greenlaw, who could also be in danger of facing a suspension after the league has a chance to review the incident. Greenlaw has totaled 37 tackles and a forced fumble in the five games he has appeared in this season.

items.name: Juwan Johnson
items.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-5 targets for 16 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
items.analysis: Johnson had hovered around 50 yards in every game before today’s loss, but a shutdown Minnesota defense was more than enough to mute the production of every New Orleans pass-catcher. Things should improve for everyone when the Saints take on the Giants next week. Johnson will be a volume-based TE2 for Week 6.

items.name: Jaylen Wright
items.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed six times for 11 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
items.analysis: Wright entered the day questionable with a foot injury and wound up playing nine offensive snaps with special teams mixed in. The 23-year-old is the clear backup to Ollie Gordon for now, he is best left off fantasy rosters.

items.name: CJ Donaldson
items.headline: CJ Donaldson rushed four times for 13 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings, adding one catch for seven yards.
items.analysis: Alvin Kamara entered this game with a back injury and played just eight snaps in the second half, freeing up some extra work for Donaldson. He led the team in snaps, but Kendre Miller was the top option between the tackles, seeing 10 carries, one of which went for a touchdown. Even if Kamara remains on the injury report for Week 6, Donaldson won’t crack the FLEX rankings versus the Giants.

items.name: Ollie Gordon
items.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 18 times for 88 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
items.analysis: Gordon continued to operate as the Dolphins’ No. 1 running back, scoring a touchdown for the second straight week. He took all of Miami’s red zone backfield touches and was tackled at the one yard line in the third quarter, coming close to his second touchdown of the day. He lost two yards the next play and the Dolphins did not convert. Gordon saw 42 snaps on the day and will be a low-end fantasy RB2 for Week 7 against the Jets after a Week 6 bye week.

items.name: Malik Nabers
items.headline: Malik Nabers caught 11-of-20 targets for 121 yards and one touchdown in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders.
items.analysis: Nabers saw 15 of his targets come in the second half after the Giants opted to abandon a mostly useless ground game in a game they trailed for most of the afternoon. Nabers came up with multiple big plays as the Giants mounted their comeback attempt, with his biggest coming on a leaping 17-yard touchdown in the end zone to tie the game at 27-27 with under two minutes to go in the game. Nabers had a key drop on a screen pass in overtime that had a chance to set up a big gain, but he made up for it later in the game with a 28-yard gain as the Giants were trying to position themselves for a potential game-winning field goal attempt. Nabers has now gone for 100-plus yards in back-to-back weeks and has found the end zone in both of those games. He seems to finally be hitting his stride after a slow start to the season, and will profile as a high-end WR2 in next week’s game against the Saints.

items.name: Christian Watson
items.headline: Christian Watson caught 6-of-8 targets for 143 yards and two touchdowns.
items.analysis: Watson’s 143-yard outburst was the third highest receiving total of his career, joining a Week 11 2024 effort and his 6/147/2 broadside against the Vikings this Week 1. Rather amazingly, the two-score effort was his seventh. This one came in true Watson fashion, as he found the end zone from 42 and 53 yards out. For the 42-yarder he ran right by the defense. For the 53-yarder, he high-pointed the ball off the defender’s helmet in the end zone. It was just that kind of day for the Packers, and it’s been just that kind of season for a wideout in Watson who continues to break out. Now firmly in the weekly WR1 mix, Watson has a potential Week 6 smash spot in the sorry Cowboys.

items.name: Alvin Kamara
items.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed three times for 12 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
items.analysis: He “added” two catches for -6 yards. Kamara rotated with Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson throughout the game. Donaldson ultimately led the backfield in snaps, while Miller’s 10 carries paced the team. Kamara only touched the ball once in the second half and spent long stretches of the final two quarters on the sidelines with his helmet off. The team was likely managing his reps while he played through a back injury. He was listed as questionable heading into today’s game. As part of a three-man committee, Kamara is barely an RB4 for his Week 6 date with the Giants.

items.name: Isaiah Likely
items.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 11-of-13 targets for 94 yards and two touchdown in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders
items.analysis: Likely set a new career-high with 11 receptions in this one, and came up with two clutch touchdowns in the process. His first score came on a three-yard strike from Jameis Winston on a third-and-goal play that the Giants needed to stay in the game, cutting the Commanders’ lead to 19-13. Then, in the fourth quarter and with the Giants facing a fourth-and-eight, Likely turned an eight-yard reception upfield for a 17-yard touchdown that nearly looked like a fumble and turnover at the goal-line. Likely has been targeted 25 times in his last two games and has now gone for 66 or more yards in three of five games to start the season. He’s starting to show good chemistry with Jameis Winston and will be on the TE1 radar in next week’s game against the Saints.

items.name: Garrett Wilson
items.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 7-of-11 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns.
items.analysis: The 100-yard effort was Wilson’s second in three weeks. It was no easy feat on a rainy afternoon in Jersey where Geno Smith completed only 17 passes. Wilson’s score was a 32-yarder where he spun out of a tackle for a catch-and-run house call. In addition to the 100-yard efforts, Wilson now has a score in three of his past four appearances. It’s like Wilson’s lost 2025 never happened, which is exactly what the Jets and fantasy managers were hoping for. A weekly fixture in the low-end WR1 ranks, Wilson has a Week 6 date with the Patriots.

items.name: Tanner Hudson
items.headline: Tanner Hudson caught 3-of-3 targets for 14 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Hudson saw three targets on the day, catching a Joe Burrow touchdown pass towards the end of the first half. The Bengals used all of their tight ends against Miami; Hudson saw 19 snaps while Mike Gesicki saw 28 and Erick All and Drew Sample tied with 33 snaps. It was a run-heavy day for Cincy, but the four tight ends all combined for nine targets. All caught all three of his targets for 25 yards while Sample caught his only target for five yards.

items.name: Mike Gesicki
items.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 1-of-2 targets for 4 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: The Bengals utilized all of their tight ends against the Dolphins, with Gesicki catching just one pass on the day. His sole reception was a touchdown on the Bengals’ opening drive, totaling four on the season and salvaging some fantasy value for those who streamed him at tight end this week. Gesicki’s value is lowered when Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are active; his red zone utilization makes Gesicki a low-end fantasy TE2 heading into the Bengals’ Week 6 bye.

items.name: Laquon Treadwell
items.headline: Laquon Treadwell caught 2-of-8 targets for 34 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: Treadwell was third on the team in targets, but he’s seeing most of his work on deep passes down the field, which Daniel Jones has had a hard time connecting on. Treadwell did play only three fewer snaps than Josh Downs and ran 39 routes on 47 dropbacks. We should note that Keenan Allen (groin) was not playing a full snap share in his first week back from injury, so Treadwell could see his role slip a bit next week. Even so, he’s a downfield threat on a team that has struggled to pass the ball, which makes it hard to roster him outside of the deepest formats.

items.name: Tai Felton
items.headline: Tai Felton caught 2-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints.
items.analysis: Jordan Addison missed this game with an ankle injury and the Vikings deployed Felton as their WR2 over Jauan Jennings. Jennings ran fewer routes and failed to catch his only target. Felton wasn’t awfully productive either, but it’s good to see the former third-round pick picking up more work in his second season. He will return to a rotational role, assuming Addison is cleared to play after the Vikings’ Week 6 bye.

items.name: Braelon Allen
items.headline: Braelon Allen rushed 24 times for 116 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns.
items.analysis: Allen surprisingly added just one catch for zero yards on four targets. Not ideal, though Allen’s rushing output nearly doubled his previous career high of 59. It was exactly what the Jets and fantasy managers needed during Breece Hall’s second straight absence with a quad injury. Allen contributed runs of 10, 17, 11 and 22 yards, with that final rush finding the end zone. He also had a 13-yarder called back by holding. In other words, he was both grinding out tough yards and providing longer gains. Isaiah Davis mixed in for only cursory breather back work. With Hall yet to resume practicing, Allen should have another plug-and-play RB2 setup in Week 6 against the Patriots.

items.name: Tyler Warren
items.headline: Tyler Warren caught 7-of-9 targets for 83 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: Warren also added a one-yard touchdown run on a tush push after Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones were stuffed on the previous three plays. The second-year tight end ran a route on 40 of the team’s 47 dropbacks and shared the team lead in targets with Keenan Allen. Daniel Jones is keeping the ceiling of this passing game in check with his inefficient play, but Warren is probably the most reliable receiver on the team and remains a TE1. He just lacks the upside to push inside the top five at the position unless Jones can get going.

items.name: Dohnte Meyers
items.headline: Dohnte Meyers caught 2-of-2 targets for 12 yards in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: With both Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins active, Meyers saw just 19 offensive snaps. He caught both of his targets but his biggest play was an 81-yard kickoff return to start things off in the first quarter. As long as Chase and Higgins are playing, Meyers is best left on fantasy benches.

items.name: Geno Smith
items.headline: Geno Smith completed 17-of-30 passes for 182 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ 17-12, Week 5 win over the Browns.
items.analysis: Smith “added” five carries for seven yards. He also lost a fumble. Coming off a generationally bad Week 4 clunker against the Bears, Smith was hardly outstanding in rainy MetLife Stadium conditions, though he was superior to Deshaun Watson. Not that you would have noticed in real time. Smith fumbled “just” once compared to Watson’s four, also taking “only” four sacks to Watson’s staggering eight. Like Watson, Smith also lost a key pass catcher to a concussion, with Kenyon Sadiq going down in the third quarter. Both before and after Sadiq’s injury, the Jets mostly rode the run, with Braelon Allen turning his 24 carries into a strong 116 yards. Smith has predictably faded a bit after his relatively “hot start,” while he now has a tough Week 6 road test in the reviving Patriots. Smith’s decent weapons — which will hopefully include Adonai Mitchell next week — keep him in the QB2 mix, but only as a low-end option.

items.name: Keenan Allen
items.headline: Keenan Allen caught 5-of-9 targets for 45 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: Allen did not play a full complement of snaps in his first week back from a groin injury. He played 32 of the team’s 71 snaps and ran a route on 28 of their 47 dropbacks. That makes him leading the team with nine targets even more impressive. Of course, the Colts were forced to throw almost 50 times because the Steelers made it a priority to contain Jonathan Taylor. It’s highly unlikely Daniel Jones throws that much going forward, but Allen remains the top target in the offense. The issue is that most of his targets are in the short-yardage areas of the field, so he is more of a fringe-FLEX option unless you’re in a full PPR league. Next week against the Titans is a good matchup for the Colts, though.

items.name: Gavin Bartholomew
items.headline: Gavin Bartholomew caught 5-of-6 targets for 33 yards in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints.
items.analysis: A sixth-round pick in 2025, Bartholomew didn’t see the field as a rookie. He logged his first career catch last week. With T.J. Hockenson leaving the game in the first quarter because of a concussion, Bartholomew stepped up as the team’s TE1. He was largely a check-down option for Kyler Murray, though that’s par for the course with Murray’s tight end. Hockenson should be cleared to return after a Week 6 bye, keeping Bartholomew off the fantasy radar for now.

items.name: Efton Chism
items.headline: Efton Chism caught 5-of-6 targets for 57 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Chism came down with some big catches to keep the chains moving. He seems to have earned the trust of the Patriots coaching staff and Drake Maye in recent weeks. Even so, his route participation has been limited and his role could shrink next week if A.J. Brown returns from his high ankle injury. For now he’s an OK stash in deeper fantasy leagues in case he carves out a bigger role in the rejuvenated New England passing offense.

items.name: Case Keenum
items.headline: Case Keenum completed 11-of-19 passes for 108 yards and an interception in the Bears’ 31-7, Week 5 loss to the Packers.
items.analysis: With the Bears trailing 31-7, Keenum was subbed in for Tyson Bagent for the fourth quarter. He provided more passing production in one quarter than Bagent did in three, but the Packers were obviously sitting back a bit in coverage. Keenum also equalled Bagent’s turnover total, as he lost a fumble in addition to his pick. Keenum was livelier than Bagent, but hardly better. With Caleb Williams appearing likely to return from his hamstring injury in Week 6 against the Falcons, this is hopefully the last we hear of the Bears’ backup situation for the foreseeable future. If it’s not, we would have to assume it’s now “advantage Keenum.”

items.name: Tee Higgins
items.headline: Tee Higgins caught 2-of-4 targets for 22 yards in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Higgins saw just four targets against the Dolphins after seeing 16 targets in Week 4. The adductor/neck injuries didn’t limit his playing time as much, seeing 45 snaps on the day, No. 2 among Bengals receivers. With Ja’Marr Chase back on the field, Higgins’ target volume decreased considerably and he totaled just 22 yards in a more run-favorable game script. Despite the dud, Higgins still belongs in the WR2 ranks and gets a mediocre Ravens defense in Week 7 after a Week 6 bye.

items.name: Josh Downs
items.headline: Josh Downs caught 3-of-6 targets for 47 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: The good news is that Downs ran a route on 44 of the Colts’ 47 dropbacks. He was also targeted down the field a few times. The bad news is that Daniel Jones was not effective and hasn’t been throughout the season. Downs did have another 15-yard completion called back due to a penalty away from the ball, but it wouldn’t have made a huge difference in his day. Downs is still on the WR3 radar because the Colts play the Titans next week, but until Jones can get it going, it’s hard to trust anybody other than Tyler Warren in this passing attack.

items.name: Romeo Doubs
items.headline: Romeo Doubs caught 1-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Drake Maye carved up the Vegas secondary to the tune of 376 yards and four touchdowns, with almost none of it going to be nominal No. 1 wideout. Doubs, who last week against the Bills had 58 yards and two touchdowns, nearly came down with a short touchdown grab in the third quarter on a nice touch throw from Maye. The potential return of A.J. Brown (ankle) in Week 6 against the Jets could limit Doubs’ targets going forward. With Maye cooking, Doubs remains a potential flex option in 14-team formats going forward.

items.name: Ja'Marr Chase
items.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 6-of-10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Chase returned from a concussion he suffered last week, seeing 10 targets in a productive fantasy day. He saw a goal-line fade target on the Bengals’ first drive and was later tackled at the one-yard line towards the end of the first half. Joe Burrow missed Chase for a 70-yard touchdown in the second half but Chase made a miraculous catch with his right arm for a 45-yard touchdown later in the half. He finishes with a successful fantasy day and is squarely in the WR1 ranks heading into the Bengals’ Week 6 bye.

items.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
items.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson had 13 rushes for 64 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding three catches for 21 yards.
items.analysis: Stevenson was splitting the backfield workload with TreVeyon Henderson before Henderson sustained a potentially serious ankle injury in the second quarter and did not return. Stevenson was somewhat efficient with his opportunities, breaking a few tackles against a low-energy, low-effort Raiders defense. His touchdown came on a goal line carry in the first half. It was his second score of the year. Stevenson will be a top-12 fantasy option next week against the Jets if Henderson is sidelined.

items.name: Jameis Winston
items.headline: Jameis Winston completed 33-of-54 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns in the Giants’ 27-27, Week 5 tie with the Commanders.
items.analysis: After a shaky first half in which he threw for just 72 yards on 16 passes, Winston locked in for the second half and nearly led the Giants to a comeback win. Winston completed 21-of-28 passes for 211-3-0 in the second half, leading the Giants on touchdown drives of 63, 75, and 72 yards. Winston connected with tight end Isaiah Likely on a three-yard touchdown pass for his first of the day, and found Likely again for a 17-yard score on a fourth-and-eight to cut Washington’s lead to 27-20. On their final touchdown drive, Winston connected with Malik Nabers four times and found him in the end zone for a leaping touchdown grab to tie the game at 27-27 with less than two minutes left in regulation. In overtime, Winston twice moved the Giants into field-goal range. Unfortunately, they would only get one chance at attempting a go-ahead field goal. After Dominic Zvada missed the first try, a fumble by Cam Skattebo would cost the Giants any hopes of a second attempt to win the game. Winston has thrown for 576 yards, six touchdowns, and two interceptions in his last two games while attempting just over 60 percent of his passes. He profiles as a mid-to-low-end QB2 next week against the Saints.

items.name: Jonathan Taylor
items.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 15 times for 45 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: Taylor added 37 receiving yards on three catches. As JJ Watt noted on the broadcast, the Steelers knew that the Colts love running off tackle, so they sent extra rushers and had their defensive ends bracket the tackles to force the Colts to run up the gut. It didn’t work out well for the Colts. Taylor had no running room all day and was stuffed inside the three-yard line three separate times. Things will likely be better next week against the Titans, but the Colts are going to need to fix their issues in the interior of their offensive line.

items.name: Jayden Daniels
items.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 17-of-25 passes for 199 yards in the Commanders’ 27-27, Week 5 tie with the Giants, adding nine carries for 103 additional yards and two touchdowns.
items.analysis: Daniels turned in one of the best games of his career on the ground on Sunday against the Giants. Daniels broke off an uncontested 38-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to put the Commanders up 19-6, and later broke free for a 26-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter to again extend the Commanders’ lead. Both runs came on scrambles where the Giants seemingly forgot Daniels was a threat to run at any moment, and Daniels made the most of his opportunities. With the Commanders in range for a game-winning field goal late in overtime, Daniels inexplicably took a sack with no timeouts left on what appeared to be an attempt to center the ball in time for the game-winning try. We’ll likely get an explanation from both Daniels and head coach Dan Quinn on that final play, but Washington snatched defeat from the jaws of victory to move to 1-3-1 on the season. Despite the late-game gaffe, Daniels looked on-point for most of the afternoon, but struggled at times against the blitz, as the Giants brought pressure in several key spots to force Daniels to get the ball out quick or throw it away. Daniels looked like the elite dual threat fantasy managers want to see, and will be firmly in the QB1 ranks in next week’s game against the 49ers.

items.name: Justin Jefferson
items.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 6-of-7 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints.
items.analysis: Jefferson didn’t miss a beat after returning from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury. He made several spectacular grabs in this game, the most amazing of which was a toe-tapping catch in the back of the end zone with three defenders covering him. Even at less than full strength, Jefferson is simply one of the best receivers in the league. He will remain near the top of the WR1 ranks when the Vikings face the Colts after their bye week.

items.name: Corey Kiner
items.headline: Corey Kiner had six rushes for 52 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding one catch for seven yards.
items.analysis: Kiner’s seven touches came after TreVeyon Henderson went down with what could be a serious ankle injury in the second quarter. While much of his work came in garbage time, Kiner could work as the Patriots’ No. 2 back behind Rhamondre Stevenson if Henderson is sidelined in Week 6. Kiner is worth a look on waiver wires this week.

items.name: Samaje Perine
items.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 14 times for 68 yards in the Bengals’ Week 5 loss to the Dolphins, adding 2 receptions for 10 yards and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Perine was involved heavily against the Dolphins, a surprising development given his lack of touches to open the season. He trailed Chase Brown by just five snaps on the day, getting involved in short-yardage situations and seeing an increase in red zone snaps after Brown’s red zone fumble in the second quarter. He caught a touchdown running a route out of the backfield and finished with 78 total yards. We don’t expect Perine to consistently see this kind of usage, but he is back on the radar as a deep-league FLEX value.

items.name: Gunnar Helm
items.headline: Gunnar Helm failed to catch his only target in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
items.analysis: 45 snaps, one target. Helm has somehow grown less relevant than his 4/28 Week 1 showing would have even suggested. He can be dropped in most leagues at this point.

items.name: DK Metcalf
items.headline: DK Metcalf caught 3-of-4 targets for 12 yards in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts.
items.analysis: This was not the game many expected against a beleaguered Colts defense. Two of Metcalf’s three catches were on screens behind the line of scrimmage, and he was only targeted 10 yards down the field once. Aaron Rodgers is not having much success throwing the ball deep down the field, which means Metcalf is likely going to be a touchdown-dependent WR3 in fantasy next week against the Bucs.

items.name: Chase Brown
items.headline: Chase Brown rushed 13 times for 39 yards and a fumble in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins, adding 3 receptions for 21 yards.
items.analysis: Brown took a surprising backseat to Samaje Perine in the Bengals’ win over the Dolphins. He still led out-snapped Perine 38-to-33, but a red zone fumble hurt his fantasy production while splitting backfield touches 50/50. Brown previously dominated all sorts of touches for the Bengals backfield, so this is a new development. Game script certainly played a factor but Brown’s ceiling as an RB1 may be considerably lessened if Perine’s usage sticks. He is a fantasy RB2 with a Week 7 matchup against the Ravens on the horizon after a Week 6 bye.

items.name: Calvin Ridley
items.headline: Calvin Ridley caught 2-of-3 targets for 33 yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Titans.
items.analysis: Is this doing anything for anybody? Ridley had a 23-yarder to open the game and vanished thereafter. He has not cracked more than two catches or three targets all year and does not need to be in fantasy consideration in the vast, vast majority of leagues.

items.name: Drake Maye
items.headline: Drake Maye completed 26-of-34 attempts for 374 yards and four touchdowns in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding seven rushes for 25 yards and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Maye had all day to operate in the pocket against a Raiders front seven that entered Week 5 with the league’s ninth highest pressure rate and fourth highest quick pressure rate. He attacked the Vegas secondary downfield from start to finish, hitting Kyle Williams and Pop Douglas for long touchdowns, and Williams for another long gain that put the Pats inside the five yard line. Maye’s rushing score came on a green scramble in the third quarter. Fully emerged from his early-season struggles, Maye is once again carving up opposing coverage units and causing fits with his scrambling ability. Maye, with eight total touchdowns over his past two outings, should be locked into lineups next week against a middling Jets secondary.

items.name: Germie Bernard
items.headline: Germie Bernard caught 6-of-9 targets for 80 yards in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts.
items.analysis: Michael Pittman (foot) was ruled out earlier in the week, and then Roman Wilson dislocated his finger during the game, so there wasn’t a lot of competition for Bernard and DK Metcalf. The rookie from Alabama played the same number of snaps as Metcalf and ran a route on 35 of the team’s 38 dropbacks. This isn’t an explosive passing attack, but Bernard looks like the WR2 in Pittsburgh now and is more of an intermediate and short-area target than DK Metcalf, which could lead to decent fantasy value over the next few weeks.

items.name: Carnell Tate
items.headline: Carnell Tate caught 1-of-5 targets for six yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
items.analysis: Well, at least last week was good. He did have a 40-plus yarder pulled off the board because of a holding penalty. Next week offers a more welcoming Colts defense and Tate should have a path to low-end WR3 numbers there.

items.name: Tyjae Spears
items.headline: Tyjae Spears rushed two times for zero yards, adding nine catches for 28 yards on nine targets, in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
items.analysis: He fumbled away one of his rushes, but with the Titans trailing for most of the second half, piled up nine catches as Cam Ward sought refuge from Houston’s pass rush. His final catch of the day — we’re not kidding — came as Ward threw it at him despite Spears having already crumpled to the ground. It lost six yards. Given the Colts likely won’t do this against the Titans next week, Spears is probably not going to keep lines like this going.

items.name: Joe Burrow
items.headline: Joe Burrow completed 23-of-32 passes for 190 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 31-24, Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
items.analysis: The Bengals offense mostly had a smooth-sailing day against the lackadaisical Dolphins defense. After a high-volume Week 4, Burrow threw 32 passes, tossing touchdowns to Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, and Tanner Hudson in the first half. He just missed Ja’Marr Chase for a 70-yard score in the second half, but later connected with Chase for a 45-yard score in the third quarter. Burrow was hardly under pressure and had plenty of time to make accurate throws and take deep shots against Miami. He is a fantasy QB1 heading into the Bengals’ bye and gets a middling defense in the Ravens for Week 7.

items.name: Tyson Bagent
items.headline: Tyson Bagent completed 12-of-21 passes for 87 scoreless yards and two interceptions before being benched in the fourth quarter of the Bears’ 31-7, Week 5 loss to the Packers.

items.name: Dylan Laube
items.headline: Dylan Laube had four rushes for nine yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots, adding three receptions for 16 yards.
items.analysis: Laube functioned as the team’s No. 2 back behind Ashton Jeanty, who battled through foot and ankle issues on his way to 77 scoreless yards against New England. Mike Washington, meanwhile, had one rushing attempt and did not catch a pass. If Jeanty misses time this season it might be Laube who leads the Vegas backfield in touches. He can be stashed in deeper formats headed into Week 6.

items.name: Tony Pollard
items.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 14 times for 52 yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
items.analysis: Pollard looks like he could be a legitimate NFL running back somewhere, but it sure can’t happen on this offense. He’s cleared 14 carries and 48 yards in each of his last four games and has just one touchdown to show for it. It’s fringe low-end RB2 land for Pollard, as usual, against the Colts next week.

items.name: Kyler Murray
items.headline: Kyler Murray completed 24-of-30 passes for 229 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ 23-13, Week 5 win over the Vikings.
items.analysis: Murray was extremely active on the ground, addnig 51 yards on 10 rush attempts. His deep ball, on the other hand, remains a work in progress. His lone touchdown of the day came on a dime to Justin Jefferson on the back of the end zone. He was hesitant to even pull the trigger on deep shots at other times, even when his receiver was wide open. Murray is largely a game-manager right now, but that’s enough to win football games when the Minnesota defense is simply shutting down every opponent they face. Murray will be a mid-range QB2 when he returns to take on the Colts after a Week 6 bye.

items.name: Daniel Jones
items.headline: Daniel Jones completed 24-of-44 passes for 267 yards in the Colts’ 34-22, Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
items.analysis: The 267 yards aren’t a terrible total for Jones, but the Colts’ offense was not effective for most of the game. They were stuffed inside the Steelers’ three-yard line at least four times during the game, and the only touchdown they scored was on a one-yard sneak to tight end Tyler Warren. Even on that play, Warren was stuffed short of the end zone and had to be pushed in from behind. Jones was unable to connect with any receivers down the field and overthrew a few deep shots on the day. The Steelers spent a lot of energy trying to corral Jonathan Taylor, and you’d assume other defenses will deploy the same strategy, which means Jones is going to need to start to make them pay. Things should get easier next week against the winless Titans.

items.name: Cam Ward
items.headline: Cam Ward completed 23-of-36 passes for 170 scoreless yards and an interception in Tennessee’s Week 5, 26-3 loss to the Texans.
items.analysis: The Titans led off the day with a 58-yard field-goal drive that fell apart from a red zone first-and-5. They would not even flirt with crossing 30 yards in a drive for the rest of the game and crossed into Texans territory on only 11 more snaps all game, including just one inside the Houston 40. Ward took four sacks and avoided several others by turning Tyjae Spears into a PPR hero. The closest he came to actually putting points on the board was a double-covered bomb to Carnell Tate’s general area. It was, well, what you would have expected from both sides in the preseason. Ward remains a last gasp supeflex QB2 heading into Week 6’s game against the Colts.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Brock Bowers caught 8-of-10 targets for 110 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots.
items.analysis: Bowers was again unstoppable both from the slot and from the boundary. The injury-ravaged New England secondary had no chance of stopping Bowers, whose ten targets led the Raiders. Bowers had three receptions of over 20 yards. His day could’ve been bigger if the Raiders had not rested their starters in the fourth quarter of the lopsided loss to the Patriots. With outrageous usage in Klint Kubiak’s offense, Bowers has as much upside as any player in fantasy for now. He gets the Bills in Week 6.

items.name: Malik Willis
items.headline: Malik Willis completed 15-of-27 passes for 137 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions and a fumble in the Dolphins’ 31-24, Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding eight rushes for 74 yards and a touchdown.
items.analysis: Willis had a poor passing day, finishing the first quarter completing 0-of-4 passes. He threw a pair of second quarter interceptions to Jordan Battle, the first coming off a tip and the second on a cross-body throw and poor decision. He also fumbled and recovered a snap in the two-minute drill while a potential third interception was dropped in the endzone in the second half. Willis recovered with a touchdown throw to Kevin Coleman in the fourth quarter but fumbled deep in the Dolphins’ own territory late in the game. He capped off his day with a quick goal-line rushing score at the end of the game but it was too little, too late. Between his decision-making and lack of ball security, Willis had a poor game but good fantasy production due to his rushing output. Willis is a fantasy QB2 heading into a Week 6 Dolphins bye week.

items.name: Hunter Henry
items.headline: Hunter Henry caught 3-of-4 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Henry was third on the team in targets and caught one of Drake Maye’s four touchdown tosses on the day. Henry has seen better involvement in the Pats offense of late; against the Bills in Week 4 he caught all five of his targets for 62 yards. The resurgence of the Patriots passing attack has made Henry viable as a streaming option. He’ll be in play next week against the Jets.

items.name: Aaron Rodgers
items.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 22-of-31 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the Steelers’ 34-22, Week 5 win over the Colts.
items.analysis: The Steelers seemed worried about the Colts’ pass rush today, so there were a lot of quick-hit passes from Rodgers. The vast majority of them went to running backs or tight ends. Only nine of Rodgers’ 22 completions went to wide receivers, and 80 of his 235 passing yards came on a short pass to Jaylen Warren that the running back took up the sideline for a long touchdown. That’s not to say Rodgers didn’t play well. He did a good job avoiding sacks and not taking negative plays, but the Steelers’ offense didn’t look very potent outside of two explosive plays from Jaylen Warren. They may find things a little bit tougher against the Bucs next week.

items.name: Dalton Schultz
items.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: If you’re thinking all Dalton Schultz lines have started to blur together, you’re not wrong. He’s had eight catches for 69 yards since his Week 2 explosion against the Bengals. There’s not much upside here, but at least he’s providing a safe TE2 floor for those of you who get five points per TE reception.

items.name: DeMario Douglas
items.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 4-of-5 targets for 65 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Douglas had his first two touchdown grabs of the season as Drake Maye sliced and diced a lifeless Vegas defense from start to finish. Douglas was wide open standing in the end zone by himself for his first score, and broke out of a bunch formation inside the ten yard line for his second score. Douglas has run significant routes in the New England offense since A.J. Brown (ankle) went down to injury. When Brown returns — perhaps this week — Douglas will take on a smaller role in the Pats pass game. He should remain on waiver wires in most formats.

items.name: Xavier Hutchinson
items.headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 4-of-5 targets for 65 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Jaguars.
items.analysis: He led the team in receiving and didn’t have any contested drops today, so that’s a step up from where he’s been most of the year. Still, he played just 27-of-65 snaps. Kayshon Boutte (39-of-65) would be our main target as Houston’s third receiver if we thought the offense was good enough to warrant that kind of respect; they aren’t.

items.name: Aaron Jones
items.headline: Aaron Jones rushed 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints, adding three catches for four yards.
items.analysis: Jones had been seeing elite workloads ever since Jordan Mason was placed on IR with a thumb injury. He hadn’t done all that much with the opportunities but finally got going downhill today. Jones ran right over a New Orleans defender for a short touchdown early in the fourth quarter. He then salted the game away with a handful of chunk gains late in the contest. Mason is eligible to return after the Vikings’ Week 6 bye, so this may be the last we’ve seen of Jones in a three-down role for now.

items.name: Jaylin Noel
items.headline: Jaylin Noel caught 5-of-5 passes for 41 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: Noel added a one-yard carry that made him the team’s leader in wideout touches. His touchdown came as C.J. Stroud extended the play by spinning backwards out of the pocket and floated towards the end zone before delivering a strike to Noel. He still played just 30 of 65 snaps, but there’s a commitment to touches for Noel that seems fantasy-interesting, at least ahead of any Marvin Harrison Jr. news on Monday. He’s a FLEX possibility next week against the Jaguars in London.

items.name: Ashton Jeanty
items.headline: Ashton Jeanty had 10 rushes for 27 yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots, adding three catches for 50 yards.
items.analysis: Most of Jeanty’s production against New England came on a 31-yard catch and run in the third quarter. Battling through foot and ankle injuries, Jeanty looked hobbled from the start and struggled to break tackles or outrun Patriots defenders to the edge. Most Raiders starters rested in the fourth quarter of a lopsided loss. Jeanty still doesn’t have a rushing touchdown on the season and hasn’t had 100 rushing yards in a game since Week 1 against the Dolphins. Until Jeanty is fully healthy he probably won’t provide much in the way of upside, including next week against a decent Buffalo run defense.

items.name: Nico Collins
items.headline: Nico Collins caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: He went for 3/45 in the first half and was mostly managed down with the Texans not really threatened in a major way after he sealed a block for their first touchdown in the third quarter. Collins took a hard fall after a leaping grab and did look a little worse for the wear on the sideline. We wouldn’t be surprised if he saw injury report time this week. That said, he looked good and the Texans simply didn’t need to throw the ball much late in this one. It’s back to the low-end WR1 line next week against the Jaguars.

items.name: Woody Marks
items.headline: Woody Marks rushed 15 times for 62 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans, adding four catches for 23 yards on four targets.
items.analysis: He had a 20-ish yard touchdown taken off the board on what appeared to be a ticky-tack holding penalty. The more important story here is that David Montgomery (groin) went down mid-game and the Texans gave Marks a full workload. He had 56-of-65 snaps and no other back received a carry or touch. Marks won’t get that kind of workload next week against the Jaguars, but if Montgomery is destined for a long absence, he should threaten 70 percent of the snaps and a majority of the workload, making him one of the day’s bigger fantasy winners.

items.name: Kirk Cousins
items.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 19-of-28 attempts for 243 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots.
items.analysis: Cousins didn’t play poorly, but didn’t do much beyond connecting with Brock Bowers for some long gains in the first half, before the Patriots avalanched the severely overmatched Raiders in the third quarter. Cousins was sacked three times while narrowly avoiding a few other big losses, as the Vegas offensive line struggled to protect him throughout. His muted showing comes after 11 touchdown tosses over the season’s first four games in Klint Kubiak’s offense. Cousins will look to bounce back in Week 6 against the Bills in what should be a high-scoring affair.

items.name: C.J. Stroud
items.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 26-of-34 passes for 261 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s 26-3, Week 5 win over the Titans.
items.analysis: He added a rushing touchdown on a goal-to-go red zone keeper. The Texans offense continues to bog down with penalties and bad runs — they went into half with four field goals — but Stroud was able to pilot the ship well enough to keep things reasonable until the Titans defense broke in the second half. He’ll head to London next week to face the Jaguars, yet another team that should keep him throwing given how good their run defense is, so he’ll be a mid-range QB2 for that one.

items.name: Jakobi Meyers
items.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 2-of-3 targets for 37 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
items.analysis: Meyers has been held to two and three catches over his past two games. It’s probably not a coincidence that Brenton Strange leads the team with 14 catches during Meyers’ two-game slump. Meyers is still operating as the Jags’ WR2, but his role will come down to matchup nuances on a week-to-week basis. He is sliding back into the WR5 fantasy ranks ahead of his Week 6 matchup with the Texans.

items.name: Brenton Strange
items.headline: Brenton Strange caught 7-of-8 targets for 68 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
items.analysis: After a quiet three games to start the year, Strange has heated up over the past two weeks. He led the team with seven catches last week and did so again today in London. Strange had seven catches in his first three games combined. He can’t be expected to pace the Jags in receiving, but Strange is back on the TE1/2 border for his Week 6 date with Houston.

items.name: Chris Rodriguez
items.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed two times for five yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
items.analysis: Rodriguez was all but phased out of the rotation in this game. His most notable touch was a goal line carry which he was stuffed on and then fumbled the ball away. He was called down on the field. Even though replay clearly showed him losing the ball, there was no clear recovery and the refs didn’t bother overturning the non-fumble. Rodriguez may still be the occasional touchdown vulture, but his role has been reduced to the point where fantasy managers can safely cut ties with him on the next run of waivers.

items.name: Kenyon Sadiq
items.headline: Kenyon Sadiq suffered a concussion in the Jets’ Week 5 game against the Browns and will not return.
items.analysis: To make matters worse, Sadiq suffered the injury in the process of losing a fumble. Targeted on a 3rd-and-9 near the goal line in the third quarter, Sadiq was short of the first down and got “Peanut punched” for the giveaway. With neither side getting anything going in rainy New Jersey conditions, Sadiq had just two receptions for three yards before going down, getting out-produced by a returning Mason Taylor in the process. Now highly questionable for Week 6 against the Patriots, Sadiq will not be on the streamer radar if given the go-ahead.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 22 times for 72 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles, adding two catches for 24 yards.
items.analysis: The Jags’ offense struggled to execute at a basic level in this game, and Tuten may have been hurt the most by errors. Their first goal line sequence of the day started with a Chris Rodriguez near-fumble. After two incomplete passes, Liam Coen dialed up a jet sweep for Tuten that was blown up for a loss of six yards. The Jags’ next goal line sequence featured a pair of delay of game penalties followed by an incomplete pass on fourth down. Tuten got the full workhorse treatment in this game, ceding just two carries and one catch to his backups. He unfortunately could not make much of the touches. Tuten will be a high-end RB2 if this role persists into his Week 6 matchup versus the Texans.

items.name: Jonah Savaiinaea
items.headline: Dolphins OL Jonah Savaiinaea is questionable to return Week 5 against the Bengals with an ankle injury.
items.analysis: Savaiinaea hurt his ankle at some point in the second quarter and was declared questionable to return. He stood on the sidelines for some time but Jarrett Kingston is in at right guard for the 22-year-old second-year lineman.

items.name: TreVeyon Henderson
items.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) has been ruled out in Week 5 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Henderson had 38 yards on five touches before suffering the ankle injury on a sideline tackle in the second quarter. He needed help getting to the locker room and did not return to action. Henderson, who has dealt with a string of injuries over the past few months, could miss significant time, leaving Rhamondre Stevenson as the Patriots’ unquestioned workhorse back for now.

items.name: Jalen Hurts
items.headline: Jalen Hurts completed 21-of-40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ 19-17, Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Hurts added a grand total of two yards on the ground. The Eagles even seemed afraid to use him for tush pushes, opting for a shotgun handoff on an early fourth-and-one. The bulk of Hurts’ production through the air came on a single deep shot to Darius Cooper. Hurts’ pass was actually a bit off the mark, but Cooper adjusted well and sprinted into the end zone for a 62-yard touchdown. Hurts had Dontayvion Wicks wide open for his second long score of the day late in the third quarter, but an all-out blitz forced him to throw off his back foot and he overshot the attempt. A field goal with eight seconds left on the clock still should have been enough to win the game. Philly’s kick coverage unit then got burned by Ameer Abdullah, setting up a walk-off kick from Cam Little. The Philly offense is as lifeless as they come. Even if DeVonta Smith returns for Week 6 versus the Panthers, Hurts will fail to crack the top-12 at quarterback for the first time in years.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: CBS Sports’ Melanie Collins reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is “walking without a limp.”
items.analysis: Brown sustained a high ankle sprain in the season opener against Seattle and has rehabbed over the past month. Patriots OC Josh McDaniels told Collins he doesn’t anticipate any delay in Brown’s return to the lineup. The team believes Brown will be ready to go in Week 6. He’ll re-enter a Patriots offense that has found its footing in recent weeks following a rough start to the year. His return would be a nice bump for Drake Maye, one of the league’s best downfield passers.

items.name: Marvin Harrison
items.headline: Cardinals declared Marvin Harrison Jr., QB Carson Beck, CB Starling Thomas, Andrew Wingard and DL Andrew Billings inactive for Week 5 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Life continues to be rough for fantasy managers rostering Harrison. The soon-to-be ex-Cardinal will not participate in what should be a fantasy-friendly game against the porous Lions defense. Bummer. Still no definitive word on where he will end up next week. Trey McBride, Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne benefit from his absence. The Cardinals will be without Wingard, one of two starting safeties, but will have DT Walter Nolen (calf) available to them.

items.name: George Kittle
items.headline: George Kittle (illness) is active for Week 5 against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: It was reported earlier on Sunday that Kittle was dealing with an illness, but that he was still expecting to play. Kittle was not listed with the 49ers’ inactives when the team announced them 90 minutes before kickoff, meaning he is good to go and can be treated as a TE1 as usual.

items.name: Roman Wilson
items.headline: Roman Wilson has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 5 against the Colts with a dislocated finger.
items.analysis: Wilson had just one target in the first half. He pinned the reception to his hip, but the ball was ripped loose by a defender, which not only made the pass incomplete but also seemed to dislocate Wilson’s finger. With Michael Pittman Jr. also hurt, we should continue to see a lot of Germie Bernard in Week 5.

items.name: Mykel Williams
items.headline: Mykel Williams is active for Week 5 against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Williams entered the weekend as questionable after being limited in practice all week. Now, the Niners DT will officially be active for a pivotal NFC West showdown against the 3-1 Seahawks. While Williams is active, the Niners did declare DL James Thompson Jr., LB Tatum Bethune, DL Nick Bosa, OL Enrique Cruz Jr., QB Kurtis Rourke, FB Kyle Juszczyk, and S Marques Sigle inactive for Week 5.

items.name: Ben Bartch
items.headline: Lions declared OG Ben Bartch, CB Rock Ya-Sin, TE Jackson Meeks, S Bishop Fitzgerald, DL Mekhi Wingo and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein inactive for Week 5 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Slowed by a foot injury, Bartch, one of the Lions’ better backup offensive linemen, will be unavailable today. Fortunately, the Lions’ offensive line health is improving and stud C Cade Mays (wrist) could return in a week or two. The Lions will also be without Ya-Sin, one of two starting perimeter cornerbacks and S Brian Branch (Achilles) is not yet ready to resume playing. This should be a high-scoring game environment, though DL Tyleik Williams (foot) is active.l

items.name: Dallas Goedert
items.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 6-of-9 targets for 38 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Goedert returned to the lineup after missing three games with a knee injury. Already without Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith, Goedert was immediately thrust into a high-usage role. He led the team in targets and catches, though much of his looks were simply check-downs. Even if that’s his role going forward, Goedert should catch enough passes to sustain borderline TE1 numbers until DeVonta Smith returns. He gets a date with the Panthers in Week 6.

items.name: George Holani
items.headline: George Holani is active for Week 5 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Holani is good to go for Sunday’s game after entering the weekend as questionable. Holani rushed seven times for 18 scoreless yards last week and shouldn’t be relied on in any fantasy format this week. While Holani is active, the Seahawks declared QB Jalen Milroe, RB Robert Henry Jr., LB Chazz Surratt, WR Montorie Foster Jr., and TE Nick Kallerup inactive for Week 5.

items.name: Ben Skowronek
items.headline: Ben Skowronek has been ruled out for Week 5 against the Colts with a calf injury.
items.analysis: There hasn’t been a lot of word on what happened to Skowronek. He went into the blue medical tent in the second quarter to have his leg looked at and then headed into the locker room. When the Steelers returned the kickoff to start the second half, Skowronek, who is a key special teamer, was not on the field. He was ruled out shortly after. With Michael Pittman Jr. already out, the Steelers are getting a little thin with their wide receiver depth.

items.name: David Montgomery
items.headline: David Montgomery (groin) will not return to Houston’s Week 5 game against the Titans.
items.analysis: He finishes with five carries for 11 yards. Initially questionable to return in the second quarter, Montgomery was ruled out after halftime. This could open some major space for Woody Marks to have a strong role going forward. We’ll keep an eye out for updates after the game, but it doesn’t look good for Montgomery.

items.name: Makai Lemon
items.headline: Makai Lemon caught 5-of-7 targets for 43 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: The good news is that Lemon set new season highs in targets, catches, and yards. The bad news: All of that resulted in a measly 9.3 PPR points. Lemon will hopefully continue to earn more opportunities as the season progresses, but DeVonta Smith’s return could just as easily stall the rookie’s progress. Lemon will be a WR4/5 if Smith remains out for Week 6 against the Panthers.

items.name: Brian Thomas
items.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. failed to catch any of his three targets in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
items.analysis: This game started with Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr. getting ejected on the opening kickoff. He would go on to catch as many passes as his wide receiver doppelganger. BTJ nearly saved face with a late touchdown, but he failed to drag his back foot and stepped out of bounds for an incompletion. Josh Cameron, the team’s WR4, saw six targets. Thomas Jr. simply doesn’t have much of a role in this offense anymore. He will be the subject of trade speculation in the coming weeks. That seems to be his only path to meaningful fantasy production.

items.name: Dontayvion Wicks
items.headline: Dontayvion Wicks caught 5-of-8 targets for 63 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the
items.analysis: DeVonta Smith was out again this week, leaving the Eagles to spread his targets around to several role players. Wicks led the team’s wideouts in targets, but it was Dallas Goedert who paced the team. On the back of one long touchdown catch, Darius Cooper led the team in receiving yards. Wicks is good for the occasional big play but isn’t a consistent enough player to be a solid fantasy option. He will be a deep FLEX option for Week 6 versus the Panthers.

items.name: Will Campbell
items.headline: Patriots OT Will Campbell (knee) exited in Week 5 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Campbell had his leg rolled on in the second quarter and was down in obvious pain for a while before being helped off the field. Campbell was taken to the locker room for further evaluation and seems unlikely to return today. An extended absence for Campbell would be a tough blow for Drake Maye and the New England passing attack.

items.name: Dameon Pierce
items.headline: Dameon Pierce rushed 11 times for 14 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Pierce “added” two catches for -2 yards. He took over as the Eagles’ lead back after Will Shipley went down with a foot injury in the first half. Carson Steele did not see the field for a single offensive snap. Pierce would presumably in line for a workhorse role in Week 6 if Shipley and Saquon Barkley are both out, but his efficiency today speaks for itself. This isn’t an offense capable of opening running lanes, nor is Pierce a back who can make a lot out of a little. Pierce is a low-priority waiver wire add for Week 6.

items.name: David Montgomery
items.headline: David Montgomery (groin) is questionable to return to Houston’s Week 5 game against the Titans.
items.analysis: He had five carries for 11 yards before leaving in the middle of the second quarter. Woody Marks will handle lead back duties for the moment.

items.name: Darius Cooper
items.headline: Darius Cooper caught 2-of-3 passes for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Cooper has been a touchdown magnet this year, scoring three times on five catches before today’s explosion. He broke loose against the Jags in the second quarter with a 62-yard grab. Cooper beat his man deep and his adjustment to the throw, which was thrown back toward the center of the field, put him in open space with a full head of steam. He ran untouched into the end zone. Cooper’s absurd touchdown efficiency can’t be sustained, but he is developing into a meaningful deep threat for a struggling Philly passing attack. He will at least warrant some FLEX consideration if DeVonta Smith remains out for Week 6 against the Panthers.

items.name: TreVeyon Henderson
items.headline: TreVeyon Henderson exited the Patriots’ Week 5 game with an apparent lower leg injury.
items.analysis: Henderson ripped off a nice 11-yard rush and was tackled low out of bounds. He was slow to get up before being helped to the New England locker room for further evaluation. The oft-injured Henderson was seeing better-than-usual usage before his injury. Rhamondre Stevenson will function as the team’s workhorse back if Henderson once again misses time.

items.name: Trevor Lawrence
items.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 24-of-39 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Jaguars’ 19-17, Week 5 win over the Eagles.
items.analysis: Lawrence gave fantasy managers what they needed with a solid box score, but he was not the reason the Jags won this game. Lawrence struggled under pressure, throwing one ugly interception while putting the ball on the ground twice via sack-fumbles. Both were recovered by the Jags. The offense was also a catastrophe in the red zone, though a series of penalties and bizarre play calls are largely to blame there. Down by one with eight seconds left, it looked like the team’s struggles on offense would be too much to overcome. Instead, Ameer Abdullah returned a kickoff 53 yards to set up a walkoff field goal from Cam Little. If the Jags can clean things up after an uncharacteristically sloppy game, Lawrence will remain a mid-range QB1 for Week 6 versus the Texans.

items.name: Parker Washington
items.headline: Parker Washington caught 6-of-9 targets for 124 yards and two touchdowns in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
items.analysis: Coming off a pair of quiet weeks, Washington paid off for fantasy managers early with a 51-yard score in the first quarter. It was somehow nowhere close to his best play of the day. Washington scored his second touchdown on a falling, one-handed grab in the end zone from 27 yards out near the end of the game. The grab was reminiscent of Odell Beckham’s famous touchdown catch. Washington remains the most talented and most involved receiver on the Jags. He will be a high-end WR2 versus the Texans next week.

items.name: KC Concepcion
items.headline: KC Concepcion suffered a concussion in the first quarter of the Browns’ Week 5 game against the Jets and will not return.
items.analysis: Making a spinning first quarter grab, Concepcion took a high hit from Minkah Fitzpatrick, who was flagged for a personal foul. It was the kind of hit the NFL is trying to legislate out of the game, but it wasn’t necessarily dirty. It was extremely unfortunate, as Concepcion did appear to be briefly out cold. He thankfully made his way to his feet and to the locker room unassisted, but he was ruled out before even undergoing a formal evaluation. He will now be highly questionable for Week 6 against the Ravens. Concepcion’s loss will mean more routes for beleaguered Jerry Jeudy.

items.name: T.J. Hockenson
items.headline: T.J. Hockenson suffered a concussion in Week 5 against the Saints and will not return.
items.analysis: Hockenson was slammed into the ground on his first catch of the day. He got up slowly and was immediately checked out by the medical staff. Hockenson was eventually evaluated for a concussion and ruled out. With a bye week on deck for Week 6, Hockenson should be able to return for the team’s next game.

items.name: Tyler Steen
items.headline: Tyler Steen (shoulder) returned to the Eagles’ Week 5 game against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Steen left with the shoulder issue earlier in the game and was listed as questionable to return. Fred Johnson took his spot at right guard for a few drives. While the Eagles are still down several key names due to injury, Steen is no longer among them.

items.name: Will Shipley
items.headline: Will Shipley (foot) will not return to the Eagles’ Week 5 game against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Shipley suffered the foot injury in the second quarter and was initially listed as questionable to return. He will now miss the remainder of the contest. Dameon Pierce is the only other running back on the roster with a touch today. Carson Steele is also active.

items.name: Michael Carter
items.headline: Michael Carter suffered an abdominal injury in Week 5 against the Jaguars and will not return.
items.analysis: Right guard Tyler Steen is questionable to return with a shoulder injury. Philly came into this game without several key players because of injuries. Now they will be without even more players on both sides of the ball.

items.name: Anton Harrison
items.headline: Anton Harrison was carted off the field with an apparent leg injury in the Jaguars’ Week 5 game against the Eagles.
items.analysis: Harrison went down with a non-contact injury in the third quarter. He rode the cart to the locker room. His day is likely over. Walker Little will take his spot at left tackle.

items.name: Rico Dowdle
items.headline: Steelers declared RB Rico Dowdle, QB Will Howard, QB Drew Allar, CB Jamel Dean, RB Eli Heidenreich, CB Terell Smith, and DT Kevin Jobity Jr. inactive for Week 5 against the Colts.
items.analysis: It was reported earlier in the day that Dowdle was unlikely to suit up due to his ongoing foot injury, so this doesn’t come as a major surprise. We could be looking at a big game for Jaylen Warren against an underperforming Colts defense. With Keenan Allen back for the Colts, the injury to Jamel Dean is a bit of a blow to this Pittsburgh secondary.

items.name: Ashton Jeanty
items.headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle, foot) is active for Week 5 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Jeanty will play through his foot and ankle injuries against New England. It wouldn’t be surprising if he cedes some backfield work to a healthy and much more explosive Mike Washington, however. Jeanty should be considered a top-24 option this week while Washington is a desperation flex. Raiders declared WR Jalen Nailor, QB Aidan O’Connell, S Tristin McCollum, RB Roman Hemby, S Dalton Johnson, OL Trey Zuhn, and DT JJ Pegues inactive against the Patriots.

items.name: Devin Singletary
items.headline: Giants declared S Jason Pinnock, RB Devin Singletary, CB Nikko Reed, DT Bobby Jamison-Travis, OT J.C. Davis, and QB Jake Haener inactive for Week 5 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Singletary is once again a healthy scratch as the Giants will roll with Cam Skattebo, Najee Harris, and Tyrone Tracy as their top three backs. J.J. McCarthy will serve as the QB2 behind Jameis Winston in what figures to be a messy game in the elements in Washington this afternoon.

items.name: Marlin Klein
items.headline: Texans declared TE Marlin Klein, CB Collin Wright, DE Chris Braswell, LB Aiden Fisher, OG Febechi Nwaiwu and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Houston’s Week 5 game against the Titans.
items.analysis: The Texans had five questionable players, including three offensive linemen with illnesses. All three of those linemen will play, and Kayden McDonald and M.J. Stewart were activated off injured reserve to make their season debuts as well as the Texans try to avoid an 0-5 start.

items.name: Keenan Allen
items.headline: Keenan Allen (groin) is active for Week 5 against the Steelers
items.analysis: Allen got in a full practice on Friday, so he seemed to be trending towards being active, but now we know for sure. With Jamel Dean out this week and Joey Porter Jr. now in Dallas, the Colts’ passing game gets a slight bump, which is good news for Daniel Jones, who really needs to get back on track. The Colts inactives are: LB Jaylon Carlies, WR Ashton Dulin, QB Riley Leonard, WR Darius Slayton, and G Dalton Tucker.

items.name: Alvin Kamara
items.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) is active for Week 5 against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Kamara will split work with Kendre Miller and C.J. Donaldson. He projects to lead the group in carries and targets, giving him some RB3 potential. Inactive for the Saints are EDGE Anfernee Jennings, S Mike Reid, LB Kaden Elliss, OL Jeremiah Wright, DL Vernon Broughton, and DL Nathan Shepherd.

items.name: Jaylen Wright
items.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) is active for Week 5.
items.analysis: Wright had back-to-back limited practices to close out the week after seemingly reaggravating a foot injury. He is active against the Bengals and will backup Ollie Gordon for Week 5. The Dolphins declared WR Caleb Douglas (ankle), RB Kaytron Allen, CB Reese Taylor, EDGE Rob Beal Jr., G DJ Campbell, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, and TE Justin Joly inactive for Week 5 against the Bengals.

items.name: Jaylen Wright
items.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) is active for Week 5 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Wright had back-to-back limited practices to close out the week after seemingly reaggravating a foot injury. He is active against the Bengals and will backup Ollie Gordon for Week 5. The Dolphins declared WR Caleb Douglas (ankle), RB Kaytron Allen, CB Reese Taylor, EDGE Rob Beal Jr., G DJ Campbell, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, and TE Justin Joly inactive for Week 5 against the Bengals.

items.name: Will McDonald
items.headline: Jets EDGE Will McDonald (calf) is active for New York’s Week 5 game against the Browns.
items.analysis: He popped up on the Friday injury report with a calf, but will try to play through it. Inactive for the Jets are RB Breece Hall (quad), LB Kiko Mauigoa (quad), OL Dylan Parham (knee), WR Adonai Mitchell (finger), EDGE Nate Lynn and CB Nahshon Wright. The four with injury statuses were ruled out on Friday, the other two are healthy scratches.

items.name: Javon Hargrave
items.headline: Packers NT Javon Hargrave (toe) is active for Week 5 against the Bears.
items.analysis: It’s a mercifully quiet injury day for the Packers in this grudge match. Inactive for the Pack are OL Jacob Monk, OG Aaron Banks, OL Donovan Jennings and DT Anthony Campbell.

items.name: Jordan Addison
items.headline: Vikings declared Jordan Addison (hamstring) inactive for Week 5 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Addison seemingly gave it a go this morning but wasn’t quite ready to play. The Vikings get a Week 6 bye, so Addison should be ready to go when they return to face the Colts in two weeks. Also inactive for the Vikings are OT Christian Darrisaw, S Jakobe Thomas, WR Odell Beckham, CB Chuck Demmings, DT Elijah Williams, and QB Max Brosmer.

items.name: Justin Jefferson
items.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is active for Week 5 against the Saints.
