items.analysis: Jordan Addison is out. Jefferson would normally see plenty of targets anyway, but the absence of Addison all but guarantees that he will see one of the highest target shares in the league. Jefferson remains a top-end WR1 versus the Saints.

items.name: Carnell Tate
items.headline: Carnell Tate (back) is active for Tennessee’s Week 5 game against the Texans.
items.analysis: The Titans had named him questionable despite Robert Saleh saying he’d play on Friday, so this outcome was no surprise. Inactive for the Titans are: RB Nick Singleton, RB Michael Carter, S Amani Hooker (concussion), CB Jaylon Jones, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE David Martin-Robinson (hamstring) and DT Jackie Marshall.

items.name: Christian Gonzalez
items.headline: Patriots declared CB Christian Gonzalez, QB Behren Morton, OL Dametrious Crownover, CB Carlton Davis III, CB Karon Prunty, and CB Channing Cananda inactive for Week 5 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: New England’s injury-ravaged secondary could have a tough time slowing down the highly efficient Vegas passing offense today. The absence of Gonzalez and Davis should be a boon for both Tre Tucker and Brock Bowers. Kirk Cousins, who has 11 touchdowns to four interceptions this season, is a solid streaming option against the Patriots.

items.name: Terry McLaurin
items.headline: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) is active for Week 5 against the Giants.
items.analysis: While it’s good news that McLaurin is active, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported earlier that he is “likely not a full go” for Sunday’s game. To make matters worse, the Commanders and Giants are expected to battle it out in soggy conditions all afternoon, which could further limit McLaurin’s upside in this one. Fantasy managers hoping to play him need to temper expectations given his status and the game’s conditions, and shouldn’t consider McLaurin as anything more than a mid-to-low-end WR3. The Commanders announced WR Stefon Diggs (hamstring), QB Marcus Mariota (knee), S Tyler Owens (hamstring), S Nick Cross (illness), S Percy Butler (hamstring), OG Tanoa Togiai, and DE Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle) are inactive for Week 5.

items.name: Tee Higgins
items.headline: Bengals WR Tee Higgins is active for Week 5 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Higgins suffered an adductor injury in Week 4 against the Jaguars and was a full practice participant Friday after DNPs the two days before. Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) both declared active. Though NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports he will play mostly “meaningful plays”, Higgins is in the WR2 ranks while Chase is back in the WR1 ranks this week. The Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, TE Jack Endries, WR Colbie Young, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 5 against the Dolphins.

items.name: Caleb Williams
items.headline: Bears declared QB Caleb Williams, RB Kyle Monangai, OT Ozzy Trapilo, LB Keyshaun Elliott, DT Jayden Loving and EDGE Jamree Kromah inactive for Week 5 against the Packers.
items.analysis: Why the Bears went through the dog and pony show of labeling Williams as “questionable” when everybody knew he would not be playing, nobody knows. Either way, Williams appears to have a strong chance of returning for Week 6 against the Falcons. Expect another run-heavy game plan, even without Monangai, in what should be the final game of the Tyson Bagent experience for the time being.

items.name: Caleb Williams
items.headline: Bears declared QB Caleb Williams, RB Kyle Monangai, OT Ozzy Trapilo, LB Keyshaun Elliott and EDGE Jamree Kromah inactive for Week 5 against the Packers.

items.name: Jalyx Hunt
items.headline: Jalyx Hunt is undergoing testing on his left leg after suffering an injury in the second quarter.
items.analysis: Hunt went down on the final play of the first half. The team initially brought out the cart for him, but he managed to limp off the field with the help of the medical staff. He doesn’t have an official injury status right now, but we’ll assume his day is over.

items.name: Tylan Wallace
items.headline: Browns declared WR Tylan Wallace (knee), QB Taylen Green (third qb), TE Carsen Ryan (calf), DT Mike Hall Jr. (ankle), G Parker Brailsford, G Teven Jenkins (back) and DT Mason Graham (knee) inactive for Cleveland’s Week 5 game against the Jets.
items.analysis: Congrats to Parker Brailsford on being the only healthy scratch. No surprises here; everyone else but Green was ruled out on Friday.

items.name: Will Shipley
items.headline: Will Shipley (foot) is questionable to return in Week 5 against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Shipley got stuffed on a carry in the second quarter and was checked out by trainers after the play. He went to the locker room after a brief trip to the blue medical tent. Dameon Pierce will be the next man up if Shipley’s day is over. Carson Steele is the only other back on the roster.

items.name: Tee Higgins
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Tee Higgins (groin/neck) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) will also play. Higgins is likely suiting up at less than full strength, but fantasy managers have to keep him in their lineups versus a Miami defense that is giving up explosive passing plays at the second-highest rate in the league this year. He will be a boom/bust WR2 for Week 5.

items.name: Ja'Marr Chase
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) will play in Week 5 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Chase cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend. With Tee Higgins (neck/groin) also expected to play, it’s business as usual for the Bengals this week. Higgins could be on a pitch count, while Chase won’t have any restrictions. Facing a pitiful Miami defense, Chase is in the running for WR1 overall this week.

items.name: Justin Jefferson
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeff Darlington reports Justin Jefferson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Jordan Addison, on the other hand, is not expected to suit up because of a hamstring issue. Even at less than full strength, Jefferson will dominate the targets for Minnesota, especially with Addison on ice. Barring a setback in warmups, Jefferson remains a top-half WR1 play for Week 5.

items.name: Jordan Addison
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeff Darlington reports Jordan Addison (hamstring) “isn’t likely to be active” for Week 5 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Addison got in two limited practices this week before being listed as questionable. He was considered a game-time decision as of this morning, but it sounds like the team is going to hold him out for at least one week. Justin Jefferson, on the other hand, is expected to suit up. The offense will run through him, per usual.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lamar Jackson (ankle) has a “real chance” to return in Week 6 against the Browns.
items.analysis: Jackson was ruled out for Week 5 on Friday after failing to practice once this week. Rapoport added that Jackson has been “working like crazy” to get back on the field next week. Per Rapoport, that is Jackson’s goal. Tyler Huntley will start for as long as Jackson remains sidelined.

items.name: Terry McLaurin
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Terry McLaurin is a “true game-time decision” for Week 5 against the Giants.
items.analysis: McLaurin is listed as questionable for Week 5 after getting in a single limited practice on Friday. Even if he does play, McLaurin will likely be on a pitch count. Stefon Diggs has already been ruled out with a hamstring issue of his own. Rookie Antonio Williams will be asked to step up whether or not McLaurin is active.

items.name: Keenan Allen
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Keenan Allen (groin) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Allen missed Week 4 with the groin issue but returned to practice this week and even managed a full session on Friday. The team still listed him as questionable, though he appeared to be on the right side of that designation heading into the weekend. Allen will be a low-ceiling WR4 for his date with the Steelers.

items.name: Jake Matthews
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jake Matthews (groin) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: The Falcons’ left tackle has started 199 consecutive games in his career. His streak appeared to be in jeopardy early in the week, but the iron-man tackle practiced in full on Friday, putting him on the right side of questionable for today’s game. He should be good to go for Week 5.

items.name: Christian Barmore
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Christian Barmore (shoulder) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Barmore missed Week 4 with the shoulder injury but appears to be good to go for today’s matchup with Las Vegas. He was listed as questionable after practicing in full on Friday. Baremore has one sack on six pressures this season.

items.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Stevenson already told reporters on Friday that he was “ready to go”, so this news item doesn’t come as much of a surprise. Stevenson will continue to operate as the Pats’ top option in high-leverage situations, though he could cede more work between the 20s to TreVeyon Henderson. Both backs are stuck as low-ceiling RB3 options this week.

items.name: Marlon Humphrey
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Humphrey logged one limited practice this week before being listed as questionable for Week 5. He’s one of several key defenders dealing with an injury heading into Sunday Night Football. EDGE Trey Hendrickson has already been ruled out, while S Kyle Hamilton is questionable with a groin injury. Even with some missing names, this defense still looks like a true test for Michael Penix.

items.name: Jayden Daniels
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports, “There are doctors around the NFL who believe it’s a matter of when, not if, Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels hurts his left elbow again.”
items.analysis: Schefter immediately added the caveat that the “overwhelming opinion” among doctors was that playing with a brace was a viable option. Daniels reportedly contemplated surgery after dislocating his elbow for the second time in less than a year. He opted against it and missed two games. Daniels is now set to return for Week 5 against the Giants. The Commanders could scale back his rushing for the time being, but OC David Blough already dismissed the idea that the playbook would be limited because of Daniels’ elbow injury.

items.name: Jayden Daniels
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports “there are doctors around the NFL who believe it’s a matter of when, not if, Jayden Daniels hurts his left elbow again.”
items.analysis: Schefter immediately added the caveat that the “overwhelming opinion” among doctors was that playing with a brace was a viable option. Daniels reportedly contemplated surgery after dislocating his elbow for the second time in less than a year. He opted against it and missed two games. Daniels is now set to return for Week 5 against the Giants. The Commanders could scale back his rushing for the time being, but OC David Blough already dismissed the idea that the playbook would be limited because of Daniels’ elbow injury.

items.name: Alvin Kamara
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Alvin Kamara (back) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Kamara is listed as questionable with a back injury. He logged two limited practices this week. In the absence of Travis Etienne, Kamara has become the leader of a three-back committee. He only saw seven carries last week but did manage five catches on seven targets. Kamara is a PPR RB3 for his date with the Vikings.

items.name: Justin Jefferson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Justin Jefferson will work out pregame to determine his status for Week 5 against the Saints.
items.analysis: The same is true of Jordan Addison. Both Minnesota wideouts are currently listed as questionable for Week 5. Jefferson is from Louisiana and has already told reporters he plans to play in the homecoming game. We expect him to suit up, but fantasy managers should have a backup plan for him and Addison to be safe.

items.name: Ashton Jeanty
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ashton Jeanty (foot/ankle) is “hopeful” to play in Week 5 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Per Rapoport, Jeanty had a flare-up of plantar fasciitis last week to go along with his ankle injury. He added that Jeanty will work out before today’s game to see how he’s feeling. If he can’t go, Mike Washington Jr. would see the bulk of the backfield touches. Washington has been an explosive complement to Jeanty this year, averaging five yards per carry on 24 attempts. He would jump to the top of the RB2 ranks if Jeanty can’t go.

items.name: Caleb Williams
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Caleb Williams is “pushing to play” in Week 6 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Williams is technically listed as questionable for Week 5 versus the Packers, but Tyson Bagent is fully expected to make the start. Still, Williams’ return to practice on Friday was a pleasant surprise for Bears fans. If all goes well in practice next week, he could return after missing just three games, which was on the short end of his projected timeline.

items.name: Cam Skattebo
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Cam Skattebo’s shoulder injury is “not a concern.”
items.analysis: Skattebo was cleared from the injury report on Friday, so he was never going to miss this game. The good news is that the Giants don’t have any plans to limit his workload. Playing in a rain-soaked matchup with the NFC East rival Commanders, Skattebo is expected to see “an extremely heavy workload”, according to Garafolo.

items.name: Rico Dowdle
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Rico Dowdle (foot) is unlikely to play in Week 5 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Dowdle got in three limited practices this week before being listed as questionable. The team doesn’t want to rush him back, only for him to aggravate the foot issue, so he’ll miss today’s game before likely returning in Week 6. Jaylen Warren will get one more week of workhorse duties, putting him in the RB1 mix once more.

items.name: Zay Flowers
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Zay Flowers (foot) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Flowers was limited in practice throughout the week but never appeared at risk of missing Sunday night’s game. The bigger issue for him will be the absence of Lamar Jackson. Flowers has been the most efficient receiver in the league on a per-route basis this year. That will come back to Earth sans Jackson, but he remains on the WR1/2 border, even with Tyler Huntley under center.

items.name: Jonathan Greenard
items.headline: Eagles declared EDGE Jonathan Greenard, WR Hollywood Brown, WR DeVonta Smith, RB Saquon Barkley, S Marcus Epps, and C Crew Kendall inactive for Week 5 against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Greenard was the only Eagle with a questionable tag headed into the weekend. The rest of their important players had already been ruled out. Greenard didn’t practice at all this week because of an ankle injury and could miss more time.

items.name: Eric Murray
items.headline: Jaguars declared S Eric Murray, WR CJ Williams, CB Alijah Huzzie, CB Jaylon Jones, OL Daniel Faalele, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis inactive for Week 5 against the Eagles.
items.analysis: Murray was listed as doubtful on Friday because of a concussion. He returned to practice but couldn’t clear concussion protocol in time. Murray has started all four games this year, though we don’t think his absence will spark a revival of the Eagles’ passing attack.

items.name: Ladd McConkey
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Ladd McConkey (foot) is not expected to play in Week 5 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: McConkey did not practice at all this week but was still given a questionable tag on Friday. He was always a long-shot to play after aggravating his foot injury in Week 4. With Quentin Johnston out this week as well, Tre’ Harris will be Justin Herbert’s No. 1 receiver. That puts him in the WR3 mix despite the Chargers’ dismal offensive performance through four weeks.

items.name: Chris Brooks
items.headline: Packers placed RB Chris Brooks (ankle) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: Brooks had been the most consistent contributor to a Green Bay backfield working to find their way in the absence of Josh Jacobs. The team appears likely to utilize journeyman Pierre Strong as the preferred passing down specialist, likely keeping the backfield in a maddening timeshare without Brooks. None are worthy of legitimate fantasy interest.

items.name: Michael Pittman
items.headline: Steelers placed WR Michael Pittman (foot) on injured reserve.
items.analysis: Pittman aggravated the foot injury that cost him Week 2 last week and will now miss four games, at minimum, while on injured reserve. Roman Wilson appears to be the primary beneficiary of Pittman’s absence and has seen six targets in each game this season while mostly playing a situational role. Wilson is a priority waiver addition over rookie Germie Bernard.

items.name: DJ Moore
items.headline: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable for Week 5 against the Rams.
items.analysis: Moore failed to practice until Saturday after aggravating a shoulder injury in Week 4, returning to the field in a limited capacity while wearing a red non-contact jersey. That was apparently enough to keep the door open for an appearance on Monday Night Football against the Rams, although he certainly appears to be on the wrong side of the questionable tag. Fantasy managers would be wise to seek alternate options considering the timing of the game.

items.name: Joshua Palmer
items.headline: Bills ruled out WR Joshua Palmer (shoulder) for Week 5 against the Rams.
items.analysis: Palmer apparently injured his shoulder in practice on Friday before being absent Saturday, ultimately ruled out for Week 5 against the Rams on Monday Night Football. Fellow wide receiver DJ Moore is listed as questionable after failing to practice until a limited session Saturday, also with a shoulder injury, potentially leaving Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir atop the depth chart at the position.

items.name: Joshua Palmer
items.headline: Bills WR Joshua Palmer (shoulder) did not practice Saturday.
items.analysis: Palmer was added to the injury report Friday with a shoulder injury, likely indicating that was where he suffered the injury. This is bigger news when taken in the context of the potential absence of DJ Moore on Monday Night Football against the Rams after Moore aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 4. Expect Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman to function as the top two receivers, should both miss Week 5.

items.name: DJ Moore
items.headline: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) practiced with a non-contact jersey Saturday.
items.analysis: This is the first time Moore has returned to the practice field after aggravating a shoulder injury in Week 4. Still no word on his game-day injury status, which will come later in the afternoon, but it a small step in the right direction for the veteran receiver. Fantasy managers likely want to continue the search for alternatives with the Bills playing on Monday Night Football.

items.name: Darius Slayton
items.headline: Colts WR Darius Slayton (knee) was ruled out for Week 5 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Slayton was listed as questionable after injuring his knee during practice on Friday. He’s since been ruled out, postponing his Colts debut for another week. Nick Westbrook-Ikene has been elevated from the Colts’ practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders beat writer Ben Standig reports RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) isn’t expected to play in Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has dealt with a groin injury all season despite playing in the Commanders’ first five games. He missed multiple practices this week and will now get two weeks off with missing the game against the 49ers ahead of Washington’s bye week. For now, expect Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler to handle the majority of the backfield touches for the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has played through multiple injuries this year. We still think he has a chance to face the 49ers in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game. Rachaad White (shoulder) sported a red non-contact jersey for the first time this week, and was downgraded to limited today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Ekeler and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) are both ailing, though the latter player sat out entirely. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Jeremy McNichols (quad) are both practicing in full. Croskey-Merritt is the only fantasy-relevant Commanders running back at this time, assuming he is good to go on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has played through soft tissue injuries for weeks now. He played through a groin injury last week, and the same issue is still bothering him today. Regardless, Croskey-Merritt still has a chance to play this week and today’s absence could actually benefit the starting running back. The Commanders face the 49ers on Monday night, so Croskey-Merritt has extra time to rest and rehab. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 11 times for 82 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie with the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt’s 82 rushing yards set a new season high. Nearly half of his yards came in the first quarter when “Bill” broke free for a 33-yard touchdown to give the Commanders a 7-0 lead on their opening drive. On the final play of the third quarter, Croskey-Merritt would rip off a 22-yard run on a drive that eventually ended on a 26-yard touchdown run by Jayden Daniels. JCM continues to be the unquestioned leader in Washington’s backfield, but he remains a touchdown-dependent fantasy option due to his lack of receiving upside. He’ll be a boom-or-bust RB2 in next week’s game against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is not on the final injury report for Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt logged two limited sessions to begin the week before upgrading to full on Friday. He should be good to go for this normal weekly role. Unfortunately, his workloads have varied, so he is more of an upside FLEX starter than he is an RB2. That said, Jayden Daniels (elbow) is returning this week, which should give the offense an efficiency boost.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: He remains on track to play, but the workload he’ll get remains more uncertain after the Commanders re-divvied carries in England last Sunday. Croskey-Merritt would make for a shaky FLEX play in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: A limited session to start the week is usually a non-issue, but JCM’s role was already suspect before getting banged up. He ran nine times in Week 4. Austin Ekeler, Kaytron Allen, and Craig Reynolds all combined for nine attempts. Rachaad White is also back at practice, giving the team another option beyond Bill. With health and workload concerns, JCM is barely an RB3 headed into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed nine times for 15 yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts, adding two catches for 35 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Bill was surprisingly involved through the air, seeing four targets, one of which he took down the sideline for a 35-yard gain early in the match. On the other hand, three different Commanders backup running backs touched the ball today. Austin Ekeler led the way with four carries. Kaytron Allen and Craig Reynolds combined for another five attempts. The Commanders have had commitment issues with Croskey-Merritt dating back to his rookie season and nothing has changed this year. He will be stuck in the back of the RB3 ranks for Week 5 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) will not play in Washington’s Week 4 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: He didn’t practice at any point this week after suffering a shoulder injury in Week 3. He has to be considered questionable for Week 5 at this point. ‘Bill’ Croskey-Merritt figures to shoulder the majority of the workload for the Commanders this week and is a reasonable FLEX play against the Colts. Freshly-signed Austin Ekeler figures to handle third-down work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Chargers have rejected trade calls and aren’t planning a fire sale.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.analysis: According to Pelissero, teams have called Chargers GM Joe Hortiz, but he’s not interested in potential trade offers despite Los Angeles’ 0-5 record. The Chargers have one game left before their bye week and if they lose to the 4-0 Chiefs, falling to 0-6, this could all change. For now, the Chargers GM doesn’t want to deal, but trade calls on veteran players aren’t going to stop without a massive turnaround. Pelissero mentions Khalil Mack, Bud Dupree, Daiyan Henley, Donte Jackson, Denzel Perryman, Dalvin Tomlinson, and Tuli Tuipulotu as potential trade candidates in the final year of their contracts with the Chargers. He adds that he wouldn’t be surprised if teams that need running back or receiver help call about Keaton Mitchell, Kimani Vidal, and Quentin Johnston.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Chargers are targeting Ravens director of player personnel Joe Hortiz as their new GM.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.analysis: Hortiz will pair with Jim Harbaugh, the brother of long-time Ravens head coach John Harbaugh, in Los Angeles, as the two will look to correct course for a team that already has a franchise quarterback in place. Hortiz has served as the Ravens’ director of player personnel since 2019 and comes from one of the best front offices the sport has to offer. With their head coach and GM now in place, the Chargers will now look to round out their staff in the coming weeks as they prepare for free agency and the draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Chargers will conduct a second interview with Ravens Director of Player Personnel Joe Hortiz for general manager.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.analysis: Fresh off of hiring Jim Harbaugh for head coach, the Chargers are now looking to lock in a general manager. After interviewing Giants assistant general manager Brandon Brown, the Chargers will interview Joe Hortiz for a second time. Hortiz has been the Ravens’ director of player personnel since 2019, receiving GM interest over the last couple of offseasons. He has already interviewed with the Chargers virtually and will have an in-person interview with the team coming up. Hortiz has experience working with a Harbaugh in Baltimore as the Chargers are looking to build with their new head coach.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Cardinals requested permission to interview Ravens director of player personnel Joe Hortiz for their general manager vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.analysis: Hortiz interviewed with the Steelers and Giants last offseason as part of their searches for a new general manager. The Ravens have weathered Lamar Jackson injuries each of the last two seasons to win 10 and eight games, respectively. Arizona has cast a wide net during their general manager interview process.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.headline: The Steelers interviewed Ravens director of player personnel Joe Hortiz for their general manager vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.analysis: The team also announced it talked to 49ers director of pro personnel Ran Carthon and Eagles vice president of player personnel Andy Weidl. The Steelers continue to cast a wide net as they hunt for Kevin Colbert’s replacement. Somewhat surprisingly, it is appearing that Colbert’s heir will likely come from outside the organization.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.headline: Giants interviewed Ravens director of player personnel Joe Hortiz for their general manager job.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.analysis: Hortiz has spent the last 19 seasons with the Ravens, working as the top executive to GM Eric DeCosta. Baltimore promoted him to director of player personnel in 2019 after years of running the college scouting department. The Giants plan to hire a general manager before they look for their next head coach.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.headline: The New York Daily News’ Pat Leonard reports Ravens director of player personnel Joe Hortiz is in consideration for the Giants’ general manager opening.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-hortiz.analysis: With Dave Gettleman gone – he technically “retired” – the Giants are on the hunt for a new decision-maker, and Giants owner John Mara has already stated that they will first hire a new general manager before they look for their new head coach. The Ravens are well-known as one of the sharpest organizations in the NFL, so it makes sense that teams in search of new brass would look to poach someone from their organization. Hortiz has spent 19 seasons with the Ravens, and he has been in charge of college scouting for the past seven years. He manages their draft day evaluation and decision-making process as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Packers EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) still isn’t practicing.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: The Packers play the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football on NBC and Peacock in Week 6, but Parsons still isn’t practicing. According to Pelissero, it’s unlikely the 27-year-old defensive end plays before Green Bay’s matchup with the Patriots in Week 9 at the earliest. The Packers’ defense has certainly struggled without Parsons, but they have enough offensive firepower to win shootouts, which only adds to the fantasy floor for Jordan Love and Green Bay’s skill players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) isn’t expected to practice next week and could return in November, reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is coming back from tearing his ACL late last season. The 27-year-old defensive end didn’t practice this week and isn’t expected to practice next week, according to Pelissero. Parsons hasn’t had any setbacks in his rehab, but still isn’t ready for the Packers to open the 21-day window for him to practice before he’s activated. Pelissero points out that it could be November before Parsons is ready for game action. Green Bay is 1-2 this year and 1-8 without Parsons in the lineup over the last two years (including playoffs).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers HC Matt LaFleur said Micah Parsons (knee) will not practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is nearing a return, but the star pass-rusher isn’t ready to get on the field just yet. LaFleur did say that Parsons has not suffered any setbacks in his recovery, while adding that this is “just part of the process.” Parsons’ return window can be opened at any time, which would then give the Packers a 21-day window to ramp him up before activating him from IR.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers placed Micah Parsons (knee) on the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: This move was expected. Parsons himself said a few weeks ago that a Week 6 return was his “most optimistic” timeline. A spot on the reserve PUP list means Parsons must miss at least the first four months of the season. He is still recovering from the torn ACL he suffered in Week 15 of the 2025 season. Parsons should still be a force on the defensive front when he’s back, but that won’t happen until at least October.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers EDGE Micah Parsons said Week 6 is his “most optimistic” return date as of right now.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Interestingly, Week 6 is when the Packers play host to the Cowboys, Parsons’ former team. The star pass-rusher did note that he could also return later and that there is always the possibility of setbacks, but it sounds like the earliest we should expect to see him is Week 6. Parsons opened camp on the PUP list, which didn’t come as a surprise given the timing of his injury last season. It’s been widely believed that Parsons would miss the first few games of the season. If he were to open the year on the PUP list, he would be forced to sit out at least the first four games of the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers placed EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) on the active/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is unlikely to return before Week 4, the question ahead of us appears to be if it’ll be Week 4 or Week 5. If it’s Week 5, Parsons can be stored on the reserve/PUP list ahead of the season. This timeline has been a consistent drum beat coming out of the Packers since March, so this placement comes as no surprise.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman considers it unlikely Micah Parsons (knee) returns before Week 4.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: The Packers are famously conservative when it comes to injury recoveries, and Schneidman reports they have a hard and fast rule of “nine months without any football activity for players rehabbing major injuries.” We still wouldn’t be stunned if Parsons is a player who ends up breaking that supposed “rule,” but it would not be the first time fans were frustrated by the slow pace of a Packers rehabilitation. For his part, Parsons reported to training camp with a sunny social media post. If he is indeed going to miss regular season time, the first month feels like a good over/under.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers EDGE Micah Parsons confirmed that he is likely to start the 2026 season on the Physically Unable to Perform List.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: “The goal for me is to complete the season,” Parsons said Wednesday. “The goal has always been playoffs.” Parsons added that the team has a strict nine-month policy for ACL rehab for players with more than one tear and that he had an associated meniscus procedure in December. The updated timeline places Parsons back to full football activities some time in September, likely looking at October before he returns to the field for the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Speaking on ESPN’s Get Up, Adam Schefter said Micah Parsons (knee) is “a candidate to be placed on the PUP list” to start the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: There’s still plenty of time for Parsons to rehab to be ready in time for Week 1, but Schefter said “the feeling within the organization has been that Parsons would miss the early part of the season” with a chance to still return fairly early on. Parsons suffered a torn ACL in Week 15 of last season, which makes being ready in time for the 2026 season a tall task. The star pass rusher totaled 12.5 sacks in the 14 games he appeared in last season and was still named a First-team All-Pro in his first season with the Pack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst said he expects EDGE Micah Parsons and TE Tucker Kraft back “early in the season.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: “They’re doing great,” Gutekunst said on an interview on SiriusXM NFL Radio. “Tuck’s been in here every day, and he’s obviously a little bit ahead of schedule, just because his injury happened earlier than Micah’s did. But Micah’s such a - he’s a little bit of a freak. So I think some of that has taken over, and he’s doing really well, as well.” He continued, “So, certainly expect both of those guys back early in the season. And they’ll be a big part of what we’re doing moving forward.” Both players are attempting to return from torn ACLs, with Kraft’s injury occurring in November and Parsons’ occurring in December of last season. It certainly sounds like both players could avoid the Physically Unable to Perform list this summer, which would give each player a good chance to make good on their general manager’s words and return early in the 2026 regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) is still a few weeks away from a return to game action.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: No surprise here. Pierce shed his cast earlier this week, but there was also a report from the Athletic’s James Boyd that he “didn’t get the sense” Pierce was close to a return. Pelissero reports that Pierce isn’t expected to return to practice next week when he’s eligible. It’s difficult to justify holding Pierce in leagues without IR spots given the circumstances.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd reports Alec Pierce (heel) is no longer wearing a cast but is not close to a return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Boyd said he “didn’t get the sense” that Pierce is close to a return. Pierce went on injured reserve with a heel injury after Week 2 and wore a cast on his left ankle/heel while rehabbing. It’s a sign of progress for Pierce, who will have his first chance to come back in the Colts’ Week 7 game against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts placed Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce will be sidelined for at least four weeks after suffering the injury in Week 2 against Kansas City. Pierce had seen 19 percent of the Colts’ targets and 53 percent of the team’s air yards in Week 1 against the Ravens, resuming his role as a strictly-downfield pass catcher. With Pierce out, Josh Downs should have every chance to operate as the Colts’ No. 1 wideout while Tyler Warren sees a bump in targets. Laquon Treadwell is likely to take over as the team’s lone deep threat. Treadwell can be picked up in 14-team fantasy formats ahead of the Colts’ Week 3 matchup with the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) will “attempt to rehab his injury rather than have surgery.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce will most certainly be out for numerous games after appearing to re-injure the heel that he had offseason surgery on in Week 2. Rapoport’s wording seems to indicate that additional surgery has not yet been ruled out, but Pierce will attempt to rehab the issue in the interim. It’s a disaster of a scenario for a team that extended Pierce while allowing Michael Pittman to walk in the offseason. Josh Downs appears most likely to become the focal point of the offense through the air in Pierce’s absence after amassing seven catches on nine targets in the team’s overtime loss to the Chiefs. When, or if, Pierce returns to the active roster in 2026 remains to be seen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (heel) aggravated the injury that required surgery in March and the Colts are “still gathering information.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: X-rays came back negative last night but Pierce couldn’t put weight on it last night and left on crutches with a boot on. The fact that it was an aggravation is not promising. It sounds like Pierce could be looking at an extended absence. If true, Josh Downs will get some WR3 hype ahead of Week 3’s date against the Texans. If you were wondering why Laquon Treadwell was on the field deep in the game on Sunday night, Pierce’s injury is the reason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Colts WR Alec Pierce’s (heel) X-rays were negative.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce evidently avoided suffering a fracture. He will undergo more testing tomorrow to determine the remaining specifics and the injury’s severity. Hopefully, the Colts’ field-stretching wide receiver is not sidelined for long, if at all. Pierce underwent surgery on his ankle/heel this offseason and spent almost the entire spring and summer rehabbing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) is questionable to return to Week 2 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce came up limping on a route on the final play of the first quarter and was escorted to the medical tent by the training staff. He appeared to be unable to put any weight on the injured leg. It’s obviously not what fantasy managers want to see after he missed most of the offseason program following surgery on the ankle and heel on the same leg in late March. He remained in the medical tent for about 10 minutes before being carted to the locker room. Pierce caught his lone target for 11 yards prior to departing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce’s Thursday absence appears to have been a rest day. The Colts reportedly plan to play Pierce more in Week 2 than they did in Week 1, when he played on 59 percent of the team’s snaps. He posted a 4/61 receiving line and can be viewed as a WR3/FLEX this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Alec Pierce (heel) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: It looks like it’s just a routine day off, but we’ll check back on Friday. The Indianapolis Star reported that Pierce told reporters before the practice that the plan is “to put him on the field more in Kansas City” in Week 2 after he played just 59 percent of the team’s snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: This could just be a rest day, though those typically happen on Wednesday. Pierce has been working his way back from his offseason heel/ankle surgery, and he reportedly had his wrist X-rayed after the Colts’ Week 1 game against the Ravens. Hopefully, the beat reporters turn up something useful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports there’s “optimism” Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield didn’t practice this week, but according to Buccaneers HC Todd Bowles he threw on Monday and was pushing to play before his “thumb swelled up on him.” It seems like Mayfield is trending in the right direction and that he could return against the Panthers in Week 7 if the swelling is no longer an issue. Jalon Daniels is starting for Tampa Bay again in Week 6 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that Baker Mayfield threw on “Monday as he was pushing hard to play and the thumb swelled up on him.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles gets another tick in the obfuscation column. On Wednesday, Bowles told reporters that Mayfield has not resumed throwing yet. Today, Palmer tells us that Mayfield “was pushing hard to play,” and, perhaps briefly, resumed throwing on Monday. Apparently, his thumb reacted poorly. Palmer adds that Mayfield is “getting better,” but that does not necessarily mean he will be able to play next week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) will not play in Tampa Bay’s Week 6 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: It’ll be the Jalon Daniels show again. Mayfield did not practice at any point this week. Todd Bowles tried to tell us that it was too early to tell earlier today; it wasn’t. We’ll need to see Mayfield on the practice field next week before we think he has a real shot to play against the Panthers in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said it’s “too early to tell” if Baker Mayfield (thumb) will be able to play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield has already been ruled out for Week 6’s game against the Steelers. After being a DNP in practice all week, Mayfield could still be another week away from returning. It was reported on Wednesday that he is still unable to grip/throw a football, so this will be a situation to keep an eye on when the Bucs begin prepping for next week’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield will be ruled out for Week 6 tomorrow. Having not thrown a football since his Week 3 thumb injury, he’s also unlikely to suit up for next week’s game against the Panthers. Jalon Daniels will draw at least one more start versus the Steelers this week. His rushing production will keep him in the QB2 ranks for Sunday’s game, but a lack of passing numbers makes him a weak fantasy option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Bucs coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (thumb) has not resumed throwing yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield did not practice today and is a safe bet to miss Week 6 as he continues to work his way back from the dislocated thumb he suffered in Week 3. The fact that he can’t even throw a football right now, let alone participate in practice, suggests Mayfield could be out beyond just Week 6. Jalon Daniels will start on Sunday versus the Steelers. Daniels has been held well under 200 passing yards in both of his starts, but he does at least have 78 rushing yards in those contests. His output as a runner will keep him in the QB2 mix for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield is unlikely to suit up this week against the Steelers, leaving Jalon Daniels to get another start for Tampa. Daniel last week in a win over Dallas completed 19-of-25 passes for 189 yards and one touchdown, rushing for 23 yards. Daniels ranked tenth in EPA per drop back on the week and 11th in drop back success rate. His rushing makes Daniels a viable superflex option this week against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Buccaneers declared QB Baker Mayfield, S Antoine Winfield, CB Benjamin Morrison, LB SirVoce Dennis, DL DeMonte Capehart, G Billy Schrauth and OG Luke Haggard inactive for Week 5 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield will miss another game due to the dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 3. His absence badly impacts the offense as a whole. Winfield’s absence in the secondary will also make it tough for a Tampa Bay defense tasked with slowing the Cowboys’ top-tier passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) will not play in Week 5 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: This was just a formality as Mayfield is expected to miss between three and six weeks with a dislocated thumb. Jalon Daniels will make his second start tomorrow against the Cowboys. Daniels struggled through the air in Week 4, throwing for just 148 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. He did, however, add 55 yards on the ground. His legs will keep him in the QB2 mix for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) was listed as DNP on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield is expected to miss “anywhere from three to six weeks” with his thumb injury, so it’s not at all surprising to see him listed as a DNP for Monday’s practice. We wouldn’t expect Mayfield to practice at all this week in the days leading up to Thursday’s matchup against the Cowboys. We’ll see if things change next week when the Bucs begin prepping for Week 6 against the Steelers. Rookie UDFA Jalon Daniels is expected to make his second career start on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Eagles aren’t planning to place QB Jalen Hurts (blood clot) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: While Hurts still has no timetable to return, the Eagles haven’t even discussed the possibility of placing him on injured reserve, according to Schefter. That could change as there’s still a possibility Hurts could wind up on injured reserve if that’s where the medical information leads them. Most blood clots are treated with anticoagulants (blood thinners), which would sideline Hurts for a minimum of six weeks, according to Schefter’s sources. The best-case scenario, according to Schefter, seems to be if the blood clot is minor enough that doctors could begin treatment with anti-inflammatories. Two team doctors that Schefter polled also speculated that the 28-year-old quarterback could miss six weeks. Tanner McKee is in line to start at least a few games while Hurts is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Eagles will decide whether to place Jalen Hurts (blood clot) on short-term injured reserve on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: Fowler reportedly spoke to “some people who are hopeful” that Hurts can avoid injured reserve. He described the situation as being “very much touch and go” and said Tanner McKee will “probably” start multiple games. The Eagles go on bye in Week 10, so if Hurts does land on injured reserve, the Eagles’ Week 11 game against the Steelers would be his earliest possible return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: Speaking on the Pat McAfee Show, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “would describe” Jalen Hurts’ (blood clot) status as being “out indefinitely.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: Hurts’ blood clot was initially a superficial issue in his calf. Unfortunately, the clot has moved and the situation now appears to be quite serious and, per Rapoport, “scary.” Rapoport said Hurts will now undergo treatment, “which, a lot of times, is blood thinners.” If that treatment option is deemed necessary, Hurts would not be allowed to play. Rapoport believes Hurts will be sidelined in Week 6 “and likely beyond.” Tanner McKee is his replacement.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Tanner McKee will start for the Eagles until Jalen Hurts’ (superficial blood clot) “medical situation is solved.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: McKee, 26, is a towering pocket passer (6'6/231) with 97 career dropbacks. He has two career starts and has made appearances in two other contests, averaging 6.8 yards per attempt and a 73.8 percent adjusted completion rate. McKee was the subject of trade rumors last offseason, but luckily, the Eagles kept him. He faces a Panthers secondary missing its two starting perimeter cornerbacks, though he has almost exactly 72 hours to get himself ready and the Eagles’ pass-catching corps is banged up. He is a viable QB2 in superflex formats, but he offers a wide range of potential outcomes. McKee is backed up by rookie Cole Payton. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo thinks the team could reunite with Andy Dalton, whom they released last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo believes the Eagles could re-sign Andy Dalton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: Dalton is “an option” for the Eagles, who are down to two available quarterbacks this week, Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton, with Jalen Hurts having been ruled out preemptively due to a superficial blood clot in his calf. The Eagles released Dalton last week. A few teams have reportedly checked in with Dalton since his release, “though there’s familiarity and a clear role in Philly for him if he decides to return.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: Jalen Hurts has a “superficial blood clot” and will not play in Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: The Eagles released an official statement announcing the news. Per their statement, Hurts took a cleat to the calf in Week 4. He went in for treatment the following Thursday and an ultrasound revealed the blood clot. Doctors ultimately cleared him to play in Week 5. He continued to receive treatment over the next two days. After practice on Wednesday (yesterday), a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. The team has now ruled him out for Week 6 as they determine the next course of action. They didn’t comment on how long Hurts will be out, but it’s possible this is a long-term issue for the veteran quarterback. Tanner McKee will draw the start versus Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: Jalen Hurts completed 21-of-40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ 19-17, Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: Hurts added a grand total of two yards on the ground. The Eagles even seemed afraid to use him for tush pushes, opting for a shotgun handoff on an early fourth-and-one. The bulk of Hurts’ production through the air came on a single deep shot to Darius Cooper. Hurts’ pass was actually a bit off the mark, but Cooper adjusted well and sprinted into the end zone for a 62-yard touchdown. Hurts had Dontayvion Wicks wide open for his second long score of the day late in the third quarter, but an all-out blitz forced him to throw off his back foot and he overshot the attempt. A field goal with eight seconds left on the clock still should have been enough to win the game. Philly’s kick coverage unit then got burned by Ameer Abdullah, setting up a walk-off kick from Cam Little. The Philly offense is as lifeless as they come. Even if DeVonta Smith returns for Week 6 versus the Panthers, Hurts will fail to crack the top-12 at quarterback for the first time in years.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: Jalen Hurts (calf) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: Hurts popped up with a calf injury on Friday, but practiced in full and seems to be expected to play. Tanner McKee, now the only game in town after Andy Dalton’s release, would take over if necessary on Sunday. It doesn’t sound like anything to be overly worried about at this point, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion said the team would continue operating under center.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: Mannion defended his approach during a Tuesday presser, two days after the Eagles offense — missing DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley — sputtered to a loss against the Rams. The Eagles have put Jalen Hurts under center and utilized play action much more than usual this season. It’s a strategy that hasn’t paid off quite yet. Hurts ranks 31st out of 38 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt on passes from under center; his 18 percent success rate from under center is by far the worst in the NFL. It’s hard to envision brighter days ahead for Hurts if Smith remains sidelined. He’s barely startable in 12-team formats for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: Jalen Hurts completed 12-of-27 passes for 93 yards and two touchdowns in the Eagles’ 24-20, Week 4 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: Hurts contributed just five carries for 18 scoreless yards. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) out and Saquon Barkley (hamstring) joining him early, the game ended up on Hurts’ shoulders. He responded by averaging 3.4 yards per attempt and generating 68 yards net passing when his four sacks for 25 yards are factored in. The Eagles went 0-12 on third down and blew a 20-10 fourth quarter lead. It, obviously, was a miracle the Eagles had a lead to begin with. Hurts’ longest completion — a fluke Darius Cooper touchdown reception — went for 18 yards. Tank Bigsby had the “long” gain of the day with a 19-yard rush. RT Lane Johnson’s last-minute deactivation was another hindrance, but this is now an Eagles offense that has spent nearly a quarter of the season looking like it is going nowhere fast. Its season high for points is 27, and it has produced 27 combined against the contending Bears and Rams. Things are unlikely to get much better against the Jags’ top-notch defense on the road in London next Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: ESPN’s Ian Rapoport reports the Patriots will likely activate WR A.J. Brown (ankle) to play against the Jets in Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown returned to practice this week after going on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. While nothing is official yet, it’s a great sign that Rapoport is anticipating a return for the 29-year-old wide receiver in Week 6 against the Jets. Brown may not play a full complement of snaps in his first game back, but is still essentially a must-start for fantasy managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle) is questionable for New England’s Week 6 game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said they’d make the decision on whether to activate him off injured reserve on Saturday, so at least Brown won’t be a game-time decision. Brown can be started with confidence if he’s active, though he’d potentially be in line for a pitch count to the point where he’d be more of a WR2 than a WR1 in his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle) said his status for Week 6 against the Jets is “still up in the air.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown was a limited participant on Wednesday. He is reportedly taking a “one step at a time” approach to his return. We’ll see how his ankle responds to Thursday’s limited practice “with full shoulder pads.” Per Brown, the team is not rushing him back and will keep the long haul in mind when deciding whether to activate him. The Patriots (3-2) are in second in the AFC East.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: Patriots designated A.J. Brown (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown will return to practice today, likely for a limited session. The team now has 21 days to officially activate him from IR. That could happen later this week, which would mean he’s ready to suit up for Week 6 against the Jets. He would likely be on some sort of pitch count in his first game back, but even a limited AJB would be worthy of a spot in the WR2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said “there’s a chance” A.J. Brown (ankle) will practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown has been rehabbing from a high-ankle sprain he suffered in the season-opener. It was reported on Sunday that Brown was walking without a limp, and last week NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that “the hope is” Brown will play in Week 6 against the Jets. The team has not opened his return window, which they will need to do in order for him to practice this week. Once that happens, the focus will then move to his practice status and whether or not he can log a full practice or two before the weekend. We would expect Brown’s 21-day return window in the next 24 hours if the team really believes there’s a chance he could return this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: CBS Sports’ Melanie Collins reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is “walking without a limp.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown sustained a high ankle sprain in the season opener against Seattle and has rehabbed over the past month. Patriots OC Josh McDaniels told Collins he doesn’t anticipate any delay in Brown’s return to the lineup. The team believes Brown will be ready to go in Week 6. He’ll re-enter a Patriots offense that has found its footing in recent weeks following a rough start to the year. His return would be a nice bump for Drake Maye, one of the league’s best downfield passers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports “the hope is” that A.J. Brown (ankle) plays in Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Garfolo made it clear that this is what the team hopes will happen, but it’s far from a sure thing. Week 6 is the first week Brown is eligible to return from injured reserve. The Pats placed him on IR after he suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 1. Previous reports had Brown out for 6-8 weeks, so fantasy managers should be skeptical that he will be back for Week 6, but it’s at least on the table.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss 6-8 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Schefter and other reporters previously called it a 4-6 week injury, which now seems unlikely. Schefter did add that Brown is moving “pretty well” and could come back on the faster side of his updated timeline. Still, it looks like Brown will miss at least half of the regular season. Romeo Doubs will operate as the team’s No. 1 receiver until he returns, though it will likely be a group effort to replace Browns’ production. Mack Hollins and Demario Douglas will also be more involved.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports A.J. Brown won’t require surgery on his injured ankle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Schefter added Brown will miss four to six weeks with the high ankle sprain he sustained on Wednesday night against the Seahawks. It could be much longer than that before Brown is back to full health and operating as the Patriots’ alpha WR1. For now, Mack Hollins will slide into three-receiver sets and Romeo Doubs — who didn’t catch any of his three targets against Seattle — will likely function as Drake Maye’s top option. Demario Douglas could be an interesting add in deeper formats after leading the team with seven targets in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: Patriots placed WR A.J. Brown (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: This doesn’t come as much of a surprise after it was reported on Thursday that Brown could miss at least the next four games. Now that he finds himself on injured reserve, the star receiver won’t be able to return until at least Week 6 when the Patriots play host to the Jets. Brown caught just three passes for 26 yards in his debut with the Patriots before exiting the game. After running just four routes in the first half of Wednesday’s game, Mack Hollins ran 22 routes in the second half and should see an increase in snaps in the coming weeks. Brown’s absence should also pave the way for Romeo Doubs to see more looks in the passing game after he saw just three targets in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.headline: Titans CEO Burke Nihill said the organization fully believes in coach Robert Saleh and general manager Mike Borgonzi.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.analysis: The Titans are 0-5 and have won only three games since Borgonzi joined the team prior to the 2025 season. Despite this, Nihill told ESPN’s Turron Davenport that he feels a “sense of stability” in the organization. Davenport, in turn, notes that the Titans “have fired a coach or general manager every year since 2022.” Nihill apologized to Titans fans, saying ownership and team executives feel “a sense of grief” about the endless losses, and “feel the sense of responsibility to deliver” for fans moving forward. We wish them luck.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.headline: Titans hired former 49ers DC and Jets HC Robert Saleh as head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.analysis: Another domino falls in the 2026 coaching carousel as Saleh gets his second crack at head coaching duties, this time with the Titans. Long heralded for his aggressive and unrelenting defensive tendencies, Saleh will look to improve upon his .357 career win rate as a head coach after a tumultuous tenure in New York after peaking at a 7-10 record in 2022 and 2023. He steps into a near full rebuild after the Titans unloaded numerous key pieces at the trade deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports the Cardinals have scheduled a second interview on Tuesday with 49ers DC Robert Saleh for their head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.analysis: Saleh is currently interviewing with the Titans for their head coaching vacancy. If he lives without a deal, he will be on his way to Arizona for a second meeting with the Cardinals on Tuesday. Saleh has made the rounds this coaching cycle, meeting with four different teams to discuss their head-coaching vacancies, with the Cardinals being the first team to put in a second request. The former Jets head coach returned to the Bay Area in 2025 to lead the Niners defense to a 13th-ranked finish in points allowed, and is clearly a valued candidate on the coaching market despite going 20-36 in his first try as a head coach.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports 49ers DC Robert Saleh is meeting in person with the Titans on Monday for their head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.analysis: Saleh was initially set to meet with the Titans virtually on Sunday, but instead pushed his interview to Monday so he could hold an in-person meeting with the team. His interview comes shortly after the team wrapped things up with former Chiefs offensive coordinator Matt Nagy, who is believed by some to be the front runner to land the position. Schultz reported earlier that Saleh, Nagy, and Jeff Hafley were believed to be the top three choices for the Titans, who recently saw Hafley get taken off the market by the Dolphins. If there’s any truth to Saleh and Nagy being the Titans’ top options, they’ll likely move quickly to close the deal with their preferred candidate as they look to find the coach best fit to lead the franchise and No. 1 overall pick Cam Ward into the future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.headline: Ravens completed an interview with 49ers DC Robert Saleh for their head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.analysis: One of the most requested head coaching candidates this coaching cycle, Saleh now adds the Ravens to the list of teams he has officially spoken with regarding their head coaching vacancies. He will follow up his interview with the Ravens with a trip to Tennessee to speak with the Titans about their opening.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.headline: Dolphins completed an interview with 49ers DC Robert Saleh for their head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.analysis: The Dolphins have been busy today. They completed an interview with Chargers DC Jesse Minter for the same role just a few hours ago. Saleh, similarly, is scheduled to interview for the Cardinals’ head-coaching vacancy later tonight, after helping the 49ers’ defense navigate their way through an injury-impacted ongoing season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.headline: Cardinals will interview 49ers DC Robert Saleh for their head-coaching vacancy tonight.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.analysis: The 49ers currently list six combined linebackers and defensive linemen on injured reserve, including defensive stars Fred Warner and Nick Bosa. Saleh has helped keep the 49ers’ Super Bowl aspirations intact in his first season back with his old team despite the personnel losses. His successes have earned him head-coaching interview requests with four different teams. Good for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.headline: Titans requested an interview with 49ers DC Robert Saleh for their head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.analysis: He’ll interview Sunday, per Ian Rapoport. Saleh has drawn requests from Miami, Baltimore, and Arizona this offseason. The 49ers DC has done an admirable job holding down the fort this year while missing stars Fred Warner and Nick Bosa for most of the season. For the Titans, he is one of 19 different interviews they’ve conducted so far. They’ll move past the initial round after this one and try to nail down a list of finalists.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.headline: Dolphins requested permission to interview 49ers DC Robert Saleh for the head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.analysis: It’s the fifth interview request for the former Jets head coach as the 2026 coaching carousel continues trudging on. Saleh has also drawn interest from the Cardinals, Ravens, Falcons, and Titans after interviewing with the Cowboys and Jaguars ahead of the 2025 season. The veteran defensive mastermind coach could be on the move once more this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.headline: Ravens requested permission to interview 49ers DC Robert Saleh for their head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/robert-sal.analysis: Since our last hit on Saleh, he’s picked up interview requests from the Falcons and Titans, so this takes him up to four interview requests in silly season after the Cardinals broke the seal on Tuesday. It’s clear other NFL teams don’t hold him accountable for what happened with the Jets in the ill-fated Aaron Rodgers Era.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) posted a video to social media indicating he will play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Normally, social media posts don’t count for much. However, earlier today, Bears coach Ben Johnson said that the Bears should have more clarity on Williams’ status by the end of the day, after the medical team put Williams through “the final stress tests” in his return-to-play program. We are inferring that Williams’ social media post suggests he passed the final medical testing, though we have not officially received word that this is indeed the case. For now, we tentatively expect Williams to play on Sunday. He can be treated as a mid-to-low QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Bears are smartly taking a conservative approach with their franchise quarterback. Williams had a limited practice session last week and practiced fully this week. Bears coach Ben Johnson told reporters that the team should have more clarity by the end of the day on whether Williams has passed his return-to-play plan’s final stress tests. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Bears’ QB1 is seemingly on track to make his return this week, when his team takes on the Falcons. When speaking to reporters after practice, though, Williams said he does not know if he is going to play yet, adding that he still has a number of tests and protocols to go through before he’s cleared. If active, Williams could end up running a little less frequently than he did early in the year, perhaps playing cautiously in his first game back. Regardless, Williams is a low-end QB1 if he is indeed active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) practiced in full Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Technically, Williams was estimated as a full participant ahead of the Bears’ Week 6 game against the Falcons. We’ll see if Williams, who has missed the past three games, practices in full on Thursday. Either way he’s likely to be under center against the pass-funnel Atlanta defense in Week 6. He should be in all lineups if he’s active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said “all signs point” to Caleb Williams (hamstring) returning in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Head coach Ben Johnson said on Sunday that Williams would be “close” to suiting up for Week 6, and he reportedly had a good workout before Week 5’s game against the Packers. Williams has missed the last three games with the hamstring injury he suffered in Week 2, but the Bears have managed to go 2-1 over that span. Williams logged one limited practice last week, after being a DNP on Wednesday and Thursday. If he can get on the practice field multiple days this week, it would be a good sign for his availability for next week’s game against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bears declared QB Caleb Williams, RB Kyle Monangai, OT Ozzy Trapilo, LB Keyshaun Elliott, DT Jayden Loving and EDGE Jamree Kromah inactive for Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Why the Bears went through the dog and pony show of labeling Williams as “questionable” when everybody knew he would not be playing, nobody knows. Either way, Williams appears to have a strong chance of returning for Week 6 against the Falcons. Expect another run-heavy game plan, even without Monangai, in what should be the final game of the Tyson Bagent experience for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Caleb Williams is “pushing to play” in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams is technically listed as questionable for Week 5 versus the Packers, but Tyson Bagent is fully expected to make the start. Still, Williams’ return to practice on Friday was a pleasant surprise for Bears fans. If all goes well in practice next week, he could return after missing just three games, which was on the short end of his projected timeline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Bears coach Ben Johnson told reporters on Monday that Tyson Bagent will start against the Packers this week. Fast forward a few days and the odds have changed slightly. Williams did a little throwing, practicing in a limited capacity today, and is progressing through his rehab plan. That said, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Bagent will “most likely” get the start. We expect that to be the case. Regardless, make sure Williams is rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Caleb Williams (hamstring) has a “progression” plan, but his return timeline is still “to be determined.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Bears have a progression plan in place for Williams’ rehab, and per Johnson, the star quarterback is “right on track.” Williams resumed throwing “a little bit the other day.” Although the team does not yet know when Williams will retake the field on game day, they have set up a series of benchmarks for him to hit. Their Week 7 Thursday Night Football game could complicate things. Bringing Williams back in Week 6 would give him a short turnaround, and he could be sore after his first game back. Expect them to handle this cautiously. The Bears currently sit in second in the NFC North with a 3-1 record.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Wiederer reports Caleb Williams has looked “spry and comfortable taking drops, planting, slinging it around.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams has already been ruled out for Week 5, but Wiederer notes that he is “progressing notably with his on-field recovery steps.” He added that the Bears having a Thursday game in Week 7 complicates things slightly. If Williams returns in Week 6, he will have an unusually short turnaround to his next game. That’s a bridge the Bears will potentially have to cross next week. For now. Tyson Bagent will draw the start again on Sunday. Ben Johnson has made magic with both of his backups so far. We fully expect the offense to survive one more week without Williams under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the NFL “could step back in and create a longer suspension” for Josh Jacobs if the video showing his altercation with a woman is released.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Fowler is surprisingly saying the quiet part out loud here, though this has been the general consensus for fans and analysts for a while. Jacobs is scheduled to come off the NFL’s Commissioner Exempt list on Monday. The NFL is reportedly trying to get hold of the video, and Jacobs has sued to block its release. Fowler adds that the woman’s attorney said her client has not participated in the league’s investigation due to privacy concerns. If the video stays under wraps, Jacobs could be allowed to continue playing in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Josh Jacobs is being removed from the NFL’s Commissioner Exempt list on Monday.
