https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: According to Schefter, “the investigation will remain open for the NFL, so it reserves the right to add further discipline if and when warranted.” Yesterday, ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reported that the league is trying to get ahold of the video showing Jacobs’ altercation with a woman at his home. Jacobs is expected to be eligible to play in Week 7 against the Lions. The situation clearly remains in flux, but Jacobs can be stashed on fantasy football benches at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reports that Josh Jacobs “has filed a civil suit seeking a permanent injunction restricting access to records from his May 23 altercation with a woman at his home.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Demovsky notes that the NFL is trying to get the video of the altercation as part of its investigation. Jacobs is trying to prevent anyone from seeing it, citing everything from protecting the woman’s anonymity to future burglary prevention. We have no idea how this will play out, but Demovsky reported in late September that Judge Marc Hammer “denied the request by the victim in the Josh Jacobs case to have the records permanently sealed.” Jacobs is appealing this ruling. It is unclear when or if Jacobs will play in the NFL again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he does not expect “an imminent return for Josh Jacobs.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacob’s current time on the Commissioner’s Exempt List is expected to count as time served toward an eventual suspension. Rapoport added, “If they get to the point where it’s five games, six games, maybe eight games, that might be when you’re looking at a potential return for Josh Jacobs.” The NFL is currently trying to obtain video footage of the incident from the Hobart/Lawrence police department. The victim in Jacobs’ case requested that it be sealed by a judge for privacy reasons, but that request was denied. Now the NFL has filed a FOIA request to obtain it. It seems like they won’t make any decisions on Jacobs’ suspension until they have viewed the video, which could take several more weeks to resolve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reports, “Judge Marc Hammer denied the request by the victim in the Josh Jacobs case to have the records permanently sealed.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: He added that the matter has been turned over to the Hobart/Lawrence police department, which is now in charge of determining whether or not the video will be released. Jacobs or the victim can then appeal that decision. The NFL has been adamant about getting the video before determining Jacobs’ pending suspension, and this increased the odds of that happening. Still, Jacobs could try to prevent that through the appeal process. Jacobs is believed to be facing a 4-6 game suspension, but the NFL can increase the length because of aggravating circumstances. This legal matter is inching toward a resolution, but a clash over the video would likely delay things even further.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Josh Jacobs could be facing a 4-6 game suspension after he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: The league is reportedly pushing to get hold of the videotaped incident that took place between Jacobs and his ex-girlfriend, but the victim has filed a motion that states the disclosure of the tape would threaten her “privacy, dignity, security, and emotional well-being.” Fowler says this motion will make acquiring the tape “increasingly harder for the league,” but that a four-to-six-game suspension is believed to be in range for Jacobs, according to people Fowler has spoken with across the league. Jacobs remains on the commissioner’s exempt list and will not be active for Week 2’s game against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the NFL plans to interview Josh Jacobs before making a disciplinary ruling.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: According to Rapoport, the league is “trying all sorts of legal maneuvers” to get the video of the incident. The court has already barred the video from being released, so it’s unclear whether the league will be able to get it from Jacobs at all. For now, Jacobs remains on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. MarShawn Lloyd will start at running back until he is removed from the list and serves an impending suspension.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Packers RB Josh Jacobs remains on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and that there is “no timetable” as to when he could be disciplined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: The NFL is “closely monitoring all developments in the matter, which remains under review of the personal conduct policy.” We expect Jacobs to receive a suspension, but the league can move at its own pace. Packers RB MarShawn Lloyd is expected to serve as the fill-in starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman reports Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs’ trial was initially slated to take place on November 17th. That date was recently moved up to today, signaling that Jacobs wanted to wrap up his legal proceedings quickly. He has been on the Commissioner’s Exempt List since the end of training camp. Roger Goodell could have kept him on the list indefinitely, especially with the trial previously scheduled multiple months into the season. With the legal matter now settled, Jacobs will likely serve a minor suspension as a result of the charges. MarShawn Lloyd is expected to handle the bulk of the carries until he returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Packers RB Josh Jacobs’ first court hearing has been moved up from November 17th to September 10th.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: The NFL placed Jacobs on the Commissioner Exempt List on August 30th, which prevents him from practicing with the team and playing in NFL games. The NFL acts independently and can make its own decision as to whether Jacobs’ behavior warrants a suspension. That said, rulings or evidence presented in court could impact the league’s decision-making. This could be consequential. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk’s inability to practice fully despite his lengthy injured reserve stint suggests he might need another week or two to get ready for an NFL game. Still, the 49ers don’t face the Commanders until Monday night. If active, he could end up warranting FLEX treatment with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) ailing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers designated Christian Kirk (calf/IR) to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: His 21-day window to practice before being activated begins today and he’ll be limited in practice. It would be surprising if Kirk were activated this week given the timing, but perhaps Week 7 will be a realistic target, assuming practice goes smoothly and there are no setbacks. He was limited in his first practice back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers placed Christian Kirk (calf) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: San Francisco also placed offensive lineman Austen Pleasants on injured reserve. Both players will miss at least four games to start the year. Kirk missed most of training camp with the calf issue. Mike Evans, De’Zhaun Stribling, and Deebo Samuel will start for the team in three-receiver sets. Even when Kirk comes back, he’s likely stuck as the WR4 on the depth chart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows reports that “a Week 1 roster spot seems to be slipping away from” 49ers WR Christian Kirk (calf).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Barrows’ phrasing leaves room for interpretation, but it seems as though he is suggesting Kirk could be a cut candidate. The veteran wide receiver was sidelined by a calf injury in the spring and reinjured it in the first practice of training camp. He should probably be avoided in fantasy drafts at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: NBCSportsBayArea’s Matt Maiocco reports 49ers WR Christian Kirk will miss time with a calf strain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk was seen leaving Sunday’s practice with trainers and was later diagnosed with a calf strain that will sideline him for the foreseeable future. The veteran receiver signed a one-year deal with the 49ers this offseason, is expected to compete for playing time with Ricky Pearsall, De’Zhaun Stribling, and Jordan Watkins. Kirk caught 28 passes for 239 yards and one touchdown in 13 games with the Texans last season

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows reports that 49ers WR Christian Kirk “walked off with a trainer midway through the session” on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk, 29, is entering his ninth NFL season. As is often the case with NFL veterans, Kirk has picked up his fair share of injuries over the years, including two hamstring strains last season. Fortunately, we are a long way from Week 1. There is no cause for concern at this time. 49ers acting head coach Chris Foerster will address the media shortly, so we could have clarity as to what the issue is soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers signed WR Christian Kirk, formerly of the Texans, to a one-year, $6 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk spent last season in a backup role with the Texans, finishing the year with 28 receptions for 239 yards and one touchdown on 52 targets. The veteran receiver has seen 99 targets in 21 games over the last two seasons while playing over 75 percent of his snaps from the slot. In 2025, current free agent Jauan Jennings led the 49ers with 142 slot snaps, but he’s unlikely to return to the team. Depending on how the rest of the offseason goes, Kirk could earn a decent role in San Francisco, but it’s hard to imagine him having too much fantasy viability outside of deep leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk caught 2-of-6 targets for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Texans’ Divisional Round loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: One of Kirk’s missed connections was a hellacious first quarter drop. A Wild Card hero, Kirk was one of many Divisional Round goats despite his 10-yard touchdown in the second quarter. Mostly a 4-6 target player out of the slot this season, Kirk was able to hold off third-round rookie Jaylin Noel, but only just. Now heading into his age-30 campaign as he prepares for free agency, Kirk could be a victim of the Texans’ receiver youth movement. Wherever he plays in 2026, the best he could hope for in fantasy is low-ceiling WR4 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Texans ruled out WR Nico Collins (concussion) for Houston’s Divisional Round game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Collins was unable to practice throughout the week. Texans slot WR Christian Kirk operated as the team’s No. 1 wide receiver last week, and is likely the best bet to do so again against the Patriots. It is an unfortunate development for Collins, who also missed his team’s Week 8 game against the 49ers due to concussion. Texans rookie WRs, Jayden Higgins and Jaylin Noel, have a chance to rise to the occasion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Texans WR Nico Collins (concussion) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M. Alexander believes Collins is “a long shot” to play on Sunday against the Patriots, given “the steps he must clear.” Unfortunately, he might be right. Collins still has time to advance through the NFL’s five-phase concussion protocol, but another absence at tomorrow’s practice would be discouraging. Veteran slot WR Christian Kirk stepped up last week, catching 8-of-9 targets for 144 yards and one touchdown in the Texans’ Wild Card win over the Steelers. We expect him to operate as the team’s top target earner if Collins cannot play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: Nick Bosa (calf) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: Bosa is on the wrong side of questionable despite prior reports and coaching comments indicating he has a chance to face the Commanders on Monday night. For now, we expect Bosa to miss another week, though the extra day off could help him return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said he’s “hoping Nick Bosa (calf) can go” in Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: Unfortunately, Bosa has not yet resumed practicing, though the 49ers have an extra day to let Bosa rehab. They face the Commanders in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game. Late last week, Bosa told reporters that it is “pretty darn likely” he plays in Week 6. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) said it is “pretty darn likely” he plays in Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: Bosa has missed two games since injuring his left calf in pre-practice warmups. He will miss his third game this weekend, but apparently the rehab progress is going well. The 49ers go on by in Week 8, and the team initially considered shutting him down until Week 9. Things are currently progressing well for the veteran pass rusher, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers ruled out Nick Bosa (knee/calf) for Week 5 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: The 49ers will be without Bosa, FB Kyle Juszczyk (knee), DL James Thompson Jr. (ankle) and S Marques Sigle (ankle) for this divisional showdown, making life a little easier on their opponent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers EDGE Nick Bosa (knee/calf) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: Bosa has yet to return to practice since injuring his calf two weeks ago in practice. He is listed with both knee and calf injuries and is seemingly not close to returning to in-game action. Bosa will need to practice before we can consider him ready to go for Week 5 or beyond.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers LT Trent Williams (stinger) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: The 49ers will have their stud left tackle active on Sunday. 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw (quad bruise) is questionable to play. 49ers EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) and DL Mykel Williams (knee) have both been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed that EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: Bosa strained his calf while going through his pre-practice warm-up routine on Thursday. The team has not yet identified Bosa’s expected return timeline, but the 49ers’ pass rusher will be out for some time. The 49ers also ruled out EDGE Romello Height (hand) for Week 3 against the Cardinals as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports 49ers DE Nick Bosa will miss “a few weeks” after pulling his calf in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: According to Schefter, the 49ers are deciding whether to place Bosa on injured reserve. The 28-year-old pass-rusher has yet to register a sack in his two games played this season and has tallied two sacks in five games since 2025. It’s just the latest in a string of injuries that has plagued Bosa in recent years. If he lands on injured reserve, the earliest he would be eligible to return is in Week 7 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers listed RB Christian McCaffrey, OT Trent Williams, LB Dre Greenlaw, and EDGE Nick Bosa as resting non-participants for Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: McCaffrey and Williams were listed as DNP simply for rest, while Bosa had a rest/knee designation and Greenlaw had a rest/Achilles designation. This is notable as the 49ers have several key veterans who have dealt with injuries throughout their career and practice reps will be managed for these players, especially coming off a Week 1 in Australia. McCaffrey reportedly dealt with cramps in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams; though he is not injured, his experiences with Achilles tendinitis will certainly lend to rest days throughout the season. We expect the 49ers to continue to rest veterans in practice throughout the season in an effort to remain healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers DC Raheem Morris said DE Nick Bosa is going to play in Week 1 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: During a media sessions late Monday, Morris was asked if Bosa would be able to go in Week 1 against the Rams, to which he responded, “Oh, he’s going out there. He’s going.” There’s no room left for interpretation about that quote, meaning Bosa is expected to make his return to the field after tearing his ACL in Week 3 of the 2025 season. Don’t expect a normal allotment of snaps in his first game in almost a calendar year, but the veteran pass-rusher can still make a significant impact when on the field. IDP managers will want to confirm his status on the team’s injury report Tuesday before making plans to insert him into Week 1 lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Even for an iron man like Evans, this is a little concerning. Frankly, we still expect Evans to play, but two missed practices due partially to Achilles “soreness” are less than ideal. The 49ers face the Commanders on Monday night. Making a backup plan is worthwhile at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles soreness) will not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: It’s tough to get a read on this. The 49ers like to describe injuries with things like “tightness” and “soreness” rather than just calling it an injury. That said, the team labeled Christian McCaffrey with “tightness” while he was in late August and it has not impacted him in the slightest, so speculating here is inappropriate. What we do know is that Evans plays through injuries that would sideline others. The 49ers face the Commanders on Monday night, giving Evans an extra day to get right. If active, he is a locked-in WR2. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans caught 7-of-10 targets for 113 yards and one touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans’ only touchdown of the game came on a two-yard pass from Brock Purdy in the first quarter to give the Niners an early 7-0 lead. Evans came up big on multiple occasions in this one, hauling in three catches of 20-plus yards, including back-to-back receptions of 23 and 28 yards that helped set up a seven-yard touchdown to Brandin Cooks. Evans then caught a pass in the end zone on the next play to convert a two-point try and put the Niners up 29-26. This was Evans’ best day as a Niner. He set season-highs in receptions, targets, and receiving yards, and has now found the end zone three times on the year. With Deebo Samuel (hamstring) potentially set to miss some time, Evans could very easily see more days like today. He will be a fringe WR1/WR2 next week against a porous Commanders secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (ribs) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 5 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: The 49ers’ star wide receiver is good to go for his team’s Week 5 game against a divisional rival. A hard hit to the midsection could change his day, but Evans is extremely tough and should be expected to handle his normal workload. He is a weekly WR2, operating as San Francisco’s passing game focal point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (ribs) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: For many NFL players, downgrading to a DNP on Thursday would be concerning. For Evans, this is business as usual unless the team says otherwise. The 49ers’ X-wide receiver regularly plays through injuries and does so effectively. We tentatively expect him to face the Seahawks in Week 5. He is a fantasy football WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans played through his rib injury last week and was surprisingly productive, posting five catches for 76 yards. He led the 49ers in targets and yards. A limited session today is a good sign that the rib injury didn’t get any worse on Sunday. He should be good to go as a fantasy WR2 for his Week 5 matchup with the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans caught 5-of-8 targets for 76 yards in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans toughed it out through a painful rib injury. He endured a couple shots to the midsection in the first half and remained in the game, eventually leading the Niners in targets and receiving yards. Accounting for 31 percent of the team’s air yards coming into Week 4, Evans profiles as a high-upside WR2 in most formats. Evans and the rest of the 49ers have a tough Week 5 matchup against a Seahawks secondary that has smothered opposing passing offenses so far this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (ribs) is active for Week 4 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans will battle through his rib injury and suit up against Denver, though it remains to be seen whether the veteran will play a full complement of snaps. Through three games Evans has accounted for 22 percent of he 49ers’ targets and 30 percent of the team’s air yards. The Niners declared QB Kurtis Rourke, DE Nick Bosa, DT James Thompson Jr., RB Jordan James, LB Tatum Bethune, CB Ephesians Prysock, and OT Enrique Cruz Jr. inactive against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Mike Evans (ribs) will be a game-time decision for Week 4 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans is officially questionable to play. He did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but in uniform and did some running on the side in the early, open portion of Friday’s practice. The grizzled veteran tends to play through injuries. He will try to play this week while wearing a compression shirt with padding in it. Evans told reporters that he has played through a similar injury previously. If active, he carries obvious re-injury risk but warrants starting as a WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (ribs) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: 49ers GM John Lynch said earlier today that Evans “will make every attempt” to play in Week 4 against the Broncos. The veteran receiver is no stranger to playing through injury. He attempted to do so last week with a hip injury, but taking a hit to the ribs knocked him out of the game. If active, he will be a WR2, albeit with re-injury risk.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: The Raiders’ starting running back is good to go for what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment. The Raiders encouragingly stopped listing Jeanty with an ankle injury this week. Hopefully, his remaining plantar fasciitis issue subsides before long as well. Jeanty is a low-end RB1 in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) said he is feeling “great” and “ready to go” for Week 6 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: The quotes read a tad bit more enthusiastically than Jeanty did while speaking to media members at his locker, but this is still good to hear. Jeanty has been dealing with an ankle injury for a long time, but the team took that injury off the weekly practice report this week. He is now listed only with the foot injury after experiencing “a flare-up of plantar fasciitis” last Friday. Jeanty is a low-end RB1 against the Bills this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty’s previous ankle designation was removed from the injury report and he was a full practice participant on Wednesday. His practice participation lines up with Raiders coach Klint Kubiak saying the 22-year-old running back was starting to “feel a lot better.” Though there were rumors of the Raiders resting Jeanty for a week, he is trending to play in Week 6 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Ashton Jeanty (foot/ankle) is starting to “feel a lot better.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Kubiak also shot down the idea of the Raiders resting Jeanty for a week, despite it being reported earlier today that the Raiders were considering giving him a week off to recover at some point. Jeanty has been dreadfully inefficient this year, averaging a meager 3.3 yards per carry, though the team’s subpar offensive line also deserves some of the blame. For fantasy purposes, his workload has been the big draw. He is averaging 22 touches per game through five weeks. Even if the foot and ankle injuries continue to bother him, Jeanty has to be treated as a mid-range RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty had 10 rushes for 27 yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots, adding three catches for 50 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Most of Jeanty’s production against New England came on a 31-yard catch and run in the third quarter. Battling through foot and ankle injuries, Jeanty looked hobbled from the start and struggled to break tackles or outrun Patriots defenders to the edge. Most Raiders starters rested in the fourth quarter of a lopsided loss. Jeanty still doesn’t have a rushing touchdown on the season and hasn’t had 100 rushing yards in a game since Week 1 against the Dolphins. Until Jeanty is fully healthy he probably won’t provide much in the way of upside, including next week against a decent Buffalo run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle, foot) is active for Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty will play through his foot and ankle injuries against New England. It wouldn’t be surprising if he cedes some backfield work to a healthy and much more explosive Mike Washington, however. Jeanty should be considered a top-24 option this week while Washington is a desperation flex. Raiders declared WR Jalen Nailor, QB Aidan O’Connell, S Tristin McCollum, RB Roman Hemby, S Dalton Johnson, OL Trey Zuhn, and DT JJ Pegues inactive against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ashton Jeanty (foot/ankle) is “hopeful” to play in Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Per Rapoport, Jeanty had a flare-up of plantar fasciitis last week to go along with his ankle injury. He added that Jeanty will work out before today’s game to see how he’s feeling. If he can’t go, Mike Washington Jr. would see the bulk of the backfield touches. Washington has been an explosive complement to Jeanty this year, averaging five yards per carry on 24 attempts. He would jump to the top of the RB2 ranks if Jeanty can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Ashton Jeanty (foot/ankle) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 5 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Kubiak didn’t get into real specifics about the injury when asked. Mike Washington just found his way into real contingency value and is a worthwhile stash/hedge anywhere he was dropped. Jeanty did not practice Friday after a limited session (and the addition of a foot tag) on Thurdsay, so this certainly doesn’t appear to be heading in the right direction. That said, we knew Jeanty would be managing something after the preseason ankle injury and the Raiders have given out rest days on Friday quite a bit already this year. Jeanty is likely something close to truly questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle/foot) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty has been dealing with the ankle injury throughout the week, but the foot injury was added after Thursday’s practice. Jeanty was officially listed as limited on Thursday, but the Raiders’ RB1 was absent from the media portion of Friday’s practice. We will receive final word on his Week 5 availability soon, but rookie Mike Washington could be in line for a busy day against the Patriots if Jeanty is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle/foot) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Oh, dear. Jeanty was a full participant yesterday, listed only with an ankle injury. Today, he was downgraded to limited and the Raiders tacked on a foot injury. The second-year running back has played through the nagging ankle injury thus far and could play through the pain again this weekend, but this situation must be closely monitored. Backup RB Mike Washington must be rostered in all formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: One of these days, Bowers will be removed from the injury report for good. For now, we will continue to let you know that the Raiders’ star player gets a half day on Wednesday before practicing in full for the rest of the week. Bowers is the overall TE1 in fantasy football each week. Start him accordingly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: The Raiders continue managing Bowers’ practice reps early in the week, though he plays unrestrictedly on game day. The Raiders face the Bills in Week 6, likely facilitating a fantasy-friendly game environment. Bowers should be treated as the overall TE1 as usual this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers continues his trend of practicing limited to open the week before upgrading to a full practice later in the week and getting cleared off the injury report. Fantasy managers can again expect to see Bowers return top-five fantasy tight end value in Week 6 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers caught 8-of-10 targets for 110 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers was again unstoppable both from the slot and from the boundary. The injury-ravaged New England secondary had no chance of stopping Bowers, whose ten targets led the Raiders. Bowers had three receptions of over 20 yards. His day could’ve been bigger if the Raiders had not rested their starters in the fourth quarter of the lopsided loss to the Patriots. With outrageous usage in Klint Kubiak’s offense, Bowers has as much upside as any player in fantasy for now. He gets the Bills in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (knee) is not on Las Vegas’ final injury report for Week 5.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: He practiced in full each of the last two days after a limited session on Wednesday. Bowers should be started with confidence in Week 5, though it looks like the knee injury will continue to limit his practice reps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: The Raiders’ No. 1 pass catcher is good to go for his team’s Week 5 game against the Patriots. Bowers primarily lines up as a wide receiver, and the Patriots could be without starting perimeter cornerbacks Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) and Carlton Davis (neck). He is an elite TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Raiders TE Brock Bowers (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers starts out the week limited, though he has played through his knee injury while getting limited practices the past couple weeks. Barring setbacks, Bowers should be cleared off the injury report Friday and will be a TE1 for Week 5 once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers caught 6-of-11 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers’ 11 targets again led the Raiders on Sunday. He’s now racked up 24 targets over the last two weeks and converted those opportunities into 16 receptions for 202 yards and two touchdowns. Bowers came up big for the Raiders late in the fourth quarter in Sunday’s game against the Chiefs. With the Raiders trailing 30-19 and less than two minutes to go in the game, Kirk Cousins avoided a sack and rolled right in the pocket to find Bowers in the end zone for a 20-yard touchdown, cutting the Chiefs’ lead to 30-25 before Cody White converted a two-point conversion try on the following play. To the surprise of nobody, Bowers has been the top target in head coach Klint Kubiak’s offense. He’ll look to build on his hot start in Week 5 when the Raiders take on the Patriots. It should go without saying that Bowers is a must-play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Raiders TE Brock Bowers (knee/illness) will play in Week 4 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Despite being questionable with a knee injury and an illness that was announced early Sunday, Bowers is active in what’s a surprisingly pivotal Week 4 matchup between undefeated AFC West teams. Bowers caught 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown on 14 targets last week and will be a high-end TE1 this week. While Bowers is active, the Raiders did declare QB Aidan O’Connell, CB Darrell Luter Jr., S Tristin McCollum, OL Jackson Powers-Johnson, and DT Jonah Laulu inactive for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Raiders are “fully expecting” Brock Bowers (knee/illness) to play in Week 4 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Today’s report is in relation to Bowers’ illness, not his knee. Earlier this morning, the Raiders announced that Bowers has come down with an illness, but the illness will not alter his game status. Bowers’ knee was a non-issue last week, and we expect it to be a non-issue again this week. He is good to go for the Raiders’ Week 4 game against the Chiefs. Treat him like an elite TE1, as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler continues to practice in a limited capacity while wearing a red non-contact jersey. He has a chance to play on Monday night, but he is clearly hurting. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) remains sidelined and Rachaad White (shoulder) has been downgraded to limited. It’s an ailing backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) are both ailing, though the latter player sat out entirely. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Jeremy McNichols (quad) are both practicing in full. Croskey-Merritt is the only fantasy-relevant Commanders running back at this time, assuming he is good to go on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Austin Ekeler rushed four times for 29 yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts, adding one catch for 11 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler made his 2026 debut in London and immediately operated as the Commanders’ backup with Rachaad White out. The team did, however, give four running backs multiple touches in this game. Ekeler’s role could grow as he gets more reps under his belt this year, but he could just as easily be made inactive once White is healthy. He’s only worth stashing in the deepest of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) will not play in Washington’s Week 4 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: He didn’t practice at any point this week after suffering a shoulder injury in Week 3. He has to be considered questionable for Week 5 at this point. ‘Bill’ Croskey-Merritt figures to shoulder the majority of the workload for the Commanders this week and is a reasonable FLEX play against the Colts. Freshly-signed Austin Ekeler figures to handle third-down work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: With two DNPs to start the week, White looks unlikely to suit up for Week 4 against the Colts. Austin Ekeler traveled with the team after signing with the team earlier this week, so he could ultimately take on White’s role. Backup running back Kayton Allen could also see more work, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt remains the clear lead back in Washington for now. He is on the RB2/3 border for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Rachaad White is receiving treatment for his shoulder injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: It sounds like White will be a question mark headed into Washington’s Week 4 game against the Colts in London. Quinn added that it’s too early to tell whether Austin Ekeler, who signed with the Commanders this week, will be active for Week 4. Jacory Croskey-Merritt could see a significant bump in carries and pass routes — and maybe targets — if White is sidelined this week. JCM, who has 58 percent of the team’s carries through three games, would be a nice flex option in that case.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Commanders re-signed RB Austin Ekeler.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler is fully recovered from a torn Achilles that ended his 2025 season after just two games. The 31-year-old running back returns to a familiar place in Washington and will sign to the 53-man roster, making him immediately eligible to play in Week 4. We expect him to have a bit of a ramp-up period before being active on game days, but Ekeler could end up having a meaningful role in a backfield that has struggled to get going through the first three weeks. Ekeler may be worth a stash in deeper leagues, but we’ll have to see what kind of role he has before we can consider putting him in lineups. Ekeler met last week with the Panthers about possibly joining their practice squad but a deal was never reached.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: ESPN’s Mike Kaye reports Austin Ekeler is not expected to sign with the Panthers today.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Ekeler worked out for the Panthers today. Kaye noted that the workout went well, so it’s possible Ekeler lands with the team in the future. With Jonathon Brooks (groin) on injured reserve, the Panthers need to make an addition or two at running back, even just for some extra depth. Regardless of who they sign, Chuba Hubbard is set for a workhorse role for the foreseeable future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: Panthers will host a workout for Austin Ekeler, formerly of the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: Carolina is in need of some backfield reinforcements after losing Jonathon Brooks to a core injury that will leave him sidelined for at least six weeks. AJ Dillon is set to fill in for Brooks while Chub Hubbard presumably continues as the team’s lead back. Ekeler, 31, who hasn’t played since injuring his Achilles last September, could be an emergency running back if Hubbard or Dillon go down with injuries in the coming weeks. First he’ll need to make the squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Commanders RB Austin Ekeler suffered a torn Achilles and will miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/austin-eke.analysis: An MRI confirmed that Ekeler suffered a torn Achilles in Thursday’s game against the Packers. The 30-year-old running back will miss the remainder of the season. Jacory “Bill” Croskey-Merritt and Jeremy McNichols figure to handle the running back duties for the Commanders going forward with Chris Rodriguez now as the third running back active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.headline: Terry McLaurin (hamstring/rest) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.analysis: The Commanders added a “rest” designation to McLaurin’s report, so fantasy managers should not be alarmed by today’s absence. The veteran wide receiver played through the injury last week and should be expected to do so again this week. McLaurin is a WR2 against the 49ers in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.headline: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.analysis: McLaurin posted a 4/62 receiving line, playing through this hamstring injury in Week 5 against the Giants. Kicking off the week with a limited session is a great sign for his Week 6 availability and overall health. Expect McLaurin to be even more involved against the 49ers on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.analysis: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he is hopeful Diggs will get some practice reps in later this week. Diggs missed Week 5 with the hamstring issue, and a DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6, even if Quinn remains optimistic. Terry McLaurin and Chig Okonkwo led the team in receiving last week. McLaurin should pull away from Okonkwo as he puts more time between himself and the hamstring injury that previously knocked him out for a week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.headline: Terry McLaurin caught 4-of-4 targets for 62 yards in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie with the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.analysis: It was reported before the game that McLaurin would not be a full go after he was limited in practice all week with a hamstring injury. While McLaurin would finish the game with the third-most snaps played by any Commanders receiver, his 28 routes run were tied for the most of any player on the team. McLaurin converted all four of his targets into receptions on Sunday, with his biggest gain coming on a 22-yard reception in overtime that looked to be the start of an eventual game-winning drive for Washington. McLaurin’s 62 receiving yards led all of Washington’s pass-catchers in this one, and he has now totaled 50 or more yards in three straight games. If Stefon Diggs, who missed this week’s game (hamstring) is able to suit up next week against the 49ers, McLaurin will profile as a fringe WR2/WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.headline: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) is active for Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.analysis: While it’s good news that McLaurin is active, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported earlier that he is “likely not a full go” for Sunday’s game. To make matters worse, the Commanders and Giants are expected to battle it out in soggy conditions all afternoon, which could further limit McLaurin’s upside in this one. Fantasy managers hoping to play him need to temper expectations given his status and the game’s conditions, and shouldn’t consider McLaurin as anything more than a mid-to-low-end WR3. The Commanders announced WR Stefon Diggs (hamstring), QB Marcus Mariota (knee), S Tyler Owens (hamstring), S Nick Cross (illness), S Percy Butler (hamstring), OG Tanoa Togiai, and DE Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle) are inactive for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Terry McLaurin is a “true game-time decision” for Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.analysis: McLaurin is listed as questionable for Week 5 after getting in a single limited practice on Friday. Even if he does play, McLaurin will likely be on a pitch count. Stefon Diggs has already been ruled out with a hamstring issue of his own. Rookie Antonio Williams will be asked to step up whether or not McLaurin is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Terry McLaurin (hamstring) will “most likely” be a game-time decision for Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.analysis: Keep it locked to Rotoworld, folks. Hopefully, we get word on McLaurin’s status on Saturday, but it appears as though we may have to wait until Sunday morning. Fowler adds that rookie WR Antonio Williams “could be a factor in the passing game regardless of whether McLaurin plays.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.headline: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.analysis: McLaurin could end up playing here, but he would be a risk for an in-game aggravation. The Commanders’ No. 1 wide receiver was sidelined on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to a limited session on Friday. Hopefully, weekend reports on the injury shed light on things. If active, he is a WR2 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is not practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.analysis: Diggs was unable to get on the practice field this week and will likely be ruled out for Week 5’s game against the Giants in the next few hours. Rookie receiver Antonio Williams would again be in line for a busy day and could be the favorite to lead the team in targets this week, especially if Terry McLaurin (hamstring) also misses this week. McLaurin’s status remains wait and see after he was spotted on the practice field Friday after being a DNP on the first two days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.headline: The Washington Post’s Tashan Reed reports Terry McLaurin (hamstring) was not on the field for the start of Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terry-mcla.analysis: McLaurin could technically return later in the session and go down as a limited participant, but we highly doubt that will happen. He will be listed as a DNP for the second day in a row, making it extremely unlikely he is available for Week 5. After facing the Giants this week, the Commanders get a slightly longer rest period before taking on the 49ers on Monday in Week 6. If they are worried about McLaurin re-aggravating the issue, they get their bye the following week, which would give him plenty of time to recover. For now, Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams will lead the team’s receiver room.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Ed Oliver is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Bills slot CB Dee Alford (ankle) is also questionable. Coach Joe Brady said a week ago that both players avoided long-term injuries. They might actually have a chance to play this week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Ed Oliver (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: The Bills’ stud defensive tackle is on the wrong side of questionable for the Bills’ Week 6 game against the Raiders. Fortunately, the pass rush is playing very effectively despite Oliver’s continued injury issues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Ed Oliver (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Oliver was listed as a non-participant in the Bills’ Wednesday walk-through report. He suffered a knee injury in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots and avoided long-term injury, though he has yet to see the practice field. Bills fans should stay tuned to his practice status the rest of the week; Oliver will need some level of participation before the Bills can consider making him active for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said the team thinks Ed Oliver (knee) avoided a long-term injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Brady said the same goes for nickel CB Dee Alford (ankle). While this is positive news for the Bills’ defense, Oliver has already missed one game this season with a hip injury. Alford is not a top-tier coverage defender, but both players will be missed in the short term.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Ed Oliver is questionable to return with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: It’s unclear when Oliver got hurt or what happened. He was on the bench without a helmet for a few drives before heading into the locker room. The Bills are down 21-17, and without T.J. Sanders as well, so they can’t afford to lose Oliver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Ed Oliver (hip) is active for Week 3 against the Los Angeles Chargers
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Oliver was a late scratch from last Thursday’s game against the Lions when he hurt himself during pre-game warm-ups. It seems that he’s feeling good now and will have a great matchup against a Chargers offensive line that is missing multiple starters in the interior.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Ed Oliver (hip) is questionable for Week 3 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Oliver was a surprise scratch in last week’s game against the Lions after suffering an injury in pre-game warmups. It was reported on Sunday that Oliver was day-to-day with “a chance” to play against the Chargers. After being limited in back-to-back practice to close out the week, it’s fair to assume he’ll have a chance to suit up on Sunday barring any setbacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Bills DT Ed Oliver (hip) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Oliver now has a chance to face the Chargers in Week 3, though nothing is certain. The Bills’ star interior defender injured his hip during pre-game warmups last week and was unable to play. The Chargers’ banged-up offensive line has underperformed thus far. This is a situation worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: Bills DT Ed Oliver (hip) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: Oliver suffered a hip injury during warmups of the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions. He did not play in the game and now starts out Week 3 not practice. Oliver could certainly still go this week against the Chargers but he will likely need at least a limited practice to be in consideration to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ed Oliver (hip) “has a chance” to play in Week 3 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-oliver/.analysis: He is considered day-to-day. Per Rapoport, Oliver experienced hip spasms during warmups ahead of the Bills’ Week 2 game against the Lions. The Bills ruled him out right at the deadline for inactives. Oliver only appeared in three games last year but still managed three sacks. He logged one TFL and a fumble recovery in Week 1 of this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.headline: Joshua Palmer (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.analysis: Palmer practiced in a red non-contact jersey on Thursday. Even if he plays this week, he is likely only relevant in single-game DFS tournaments. He mostly provides Josh Allen with another viable target on a couple of plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.headline: Joshua Palmer (shoulder) was seen practicing in a red non-contact jersey on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.analysis: This is a good first step, but Palmer may need another week or so off before he returns to the field. Palmer injured his shoulder in practice last week and was unable to face the Rams in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.headline: Bills ruled out WR Joshua Palmer (shoulder) for Week 5 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.analysis: Palmer apparently injured his shoulder in practice on Friday before being absent Saturday, ultimately ruled out for Week 5 against the Rams on Monday Night Football. Fellow wide receiver DJ Moore is listed as questionable after failing to practice until a limited session Saturday, also with a shoulder injury, potentially leaving Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir atop the depth chart at the position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.headline: Bills WR Joshua Palmer (shoulder) did not practice Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.analysis: Palmer was added to the injury report Friday with a shoulder injury, likely indicating that was where he suffered the injury. This is bigger news when taken in the context of the potential absence of DJ Moore on Monday Night Football against the Rams after Moore aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 4. Expect Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman to function as the top two receivers, should both miss Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.headline: Joshua Palmer (shoulder) was added to the injury report on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.analysis: Palmer seemingly injured his shoulder in practice today. The Bills may already be without WR DJ Moore (shoulder) on Monday night. While Palmer is not relevant in 12-team leagues, his potential absence would improve Keon Coleman’s stock.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said Keon Coleman (ankle) is questionable and will be a game-time decision for Buffalo’s Week 3 game against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.analysis: Coleman didn’t practice on either Wednesday or Thursday, but made some movement on Friday by showing up to a practice even if media reporters weren’t truly sure if he was giving a lot of effort. Josh Palmer would be a reasonable FLEX play if Coleman were ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.headline: Keon Coleman caught all six targets for 63 yards in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.analysis: Coleman could be a hot name on the waiver wire following Week 2 after DJ Moore departed with what appeared to be a significant shoulder injury in the first half. The third-year veteran continues to tease at untapped upside in this high-powered offense but has yet to fully break through for consistent production. Maybe that changes now as his role potentially grows without Moore. It will also be interesting to see how, if at all, his route tree changes in the absence of Moore, particularly considering the team has Joshua Palmer to operate as the field-stretching, Z-type receiver, the latter of whom caught his only target for a 43-yard touchdown on a broken coverage against the Lions. Coleman is a speculative waiver addition ahead of a much more forgiving matchup against the Jets in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.headline: Josh Palmer caught a 34-yard touchdown on one of his two targets against the Texans in Week 1.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.analysis: It was a go-ahead score, one that Josh Allen rocketed on to Palmer’s chest. Palmer played just 18 of 57 snaps per PFF’s early data and looks to be behind Keon Coleman (29 snaps), though this at least will help keep him on the radar in the passing game. Palmer is more of a deep-league stash than anyone we want to start right now, but it’s not completely impossible for him to return value in this offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.headline: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia believes the Bills are still likely to add another wide receiver after trading for DJ Moore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.analysis: The Joshua Palmer fantasy stock could be in shambles, folks. Buscaglia connects the Bills to a wide assortment of receivers, notably stopping for a beat on Romeo Doubs, Jalen Nailor, and Calvin Austin as particularly good fits for Buffalo. Moore and Khalil Shakir are the two easy top targets, any other additions would likely sink Palmer into a background role in the second year of his contract.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.headline: Bills placed WR Joshua Palmer (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joshua-pal.analysis: Palmer failed to practice all week before initially drawing the questionable tag, eventually ruled out on Saturday for the team’s Wildcard Round game against the Jaguars. He was then placed on injured reserve, ending his season. Keon Coleman is expected to be active due to the absence for a team in desperate need of play makers behind quarterback Josh Allen and running back James Cook. The team elevated DE Andre Davis and RB Frank Gore Jr. in an associated move.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia notes that Moore resumed practicing today after sitting out on Wednesday and Thursday. He did the same thing last week before being labeled questionable and ultimately ruled out on game day. It looks like he’s a game-time decision again this week. If active, he can be started as a WR2, but re-injury remains a risk.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: It looks like the Bills could again be without their No. 1 wide receiver on game day. Josh Allen and Co. take on the Raiders this weekend, in what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment. Hopefully, Moore resumes practicing soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 4 and only practiced with a non-contact jersey on Saturday of last week. After missing Week 5, Moore starts out as a non-practice participant in the Bills’ Wednesday walk-through. He will need at least a limited practice before fantasy managers can start considering him for Week 6 lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) is inactive for Week 5 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore’s absence leaves only Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir, Greg Dortch, and Skyler Bell as healthy wide receivers on the active roster with Joshua Palmer also sidelined. Expect heavy snap rates for Coleman and Shakir alongside tight end Dalton Kincaid, with the possibility the team elevates their 12-personnel rates through the inclusion of Dawson Knox. Also inactive for the Bills are WR Joshua Palmer, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL Ed Oliver DL, Landon Jackson, and NCB Dee Alford.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable for Week 5 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore failed to practice until Saturday after aggravating a shoulder injury in Week 4, returning to the field in a limited capacity while wearing a red non-contact jersey. That was apparently enough to keep the door open for an appearance on Monday Night Football against the Rams, although he certainly appears to be on the wrong side of the questionable tag. Fantasy managers would be wise to seek alternate options considering the timing of the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) practiced with a non-contact jersey Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: This is the first time Moore has returned to the practice field after aggravating a shoulder injury in Week 4. Still no word on his game-day injury status, which will come later in the afternoon, but it a small step in the right direction for the veteran receiver. Fantasy managers likely want to continue the search for alternatives with the Bills playing on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: The Bills’ No. 1 wide receiver is on the wrong side of questionable for his team’s Monday Night Football game against the Rams. Moore sprained the AC joint in his left shoulder in Week 2. He aggravated it in Week 4 with a hard fall and was unable to continue playing. If active, Moore will be a risk-reward WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was not spotted in the media-viewing portion of practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Joe Brady is quoted as saying that if Moore feels he’s healthy enough to play, he “owes it to the WR to let him be out there.” It’s not exactly a quote that inspires a lot of confidence in Moore’s availability for Monday night’s matchup with the Rams after he left Week 4’s game due to landing on the shoulder. We would regard Moore as on the doubtful side of questionable at this point, but there’s time to turn that around on Friday and Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore is doubtful to return to Week 4 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore landed on his left shoulder while trying to make the catch on a pass in the second quarter. It’s the same shoulder that he injured in the Week 2 win over the Lions. Obviously, the fact that it’s the same shoulder is not a great sign, as is Moore’s long injury history. We should get an update at halftime, but Keon Coleman figures to step into a larger role for the remainder of the game. Moore had just one catch for 11 yards before leaving with his injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) is not on Buffalo’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: He’ll be good to go against the Christian Gonzalez-less Patriots. Moore is evidently still dealing with some soreness as he practiced in a non-contact jersey at points this week, but he’ll be a worthy WR2 in an elevated matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.headline: Free agent Terrell Jennings worked out for the Patriots on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.analysis: Free agent running backs Ulysses Bentley and Josh Pitsenberger also worked out for the Patriots. TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Jets. Perhaps the Patriots are making backup plans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.headline: Free agent RB Terrell Jennings worked out for the Steelers on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.analysis: Perhaps one of the Steelers’ backup running backs got dinged up in their Thursday Night Football game against the Browns. Adding Jennings would make sense for depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.headline: Patriots placed RB Terrell Jennings on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.analysis: Jennings spent time on the active/non-football injury list this summer. He was activated 10 days ago. It is unclear whether the same issue that sidelined him then caused his injured reserve placement. The Patriots correspondingly signed RB JaMycal Hasty.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.headline: Patriots activated RB Terrell Jennings from the active/non-football injury list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.analysis: Jennings is good to go after an undisclosed injury sidelined him for the first week of training camp. The third-year back is expected to compete for RB3 duties this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.headline: Patriots placed Terrell Jennings (undisclosed) on the active/non-football injury list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.analysis: He can be pulled off at any time. Jennings was the RB3 last year for New England when healthy and figures to be part of the competition again this year if healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that Terrell Jennings “appears to have the early edge” for the Patriots’ RB3 role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.analysis: Reiss bases his conclusion on Jennings’ work with the first-unit punt protection team. Jennings, 25, rushed 23 times for 73 yards and one touchdown, and turned his lone target into a nine-yard gain last year. Jennings is a name to know for waiver wire purposes, in case RBs Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson miss time. Aside from that, Jennings will not be scoring fantasy points on the punt squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.headline: Patriots downgraded RB Terrell Jennings (concussion) and DT Joshua Farmer (hamstring) to out for the Conference Championship against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.analysis: Both players came into the weekend listed as questionable but will ultimately be held out for the team’s Conference Championship game against the Broncos. Jennings was not activated from injured reserve after being placed there in Week 13 with a concussion. Expect veteran journeyman D’Ernest Johnson to be active on Sunday and serve in an emergency role behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.headline: Patriots EDGE Harold Landry (knee) is questionable for New England’s Divisional Round game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.analysis: He didn’t practice today. Landry played 26 snaps against the Chargers last week and would figure to be part of a rotation at EDGE if he were able to go — the Pats have managed him through practices so we’re not surprised to see him on the injury report, but a DNP on Friday is different than the norm for him. Backup RB Terrell Jennings (concussion) is questionable after two full practices on Thursday and Friday and could come off injured reserve tomorrow. Khyiris Tonga (foot) is not on the injury report at all after two full sessions. His return is great news for the New England run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.headline: Patriots designated RB Terrell Jennings (concussion) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.analysis: Jennings landed on injured reserve after suffering a concussion back in December. He handled short-yardage rushing duties from roughly Weeks 7-10, but burly RB Rhamondre Stevenson and rookie RB TreVeyon Henderson have seemingly established themselves as a reliable duo for head coach Mike Vrabel. Jennings is a nice backup to have active on game day, though. Jennings was limited on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Patriots RB Terrell Jennings (concussion) will be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/terrell-je.analysis: Jennings was already ruled out for Week 15’s matchup with the Bills, but now he’s set to miss the next four games after being placed on injured reserve. Jennings had already seen his role in the offense evaporate with the return of Rhamondre Stevenson. D’Ernest Johnson will serve as the Patriots’ third running back in Jennings’ absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: Elijah Arroyo (shoulder) underwent further testing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: No update yet on what was learned, and we may have to wait until next week’s first injury report to learn more. The Seahawks’ young tight end has faced multiple injuries in his short career. Hopefully, this one is not serious.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: Elijah Arroyo (arm) was taken to the locker room in the second quarter of week 6 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Arroyo was injured while trying to recover a Rashid Shaheed fumble in the second quarter and was promptly escorted to the locker room with trainers helping to stabilize his arm. It appeared to be a potential wrist or shoulder injury based on how the staff helped him off the field. The second-year tight end was not targeted prior to departing and appears to be on the wrong side of questionable to return to Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: AJ Barner caught 1-of-1 targets for eight yards in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals, adding one rush for one yard and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Up 24-7 on 4th-and-goal with just over three minutes left in the game, the Seahawks started a fresh set of downs from the Cardinals’ three-yard line. Both RB George Holani and RB Emanuel Wilson were given chances to punch it in before Seahawks OC Brian Fleury dialed up a Tush Push play for Barner on 4th-and-goal. Barner jumped up and across the line, bringing his fantasy stat line from something unusable to something we can live with. He remains a boom-bust TE1 against the Commanders next week. Seahawks TE2 Elijah Arroyo nabbed a 17-yard pass on a post route, but that was it for him. So far, the Seahawks’ reported uptick in usage for the tight end position has not panned out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: The Athletic’s Andrew Destin believes Seahawks TE AJ Barner “will likely see an uptick in production, as should backup TE Elijah Arroyo” this year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Destin notes that new Seahawks OC Brian Fleury served as the 49ers’ TE coach for four seasons “and is expected to feature the position prominently.” Aside from that, and an increase in shifts and motion, he thinks the offense is “going to look very similar” to last year. Barner underwent two offseason surgeries, one of which was to address a nagging ankle injury that Barner said he initially suffered during the 2024 Senior Bowl before the Seahawks drafted him. After turning in the PPR TE14 performance last season, Barner might have a shot to crack the position’s top 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: Seahawks TE Elijah Arroyo caught 2-of-3 targets for 50 yards and one touchdown in Sunday’s preseason game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Arroyo played three drives this evening, scoring from 36 yards out on the first one. Arroyo lined up in line on the left side, ran a route up the seam, shaking a safety along the way and easily hauled in the uncontested pass from tonight’s starting QB Drew Lock. Scoring against the Titans’ first-string defense is a plus, but playing while the rest of the Seahawks starters sat was not a great sign. Arroyo seems to be firmly behind TE AJ Barner on the depth chart right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler believes AJ Barner is an “ascending” player in the Seahawks offense.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Fowlers said the team expects Barner to be more involved as a pass catcher in 2026 after recording 52 receptions for 519 yards and six touchdowns last season (while being targeted on 19 percent of his routes). Barner, following multiple offseason surgeries to clean up nagging injuries, is fully healthy and ready for a more prominent role in Seattle’s offense. New Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury, meanwhile, is expected to use plenty of two tight end sets in 2026, meaning TE Elijah Arroyo could see an increase in snaps and routes. Barner has a little bit of extra hidden upside as the Seahawks’ primary tush push option near the goal line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: ESPN’s Brady Henderson reports TE Elijah Arroyo has been a standout through the first week of Seahawks training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: That apparently includes in both pad-less and padded practices. Henderson does add the same was true last summer before the then No. 50 overall pick went on to have a quiet rookie year. Arroyo dealt with knee issues after they were a red flag during his pre-draft process. Drafted in part to be an after-the-catch weapon, Arroyo could be left fighting for designed touches to begin the season. He is comfortably behind AJ Barner on both the depth chart and in average draft position. We’ll let you know if he keeps lighting up camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: Seahawks TE Elijah Arroyo (undisclosed) resumed practicing at mandatory minicamp on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald revealed on Wednesday that Arroyo was working through something, but was expected to be ready for training camp. Getting back early, even in a limited capacity, is good to see. Arroyo’s past few years, both in college and in his NFL rookie season, have been slowed by knee issues. Fellow backup TE Eric Saubert resumed practicing as well. Hopefully, both players are practicing fully before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: Seahawks TE Elijah Arroyo (undisclosed) is expected to be ready for training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Apparently, Arroyo and fellow TE Eric Saubert are not practicing this week. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said that “they’re just working through some stuff, but it’s positive for training camp.” Saubert is not expected to be fantasy-relevant, but this is a tad concerning for Arroyo, who entered the NFL as a 2025 rookie with injury-related concerns. Continued knee issues landed Arroyo on injured reserve last season. We hope to see him take the field at, or before, training camp next month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: Elijah Arroyo was held without a catch in the Seahawks’ Super Bowl LX victory over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Arroyo was not targeted as he made his postseason debut after battling a knee injury. The No. 50 overall pick of the draft, Arroyo ended up languishing behind second-year fourth-rounder AJ Barner. Arroyo caught more than two passes one time all year, and was a non-factor for the season’s stretch run. Arroyo is young (23 in April) at a complex position, but so is Barner. Arroyo’s draft pedigree means he should maintain some long-term benefit of the doubt in dynasty leagues, but 2026 seems unlikely to be the year he breaks out in fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold’s starting quarterback job is not in jeopardy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: The Seahawks’ head coach stood by his quarterback today, saying Darnold is “definitely part of the solution” to the offense’s recent struggles. Darnold returned somewhat quickly from a glute tendon strain a couple of weeks ago. One wonders if he is still rounding back into form following the early-season ailment. Backup Drew Lock played well in his stead, but the Seahawks believe their Super Bowl-winning quarterback should keep his job. That makes sense to us. He’s a QB2 next week against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 27-of-51 passes for 278 yards and two interceptions in the Seahawks’ 17-14, Week 6 loss to the Broncos, adding 19 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: The Seahawks struggled to move the football throughout against the tenacious situational play calling from Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, scoring only three points until just over five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. A late-game surge saw them punch on in and a successful two-point conversion drew the team within three points. They would stop the Broncos on the subsequent possession but an interception in Denver territory put the game in jeopardy. The defense would do their job and force a three-and-out that took only 15 seconds off the clock, giving the ball back to Darnold to lead a two-minute drill to send the game to overtime through a chip shot field goal. Darnold would throw his second interception in overtime, watching from the sideline as the Broncos walked it off with a 53-yard Will Lutz field goal. The loss sends the Seahawks to 3-3, matching the total number of losses from a season ago through only six weeks of the 2026 season. The Seahawks have work to do to make up ground in the NFC West, now 2.5 games behind the undefeated 49ers through the first third of the regular season. Darnold and the Seahawks now have a long week to prepare for the now-undefeated Chiefs at home in Week 7, where Darnold will be a fringe QB2 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 18-of-29 passes for 195 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Seahawks’ 32-29, Week 5 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: It was a rough outing for Darnold, who was picked off on his first pass attempt of the day and absorbed a season-high five sacks. His lone touchdown pass came on a 16-yard pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Darnold completed a short two-yard pass to JSN, who turned it upfield for the score to give the Seahawks the 23-21 lead with just over five minutes left in the third quarter.
