On the Seahawks’ final drive of the game, Darnold found JSN for a 35-yard completion, but three straight incompletions, including an uncharacteristic drop by JSN, put the Seahawks in a fourth-and-10 situation that they were unable to convert after Cooper Kupp came up a yard short on his second reception of the night. Darnold has now thrown seven touchdowns and six interceptions in his last three games since returning from injury, and now faces a short week to get ready for the Broncos on Thursday night. He profiles as a mid-to-low-end QB2 in what could be a tough road matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 13-of-22 passes for 168 yards with two touchdowns and an interception in the Seahawks’ 30-23, Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold’s first pass of the game was intercepted on a throw to the flat that should have gone basically anywhere else. He connected on a screen pass with Emanuel Wilson for his first score, and found Tory Horton on a short slant for his second. The 29-year-old wasn’t close to his best, but could enough against the less-than-spectacular Chargers’ defense. He’ll have a marquee matchup in Week 5 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 31-of-45 passes for 379 yards with four touchdowns and two interceptions in the Seahawks’ 33-31, Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: It was his first action since leaving in the first series of Week 1 against the Patriots with his hip/glute injury. Darnold’s first interception was a doink off a defensive lineman that landed in the hands of Sonny Styles. The second was an egregious offering that resulted in a pick six. Outside of that, the 29-year-old played relatively well, with two touchdown throws to Jaxon Smith-Njigba and another pair to Cooper Kupp and Eric Saubert. He’ll look to limit the turnovers and find JSN more often in Week 4 against the Chargers at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold upgraded to full participation yesterday, so today’s news tracks. In an interview on the Rich Eisen Show earlier today, Seahawks WR Smith-Njigba basically let slip that Darnold would be back, but Eisen let him out of the situation with only a soft follow-up. Darnold can be started as a borderline QB1/2 against a fantasy-friendly Commanders defense in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold said today that he is “striving” to play in Week 3 against the Commanders. It sounds like his striding is going well, too. The Seahawks’ starting quarterback is now seemingly on track to play on Sunday. Darnold’s strained glute tendon has healed faster than expected. If active, he can be treated as a high-end QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold was officially listed as a limited practice participant on Wednesday, returning to practice for the first time since his opening day injury. He split first-team reps with Drew Lock and did some throwing off to the side. The Seahawks will make a decision Friday on Darnold’s game status for Week 3 but the 29-year-old has an outside chance of returning against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said QB Sam Darnold (glute) will resume practicing, but won’t take every rep on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: This means Darnold will likely be listed as a limited participant today. The plan is to ramp him up as the week goes on, and Macdonald said the team would like to have a decision by Friday on whether Darnold will face the Commanders this week. The Seahawks’ quarterback has been sidelined since straining a glute tendon in Week 1. He will probably need to be treated as a QB2 with QB1 upside in his first game back, but his practice participation will clarify his readiness.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) “has a chance” to play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: To be clear, Rapoport’s tone was controlled and cautionary here. Darnold can only be considered questionable, at best. The Seahawks’ quarterback “is healing faster than anyone had imagined,” but Rapoport adds that the team wants to be “cautious” with him. Backup QB Drew Lock should probably be viewed as the presumptive Week 3 starter at this time, but it sounds like Darnold can reasonably be expected to play in Week 4 at the latest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: He got in a limited session and the Rams apparently trust him to play despite a pair of missed practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Colby Parkinson (shoulder) also avoided the final report. Tyler Higbee is the Rams tight end you should be using at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen remains out, and Parkinson (shoulder) remains limited. Tyler Higbee has played productively in the Rams’ No. 1 tight end role, and he should be expected to do so again this week against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen is dealing with a foot injury and is listed as a DNP on the Rams’ estimated practice report. Fellow tight end Colby Parkinson (shoulder) was listed as limited, though he has been dealing with the shoulder injury for a few weeks now and the Rams are likely managing his workload. Parkinson is trending to play. Allen’s potential absence may lead to the Rams activating rookie Max Klare to play alongside Parkinson and fantasy streaming option Tyler Higbee in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen is being evaluated for a concussion.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen has one catch for 13 yards, and likely is done for the day. The 25-year-old backup will need to clear protocol to play in Week 2 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Rams TE Davis Allen (quadricep) missed practice Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Speaking to media Monday, head coach Sean McVay relayed that it would be “some time” before Allen returns to the practice field considering the nature of the soft tissue injury. McVay added, “You don’t want to rush him back, Davis is going to be a big part of what we do this year.” Allen set career highs in his third professional season in 2025, catching 24 passes for 208 yards and three touchdowns, ranking second on the team in offensive snaps behind only Colby Parkinson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: ESPN’s Matt Bowen believes TE Kenyon Sadiq could be a “matchup player” in the Rams offense.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Sadiq out of Oregon is widely expected to be a first round pick after setting record at the NFL Combine. Bowen believes the hyper-athletic tight end could be a situation matchup player for Sean McVay, who used three tight end sets at the NFL’s highest rate in 2025. “With his frame and 4.39 speed, Sadiq could be a seam stretcher for quarterback Matthew Stafford. Plus, McVay could use Sadiq as a backside X receiver/power slot to draw favorable man matchups.” Sadiq, who had 80 receptions over three seasons at Oregon, could fit the LA offense “as a catch-and-run target on boot action concepts,” Bowen said. Stafford last season led the NFL with 75 pass attempts on designed rollouts. It’s a crowded tight end room in LA, with Colby Parikson, Tyler Higbee, Terrance Ferguson, and Davis Allen on the roster. Sadiq would likely function as a rotational player if he lands with the Rams, who have the 13th pick in the 2026 draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen was not targeted in Los Angeles’ NFC Championship loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen went untargeted in the playoffs despite a strong snap share — he’s clearly the blocking tight end of the four-headed 3TE attack the Rams run. He enters the final year of his rookie contract in 2026 looking like a solid use of a roster spot for the Rams and someone fantasy managers should never, ever call on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen caught 3-of-4 targets for 16 yards in Los Angeles’ Week 15 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen finished with 54 snaps, just behind Terrance Ferguson (1/6 with a missed connection deep shot) at 56 for the lead amongst non-Colby Parkinson tight ends. It feels like Ferguson is the more likely of the two to erupt in any given week, while Allen is the one that delivers this floor that’s slightly above ground. You don’t want this floor for fantasy purposes. But here it is.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Colby Parkinson caught 4-of-5 targets for 41 yards and a touchdown in Los Angeles’ Week 10 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: The Rams have created an incredible situation where none of their tight ends are actually fantasy-reliable, but all of them are threats to score off play-action in jumbo packages. Parkinson (39 snaps), Tyler Higbee (3/33, 36 snaps), Davis Allen (2/8/1, 35 snaps) and Terrance Ferguson (1/32, 22 snaps) are all potential TE2 plays right now given the situation. It’s impossible to figure out which of them will blow up every week given the playing time split.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen caught 3-of-4 targets for 37 yards in the Rams’ Week 9 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Although the Rams secured the win, Allen had a rough day. The young tight end scored on a play-action catch-and-run sequence on the Rams’ fifth drive, but the touchdown was called back after referees viewed the replay, which clearly showed Allen stiff-arming his way down the field by pushing his would-be tackler’s facemask back and forth as the two strode together through the red zone. Rams K Joshua Klarty missed the ensuing field goal attempt wide right by a significant margin. Allen later helped fellow TE Tyler Higbee score a touchdown from one yard out by catching the defense’s attention going in motion pre-snap. Rams TE Colby Parkinson caught 2-of-2 targets for 10 yards as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.headline: Lions placed Ben Bartch on injured reserve with a foot injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.analysis: The Lions lose one of their top backup offensive lineman and LB Devin White (forearm) to injured reserve. Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters post-game last week that White would likely require surgery.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.headline: Lions declared OG Ben Bartch, CB Rock Ya-Sin, TE Jackson Meeks, S Bishop Fitzgerald, DL Mekhi Wingo and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein inactive for Week 5 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.analysis: Slowed by a foot injury, Bartch, one of the Lions’ better backup offensive linemen, will be unavailable today. Fortunately, the Lions’ offensive line health is improving and stud C Cade Mays (wrist) could return in a week or two. The Lions will also be without Ya-Sin, one of two starting perimeter cornerbacks and S Brian Branch (Achilles) is not yet ready to resume playing. This should be a high-scoring game environment, though DL Tyleik Williams (foot) is active.l

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.headline: Lions RT Blake Miller (knee) is not on the injury report for Week 3 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.analysis: Lions LG Christian Mahogany (hip) will also make his return after a week-long absence, and RG Tate Ratledge (elbow) is good to go after two limited sessions early in the week. The Lions’ starting offensive line’s health is improving. Backup OG Ben Bartch (foot) has been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.headline: Lions signed G Ben Bartch, formerly of the 49ers, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.analysis: Bartch has started games in each of the last two seasons for the 49ers, but has spent a lot of time on injured reserve and hasn’t been able to take advantage of chances to win a full-time role. The Lions will add him as depth and hope he can stay healthy. Bartch has respectable PFF grades of 71.7 and 74.8 in his last two seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.headline: 49ers ruled out EDGE Bryce Huff (hamstring) in Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.analysis: The 49ers also ruled out EDGE Yetur Gross-Matos (hamstring) and C Jake Brendel (hamstring), while labeling DT Jordan Elliott (ankle/personal matter), LB Dee Winters (knee), DL Sam Okuayinonu (ankle), OG Ben Bartch (ankle) and OL Spencer Burford (knee) questionable for Week 9. The 49ers’ defense is officially one to target for fantasy purposes and their poor health should also reinforce the offense’s passing volume.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.headline: 49ers signed OL Brandon Parker, formerly of the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.analysis: The 49ers correspondingly placed OG Ben Bartch on injured reserve with an ankle injury and promoted TE Brayden Willis from the practice squad. Parker was a liability as a run blocker and pass protector but the former 2018 third-round pick is at least an experienced veteran.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said OL Ben Bartch (ankle) will be out “for a while.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.analysis: Bartch suffered a high-ankle sprain and was replaced by Connor Colby, a seventh-round pick from Iowa who played fairly well in his debut. It sounds like Bartch will be headed to injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.headline: 49ers LG Ben Bartch was forced from San Francisco’s Week 2 game against the Saints with an ankle injury and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.analysis: Bartch was deemed “questionable” before the break but never returned. A fill-in for an already banged up offense line, Bartch’s loss further thins San Francisco’s shaky depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said G Dominick Puni (knee) is “iffy” for Week 1.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.analysis: Puni suffered a PCL sprain in San Francisco’s second preseason game. The 49ers signed G Michael Dunn on Wednesday, so it’s clear that they’re at least making sure they can get through their third preseason game with some healthy guards as Ben Bartch (elbow) also is currently shelved. If Puni does miss time, Shanahan mentioned Spencer Burford as a potential fill-in at guard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.headline: 49ers activated OL Ben Bartch (quad) from the non-football injury list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-bartch.analysis: Per ESPN’s Nick Wagoner, Bartch “jumped right into team periods at left guard with the first unit.” He will compete with OL Nick Zakelj for the role, though Wagoner believes the team hopes Bartch secures the job quickly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Budda Baker (groin) is questionable for Arizona’s Week 6 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: It was a pop-up DNP for Baker on Friday after he had initially been listed as NIR-Rest on Wednesday. Ominous. Baker stands a real chance at missing Sunday’s game and throwing the Cardinals defense into (checking notes) further chaos against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals HC Jonathan Gannon said Budda Baker (concussion) will not play in Week 17 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker entered the league’s concussion protocol earlier this week after going down in Week 16’s game against the Falcons. The star safety will miss at least one game due to his brain injury, with backup safety Kitan Crawford looking like the next man up to fill his role. In addition to Baker, the Cardinals also ruled out LT Paris Johnson (knee), and CB Kei’Tre Clark (knee) for Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals S Budda Baker entered the NFL’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker was evaluated for a brain injury in Week 16 against the Falcons but re-entered the game, only to report concussion-like symptoms on Wednesday. Baker is likely to sit out this week against the Bengals, creating an even better matchup for Joe Burrow and the Bengals pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals S Budda Baker returned to Week 16 against the Falcons after being evaluated for a concussion.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker remained down after making a tackle and took a minute to make his way to the sideline. After meeting with the training staff on the sideline, he jogged to the locker room for the concussion evaluation. After a short time, he was able to return to the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals S Budda Baker (hamstring) is active for Week 10 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker was limited through most of the week in practice but will suit up against Seattle after practicing in full on Friday. Cardinals declared OT Josh Fryar, OT Demontrey Jacobs, CB Will Johnson, CB Max Melton, DT Bilal Nichols, WR Xavier Weaver, and LB Mack Wilson inactive against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals CB Will Johnson (back/hip) will not play in Arizona’s Week 10 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Neither will (inhale): CB Max Melton (concussion), LB BJ Ojulari (knee), or LB Mack Wilson (ribs) — the good news is that Budda Baker (hamstring) upgraded to full today and has been removed from the injury report. Arizona’s defense looked good against the Cowboys on Monday night, but their cornerback depth will be tested against Jaxson Smith-Njigba and Rashid Shaheed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals trained were seen examining WR Michael Wilson (head) and S Budda Baker (shin) after the two players collided in practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Per AZ Central Sports’ Theo Mackie, Baker appeared to pass his exam and attempted to resume practicing before DC Nick Rallis talked him out of it. Wilson left the field with training staffers and will undergo further examination.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals signed S Budda Baker to a three-year, $54 million extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: The Cardinals sign Baker for $18 million per year, the third largest among safeties in NFL history. The $54 million total includes $30 million guaranteed over three years for the 28-year-old. Baker is a two-time first-team All-Pro, one-time second-team All-Pro, and six-time Pro Bowler initially drafted by the Cardinals in the second round of the 2017 NFL Draft. He has been an every-day starter since 2018 and has tallied 879 combined tackles, 9.5 sacks, and seven interceptions over eight seasons. Baker is having another solid season and the Cardinals get him signed through 2027 before his impending free agency in the offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals S Budda Baker (illness) is questionable for Week 15 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker was added to the injury report on Sunday morning. We expect him to play through the issue, though we won’t know definitively until 90 minutes before kickoff. Baker has 58 tackles and three TFLs in eight games this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals activated S Budda Baker from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker will make his much anticipated return to the active roster against the division rival Seahawks in Week 7 after missing the previous four games with a hamstring injury. The Cardinals started the season with two solid defensive showings against the Commanders and during the first half of their game against the Giants, largely failing to adjust to life without Baker since. He will bring a needed jolt to head coach Jonathan Gannon’s modified two-high-shallow defensive shell that asks a lot of its safeties.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs (hamstring/rest) is not on Indianapolis’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Given how Downs’ season is going, it’s hard to believe he’s going to do much with the extra runway, but Tyler Warren (groin) popping up on the report could shift more targets to Downs and Keenan Allen on Sunday against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs (hamstring/rest) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: The good news is that it looks like Downs is trending towards getting off the injury report on Friday. The bad news is that it’s hard to make much more than a WR3 case for the receiver given how bogged down Indianapolis’ passing offense looks at the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs (hamstring/rest) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Typically, rest days are entirely inconsequential. Recently, the Colts listed Keenan Allen with a rest designation on Wednesday. He picked up a groin injury during the practice week, and although they added the groin injury to the injury report, they kept the rest designation on there as well. He didn’t play. Downs could end up being perfectly fine, but given the Colts’ recent handling of a similar situation, his participation levels on Thursday and Friday are worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 3-of-6 targets for 47 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: The good news is that Downs ran a route on 44 of the Colts’ 47 dropbacks. He was also targeted down the field a few times. The bad news is that Daniel Jones was not effective and hasn’t been throughout the season. Downs did have another 15-yard completion called back due to a penalty away from the ball, but it wouldn’t have made a huge difference in his day. Downs is still on the WR3 radar because the Colts play the Titans next week, but until Jones can get it going, it’s hard to trust anybody other than Tyler Warren in this passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 3-of-4 targets for 16 yards in the Colts’ Week 4 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: With Alec Pierce and IR and Keenan Allen ruled out, this was supposed to be Downs’ breakout performance. Instead, Downs went missing for most of the game. He caught two passes in the first quarter, another in the second, and did not touch the ball again for the remaining 35 minutes of the contest. Downs finished fourth on the team in targets and was used primarily for check-down duties, though that’s all Daniel Jones was capable of today. Downs should still be treated as the team’s No. 1 receiver for Week 5 versus Pittsburgh, but his stranglehold on the targets is at least in question now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) is questionable for Week 4 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: This one went under the radar. Allen was limited on Wednesday with a “rest” designation. He remained limited on Thursday, but the Colts tacked a groin injury next to his name while maintaining the “rest” designation and hope for a Week 4 appearance along the way. Allen was downgraded on Friday, unable to practice, and should be considered truly questionable to face the Commanders this week. Were he to sit, No. 1 wide receiver Josh Downs would get a helpful target share boost.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 5-of-11 targets for 77 yards in Indianapolis’ Week 3 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: This target boost brought to you by Alec Pierce’s heel injury. The Colts didn’t really land any deep targets but they pounded the Texans’ middle-of-field zone coverages and Downs was a main beneficiary. He’ll be in the WR3 ranks next week against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Colts placed Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Pierce will be sidelined for at least four weeks after suffering the injury in Week 2 against Kansas City. Pierce had seen 19 percent of the Colts’ targets and 53 percent of the team’s air yards in Week 1 against the Ravens, resuming his role as a strictly-downfield pass catcher. With Pierce out, Josh Downs should have every chance to operate as the Colts’ No. 1 wideout while Tyler Warren sees a bump in targets. Laquon Treadwell is likely to take over as the team’s lone deep threat. Treadwell can be picked up in 14-team fantasy formats ahead of the Colts’ Week 3 matchup with the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 7-of-9 targets for 72 yards in the Colts’ Week 2 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Downs operated as the unquestioned top dog through the air following the first quarter departure of Alec Pierce, the latter of whom left with a heel injury on the same foot as his offseason surgery. That setup appears likely to continue should Pierce miss time, although the short-area nature of Downs’ role all but requires significant volume to return scores beyond WR3 production. Even so, Downs should mostly avoid the lockdown perimeter corners of the Texans in Week 3, where he will be an upside WR3 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 2-of-4 targets for 37 yards in the Colts’ Week 1 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Both of Downs’ catches came on the Colts’ opening drive. The fourth-year receiver looked explosive on his first reception when he turned a short catch into a 25-yard gain to move his team into Ravens territory, and he picked up another 12 yards through the air two plays later. Three of Downs’ four targets came on that drive, as he managed just one target the rest of the way. Downs’ drop-off after the opening possession largely stemmed from the Colts’ inability to move the ball. They averaged just 4.2 yards per play after that first drive and totaled only 107 passing yards over that span. The early targets were encouraging. Hopefully Downs will be in line for a better outing in Week 2 against the Chiefs. He shouldn’t be treated as anything more than a WR3 in next week’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) is questionable for Indianapolis’ Week 6 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren popped up on the injury report on Friday after suffering the injury in practice. Fantasy managers who were relying on Warren likely won’t find a good enough option to replace him with proactively on waivers at this point, so it makes some sense to sit and wait for more reporting to come out or for him to be ruled out. This was, frankly, the last thing the Colts needed given how banged up their receiving corps has been.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren caught 7-of-9 targets for 83 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren also added a one-yard touchdown run on a tush push after Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones were stuffed on the previous three plays. The second-year tight end ran a route on 40 of the team’s 47 dropbacks and shared the team lead in targets with Keenan Allen. Daniel Jones is keeping the ceiling of this passing game in check with his inefficient play, but Warren is probably the most reliable receiver on the team and remains a TE1. He just lacks the upside to push inside the top five at the position unless Jones can get going.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren caught all five of his targets for 41 yards in the Colts’ Week 4 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren tied for a team high in catches but was out-targeted by Laquon Treadwell and Ashton Dulin. If you couldn’t tell, the passing attack did not look good. Daniel Jones was horribly inaccurate and the Commanders were largely successful in slowing down Warren and Josh Downs. Better days should be ahead for Warren, but he’s averaging a dismal 32.5 yards per game right now. He’s falling to the back of the TE1 ranks ahead of Indy’s Week 5 date with Pittsburgh.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren caught 9-of-10 passes for 55 yards in Indianapolis’ Week 3 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: With Alec Pierce gone, the targets heavily concentrated to Warren and Josh Downs. Warren, still an extension of the run game, just doesn’t look like he’s going to generate much yardage on his catches unless he breaks a tackle. But the PPR points all count the same, and nine catches at tight end is nine catches at tight end. He’ll remain on the TE1 line against the Commanders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren caught 6-of-7 targets for 21 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 2 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: The seven targets and a score look nice in the box scores, but it is hard to overlook just how reliant Warren is on screens and leak concepts in this offense, almost all of which are built behind play action. That’s good news for fantasy managers when the ground game is cooking, as it was against the Chiefs, but we’ve also seen how ineffective it can be when the Colts aren’t able to control games as they did to start the 2025 season. Losers of nine straight games dating back to last season, Warren could struggle to return enough yardage to truly emerge as a locked-in TE1 until this team starts winning some games. His performance against the Chiefs now marks consecutive games with 21 yards or fewer, although a touchdown in each contest has kept his fantasy value afloat. He’ll be a difficult start against the lockdown Houston defense in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren caught 3-of-5 targets for 13 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 1 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren’s underwhelming line can be blamed on the offense’s struggle to move the ball all afternoon. The second-year tight end tallied two receptions in the first half, both for two yards, with his longest play coming on a nine-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. His five targets were good for second-most on the team, but the Colts offense left a lot to be desired this week. The expected volume will keep Warren in the TE1 mix for Week 2 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Alec Pierce (heel) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Pierce is recovering from offseason surgery that caused him to miss the entirety of training camp and the preseason. The lack of reps could leave him a little rusty heading into Week 1, but the good news is that a limited practice today means he should be active versus the Ravens. Pierce will be a high-risk WR4 for the first slate of the season. Josh Downs and Tyler Warren were not on the injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) practiced Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren is recovering from an apparently minor groin injury. By all accounts he should be a full go for Week 1. Warren last season was top three among tight ends in targets per route run and first-read target rate in the balanced Colts offense. He’ll offer a sturdy weekly floor and could lead the team in targets in 2026 if he stays healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Colts TE Tyler Warren (groin) “is going to be ready for” Week 1 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Rapoport believes Warren will resume practicing in “a week or so.” He also expects “Warren’s role to grow” in his second NFL season. That makes sense. Warren’s 106 targets trailed only WR Michael Pittman’s 110. Pittman left Indy to join the Steelers this offseason, clearing the way for Warren to be the team’s top target earner. The soft-tissue injury adds some risk to Warren’s profile, but he should still be drafted as a mid-to-high TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen confirmed TE Tyler Warren suffered a groin injury on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Steichen adds that the team will be cautious with Warren’s recovery, but chose not to share details regarding the injury’s severity beyond that. If healthy, the second-year tight end is a candidate to lead the team in targets this season after racking up 106 as a rookie. The Colts’ pass-catching corps is in a tough spot, with WR Alec Pierce (ankle) still sidelined. If Warren cannot play in Week 1, WR Josh Downs would presumably handle a sizable target share, operating as the team’s clear-cut No. 1 target earner. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 6 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears didn’t practice Thursday but was a full-go on Friday. He’ll be a sketchy FLEX option against the Colts in Week 6 assuming he plays; it sure does seem like he will after a full session.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: It was a surprising downgrade from Wednesday’s limited session, putting Spears’ status for Week 6 into real question. If he sits, we’re not entirely sure which Titans third-string back would get breather duties. Kalel Mullings, who was a practice squad activation, got the only non-Tony Pollard/Spears snap in Week 5. Nicholas Singleton and Michael Carter are also both on the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: The Titans’ receiving specialist has been an injury report staple thus far, though he has previously been listed with an ankle issue. An early-week limited session puts him on track to play, though he is only relevant in PPR leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears rushed two times for zero yards, adding nine catches for 28 yards on nine targets, in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: He fumbled away one of his rushes, but with the Titans trailing for most of the second half, piled up nine catches as Cam Ward sought refuge from Houston’s pass rush. His final catch of the day — we’re not kidding — came as Ward threw it at him despite Spears having already crumpled to the ground. It lost six yards. Given the Colts likely won’t do this against the Titans next week, Spears is probably not going to keep lines like this going.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears rushed two times for seven yards in the Titans’ Week 4 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears also caught his lone target for what resulted in a one-yard loss. It was yet another underwhelming game for Spears, who has totaled a combined 40 yards from scrimmage in his last two games on eight touches. There’s nothing of fantasy value here. Spears can be left off the fantasy radar for Week 5’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (ankle) is active for Week 4 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears is good to go for Sunday’s game against the Ravens after entering the weekend listed as questionable. He has totaled 99 scoreless yards from scrimmage this season on 17 touches, and has caught four passes on the year. Spears shouldn’t be considered as anything more than a fringe RB3/RB4 against a stout Ravens defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tyjae Spears (ankle) is expected to play in Week 4 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears played through the ankle issue last week and there was no indication during this week’s practice that he suffered any sort of setback. He is good to go for Week 4, though fantasy managers can’t count on him for much. He touched the ball just three times last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 4 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears played through the injury last week. This week, he went DNP, LP and FP, so he is seemingly on track to play. Regardless, he is a low-floor, touchdown-dependent FLEX against the Ravens this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: It’s a little better than he did last week, when Spears only made it on to the practice field on Friday with this same ankle listing. It’s plausible he gets off the questionable line on Friday, but it certainly wouldn’t be surprising if he was listed there again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tony Pollard (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Neither did Tyjae Spears, who is also dealing with an ankle issue. Both backs played through their injuries last week and head coach Robert Saleh said today that he isn’t concerned about either of them missing Week 4. The Titans held them out of last Wednesday’s practice as well, so this seems to be the new norm for the backfield tandem. Pollard remains a volume-based RB3 after seeing 21 touches last week. Spears is nothing more than a backup right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eli Stowers (quad) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers is only notable because of his draft capital. The second-round rookie has not carved out a role for himself and would not be fantasy-relevant if the Eagles activate him from injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eli Stowers (quad) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers had his 21-day practice window opened after he started the season on the injured reserve due to hamstring and quad injury. The Eagles also opened fellow TE Grant Calcaterra’s practice window; Calcaterra was also limited due to a back injury. Both have a chance to return Week 6 against the Panthers or Week 7 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eagles placed TE Eli Stowers (hamstring, quad) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers entered his rookie season unlikely to contribute in a meaningful way but will now be forced to miss the next four games, at minimum, while on injured reserve, something that could stunt his growth at the professional level further. Dallas Goedert remains a locked-in TE1 in fantasy circles moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eagles TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) is questionable for Week 1 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers is listed as the Eagles’ co-TE3, so even if he is absent, that will not be a huge deal. The team is undoubtedly hoping he develops over the course of the season, so tracking his recovery is worthwhile. For now, though, TE Dallas Goedert is the clear-cut tight end to roster in Philadelphia.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eagles TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers had a rough training camp and has been sidelined since late August by the hamstring injury. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eagles TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers has been dealing with a hamstring injury he suffered in the preseason and he opens Week 1 with a limited practice. The 23-year-old rookie was already in line for a limited role this season after a subpar training camp but now may be limited even further with a soft tissue injury. Stowers is off fantasy radars in redraft leagues but his absence propels Dallas Goedert into borderline top-10 tight end territory.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eagles TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) missed his second straight practice Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers missed his second straight practice Tuesday as he deals with a hamstring issue. There is no indication this is a major injury yet, but something to keep an eye on as the Eagles prepare for preseason Week 3. The rookie second-round pick has struggled in camp and comes into the NFL as a raw tight end prospect. Don’t expect the Eagles’ tight end rotation to change drastically should Stowers miss time in the 2026 regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: Eli Stowers caught all three targets for 12 yards in Saturday’s preseason game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers was somewhat involved in the first half but the rookie tight end had a long gain of just six yards in the first exhibition game of the season. The 23-year-old has significant long-term upside because of his athleticism, but it’s very clear — at least early on — that Stowers has work to do before he’s a fantasy option in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: The Athletic’s Brooks Kubena reports that Eagles TE Eli Stowers “has yet to move up the depth chart.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Stowers is reportedly still working with the third-team offense. The rookie tight end has been a late-round target for best ball drafters hoping to secure late-season production from their TE3. While that outcome is still possible, it would be nice to see Stowers gain a little ground this month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.headline: The Philly Voice’s Jimmy Kempski reports the Eagles TE Dallas Goedert and TE Johnny Mundt “are clearly ahead” of rookie TE Eli Stowers on the depth chart.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eli-stower.analysis: Kempski believes Mundt’s blocking ability keeps him in the TE2 spot for now. He also notes that “Stowers was quiet during spring practices, and even seemed limited in practice due to an injury,” sporting a sleeve on one leg. Missing spring practice reps would certainly slow down a rookie’s development. Regardless, if Stowers is going to show up in the box score, he will likely do so late in the 2026 season. For now, treat him as a worthwhile best ball TE3, and a name to know for late-season waiver wire purposes in re-draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.headline: Drew Kendall (knee) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.analysis: Kendall, the Eagles’ starting center, and LG Landon Dickerson (knee) were both limited on Friday, resulting in questionable game tags. Dickerson remains on injured reserve. The team would need to activate him, if he is going to play. Eagles EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle) was cleared to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.headline: Drew Kendall (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.analysis: The Eagles’ starting center now has a chance to play in Week 6 against the Panthers. Eagles LG Landon Dickerson (knee) was also limited again, as was EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.headline: Eagles activated LG Landon Dickerson’s (knee) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.analysis: The Eagles desperately need offensive line health. Dickerson’s return cannot come soon enough. New Eagles C Drew Kendall (knee) was not seen practicing today, though Dickerson has officially resumed practicing in some capacity, which is great news. He was seen taking the field with his teammates this afternoon. The Eagles also opened DB Jakorian Bennett, TE Grant Calcaterra and TE Eli Stowers’ (hamstring/quad) practice windows.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.headline: Eagles C Drew Kendall (knee) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 5 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.analysis: Kendall will leave the center position to practice squad C Jake Majors, who will join Willie Lampkin as Cam Jurgens’ replacement at guard. Just two players who have never started in the NFL before. What could go wrong?

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.headline: Eagles C Drew Kendall (knee) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.analysis: With C Cam Jurgens now a Raven, Kendall is the Eagles’ starting center. Unfortunately, he is not practicing this week, leaving practice squad C/OG Jake Majors as his potential Week 5 fill-in. Potential starting OT Fred Johnson (knee) is practicing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.headline: Eagles declared QB Sam McKee, DE Azeez Ojulari, RB Will Shipley, DE Ogbo Okoronkwo, LB Patrick Johnson, OL Drew Kendall and OL Kenyon Green inactive for Week 3 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.analysis: McKee will be the third QB for the tilt against Los Angeles, with Sam Howell operating as the backup to Jalen Hurts. Shipley is out with an oblique injury, paving the way for Tank Bigsby and A.J. Dillon — not necessarily in that order — to get the carries behind bellcow Saquon Barkley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.headline: Eagles selected Boston College C Drew Kendall with the No. 168 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.analysis: Kendall (6’4/308) started 31 consecutive games at center for Boston College. He stands out as a pass blocker, is quick off the ball, and has good awareness, peeling off from one guy to the other. He posted an 81.5 PFF grade as a pass blocker, giving up just one sack and two QB hits in 2024. He does tend to have late reactions when his opponents come at him quickly, which causes Kendall to panic and get pushed around a bit. As a run blocker, Kendall is quick off the ball and is physical, posting a 75.9 PFF grade. He’s aggressive when he pulls and shows a high motor off the ball. Kendall does well as a zone blocker. He has fluid hips and shows a good amount of upper body strength; however, there are times where Kendall isn’t as physical in zone blocking schemes, causing him to lose leverage. Overall, Kendall is more of a mid round prospect, but he brings plenty of experience to the table, and his skill set would make a good depth piece on an NFL team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.headline: Boston College received a verbal commitment from four-star 2021 OL Drew Kendall.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.analysis: Kendall was coveted by just about every program in the eastern half of the States. Michigan, Duke, Penn State, Virginia, and a slew of others all seemed to be high on Kendall’s priority list. In the end, it was Jeff Hafley and Boston College who swung in to secure Kendall. At 6-foot-4 and 255-pounds, Kendall is too light to play right away, but the hope is that a year or two in a good weight program will get him into good shape for the FBS.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.headline: Rivals’ Adam Friedman writes that Michigan looks to have a “commanding lead” for uncommitted four-star 2021 G Drew Kendall.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.analysis: “Michigan has done a great job showing consistent interest in [Kendall] along with building a very strong relationship with him and his family,” Friedman writes of the 6-foot-4, 255-pounder while adding that he has “even been in touch with teachers at the school to make sure he feels comfortable with the academic plan at Michigan.” Looking beyond the Wolverines in the pole position, Friedman ranks the other contenders (in order) as Stanford, Boston College and Penn State. Duke and Virginia are also potentially in play as dark horses, here. Rivals ranks the Boston native as the No. 65 overall prospect in the 2021 class.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.headline: Uncommitted four-star 2021 G Drew Kendall will take an unofficial visit to Duke on March 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-kenda.analysis: Kendall (6'4/255) initially planned on visiting Duke prior to the February dead period, but ended up rescheduling for March. Michigan, UVA and Stanford could also see spring visits from the Dedham, Massachusetts, native, though nothing is set in stone on those fronts as of yet. While Kendall will need to add a fair bit of weight for the rigors of college ball, he already plays with palatable attitude and physicality. On the 247Sports composite board, Kendall slots in as the No. 62 overall prospect in the 2021 class.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney (neck) is not on New York’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney turned seven targets into 14 yards last week and does not need to be trusted to do better this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney (neck) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney’s participation puts him on track to face the Saints in Week 6. He does not need to be in 12-team lineups, and his presence, unfortunately, keeps Malachi Fields from potentially playing in a full-time role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney (neck) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: He still has multiple practices left to improve his status. If Mooney were to miss time, Malachi Fields, who is tied with him for third on the team in targets, could see his role expand, though target volume could be limited behind Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney caught 2-of-3 targets for 26 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney has exactly two catches in each of his first three games as a Giant. He has hit on a few chunk plays in New York but isn’t seeing enough targets to be a weekly fantasy option. He is not on the FLEX radar for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney caught 2-of-3 targets for 48 yards in the Giants’ Week 2 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney played well behind Malik Nabers and rookie Malachi Fields but was able to cash in on a 33-yard reception to pad his counting stats in the loss. Fantasy managers of Nabers will want to track his status closely in the coming week after the talented youngster briefly departed with a shoulder injury. An absence could thrust Mooney into a near every-down role against the Titans in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: The rookie wide receiver showcased a polished all-around skillset, reinforcing offseason reports that he had locked down the WR2 role opposite Malik Nabers. His 6'4, 220-pound frame was on full display as he was continually utilized as both a down-blocker and blocker in the second level on runs, something that should allow him to continue to operate as the clear-cut WR2 for the Giants throughout his rookie campaign. That said, the box scores highlights the obvious distinction that his snap rate — he led all Giants wideouts with 50 — won’t always translate to fantasy production while playing alongside Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely, the latter two of whom commanded 17 targets on 29 Jaxson Dart pass attempts. The good news is that he played well ahead of veterans Darnell Mooney and Odell Beckham Jr., with Mooney having 39 snaps and Beckham just 11. Fantasy managers are best off viewing Fields as a high-end stash at the end of benches for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: North Jersey’s Art Stapleton believes Giants WR Darnell Mooney and WR Calvin Austin “will get chances” to compete for targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: This is not much of an endorsement. With Giants WR Malik Nabers (knee) and WR Darius Slayton (core muscle) sidelined by recent surgeries, Mooney and Austin are reportedly earning targets behind TE Isaiah Likely and TE Theo Johnson at organized team activities. Mooney ($10 million) and Austin ($4.5 million) signed one-year deals with the Giants in free agency. Nothing Stapleton “saw today would indicate that there’s no room” for free agent WR Odell Beckham Jr. in this wide receiver group. Avoiding the Giants’ healthy wide receivers in spring drafts is a prudent call.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Giants agreed to terms with WR Darnell Mooney, formerly of the Falcons, on a one-year, $10 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: This one is a bit head-scratching. Mooney’s skillset seems to carry significant overlap with returning veteran Darius Slayton, the latter of whom recently signed a new three-year deal that ties him to the franchise through 2027. Mooney did play from the slot at a 41% frequency a season ago and the team saw Wan’Dale Robinson walk in free agency, although Mooney will have to compete with veteran holdover Isaiah Hodgins and recent signee Calvin Austin for snaps inside, if that is the vision from the team. The size of the contract seems to indicate he will have a legitimate role in the offense in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Falcons released WR Darnell Mooney.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Ian Rapoport was first on the news, which will be made official before the new league year next week. Atlanta saves $7.4 million in cap space with his release. Mooney looked like a steal one year into his three-year, $39 million contract. He went for 992 yards and five scores in 2024. The wheels then fell off in 2025 and he managed just 443 yards and one score on 32 grabs. Mooney dealt with several injuries, but his drops and overall inconsistent play were too much for Atlanta to keep him around this year. He should still have several suitors in free agency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney caught 3-of-7 targets for 20 yards in the Falcons’ Week 18 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: It was a fitting end to a disastrous, injury-marred campaign for the 28-year-old after he flirted with 1,000 yards a season ago, his first in Atlanta. This time around, Mooney finishes with 443 yards in 15 games, and as one of the league’s least-efficient wideouts. He averaged under a yard per route, a ghastly number for a player on the field as much as Mooney. Mooney will blame his summer collarbone break and in-season soft-tissue issues, but it’s never a good sign when injuries are your alibi, especially at Mooney’s advancing age. Out of guaranteed money and due a preposterous $10.97 million in 2026, Mooney will either be released or restructured.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Apparently, Wicks’ day off on Thursday was only a rest day. The Eagles’ veteran wide receiver was limited on Wednesday and practiced fully today. Wicks played through the injury last week, posting a 5/63 receiving line with DeVonta Smith sidelined. Smith is back this week. Wicks is a boom-bust FLEX starter, catching passes thrown by backup Tanner McKee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks played through the hamstring injury in Week 5 and may have made it worse. Downgrading to a DNP on Thursday is a bad sign. He is unlikely to play at this time, and if active, he would be prone to re-injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks suffered the hamstring injury in practice last week but played through the injury in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars. Also limited was Hollywood Brown (ankle). Brown has not played since suffering an ankle injury in Week 2 but has a chance to return this week. Expect Wicks to play in Week 6 while Brown is truly questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks caught 5-of-8 targets for 63 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: DeVonta Smith was out again this week, leaving the Eagles to spread his targets around to several role players. Wicks led the team’s wideouts in targets, but it was Dallas Goedert who paced the team. On the back of one long touchdown catch, Darius Cooper led the team in receiving yards. Wicks is good for the occasional big play but isn’t a consistent enough player to be a solid fantasy option. He will be a deep FLEX option for Week 6 versus the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: He only got in a limited session today, but apparently that was all the Eagles needed to see. He’ll still be a tough start against Jacksonville in what is projected to be a low-scoring game as Philadelphia’s passing offense looks to rebound from last week’s rough showing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks was listed as a limited participant today, indicating that he strained his hamstring during Thursday’s practice. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) still sidelined, rookie WR Makai Lemon could be the de facto top receiver, though the team has struggled to use him effectively thus far. Hollywood Brown (ankle) also remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks caught 3-of-5 targets for 18 yards in the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks was in theory the Eagles’ No. 1 receiver with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) sidelined, but in reality he does not really have a “scaleable” skill-set. It wasn’t surprising Wicks and Jalen Hurts failed to get anything going down the field with the Rams constantly in Hurts’ grill in rainy conditions. Smith seems to be looking at a multi-week absence, but Wicks will be hard-pressed to rise above WR4 status in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: ESPN’s Tim McManus reports that the Eagles are preparing to play without DeVonta Smith (hamstring) in Week 4 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: The Eagles limited Smith’s practice reps last week, and he successfully suited up on game day, nabbing 6-of-8 targets for 65 yards. Apparently, the performance took a toll. The Eagles will likely be without their No. 1 wide receiver this week. Dontayvion Wicks will fill in as the team’s top receiver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks caught 2-of-5 targets for 32 yards in the Eagles’ Week 3 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: For his part, Wicks was consistently breaking free of coverage with smooth route-running ability, but the offense managed just over 23 minutes time of possession on 47 offensive plays, leaving all involved stuck on a sinking ship. Better fantasy days should be ahead for Wicks in the immediate future, at least for as long as tight end Dallas Goedert remains sidelined with an MCL sprain. That said, he draws a difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 4. Treat Wicks as a viable FLEX option in a tough spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Eagles WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: This is unfortunate. Smith dealt with a hamstring injury back in August, but rehabbed it successfully before the season began. The Eagles have an extra day to rest, with their Week 3 game against the Bears airing as this week’s Monday Night Football game, but he must be treated as questionable to play at this time. Eagles WR Dontayvion Wicks would handle No. 1 wide receiver duties if Smith cannot play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Theo Johnson (neck) will not play in New York’s Week 6 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: It’s Thomas Fidone hours in New York, marone.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Isaiah Likely (foot) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Theo Johnson has a neck injury and was limited in practice. Both tight ends should be able to suit up on Sunday. Coming off a career-high in targets (13), Likely is looking more like a top-five fantasy tight end every week. He should be in every fantasy lineup for his Week 6 date with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Giants TE Theo Johnson (shoulder) is practicing fully for Week 1 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Johnson was seen practicing in a non-contact jersey last week, so today’s full session is positive. Unfortunately, Johnson’s path to fantasy football TE1 status is likely blocked by TE Isaiah Likely, so Johnson is not on the radar for most leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Theo Johnson (shoulder) participated in practice Tuesday wearing a non-contact jersey.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: John Harbaugh has said that Johnson “will be fine,” but we’re going to cover our bases on this one with the Giants keeping five tight ends. Johnson has a week and change to get healthy for Sunday Night Football in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: North Jersey’s Art Stapleton reports that Giants TE Isaiah Likely and TE Theo Johnson are currently the team’s top-two pass catchers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: This is the third positive report in as many months for Likely, who is set to handle TE1 duties for his new team. Johnson is slated for the TE2 role after posting a 45/528/5 receiving line in his second NFL season last year. Giants WR1 Malik Nabers recently underwent a clean-up procedure on his knee and field-stretching WR Darius Slayton is recovering from core muscle surgery. Nabers will retake the No. 1 pass-catching role when healthy. Slayton, 29, is on the downslope. Likely is in the low-end TE1 tier and could improve his stock through the spring and summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reports TE Isaiah Likely is “expected to be a featured piece” of the Giants offense in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Likely followed former Ravens head coach John Harbaugh to New York in free agency, as expected, and signed a three year deal worth up to $47.5 million — a hefty deal considering Likely’s 2025 struggles in Baltimore. With the signing, the Giants “essentially swapped Likely in for Wan’Dale Robinson, signaling the shift in their offensive approach,” Duggan said (Robinson signed with the Titans). Likely will be “paired often” with TE Theo Johnson in a New York offense that should be among the league leaders in two tight end usage, just like Harbaugh’s Ravens, Duggan added. Likely, who should operate as a big slot receiver for Jaxson Dart, could have volume-based upside in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Giants declared TE Theo Johnson, S Jevón Holland, WR Ryan Miller, WR Jalin Hyatt, RB Dante Miller, OLB Caleb Murphy, and QB Russell Wilson inactive for Week 18 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Johnson was courtside at the Knicks game on Friday night and was featured on the Jumbotron, but is apparently not feeling well enough to suit up on Sunday. The Giants are no longer likely to earn the first pick in the draft after their win over the Raiders in Week 17, but they could still nab a top-three selection with a loss today and some help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Giants TE Theo Johnson (illness) won’t play in New York’s Week 18 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Two weeks missed with an illness is rather unusual. We hope Johnson is alright and the story about the illness isn’t too gruesome. Johnson returned five touchdowns with a 45/528 line, becoming more involved with the offense when Jaxson Dart took over against the Chargers in Week 4. It’s possible that Johnson exits the 2026 offseason with a TE1 case, but he feels more like a high-end TE2 from where we sit today. His absence in Week 18 gives Daniel Bellinger a chance to feast against Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Giants TE Theo Johnson (illness) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Johnson came down with a bug last Friday and was unable to play in Week 17 against the Raiders. He must be really going through it. Fortunately, Johnson was seen observing practice from the sideline. Yesterday, he was reportedly among a group of ill players sent home by the coaching staff. He has a chance to play this week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Giants TE Theo Johnson (illness) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Per ESPN’s Jordan Raanan, Johnson was among three players who “were sent home or not at practice as they deal with illnesses.” Dang. Johnson got sick last Friday and was unable to play in Week 17. Hopefully, he returns to good health by the end of the week. He has blossomed into a trusted pass catcher for QB Jaxson Dart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Andrew Thomas (groin) is questionable for New York’s Week 6 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: This is a marked downgrade for Thomas, as he had been skipping plenty of practice days but at least had been cleared off the injury report on Fridays the last few weeks. John Harbaugh said Thomas was “basically full go” today, which seems sketchy in light of this listing. If we take the coach at his word, it seems likely that Thomas will play through this. Ditto Jermaine Eluemunor, who also is questionable after missing the first two days of practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Andrew Thomas (groin) was seen working off to the side on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: Thomas, the Giants’ left tackle, RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and EDGE Abdul Carter (calf) were all seen without jerseys, working on the side field with the training staff today. Expect to see all three listed as non-participants. Thomas has played through a couple of injuries this season, and seemingly has a good chance of suiting up in Week 6 against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: Eluemunor told reporters he felt his calf pop during Week 5 against the Commanders. He left the game and Marcus Mbow took his spot at right tackle. Head coach John Harbaugh called him day-to-day on Monday, so it’s at least not a long-term issue, though he still looks like a coin flip for Week 6. Left tackle Andrew Thomas did not practice, though that’s standard fare for him as he continues to play through a groin injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports Giants RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) is feeling better post-game, but the team will have to see how he feels as the week progresses.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: According to Raanan, Eluemunor felt his calf pop and left today’s game against the Commanders. Fortunately, he was able to walk around on his own, which is a good sign. The Giants went to Marcus Mbow at right tackle in Eluemunor’s absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Andrew Thomas (groin) is not on New York’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: Thomas is on the Terron Armstead plan — very limited practice reps, zero chance of him missing the game. He only got in a limited session on Friday after a pair of DNPs on Wednesday and Thursday. It does not actually seem to matter. Thomas will go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Giants RB Tyrone Tracy (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: The Giants’ RB3 is seemingly on track to be active for Week 4 against the Cardinals. Unfortunately, Giants LT Andrew Thomas (groin) was not seen practicing during the portion of practice open to the media. He did not practice yesterday either and should currently be considered questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Giants RB Tyrone Tracy (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: The Giants’ backup is not presently fantasy-relevant, and a knee injury certainly won’t improve his stock, though coach John Harbaugh said he is only “day-to-day.” Giants LT Andrew Thomas (groin) was also sidelined, but he played through it last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Giants T Andrew Thomas (groin) said he’ll play in New York’s Week 3 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: Players aren’t always the most reliable source and Thomas may still be listed as questionable, but Thomas did practice in full today per John Harbaugh. The Giants star left tackle will protect Jameis Winston against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Giants LT Andrew Thomas (groin) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: Thomas left the Giants’ Week 2 game against the Rams with a groin injury. He dealt with an ankle injury in practice last week. It is possible that fill-in starter, QB Jameis Winston, will be without his top pass protector in Week 3 against the Titans. Thomas was limited yesterday. It appears as though he will be a DNP today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Giants LT Andrew Thomas (ankle) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: Giants RG Francis Mauigoa (shoulder) was limited as well. Both offensive linemen are on track to face the Rams in Week 2’s Monday Night Football game, which is good news for QB Jaxson Dart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) is questionable for Dallas’ Week 6 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter downgraded from full to limited on Friday and wound up with this status despite practicing all three days this week. Peculiar. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson would be better off on Sunday if Porter wasn’t able to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Cowboys declare CB Joey Porter, LB DeMarvion Overshown, CB Cobie Durant, OLB James Houston, OG Ajani Cornelius, OT Drew Shelton and WR Camden Brown inactive for Week 5 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter’s bumpy 2026 campaign takes another surprising turn. The Cowboys’ new cornerback was set to expand his involvement this evening, but he is evidently unable to play due to an illness. Fortunately for the Cowboys, the Buccaneers’ offense is hamstrung by Baker Mayfield’s (thumb) absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter (back/conditioning/contract) is not on the injury report for Week 4 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said on Friday, “we actually think Joey Porter will get snaps.” ESPN’s Todd Archer notes that prior to the mid-week trade, Porter was ruled out of Thursday’s game between the Steelers and Browns, saying his back was tight. He practiced the last two days “without issue.” Porter might be on a snap count this week, but it looks like he will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports there is “a chance” that Joey Porter Jr. (back/conditioning/contract) plays in Week 4 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter Jr. missed the first three games of the year with a back issue. The Steelers also listed conditioning under his name on the injury report and even took the back injury off entirely at one point. All of that is to say that his absences were ultimately contract-related, which everyone knew in the first place. He was ruled out for Thursday’s game by Pittsburgh, but is eligible to play for the Cowboys this week if they can get him up to speed on the playbook ahead of Sunday’s game. He will likely play on specific packages if he does suit up, but that would still be an upgrade for a banged-up Dallas secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Cowboys “will not be immediately extending Joey Porter Jr.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Schultz added that the plan is to have him play first and “the contract will take care of itself from there.” That’s not exactly what Porter Jr. was looking to get out of this move, but it also points to the fact that his relationship with the Steelers was simply fractured beyond repair. Pittsburgh’s somewhat archaic rules around contract negotiations drove a wedge between them and their star corner. They don’t extend players during the season and, with rare exceptions, they do not guarantee money beyond the first year of a new deal. If Porter Jr. suits up next week and puts a few good games on tape, we suspect the Cowboys will feel comfortable giving him the contract he wanted from the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reports that the Cowboys have acquired Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: In exchange for Porter, the Cowboys will send the Steelers a second-round selection in 2028 as well as a conditional sixth-round pick. Pelissero noted in his blog that trade talks between Dallas and Pittsburgh had picked up over the past few weeks, and the deal will soon become official. Porter has yet to play a snap in 2026 as he has dealt with a back injury, and also a contract dispute. The 26-year-old is one of the more talented corners in football, and Dallas has struggled considerably to stop the pass over the first three weeks. Assuming good health, Porter should be a vast improvement over what the Cowboys have gotten out of their corners to begin 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Jalen Ramsey (wrist) is questionable for Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Ramsey was listed as limited for all three practices this week. He is attempting to play through a broken wrist and will likely wear a cast or brace if he is active. As expected, Joey Porter Jr. remains out this week admist his contrat dispute with the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. (NIR/conditioning) was a full participant in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Though Porter has been listed on the injury report with a back issue to start the season, he was listed for “conditioning” to open this week. It’s no secret Porter is in a contract dispute and the Steelers have been getting trade calls on the 26-year-old. However, he is practicing fully ahead of a Week 4 Thursday matchup against the Browns and could certainly play. When asked if Porter will play, head coach Mike McCarthy said, “We hope so.” With Jalen Ramsey dealing with a broken wrist, Porter’s help will be welcome in the secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter Jr. (back) will not play in Week 3 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Who could have seen this coming? Porter has yet to suit up for a game this season, and it’s due to either a back issue, his current contract situation, or a mixture of the two. Teams have inquired about his availability via trade, but no deal appears on the horizon for the 26-year-old corner. In addition to Porter, the Steelers also declared RB Rico Dowdle, QB Drew Allar, QB Willi Howard, RB Eli Heidenreich, DE Kevin Jobity Jr., and DE Gabe Rubio inactive for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Lions and Cowboys “have begun making inquiries about the availability of Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Schefter noted that a handful of teams have called Pittsburgh, so it’s likely more than just Dallas and Detroit. Porter has been locked in an ugly contract dispute with the Steelers since the early offseason, and the team does not negotiate extensions during the season.
