They also rarely guarantee money beyond the first year of an extension, which has been another sticking point for JPJ’s camp. Per Schefter, the Steelers are willing to listen to offers but want a “strong compensation package” in return. Porter is questionable for Week 3 with a back issue, though the team is simply calling it a matter of conditioning, casting doubt on the validity of Porter’s supposed injury. He has yet to play this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: Keisean Nixon (groin) is not on Green Bay’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: He got in a pair of limited sessions on Thursday and Friday to get off the report. Nixon will be tasked with the unenviable duties of taking on George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb in front of a national audience on Sunday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: Keisean Nixon (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: Nixon is the Packers’ top outside corner. He has three pass breakups and one interception this year. His absence would be a big loss for a defense that is only slightly above average in EPA per play and points allowed this year. It would be a particularly big development for George Pickens, who leads the Cowboys in outside receiver routes this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: Packers CB Keisean Nixon (neck) left Green Bay’s Week 12 game with the Vikings and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: He suffered a stinger. Kamal Hadden took over at outside corner for the Packers. Luckily for them, Minnesota doesn’t seem to have any interesting in throwing the football today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: Packers agreed to terms with DB Keisean Nixon on a three-year, $18 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: Nixon totaled 80 tackles and one interception for the Packers last season, but he’s been more known for his play on special teams. Nixon has been named a First-team All-Pro in back-to-back seasons for his return efforts and has led the league in kick return yards in both of those seasons. Nixon is now under contract with the Packers through the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: Packers re-signed CB/KR Keisean Nixon to a one-year, $6 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: In his first year as a returner, Nixon turned in an All-Pro effort, leading the league in kick returns (35) and kick return yards (105). Nixon also appeared on 290 defensive snaps last season, but was a liability in coverage, allowing 22 receptions on 28 targets for 214 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: Packers signed CB Keisean Nixon, formerly of the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: Nixon is a three-year NFL vet who joined the Raiders as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2019. Nixon has appeared in 40 career games throughout his career, with most of his snaps coming on special teams. His signing with the Packers reunites him with former Raiders interim head coach Rich Bisaccia, who is now Green Bay’s special teams coach.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: South Carolina senior CB Keisean Nixon (neck) has been ruled out for the Belk Bowl.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: Nixon (5'11/193) was experiencing numbness and soreness during the regular season, with a CAT scan administered after the close of the campaign revealing that he was dealing with a fracture in his neck. Yikes. This injury for all intents and purposes ends the cornerback’s season. He has already accepted an invitation to the East-West Shrine Game as he looks to get his draft process started. Just how healthy he will be for that postseason evaluation bowl remains to be seen. Draft Analyst’s Tony Pauline stamped him with a UDFA grade over the summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: South Carolina senior CB Keisean Nixon accepted an invitation to the East-West Shrine Game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: Nixon (5'11/193) was a four-star commitment from the JUCO ranks who spent two years in the Gamecocks secondary. He gets quality reviews for his ability to help in the run game, and also as an instinctive defender as a cover corner. He profiles best in the slot, but he’ll get a chance to show his coverage skills on the outside as well. He projects as a Day 3 selection at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.headline: South Carolina signed four-star JUCO DB Keisean Nixon.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keisean-ni.analysis: Score one for Will Muschamp, who also grabbed former Clemson cornerback Kaleb Chalmers on the JUCO trail. Nixon enrolled at South Carolina this month, which means he’ll be ready to roll for spring practices. “Nixon is a 6-foot, 200-pound cornerback with the length and physicality to play anywhere in the secondary,” wrote ESPN’s Gerry Hamilton. “A complete player, Nixon sheds blocks quickly and closes with the ability to strike against the run. In coverage, he’s instinctive and adept in zone with quick and explosive reactions to get his hands on passes.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring/toe) is not on the final injury report for Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith sat out on Wednesday, but practiced in a limited capacity on Thursday before upgrading to full on Friday. Smith told media members earlier today that he is “good,” and that the toe injury is not an issue. Jalen Hurts (blood clot) is out indefinitely, so Smith will be working with pocket-passing backup Tanner McKee. The Panthers are currently without both of their starting perimeter cornerbacks. It might be a bit uncomfortable, but Smith is a WR2 in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring/toe) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo said he is “still hearing optimism he’ll play Sunday. We’ll see.” Given his follow-up comment, it doesn’t seem like he shares the organization’s optimism. If active, Smith would be catching passes thrown by backup Tanner McKee. Jalen Hurts is sidelined indefinitely by a blood clot. McKee, a pocket passer, could lock onto Smith, keeping him in the WR2 tier if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Devonta Smith (hamstring/toe) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith was already reported to be working off to the side on Wednesday, but he now adds a toe injury to his existing hamstring injury on the official practice report. Given he is not practicing yet and a new injury is added to his designation, Smith is currently trending in the wrong direction for Week 6 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Devonta Smith (hamstring) was seen working off to the side on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith could end up being listed as a limited participant, but this will likely result in a DNP. That said, the fact that he is out there working with the training staff is a good sign. Smith attempted to play through his hamstring injury back in Week 3, posting a 6/65 receiving line before apparently suffering a re-injury. He has not played since, but has a chance to suit up in Week 6 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has “a shot” to return for Week 6’s game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith hasn’t been seen on the practice field since Week 3 ended, so to say the practice week matters would perhaps be underselling it. Expect Smith to play if he practices at all, though, as the veteran often has suited up with little practice time in the past.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 5 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith hasn’t looked anywhere close to playing since popping up on the injury report ahead of Week 5, not practicing a single session yet. His status for Week 6 remains murky at best. Makai Lemon and Dontyavion Wicks (if healthy) will get a targets boost in what looks to be a very thin offense at the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith is on the wrong side of questionable for the Eagles’ Week 5 game against the Jaguars, and at this point, we expect him to be ruled out tomorrow. Dallas Goedert (knee) is practicing and could end up operating as the team’s top pass catcher.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Eagles WR Devonta Smith (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith still has not returned to practice since last week, continuing to deal with a hamstring injury. Given his lack of practice reps ahead of travelling to London for Week 5, Smith is on the wrong side of questionable for this week’s matchup against the Jaguars. Also not practicing was WR Hollywood Brown (ankle). The Eagles will play Week 5 with a severely banged-up skill position group.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Eagles declared WR DeVonta Smith, WR Hollywood Brown, TE Dallas Goedert, LB Zack Baun, QB Cole Payton S Marcus Epps, OT Lane Johnson and OT Fred Johnson inactive for Week 4 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: The question with Smith now becomes if he’s ready to return for Week 5 against the Jaguars. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo has reported it is unlikely. It’s a brutal, brutal development for fantasy managers who thought they were getting a breakout WR1 after Smith’s years of WR2 grinding. Dontayvion Wicks and first-round rookie Makai Lemon will try to pick up the targets slack, though veteran TE Zach Ertz will undoubtedly do some of the dirty work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garfaolo reports DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is “at very best” questionable for Week 5 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith has already been ruled out for Week 4. The Eagles take on the Jags in London next week. It sounds like fantasy managers should be prepared to be without their start receiver for that contest as well. Dontayvion Wicks currently profiles as the team’s top wideout, but it’s hard to imagine the team not getting first-round rookie Makai Lemon more involved as well. Both players are solid FLEX options for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.headline: Skyy Moore (ankle) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 6 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.analysis: We’re Skyying less and less. Assuming Savion Williams (ankle) isn’t activated off injured reserve, J. Michael Sturdivant could become a deep-league stab or DFS punt against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman reports Skyy Moore (ankle) was wearing a walking boot Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.analysis: Moore has been the Packers’ leading returner and third receiver since teammate Jayden Reed was placed on injured reserve. Moore hasn’t been much of a factor for fantasy managers, but if he were to miss time, Bo Melton would likely take over return duties, while rookie J. Michael Sturdivant could see additional snaps at receiver. The Packers face the Cowboys in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.headline: Packers agreed to terms with WR Skyy Moore, formerly of the 49ers, on a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.analysis: Moore primarily operated as a return man for the 49ers last season, returning 25 punts for 291 yards and 33 kicks for 907 yards. This included a 98-yard kick return, though he did not score on the play. Moore adds little as a receiver, tallying just five receptions for 87 yards last season after seeing just three targets in 2024 with the Chiefs. He will likely be used as a return specialist by the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.headline: 49ers acquired WR Skyy Moore from the Chiefs in exchange for swapping 2027 sixth and seventh-round picks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.analysis: Moore was a second-round pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, but could never really stick with the Chiefs’ receiving corps. He caught 43 passes for 494 yards and a touchdown over his first two seasons, while failing to catch any of his three targets last season. Moore adds value as a returner, recently returning a punt for a touchdown in the Chiefs’ preseason Week 2 game. The 49ers’ receiver group has been decimated by injuries and the recent suspension to Demarcus Robinson. They now add Moore, who is a shot in the dark at some production from the receiver spot. He is unlikely to hold fantasy relevance heading into the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.headline: Skyy Moore (abdomen) is doubtful for Super Bowl LIX against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.analysis: Moore remains on injured reserve because of the abdomen injury he suffered in October. He was designated to return last week but never progressed past a limited practice. The Chiefs could activate him over the weekend, but all signs point to the two-time Super Bowl champ sitting this one out. Moore did not catch a pass in his third NFL season and will be heading for a roster spot during the summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.headline: Skyy Moore (abdomen) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.analysis: Moore has a chance to be activated off of injured reserve in time for the Super Bowl, but even if he is activated, his contributions are expected to be minimal. Moore has now been limited in back-to-back practices to start the week. We’ll likely know his availability before the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.headline: Skyy Moore (abdomen) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.analysis: The two-time Super Bowl champion has not yet caught a pass this season, but he appears to be on track to play in Super Bowl LIX. Moore may be able to contribute via special teams against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.headline: Chiefs designated WR Skyy Moore (core) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.analysis: Moore suffered a core injury back in October and hasn’t played since. It seems highly unlikely the third-year pro will be activated from injured reserve for the Super Bowl, but even if he is, he wasn’t playing a meaningful role before his injury. Moore’s stock has steadily declined every year since the Chiefs made him a second-round pick in the 2022 NFL Draft. He caught zero passes in six games this season before his injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.headline: Chiefs placed WR Skyy Moore (core) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.analysis: This move corresponds with the trade for DeAndre Hopkins becoming official. Moore was a second-round pick of the Chiefs in 2022 but has slowly fallen down the depth chart to the point where he has yet to catch a pass in any of the team’s six games this season. Moore will be eligible to return in Week 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.headline: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid announced Monday that Juju Smith-Schuster (hamstring) will not play in Week 8 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/skyy-moore.analysis: Smith-Schuster left Sunday’s win over the 49ers with a right hamstring injury, and the wideout will miss at least one more contest with the issue. With the 27-year-old unavailable, it makes Xavier Worthy the top wide receiver in the passing attack, and should lead to more targets for players like Mecole Hardman and Skyy Moore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Eagles ruled out RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) for Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: It was pretty clear that this was where things were headed when Barkley was unable to practice on Wednesday and Thursday. We do not yet know Barkley’s official Friday practice participation level, but he was not seen practicing during the portion of practice open to the media. Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue will likely split touches this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for his team’s Week 6 game against the Panthers, potentially leaving Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue to split touches. Hopefully, reports clarify whether Pierce would handle a sizable workload as the de facto starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Technically, a limited session is possible, but we expect to see Barkley listed as a non-participant since he skipped warmups. Barkley still has a chance to face the Panthers this week, but ideally, he would be out there right now, beginning his ramp-up period. Eagles RBs Dameon Pierce and Carson Steelers are on the active roster, while RB Jaydon Blue currently sits on the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said he’s “hopeful” he will receive offensive reinforcements in Week 6 when asked about Saquon Barkley’s (hamstring) status.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Sirianni was asked about both Barkley and DeVonta Smith, who is also dealing with a hamstring injury. Sirianni didn’t commit to either player practicing this week, but we’ll see how things look on Wednesday when the Eagles release their first injury report. Philly suddenly finds itself in desperate need of help at running back after Tank Bigsby (core) was placed on IR last week and Will Shipley (foot) was diagnosed with a partial tear in his plantar fascia that’s expected to sideline him for several weeks. If Barkley is unable to play in Week 6, Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue would be next in line to lead the Eagles’ banged up backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) has been ruled out for Week 5 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: With Barkley ruled out and Tank Bigsby (core) on injured reserve, the Eagles will officially go with Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce as their top two backs. Shipley feels like a safe bet to serve as the team’s primary pass-catching back, but whether or not he sees the majority of rush attempts is to be determined. It wouldn’t be surprising if Pierce, who profiles as more of an early-down grinder than Shipley, leads the Eagles’ backfield in carries this week, but fantasy managers shouldn’t rush to add him to their lineups. Shipley will likely fall somewhere in the RB2 rankings this week, while Pierce is nothing more than a stash at the end of fantasy benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley will likely be listed as a non-participant on today’s official injury report. He is unlikely to play in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Aside from Barkley, the Eagles have RBs Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce on the active roster. Shipley will probably lead the backfield in touches this week, but it could be a messy workload split.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was not present at Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: The Eagles will drop their official injury report later today, but this can be chalked up as a DNP for Barkley. He was already considered week-to-week after suffering a hamstring injury on Sunday, so today’s DNP doesn’t come as a surprise. He is a long-shot to play in Week 5. With Tank Bigsby on IR, Will Shipley will lead the backfield versus Jacksonville. He profiles as a low-end RB3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Eagles RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is considered “week-to-week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley departed the team’s Week 4 loss to the Rams in the second quarter and did not return, with Ian Rapoport relaying that the team views him as “week-to-week,” for the time being. Rapoport added that the team does not view the injury as a long-term issue. Regardless, Barkley appears set to miss multiple games with the soft tissue injury, leaving the team paper thin at running back after backup Tank Bigsby inured a core muscle that requires surgery. Will Shipley is the only other back currently on the active roster, while Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele, and Jaydon Blue are with the team on the practice squad. Shipley warrants a waiver addition while managers in deeper leagues can consider taking an early flier on Blue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tank Bigsby will have core muscle surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Rapoport reports there are hopes that Bigsby will be back “in six weeks or shorter.” The 24-year-old back will be required to miss at least four games now that he’s headed for an IR stint. With Saquon Barkley (hamstring) also at risk of missing at least one game, third-string RB Will Shipley could be in line for a busy day in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Shipley rushed six times for 23 yards in Sunday’s loss to the Rams, but could be a sneaky option in PPR leagues given his pass-catching profile during his days at Clemson, when he caught 85 passes over three seasons. It also wouldn’t be surprising if Dameon Pierce or Jaydon Blue were promoted off the practice squad and saw early down touches while Shipley serves in more of a third-down role. There’s a lot to figure out here over the next few days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said he’ll “have more answers Wednesday” on Saquon Barkley’s hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley went down early in Sunday’s loss to the Rams and did not return to the game. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said earlier on Monday that Barkley’s injury “does not seem to be overly serious,” but with the Eagles taking on the Jaguars in London next week, it wouldn’t be surprising if he missed at least one game. Backup Tank Bigsby led the Eagles with 55 rushing yards on 14 carries and could be a viable RB2 if Barkley is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Savion Williams (ankle/PUP) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 6 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams was limited in practice all week, making it seem like he could wait another week on the PUP list. When he does come back, the WR3 role would seem to be wide open for him after Jayden Reed’s injury. He remains a decent fantasy football stash if you have extra injured reserve spots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Savion Williams (ankle/IR) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 5 game against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams isn’t a half-bad IR stash though with almost all of the offense flowing through Christian Watson and Matthew Golden right now. The WR3 room has been thinned with injuries and Jayden Reed (neck) won’t return this year. Williams could play a major role once activated from IR; this is just the first week of his 21-day window where he was designated to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst said WR Savion Williams (ankle/IR) has a high-ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams was placed on IR at last cuts without an explanation of the injury, so here it is. Gutekunst said he thinks Williams will be ready when the four-week mandatory stay on IR is over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Packers placed WR Savion Williams on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams, 24, was a non-factor for Green Bay in 2025 with 10 catches for 78 yards; although he did a solid job as a kick returner with 717 yards on his 28 attempts. The 2025 third-round pick has the athleticism to be a helper in 2026, but fantasy managers in redraft leagues shouldn’t count on it .

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Packers WR Matthew Golden (wrist) is not on Green Bay’s final Week 16 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Despite his first useful fantasy game (3/55) in some time last week against Denver, we’d caution against starting Golden in Week 16 as Christian Watson seems likely to play. Savion Williams (foot) is also off the injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Packers WR Jayden Reed (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Reed returned from foot and shoulder injuries to play in Week 14, getting four targets on the day. He saw a sizeable role, running over 60 percent of available routes; the Packers will limit his practice workload to start the week. Also limited were fellow wide receivers Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) and Savion Williams (foot). Wicks played through the ankle injury in Week 14 while Williams did not practice all of last week. Reed is still trending to play and is the best receiver out of the three, while Wicks is worth a speculative deep league dart throw and Williams is not fantasy relevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Packers WR Dontyavion Wicks (ankle) is not on Green Bay’s final Week 14 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: We’d be surprised if he did anything close to what he did on Thanksgiving against the Bears, but perhaps the 24-year-old has turned over a new leaf with this offense. He’s still a FLEX play at best. The Packers also ruled out WR Savion Williams (foot), who did not practice all week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Savion Williams (foot) did not practice Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: He played through the foot listing last week, generating zero yards on his lone touch. Non-dynasty managers don’t have to worry about Williams this season between his lack of progress and Green Bay’s lack of interest in throwing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Packers WR Romeo Doubs (wrist) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nearly the entire Packers pass-catching group was either limited or not practicing on Wednesday. Doubs was listed as a limited participant with a wrist injury, along with three other Packers wideouts listed as limited and Savion Williams (foot) listed as a non-participant. Doubs is the current lead receiver in an offense that does not have a definitive No. 1 receiver. If he were to miss time, Christian Watson would be first up for a bump, followed by the rookie Matthew Golden. Stay tuned to Doubs and the rest of the Green Bay receivers’ statuses this week; the Packers’ fantasy hierarchy could see a shake-up if multiple receivers cannot play Week 12 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Savion Williams caught a 33-yard pass in the Packers’ Week 11 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The third-round rookie’s lone target was his fourth quarter grab which came against extremely tight coverage on 3rd-and-10. It was a highlight-reel level play, and the longest reception of his young career. Williams is playing extremely few snaps even as the Packers hunt for playmakers, but the rare times he’s on the field, he seems to command targets. Six days shy of his 24th birthday, Williams’ advanced age limits his long-term dynasty appeal, but he remains worth an end-of-bench spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Eagles placed Will Shipley (foot) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four weeks. Shipley was diagnosed with a partially torn plantar fascia and was set to miss multiple weeks per reporting, so this makes sense. By the time he comes back, Saquon Barkley should be healthy, so he’s not a must-keep in short-bench leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Eagles RB Will Shipley (foot) suffered “a partial tear of his plantar fascia” in Week 5’s loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: The Eagles’ running backs room continues to take hits. After losing Tank Bigsby (core) last week to a multi-week injury, the team is now preparing to be without Shipley for multiple weeks. Saquon Barkley, who missed Week 5 with a hamstring injury, could be back as early as Week 6 against the Panthers, but if he’s unable to play, the Eagles could be looking at Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue as their top two backs. Shipley totaled 13 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown on six touches before going down yesterday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley (foot) will not return to the Eagles’ Week 5 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: Shipley suffered the foot injury in the second quarter and was initially listed as questionable to return. He will now miss the remainder of the contest. Dameon Pierce is the only other running back on the roster with a touch today. Carson Steele is also active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley (foot) is questionable to return in Week 5 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: Shipley got stuffed on a carry in the second quarter and was checked out by trainers after the play. He went to the locker room after a brief trip to the blue medical tent. Dameon Pierce will be the next man up if Shipley’s day is over. Carson Steele is the only other back on the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: Barkley will likely be listed as a non-participant on today’s official injury report. He is unlikely to play in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Aside from Barkley, the Eagles have RBs Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce on the active roster. Shipley will probably lead the backfield in touches this week, but it could be a messy workload split.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was not present at Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: The Eagles will drop their official injury report later today, but this can be chalked up as a DNP for Barkley. He was already considered week-to-week after suffering a hamstring injury on Sunday, so today’s DNP doesn’t come as a surprise. He is a long-shot to play in Week 5. With Tank Bigsby on IR, Will Shipley will lead the backfield versus Jacksonville. He profiles as a low-end RB3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Eagles activated RB Dameon Pierce to the team’s active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: Pierce will probably operate as the team’s No. 2 back behind Will Shipley this week against the Jaguars, one of the league’s best rush defenses. Tank Bigsby and Saquon Barkley are sidelined, leaving the Eagles scraping bottom for backfield depth. Look for Pierce to get some early-down work against the Jaguars. Shipley, who had six carries for 23 yards last week, is the only viable fantasy option of the two, though head coach Nick Sirianni heaped praise on Pierce Wednesday. “He’s an NFL starting running back,” Sirriani said of Pierce. “Maybe wouldn’t have said that when he was on our practice squad publicly, because of the fear of losing him. But he’s an NFL starting running back.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tank Bigsby will have core muscle surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: Rapoport reports there are hopes that Bigsby will be back “in six weeks or shorter.” The 24-year-old back will be required to miss at least four games now that he’s headed for an IR stint. With Saquon Barkley (hamstring) also at risk of missing at least one game, third-string RB Will Shipley could be in line for a busy day in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Shipley rushed six times for 23 yards in Sunday’s loss to the Rams, but could be a sneaky option in PPR leagues given his pass-catching profile during his days at Clemson, when he caught 85 passes over three seasons. It also wouldn’t be surprising if Dameon Pierce or Jaydon Blue were promoted off the practice squad and saw early down touches while Shipley serves in more of a third-down role. There’s a lot to figure out here over the next few days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley rushed six times for 23 yards in the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: Shipley was the carries understudy to Tank Bigsby after Saquon Barkley suffered a hamstring injury on the game’s second series, though they played a near-even amount of snaps. Bigsby, who himself has been nursing an abdomen issue, was also banged up late. Needless to say, this is a backfield that is going to require many updates between now and Week 5. Hopefully we have a little clarity before waivers bids are due overnight Tuesday into Wednesday. Even if Bigsby is declared fine, Shipley is certainly worth an addition.

https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.headline: Will Shipley (foot) is not on Philadelphia’s final injury report for Week 4.
https://www.nbcsports.com/will-shipley/0.analysis: It’s a surprising twist after Shipley missed both of the first two practices of the week; he got in a full session today and seems likely to be more involved as a pass-catcher with DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert down. Even with that, he’ll struggle to find FLEX value against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.headline: Trey Hendrickson (finger) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.analysis: He practiced in full all week after missing the last two games following finger surgery. The Ravens’ big free-agent acquisition will be full go against the Browns in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.analysis: The Ravens’ new starting center is still recovering from his recent concussion, but he seemingly has a chance to face the Browns this week. Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) and S Kyle Hamilton (stinger) are practicing fully, while RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), OG John Simpson (groin), OG Andrew Vorhees (foot), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) were limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.headline: Ravens DL Trey Hendrickson (finger surgery) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 5 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.analysis: He didn’t practice this week after undergoing surgery late last week, and remains a question mark for Week 6. In theory this shouldn’t cost him too much time, but we don’t have enough details to say that for sure.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.headline: Ravens DL Trey Hendrickson (finger) underwent surgery and will not play in Baltimore’s Week 4 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.analysis: Jesse Minter announced the news and did not provide a timetable for a return. Hendrickson had played through the ailment in Weeks 2 and 3. It’s plausible that he’s back in Week 5 assuming this wasn’t a major procedure, and if he was going to miss one game, the Titans game would be the one to miss.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.headline: Trey Hendrickson (finger) did not practice Wednedsay.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.analysis: Hendrickson broke his finger a few weeks ago. He failed to practice last Wednesday and was ultimately cleared from the injury report on Friday. We expect a similar outcome this week. Hendrickson has one sack on 14 pressures through three weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.headline: Trey Hendrickson (finger) isn’t on Baltimore’s final Week 3 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.analysis: Questionable with this ailment last week, Hendrickson played in Week 2 with a cast. It seems like that will be the plan going forward. Hendrickson got in a full session today. Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) was also not on the injury report and is slated to make his season debut in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.headline: Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.analysis: Hendrickson reportedly broke his finger “into several pieces” last week, yet still managed to record six quarterback pressures and one sack in Week 2. He should play again in Week 3 against the Cowboys in Brazil.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.headline: Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.analysis: Hendrickson recently broke his finger “into several pieces.” Ouch. Hendrickson played through the pain last week, collecting six quarterback pressures and one sack. We expect him to suit up again in Week 3, though the team will manage his reps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.headline: Trey Hendrickson (finger) will play in Week 2 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.analysis: Hendrickson reportedly broke his finger “into several pieces,” but that won’t be enough to keep him out against his former team this week. Ravens writer Ryan Mink said Hendrickson’s fingers are “heavily wrapped” and that he’ll play with a cast on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Trey Hendrickson (finger) is “slated to play” in Week 2 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-hendr.analysis: Rapoport notes that Hendruckson broke his finger “into several pieces this week.” Ouch. He will play with a cast on his hand for Week 2 and likely much longer. With Hendrickson available, the Ravens’ defense is one of the better fantasy options versus a pass-happy Saints offense this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Andrew Vorhees (foot) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 6 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: The guard got in three limited sessions, he and Emery Jones Jr. (ankle) are both questionable. Ronnie Stanley, John Simpson and Roger Rosengarten were removed from the injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Jurgens still has a chance to play, but we had hoped to see him upgrade to full participation. Ravens EDGE Mike Green (hamstring) was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. Ravens OG Andrew Vorhees (foot) joins him in the limited column. Ravens RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) upgraded to full participation. Ravens OG John Simpson (groin) downgraded to a DNP.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: The Ravens’ new starting center is still recovering from his recent concussion, but he seemingly has a chance to face the Browns this week. Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) and S Kyle Hamilton (stinger) are practicing fully, while RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), OG John Simpson (groin), OG Andrew Vorhees (foot), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) were limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Ravens RG Andrew Vorhees (foot) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 4’s game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Vorhees exited late in the first half against the Titans and was replaced by Emery Jones. Vorhees was making his first start of the season this week and played on just eight snaps in last week’s game against the Cowboys. Hopefully this isn’t anything too serious, as the Ravens’ interior offensive line has already been hit with multiple injuries this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Ravens RB Rasheen Ali (neck, IR) is questionable for Week 5 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Ali opened the year on injured reserve after suffering a neck injury ahead of Week 1. He was a full participant in Friday’s practice, suggesting he has a good chance of suiting up this week. His return would give the Ravens another backup option behind Derrick Henry. Guard Andrew Vorhees is listed as questionable but appears likely to play versus the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Ravens OG Andrew Vorhees (ankle) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Vorhees was listed as doubtful for Week 4 on Friday and got ruled out with inactives before kickoff. His return to practice suggests the second-year guard will be back on the field this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Ravens C Tyler Linderbaum (knee) is questionable for Week 4 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Linderbaum was a full participant in Friday’s practice and should be good to go. Right tackle Patrick Mekari is also good to go despite dealing with a minor neck injury. Left guard Andrew Vorhees, on the other hand, is doubtful. Though losing Vorhees isn’t ideal, getting two of the three banged up linemen on the field this week is a good outcome for Lamar Jackson and the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Tyler Linderbaum (knee) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Linderbaum and fellow lineman Patrick Mekari (neck) both returned to practice after being DNPs on Wednesday. Left guard Andrew Vorhees, however, remained sidelined. Barring any setbacks, it appears safe to say Linderbaum and Mekari will both be good to go for Sunday’s contest against the Bills. Vorhees’ availability remains TBD.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Ravens C Tyler Linderbaum (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: RT Patrick Mekari (neck) and LG Andrew Vorhees (ankle) were also unable to practice on Wednesday. The Ravens face a Bills pass rush that ranks seventh among NFL teams in pass-rush win rate (50.4%). All three players will be needed for an AFC showdown with playoff implications.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.headline: Ravens GM Eric DeCosta said “We have every expectation that (Andrew Vorhees) will be playing winning football for us in 2024.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-vor.analysis: Translation: Expect the 2023 season to be spent on IR for the USC guard after he tore his ACL at the NFL Combine. The Ravens will use this as a redshirt year for the guard and hope he can compete for a roster spot in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 6 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane practiced in full all week, lending credence to the idea that he’ll be activated. Ravens coach Jesse Minter stopped short of saying Lane would play when given a chance, saying they’d “figure that out,” but said he had a great week of practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Bateman played through the shoulder injury last week. He was limited yesterday, but coach Jesse Minter said he wasn’t worried. Downgrading to a DNP is not a good sign. Meanwhile, Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing fully this week and could hop right into WR2 duties for the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Earlier today, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that Lane has “a shot” to face the Browns in Week 6. His full participation furthers that notion. The talented rookie drew rave reports all summer before suffering an unfortunate wrist fracture in Week 1. While he makes for a dicey FLEX if Tyler Huntley is under center, Lane should at least be safely stashed on fantasy football benches in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) has “a shot” to play in Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lane, who injured his wrist in the season opener against the Colts, will return to practice this week and could suit up this weekend against the Browns. Lane had impressed Ravens coaches and beat writers through training camp and in Week 1 he caught one of three targets for 11 yards before exiting with the wrist injury. Lane’s return to the Baltimore lineup could limit snaps and routes for Rashod Bateman Devontez Walker. Lane should be picked up in 14-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ravens placed WR Ja’Kobi Lane on injured reserve with a wrist injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane underwent surgery to address a fracture in his wrist and will now miss at least four games on short-term injured reserve. He will be eligible to return in Week 6. Ravens No. 1 WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) is also nursing an injury. Theoretically, fellow rookie WR Elijah Sarratt should be active in Week 2 against the Saints, though it is unclear if he would have a meaningful role if Flowers plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is expected to undergo surgery “in the coming days.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane fractured his wrist in the Ravens’ Week 1 victory over the Colts, catching one pass for 11 yards in his rookie debut. The 22-year-old operated as a top-three receiver in the Ravens offense and was set for a sizeable role prior to the injury. He was seeking multiple opinions on the injury as of Monday, but Zenitz now reports Lane is expected to have surgery on his wrist very soon. Zenitz adds that the hope is for the rookie to be able to return in a month. Injured reserve will be a consideration for Lane, which would be a four-game absence at the minimum.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ravens HC Jesse Minter said Ja’Kobi Lane will seek second and third opinions after suffering a fractured wrist in Week 1’s win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: It was reported Sunday night that Lane was likely to miss several weeks, but on Monday, Minter said Lane could be out a bit longer than expected. The rookie third-rounder caught 1-of-3 targets for 11 yards in his pro debut but was seeing a good amount of work before exiting. Lane’s 24 first-half snaps were the second-most of any Ravens receiver. We’ll likely have a better sense of how long Lane will be sidelined in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane suffered a fractured wrist and will undergo further testing to determine the full extent of the injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Garafolo’s colleague, Ian Rapoport, adds that Lane will be sidelined for “several weeks.” This is an unfortunate development for both the player and the team. Fellow Ravens WR Zay Flowers aggravated the hamstring injury he recently rehabbed as well. Expect rookie WR Elijah Sarratt to be active in Week 2 against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 1’s game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane caught 1-of-3 targets for 11 yards in his pro debut and had a short touchdown overturned in the second quarter on a holding penalty. Lane was seeing significant work in the first half. His 24 first-half snaps, per TruMedia, were good for the second-most among Ravens receivers. We’ll now wait for word on his status ahead of Week 2’s game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta described WR Ja’Kobi Lane as a “ball of clay with a lot of upside.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane, selected with the 80th pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, has wowed coaches and beat writers throughout training camp with highlight contested catches while earning the trust of Lamar Jackson and first-year OC Declan Doyle. Lane, according to The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec, has “made a highlight-reel catch, several with one hand, on almost a per-practice basis over the past month.” In a preseason tilt against the Eagles, Lane caught all three of his targets for 38 yards and a touchdown. “This guy is different,” Jackson told reporters afterward. It would be surprising if Lane did not start the regular season as an every-down wideout in the Baltimore offense. His connection with Jackson should instantly make him the team’s No. 2 wideout behind Zay Flowers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman was a surprise DNP on Thursday, but got in a full session today. He remains an uninspiring FLEX option against the Browns in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman played through the shoulder injury last week. He was limited yesterday, but coach Jesse Minter said he wasn’t worried. Downgrading to a DNP is not a good sign. Meanwhile, Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing fully this week and could hop right into WR2 duties for the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: We won’t know what Bateman’s injury is until the Ravens drop their first injury report of Week 6 later today, but head coach Jesse Minter wasn’t worried. He downplayed the issue and told reporters he expects Bateman to play this week. Barring a setback, Bateman will remain a deep-cut FLEX option for Week 6 versus the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman caught 5-of-6 targets for 62 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman had a relatively quiet game until notching 38 yards on three receptions on the team’s final possession of regulation, helping to spur an improbable comeback victory in overtime. The team took the ball with just over two minutes remaining down by eight, eventually driving the field and tacking on a two-point conversion to send the game to extra time. Bateman remains a shaky FLEX option for as long as Zay Flowers remains healthy. He won’t be worth starting in most leagues in a Week 6 meeting with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: He’ll play. It won’t matter for fantasy football players. Tyler Huntley seems much less likely to randomly connect with Bateman downfield than Lamar Jackson did, and even Jackson was barely doing it much.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Despite being listed as full, Bateman played in a red non-contact jersey per reporters. We suppose this technically qualifies as “fantasy football news” but Bateman isn’t a real threat to do much in Week 5, especially with Tyler Huntley likely under center for the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman and WR Chris Moore (ankle) were both limited to begin the week. Neither player will be fantasy-relevant if backup QB Tyler Huntley gets the start in Week 5 against the Falcons though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman caught 2-of-3 targets for 37 yards in the Ravens’ Week 3 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: As expected, Bateman was reduced back to a lightly used WR2 with Zay Flowers back in the lineup. After going for 7-88-1 on nine targets last week against the Saints, Bateman saw just three targets in Sunday’s win, with one of those resulting in a 31-yard gain. Bateman’s 20 routes run led the Ravens’ in Sunday’s win, but he offers nothing of fantasy value as long as Flowers is in the lineup. Fantasy managers who added him after his Week 2 breakout can send him back to waivers ahead of Week 4’s game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: ESPN’s Jamison Hensley reports Zay Flowers (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Barring a surprise, Flowers will be a DNP when the team posts its first injury report of the week. Flowers missed Week 1 with the hamstring injury. Head coach Jesse Minter said earlier this week that he has “a good shot” at playing in Week 3, but a DNP today casts some doubt on his optimism. Rashod Bateman would be in line for another solid workload if Flowers remains out. Bateman caught seven passes for 88 yards and one score on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman caught 7-of-9 targets for 88 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 2 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman came up in a big way for the Ravens, who were without Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) in this one. Bateman’s nine targets would end up leading all Ravens pass-catchers, and he came up with a big 22-yard touchdown late in the second quarter to extend the Ravens’ lead to 14-6 heading into halftime. It was an encouraging game overall for Bateman, who saw only one target last week while running 27 routes. Despite a strong day, Bateman will be hard to trust in next week’s game against the Cowboys if Flowers is able to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (toe) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Perhaps feeling a bit wistful after spending a little of every week of the season on the injury report, Flowers got re-added Thursday with a limited session. He was limited again on Friday but is expected to play. There’s no further word on how serious this toe injury was, but he’s doing enough on the field in his limited time so far this year that nobody is seriously benching Flowers anyway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (toe) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers played through a foot injury last week, catching 8-of-9 targets for 53 yards and rushing once for 13 yards. This injury could be related, but we really don’t know. Flowers’ productivity took a hit with Tyler Huntley running the offense last week. Huntley is currently in line to start again, though Lamar Jackson’s (ankle) status is still up in the air. If the toe injury limits Flowers, that further complicates things, but he still must be started if active. Hopefully, he practices tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-9 targets for 53 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons, adding 13 yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers was largely confined to short area work with Tyler Huntley under center and also saw a 26-yard reception erased from his ledger due to a 29-yard pass interference penalty on the play. It was a weird situation in which the penalty yardage was greater than his reception. Fantasy managers might be forced to continue waiting on the return of Lamar Jackson after it was reported this week that the All Pro starter could be forced to miss another week. Flowers is a locked-in WR2 against the Browns in Week 6 with Huntley under center and an elite WR1 should Jackson return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Ravens declared QB Lamar Jackson, OLB Trey Hendrickson, C Cam Jurgens, G Andrew Vorhees, WR Elijah Sarratt, and DT Aeneas Peebles inactive for Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Jackson had already been ruled out earlier in the week and reportedly could be looking at a multi-game absence due to an ankle injury suffered before halftime in Week 4. Tyler Huntley will start under center for the Ravens as they look to subdue the momentum of the Falcons, who have won both games started by Michael Penix. Wide receiver Zay Flowers is officially active for Sunday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Zay Flowers (foot) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers was limited in practice throughout the week but never appeared at risk of missing Sunday night’s game. The bigger issue for him will be the absence of Lamar Jackson. Flowers has been the most efficient receiver in the league on a per-route basis this year. That will come back to Earth sans Jackson, but he remains on the WR1/2 border, even with Tyler Huntley under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (foot) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 5 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers got in three limited sessions while dealing with the foot injury. He loses ceiling with Tyler Huntley under center, but remains a rock solid low-end WR1 in terms of how much volume he amasses in this passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers appears well on track to play this week after two limited sessions on Wednesday and Thursday. His ceiling will probably take a small hit with Lamar Jackson out, but he remains the only game in town in Baltimore and should still have WR1 viability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers was not present during the portion of practice open to the media earlier today, though it was assumed that this was a maintenance issue relating to his multi-week hamstring strain. It turns out Flowers is dealing with a new injury. It is unclear when the injury occurred. If it was an in-game issue last week, then beginning Week 5 with a limited practice is a great sign for his availability. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Initially, it looked like Flowers might not practice today. He was not present during the portion of practice open to the media, but apparently joined his teammates later on. He will likely be catching passes from backup QB Tyler Huntley against the Falcons this weekend, but he remains WR2-viable at worst.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lamar Jackson’s ankle sprain is “unconventional.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: The sprain Jackson sustained in Week 4 against the Titans, according to Rapoport, is neither low nor high. Rapoport said Monday that Jackson has an “outside” shot at suiting up in Week 5 against the Falcons and could miss multiple games with the unique ankle situation. Tyler Huntley will once again sub in for Jackson until he’s ready to return. Baltimore will likely be far more run heavy with Huntley under center, limiting targets for Zay Flowers and the rest of the Ravens pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.headline: Will Campbell (knee) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.analysis: Campbell injured his knee in Week 5, initially causing quite the scare. Fortunately, he was able to practice all week and has a chance to face the Jets and their talented pass-rush group in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.headline: Will Campbell (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.analysis: The Patriots’ left tackle seemingly has a chance to play in Week 6 against the Jets. According to Mass Live’s Mark Daniels, Campbell “was out here moving well in full pads,” and lined up with the starters during the portion of practice open to the media. This is great news for Drake Maye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Will Campbell avoided a major knee injury in Week 5.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.analysis: Campbell went down with what looked like a serious injury in the first half of New England’s win over the Raiders. He did not return to action. Campbell, per Pelissero, will be “week to week” headed into Week 6. The Patriots will likely be without him this weekend against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Patriots OT Will Campbell is believed to have suffered a knee sprain and will likely miss some time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.analysis: Campbell will undergo an MRI tomorrow to fully assess the injury, but it seems likely that Drake Maye will be playing without his left tackle for a few weeks. They face the Jets, Bears and Dolphins over the next three weeks. Keeping Jets rookie EDGE David Bailey at bay could prove challenging.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.headline: Patriots OT Will Campbell (knee) exited in Week 5 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.analysis: Campbell had his leg rolled on in the second quarter and was down in obvious pain for a while before being helped off the field. Campbell was taken to the locker room for further evaluation and seems unlikely to return today. An extended absence for Campbell would be a tough blow for Drake Maye and the New England passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Will Campbell will remain at left tackle in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.analysis: Vrabel on Tuesday offered a vociferous defense of the rookie following his postseason struggles while playing through a major knee injury. “Will is 22 years old. He’s our left tackle. He’ll get better. He’ll get stronger,” Vrabel said. “There’s plays he’d like to have back. We’re not moving Will to guard, center, tight end or anywhere else.” Pro Football Focus graded Campbell 110th out of 200 qualifying offensive linemen in pass blocking this season. He was graded 81st in run blocking. Campbell allowed nine sacks in 2025, the third most among all NFL offensive linemen. Assuming he’ll undergo offseason knee surgery, Campbell should be good to go for the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.headline: Patriots LT Will Campbell said he played through a torn knee ligament this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.analysis: Campbell said the injury was no excuse for his abysmal play in the postseason, including in the Patriots’ Super Bowl loss to the Seahawks. Campbell was overwhelmed by the Seattle front seven from start to finish, as Drake Maye was pressured on 29 of his 53 drop backs and sacked six times. Campbell will presumably have offseason surgery to fix the injury. Hopefully for the Patriots, Campbell — the fourth overall selection in the 2025 NFL Draft — will be better in 2026 than he was during his disastrous finish to the 2025 campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.headline: Patriots LT Will Campbell (knee) is active for Week 18 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.analysis: The Patriots’ rookie left tackle is active for the first time since Week 12. He could be on something of a snap count as he looks to get his legs back ahead of the postseason, but the Pats remain in contention for the AFC’s No. 1 seed, if only faintly. Perhaps Campbell will play more than expected if circumstance dictates. Inactive for the Patriots are OT Marcus Bryant, OG Caedan Wallace, QB Tommy DeVito, EDGE Harold Landry, LB Robert Spillane, DT Khyiris Tonga and OG Jared Wilson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.headline: Patriots LT Will Campbell (knee) will return to practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.analysis: Campbell was placed on injured reserve after suffering a torn MCL in Week 12 against the Bengals. The 21-year-old left tackle will have his 21-day practice window opened this week. He’s eligible to return from injured reserve for Week 18’s matchup with the Dolphins, though the Patriots will have to see him practice first. If all goes well, it looks like the Patriots will be getting a big piece of their offensive line back ahead of a potentially deep playoff run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.headline: Patriots placed LT Will Campbell (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-campb.analysis: As expected, Campbell will miss at least four games. Campebll suffered a torn MCL in Week 12 and may be out until the playoffs, if not longer. Vederian Lowe took Campbell’s spot in the lineup last week. Head coach Mike Vrabel was noncommittal earlier in the week when asked about Campbell’s replacement. Rookie Marcus Bryant could also get a shot at the job. Either way, expect Drake Maye to be pressured far more often without his starting left tackle on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the NFL has reinstated Broncos OLB Jonathon Cooper from the commissioner’s exempt list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.analysis: Cooper missed the first six games of the season while on the list, and his felony court case has been moved to after the season. It’s unclear if the league considers time served on this list as separate from a personal conduct policy violation; it’s possible Cooper faces another suspension at some point. For now, it seems the NFL is content to let him play in Week 7 despite unresolved felony assault charges and domestic violence and harassment charges.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.headline: Broncos EDGE Jonathon Cooper was granted permission to travel to the team’s away games this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.analysis: Cooper, who is facing felony assault charges and domestic violence and harassment charges, appeared in court on Monday and is currently on the commissioner’s exempt list. With his pretrial set for February 19th and his new trial date set for March 2nd, it’s possible Cooper could be removed from the exempt list now that his trial is set for after the season. Cooper has not played a game for the Broncos this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the NFL will place Broncos EDGE Jonathan Cooper on the commissioner’s exempt list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.analysis: Cooper is facing felony assault charges in addition to other chargers including domestic violence and harassment. The 28-year-old was slated to be Denver’s starting outside linebacker opposite Nik Bonitto, but now they’ll have to look at depth options while waiting for the commissioner to clear Cooper.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.headline: Broncos LB Jonathon Cooper is participating in training camp while facing felony assault charges.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.analysis: Cooper is facing six different charges stemming from domestic violence and harassment cases. He was excused from minicamp as a result, but returns to training camp as a full practice participant. Head coach Sean Payton said the Broncos have met with Cooper and the team is proceeding according to league protocol. Cooper is slated to have an arraignment hearing at the end of August. The NFL will conduct its investigation as the legal process plays out. In the meantime, Cooper is on the practice field with the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.headline: Jonathon Cooper has been excused from mandatory minicamp while he works through his legal and personal issues.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.analysis: Cooper was arrested for six different charges over the last few weeks, including second-degree assault and domestic violence. It’s certainly a situation that could lead to an NFL suspension at some point once all due diligence is taken care of. Cooper’s status appears to be uncertain going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.headline: The Athletic’s Nick Kosmider reports Broncos LB Jonathon Cooper was arrested on Thursday on four new charges.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.analysis: A week after being arrested for domestic violence and criminal mischief, Cooper again finds himself in trouble. This time, the Broncos’ pass rusher is being charged with misdemeanor harassment, violating a protective order, and a felony charge of second-degree assault has been added to his list of charges from last week. According to the Denver Post , the felony charge comes after forensic evidence revealed Cooper’s former girlfriend had been strangled, while his most recent arrest comes after Cooper reportedly showed up to her house on Thursday and knocked on her door for “5-10" minutes and also attempted to contact her multiple times over the phone. He remains in custody and is scheduled to appear in court later today. Earlier this week, Cooper pled not guilty to the charges that stemmed from his first arrest and had a jury trial date set for July 22nd. In a statement released by the Broncos, the team said they are “disappointed to learn of Jonathon Cooper’s arrest on Thursday and continue to review the matter.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.headline: Broncos LB Jonathon Cooper pleaded not guilty to charges of domestic violence and criminal mischief on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.analysis: Cooper was arrested last week and charged with two counts of domestic violence and one count of criminal mischief. The 28-year-old linebacker now has a jury trial set for July 22nd, which could cut into the beginning of training camp. Whether Cooper faces any disciplinary action from the league will likely be determined once his case is settled, but he could be in line for a suspension at some point in 2026 or 2027. Cooper totaled 50 tackles, eight TFLs, and eight sacks for the Broncos last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.headline: The Athletic’s Nick Kosmider reports Broncos LB Jonathon Cooper was arrested on Thursday on charges of criminal mischief with a domestic violence enhancer.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.analysis: Cooper was arrested on Thursday night and booked into a Douglas County jail on Friday. Few details are known about his arrest outside of the charges, but the veteran pass-rusher is reportedly scheduled to go before a judge on Friday with another hearing scheduled for Monday, per an article put out by TMZ . Cooper totaled eight sacks for the Broncos last season and is in the second year of a four-year extension he signed in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.headline: Broncos signed LB Jonathon Cooper to a four-year, $60 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.analysis: Cooper’s deal includes $33 million in guaranteed money , per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Cooper was a seventh-round pick of the Broncos back in 2021 and has carved out a nice career for himself thus far. He’s totaled 18.5 sacks in 56 career games and is sitting on 5.5 sacks through his first nine games of this season. He’s on pace to surpass last season’s 8.5 sack total — which set a new career high, and has been an instrumental piece of Sean Payton’s defense since Payton arrived in the Mile High City in 2023. Now secured through the 2028 season, Cooper will remain a key piece of the defense for years to come.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.headline: Broncos declared OT Billy Turner (knee) inactive for Week 3’s game against San Francisco.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-c.analysis: Turner has struggled with the knee injury dating back to camp and still isn’t ready to set foot on the field against the 49ers. Cameron Fleming will protect the blindside for Russell Wilson against San Francisco’s pass rush. Also inactive for the Broncos are: WR Jalen Virgil, WR Tyrie Cleveland (hamstring), CB Darius Phillips (hamstring), S Delarrin Turner-Yell, OLB Jonathon Cooper (hamstring), and DL Eyioma Uwazurike

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Gonzalez has not played since Week 3, but he returns in time to cover Garrett Wilson in a divisional showdown. Gonzalez primarily lines up on the perimeter, but he has taken 15 combined snaps in the slot and in the box. He could take a few reps on the inside this week, but perimeter CB2 Carlton Davis (neck) is out, so Gonzalez could be asked to simply stay out wide.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) said he is “ready” to play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Gonzalez told ESPN’s Mike Reiss that his shoulder is feeling “good” after sitting out in Weeks 4-5 to let it heal. This is an important game for the Patriots (3-2), who currently sit second in the AFC East, one spot ahead of the Jets (2-3). Gonzalez has traveled around the formation, at times covering the slot this season. This week, he will likely be tasked with covering Garrett Wilson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Patriots declared CB Christian Gonzalez, QB Behren Morton, OL Dametrious Crownover, CB Carlton Davis III, CB Karon Prunty, and CB Channing Cananda inactive for Week 5 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: New England’s injury-ravaged secondary could have a tough time slowing down the highly efficient Vegas passing offense today. The absence of Gonzalez and Davis should be a boon for both Tre Tucker and Brock Bowers. Kirk Cousins, who has 11 touchdowns to four interceptions this season, is a solid streaming option against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez will not play in New England’s Week 5 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: He has not practiced or played since Week 3. Nothing we’ve seen has suggested he’ll be a Saturday IR candidate, but it also wouldn’t necessarily be surprising if that happened. The Pats also ruled out fellow starting CB Carlton Davis (neck) for Week 5, leaving non-existent Raiders receivers with matchup upgrades. (Cody White is about to touch the end zone paint again.)

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Gonzalez and fellow starting perimeter CB Carlton Davis (neck) have missed each of the Patriots’ first two practices this week, putting them on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Raiders. Las Vegas lines up Brock Bowers as a wide receiver most of the time. Missing both starting coverage defenders would make life tough on the defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Gonzalez has been sidelined with a shoulder injury since last week, missing the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills. Also not practicing were Carlton Davis (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring). We’ll see if any of these corners can practice enough to play for Week 5, but Raiders WR Tre Tucker is headed for a good matchup against a banged up Patriots secondary this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) will not play in New England’s Week 4 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Gonzalez did not practice at any point this week after popping up on the injury report Wednesday; his status seems to be in doubt for Week 5 at this point as well. The Patriots also ruled out DT Christian Barmore. They’ll be without their best coverage player against the Bills, elevating the matchup for D.J. Moore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Back-to-back missed practices throw Gonzalez’s Week 4 status in real jeopardy. There are few players who mean as much to their defense as Gonzalez does, and if he is out against the Bills it will be open season for D.J. Moore and Khalil Shakir in what oddsmakers are predicting to be a shootout. Patriots DT Christian Barmore (shoulder) remained sidelined as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: This is one to watch for fantasy purposes. The Patriots are tasked with keeping the Bills’ passing offense in check this week. Doing so without their top coverage defender will be difficult. This is a new injury for Gonzalez. Patriots DT Christian Barmore (shoulder) was also sidelined on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: The Patriots and CB Christian Gonzalez are in agreement on a four-year, $135 million deal, according to ESPN’s Ian Rapoport.
