https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: It’s $102 million guaranteed for the 24-year-old Gonzalez, who is entering his fourth season after being drafted 17th overall in 2023. Gonzalez went without an interception during the regular season last year, but he was a Pro Bowler anyway and he did come up with a huge pick in the fourth quarter of the AFC Championship versus the Broncos. The Patriots had him under control for two more years after exercising his fifth-year option in April.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is questionable for New York’s Week 6 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: He did upgrade to a full practice and Aaron Glenn told reporters he expects Sadiq to play. Sadiq’s fantasy upside is well-known, but with Mason Taylor back and Omar Cooper Jr. also pushing to play, his target volume has shrunk quite a bit from some of the early-season scenarios we’ve seen. He’s likely a TE2 at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: He has been limited twice and doesn’t look close to clearing concussion protocol. It’s become rarer for players to launch a Friday comeback to get off protocol, but it’s not unprecedented. Sadiq looks like he’s on the doubtful side of questionable heading into Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq remains in the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: The good news is that Sadiq was able to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday. Sadiq suffered the head injury in Week 5 against Cleveland and did not return to action. Mason Taylor led the team’s tight ends with a 59 percent route rate against the Browns, catching all three of his targets for 23 yards. If Sadiq remains in the protocol tomorrow, he would be a long shot to play in Week 6. Taylor in that case would be a desperation streaming option in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq suffered a concussion in the Jets’ Week 5 game against the Browns and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: To make matters worse, Sadiq suffered the injury in the process of losing a fumble. Targeted on a 3rd-and-9 near the goal line in the third quarter, Sadiq was short of the first down and got “Peanut punched” for the giveaway. With neither side getting anything going in rainy New Jersey conditions, Sadiq had just two receptions for three yards before going down, getting out-produced by a returning Mason Taylor in the process. Now highly questionable for Week 6 against the Patriots, Sadiq will not be on the streamer radar if given the go-ahead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Jets TE Mason Taylor (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Taylor’s return could be problematic for rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq. Sadiq posted a 7/105/1 receiving line two weeks ago before goose-egging last week. Taylor is not a serious receiving threat, but he can eat into Sadiq’s snap share. Sadiq likely remains a viable TE1, but his volatility just increased a tad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq did not catch any of his three targets in the Jets’ Week 4 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: A week after breaking out with 105 yards on seven catches against Detroit, Sadiq came up empty. He ran a route on 12 of the Jets’ 20 drop backs on a miserably low volume day for the New York offense. Sadiq split routes with Jeremy Ruckert, a less-than-bullish sign for the rookie’s involvement in the Jets offense moving forward. Sadiq will have some streaming appeal in Week 5 against the Browns if Mason Taylor remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (back) is questionable for New York’s Week 4 game against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: He did get in another limited session today, his third in a row, which would suggest he has a strong chance of playing. Sadiq will get a rankings boost with Breece Hall, Adonai Mitchell, and Mason Taylor all ruled out. He’s a fringe TE1, but one with an extremely high ceiling after last week’s 7/105/1 line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: It seems like he’ll be trending towards playing in Week 4, though it would be nice to see a full session on Friday. Sadiq isn’t necessarily a must-play TE1, but with Adonai Mitchell and Mason Taylor trending towards not playing, the circumstances that created his 105-yard explosion in Week 3 are certainly in place for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: We don’t know exactly what the issue is yet, but Sadiq hit the ground hard on his diving touchdown grab versus the Lions. He was slow to get up and grabbed his abdomen before slowly walking off the field. Sadiq eventually returned and was highly productive during the second half, so it doesn’t appear to be a major concern for Week 4. He is on the TE1/2 borderline, with both Mason Taylor and Adonai Mitchell looking unlikely to suit up this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught 7-of-8 targets for 105 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 3 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: With Mason Taylor and Adonai Mitchell out this week, Frank Reich treated Sadiq as his No. 2 receiver and the results were marvelous. Sadiq scored his first career receiving touchdown on a 24-yard diving grab into the end zone in the second quarter. He appeared to get banged up as he hit the ground and was slow to get up, but the first-round rookie eventually shook it off and remained productive in the second half. Sadiq’s role could take a hit if either Mitchell or Taylor is back next week, but it’s hard to imagine the team scaling things back all that much after this breakout performance. Sadiq will flirt with a TE1 ranking when he takes on the Bears in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: The Patriots’ No. 2 running back was limited all week after being diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain. He told reporters today that he was surprised he could practice this week, and is feeling “pretty good.” If active, he will be a FLEX starter, but Rhamondre Stevenson should lead the backfield in touches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Unlike yesterday, Henderson was spotted at the open portion of practice and appears to be making a real run to play in Week 6. If not for the report that he’d miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain, this would be a pretty clear trend towards Henderson playing. As is, we’ll see what happens on Friday. It sure seems like he’ll hit the questionable line one way or another, but how it looks will be important as far as figuring out his Week 6 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson wasn’t spotted during the portion of practice open to the media but apparently got on the field at some point later in the session. It’s a truly stunning development for Henderson, given that it was reported this morning that he is expected to miss multiple weeks. We still expect him to sit for Week 6, but even that isn’t guaranteed at this point. Henderson would likely be on a relatively strict pitch count if he plays, but his presence would, at a minimum, be a thorn in the side of Rhamondre Stevenson’s fantasy backers. This is officially an injury report to keep a close eye on throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson suffered his latest ankle injury in Week 5 against the Raiders. Schefter said Henderson is “regarded as a quick healer, so the Patriots are hoping his return is sooner rather than later.” Still, he could be sidelined for the next few weeks, leaving Rhamondre Stevenson as the team’s clear lead back. Corey Kiner, meanwhile, appears to be in line as the Patriots’ RB2 after seeing seven touches last week against the Raiders. Kiner should be stashed in most 12-team fantasy leagues for now. Stevenson profiles as a top-12 play until Henderson returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) has been ruled out in Week 5 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson had 38 yards on five touches before suffering the ankle injury on a sideline tackle in the second quarter. He needed help getting to the locker room and did not return to action. Henderson, who has dealt with a string of injuries over the past few months, could miss significant time, leaving Rhamondre Stevenson as the Patriots’ unquestioned workhorse back for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson exited the Patriots’ Week 5 game with an apparent lower leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson ripped off a nice 11-yard rush and was tackled low out of bounds. He was slow to get up before being helped to the New England locker room for further evaluation. The oft-injured Henderson was seeing better-than-usual usage before his injury. Rhamondre Stevenson will function as the team’s workhorse back if Henderson once again misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Stevenson already told reporters on Friday that he was “ready to go”, so this news item doesn’t come as much of a surprise. Stevenson will continue to operate as the Pats’ top option in high-leverage situations, though he could cede more work between the 20s to TreVeyon Henderson. Both backs are stuck as low-ceiling RB3 options this week.

The game ended shortly after that, so we didn’t get an official update on his injury from the team. Vrabel told reporters there is a chance he plays in Week 5, but it sounds like the veteran is on the wrong side of questionable as of Wednesday. TreVeyon Henderson’s role was dwindling in recent weeks, but Stevenson’s absence will thrust him right back into a workhorse role. He would be a high-end RB2 if Stevenson is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson rushed 14 times for 42 yards in the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson operated as the backup to Rhamodre Stevenson, playing on 25 of the team’s 70 snaps, compared to 49 for Stevenson, and seeing 14 runs to Stevenson’s 13. Stevenson also ran a route on 20 of the team’s 43 dropbacks, compared to 12 for Henderson. Henderson did show off his speed on an 11-yard run, his long of the day, when it seemed like the Bills had him dead to rights on a reverse, but he was able to beat safety Cole Bishop to the edge and turn it upfield. It also seemed like Stevenson hurt his knee on the final drive of the game, so Henderson could be in for a much bigger role if his backfield mate were to miss any time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson had eight rushes for 23 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars, adding one catch for six yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson and Rhamonrde Stevenson were bottled up in the first half before the Patriots abandoned the run game in the second half, down by three scores. Henderson nearly broke a couple runs in the first half but was tripped up before a big play could develop. A boom-bust running back option, Henderson will remain big-play dependent in Week 4 against a gettable Buffalo run defense. His lack of pass-game involvement will be an issue in PPR formats.

The Chargers are off to an 0-2 start and will be desperate to turn things around in Week 3 against the 2-0 Bills on the road in Buffalo. The veteran safety has totaled 10 tackles and one pass breakup in the first two games of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Chargers signed S Derwin James to a three-year, $75.6 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: James will now be making $25.2 million per year, slightly nudging out the Ravens’ Kyle Hamilton ($25.1 million per year) for highest-paid safety in the league. The deal includes $57.5 million guaranteed. James entered the offseason wanting a new contract before training camp and he gets one coming off back-to-back seasons of Pro Bowl and second-team All-Pro honors. He remains a versatile and hard-hitting centerfielder for the Chargers, captaining the defense for seven seasons, making five Pro Bowls in that time. James tied his career-high with three interceptions last seasons and finished with an 81.2 overall PFF grade, good for No. 8 among safeties. He was set to enter the final season of his contract but will now be signed to the Chargers through 2029.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz contract extension talks with S Derwin James and OLB Tuli Tuipulotu “will heat up after the draft.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: ESPN’s Kris Rhim said earlier this week that James “almost certainly want[s] a new deal before training camp starts” in mid-to-late July. The Chargers’ organized team activities are scheduled to run May 26-27, May 29, June 2-4 and June 8-11. Mandatory minicamp will run from June 16-18. If extensions have not been agreed upon by the time mandatory minicamp rolls around, James and Tuipulotu could choose to hold out. That at least gives us a benchmark to check up on. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: ESPN’s Kris Rhim believes Chargers S Derwin James “almost certainly want[s] a new deal before training camp starts.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: Entering his age-30 season, James has bounced back from early-career injuries and been one of the most dependable and versatile defenders in the NFL over the past four years. He posted an 83.7 PFF coverage grade in 2025 playing in the box, at slot, and even manning the defensive line at times. Rhim adds the usual “it seems likely that a deal will get done,” but the curious part here is: “Whether [Chargers GM Joe] Hortiz is willing to give a 30-year-old James a record deal is one of the biggest questions ahead of this season.” It sure sounds like James could be a potential trade candidate based on that sentence. The Chargers have not exactly been big spenders under Hortiz.

Lambert-Smith’s absence on kick returns will have more of an impact if he cannot go in the Wild Card against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.headline: Trey Lance completed 20-of-44 passes for 136 yards, one interception and lost one fumble in the Chargers’ 19-3, Week 18 loss to the Broncos, rushing nine times for 69 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.analysis: Chargers veteran slot WR Keenan Allen functioned as the offensive focal point this afternoon. Unfortunately, for Lance, Allen mostly ran quick-hitting routes that relied on the 33-year-old to pick up yards after the catch. Chargers rookie WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith is to blame for Lance’s interception, tipping a catchable pass into Broncos slot CB Ja’Quan McMillian’s hands for the pick-six. Lance did a great job evading Broncos OLB Nik Bonitto for much of the game, but Bonitto got the better of Lance late in the game by forcing a fumble with a well-aimed punch. Lance connected with WR Derius Davis for a short touchdown late in the game, but it was called back due to an illegal formation penalty. The 25-year-old backup heads back to the bench for the Chargers’ Wild Card Weekend matchup against the Patriots.

Benton missing time would be another blow to a defensive line already playing without second-year defensive tackle Derrick Harmon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.headline: Steelers signed DL Keeanu Benton to a four-year, $72 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.analysis: The deal was first reported by NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Benton, who turned 25 in July, is entering his fourth season in the league after the Steelers selected him in the second-round of the 2023 NFL Draft. Coming off a career-best season that saw him record 5.5 sacks, Benton would’ve been set to hit free agency next offseason without a contract extension. Now Benton joins LB Nick Herbig, TE Darnell Washington and K Chris Boswell on the list of Steelers to receive extensions this offseason. With his $18 million per year contract, Benton is now the highest-paid defensive lineman in Steelers history.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.headline: Speaking on the Kaboly And Mack podcast, Mark Kaboly said Steelers DL Keeanu Benton could be “the odd man out” for an extension this summer.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.analysis: Kaboly and his co-host, Chris Mack, were wondering aloud why the Steelers have not yet signed CB Joey Porter to an extension this offseason when the conversation shifted to Benton. Both Kaboly and Mack were seemingly of the opinion that signing Benton, 24, to an extension does not appear to be a priority for the front office. Since joining the Steelers as a 2023 second-round pick, Benton ranks fifth on the team in sacks (nine) and quarterback pressures (75), 10th in solo tackles (82) and ties for sixth in TFLs (13). He is a capable defender, who should stick around in the league, but he may not earn a lucrative extension from team that drafted.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.headline: Steelers signed DL Keeanu Benton to his rookie contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.analysis: Benton, the 49th pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, signed a contract that includes guaranteed money in the third year -- an unprecedented deal, per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Benton performed well at the NFL Combine after serving as the anchor of Wisconsin’s defensive line, recording 60 tackles in his final two collegiate seasons. He should be a plus for a Steelers defense graded by PFF as 2022’s tenth best run-defending unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.headline: Steelers selected Wisconsin DL Keeanu Bentonwith the No. 49 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.analysis: The Senior Bowl standout boosted his stock at every step of the pre-Draft process, also posting an 8.65 RAS at the Combine. His 3-cone time in the 91st-percentile reflects his lacrosse background, while the explosion indicated by his 85th-percentile Broad Jump is apparent in his play. While amassing 60 tackles in his final two seasons in Madison, Benton showed great ability to anchor in the middle of a stout Badger defense. He has a great punch that knocks many offensive linemen off their spots while his chops and rips have martial art precision. Despite not being put in a position to put up multiple sacks, he still ended up with six sacks in his junior and senior seasons, resulting in All-B1G honors. The biggest problem with Benton is his tendency to play with a high pad level thus losing his anchor. He’ll join a Steelers defense with a rush defense graded by PFF as last season’s tenth best.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.headline: Wisconsin sophomore NT Keeanu Benton is considered to be a “special” talent by DL coach Ross Kolodziej.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.analysis: “Keeanu’s special,” Kolodziej told The Athletic. “He’s got great athleticism. A really good understanding of pressure and how to use his body and use blockers, momentum and position against them. Really, the guy has an upside. Not many guys come through here with the talent and ability and the ceiling that he has.” Benton (6'4/315) appeared in a total of 20 games during his first two seasons in Madison, accounting for 20 total tackles (12 solo, 4.0 for loss), 2.0 sacks and one forced fumble. The presence of he and Bryson Williams, who’s back to full strength after suffering a knee injury, is one of the reasons why many expect the Badgers to bounce back after going 4-3 in 2020.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.headline: Jalen Ramsey (wrist) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.analysis: Ramsey has a fracture in his wrist. He logged two limited sessions to close out the week. The Buccaneers’ passing attack is hardly imposing with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined, but the Steelers would surely love to have Ramsey out there.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.headline: Jalen Ramsey (wrist) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.analysis: It’s an upgrade from Wednesday’s DNP. Ramsey initially played through the wrist ailment in Week 4 and seems likely to continue to do so in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.headline: Jalen Ramsey (wrist) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.analysis: Ramsey is playing through a broken wrist. He missed last Wednesday’s practice and wound up playing every defensive snap for the Steelers on Sunday. A Wednesday DNP appears to be the new norm for him. We fully expect Ramsey to play in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.headline: Jalen Ramsey (wrist) is active for Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.analysis: Ramsey will attempt to play through a broken wrist this evening. He was limited in practice all week. The Steelers declared RB Rico Dowdle, QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, RB Eli Heidenreich, DL Kevin Jobity Jr. and DE Gabriel Rubio inactive for Week 4 against the Browns. Howard will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.headline: Jalen Ramsey (wrist) is questionable for Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.analysis: Ramsey was listed as limited for all three practices this week. He is attempting to play through a broken wrist and will likely wear a cast or brace if he is active. As expected, Joey Porter Jr. remains out this week admist his contrat dispute with the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.headline: ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reports Steelers CB Jalen Ramsey has a broken wrist.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.analysis: Ramsey has been listed as a limited practice participant for the Steelers’ first two practice reports. He told Pryor that his wrist is broken but still has a chance to play against the Browns on Thursday. If he does play, Ramsey will likely wear a brace/cast on his wrist after wearing one in practice this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.headline: Steelers DB Jalen Ramsey (wrist) was spotted in a sling at Monday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.analysis: This is a new injury for Ramsey, so we’ll see how it may affect his Week 4 status when the Steelers release their estimated injury report later in the day. Ramsey has appeared on 172 defensive snaps through the first three games of the season, totaling 17 tackles and one pass breakup thus far. Assuming this isn’t anything too severe, Ramsey could still have time to be ready to go for Thursday night’s game against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.headline: Steelers activated CB Jalen Ramsey from the active/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.analysis: Ramsey was placed on the PUP list due to a knee injury he suffered in minicamp, but it never sounded like this would be something that could keep him out for an extended period of time. The 31-year-old corner will presumably resume practicing with the team this week and should be in good shape for Week 1’s game against the Falcons barring any setback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.headline: Steelers placed CB Jalen Ramsey on the Physically Unable to Perform list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.analysis: Ramsey reportedly suffered a knee injury during minicamp and will begin camp on the PUP list. The 32-year-old corner can be removed from the list at any point, with general manager Omar Khan stating Tuesday that “it’ll take a couple weeks.” The move appears to be purely administrative.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.headline: ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reports the Steelers are expected to retain CB/S Jalen Ramsey.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-rams.analysis: There were some thoughts that the Steelers could move on from Ramsey, who is entering his age-32 season and has a $19.5 million cap hit, none of which is guaranteed. They apparently value his instincts enough to keep on keeping on with the veteran corner, who has shifted into more of a nickel and safety role as he’s aged.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: He did not practice this week and Jim Harbaugh called him “week to week.” Harris stands a chance at returning after Los Angeles’ Week 7 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Tre’ Harris (hamstring) is “more of a week-to-week [thing].”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris will probably have a real chance to play in Week 8, after the Chargers’ Week 7 bye. He thudded to a 16-yard outing in his big chance last week with Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey out and doesn’t necessarily need to be rostered if you’re in a bye week crunch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre Harris caught 2-of-4 targets for 16 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris was a complete non-factor even against the depleted Broncos’ secondary. The second-year wideout was the top target with Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston unavailable, and that extra attention didn’t help. Harris will try and bounce back in Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Ladd McConkey (foot) is not expected to play in Week 5 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: McConkey did not practice at all this week but was still given a questionable tag on Friday. He was always a long-shot to play after aggravating his foot injury in Week 4. With Quentin Johnston out this week as well, Tre’ Harris will be Justin Herbert’s No. 1 receiver. That puts him in the WR3 mix despite the Chargers’ dismal offensive performance through four weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 5 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Johnston got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday, so it was surprising to see him sent straight to “not playing.” Tre’ Harris figures to step in as Los Angeles’ top outside receiver by snaps this week and is a worthwhile FLEX play, even against a formidable Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Johnston and TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) both remained limited today, though WR Brenen Thompson (quad) downgraded. He did not practice, nor did Ladd McConkey (foot). Tre’ Harris could end up being the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver, but he would only be a FLEX against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre Harris caught 3-of-5 targets for 60 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: For the second straight week, Harris finished with the most receiving yards on the day for the Chargers. For the second straight week — and fourth week in a row for Los Angeles — it wasn’t enough. If Ladd McConkey (foot) is unable to go, Harris will be the top target again in Week 5 against the Broncos, but against that tough group, he can’t be treated as more than a FLEX option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris caught 6-of-7 targets for 76 yards receiving in a Week 3 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This is the second game in a row that Harris has led the Chargers in receiving, but this was not simply because of one catch, like last week. Harris looked good in this one, making a few nice hands catches and showing some ability to gain yards after the catch. He only ran a route on 27 of the team’s 43 dropbacks, but with the team now 0-3, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see the Chargers try to get Harris involved more next week against the Seahawks. Even if he doesn’t produce in a tough matchup, he’s worth a bench stash in most league types.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris caught 1-of-3 targets for 53 yards in the Chargers’ Week 2 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris broke free for a 53-yard strike early in the second half. He nearly took it to the house but was pushed out of bounds at the five-yard line, setting up an eventual Oronde Gadsden touchdown. Harris wasn’t heavily involved in the Bolts’ passing attack despite Ladd McConkey being hampered by a rib injury. With McConkey presumably getting healthier for Week 3, Harris is deep in the WR6/7 range for his upcoming matchup with Buffalo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre Harris caught 3-of-6 targets for 20 yards in the Chargers’ Week 1 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris saw a boost in playing time with Ladd McConkey sidelined with a chest injury. Most of Harris’ looks from Justin Herbert were of the short-area variety; he averaged 7.5 air yards per target and averaged 2.9 yards after contact per reception. Harris could have some draw in deeper leagues if McConkey misses time. The Chargers have a favorable matchup in Week 2 against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said he did not know if McConkey or Quentin Johnston would be on snap counts on Sunday. Cool. What we do know is that the Chargers desperately need a win and McConkey is their best receiver, so the incentives are certainly aligned to get McConkey into the fantasy WR3 discussion even with a pitch count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey is on track to once again be active on game day, but it is unclear how involved he will be. Two limited sessions are a good sign, but it would be great to see him practice fully tomorrow. In that instance, starting him as a WR2 would be far more palatable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said he expects Ladd McConkey (foot) to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: We, in turn, expect McConkey to be listed as a limited participant. An update will be provided if he practices in full. The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver was an emergency active last week, goose-egging in the box score. His early-week return to practice puts him on track to play in Week 6 against the Chiefs, but it would be great to see him practice in full by the end of the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said it’s “possible” that Ladd McConkey (foot) is “working back in this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey was active last week but an emergency-only player and played zero snaps. With the Chargers having a Week 7 bye, we’d be surprised if they pushed McConkey to play unless they really needed him. Unfortunately, since he was already active last week, we know that they may really need him. His status is up in the air ahead of Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Ladd McConkey (foot) is not expected to play in Week 5 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey did not practice at all this week but was still given a questionable tag on Friday. He was always a long-shot to play after aggravating his foot injury in Week 4. With Quentin Johnston out this week as well, Tre’ Harris will be Justin Herbert’s No. 1 receiver. That puts him in the WR3 mix despite the Chargers’ dismal offensive performance through four weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 5 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey did not practice all week — though they might tack something on in the non-media period on Friday to make it look better — and is clearly just trying to gut it out at this point. He’ll likely be on a snap count if he does play. But Denver’s cornerback room is severely banged up, so McConkey likely remains in low-end WR2 range this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey is firmly on the wrong side of questionable at this point, and unfortunately, the rest of the Chargers’ wide receiver corps is fairly banged up. The Chargers are on bye in Week 7. Hopefully, McConkey’s foot injury is not serious enough to keep him out until Week 8. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (foot) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Though head coach Jim Harbaugh ambiguously said we would get McConkey in practice, the 24-year-old is officially listed as a non-participant on Wednesday. Harbaugh also previously stated McConkey will be day-to-day after he re-aggravated the foot injury in Week 4. Ultimately, it’s unclear if McConkey will play this week given he generally pushes through injuries with little practice time, but a re-aggravation could lead to a game missed this time around. Stay tuned for practice reports later in the week to provide clarity on his Week 5 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Ladd McConkey (foot) will be at practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: The phrasing is slightly ambiguous, but we believe he is saying McConkey will be present and participating in some capacity — likely as a limited participant. Harbaugh told reporters yesterday that McConkey was considered day-to-day after aggravating his foot injury in Week 4 against the Seahawks. Getting in a limited session to begin the week gives him a chance to play in Week 5 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Ladd McConkey (foot) is day to day.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey has spent this season as more minute to minute than day to day. He left Week 4’s game with a re-aggravation of his foot injury that was managed all week leading up to the game. It would be unsurprising to see him managed again this week, and he is no sure thing to suit up against the Broncos on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Joe Alt (neck) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Alt was off to see a specialist, per Jim Harbaugh, on Monday. He did not practice. At this point an IR stint seems more likely than not. The four rookie line should be intact for the Chargers this week with Kayode Awosika also ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Joe Alt (neck) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Chargers OG Kayode Awosika (fibula), S Derwin James (hamstring) and CB Donte Jackson (hamstring) also remained sidelined. The Chargers take on the division-rival Chiefs this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Joe Alt (neck) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Alt missed Week 5 after not practicing last week and opens up Week 6 as a non-participant. Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Tuesday that Alt would visit a specialist for his neck injury. G Kayode Awosika (fibula) is also still sidelined. Justin Herbert’s offensive line looks like it will still be missing both players this week; the Chiefs’ defensive line will have a good day against the inexperienced depth that will start for the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said OT Joe Alt (neck) will see a specialist.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Last week’s offensive line in front of Justin Herbert featured four rookies and Cole Strange. It doesn’t look like it’s getting much better in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chargers OT Joe Alt (neck) is expected to miss Week 5 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: An already disappointing season continues to tumbler for the Chargers. LT Rashawn Slater (ankle) is already out this week and Alt will join him on the injury report. Neither starting tackle has been able to stay healthy over the course of their careers, making life difficult for QB Justin Herbert. Though Alt is expected to miss this week against the Broncos, Rapoport adds that there are “no plans” for him to go on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Joe Alt (neck) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: In true Chargers fashion, their once-promising offensive line has been scattered to the winds by injuries. Left tackle Rashawn Slater won’t play this week because of an ankle injury. Now their right tackle could also be put on ice. Already one of the most disappointing offenses of the year, there’s almost no hope for the Bolts to turn things around this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said RT Joe Alt (neck) is still being evaluated after Los Angeles’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Alt suffered the injury in Week 4 when Nick Emmanwori slammed into him from behind while trying to down Justin Herbert. It sounds like there’s a real chance that he misses Week 5. Somehow, the 2025 Chargers offensive line has returned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Joe Alt (ankle) and Rashawn Slater (knee) have been medically cleared for the start of training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Harbaugh didn’t say exactly how much either player would participate in the opening practices of camp and even noted that the whole team is starting off in a “ramp-up” stage. Alt suffered two high-ankle sprains last year, the second one requiring season-ending surgery. Slater did not play at all in 2025 because of a ruptured patellar tendon. Though it would make sense for both players to be limited during the first few practices of training camp, it doesn’t sound like any player will have any lingering issues heading into 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said it, “It looks that way,” when asked if Joe Alt (ankle) and Rashawn Slater (knee) will be ready for training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Chargers GM Joe Hortiz said both players were ahead of schedule when asked about them a week before the NFL Draft. Slater suffered a season-ending ruptured a patellar tendon last August and did not play a snap in 2025. Alt was unable to recover from a high-ankle sprain during the season and finished the year on injured reserve. All signs point to the Chargers having their elite tackle duo healthy for the start of the year. With an improved offensive line and Mike McDaniel on the headset, this is truly a make-or-break year for Justin Herbert.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz thinks OTs Rashawn Slater (knee) and Joe Alt (ankle) will be “involved in some capacity” at the team’s first workout next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Both players are ahead of schedule, though Hortiz smartly notes, “coming back from injuries, you don’t rush anything.” The goal is for both players to be ready for the start of training camp. Slater ruptured a patellar tendon last August, ending his 2025 season before it began. Alt attempted to come back from a high-ankle sprain in-season last year before suffering a second high-ankle sprain in the same joint, ending his season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.headline: Steelers ruled out Roman Wilson (finger) for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.analysis: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported earlier this week that Wilson was going to miss a couple of weeks, so this is not breaking news. The Steelers’ wide receiver corps is very thin. DK Metcalf (illness) is now questionable to play. Germie Bernard should be in fantasy lineups this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Steelers WR Roman Wilson is expected to miss a “couple of weeks” after suffering a finger injury in Week 5 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.analysis: According to Fowler, Wilson is seeking a second opinion on his injury. He was initially diagnosed with a dislocated finger, but given today’s report, it sounds like this may be more severe than initially expected. Wilson entered Week 5 with back-to-back 60-plus-yard games and had been targeted six times in each of his first four games. Rookie Germie Bernard, who caught 6-of-9 targets for 80 yards in Week 5’s win over the Colts, will be worth a claim on waivers this week and profiles as a WR4/FLEX option in PPR leagues for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.headline: Roman Wilson has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 5 against the Colts with a dislocated finger.
https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.analysis: Wilson had just one target in the first half. He pinned the reception to his hip, but the ball was ripped loose by a defender, which not only made the pass incomplete but also seemed to dislocate Wilson’s finger. With Michael Pittman Jr. also hurt, we should continue to see a lot of Germie Bernard in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.headline: Steelers placed WR Michael Pittman (foot) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.analysis: Pittman aggravated the foot injury that cost him Week 2 last week and will now miss four games, at minimum, while on injured reserve. Roman Wilson appears to be the primary beneficiary of Pittman’s absence and has seen six targets in each game this season while mostly playing a situational role. Wilson is a priority waiver addition over rookie Germie Bernard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Michael Pittman re-aggravated his foot injury and will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.analysis: McCarthy told reporters the team is evaluating Pittman’s roster spot, meaning they could place him on injured reserve. He would miss at least four weeks while on IR. Pittman tried to play through the foot injury but only made it two weeks before aggravating the issue. He was spotted using a scooter to support his foot in the locker room on Wednesday. We suspect the Steelers will place him on IR to give Pittman enough time to fully recover. Germie Bernard will now operate as the team’s permanent WR3, with Roman Wilson taking on more work as the clear No. 2 receiver. Both players will be decent FLEX options for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.headline: Roman Wilson caught 3-of-6 targets for 74 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.analysis: Wilson got the scoring started in the first quarter to cap a 17-play opening drive from 12 yards out. He continued to work in a downfield role, padding his stats with 62 additional yards on two more receptions, in addition to drawing an illegal contact penalty earlier on the first drive. Wilson wold briefly depart late in the fourth quarter following his final reception of the game as he appeared to land on the ball awkwardly going out of bounds. Fantasy managers will want to track his practice status closely ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Colts, where Wilson will carry interesting FLEX appeal in a growing role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.headline: Roman Wilson caught 3-of-6 targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.analysis: Most of Wilson’s production came on the Steelers’ opening drive. He caught a five-yard pass on the second play of the game, and two plays later, he would find himself on the receiving end of a 38-yard touchdown pass from Aaron Rodgers after beating his defender in single coverage down the left sideline for the score. Wilson appeared in 18 offensive snaps through the team’s first four possessions, but appeared on only five snaps after he let a ball bounce off his hands and land in the arms of a Bengals defender for an interception. Wilson’s six targets were still enough to lead all Steelers’ receivers on the day, but he’ll need to provide more consistent production before he can be considered a legit fantasy option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.headline: Roman Wilson caught 5-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.analysis: Wilson tied with rookie Germie Bernard for second-most wide receiver snaps on the team, both tallying 55 snaps. He saw mostly short-yardage targets, with his longest reception tallying nine yards. Wilson’s role is as the clear WR3 in the Steelers offense; he did not see a role increase with Michael Pittman out of the game. Playing in a low-ceiling Steelers offense, Wilson is a WR5 at best for Week 3 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.headline: Roman Wilson caught 3-of-6 targets for 26 yards in the Steelers’ Week 1 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.analysis: Wilson’s six targets tied him for second on the team and also don’t include a defensive pass interference penalty he drew on a deep ball in the first half. Wilson also had a near touchdown when a deep pass was broken up as he was going to the ground with the ball. Despite having so many more targets than Michael Pittman Jr., Wilson ran 29 routes to Pittman Jr.'s 42, so Wilson remains the clear WR3 in a potentially low-scoring offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.headline: Aaron Rodgers said Roman Wilson had a “fantastic camp.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/roman-wilson/0.analysis: It was a bit of a compliment sandwich, with Rodgers opening his comments by mentioning a route Wilson screwed up early in camp and again today. Rodgers did, however, say Wilson will have to play a big role for the team and that he has the utmost confidence in him. Rodgers is infamously punitive to his younger players, and the Steelers have second-round rookie Germie Bernard behind Wilson on the depth chart. Wilson is firmly ahead of Bernard for now, but one mistake during the regular season could flip the WR3 role in an instant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf (illness) is questionable for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: This is unfortunate. The Steelers placed Michael Pittman on injured reserve recently, and both Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek are out this week. Metcalf has a chance to play this week, but fantasy managers must, unfortunately, keep an eye on the news over the next 48 hours. Rookie Germie Bernard could lead the team in targets again this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 3-of-4 targets for 12 yards in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: This was not the game many expected against a beleaguered Colts defense. Two of Metcalf’s three catches were on screens behind the line of scrimmage, and he was only targeted 10 yards down the field once. Aaron Rodgers is not having much success throwing the ball deep down the field, which means Metcalf is likely going to be a touchdown-dependent WR3 in fantasy next week against the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 5-of-9 targets for 115 yards in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Metcalf managed just three receptions through the first three-plus quarters of play before making two grabs for 50 yards on the team’s penultimate possession, eventually resulting in a tie game with under two minutes to play following a successful two-point conversion. Even though this marks the third game in four tries with nine or more targets, Week 4 was the first game with more than 40 yards for Metcalf as he works to strengthen his connection with Rodgers in a downfield role. In fact, Metcalf more than doubled his year-to-date yardage total from the previous three games against two of the better coverage corners in the league. The individual matchup doesn’t get much easier ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Colts, who boast another top corner duo in Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward. Metcalf remains a wide range of outcomes weekly WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 3-of-5 targets for 31 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Metcalf has yet to crack 40 yards in a game this season, but he did manage to find the end zone for a six-yard touchdown late in the third quarter. The big plays have not been there for Metcalf thus far, who has a long catch of 16 yards. Metcalf will be on the WR3/WR4 radar for next week’s game against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 4-of-9 targets for 27 yards in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Metcalf had an inefficient day, finishing fifth on the Steelers in yards despite leading the team in targets. He was unable to get open downfield and Aaron Rodgers’ struggles made many intermediate targets fell incomplete. Metcalf dropped a critical third-down pass in the third quarter, continuing his drop issues from last week. A second straight inefficient week despite a high volume of targets makes Metcalf a rough fantasy play moving forward. Despite Michael Pittman’s absence, the fantasy points are just not consistent for Metcalf in the Steelers passing game. He will be a low-end fantasy WR3 for Week 3 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: Steelers WR Michael Pittman (foot) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Pittman did not practice at all this week. If he plays, he could be fairly limited. We tentatively expect him to be inactive on game day, though. Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth had a solid role last week and could take on No. 2 pass-catcher duties if Pittman indeed cannot play. Steelers WR DK Metcalf will almost assuredly take on a larger role, operating as the team’s receiving focal point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: Aaron Rodgers said he’s “going to keep feeding” DK Metcalf.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: Metcalf caught just 4-of-10 targets in Week 1 and was flagged twice for offensive pass interference while struggling to make contested catches. It wasn’t ideal. But Rodgers’ words should sooth any thought of bumping Metcalf down the ranks just yet. “I’m not worried about DK at all, man,” Rodgers said.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: DK Metcalf caught 4-of-10 targets for 40 yards in the Steelers’ Week 1 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: It could have been a much bigger day for Metcalf, who dropped an easy 20-yard catch over the middle of the field and also a potential long touchdown pass. The touchdown pass would have been a difficult grab in tight coverage, but it did hit him in the hands. Metcalf ran a route on every dropback for the Steelers, but Aaron Rodgers continued to show that he’s far more comfortable over the middle of the field than deep down the field at this point in his career. That will continue to make Metcalf a TD-dependent option in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reports Steelers WRs DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman are “expected to be ready” for Week 1.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: This was always though to be the case, with the team’s decision to keep only six receivers through cuts Sunday seemingly backing that notion up. Pryor adds that the teams is expected to “ease in” both Metcalf and Pittman, but it certainly sounds as if each receiver will be on the field in less than two weeks for Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.headline: Steelers restructured DK Metcalf’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dk-metcalf.analysis: It’s a simple restructure, converting base salary into a signing bonus. Per ESPN’s Field Yates, the move creates nearly $18 million in cap space for Pittsburgh. The transaction could be an indication that the Steelers need cap space for another move, but it’s much more likely that the team simply wants flexibility down the road. Metcalf remains signed through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton Jr. (hamstring) is getting “closer” but won’t play in Las Vegas’ Week 6 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton is in Week 2 of his 21-day window and figures to return in Week 7 or Week 8. Obviously there’s not much reason to trust him in fantasy at this time, but he may find a real role on Las Vegas’ depth chart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders ruled out Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) for Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: The Raiders activated Thornton’s 21-day practice window this week. Despite the young wide receiver saying he feels “ready to play,” the team has determined that he needs more time. With Jalen Nailor (concussion) also ruled out, Cody White (ankle) and Malik Benson will round out three-wide receiver sets behind Tre Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) returned to practice and feels “ready to play.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has been on injured reserve since late August, practicing in full for the first time on Wednesday. He told Raiders media that he is “overly confident” in his hamstring and is “ready to play.” With Jack Bech on injured reserve, there is room for the 23-year-old speedster to earn targets if he plays in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said it’s too early to say whether WR Dont’e Thornton Jr. (undisclosed) will resume practicing next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: The lanky speedster was placed on injured reserve late in August. He is not exceptionally talented, but he can contribute meaningfully to an NFL offense. Getting him back would help keep safeties honest. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders placed WR Dont’e Thornton Jr. on the reserved/injured list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has been dealing with an undisclosed injury that has prevented the wideout from practicing over the last month. The 23-year-old can return in four weeks, but there’s no timeline as to when the 2025 fourth-round pick will return to the Vegas lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton is still working his way back from an undisclosed injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: We still don’t know what Thornton is dealing with, but the second-year receiver hasn’t practiced since August 7th. Kubiak said earlier this month that he expected Thornton to return sometime during the preseason, but that didn’t come to fruition. Even if he’s able to make it back on the practice field ahead of Week 1, Thornton is unlikely to make any major contributions to the offense at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said he expects Dont’e Thornton (undisclosed) to return at some point in the preseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has missed nearly a whole week of practice, paving the way for Jack Bech and rookie Malik Benson to see more reps. Kubiak said Thornton has “been banged up a little bit” this training camp, but did not go into further detail on his situation. Thornton caught 10 passes for 135 scoreless yards last season after generating plenty of camp hype. He is not on the fantasy radar at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders WR Dont’e Thornton (undisclosed) missed his fourth straight practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton was at practice in street clothes Tuesday, missing his fourth straight. He left a training camp practice early last week and has not received a diagnosis or return timetable. Jack Bech, Jalen Nailor, and Tre Tucker are listed as the Raiders’ starting wide receivers on the team’s first unofficial depth chart of the preseason. Thornton is listed as Nailor’s backup but may be losing ground to Malik Benson as he misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders WR Malik Benson operated as the team’s WR2 with WR Jalen Nailor and WR Dont’e Thornton “nicked up” on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: The depth chart placement is a tad curious because it suggests Benson ran ahead of either WR Tre Tucker or WR Jack Bech. Benson has been rotating in with the first-team offense for more than a week, so this isn’t groundbreaking news, but one wonders if he can use the opportunity to make a compelling case for a starting role in three-wide receiver sets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: ESPN’s Ryan McFadden reports that Raiders WR Malik Benson is taking reps with the first-team offense.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: The Raiders are reportedly rotating five different wide receivers through team drills, including Tre Tucker, Jack Bech, Jalen Nailor and Dont’e Thornton. Tucker is the most proven player of the bunch and should be expected to secure a starting role. Things are fluid beyond that. McFadden named Benson, a sixth-round rookie, his “biggest surprise” of spring practices. He reportedly fostered a strong connection with QB Fernando Mendoza. Given his draft capital, Benson is likely a long shot to earn a starting role, but he also possesses intriguing upside as a field stretcher. Don’t bank on a breakout, but keeping an eye on him this summer is worthwhile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) will play in Las Vegas’ Week 6 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: This per coach Klint Kubiak, so we assume Nailor has passed protocol. He’s only a FLEX play at this point as it’s hard to trust any weapons in the Vegas offense beyond Brock Bowers, even in a good matchup against a struggling Bills defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) resumed practicing in a red non-contact jersey.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor will likely end up being listed as a limited participant today. He has a chance to play in Week 6 against the Bills, but his odds would be better if he had returned yesterday. If active, Nailor would only be a boom-bust WR5/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor suffered a concussion in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs, missing Week 5 against the Patriots while still in the protocol. He starts out the week not practicing, indicating he is not close to clearing protocol. Though he still has a chance to play this week, Nailor does not need to be stashed for fantasy purposes amid a murky wide receiver corps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Raiders ruled out Jalen Nailor (concussion) for Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: The Raiders entered the season with a thin wide receiver corps, and the unit just got thinner. Tre Tucker will continue functioning as the team’s top wide receiver and second pass catcher, backed up by Cody White (ankle) and rookie Malik Benson. Nailor does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Raiders WR Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor will almost assuredly sit out the Raiders’ Week 5 game against the Patriots. Fellow WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) is practicing in full, and WR Cody White (ankle) remains limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Raiders WR Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor suffered a concussion against the Chiefs in Week 4 and starts out the week not practicing. This indicates he is on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Patriots. Fellow WR Cody White (ankle) was limited as well, though Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) returned to practice, giving the Raiders some reinforcement with Nailor still in concussion protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) will not return in Week 4 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor took a hard hit from Chiefs S Nohl Williams in the second quarter and was forced to go to the sideline to be evaluated. The team has now announced that Nailor will not be returning for Sunday’s game. Nailor will end the day with zero receptions on zero targets and will need to clear concussion protocol if he hopes to return in Week 5 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor picked up on first down on the Raiders’ opening drive after going in motion and running a crossing route. Raiders QB Kirk Cousins was off-target on his other two throws to Nailor. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for nine yards in the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor caught three passes for 27 yards on five targets last week. His role shrank this time around with Tre Tucker erupting for 119 yards and a score. It will be hard for him to see more work in Week 3 if Brock Bowers is back. He is buried in the WR6 ranks ahead of the Raiders’ upcoming game versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 3-of-5 targets for 27 yards in the Raiders’ Week 1 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor picked up eight yards on QB Kirk Cousins’ first pass of the day, but quieted down after that. His next catch came with just two minutes left in the first half. Nailor’s role looked too unreliable for serious FLEX consideration in Week 2 against the Chargers, even if the Raiders will pass more there.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Monangai is “trending in the right direction,” but remains week-to-week. D’Andre Swift should handle a sizable workload with Monangai sidelined. Roschon Johnson may be able to catch a few passes, but he makes for a shaky FLEX bet. Monangai should be stashed safely on fantasy football benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Exactly one week ago, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Monangai’s turf toe injury jeopardized his availability over the next 1-2 weeks. Unfortunately, he is on the wrong side of questionable at this time. Roschon Johnson could contribute on passing downs if Monangai cannot play, but D’Andre Swift will handle the majority of the backfield touches this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai missed Week 5 due to thumb and toe injuries; he did not practice all of last week and was estimated as a non-participant for the Bears’ Wednesday walk-through. A DNP listing after already missing a week is not a good sign for the 24-year-old’s availability. Starter D’Andre Swift (hip) was notably not on the injury report. Monangai will need to practice to have a chance to play but fantasy managers will need to start looking at backup Roschon Johnson as a potential fill-in for Week 6 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) will not play in Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai is currently in a walking boot and is considered week-to-week, per head coach Ben Johnson. Monangai reportedly consulted a specialist for his turf toe after the injury was revealed to be worse than initially expected, but he is not considered a candidate for injured reserve at this time. Backup Roschon Johnson will be elevated to RB2 duties for the foreseeable future, but we wouldn’t expect him to see the same volume as Monangai, who has averaged 15 carries/gm through the Bears’ first four games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the “belief is that D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) should be able to go” in Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: We will get a better sense of Swift’s availability soon when the Bears release their final injury report of the week. After being a DNP in Wednesday’s practice, Swift was able to log a limited session on Thursday, which is a good sign for his availability with one practice left to go. Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), who has yet to practice this week, could be at risk of missing Week 5, which could lead to a busy day for Swift, while Roschon Johnson would serve as the Bears’ RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Kyle Monangai has a turf toe injury, “placing uncertainty around his availability over the next 1-2 weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: At the beginning of the week, Monangai’s thumb injury was the initial cause for concern. The team kept quiet about the toe issue until Wednesday’s injury report. Per Fowler, Monangai is hoping to play through the turf toe injury, but consecutive absences to begin the week put him on the wrong side of questionable. Given the Bears’ run-heavy tactics, RB3 Roschon Johnson is worth adding for running back-needy fantasy managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Ben Johnson has repeatedly said this is not an issue and that Monangai is “going to be okay,” but we’d sure like to see a Friday full session to prove that. As is, Monangai may be headed for a questionable listing for Week 5, even if the supposition will continue to be that he’ll play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Bears coach Ben Johnson continues to indicate the Monangai will be good to go for Week 5, but it is worth monitoring the Bears’ practice reports. D’Andre Swift (knee/hip) was also sidelined to begin the week. If Swift is unable to play, Monangai would take on a sizable workload in Week 5 against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Kyle Monangai’s thumb injury is “not an issue.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Johnson did add, “He had 30 carries, and he feels like he had 30 carries.” Monangai will play in Week 5 versus the Packers, but it doesn’t sound like he will double up D’Andre Swift in carries for the second week in a row. Expect a more even split of the work this week, with Swift potentially returning to his normal lead-back role. Even with fewer carries, Monangai is locked in as a fantasy RB3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Kyle Monangai (thumb) is “going to be OK” and that it was a “day to day deal.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai seemingly winds up on the injury report every other week, but he keeps playing and keeps playing well. We wouldn’t be surprised to see him listed again this week, but it sounds like he’s very much in line to play against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said Jawhar Jordan will be elevated off the practice squad to play against the Jaguars on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: Though he’s nominally the third back with David Montgomery out, the Texans tipped how they felt about Dare Ogunbowale as a running back by not using him a single time after Montgomery was ruled out against the Titans in Week 5. It seems likely that Jordan will be the main Woody Marks change-up in London, though given how poorly the Texans have ran the ball this year that probably doesn’t equate to much fantasy equity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans RB Jawhar Jordan (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in the Divisional Round against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: Jordan practiced fully on Friday, which is a great sign. He was unable to play in the Wild Card Round after injuring his ankle in Week 18. We expect Jordan to handle No. 2 rushing duties behind starting RB Woody Marks, though Marks could ultimately dominate touches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans RB Jawhar Jordan (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: Two sessions would seemingly give him a real chance to suit up, though it’s unclear if the Texans would make him the No. 2 back ahead of Nick Chubb after Chubb’s output against the Steelers last Monday night. Jordan is probably trending towards a questionable tag on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans RB Jawhar Jordan (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: Jordan suffered an ankle injury in Week 18 which caused him to miss the Wild Card win over the Steelers. The 26-year-old played well in a reserve role and was the Texans’ RB2 in Week 18 with Nick Chubb a healthy scratch. A limited practice session early in the week indicates Jordan is trending to return in the Divisional Round against the Patriots, though the Texans may keep both Jordan and Chubb active behind Woody Marks if Jordan is not fully healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans ruled out RB Jawhar Jordan (ankle) for the Wildcard Round against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: Jordan injured his ankle in Week 18 and failed to practice all week, eventually ruled out with the ailment. That leaves very little depth behind starting rookie Woody Marks, who could find himself in a workhorse role for the team’s Wildcard matchup against the Steelers. Nick Chubb appears likely to operate as the primary change of pace option while Dare Ogunbowale could rotate in on obvious passing situations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans RB Jawhar Jordan (ankle) did not practice Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: He looks incredibly unlikely to go based on the reporting that he suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 18. Nick Chubb will probably be a pure fill-in back on a few downs for the Texans behind Woody Marks on Monday night, making Marks a high-volume play for DFS or Playoff Best Ball purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans RB Jawhar Jordan (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: NBC Sports Houston’s Aaron Wilson reported this morning that testing confirms Jordan suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 18 against the Colts. He was unsurprisingly unable to practice on Thursday. The Texans face the Steelers on Monday. Veteran RB Nick Chubb would get his old job back as the team’s No. 2 rusher if Jordan cannot play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Jawhar Jordan rushed five times for three yards in the Texans’ Week 18 win over the Colts
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: The more noteworthy bit is that Jordan played ahead of Nick Chubb, who was a healthy scratch in Week 18. Jordan could wind up being Houston’s No. 2 back in the playoffs. He’s more of an outside zone specialist than someone the Texans trust all the time, but Jordan undoubtedly has more physical upside than Chubb at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Jawhar Jordan rushed eight times for 36 yards in the Texans’ Week 17 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: Jordan out-snapped veteran RB Nick Chubb 11-to-5 and out-touched him 8-to-1 against the Chargers on Saturday. After starting RB Woody Marks took a hard hit from Chargers OLB Khalil Mack in the fourth quarter, it was Jordan, not Chubb, who replaced Marks briefly in the lineup. He is the Texans’ No. 2 running back and should be stashed accordingly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Jawhar Jordan rushed 15 times for 53 yards in the Texans’ Week 16 win over the Raiders
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: He added 17 yards on five catches on his five targets, a performance some are calling “one catch short of a Rex Burkhead.” Jordan got the majority of the carries, but was held just under half the offensive snaps at 30 of 62 per PFF’s early data. It wasn’t particularly impressive, but Jordan was weighed down by a few ghastly Nick Caley calls that were dead on arrival. Jordan will only be a FLEX play next week if he retains this role, but Woody Marks (ankle) probably has a real chance to play in Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said “We’ll see. We’ll find out,” when asked if the Giants have reached the point where he’ll make adjustments due to the team’s fumbling issues.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Giants beat writer Dan Duggan chimed in with “I would be very surprised if [Cam] Skattebo has the same RB1 workload on Sunday that he’s had in the first five games.” Skattebo has put the ball on the ground four times in the first five games. Najee Harris has one in 27 carries and Tyrone Tracy has added two. It sounds like Harris may start to be a significant thorn in the side of Skattebo-reliant managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 13 times for 59 yards in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders, adding two receptions for 12 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo rushed for just 12 yards on six carries in the first half as he and the Giants struggled on the ground for most of the day. He would come up with a few big runs in the second half, one of which resulted in a 19-yard gain in overtime as the Giants were attempting to drive into position for a game-winning field goal. Unfortunately for Skattebo, disaster struck later on the drive when he lost a fumble on the Commanders’ 24-yard line, which was recovered by Washington and ended any hopes of a Giants’ victory. Poor late-game clock management by the Commanders made Skattebo’s fumble a little less costly, as the two sides would end Sunday’s game in a tie, but it’s impossible to overstate how big a 4-1 start to the season would be for the Giants, who are playing in a struggling NFC East. Skattebo hasn’t rushed for more than 81 yards in any game this season and has only one touchdown to his name. His reliable volume continues to put him in fringe RB1/RB2 territory, but it’s been a disappointing start for the second-year back. He’ll look to turn things around next week against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Cam Skattebo’s shoulder injury is “not a concern.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo was cleared from the injury report on Friday, so he was never going to miss this game. The good news is that the Giants don’t have any plans to limit his workload. Playing in a rain-soaked matchup with the NFC East rival Commanders, Skattebo is expected to see “an extremely heavy workload”, according to Garafolo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (shoulder) will play in Week 5 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo was limited in Wednesday and Thursday’s practices but will be good to go in what he called a “slogfest” on Sunday against the Commanders. With rain and wind forecast for Sunday’s game, the Giants will likely lean heavily on Skattebo, who has rushed for 68-235-1 this season while averaging a subpar 3.5 YPC.
