Skattebo profiles as a volume-based RB2 against a defense that has been stout against the run out of the gate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo was limited for the second day in a row, but he at least ditched his red non-contact jersey. The Giants’ lead running back should be good to go for Week 5 against the Commanders. He sits on the RB1/2 border once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (shoulder) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo was participating in a red non-contact jersey today. His limited participation puts him on track to play in Week 5 against the Commanders, but this is obviously worth tracking. The Giants’ starting running back has handled reliably larger workloads this season. Hopefully, he is feeling up to the task again on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 18 times for 58 yards in the Giants’ Week 4 win over the Cardinals, adding an eight-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: With the G-Men and Cardinals trading sacks and turnovers in a sloppy but close contest, Skattebo seemed to be in a 50-50 committee with Najee Harris. That is until Harris got “Peanut punched” at the 11:14 mark of the fourth quarter, losing a fumble. Harris was never heard from again as Skattebo received seven touches from that point forward. The G-Men are understandably hunting for some sort of alternative or caddie for their unexplosive, default lead back in Skattebo, but unsurprisingly, Harris is not going to be the answer in that regard. Skattebo will keep hanging around the low-end RB2 ranks heading into Week 5 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 20 times for 60 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans, adding three catches for 40 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: With the Titans struggling to amass more than a handful of first downs, John Harbaugh was more than happy to grind out three yards per carry with his lead back for the better part of four quarters. Skattebo’s only explosive play came on a downfield shot from Jameis Winston. Skattebo got open deep while Winston fled the pocket and the two connected for a 30-yard gain. That alone was enough to make Skattebo the team’s leading receiver. Skattebo’s strong workload will keep him in the RB2 ranks for Week 4 against the Cardinals, even though the offensive environment has taken a massive hit with Jaxson Dart out for the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 12 times for 36 yards in the Giants’ Week 2 loss to the Rams, adding 19 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: The Giants’ game plan was thrown for a loop when quarterback Jaxson Dart was forced from the game on the team’s first possession and were largely unable to get anything going with Jameis Winston under center. The result was a haphazard scheme thrown together to minimize Winston’s exposure to a relentless Rams defensive front, which drowned the fantasy production of all parties, to include Skattebo. More startling to Skattebo’s fantasy managers was the involvement of Najee Harris in the red zone, who was unable to cash in on two carries from the six on consecutive plays in the second quarter. Skattebo gets a plus matchup against the Titans in Week 3, where he returns to a viable RB2 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Although Skattebo was not targeted in the pass game, his 18 carries handily led the team. Furthermore, presumed backup Tyrone Tracy lost a fumble on one of his two carries, resulting in Devin Singletary taking over primary backup duties for the remainder of the game. Those two variables should keep Skattebo’s weekly volume high after showing no ill effects of the devastating ankle injury suffered in 2025. His touchdown now gives him eight total scores in nine professional appearances despite only six of those being starts, a rate that will keep Skattebo in the weekly borderline RB1 discussion moving forward. Tracy managed just two snaps to Singletary’s 25, leaving Singletary as the primary backup for the moment. It’s possible Najee Harris gets into this discussion after being a healthy scratch in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie reportedly injured his groin during Thursday’s practice, and is now questionable to play. Frankly, the Rams can probably get by without their No. 1 cornerback this week, though obviously it would be preferable to have him out there. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Rams signed CB Trent McDuffie to a four-year, $124 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter was the first to report the deal, which includes $100 million in guaranteed money. The two-time All-Pro becomes the highest-paid corner in NFL history and will now be under contract through the 2030 season. The Rams traded a bevy picks to the Chiefs last week, including a 2026 first-rounder, to acquire McDuffie, who totaled 63 tackles, one interception, and seven pass breakups last season before a knee injury prematurely ended his season. The Rams hope McDuffie, who will turn 26 shortly after the start of next season, will prove to be the missing piece they need to make a deep postseason run in the limited time they have left with Matthew Stafford under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Rams have made “significant progress” on an extension for CB Trent McDuffie.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Garafolo reports the team hopes to sign McDuffie to a deal “in the near future,” adding that he’ll likely become the highest-paid corner in the league when all is said and done. McDuffie, 25, was acquired by the Rams last week in exchange for a haul of picks that included the Rams 2026 first-round pick. The fourth-year corner totaled 63 tackles, one interception, and seven pass breakups in 13 games last season and was named a First-team All-Pro in 2023 and a Second-team All-Pro in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Rams acquired CB Trent McDuffie from the Chiefs in exchange for 2026 first, fifth, and sixth round draft picks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie, who has three interceptions over 56 NFL games, was a first-round pick of Kansas City in 2022 and was set to play on his fifth-year rookie option before being dealt to the Rams, who last season allowed the sixth lowest drop back EPA in the NFL. McDuffie, 25, finished the season on IR with a knee injury. He’ll likely sign a long term deal with the Rams. Shipping McDuffie to LA could suggest the Chiefs are finally ready to build via the draft, including, perhaps, improving the receiving room for Patrick Mahomes as he returns from a 2025 knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Chiefs GM Brett Veach said he’d like to have CB Trent McDuffie “back for the long-term.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie is entering the fifth-year option season on his rookie contract and the Chiefs could chop down his cap number for 2026 with an extension. Forced to play outside more over the past few years, McDuffie finally managed to be left off an All-Pro team in 2025. He managed a 75.6 PFF grade — as opposed to 82.0 and 84.8 the two seasons before that — in 688 snaps with the Chiefs while dealing with a knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Chiefs placed CB Trent McDuffie (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Fellow cornerback Jaylen Watson is joining him on injured reserve. With nothing left to play for, the Chiefs are packing it in for the year. McDuffie leads the team in pass breakups at six. Watson is one behind him. Down their top two corners, Kansas City will be an easy target for Bo Nix this week. Fantasy managers can feel free to fire Nix up as a QB1 one last time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Chiefs CB Trent McDuffie (knee) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie is listed as DNP for the second straight day. He has been dealing with the knee issue since Week 14 and may not play the rest of this season with the Chiefs eliminated from playoff contention. Fellow CB Jaylen Watson (groin) was also DNP for the second straight day. Both are on the wrong side of questionable with a Christmas game against the Broncos on the horizon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Chiefs CB Trent McDuffie (knee) remained sidelined on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie, who missed the team’s Week 16 loss to the Titans, continues to deal with a knee injury sustained in Week 14, which is a massive blow to a defense that operates primarily from nickel. It remains to be seen if McDuffie will make it back this season or if the team will simply place him on season-ending injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Chiefs CB Trent McDuffie (knee) will not play in Kansas City’s Week 16 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Neither will LB Leo Chenal (shoulder), who did not practice all week. McDuffie gave us a courtesy limited on Thursday, but it doesn’t look like the Chiefs are planning on making him play hurt while they’re eliminated. Chiefs non-McDuffie corners versus Titans wideouts is a matchup that screams “meaningless Week 16 game.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Chiefs CB Trent McDuffie (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Reporters expected a DNP, but McDuffie got in a limited session officially. We still consider him at least a bit unlikely to miss Week 16’s game against the Titans, but McDuffie is at least making a play to be active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Josh Simmons (back) won’t play in Kansas City’s Week 6 game against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Simmons did actually practice this week, so he’s trending in the right direction, but Khalil Benson gets another start while Simmons tries to get past a bulging disc in his back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Josh Simmons (back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: The Chiefs’ starting left tackle might need more time off, but his continued practice participation is good to see. The Chiefs take on the struggling Chargers this week, and may be able to get by alright without him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Josh Simmons (back) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Simmons has been held out of practice for roughly two months while dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back. Kansas City’s starting left tackle has yet to play a snap this year while dealing with the back injury. Head coach Andy Reid said the team will “ease him back in, but on a limited basis.” There is currently no timetable for when Simmons will return. Undrafted Khalil Benson has been serviceable as the team’s starting left tackle, but Simmons will ultimately be a notable upgrade whenever he returns to action. Benson is still expected to start this week versus the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs ruled out LT Josh Simmons (back) for Week 4 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Earlier this week, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Simmons is dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back. Brutal. On the plus side, CB Chamarri Conner (knee) will make his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Josh Simmons is dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Simmons hasn’t played or practiced this year. Reid told reporters that he was making progress but will remain out of practice today. Kahlil Benson will presumably draw another start at left tackle in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs LT Josh Simmons (back) will not play in Kansas City’s Week 3 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Kahlil Benson draws another start. Simmons has not been spotted at practice since the regular season started.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs declared OT Josh Simmons, S Chamarri Conner, TE Jared Wiley, QB Garrett Nussmeier, DT Bryson Eason, OT Diego Pounds, and DE Jack Pyburn inactive for Week 2 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: The Chiefs enter Week 2 relatively healthy as they look to start the season with consecutive victories. It will be interesting to see if the Chiefs carry forward a run-heavy attack after pounding the football on the ground in a Week 1 win over the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs ruled out LT Josh Simmons (back) for Week 2 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Backup OT Kahlil Benson will start in Simmons’ stead. He did so last week and avoided major mistakes. The Chiefs also ruled out CB Chamarri Conner (knee).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Josh Simmons (back) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Simmons missed the Chiefs’ 2026 opener with the back issue and isn’t likely to suit up this week either. Kahlil Benson, a UDFA rookie, took his spot at left tackle in Week 1. Benson allowed three pressures and was penalized once, but he did not allow a sack and held his own in the run game. He will draw the start in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said “there’s a good chance” Josh Simmons (back) won’t play this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: “He has a (back) issue there he’s working through. Josh is rehabbing. He’s working his tail off. This isn’t anything other than him having an issue with his back,” Reid said, asking what about his ‘My left tackle has a back issue he’s working through” t-shirt was unclear. Simmons’ status appears to be in some short-term doubt and we wouldn’t rule out an IR stint for him ahead of the opener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers ruled out Antoine Winfield (ribs) for Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Winfield’s absence is consequential. The centerfield prowler makes an impact when he is in the game. The Steelers should have a slightly easier time moving the ball against the Buccaneers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Antoine Winfield (ribs) has a fracture and will miss 2-4 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: That timeline makes it possible he’ll be sent to injured reserve before Week 5’s Thursday Night Football game against the Cowboys. Winfield missed only five snaps in Tampa’s loss to the Packers; this would appear to open a pretty deep hole.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers S Antoine Winfield (toe) is not on Tampa Bay’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: He and Lavonte David (knee/rib) both upgraded to full practices on Friday and were removed from the report. The Buccaneers will have their back-seven leaders ready for a divisional matchup against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Bucs S Antoine Winfield (toe) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: It seems like, with Wednesday’s practice being a walkthrough, the Buccaneers opted to go easy on some of their veterans. Lavonte David (knee/rib) and Winfield both upgraded from DNPs to limited sessions on Thursday, putting them in line to play. The same can’t be said for EDGE Haason Reddick (ankle/knee), who remained a DNP and could be in line to miss more weeks. We’re a little surprised Todd Bowles didn’t rule out Reddick when he said that Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin weren’t going to play this week, but he did say they were still waiting for the results of his MRI when asked about it on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Bucs EDGE Haason Reddick (ankle/knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Several Tampa Bay defenders did not practice on Wednesday. Lavonte David and Antoine Winfield are among the most notable names on the list. David is dealing with knee and rib issues while Winfield has a toe injury. Coming off a Monday night game, the Bucs might be giving their veterans some maintenance days because of the short week. Still, it’s notable just how many big names they have on the injury report. A banged-up Bucs defense could help Spencer Rattler get back on track after throwing three interceptions in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers restructured S Antoine Winfield Jr.'s contract to free up 2025 cap space.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Winfield had a $21 million base salary that was shifted to a minimum salary and bonus, with the Bucs also adding a void year. He signed a four-year, $84.1 million contract last offseason and now Tampa Bay frees up $15.86 million in cap space for 2025 by restructuring a contract that ends in 2027. The Bucs also restructured WR Mike Evans’ contract, though it was not for any cap savings. Evans had some compensation moved forward to pay him sooner, but cap space was not created.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Cade Otton (knee, questionable) is expected to play in the Wild Card Round against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Otton is one of five players who entered the weekend listed as questionable who are expected to play on Sunday night. The third-year tight end who broke out for 59-600-4 in 14 games this season has missed the last three weeks due to a knee injury but will be back in the mix on Sunday night, barring anything unexpected. In addition to Otton, safeties Antoine Winfield Jr., and Mike Edwards, along with cornerback Jamel Dean, and defensive end Logan Hall are also expected to play despite being listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Antoine Winfield will play in the Wild Card Round against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: The Bucs will also have Jamel Dean back in the lineup after Dean missed Week 18’s game with a knee injury. Winfield, who hasn’t played since Week 14, is also returning from a knee injury, providing two immediate boosts to a secondary ahead of the Buccaneers’ biggest game of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Buccaneers S Antoine Winfield Jr. (knee) practiced in full on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Winfield has been unable to suit up on game day since suffering the knee injury in Week 14 and his return could prove pivotal in a potentially high-scoring game against the Commanders. Winfield returned to practice in a limited capacity last week so his continued improvement is a great sign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.headline: Cade Otton (knee) will not play in Week 17 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/antoine-wi.analysis: Head coach Todd Bowles said Otton, along with wide receiver Sterling Shepard (hamstring/foot) and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (knee) will also miss Week 17’s contest. The Buccaneers find themselves in a must-win situation against the Panthers if they hope to keep their playoff hopes alive. The absence of Otton and Shepard should lead to an increased target share for Jalen McMillan, who has found the end zone in three straight games, and will also open the door for Payne Durham to make another start. Durham caught 5-of-7 targets for 29 yards in last week’s loss to the Cowboys, but will be hard to trust as anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) won’t play in Kansas City’s Week 6 game against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: It seems like Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce will be getting Only Game In Town treatment against the Chargers, with Cyrus Allen and Jalen Royals also in the mix at wideout now that Rice and Tyquan Thornton are both out. Andy Reid said Rice is “wanting to jump in on everything” but he did not practice this week. He has to be regarded as questionable for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice strained his hamstring in Week 4. Although Chiefs coach Andy Reid initially said Rice only “tweaked” it, The Athletic’s Mike Silver reported a few hours later that Rice could be out for several weeks. The fact that Rice remains sidelined for the first two practices following his team’s Week 5 bye is a bad sign. He is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6 against the Chargers. If he can get in a limited session tomorrow, that could put him on track to play in Week 7 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice appeared to have a good chance at suiting up for Week 6 when Andy Reid spoke about it after Week 4’s win over the Raiders. Reid only said he “tweaked” his hammy. Even with a bye week to rest, it looks like Rice is now on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6. With Tyquan Thornton on IR, Xavier Worthy may be tasked with WR1 duties this week. He totaled four catches for 70 yards in his last outing and would be a solid FLEX play versus the Chargers if Rice can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: The Athletic’s Mike Silver believes Rashee Rice (hamstring) could be out for several weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: After the game, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Rice “tweaked” his hamstring, seemingly downplaying the severity of his injury. It’s possible Silver is speculating on how long Rice could be out given what we know about soft-tissue injuries. Rice didn’t return to the game on Sunday against the Raiders, but he could be seen working out on the sideline at various times and was also on the exercise bike. With the Chiefs now entering their bye week, it’s possible we won’t have more clarity on Rice’s potential absence until they return to prepare for Week 6 against the Chargers. We will check back in with any updates as the team provides them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Chiefs downgraded WR Rashee Rice (hamstring) to doubtful to return in Week 4 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: The Chiefs aren’t formally ruling him out just yet, but Rice’s day is as good as done with this latest update. He continues to go through tests on the hamstring he injured in the first quarter of Sunday’s game and will likely be ruled out in the near future. If his day is done, Rice will finish with zero receptions on zero targets in just six offensive snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) is questionable to return in Week 4 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: This news comes from the team’s X account. Rice exited in the first quarter of Sunday’s game and eventually made his way to the locker room after initially refusing to leave the field. CBS Sports’ Tracy Wolfson reported that Rice was noticeably frustrated on the sideline, which isn’t an encouraging sign as far as his return for this game is concerned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (leg) exited in the first quarter of Week 4’s game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: It’s hard to tell what may have happened here, but Rice appeared to land awkwardly on his left foot after making a catch on a play that would be overturned by a penalty. Rice appeared to be grabbing at the back of his leg and immediately made his way to the sideline. We will provide an update when we receive one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice caught 7-of-9 targets for 88 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice’s seven receptions were easily a new season best, though he’s now cleared 80 yards in back-to-back contests. Rice’s nine targets were no joke on a day where Patrick Mahomes was limited to 24 attempts as the Chiefs ran just 49 plays. Rice was also the intended target on Mahomes’ “interception,” which in reality was a ball Rice batted into the air. Not good, but neither was the pass. It was behind the wideout, who was laying on the ground. We doubt Mahomes holds it against him. Rice will remain a solid WR2 for Week 4 in Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice caught 4-of-6 targets for 83 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 2 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: An interesting development from this one were the 10 targets filtered to running back Kenneth Walker, who gained emphasis through the air in the short areas of the field typically accounted for by Rice and tight end Travis Kelce. The Colts also utilized elevated rates of man coverage until the departure of cornerback Charvarius Ward, against which Rice has clear negative splits. He did break free for a 31-yard gain, one of two Mahomes completions to go for more than 30 yards. Rice remains a volume-driven WR2 with clear WR3 downside, in an offense now more intent on featuring the backfield. He remains a touchdown-dependent WR2 against the Dolphins in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice earned only two targets in Week 1, yet still technically warrants WR2 treatment based on his theoretical role in the offense, along with his past WR1 performances. The Chiefs notably faced the Broncos’ top-tier defense last week and will get a far softer matchup against the Colts in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: FOX Sports’ Greg Auman reports that Sean Tucker (quad) will be a pregame decision for Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: We expect to see Tucker officially listed as questionable to play when the injury report drops later today. If he ends up being inactive, that is good news for Bucky Irving, who handled 23 touches last week, ceding seven to Kenny Gainwell and five to Tucker. Irving warrants borderline RB1/2 treatment at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Sean Tucker (quad) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker missed Wednesday’s session with a quad issue. He previously missed one game due to a hamstring injury. Tucker should be good to go for Week 6, though we don’t expect much fantasy production from the Bucs’ RB3. He has eight carries and zero catches over the past two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Sean Tucker rushed three times for 10 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Bucs OC Zac Robinson talked about getting Tucker the ball more earlier this week. Tucker entered this game with zero touches on offense. Though his role was limited, Robinson subbed him in where it counts the most and Tucker punched in a goal line score in the first half. He still doesn’t have much standalone fantasy value, but Tucker reclaiming the goal line role he had last year would be brutal for Bucky Irving’s fantasy outlook. Tucker is, at best, a touchdown-based RB5 for Week 5 versus Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said game flow and productivity have limited RB Kenny Gainwell’s usage.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: The Buccaneers are 0-3, so if trailing game scripts aren’t the ideal setup for a receiving specialist, we aren’t sure what is. Robinson said he would like to get Gainwell more involved, but also added that Gainwell has to earn those reps by being more productive. Robinson said he also wants to get RB3 Sean Tucker more involved during the same presser. It sounds like this backfield still belongs to starting RB Bucky Irving, who is dealing with a glute injury, but changes are at least being considered.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said he wants to get RB Sean Tucker going.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Robinson described Tucker as being “special with the ball in his hands,” and said that it’s on the coaching staff to find spots to mix him in. Whether this impacts starting RB Bucky Irving basically comes down to how and when — and if — the Buccaneers get Tucker involved. Taking a few snaps away from RB2 Kenneth Gainwell would be no big deal. Utilizing Tucker in the red zone would be consequential for Irving. Hopefully, Robinson provides more insight before his team’s Week 4 game against the Packers. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Sean Tucker (hamstring) is active for Week 2 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker was out last week with the hamstring issue. His return to the Tampa lineup could take a few touches away from Bucky Irving and/or Kenneth Gainwell. Last week against the Bengals, Irving out-carried Gainwell 8-5 and led the backfield with a 59 percent route share. Bucs declared CB Jacob Parrish, CB Ayden Garnes, DL Elijah Simmons, DL DeMonta Capehart, OL Billy Schrauth, and OL Luke Haggard inactive for Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Buccaneers RB Sean Tucker (hamstring) is practicing in full for Week 2 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: The Buccaneers should have their RB3 on hand against the Browns this weekend, though Tucker is not expected to contribute in a fantasy-relevant manner. He is just a deep-league bench stash at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Sean Tucker (hamstring) is inactive for Week 1 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker’s expected absence is a nice little boost for Bucky Irving as he looks to shore up his RB2 value following a disastrous 2025. Kenneth Gainwell is unlikely to battle Iriving for goal-line handles. Seeing as Tucker received a “doubtful” tag for Week 1, he’s likely on the wrong side of questionable for Week 2, but his return will at least be a possibility.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Jalen McMillan (knee) is doubtful for Week 1 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: In addition to McMillan, the Buccaneers are also listing RB Sean Tucker (hamstring) as doubtful, putting both players on the wrong side of being active for Week 1. McMillan was able to log a limited week of practice, so hopefully he’ll have a chance to suit up in Week 2 when the Buccaneers take on the Browns. Rookie WR Ted Hurst should make for an interesting dart throw in DFS as he looks to be in line for more work with McMillan sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Buccaneers RB Sean Tucker (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: The Buccaneers’ No. 3 running back is only a bench stash at this time, but he could take on a few touches if he is active against the Bengals this weekend. He should be considered questionable to play at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 6 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara practiced each day this week, so it’s a bit surprising to see him here. Assuming no rough quotes or reports come out, we’d regard him as on the optimistic side of questionable. He’s a reasonable FLEX play against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara played through this injury in Week 5, and it doesn’t seem like he’s in any real danger of missing this one. It would be nice to see a full practice on Friday, but even if we don’t get that, Kamara should be a FLEX consideration for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara played through the back injury last week but only touched the ball five times. Kendre Miller rushed 10 times and CJ Donaldson led the team in snaps. The Saints are likely managing Kamara’s workload as he deals with this back issue. Kamara is not on the fantasy radar for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed three times for 12 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: He “added” two catches for -6 yards. Kamara rotated with Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson throughout the game. Donaldson ultimately led the backfield in snaps, while Miller’s 10 carries paced the team. Kamara only touched the ball once in the second half and spent long stretches of the final two quarters on the sidelines with his helmet off. The team was likely managing his reps while he played through a back injury. He was listed as questionable heading into today’s game. As part of a three-man committee, Kamara is barely an RB4 for his Week 6 date with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) is active for Week 5 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara will split work with Kendre Miller and C.J. Donaldson. He projects to lead the group in carries and targets, giving him some RB3 potential. Inactive for the Saints are EDGE Anfernee Jennings, S Mike Reid, LB Kaden Elliss, OL Jeremiah Wright, DL Vernon Broughton, and DL Nathan Shepherd.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Alvin Kamara (back) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara is listed as questionable with a back injury. He logged two limited practices this week. In the absence of Travis Etienne, Kamara has become the leader of a three-back committee. He only saw seven carries last week but did manage five catches on seven targets. Kamara is a PPR RB3 for his date with the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 5 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara practiced on Thursday and seems likely to be the “lead” back in New Orleans’ committee against Minnesota on Sunday. If he is ruled out, Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson will receive boosts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was spotted at practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Saints coach Kellen Moore told reporters that Kamara’s knee checked out okay when asked about it yesterday, it seems this back injury won’t be serious enough to keep Kamara out of Week 5 either. He’ll be a reasonable FLEX play against the Vikings if he plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara briefly left the Saints’ Week 4 game against the Falcons to deal with a knee injury. Today, he is sidelined by a back injury. It’s perhaps unsurprising for a 31-year-old player who has clearly lost a step at this point in his career. He is backed up by Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson. Either player can be stashed in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed seven times for 23 yards and two touchdowns in the Saints’ Week 4 loss to the Falcons, adding 35 yards on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The Saints mustered just 16 running back carries in the first game without Travis Etienne, gaining just 50 yards on the ground in the blowout loss. The New Orleans offensive line was completely out-classed by the stout Atlanta defensive front. Kamara briefly departed with a knee injury that required two trips to the medical tent but would return to score his second touchdown of the evening in the fourth quarter. Kamara should continue to lead the backfield in the absence of Etienne and suddenly finds himself as an RB2 in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 6 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave missed the first two days of practice this week with the illness, but we’d ultimately still expect him to play. He should be regarded as on the optimistic side of questionable. He’ll be an easy WR1, assuming he plays, against the Giants in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Unless we get word that it’s an exceptionally rough illness, we’d expect no worse than a questionable listing on Friday despite the two missed practices. Olave should remain a smash WR1 against the Giants in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (illness) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: We expect Olave to be fine for the Saints’ Week 6 game against the Giants. There is currently no cause for concern, but this is worth keeping an eye on. Olave experienced blood clots in his lung last season, and spent much of the offseason recovering. We are not doctors and cannot opine on the matter. For now, expect him to play, but keep an eye out for his hopeful return to practice tomorrow or Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 4-of-6 targets for 46 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave was averaging over 120 yards per game before today’s contest. The Saints’ extreme play volume and tilt to toward passing the ball turned his great role into elite fantasy production. That finally came to a halt with Brian Flore’s defense shutting down Tyler Shough. The second-year passer completed just 16 throws for 96 yards. Shough and the entire passing attack should improve drastically versus the Giants next week. Fantasy managers can keep treating Olave as a WR1 despite this speed bump.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (foot) is not on the final injury report for Week 5 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: The Saints gave Olave a rest day on Wednesday. He then logged a limited practice on Thursday, listed with a new foot injury, and was reportedly seen sporting a walking boot after practice. ESPN’s Kat Terrell notes, however, that “walking boots are often a precautionary measure.” The fact that the team cleared him right away is reassuring. He can be treated as a low-end WR1, as usual. Olave later told Terrell that his “foot got a little bruised in Thursday’s practice, but he’s good.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (foot) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: It is tough to say when exactly the injury happened. This is bizarre. Olave took a hard hit to the lower body late in Week 4 and subbed himself out for the team’s final possession. He did not practice on Wednesday. The team listed it as a rest day, and New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill reported that coach Kellen Moore clarified three times that Olave’s Wednesday absence was not injury-related. Olave resumed practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday with a foot injury. If this injury occurred in-game, he should be considered likely to play. If it occurred in practice today, he would be firmly in the questionable column. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 8-of-12 targets for 116 yards in the Saints’ Week 4 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave found himself with a relatively quiet receiving line in the first half as the Saints struggled to consistently move the football, something that has become far too familiar under head coach Kellen Moore’s tutelage. As has been the case for some time, Olave got going after the break, ending with his third 100-yard game in four tries, now trailing only CeeDee Lamb in receiving yards through the first month of the season. Fantasy managers will want to monitor the electric wide receiver’s practice status in the coming days after he pulled himself out of the game on the team’s final possession with some sort of ailment. If healthy, Olave remains an elite WR1 ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 9-of-13 targets for 107 yards in the Saints’ Week 3 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave won at every level, be it on outs, corners or crossers. He nearly scored three times. Once on the Saints’ first possession, another on the third and again on the fourth. Tyler Shough overthrew him on the first sequence. Olave had his defender beat as he broke inward at the Raiders’ 10-yard line. On the second one, Shough tried to force a tight-window throw from the Raiders’ three-yard line but two Raiders defenders swatted the pass down at the line of scrimmage. The last one was perhaps the biggest heartbreak. Shough connected with Olave on a slant route from the Raiders’ seven-yard line and Olave was tackled immediately after catching it at the one-yard line. Saints TE Juwan Johnson scored two plays later. Olave remains a WR1 against the Falcons next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave caught 8-of-10 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 2 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave was solid despite playing through a hamstring injury that had him listed as questionable entering the day. His 10 targets led all Saints receivers as he hauled in several key passes to keep the offense on schedule in a game the Saints trailed most of the way. Olave found the end zone in the fourth quarter on an uncontested 21-yard reception to cut the Ravens’ lead to 17-15, setting the Saints up to score on a two-point conversion and tie the game on the next play. Olave has seen 23 targets in his first two games and can be treated as a high-end WR1 in next week’s game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.headline: Chris Olave (hamstring) is active for Week 2 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-olav.analysis: Olave is officially active after popping up on Thursday’s injury report with a hamstring issue. He logged a limited practice Friday, so hopefully he won’t be too hampered in what could be a high-scoring game. Assuming a normal workload, Olave projects as a solid WR1. While Olave is active, the Saints did declare RB Kendre Miller, QB Zach Wilson, CB Decamerion Richardson, LB Isaiah Stalbird, DL Christen Miller, OL Mason Murphy, and DL John Ridgeway III inactive for Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) will not play in Baltimore’s Week 6 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: Jurgens has now missed each of his first two weeks with the Ravens as he tries to shake a brain injury he suffered while with the Eagles. Vega Ioane will likely man center again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: Jurgens still has a chance to play, but we had hoped to see him upgrade to full participation. Ravens EDGE Mike Green (hamstring) was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. Ravens OG Andrew Vorhees (foot) joins him in the limited column. Ravens RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) upgraded to full participation. Ravens OG John Simpson (groin) downgraded to a DNP.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: The Ravens’ new starting center is still recovering from his recent concussion, but he seemingly has a chance to face the Browns this week. Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) and S Kyle Hamilton (stinger) are practicing fully, while RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), OG John Simpson (groin), OG Andrew Vorhees (foot), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) were limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Ravens C Cam Jurgens (concussion) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 5 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: He didn’t practice all week after coming over from the Eagles. It’s likely to be Vega Ioane at center again as they try to get Jurgens healthy to man the pivot in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Ravens acquired Cam Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Eagles in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: The Ravens have sustained several interior offensive line injuries in recent weeks. Things got so bad that they did not have a healthy center on the active roster or practice squad after Week 3. Jurgens is currently in concussion protocol and may not suit up this week, but he will take over as the team’s starter once healthy. The Eagles, in turn, will move forward Drew Kendall at center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Eagles removed C Cam Jurgens (concussion) from the injury report ahead of Week 12 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: Jurgens departed the team’s Week 11 win over the Lions to be evaluated for a concussion. He increased his participation in each practice this week before drawing the questionable tag, ultimately removed from the injury report Saturday ahead of a matchup with the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Eagles C Cam Jurgens (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: Jurgens sat out Wednesday, was limited Thursday and practiced fully on Friday. He has not yet been cleared, but as long as he remains symptom-free, he is on track to play. The Eagles’ offense gets a boost with their reliable center on the field. Hopefully, he is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Eagles C Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: Jurgens is making progress in the NFL’s concussion protocol, but he has a ways to go before he can be viewed as more than questionable. Having their reliable center on the field would be great for a struggling Eagles offense as they take on the division-rival Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Eagles C Cam Jurgens (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: Jurgens will likely miss Week 12 because of the brain injury. Right tackle Lane Johnson is also out this week. He is dealing with a Lisfranc injury and is expected to miss at least a month. Luckily for the Eagles, their banged-up line is facing Dallas’s bottom-tier pass-rush on Sunday. There are certainly worse matchups to be without two starters for.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Eagles C Cam Jurgens (knee) is active for Week 11 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: Jurgens returns to the Philadelphia offensive line after missing the previous two games with a knee injury sustained in Week 7, just in time for one of the more difficult rushing matchups in the league against the Lions. Inactive for the Eagles are QB Sam Howell. RB A.J. Dillon, CB Mac Williams, G Drew Kendall, and NT Ty Robinson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (knee) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: His Wednesday DNP suggested worse, but Howard will try to play through the knee injury that cost him roughly half of Cleveland’s snaps against the Jets last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: It’s good progress after he had a Wednesday DNP. Howard should have a real chance at playing on Sunday as long as his Friday status stays neutral or trends positively.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: The Browns acquired Howard from Houston in the offseason. Howard left Week 5 with the knee issue and a DNP today suggests he will miss at least one week. Dawand Jones took his spot in the lineup on Sunday and would presumably draw the start at right tackle if Howard is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Browns acquired RT Tytus Howard from the Texans in exchange for a fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: This is the first big move the Browns have made to address their offensive line. The acquisition of Howard gives them an experienced right tackle who has started all 16 games he has appeared in for each of the last two seasons, and he has allowed just five sacks on 1,175 pass blocking snaps per TruMedia. Shortly after trading for Howard, the Browns announced they would be signing him to a three-year, $63 million extension, keeping him with the team through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Texans G Ed Ingram (knee) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: After missing each of the last two games with a knee injury, Ingram looks likely to go on Thursday night. Ingram has posted back-to-back full practices this week. Tytus Howard (ankle/knee) and Trent Brown (hand/knee) were both limited participants on Monday and Tuesday and also look to be trending towards playing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Texans OL Ed Ingram (knee) is questionable for Houston’s Week 11 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: Ingram, one of Nick Caserio’s better OL scrapheap finds this year, missed last week’s game with the injury but had limited practices on Thursday and Friday after a full on Wednesday. Juice Scruggs wound up seeing most of the time at right guard after an ugly debut series from Sidy Sow. Tytus Howard (concussion) cleared protocol and will start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Texans T Tytus Howard (concussion) will not play in Houston’s Week 10 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: Neither will Ed Ingram (knee), making way for Juice Scruggs and Blake Fisher to join the starting lineup. Davis Mills’ supporting cast isn’t going to be doing the quarterback any favors in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Texans RT Tytus Howard (concussion protocol) left Houston’s Week 9 game against the Broncos and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: He was concussed shortly before halftime and wasn’t in on Houston’s final two drives. Howard, Houston’s best remaining offensive lineman, leaves a big void for second-rounder Blake Fisher to fill. Ed Ingram (ankle) is also questionable to return, with Juice Scruggs stepping into his role at right guard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: Howard being a late addition to the injury report is concerning for his Week 5 availability, but if he’s able to get on the field Friday, he should be good to go. In the event he can’t start, second-year tackle Nick Broeker is listed behind him on the depth chart and would presumably get the nod against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Texans RT Tytus Howard (knee) was seen practicing during the first day of training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: A knee injury suffered in late November ended Howard’s 2023 season, as the veteran tackle required surgery to correct the issue. While we don’t know the specifics of the injury, we do know that Howard was sidelined for the majority of OTAs and minicamp while recovering. Now appearing healthy to kick off the first day of training camp, it looks as if Howard is nearing a full return in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: He’ll be a usable WR3 against the Ravens this week. Boston has returned at least 41 yards in every start this year while hitting a deep gain seemingly weekly. The 22-year-old should be Cleveland’s No. 1 target again this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Of the (many) Browns in real danger of missing this week’s game against the Ravens, Boston seems to be in the best shape of actually playing. Still, it is two limited sessions in two tries and we wouldn’t be surprised if he wound up with a questionable tag on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: A limited practice to start the week is usually nothing more than maintenance. Boston should still be a safe bet to suit up on Sunday. The second-round rookie has already cemented himself as an impressive downfield threat with three touchdowns and three catches of 40+ yards. He’s managed several spike weeks despite the Browns’ up-and-down performances on offense. Health permitting, Boston will be a low-end WR3 for Week 6 versus Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 3-of-7 targets for 47 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 5 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston’s score was his third in five games as a pro. This one was a 29-yard strike down the left sideline where Boston won a 1-on-1 matchup with CB Brandon Stephens. Boston’s yardage totals are not popping off the page in this limited offense, but his play-making ability has been. He has also reached at least 40 yards all five times out, giving him a non-zero floor. The rookie second-rounder continues to press his WR3 case heading into Week 6 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 4-of-7 targets for 89 yards in the Browns’ Week 4 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston has now led the Browns in receiving in three of the team’s first four games, made more impressive by the fact that those were the first four contests of the youngster’s professional career. The second-round rookie continues to flash big play potential after catching his third pass of 46 yards or longer, this time unable to find the end zone after scoring twice in his first two games. Boston still has room to grow considering he has seen just 22 targets in the first month of the season, and could reward fantasy managers that invested late-round picks in his services handsomely in the second half of his rookie year. He’ll be an upside FLEX option against the Jets in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that the Browns “love” Denzel Boston, and he is viewed as a “possible future star.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: What to do with this info? Stash Boston at the very least. Per Palmer, the Browns “felt he was a true pro from the day he walked into the building.” In the same pre-Thursday Night Football news dump, Palmer said that Harold Fannin is the team’s No. 3 pass catcher, despite Fannin leading the team in targets. This could indicate that the Browns plan to ramp up Boston’s offensive involvement as the season progresses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer believes Harold Fannin is the Browns’ No. 3 pass catcher.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: This comes from Palmer’s pre-Thursday Night Football notes. After sharing the info, he tells readers to “read into that how you want.” Fannin currently leads the team in targets (18), though rookie WRs KC Concepcion (17) and Denzel Boston (15) are right behind him. If Palmer’s report is accurate, Fannin could slip to third in target share as the season progresses, but he remains a very talented player and target earner, deserving of a weekly TE1 ranking. Just file this away for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 2-of-4 targets for 41 yards in the Browns’ Week 3 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston’s 41 yards were his fewest in three games as a pro, though he has now contributed at least one 20-yard catch all three times out. On the rare occasions Deshaun Watson actually throws down-field, he’s looking only for Boston. That will lead to some spiked weeks, but Boston’s floor is too low to rank him inside the top 36 on a regular basis, including Thursday’s short-week home date with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 5-of-7 targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 2 win against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: It’s the rookie’s second touchdown grab in as many weeks. After catching an intermediate pass from Deshaun Watson, Boston spun out of a tackle and raced to the end zone for a 55-yard score — by far the biggest play of the game. Boston is cementing himself as the clear WR1 in the Cleveland offense, well ahead of KC Concepcion — who had another inefficient day on Sunday — and Jerry Jeudy, who did not catch his lone target against Tampa. Boston will have plenty of deep league fantasy appeal in Week 3 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 2-of-4 targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 1 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston saw a few deep targets from Deshaun Watson against the Jaguars, ultimately capitalizing with a 46-yard score in the fourth quarter. It came with the game out of reach but we got a taste of how Todd Monken would like to utilize the 22-year-old rookie. He started on the outside for Cleveland and led all wide receivers in snaps, though that may have been inflated with much of the offensive volume coming with the Browns down four scores in the second half. Boston looks to be a boom-or-bust WR5 play for Week 2 against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: The Cardinals officially ruled Love out for this Sunday’s game against the Rams after he was. DNP in practice all week. Head coach Matt LaFleur said Love is not considered a candidate to be placed on injured reserve at this time, but the fact that he even has to mention that is cause for some concern that Love could be looking at a multi-week absence. We’ll have to keep an eye on his practice status next week when the Cardinals begin preparing for the Broncos. Tyler Allgeier should be in line for a busy day against the Rams and will be a volume-based RB2 play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Tyler Allgeier should be rostered in 10-team leagues. The Cardinals have downplayed Love’s ankle issues, but two missed practices are not a good sign. He still has a chance to suit up in Week 6 against the Rams, but he is currently on the wrong side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: The Cardinals are listing Love with just one ankle injury, but recent reports, including quotes from LaFleur, have said that Love is still managing the high-ankle sprain he suffered in the preseason and may have injured the other ankle in Week 4. LaFleur said the current plan is to “give it a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on.” Tyler Allgeier offers little standalone value, but he should be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said he wasn’t sure about getting Jeremiyah Love more involved in the pass game because the team needs extra blocking.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Asked about Love’s lack of route running — he has a 29 percent route participation rate on the season — LaFleur said the Cardinals’ pass blocking struggles often prevent Love from functioning as a pass catcher. “I wasn’t too confident in terms of getting into some of those ‘scat’ protections and stuff like that and five-man protections,” LaFleur said. “We wanted to have that extra body in there. There were a couple of times where I wanted to get him on some choice routes and stuff like that, but like I said I didn’t feel confident that we were going to be able to execute at the level that we needed to. But it is a good question.” Love, who has 13 targets and has been targeted on 21 percent of his pass routes, would need much more pass game involvement if he were to operate as an RB1 in fantasy leagues this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love rushed 12 times for 22 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Love played extensively early in the game. He was the only Cardinals running back to record a carry in the first quarter. The Lions began running up the score in the second quarter, and Love was seemingly simply phased out as Jacoby Brissett repeatedly fired passes downfield. Later, in the fourth quarter, the camera suddenly showed Love standing on the sideline without his helmet. A reporter chimed in to say that Love had not received attention from the training staff, but noted that Love told her he is still managing the ankle injury he suffered in training camp. Reports also indicated that he tweaked his other ankle last week. Love’s weekly floor is sinking as his production becomes increasingly touchdown-dependent. That said, he should be in fantasy lineups as an RB2/3 against the Rams next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is not on Arizona’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said “It’s a maintenance thing with ankles, you guys see the way he cuts...I don’t know what he’s totally feeling, only he knows...but he’s doing good.” Great, not cryptic at all, Mike. Love is a reasonable low-end RB2 if his ankles decide he wants to play his full allotment of the 50/50 split against the Lions in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: The Cardinals’ star rookie running back appeared downtrodden after last week’s game after injuring his other ankle. His continued participation puts him on track to play, but his comments about occasionally preferring a snap count, coupled with his new injury, put him in the RB2/3 category. That said, the Cardinals’ game environment against the Lions this week should be fantasy-friendly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Love was listed as a limited practice participant after he tweaked his ankle in the Cardinals’ Week 4 loss to the Giants. Though he seemingly seized command of Arizona’s backfield in Week 3, Tyler Allgeier was heavily involved in Week 4 as Love hurt his ankle. He was already nursing his other ankle heading into the season and may see limited touches again with this latest tweak. Love is still trending to play Week 5 against the Lions but may sit back on the RB2/3 borderline as his ankle heals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love’s ankle injury “shouldn’t impact” him for Week 5 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Love will presumably have his practice reps monitored, but he isn’t at risk of missing Week 5. He went down with a new ankle injury late in the second quarter of Week 4. Love played sparingly in the second half but denied getting injured at all after the game. It sounds like it’s not a major issue, but it’s hard to feel confident in him handling a heavy workload after how things unfolded last week. He is tumbling back into the RB3 ranks for his upcoming game against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love tweaked his other ankle in Week 4’s loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: It’s been an odd 24 hours for Love, who was quoted after Sunday’s game saying this is shaping up to be the “longest year” of his career while also adding that he’s “tired” and would be willing to pass off work to Tyler Allgeier or Bam Knight in the event that he doesn’t think he can do what is being asked of him. As for this latest injury, LaFleur said the ankle injury isn’t the same one Love injured in the preseason, meaning he now has two ankle injuries to manage for the rest of the season. The Cardinals’ backfield was already proving hard to predict, and the latest quote from Love, coupled with the injury news, doesn’t exactly instill more confidence in him going forward. He draws a plus Week 5 matchup against the Lions, but should be treated as a fringe RB2/RB3 for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: Browns coach Todd Monken said KC Concepcion (concussion) has cleared protocol and will play in Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Concepcion will have some low-end WR3/FLEX appeal with four teams on bye in PPR leagues. He simply hasn’t been able to find much space with his opportunities so far, with two 25-yard catches and 16 other catches that went for just 99 yards in his first five weeks of action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: He’s still in concussion protocol, but it looks like he’ll have at least some chance of clearing before Sunday’s game against the Ravens. Concepcion would struggle to be more than a FLEX option here even if healthy, so fantasy managers should probably look at alternatives this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion (concussion) will practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: It’s a remarkable turn after Concepcion was knocked out cold on the field in Week 5 against the Jets. If Concepcion is able to practice in the coming days he should be active for Week 6 against the Ravens. The rookie leads the Cleveland offense with a 23 percent target per route rate, used primarily as a gadget player near the line of scrimmage. He would be a flex option in PPR formats if he suits up against Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion suffered a concussion in the first quarter of the Browns’ Week 5 game against the Jets and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Making a spinning first quarter grab, Concepcion took a high hit from Minkah Fitzpatrick, who was flagged for a personal foul. It was the kind of hit the NFL is trying to legislate out of the game, but it wasn’t necessarily dirty. It was extremely unfortunate, as Concepcion did appear to be briefly out cold. He thankfully made his way to his feet and to the locker room unassisted, but he was ruled out before even undergoing a formal evaluation. He will now be highly questionable for Week 6 against the Ravens. Concepcion’s loss will mean more routes for beleaguered Jerry Jeudy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion caught 5-of-8 targets for 64 yards in the Browns’ Week 4 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Concepcion continues to operate as the primary slot receiver for a Browns team clearly looking to their youth while phasing out veteran Jerry Jeudy, the latter of whom managed three receptions on three targets for 36 yards. Concepcion has yet to lead the team in receiving while working in a short area role, with this the first game thus far which he has gained more then 43 yards. He’ll be a difficult start in fantasy circles when the Browns take on the Jets in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Browns want Deshaun Watson to get KC Concepcion more involved.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Concepcion ranks second on the team with 17 targets, but his chemistry with Watson remains a work in progress. The rookie wide receiver has turned a team-high 12 receptions into just 80 yards. Concepcion is FLEX-viable against the Steelers on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer believes Harold Fannin is the Browns’ No. 3 pass catcher.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: This comes from Palmer’s pre-Thursday Night Football notes. After sharing the info, he tells readers to “read into that how you want.” Fannin currently leads the team in targets (18), though rookie WRs KC Concepcion (17) and Denzel Boston (15) are right behind him. If Palmer’s report is accurate, Fannin could slip to third in target share as the season progresses, but he remains a very talented player and target earner, deserving of a weekly TE1 ranking. Just file this away for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion caught 2-of-9 targets for nine yards in the Browns’ Week 3 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Well that’s not going to cut it. As ESPN’s Mike Clay points out, rookie first-rounder Concepcion is up to 20 targets over three appearances but has just 80 yards to show for it. He is not being put in position to make explosive plays, and he is very much not doing so. With a yards per catch more befitting of a sluggish running back (6.6), Concepcion is best left outside the WR4 ranks ahead of a tough Week 4 date with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion caught all six of his targets for 28 yards in the Browns’ Week 2 win against the Bucs, adding one rush for -6 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: The good news: Todd Monken is intent on getting the football into the hands of the shifty rookie wideout. The bad news: Designed plays have been borderline disastrous for Concepcion, who was buried for a six yard loss on a first quarter carry. Denzel Boston — who caught his second touchdown of the season — was the only Browns pass catcher to see more targets for Concepcion on Sunday. Concepcion’s role in the low-wattage Cleveland offense leaves little room for weekly upside. He should be rostered in deeper formats though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion caught 4-of-5 targets for 43 yards and a fumble in the Browns’ Week 1 loss to the Jaguars, adding three carries for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Concepcion was utilized like the Browns’ top offensive weapon on the day, seeing three carries and five targets. He was used in motion and targeted underneath frequently. Concepcion’s fumble occurred on a screen pass where he attempted to evade multiple defenders downfield in the second quarter. His usage is certainly encouraging for fantasy managers as he led all Browns wide receivers in targets and receptions. In an offense that will likely find itself trailing frequently this season, Concepcion will see heavy usage, though getting high leverage opportunities may be difficult if the Browns continue to face the same offensive issues they did in Week 1. Concepcion is a fantasy WR4 for Week 2 against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Carson Schwesinger (ankle) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Schwesinger played through a high-ankle sprain last year, so we anticipate he’s more likely to be active than not after returning to practice today. The second-year star linebacker will likely attempt to power through against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Carson Schwesinger (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Mason Graham is expected to miss multiple weeks with an ankle injury of his own and Maliek Collins missed today’s practice with a foot injury. That’s three front-seven starters potentially out for Week 6. With Lamar Jackson still banged up, expect the Ravens to give Derrick Henry all the touches he can handle this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Browns LB Carson Schwesinger is dealing with a Grade 1 ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Schwesinger has not been ruled out for Week 6’s game against the Ravens, and attempted to play through the injury at one point. With a big AFC North matchup on tap for this week, it wouldn’t be surprising if the Browns gave Schwesinger every opportunity to play. His practice status will be one to keep an eye on throughout the week. The 2025 Defensive Rookie of the Year has totaled 43 tackles, one sack, and one forced fumble this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Carson Schwesinger was named Defensive Rookie of the Year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Schwesinger notched 156 total tackles, 67 solo tackles, 2.5 sacks, 11 TFLs, three pass breakups and two interceptions despite missing Week 18 with a high-ankle sprain. It was an extremely impressive season for the No. 33 overall pick in last year’s draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Browns LB Carson Schwesinger (quad/ankle) won’t play in Cleveland’s Week 18 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Schewsinger battled through 16 games despite an ankle injury and looks to be the favorite to walk away with the defensive rookie of the year award after posting 156 tackles, 2.5 sacks, and two interceptions in his inaugural season. Bengals running backs could operate a little more freely than usual in Week 18.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Browns LB Carson Schwesinger (ankle) is questionable for Week 10 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Schwesinger suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 8’s loss to the Patriots. The rookie linebacker avoided landing on injured reserve, but only managed to get on the field for one practice this week. The questionable designation may be a bit too optimistic for Schwesinger this week, but he’s clearly trending toward a return and could be good to go for Week 11 if not this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports tests confirmed a high-ankle sprain for Browns LB Carson Schwesinger.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Now that we have the diagnosis, it’s safe to assume the rookie second-rounder is likely looking at a multi-week absence. Schwesinger has stepped in to make an immediate impact for the Browns’ defense this season, leading the team with 64 tackles while also tallying one interception, one sack, and four TFLs. The Browns are now entering their Week 9 bye. If they believe Schwesinger, who will be reevaluated after the bye , can return inside of the four-game minimum he would be required to miss on injured reserve, it’s possible they opt to keep him on the roster in hopes of a return in 2-3 weeks. Regardless, his loss is a massive one for a defensive unit that has been among the league’s best despite their 2-6 record.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Browns placed LB Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah (neck) on the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Owusu-Kormaoah reported to Browns offseason activities last month, but didn’t practice with the team after suffering a serious neck injury in Week 8 against the Ravens last season. The Browns released a statement saying that they “will not make any predictions on Jeremiah’s football future at this time.” Landing on the reserve/PUP list means that Owusu-Koramoah will miss the entire 2025 season. Second-round pick Carson Schwesigner would seem to have a chance to compete for a starting role in his rookie season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Browns signed fourth-round pick RB Dylan Sampson to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Sampson (5'8/200) totaled both the fourth-most offensive touches (278) and missed tackles forced (83) among Power Five running backs last season, despite his compact frame.
