He is not guaranteed a year one role with Quinshon Judkins set to start and Jerome Ford still in-house but Sampson should be on re-draft radars as a player to watch in training camp. The Browns announced Sampson’s signing in conjunction with second-round pick LB Carson Schwesinger. Per NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero, Schwesinger became just “the second second-round pick in NFL history to have a fully guaranteed deal.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Browns selected UCLA LB Carson Schwesinger with the No. 33 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Schwesinger (6’2/242) walked onto UCLA in 2021 with the hopes of being a FBS football player and quickly established himself as a valuable member of the Bruins’ roster. He earned a scholarship in 2022 as a special teams ace and part-time ‘backer who racked up 27 tackles in 26 games over the next two seasons before ascending to a starting role in 2024. He made the most of the opportunity, leading the FBS with 90 solo and 136 total tackles with 8.5 TFLs, 50 stops and 4.0 sacks while playing in 12 games. The First Team All-American excelled in every phase of the game, especially rushing the passer where he earned a 90th percentile rush grade. Schwesinger is extremely elusive and flexible when blitzing, as his absurd 27.4% pressure rate will attest, disguising his intentions right up until it’s time to go leaving blockers confused with their assignments. A smart, twitched up player whose motor runs hot, he possesses advanced instincts and knows how to get skinny to slip around blocks. His svelte frame affects his ability to take on pulling linemen, but his relentless determination and athleticism make Schwesinger a complete three-down linebacker prospect.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson will miss a second straight game with his ankle injury despite reports at the beginning of the week that said he had a “realistic” chance to play in Week 6. It was also reported after the team’s overtime win against the Falcons that Lamar was “closer than people realized” to playing in Week 5. Jackson and the Ravens will now set their sights on having him ready to go in Week 7 at home against the Bengals, while Tyler Huntley will draw the start this week against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: All signs are pointing to Tyler Huntley making his second straight start. Jackson was a DNP for all three practices this week and will likely be ruled out in the next few hours, meaning Huntley will have a chance at a “revenge game” against a Browns team that he spent part of the 2024 and 2025 seasons with. Huntley threw for 201-2-0 in last week’s win over the Falcons and rushed for another 20 yards and one touchdown. He’ll have some appeal in 2QB and Superflex leagues on the road against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson still has a chance to face the Browns this week, albeit a very small one. Backup Tyler Huntley will likely be under center for the second week in a row, although coach Jesse Minter said last week that Jackson doesn’t have to practice “much” before being cleared to play. Huntley is a viable QB2 if he gets the start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) is considered day-to-day.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Minter confirmed that Jackson would not practice today. He did not practice once last week before being ruled out on Friday. Jackson appears to be on the wrong side of questionable after missing today’s session, though Minter did note that Jackson is the caliber of player who can suit up on Sunday despite missing all three practices. If he can’t go, Tyler Huntley will draw the start. With Cincinnati and Buffalo on deck after Cleveland this week, the Ravens may opt to give Jackson one more game off before getting him back in the lineup for a pair of must-win games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) was not present at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson could always return for the portion of practice not open to the media, but this is still a concerning start to the week for the superstar quarterback. Jackson missed Week 5 with the ankle injury after failing to practice once during the week. If he remains sidelined for Week 6, Tyler Huntley will make his second start of the year. Huntley acquitted himself well on Sunday night with 201 yards and two touchdowns through the air, plus a score on the ground, in Baltimore’s overtime win over the Falcons. He will be a solid QB2 for Superflex players if Jackson is out again this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Lamar Jackson (ankle) has a “realistic” shot to play in Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson’s ankle injury, which has been described as neither high nor low, kept him sidelined in the Ravens’ win over the Falcons. It’s possible the Ravens will be cautious with Jackson and have Tyler Huntley start one more game in Week 6 against the Browns. Huntley against the Falcons threw for 201 yards and two scores. He was the seventh most accurate QB of the week. Jackson’s practice participation will be closely monitored over the next few days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) is “definitely doing better” after missing Week 5’s game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: While this is good news for Jackson, Minter also said he wasn’t sure if Jackson would be back on the practice field on Wednesday. It was reported earlier on Monday that there was “some hope” that Jackson would play in Week 6 after he was “closer than people realized” to playing in Week 5 against the Falcons. This is shaping up to be another week where we are forced to monitor Jackson’s practice status up until Friday, when the team releases its final injury report. The Ravens are 4-1 and set to face a 3-2 Browns team in a pivotal AFC North matchup. If Jackson is unable to start, Tyler Huntley would make his second start of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports there is “some hope” Lamar Jackson (ankle) will play in Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: According to Rapoport, Jackson was “closer than people realized” to playing in Week 5 against the Falcons, which is an encouraging sign as the Ravens enter a pivotal matchup against the Browns. Jackson’s injury didn’t appear too severe when it initially happened in the second quarter of Week 4’s win over the Titans, so it’s not too surprising to hear that he nearly suited up for Sunday night’s game. That said, Jackson’s injuries have lingered in the past, so we’ll be monitoring his status throughout the week. If he’s not able to go, Tyler Huntley would make a second straight start for the Ravens, who currently lead the AFC North with a 4-1 record.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens declared QB Lamar Jackson, OLB Trey Hendrickson, C Cam Jurgens, G Andrew Vorhees, WR Elijah Sarratt, and DT Aeneas Peebles inactive for Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson had already been ruled out earlier in the week and reportedly could be looking at a multi-game absence due to an ankle injury suffered before halftime in Week 4. Tyler Huntley will start under center for the Ravens as they look to subdue the momentum of the Falcons, who have won both games started by Michael Penix. Wide receiver Zay Flowers is officially active for Sunday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lamar Jackson (ankle) has a “real chance” to return in Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson was ruled out for Week 5 on Friday after failing to practice once this week. Rapoport added that Jackson has been “working like crazy” to get back on the field next week. Per Rapoport, that is Jackson’s goal. Tyler Huntley will start for as long as Jackson remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: He only got in a limited session on Friday, leaving us to conclude this is likely a true questionable situation. The viability of Jaleel McLaughlin as a FLEX play will probably be determined by if Judkins is active or not. It’s also possible Judkins plays on a pitch count. He’ll be a shaky low-end RB2 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) returned to practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: This is an improvement for Judkins, who was a DNP for the team’s first two practices this week. Head coach Todd Monken said earlier this week that Judkins was considered day-to-day, so we’ll see if he has a shot at playing when the team releases its final injury report in a couple of hours. It seems unlikely that Judkins will be fully removed from the injury report, meaning he’ll likely carry a questionable designation heading into the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: It sure seems to be trending in the direction of Jaleel McLaughlin, Lead Back in Week 6 against the Ravens. We’ll see if Judkins can get back on the field or generate any kind of positive momentum on Friday, but we’d be surprised if he did better than a questionable listing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Judkins suffered a potentially serious ankle injury in Week 5 and could miss Week 6 against the Ravens if he’s unable to practice in the next couple days. That could leave Jaleel McLaughlin as the Browns’ lead back against Baltimore. Dylan Sampson (knee) could also suit up if he’s able to practice after a four-week stint on IR.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Browns RB Dylan Sampson (knee) is designated to return and eligible to return to practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Sampson was placed on injured reserve in mid-September with a knee injury. His return could be an immediate factor in the Browns backfield with Quinshon Judkins likely out with an ankle injury. Sampson could compete for backfield touches with Jaleel McLaughlin in Week 6 against the Ravens if he’s active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Quinshon Judkins is considered day-to-day with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Monken was spotted in a walking boot after Sunday’s loss to the Jets, but Monken said his RB1 will have a chance to play in Week 6 against the Ravens. Judkins rushed 14 times for 44 yards last week and has a rushing line of 73-221-1 for the season, along with 18 receptions for 102 additional yards. Judkins’ practice status will be one to monitor throughout the week. If he’s not able to play, Raheim Sanders would likely handle the early-down work, with Jaleel McLaughlin mixing in as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins rushed 14 times for 44 yards in the Browns’ Week 5 loss to the Jets, adding three receptions for six yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Not a great day in the rain, one that got worse when Judkins was spotted in the Browns’ locker room after the fact with his right foot in a walking boot. Boots are frequently precautionary, but they are always noteworthy. Also noteworthy is that Judkins finished the game without an injury announcement. Hopefully he’s just managing a little something ahead of Week 6 against the Ravens. If not, the Browns’ backfield is a mess behind Judkins, with Raheim Sanders and Jaleel McLaughlin the next backs up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins rushed 17 times for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 4 win over the Steelers, adding 43 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: The rushing efficiency remains a big issue for Judkins and the Cleveland ground game, this time overcoming just 3.1 yards per carry with a short touchdown plunge and significant involvement through the air. The end result was the first start-worthy fantasy line for Judkins through four games. The poor performances on the ground don’t appear to be in line for remedy ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Jets, although Judkins could be headed for another robust workload considering the expected game environment between two teams whose identity is driven by their defense. He’ll be a volume-driven RB2 after seeing 27 of 32 available running back opportunities against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins rushed 18 times for 70 yards in the Browns’ Week 3 win over the Panthers, adding two receptions for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Both Judkins’ carries and yards were new season highs, though so was his 3.9 yards per carry. That tells you all you need to know about his explosive-play odds in this low-ceiling attack. Judkins at least remains unchallenged for touches. Judkins’ usage gives him a low-end RB2 floor, but the same seems true of his ceiling. The Steelers are not a good Week 4 matchup for the Dawg Pound.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins had 12 rushes for 21 yards in the Browns’ Week 2 win against the Bucs, adding five catches for 27 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Judkins nearly scored a couple times inside the ten yard line, but couldn’t quite punch it in. The second-year back has a solid role if/when the Browns are able to hang with their opponents and produce sufficient neutral and positive game script. On Sunday against the Bucs, Judkins accounted for 12 of the Browns’ 15 running back carries and was targeted frequently out of the backfield as Deshaun Watson posted an aDOT of 3.6. Judkins should be a top-24 option in Week 3 against a middling Panthers defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) won’t play in Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Sampson practiced each of the last two days, but it was too little, too late, for Week 6. He stands a chance at returning in Week 7. As long as Quinshon Judkins is relatively healthy, Sampson won’t have standalone value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: This is at least some positive momentum towards being activated and helping the Browns out on Sunday, though even if Sampson was activated he’d likely be in a committee. We’ll see what Friday brings, but unless it’s a full session, we’d be surprised if Sampson was more than a sketchy questionable for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: The Browns opened Sampson’s practice window today, so it’s a bit odd to see him sit out of the session entirely. They were likely giving Sampson the option to suit up even though he may not be fully ready to return. With Quinshon Judkins injured and Raheim Sanders on IR, the Browns are clearly desperate at running back. If Sampson doesn’t play on Sunday, the backfield will be split between Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime. This is likely a fantasy situation to avoid at all costs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Judkins suffered a potentially serious ankle injury in Week 5 and could miss Week 6 against the Ravens if he’s unable to practice in the next couple days. That could leave Jaleel McLaughlin as the Browns’ lead back against Baltimore. Dylan Sampson (knee) could also suit up if he’s able to practice after a four-week stint on IR.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Browns RB Dylan Sampson (knee) is designated to return and eligible to return to practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Sampson was placed on injured reserve in mid-September with a knee injury. His return could be an immediate factor in the Browns backfield with Quinshon Judkins likely out with an ankle injury. Sampson could compete for backfield touches with Jaleel McLaughlin in Week 6 against the Ravens if he’s active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Browns placed RB Dylan Sampson (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four games with a knee ailment that had him spotted on crutches. It will likely be longer than that. Sampson can be dropped in standard leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports RB Dylan Sampson (knee) is expected to miss significant time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: He was spotted in crutches after the game. Sampson’s absence will leave Raheim Sanders as a potential third-down back and primary backup for Quinshon Judkins. Jaleel McLaughlin is a potential practice squad elevation if Sampson is placed on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Browns RB Dylan Sampson (knee) is ruled out for Week 1 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Sampson returned a kickoff and played on a third down play against the Jaguars before exiting in the first quarter. He left for the locker room with a knee injury and was promptly ruled out. Third-string running back Raheim Sanders will get more run with Sampson out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Browns RB Dylan Sampson (knee) went to the locker room and is questionable to return Week 1 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Sampson went to the medical tent during the first quarter of the Browns’ Week 1 game against the Jaguars. He then headed to the locker room to be further evaluated for a knee injury and is questionable to return. Sampson is the Browns’ third-down/passing-down back; Quinshon Judkins will see more of those snaps while Sampson is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Browns RB Quinshon Judkins did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: According to Cleveland’s Mary Kay Cabot, Judkins was “the object of much of the chippiness on Tuesday.” According to multiple beat reporters, Browns coach Todd Monken abruptly ended practice early yesterday because defenders were being a little too physical. The team could simply be giving Judkins the day off after taking some hits yesterday, but this is worth keeping an eye on. Browns No. 2 RB Dylan Sampson operated as the team’s starter with Judkins sitting out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix has been removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was reported the day after the Falcons’ overtime loss to the Ravens that there was “optimism” that Penix would start in Week 6. After being upgraded to a full participant on Thursday’s practice, he seemed like a lock to be ready to go by Sunday, so Friday’s news isn’t all that unexpected. Penix has thrown for 719 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception this season, throwing one touchdown in each of his first three games. He’ll be on the fantasy radar in 2QB/Superflex leagues against a Bears defense that has allowed just two top-12 fantasy finishes to opposing QBs this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This is great news for the Falcons’ offense, which can barely function with Tua Tagovailoa at the helm. Penix is firmly on track to play in Week 6 against the Bears, as long as he gets through the week setback-free. Penix can be viewed as a high-end QB2 with four teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) will practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: “We’ll see how he’s feeling,” head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters Wednesday morning, adding that Penix should be able to play through the injury. Even if it’s a limited practice session for Penix, it’s good news for his Week 6 availability following his Sunday night rib injury against the Ravens. Penix, operating under center at a much higher rate than last season, is among the most efficient quarterbacks in the league through Week 5. If Penix is out, Tua Tagovailoa would represent a major downgrade for all Atlanta pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports there’s “optimism” that Michael Penix (ribs) will be able to play in Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix said after Sunday’s loss that he didn’t believe his injury would be long-term. He was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa in overtime because of his injury, but he also added that he likely would have gone back on the field had the Falcons received the ball to start the extra quarter. Instead, Penix said his pain worsened the longer he sat, which was why he ultimately didn’t go back in. Penix’s status will be one to monitor throughout the week. If he can’t start in Week 6, Tagovailoa would be in line to start his first game of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix (ribs) said he doesn’t believe his injury will be a long-term issue.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix will undergo an MRI on Monday to confirm the severity of his injury, but it doesn’t sound like he’s at risk of missing much time. Penix exited in the fourth quarter of Sunday night’s game against the Ravens and was forced to stay on the sideline in overtime to watch Tua Tagovailoa throw the game-losing interception shortly after the Ravens scored the go-ahead touchdown. Penix threw for 240 yards and a touchdown and has been solid in his three games since returning from injury. If he’s not able to start in Week 6, Tagovailoa would presumably draw the start at home against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Falcons QB Michael Penix (ribs) is questionable to return to Week 5 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix took the full brunt of a brutal hit to the midsection late in the fourth quarter of Week 5 against the Ravens. He would leave for one play due to the medical timeout, return for one play, and then retreat to the sideline. Tua Tagovailoa came on in relief in overtime, with the team designating Penix questionable to return with an injury to his ribs. Penix completed 19-of-32 passes for 240 yards and one touchdown prior to departing, adding eight yards on two carries. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his practice status in the coming days ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix completed 15-of-20 passes for 223 yards and one touchdown in the Falcons’ 45-24, Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix wasn’t asked to do much with his arm as the Falcons tied a franchise record with five rushing scores, but the threat of consistent and reliable passing has done wonders for a Falcons offense that looked lost through two games behind poor quarterback play. It also doesn’t hurt when your All Pro running back goes for a 59-yard touchdown on his first touch of the game. The Falcons were never threatened by an underperforming Saints team after jumping out to a 14-point lead in the first quarter. Penix has yet to be called on for increased passing volume through two starts, something that could change, pending the health of Lamar Jackson, in Week 5 when they host the Ravens. Penix remains a middling QB2 and does not warrant starting in all formats outside of two-quarterback leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Michael Penix completed 18-of-25 passes for 256 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Falcons’ 35-14, Week 3 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The final stat line looks more impressive when you consider Penix started the game 1-of-5 passing with an interception, settling into the game from there to go on to complete 17 of his final 20 pass attempts. As was the case during his rookie season, Penix leaned on his top option through the air, feeding Drake London 10 targets that the talented receiver parlayed into a gaudy 194 yards, with no other pass-catcher surpassing the 19 yards receiving of running back Bijan Robinson. The Falcons improve to 1-2 on the young season while handing the Packers their first home opener loss in 14 years. Penix has all the look of an upside QB2 and deserves streaming consideration ahead of a road matchup with the Saints in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Amazon Prime’s James Palmer reports Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) will play in Week 3 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Tagovailoa, fighting injuries for much of the offseason, missed Atlanta’s first two games with an oblique issue. He’ll return just in time to serve as backup to Michael Penix, who’s returning from a 2025 ACL injury. Penix is set to start Thursday night against a Packers defense allowing the ninth lowest adjusted yards per pass attempt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Falcons named Michael Penix as the starter for Week 3 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Penix will make his first start since Week 11 of last season, when he suffered a torn ACL against the Panthers. If he plays well enough, Penix will have a chance to secure the starting job for the remainder of the season, but he will have Tua Tagovailoa looming in the background once he is fully recovered from his oblique injury. Penix has struggled early in his career, throwing for 2,757-12-6 in 14 career games while completing just 59.6 percent of his passes. It seems unlikely that he will hold onto the job for the remaining 15 games of the season, but he’ll get the first legitimate crack at it after the Falcons were forced to start Cooper Rush for the first two weeks of the season. Penix shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a low-end QB2 for fantasy purposes on Thursday night against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Monroe Freeling (knee) is doubtful for Carolina’s Week 6 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: The rookie got in back-to-back limited sessions, but they must have indeed been quite limited for him to wind up with the rarely-used doubtful tag. It’s very unlikely he plays this weekend. Taylor Moton (blood clot) is questionable after three full practices and would seem to be the favorite to start at right tackle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Monroe Freeling (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP. Freeling played 64 percent of the snaps in Week 4 and looks to be trending in the right direction for Week 6 after the Week 5 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Taylor Moton (blood clots) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: Moton is tentatively on track to make his return from injured reserve this week. Meanwhile, RT Monroe Freeling (knee) sat out on Wednesday. Panthers DT Tershawn Wharton (neck) is practicing in full, while EDGE Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said he is “hopeful” Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) will be able to play in Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: Phillips went down with a hamstring injury late in Sunday’s game against the Lions and didn’t return to the field. For a player with Phillips’ injury history, there were immediate concerns regarding the severity of the injury, but with a Week 5 bye on tap, the hope is Phillips won’t miss much time, if any. Phillips has totaled two sacks in his first four games of the season. In addition to Phillips, the team is also hopeful that OT Monroe Freeling (knee) will be able to return in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Monroe Freeling (concussion) will play in Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: The Panthers entered the season down both of their starting tackles. They will also be without left guard Damien Lewis this week. Getting Freeling back is a big win for Bryce Young and the offense. Freeling has struggled in pass protection so far but is serviceable in the run game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Xavier Legette (knee) will not play in Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: Legette will miss a second straight game with his knee injury. He has caught just two passes for 64 yards on six targets this season and wouldn’t be on the fantasy radar even if he were active. In addition to Legette, the Panthers also ruled out OG Damien Lewis (elbow) for Week 4 against the Lions while OT Monroe Freeling (concussion), DT Lee Hunter (foot), and DT Cam Jackson (knee) were all listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Panthers RT Monroe Freeling (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported earlier this week that stud Panthers LG Damien Lewis (elbow) will be out “a few weeks.” The Panthers have a fantasy-friendly matchup against the Lions this week, but Freeling’s health is worth tracking.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Panthers placed RT Taylor Moton on the reserve/non-football injury list with blood clots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: He’s joined by CB Jaycee Horn, who cut his foot while running and required stitches. Horn’s injury is expected to be a minor one. Moton, on the other hand, is expected to miss the start of the season and the “belief” is he’ll play in 2026. The Panthers later clarified that Moton is hopeful to return from clotting in his lung at “mid-season.” Rookie first-round tackle Monroe Freeling figures to step in for Moton early.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Panthers selected Georgia OT Monroe Freeling with the No. 19 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: The giant Freeling will be blocking for the diminutive Bryce Young in Carolina. The Panthers offensive line in 2025 were graded by PFF as the league’s 17th best pass blocking unit. Freeling (6’7/315) enters the 2026 NFL Draft as one of the most physically gifted offensive linemen in the class, boasting rare movement skills and length for the position. The Bulldogs tackle brings a prototype frame at roughly 6-7, 315 pounds with nearly 35-inch arms, pairing that length with elite athletic traits highlighted by a freakish 9.99 Relative Athletic Score, including a 4.93s forty, 33.5-inch vertical and 9’7” broad jump. Freeling’s athleticism shows up consistently on tape, showing advanced movement capabilities in space, executing reach blocks, lead assignments and screen duties while displaying the quick feet to mirror edge rushers in pass protection. After a developmental sophomore season, Freeling made a major leap in 2025, posting an 86.1 PFF pass-blocking grade while allowing just two sacks and eight total pressures across 469 pass-blocking snaps. His length, quick redirect ability and fluidity passing off twists make him particularly effective against speed rushers and stunts. However, Freeling can struggle to maintain leverage and hand placement at times, with inconsistent run-blocking landmarks and occasional balance issues when he leans into contact.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (toe) is not on Carolina’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: He upgraded to a full practice today. Waller will be a low-end TE2 with Jalen Coker (quad) playing in Week 6 against a Jalen Hurts-less Eagles outfit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (toe) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: He appears to be trending towards playing, though Waller is old enough that we probably shouldn’t count it as a sure thing that he’ll get off the questionable line. Waller would be a reasonable TE2 if he plays against the Eagles on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (toe) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: The Panthers should have their veteran receiving tight end on the field when they take on the Eagles this week. Waller remains a viable TE1, albeit as a somewhat volatile producer. We expect him to be practicing in full by the end of the week, coming off a restful bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught 3-of-6 targets for 36 yards in the Panthers’ Week 4 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller saw minimal involvement as quarterback Bryce Young leaned into his top option through the air, feeding Tetairoa McMillan 16 targets on 41 pass attempts in the absence of both Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette. Fantasy managers that scooped Waller off of waivers following his two-touchdown game in Week 2 are surely left disappointed in the recent returns, making Waller a potential drop candidate as the Panthers head to their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught 5-of-8 targets for 51 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: With Xavier Legette (knee) sidelined and Jalen Coker (quad) joining him, Panthers tight ends Waller, Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans combined for 11/128. It was Waller’s most prolific receiving day of the season even though he didn’t find the end zone. Waller is undoubtedly providing valuable real-life reps for the Cats, but with 10 total receptions through three contests, he is looking like too much of a role player to rise above TE2 streamer status heading into Week 4 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught all three of his targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 2 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller saw as many targets as Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans combined. Unlike the other Carolina tight ends, Waller is still an explosive pass-catcher and a de facto wide receiver. When Bryce Young looked his way, it was for a big play. He made good on the minor role with his first two touchdowns as a Panther. Waller only has five targets through two weeks. He will make the occasional big play, but it’s hard to get him in fantasy lineups with such a limited role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught both of his targets for 28 yards in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller had a short touchdown grab called back on offensive pass interference while rotating snaps and routes with Tommy Tremble. Both Panthers tight ends ran 19 routes on the day and saw two targets from Bryce Young. Waller will continue as a touchdown-reliant TE2 option in Week 2 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Panthers declared TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, WR John Metchie, QB Haynes King, S Zakee Wheatley, OT Albert Reese, OLB Patrick Jones II, and DT Cam Jackson inactive for Week 1 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Sanders, who worked through a lingering ankle injury this offseason, won’t suit up for the team’s season opener. That leaves Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble as the Panthers’ top two tight ends against Chicago. Waller will be a touchdown-dependent TE2 option who probably won’t run many routes in the run-first Carolina offense. Tremble should remain on waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Panthers TE Darren Waller practiced on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller looked “big and fast” in Monday practice, per head coach Dave Canales, and reportedly hit 20 MPH on one of his routes. The veteran tight end was seen catching passes from Bryce Young and could have a chance to suit up for the Panthers’ Week 1 game against the Bears. It’s still too early to know how significant a role Waller will have in Canales’ offense, but he could have some fantasy viability as a streaming option in what is a very thin tight end room in Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: The Charlotte Observer’s Alex Zietlow said the Panthers have not determined when Darren Waller will make his debut.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: While the team has yet to decide when Waller will make his 2026 debut, Waller said his readiness for the upcoming season is “night and day from last year to this year.” Last season, Waller was returning from retirement and needed a lot of time to ramp up. Now, it sounds like Waller could be in a position to at least be ready for the start of the season for a Panthers team that’s in need of help at the tight end position. While his days as a weekly TE1 are well behind him, Waller could have some upside as a matchup-based streamer once we get a better sense of his role in the offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.headline: Trevor Etienne (ankle) is questionable for Carolina’s Week 6 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.analysis: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Etienne would be activated off injured reserve for this week. Etienne practiced in full all week and, with AJ Dillon ruled out, the Panthers currently have just one healthy back on the 53-man roster. Perhaps he’ll be joined by a practice squad player as well. Either way, Etienne has no stand-alone value this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.headline: Trevor Etienne (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.analysis: The Panthers’ backup running back is on track to return this week against the Eagles, while fellow backup A.J. Dillon (ankle) may need more time off. Dillon was unable to practice at all today. Etienne can be stashed in 12-team formats, though he may only qualify as FLEX-viable if he were to get a fill-in start at some point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.headline: Panthers designated RB Trevor Etienne (ankle/IR) to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.analysis: A report in September told us that Etienne would be ready to come off injured reserve ahead of Week 6’s game against the Eagles. That appears to be coming to fruition. He’ll try to cut into AJ Dillon’s reserve role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.headline: Trevor Etienne (ankle) said he will be ready to come off injured reserve before Week 5’s game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.analysis: Etienne suffered a high-ankle sprain in the final preseason game. He may return as the nominal No. 2 back behind Chuba Hubbard after Jonathon Brooks was injured in Week 2, giving him non-zero deep-league value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.headline: Panthers placed RB Trevor Etienne on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.analysis: Etienne will be eligible to come off IR after the first four weeks of the 2026 regular season. He got some buzz during offseason workouts and training camp but has exceedingly little chance of seeing significant regular season snaps for Carolina. Etienne as a rookie in 2025 had 20 carries for 94 scoreless yards, functioning mostly as a kick returner. AJ Dillon will be the depth back behind Chuba Hubbard and Jonathon Brooks as things stand right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.headline: The Charlotte Observers’ Mike Kaye reports that Panthers RB Jonathon Brooks took some first-team reps at training camp on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.analysis: Earlier today, NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reported that “there will be no limitations” for Brooks (knee). First-team usage seemingly affirms that. The team hopes Brooks forms a one-two punch with RB Chuba Hubbard before taking over as the starter at some point. Backup RB Trevor Etienne “also got his fair share of reps, and he worked with the starters as well in the running back rotation.” This is somewhat surprising, and worth keeping an eye on. Regarding Brooks’ showing, Kaye says he “looked quick as he bobbed and weaved with the ball in his hands.” He notably took “a mild hit,” but “showed no signs of struggle afterward.” Brooks looks like a high-upside, risk-reward type of pick right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports the Panthers are “at least hopeful” that Jonathon Brooks (knee) can contribute this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.analysis: It’s part of the reason why the Panthers are willing to let Rico Dowdle leave in free agency. With Chuba Hubbard as the main back, Brooks would likely not be a major part of the offense even if he got to camp healthy after losing most of his NFL career to date to ACL tears. Still, he’s going to be just 23 this offseason, it’s hard to completely give up hope on him. He’ll battle Trevor Etienne for the main backup role if the Panthers don’t bring in anyone else.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.headline: Trevor Etienne rushed one time for four yards in the Panthers’ Wild Card Round loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.analysis: His most important contribution against the Rams was letting one punt return clank off his helmet to be recovered by the Rams, then nearly losing a second one later in the exact same way. Etienne never truly entered the backfield derby in Carolina, topping out at 7/33 against the Patriots in a 42-13 drubbing where he mostly played late. The 114th overall pick in last year’s draft, Etienne could wind up as Chuba Hubbard’s No. 2 back this offseason if the Panthers don’t add anyone else to the room, but this year’s usage doesn’t exactly demonstrate a commitment from the Panthers that leads us to think they want him to be that player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.headline: Trevor Etienne rushed three times for 17 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.analysis: His longest play of the day, an 11-yard run deep in the fourth quarter, came with the Cowboys figuratively begging him to score so they could get the ball back, not even attempting to tackle him. Etienne smartly slid down. He’s got no role worth speaking of at the moment and will fall even further once Chuba Hubbard is healthy again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.headline: Trevor Etienne rushed four times for 22 yards in the Panthers’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-eti.analysis: Etienne was used sparingly even with Chuba Hubbard out this week. Rico Dowdle was the team’s lead back and he gave them no reason to turn to the rookie. Dowdle ran for 206 yards on 23 attempts and scored once. Half of Etienne’s carries came on the Panthers’ penultimate drive while Dowdle was dealing with cramps. Needless to say, Etienne is not on the fantasy radar heading into Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: AJ Dillon (ankle) will not play in Carolina’s Week 6 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: He didn’t practice all week. With Jonathon Brooks also out, it seems likely that Trevor Etienne will be activated to serve as Chuba Hubbard’s main backup. Hubbard will project to get most of the volume here and has stumbled into high-end RB2 value this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: Trevor Etienne (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: The Panthers’ backup running back is on track to return this week against the Eagles, while fellow backup A.J. Dillon (ankle) may need more time off. Dillon was unable to practice at all today. Etienne can be stashed in 12-team formats, though he may only qualify as FLEX-viable if he were to get a fill-in start at some point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: AJ Dillon rushed four times for 16 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: With Jonathon Brooks joining Trevor Etienne on injured reserve, Dillon was indeed the Panthers’ No. 2 back behind Chuba Hubbard. Good for him, though Pro Football Focus charted him with zero first half snaps. Were Hubbard to ever go down with injury, Dillion would form some sort of committee with a practice squad elevation or free agent addition.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: ESPN’s Mike Kaye believes AJ Dillon could spell Chuba Hubbard on “obvious passing downs” in Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: Dillon will step into the main backup role for Week 3 after Jonathon Brooks (groin) wound up on injured reserve. There’s no real timeshare here; Hubbard will be the main back. But Dillon could cut into PPR point territory as Panthers OC Brad Idzik was described as “pleasantly surprised” by the veteran’s receiving ability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: Panthers signed AJ Dillon, formerly of the Eagles, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: Dillon missed all of the 2024 season while recovering from a neck injury he suffered late in the previous year. He returned in 2025 on a one-year deal with the Eagles. Dillon appeared in the first six games of the year but eventually fell off the game-day roster with Philly’s addition of Tank Bigsby. He finished the season with 12 carries for 60 yards. Dillon will be fighting for a roster spot in Carolina during training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: Eagles declared RB A.J. Dillon, CB Mac McWilliams OL Drew Kendall TE Grant Calcaterra and QB Sam Howell inactive for Philadelphia’s Week 7 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: Will Shipley will assume second RB duties, with Tank Bigsby perhaps working in more on offense after the mini-bye. Active for the Eagles are OL Landon Dickerson (ankle) and DT Jalen Carter (heel), the latter of whom was questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: Eagles listed Saquon Barkley (knee) as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: It’s only an estimated report, but an estimated DNP is still concerning for Barkley, who has struggled on the ground to start the season. We’ll see if things change come Tuesday when the Eagles actually hold a practice, but this is clearly something worth monitoring until we receive word that Barkley is in the clear for Thursday night’s game against the Giants. If Barkley is unable to go, A.J. Dillon could be in line to handle early-down touches while Will Shipley mixes in on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: Eagles RB Will Shipley (oblique) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 2 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: Shipley didn’t practice all week with his “oblique” injury (reports are that he is dealing with fractured ribs) and is a candidate to be placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Tank Bigsby will take Shipley’s role in the offense, although it is possible that AJ Dillon gets more snaps as the Eagles figure out how they want to implement the newly-acquired Bigsby.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: A.J. Dillon rushed five time for 27 yards and caught 3-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Eagles’ preseason Week 1 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: Dillon forced one missed tackle along the way. Reports have suggested that Dillon is playing well as a pass catcher, and his preseason showing reflected that. He appears to be in the hunt for the No. 2 job.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports the Eagles have ‘been impressed with A.J. Dillon’s ability to catch the ball out of the backfield” in training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: Dillon caught just 21 passes in three seasons at Boston College, but surprised everyone in 2021 when he caught 34 passes for 313 yards and two touchdowns. He would go on to catch 28 passes in 2022 and had another 22 receptions in 2023, suggesting he had more to offer in the passing game than we initially believed. Dillon missed all of 2024 with a neck injury and signed a one-year contract with the Eagles this offseason. He’s currently battling with Will Shipley for RB2 duties behind Saquon Barkley, but Graziano believes Dillon “would be the one to benefit the most” if Barkley were to ever miss time. He also noted that he expects Shipley to have a role regardless of Barkley’s health, although we wouldn’t expect that to turn into a reliable one for fantasy managers given Barkley’s bell cow usage. Both Dillon and Shipley make for interesting stashes in an offense that ranked second in neutral rush rate last season (52 percent), but it’s hard to imagine anybody but Barkley having standalone value on a week-to-week basis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: After missing all of practice last week and being a DNP on Thursday, Diggs was back on the field Friday, which is a good sign for his Week 6 availability with one practice left to go in the week. The Commanders take on the 49ers on Monday Night Football this week and will likely announce Diggs’ availability sometime Saturday, but he could be on track to return in what is a must-win game for the 1-3-1 Commanders. Diggs has caught 18 passes for 170 yards and three touchdowns this season and would be in the mix as a fringe WR3/WR4 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he is hopeful Diggs will get some practice reps in later this week. Diggs missed Week 5 with the hamstring issue, and a DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6, even if Quinn remains optimistic. Terry McLaurin and Chig Okonkwo led the team in receiving last week. McLaurin should pull away from Okonkwo as he puts more time between himself and the hamstring injury that previously knocked him out for a week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) will not play in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs did not practice this week and was ruled out by the team shortly after Friday’s practice concluded. His absence will give rookie Antonio Williams, who ran 30 routes last week, a chance to take on a bigger role. Williams tied for the team lead with eight targets in Week 4’s game against the Colts and could be treated as a desperation WR4/FLEX play. Fantasy managers considering Williams for their lineups may want to check the weather, as rain and wind are currently forecasted for the area, which could create a suboptimal environment for Washington’s passing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is not practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs was unable to get on the practice field this week and will likely be ruled out for Week 5’s game against the Giants in the next few hours. Rookie receiver Antonio Williams would again be in line for a busy day and could be the favorite to lead the team in targets this week, especially if Terry McLaurin (hamstring) also misses this week. McLaurin’s status remains wait and see after he was spotted on the practice field Friday after being a DNP on the first two days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: This runs contrary to media reporters that said he was participating. Welp. Diggs is officially in danger of missing Week 5 after two DNPs to start the week. Perhaps the Commanders deep wideouts will merit some desperation FLEX plays this week with Jayden Daniels under center. Or perhaps Diggs will turn it around enough on Friday to get a questionable tag.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs was held out of Wednesday’s session because of the hamstring issue. Even a limited practice today puts him on track to suit up on Sunday. Terry McLaurin, on the other hand, looks likely to miss another week with a hamstring injury of his own. That will put Diggs in the WR1 seat for Week 5 against the Giants. Antonio Williams will continue to operate as the team’s No. 2 receiver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs didn’t appear to get hurt during the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts, but it looks like he felt something after the game. With Terry McLaurin also sidelined for today’s practice, Antonio Williams could be the Commanders’ No. 1 receiver in Week 5. He saw eight targets on Sunday, only one fewer than Diggs. The Commanders’ absurdly long injury report will be one to monitor as the week progresses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 5-of-9 targets for 35 yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs was the Commanders’ No. 1 receiver with Terry McLaurin out. That was good for a 24 percent target share and a handful of PPR points, but not much else. Marcus Mariota went down on the second drive and Athan Kaliakmanis took his place for the remainder of the game. Kaliakmanis made a few big throws but the offense struggled on the whole. Diggs could be in line for a big boost in fantasy production if Jayden Daniels is back next week, but McLaurin could just as easily return and take back his WR1 role. Diggs’ Week 5 fantasy outlook could swing wildly depending on how those injuries shake out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 4-of-7 targets for 33 yards in the Commanders’ Week 3 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs didn’t catch any passes in the first half on his three targets, but “bounced back” in the final two quarters to turn a disaster of a game into a middling one. The wideout was able to score two touchdowns in Week 2 against Dallas, but was closer to non-factor than threat against a tougher Seattle defense. He’ll look to rebound and find the end zone again as the second option behind Terry McLaurin against the Colts in London in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 5-of-6 targets for 47 yards and two touchdowns in the Commanders’ Week 2 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs’ six targets were tied for the second-most on the Commanders in Sunday’s loss. Diggs was responsible for both of his team’s touchdowns, with his first coming on a four-yard pass in the end zone from Jayden Daniels, who exited at the end of the second quarter with what has now been diagnosed as a dislocated elbow. In the fourth quarter, Diggs connected with Marcus Mariota for a leaping 20-yard score to cut the Cowboys’ lead to 30-20, but that would be the closest Washington would get to any hopes of a comeback. Diggs has now scored in each of his first two games with the Commanders but will be hard to trust as anything more than a WR3/WR4 against a stout Seahawks defense next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-wins.headline: Kevin Winston (undisclosed) will not play in Week 6 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-wins.analysis: Winston has been a DNP in practice all week and has now been ruled out for Week 6’s game against the Colts. The second-year safety has started all four games he has appeared in this season, totaling 29 tackles and one forced fumble while earning a PFF coverage grade of 47.2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-wins.headline: Titans placed S Kevin Winston Jr. (hamstring) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-wins.analysis: He’s joined there by fellow safeties Mike Brown (ankle) and Xavier Woods (hamstring) as the Titans signed Erick Hallett and Sanoussi Kane off the Lions and Ravens practice squads. It is certainly End Of Season Hours in Tennessee. 2025 third-round pick Winston finishes his rookie season with a 89.4 PFF run defense grade, but just a 43.4 PFF coverage grade. It was a land of contrasts. He’ll probably be the favorite to start next to Amani Hooker next season if he’s healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-wins.headline: Titans declared S Kevin Winston, RT JC Latham, WR Bryce Oliver, OT John Ojukwu, OL Jackson Slater and CB Samuel Womack inactive for Tennessee’s Week 4 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-wins.analysis: Winston (hamstring) has not been active yet this year as a third-round pick, dealing with an ACL recovery and a litany of other injuries. Oliver is out with a knee and Latham with a hip. The other three are healthy scratches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-wins.headline: Titans selected Penn State S Kevin Winston Jr. with the No. 82 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-wins.analysis: Winston (6’1/215) is a traits-based projection who flashed starting-caliber tools at Penn State before a knee injury prematurely ended his 2024 campaign. A long, physical boundary safety in Tom Allen’s 4-2-5 scheme, Winston lined up high and low but showed his best work downhill near the line of scrimmage. His 2023 film speaks volumes: 61 tackles, 2.5 TFLs, a pick, and five pass breakups to go with a stout 91.1 run defense grade and 92.8 tackling mark per PFF. His game is built on power and urgency, and he triggers quickly on run fits, attacks blocks with authority, and finishes tackles with minimal wasted motion—when he’s in position. He thrives in the box and can match up with tight ends due to his frame and competitiveness at the catch point. NFL personnel rave about his makeup as a team captain with high-end football character. The red flags, however, lie in the processing and fluidity departments. Winston can be a tick slow diagnosing route concepts from deep alignments and is inconsistent transitioning in space, particularly when backpedaling or flipping his hips. His reactive quickness is still developing, and his missed time in 2024 limits the sample size to fully gauge growth in those areas. A strong fit as a tight end eraser or big nickel in sub-packages, Winston profiles as a developmental starter with box safety dimensions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-wins.headline: Uncommitted three-star 2022 S Kevin Winston Jr. announced a top-two of Maryland and Penn State.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-wins.analysis: Winston (6'2/190) has taken three official visits this month, with his trip to Happy Valley (June 4) being followed by stops at Michigan State (June 11) and Maryland (June 18). At this point in the DeMatha Catholic safety’s recruitment, it appears that Michigan State has fallen out of contention. Winston spoke highly of Maryland after his visit to College Park, and it’s also worth noting that the Terrapins have yet to receive a commitment from a safety in the 2022 class. On the other hand, Penn State already has two safeties in its 2022 crop to date. Winston has yet to decide when he will announce which school he’ll attend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Eagles signed Joe Milton, formerly of the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Milton will join Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton on the Eagles’ 53-man roster. This move comes a day after it was revealed that Jalen Hurts would be out indefinitely due to a superficial blood clot that could sideline him for the next several weeks. Milton will likely serve as the Eagles’ emergency third QB on game days and seems unlikely to see any playing time at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Cowboys signed QB Joe Milton to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Milton initially made the 53-man roster but was let go after the initial wave of waiver claims. He went unclaimed when waivers ran Tuesday and now returns to the Cowboys on the practice squad. With Sam Howell winning the QB2 job, Milton will be QB3 heading into the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Joe Milton was not claimed on waivers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: He’ll likely catch on with a practice squad in the next day or two, perhaps with the Cowboys again. Milton had initially made the 53-man roster in Dallas but lost his spot when they claimed Emari Demercado off waivers. The 26-year-old has an arm that was made to play quarterback and a decision-making process that was made to play quarterback in 1975.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Sam Howell and Joe Milton will compete for the No. 2 quarterback job this summer.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: This is mostly just a housekeeping item for dynasty managers, but re-draft managers can still file it away for a potential rainy day in Dallas. Things could change via the 2026 NFL Draft, but these two are set to duke it out for now. Milton flubbed his second-half opportunity in Week 18 last year, perhaps prompting the Cowboys to search for a more reliable No. 2 option. The team certainly has a type. Both Howell and Milton possess very strong arms, which should allow the Cowboys to continue attacking downfield if starting QB Dak Prescott were to miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Joe Milton III completed 7-of-13 passes for 73 yards and an interception in the Cowboys’ 34-17, Week 18 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: A year after destroying the Bills’ backups in the final game of the 2024-25 season, Milton failed to deliver the same kind of fireworks here. He started the second half for the Cowboys and led five drives, only one of which resulted in points. He’ll finish the season 15-of-24 for 183 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, while adding four rushes for 45 yards. He will return as Dak Prescott’s backup in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Dak Prescott completed 19-of-31 passes for 188 yards and two interceptions in the Cowboys’ 44-24, Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: He was benched with eight minutes left in the game and Dallas down by 27 points, Joe Milton led a touchdown drive with things out of hand. Both of Prescott’s picks were pretty weird, one of them by dropping edge player Deondrea Tillman. He was hit hard today, taking 14 pressures in 38 dropbacks per PFF. Obviously, this wasn’t the QB1 game you were promised — it didn’t look like the Cowboys had a real answer for their easy underneath stuff getting poached. Prescott will look to rebound in Week 9 against the Cardinals and should remain on the QB1 line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Dak Prescott completed 31-of-40 passes for 251 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Cowboys’ 31-14 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Testing the limits of what an all-Jake Ferguson offense could deliver to the world, one of Prescott’s picks deflected off George Pickens’ hands, and the other got him benched for Joe Milton in a 17-point deficit the Cowboys were obviously not overcoming. (Milton went 3-of-5 for 41 yards and a pick of his own.) The pass offense lost a lot of oomph without Lamb, and now Prescott gets to deal with an absolutely livid Packers front seven on Sunday night next week. If Lamb misses Week 4, it would be hard to fire up Prescott as more than a borderline QB1. The Dallas defense has forced plenty of passing situations for the Cowboys, as Prescott has 126 pass attempts in three games, but it would be a tough sell against a great defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Joe Milton completed 9-of-18 passes for 122 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Cowboys’ preseason game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: At one point, Milton was 3-of-10 passing. The second-year quarterback who took a sack for a safety on his team’s opening drive looked as erratic as we’ve seen during his time as a pro, and ended the day with an absurd 15.2 ADOT. Milton missed his intended target all night, with PFF attributing just one of his incompletions to a dropped pass. His best play on the night came on a 49-yard completion to Jonathan Mingo, but it’s hard to ignore what we’ve witnessed from Milton through two preseason games. He’s completed 26-of-47 passes (55.3 percent) for one touchdown and two interceptions, and has taken three sacks on 10 pressures. Thankfully for the Cowboys, Dak Prescott is healthy, but it may be time for the Cowboys to explore additional depth behind their QB1 after Milton appears to have reverted to the player we saw for parts of six college seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Joe Milton completed 17-of-29 passes for 143 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Cowboys’ 31-21 preseason loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Milton also rushed for 22 yards on five carries. The 2024 sixth-round pick drew that start in Saturday’s exhibition, and limited mistakes for most of the evening, taking just one sack while throwing an interception that bounced off his receiver’s hands. His lone touchdown pass came on a seven-yard completion to Rivaldo Fairweather, who broke free from his defender in the end zone. Known for his rocket arm and erratic accuracy, Milton continues to impress when given the opportunity and should be in line for more playing time next Saturday when the Cowboys play host to the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Cowboys acquired QB Joe Milton and a seventh-round pick from the Patriots in exchange for a fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: The 2024 sixth-round pick made one appearance as a rookie, taking over for Drake Maye mid-game in a meaningless Week 18 affair. Milton played extremely well in his brief time in the spotlight, throwing for 241 yards and a touchdown while rushing for 16 yards and another score. The Pats signed Joshua Dobbs to a two-year deal in free agency, locking him in as the backup to Maye for 2025. In turn, the team got what it could for Milton and gave him a chance to be a QB2 behind Dak Prescott. With Prescott under contract through 2028, Milton doesn’t have much fantasy value, even in deep dynasty leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. will play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper had his 21-day practice window opened earlier this week, but is officially set to return after logging a full practice on Friday. The rookie receiver could step into an immediate role for the Jets with Adonai Mitchell (finger) out for at least one more week, but he could still be a few weeks away from fantasy relevance. Cooper played on just five snaps in Week 1 before his injury, but did catch one pass for 30 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets opened the 21-day practice window for Omar Cooper (ankle).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper has been on injured reserve since sustaining a high ankle sprain in Week 1. He could return as soon as this week against the Patriots, though he could see his snaps and routes limited. Cooper can be rostered in deeper 12-team formats. Garrett Wilson’s domination of the New York passing offense makes it tough for anyone else to post fantasy-relevant numbers for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets placed WR Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: The news was first reported by NFL Insider Ian Rapoport. Cooper is going on injured reserve for an ankle sprain. He’ll be sidelined for at least four games with a designation to return. Rapoport mentions that Cooper should be back “shortly.” Cooper could still make an impact in the second half of his rookie season, but he isn’t worth holding in most fantasy formats at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) will not play in Week 2 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: This was always expected to be the case, but head coach Aaron Glenn said on Friday, while speaking with the media, that Cooper, RB/KR Kene Nwangwu (back), S Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin), and EDGE Joseph Ossai (foot) will all miss Sunday’s game against the Packers. It was reported earlier this week that the Jets are hoping to have Cooper back “within the next four weeks,” so it wouldn’t be surprising if he also missed Week 3’s game against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) is “week to week, with the hope that he returns within the next four weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: The phrasing at the end of that sentence makes it clear the Jets are pondering not sending him to injured reserve. Fantasy managers who took the plunge in non-dynasty leagues do not necessarily have to hold on to Cooper through the early weeks if something catches their eye on the wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that Jets WR Omar Cooper is believed to have suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Pelissero also reported that Cooper will undergo an MRI to further assess the injury on Monday, confirming NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport’s report from earlier this evening. Cooper could be looking at a multi-week absence, but only time will tell. Hopefully, it is just a mild injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Jets WR Omar Cooper’s (ankle) X-rays were negative, and he will now undergo an MRI.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper got hurt at the end of a 30-yard catch-and-run against the Titans, when another player rolled up on his right ankle. Cooper helped bring his offense to the Titans’ four-yard line. It was his only time touching the football. For now, we wait and see what the diagnosis is, but the fact that he needs more imaging is a little discouraging.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. suffered an ankle injury in the Jets’ Week 1 game against the Titans and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: The maligned first-round rookie had a rugged, 30-yard catch-and-run to the Titans’ four-yard line on the Jets’ opening series, but got his right ankle rolled up on in the process. He required the assistance of a cart, but the Jets claimed he might still return. He was then ruled out at halftime. It’s a brutal blow for a first-rounder who supposedly had a rough summer. Despite the delayed ruleout, Cooper should definitely be considered on the wrong side of questionable for Week 2. If he is occupying one of your final bench spots, he will be a shaky hold during this week’s all-important waivers run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: The Athletic’s Zack Rosenblatt believes Omar Cooper Jr.'s role “should grow over time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper “started to show some signs of life by the end” of training camp. The first-rounder will split time with Isaiah Williams in the slot and also operate “as a gadget player.” Keep him out of lineups early, but he is still on the dynasty radar and should be monitored on the waiver wire in shallow leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets WR Omar Cooper caught 1-of-1 targets for nine yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper played extensively in the Jets’ first preseason game, prompting The Athletic’s Zach Rosenblatt to write that WR Isaiah Williams appeared to have overtaken Cooper for the starting slot receiver job. This week, Cooper out-snapped WR Isaiah Williams six to one on the first drive. Williams continued playing on the second drive before rotating with Cooper on the third. PFF’s Nathan Jahnke notes that when Cooper returned, he lined up out wide while Williams manned the slot. Williams caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards and one fumble, though it was recovered by the Jets. It appears as though Cooper may have regained his spot as the Jets’ WR3 behind WR1 Garrett Wilson and WR2 Adonai Mitchell. Cooper still makes for a risky late-round dart throw, but he will get more chances to contribute.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will not play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: It was reported earlier this week that Mitchell underwent a “small procedure” on the finger he injured in practice ahead of Week 3. Given that news, it doesn’t come as much of a surprise to learn that Mitchell will miss his fourth straight game with the injury. With rookie Omar Cooper Jr. set to play in his first game since Week 1, Mitchell could face additional competition for targets when he finally returns to the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell underwent a “small procedure” on his hand.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: As expected, he did not practice today. Per Glenn, Mitchell remains week to week. This explains the lengthy absence for Mitchell, who hasn’t played since injuring his finger in practice ahead of Week 3. According to Glenn, Mitchell is moving his fingers around well, which is hopefully a sign that he will be back soon. With Omar Cooper Jr.'s practice window now open, Mitchell could return to a rather crowded receiver room once he is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will not play in Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell will miss his third straight game with the finger injury he sustained in practice, ahead of Week 3’s game against the Lions. During Mitchell’s absence, Isaiah Williams has run 59 routes, the second-most of any Jets receiver, but has seen just five targets. Garrett Wilson is the only reliable receiver in this passing game, while rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq is a boom-or-bust option against a defense that has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points to tight ends this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) remains week to week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell will likely miss his third straight game with the finger issue. He suffered the injury just as he was coming on as the team’s clear No. 2 wideout behind Garrett Wilson. With Mitchell sidelined last week against the Bears, Isaiah Williams was second on the team in pass routes, saw three targets, and caught a 58-yard touchdown from Geno Smith. Williams will have some deep-league viability in Week 5 against a Browns defense allowing the most air yards in the NFL. Adonai was officially a non-participant on Wednesday’s injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets declared WR Adonai Mitchell, RB Breece Hall, CB Nahshon Wright, LB Kiko Mauigoa, DE Kingsley Enagbare, OL Dylan Parham, and TE Mason Taylor inactive for Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell will miss another game with his finger injury and Hall will be sidelined with a quad injury he sustained last week against the Lions. Garrett Wilson, with Mitchell out, should continue dominating air yards and targets in the balanced Jets offense. Braelon Allen will take over as New York’s lead back for now and should be in all fantasy lineups against a suspect Chicago run defense. Kenyon Sadiq has some streaming appeal with Mitchell out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will not play in Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell was a DNP in Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices, so the team’s decision to rule him out on Friday doesn’t come as a surprise. Mitchell will now aim to return in Week 5 against the Browns. Rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq, who saw a season-high eight targets last week in Mitchell’s absence, will be on the fantasy radar as a fringe TE1 with Mitchell again sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: It’s trending in the wrong direction for Mitchell’s odds of playing in Week 4. We imagine he’ll get in at least a limited session Friday to see how natural it is for him to catch the football with his injured finger, but he looks headed for the questionable line — at best — against the Bears.
