https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell hurt his finger late last week and missed New York’s Week 3 game against the Lions. He could miss their Week 4 tilt against the Bears too. With Mitchell sidelined last week, Garrett Wilson had a dominant 49 percent air yards share to go along with 13 targets. Kenyon Sadiq, who had eight targets in Week 3, would once again be viable if Mitchell is sidelined in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets declared Adonai Mitchell (finger) inactive for Week 3 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: The Jets took things down to the wire with Mitchell but will ultimately hold him out for at least a week as he works through the finger injury. The Jets are now extremely thin at receiver with first-round rookie Omar Cooper Jr. on IR on top of the Mitchell injury. Isaiah Williams will take over as the team’s No. 2 receiver this week. Also inactive for the Jets are CB Nahshon Wright, TE Mason Taylor, LB Kiko Mauigoa, RB Kene Nwangwu, K Blake Grupe, and S Minkah Fitzpatrick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Adonai Mitchell (finger) is expected to miss Week 3 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: We’ll get official word from the team in a few minutes. If Mitchell is indeed out, Isaiah Williams would step in as the team’s No. 2 receiver. Rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq would also take on a larger role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 6 against the Patriots
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction for Hall all week. The 25-year-old back was a DNP on both Wednesday and Thursday, and will now miss a third straight game as a result of his injury. Braelon Allen will again lead the Jets’ backfield this week against the Patriots and has handled 44 of the Jets’ 48 running back opportunities since Week 4. Allen will be a volatile RB2 against a Patriots defense that ranks 18th against running backs in fantasy scoring this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: ESPN’s Rich Cimini reports that Breece Hall (quad) is working with trainers on the side field on Thursday, yet remains week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: This is a small but positive update. Hall typically works on his quad rehab program elsewhere or simply observes practice. Today’s return to the side field will still result in him being listed as a non-participant, but as Cimini says, this is measurable “progress” for the Jets’ top running back. Braelon Allen will undoubtedly get the start this week, but perhaps Hall has a chance to return in Week 7 against the Dolphins. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) remains week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall will not practice today, and it sounds like he will not practice on Thursday or Friday either. Braelon Allen has played productively in his stead, most recently rushing 24 times for 116 yards and a touchdown against the Browns. Allen is a locked-in RB2 until Hall returns from his upper-leg injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Braelon Allen will once again be in line to lead the Jets’ backfield with Hall sidelined for a second consecutive week. Hall did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday and will presumably be a DNP again on Friday, now that he has been ruled out ahead of practice. Allen saw 100 percent of the Jets’ running back opportunities last week, rushing 14 times for 59 scoreless yards while adding two receptions for an additional eight yards on two targets. He’ll be a fringe RB1/RB2 in what should be another high-volume day for the third-year back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) is still “week to week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: It doesn’t look like Hall will practice this week as he recovers from the injury he sustained in Week 3. That would mean Braelon Allen, who saw all 14 running back rushes for New York in Week 4, will again function as the team’s workhorse in Week 5 against the Browns. Allen should still be considered a top-24 option despite the Jets’ immense offensive struggles last week against Chicago. The Browns’ defense is allowing the sixth-highest EPA per rush this season. Hall was officially a non-participant on Wednesday’s injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets declared WR Adonai Mitchell, RB Breece Hall, CB Nahshon Wright, LB Kiko Mauigoa, DE Kingsley Enagbare, OL Dylan Parham, and TE Mason Taylor inactive for Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Mitchell will miss another game with his finger injury and Hall will be sidelined with a quad injury he sustained last week against the Lions. Garrett Wilson, with Mitchell out, should continue dominating air yards and targets in the balanced Jets offense. Braelon Allen will take over as New York’s lead back for now and should be in all fantasy lineups against a suspect Chicago run defense. Kenyon Sadiq has some streaming appeal with Mitchell out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall was initially mentioned as being week-to-week when he was diagnosed with his quad injury, so he was never really considered a candidate to play in Week 4 despite the team waiting until the end of the week to rule him out. With Hall out, the Jets will look to Braelon Allen to handle most of the backfield duties. Allen will profile as a solid RB2 candidate with a chance for more upside in what could be a high-volume day against the Bears. In addition to Hall, the Jets also ruled out OG Dylan Parham (knee), TE Mason Taylor (thumb), and LB Kiko Mauigoa (quad) for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: A “Week-to-week” designation leaves us struggling to see any way that Hall plays this week. Braelon Allen should be a reasonable RB2 in Hall’s absence. Hall will likely be questionable at best for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) did not practice Wednsday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall went down with a quad injury on Sunday against the Lions and did not return to the game. Braelon Allen took over as the Jets’ lead back, a role he’ll likely continue to occupy in Week 4 against the Bears’ gettable rush defense if Hall is sidelined. Allen should be rostered in all leagues and could be a top-20 option in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Breece Hall is considered week-to-week with a quad injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: According to Rapoport, Hall received “good news after the MRI” he received after he suffered a thigh injury in the Jets’ Week 3 loss to the Lions. It doesn’t sound like Hall will be in line to suit up for Week 4’s game against the Bears, but he could avoid being placed on IR if the Jets believe he can return in less than four weeks. Braelon Allen will presumably take over as the Jets’ lead back during Hall’s absence, while Isaiah Davis could also see some work on offense after playing primarily on special teams through the first three weeks of the season. Allen has rushed 19 times for 61 yards and a touchdown this season while also tallying four receptions for 11 yards. He will border on the RB2/RB3 range in Week 4 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.headline: Colts released Darius Slayton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.analysis: Slayton signed with the Colts less than a month ago but never suited up for the team on game day. The 29-year-old speedster was briefly considered as a candidate to replace Alec Pierce (foot), but he’s once again on the open market in search of work. A knee injury resulted in Slayton being scratched from Week 5’s matchup against the Steelers, so it’s possible he’ll have to prove he’s healthy before signing elsewhere this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.headline: Colts WR Darius Slayton (knee) was ruled out for Week 5 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.analysis: Slayton was listed as questionable after injuring his knee during practice on Friday. He’s since been ruled out, postponing his Colts debut for another week. Nick Westbrook-Ikene has been elevated from the Colts’ practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.headline: Colts WR Darius Slayton (knee) is questionable for Week 5 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.analysis: The Colts are banged up at wide receiver and ESPN’s Stephen Holder believes this might have been the week the Colts finally got Slayton involved. He suffered a knee injury in Friday’s practice, though. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.headline: Colts signed WR Darius Slayton, formerly of the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.analysis: The seven-year veteran was released by the Giants prior to the start of the regular season, now landing on his feet in Indianapolis to presumably fill in for the injured Alec Pierce. Pierce recently re-injured the heel he had offseason surgery on and will miss an undetermined number of games. Slayton brings a similar, field-stretching archetype to a Colts team in desperate need of someone to elongate the middle of the field. It remains most likely that Josh Downs steps into the featured role through the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.headline: Giants released WR Darius Slayton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.analysis: The longest-tenured Giants player is now in search of a new home after the team opted to release the 29-year-old receiver on Monday. Slayton was reportedly at risk of not making the initial 53-man roster out of camp, but survived the initial cuts only to be released a week later. During his seven seasons with the Giants, Slayton totaled 296 receptions for 4,435 yards and 22 touchdowns while serving primarily as a field stretcher. He posted four seasons of 724 or more receiving yards and had an impressive rookie campaign when he went for 48-740-8 as a rookie fifth-rounder out of Auburn. Slayton should have no trouble finding a new home in the coming days, but it may take some time before he’s back to seeing the field in a meaningful capacity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Darius Slayton underwent core-muscle surgery but is “expected to be a full go for training camp.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.analysis: Slayton will likely miss all of the early offseason program leading up to camp. His absence could give rookie wideout Malachi Fields more reps with the first-team offense. Free agent addition Darnell Mooney will likely run with the ones as well. Slayton has been a consistent deep threat for the Giants since being drafted in 2019, but the team’s moves at wideout this offseason suggest a smaller role is likely for the veteran wideout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.headline: Darius Slayton caught 4-of-9 targets for 34 yards in a Week 18 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.analysis: Slayton had a huge 72-yard touchdown catch called back due to an offensive pass interference penalty that didn’t seem necessary. He will end the season with 37 catches on 63 targets for 538 yards and one touchdown in 14 games. Slayton is under contract for one more season, but the Giants can opt out of it if they want to take on $3 million in dead cap space. It’s more likely that Slayton remains as the team’s deep threat in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.headline: Giants WR Wan’Dale Robinson (rib) won’t play in New York’s Week 18 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.analysis: Robinson enters free agency off his first career 1,000-yard season, shedding his label as a quick-game only option by setting a career-high with 11.0 yards per reception. He turns 25 in a few days and will be one of the premiere free agents at wideout to hit the market if the Giants don’t tag him or otherwise extend him. The final seasonal line will be 92/1014/4 for Robinson, and his absence leaves Darius Slayton as a fine FLEX play in Week 18.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.headline: Darius Slayton caught 2-of-3 targets for 36 yards in the Giants’ Week 17 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.analysis: Slayton lined up in the slot on the Giants’ fourth drive, got open on a corner route and hauled in a pass from QB Jaxson Dart that netted him 18 yards. Unfortunately, Slayton had to backpedal to nab the ball and ultimately fell over after securing the pass. He was quickly touched down by a Raiders defender. Slayton earned an end zone target from nine yards out on the following drive, but a Raiders defender successfully contested the catch in the air. Slayton is just a boom-bust FLEX against the Cowboys next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.headline: Darius Slayton caught 1-of-2 targets for eight yards in the Giants’ Week 16 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-sla.analysis: Slayton saw 10 targets last week and went for 53 yards on four grabs. He failed to repeat the solid performance and instead committed yet another drop. His hands have been a liability all year and his latest drop could result in less playing time next week. He isn’t on the fantasy radar heading into Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught both targets for 13 yards in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram has not seen more than five targets in a game this season and has been held out of the end zone since Week 1, making him a difficult start in fantasy leagues of all sizes. He can safely remain on the bench in an enticing matchup against the Cardinals in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught all four targets for 55 yards in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram did a large portion of his damage on a busted coverage that allowed him to pick up 34 yards and come just short of a receiving score. The 55 yards are a season high, and it’s encouraging to see more involvement after being a non-factor in the previous two weeks. Engram will hope to build on this effort in Week 6 against the Seahawks, but fantasy managers shouldn’t bet on it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught 1-of-5 targets for six yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram again had a good route rate but didn’t make the most of his short targets from Bo Nix. Engram, who now has five receptions through four games, is not a fantasy option in any format and should remain on waiver wires for now. He’s been targeted on just 11 percent of his routes this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught his lone target for 17 yards in the Broncos’ Week 2 win against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram followed up his four catch, 43 yard, one touchdown Week 1 performance with a dud against his former team. Engram ran a route on just 15 of Bo Nix’s 34 drop backs, a far lower rate than he had in Week 1 against the Chiefs. That kind of role and usage would mean Engram is unusable in fantasy formats. He should remain on waiver wires ahead of the Broncos’ Week 3 matchup against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught 4-of-5 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 1 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram’s trip to paint came from 19 yards out on the team’s second possession to knot the score at seven in the first quarter, which would be the last time the team would be within striking distance for the remainder of the game. Nix’s timing was continually thrown off while under mounting pressure from Steve Spanguolo’s Kansas City defense, resulting in numerous off-target throws. Engram managed to corral two such throws and turn otherwise poor passes into completions for his young quarterback. Regardless of the low yardage total, Engram managed to score for the second time wearing the Denver blue and orange after notching just one touchdown in his first year with the team in 2025. Engram remains a low-upside TE2 ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: The Denver Post’s Parker Gabriel believes “it would be a surprise” if Adam Trautman didn’t outsnap Evan Engram again in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: There’s been some mild hype for Engram again in the early offseason, but it’s hard to understand why the Broncos would have brought in Jaylen Waddle if they thought getting Engram more involved in the offense would have been a notable upgrade. Engram belongs in TE2 purgatory for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: The Denver Post’s Troy Renck believes readers should “buy” into Broncos TE Evan Engram’s performance at organized team activities.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram is “making light work of linebackers in coverage with eye-widening catches,” which Renck thinks could suggest Engram is headed toward a bounce-back campaign. Renck also believes Engram will be more involved in the offense thanks to Davis Webb’s promotion to offensive coordinator. Webb recruited Engram, his former teammate, to join the Broncos last year. Renck also rightly believes new WR Jaylen Waddle will command safety attention, clearing out the middle of the field for Engram. However, he does not address the fact that Waddle represents a massive increase in target competition. Renck also spends the entire piece comparing Engram to a banana and asks whether said banana is ripe or stuck in a tailpipe. Seriously. Engram can be viewed as a potential TE2 candidate in best ball, but we fear a tailpipe scenario is in play for those hoping he produces a TE1 outcome.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Broncos general manager George Paton said the team wants to add to TE Evan Engram’s workload next year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: The Broncos have also been heavily scouting the incoming tight end class. Per Paton, the group has “a nice variety of different types.” The team has hosted at least three tight ends on top-30 visits. Engram, 31, earned 77 targets last season. It is tough to envision him meaningfully increasing that number, but the Broncos obviously do not want to tip their hand ahead of next week’s draft, if they do intend to select a tight end. Paton adds that the team is “really honed in” on the players they expect to be available in the picks 45-75 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Broncos are hosting a top-30 pre-draft visit with Vanderbilt TE Eli Stowers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Stowers, who won the Mackey Award in 2025 after catching 62 balls for 769 yards and four touchdowns at Vanderbilt, has gained a little bit of steam ahead of the 2026 draft. He’s widely expected to be the second tight end off the draft board after Oregon TE Kenyon Sadiq. Evan Engram’s role in the Denver offense would become an uncertain one if the Broncos invest significant draft capital in Stowers, whose statistical and efficiency profiles are far superior to the hyper-athletic Sadiq. Stowers has also made pre-draft visits with the Cowboys, Rams, and Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught 2-of-3 targets for 19 yards in the Broncos’ Conference Championship loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram again failed to replicate the success he had with the Jaguars from 2022 to 2023, when he amassed 1,729 receiving yards on 187 catches while also scoring eight times. The 31-year-old tight end, who has made a name for himself as a short-yardage merchant, averaged a career-low 4.2 ADOT this season, but still managed 5.9 yards after the catch. Engram signed a two-year contract with the Broncos this offseason and carries a dead cap hit just north of $10.3 million if the team were to release him. Despite obviously being on the back nine of his career, Engram remains a solid option in short-yardage situations and should be locked in for at least one more season with the Broncos. That said, he’ll be hard to trust for fantasy purposes after finishing as a top-12 PPR tight end just twice in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-3 targets for 19 yards in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Nix’s only incompletion when targeting Sutton resulted in the veteran receiver getting rocked over the middle of the field on a ball Nix led him directly into oncoming contact. Sutton vented his frustration by repeatedly pounding the ground following the hit, with it unclear whether it was due to the hit or the incompletion on third down on a night the Broncos struggled to move the football to the tune of only 168 yards of total offense. Fantasy managers likely aren’t utilizing Sutton as a weekly option, but will want to track his practice status ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Cardinals if bye week fill-ins are required.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-3 targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: It’s the first touchdown for Sutton on the season, and it tied the game at 17-17. The 31-year-old was unable to find room versus the Chargers’ secondary, and for the fifth-straight week, Sutton was held under 50 yards. His size could give the smaller Seahawks’ defensive backs trouble, but he’s essentially a touchdown-dependent FLEX for Week 6 against Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 1-of-6 targets for four yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton was the recipient of a couple off-target intermediate looks from Bo Nix, who struggled to place the ball against the 49ers secondary. Sutton could see an expanded role in the Denver offense if Pat Bryant is out long term following his leg injury in Week 4. Sutton has been targeted on 16 percent of his pass routes this season; he has nine receptions through four games. Sutton should only be rostered in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 3-of-7 targets for 46 yards in the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton tied for the team lead in targets while pacing the offense in yards, which highlights the struggles that persist in Davis Webb’s offense through three games. He will be off the FLEX radar ahead of a Week 4 showdown against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 3-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Broncos’ Week 2 win against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton’s lone end zone target was intercepted on a poor throw from Bo Nix. Last week Sutton had just 11 yards on five targets in the Broncos’ season-opening loss to the Chiefs. Jaylen Waddle, with 148 yards in Week 2, has established himself as the clear-cut WR1 in the Denver offense. Sutton will be a touchdown-dependent WR3/4 option in Week 3 against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Bo Nix called the Broncos’ Week 1 offensive performance “pretty pitiful.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Nix during his postgame presser defended offensive play caller Davis Webb, who took over for head coach Sean Payton this offseason. “The players did not make it easy on [Webb] today,” said Nix, who completed 17-of-28 passes for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Monday night’s loss to Kansas City. “Pretty pitiful, actually.” Denver had the league’s second lowest drop back EPA of Week 1; only the Falcons were worse. Nix, meanwhile, ranked 28th out of 32 qualifying QBs in Week 1 accuracy. “We called exactly what we prepared for and what we wanted to get to and we just didn’t execute,” Nix said. “Then we were behind.” Webb and the Broncos will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a tough Jaguars defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-5 targets for 11 yards in the Broncos’ Week 1 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: The good news for Sutton’s fantasy managers is that he tied for second on the team in targets. The bad news is everything else. Sutton was locked down by the aggressive Kansas City secondary, failing to generate separation as the offense struggled to move the football. It is difficult to count on Sutton as being any higher than third on the team’s pecking order for targets following the addition of Jaylen Waddle this offseason. The veteran incumbent turns 31 in October and appears likely to struggle when he’s not finding the end zone. Sutton is a low-upside WR4 ahead of a pass-funnel matchup against the Jaguars in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: The Athletic’s Nick Kosmider reports that Broncos WR Courtland Sutton is “being limited as part of the team’s ‘protocols’ for the veteran wide receiver.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton did not practice at all over the past two days. He participated in a walkthrough and individual drills today, but sat out team drills. Broncos coach Sean Payton says he is not dealing with an injury, and Sutton said the protocol was set in place due to the fatigue that set in late last year. It sounds like this really is all part of a management plan for the 30-year-old veteran. He warrants FLEX treatment, entering his new role as the Broncos’ WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton said he would be willing to sacrifice targets and overall numbers “if it’s what the offense needs” this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: “I don’t think that we have any individuals or personalities in our offense that are saying, ‘Hey, I need this, I need that,’” Sutton told The Athletic’s Nick Kosmider. “I think we have a bunch of guys that are willing to put their pride aside and say, ‘What do I need to do for this team to be successful?’” Kosmider guesses that the Broncos won’t have two 1,000-yard receivers this year as they spread the ball around. Sutton is coming off the board around the WR35 mark, surrounded by rookies and other players with real usage or injury questions. This is a great quote for Broncos fans, but fantasy managers would probably prefer a squeakier wheel from Sutton. He may fade into the WR4 picture if the Broncos decide to feature new additional Jaylen Waddle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: The Denver Post’s Luca Evans said he saw “a lot of passes being caught over the middle” at the Broncos’ mandatory minicamp this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Broncos OC Davis Webb will add elements to Denver’s offense this season. Last year, the Broncos attempted the sixth-fewest (51) passes thrown 10-plus yards downfield and between the painted numbers. For reference, the league-leading Lions attempted 102 passes in this area of the field. Evans did not provide an average target depth in today’s report, but we are pleased to hear Webb is focusing on the middle of the field, regardless. Passes thrown in this area give the pass catcher more room to work, both before and after the catch, which helps them score fantasy points. Even a moderate increase in targets thrown to this area of the field would be great for QB Bo Nix and his pass catchers, like WR Jaylen Waddle and WR Courtland Sutton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey rushed six times for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks, adding 31 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The fact that the 31 yards through the air led the team in receiving is a comment on the state of an offense that gained only 168 yards of total offense against the defending Super Bowl Champions. Even so, a relentlessly aggressive defense willed the team to victory behind a consistently positive game script, which allowed J.K. Dobbins to handily lead the backfield in opportunities. Harvey remains a matchup-dependent fantasy option best utilized in trailing game environments, which is unlikely to be the case when the Broncos face the struggling Cardinals in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey picked up seven yards on three carries in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey was a non-factor in this one, and a week after his big receiving game, he was held without a catch with just one target. The second-year tailback was clearly the backup to JK Dobbins, and was unable to make the most of his limited opportunities. He’s off the radar for Week 6 versus the Seahawks on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: JK Dobbins had 11 rushes for 40 yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding two catches for 12 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Dobbins, as usual, led the Denver backfield in carries but lost out to RJ Harvey on pass routes and targets. In fact, Harvey led the Broncos with ten catches on ten targets in a check-down heavy game plan for Bo Nix and OC Davis Webb. Dobbins has been touchdown-reliant as the Broncos’ lead back, and sensitive to game script, as we saw in Week 4. Dobbins can be used as a flex next week against a vulnerable Chargers run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey had seven rushes for 25 yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding ten catches for 68 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Playing against a 49ers defense allowing the league’s highest target share to running backs, Harvey led the Broncos in targets and receptions — thanks in part to negative game script that forced Denver to go pass heavy in the second half. It was a nice little PPR cheat code outing for Harvey, who now has 20 receptions in three games this year. JK Dobbins, meanwhile, led the Denver backfield with 11 rushes in Week 4. Harvey could be a PPR flex play next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: J.K. Dobbins (hip) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: RJ Harvey was checked for a concussion in Week 3 and is not on the injury report today, meaning both backs are good to go for Week 4. Dobbins saw 17 carries versus the Rams compared to just two for Harvey, though the latter caught six passes. Dobbins caught one pass. The rushing advantage will keep Dobbins in the RB3 mix for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey rushed twice for six yards in the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams, adding 41 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey took an awkward tackle and appeared to stumble following the play. He was removed during the commercial break and taken to the locker room to be evaluated for a concussion. Harvey gained six yards on two carries prior to departing, adding 39 yards on five receptions, but would return for the fourth quarter to add two additional yards on one additional catch. Harvey continues to add value through the air but could struggle to return value better than RB3 in fantasy circles given the current struggles of the offense. He’ll be an RB3 against the 49ers in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey (hamstring) is not on Denver’s final Week 3 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: He’ll hold the receiving end of Denver’s RB tandem in Week 3 against the Broncos, giving him fringe RB2 status against a tough defense. We’d probably rather start Harvey than committee mate J.K. Dobbins this week with Jonah Coleman (ankle) out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos RB RJ Harvey (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey is on track to return in Week 3 against the Rams after sitting out the Broncos’ Week 2 game against the Jaguars. With RB Jonah Coleman (ankle) ailing, Harvey could take on a slightly larger-than-normal workload, though not enough to treat him as anything higher than a FLEX option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos RB RJ Harvey (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey strained his hamstring in Week 1 and logged two limited sessions in Week 2 practices before being declared inactive on game day. His continued limited practice participation puts him on track to backup starting RB J.K. Dobbins (hamstring), who is also rehabbing after experiencing cramps in Week 2. RB3 Jonah Coleman (ankle) is currently sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos RB J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Hamstring cramps forced Dobbins out of the Broncos’ Week 2 game against the Jaguars. Follow-up reports on the issue have been positive, and it sounds like he has a real chance to play in Week 3 against the Rams, potentially as the leader of a banged-up committee. Keep an eye on his practice participation this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed 17 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins found little room to run on a night the Broncos gained only 168 yards of total offense but handily led the backfield in opportunities in what was a consistently positive game script due to the dominance of their defense. Dobbins has now failed to eclipse a modest 50 yards on the ground in four of five appearances but might be useful as a bye week fill-in when the Broncos travel to Arizona to face the Cardinals in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins was the most effective offensive player for both teams, which isn’t quite the compliment you’d think it is. The 27-year-old was the bellcow for the Broncos, however, and he was able to keep the chains moving enough to give Denver the victory over the winless Chargers. Dobbins will likely find the sledding tougher in Week 6 when the Broncos face the Seahawks on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: JK Dobbins had 11 rushes for 40 yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding two catches for 12 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins, as usual, led the Denver backfield in carries but lost out to RJ Harvey on pass routes and targets. In fact, Harvey led the Broncos with ten catches on ten targets in a check-down heavy game plan for Bo Nix and OC Davis Webb. Dobbins has been touchdown-reliant as the Broncos’ lead back, and sensitive to game script, as we saw in Week 4. Dobbins can be used as a flex next week against a vulnerable Chargers run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins practiced in full this week, so he should be ready to handle his typical workload against the 49ers this week. The Broncos’ lead rusher has played very unproductively this season, failing to hit 7.0 PPR points each week. The Broncos’ defensive line has been hit hard by injuries. Perhaps Dobbins can steady himself in the RB2/FLEX ranks against them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins (hip) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: RJ Harvey was checked for a concussion in Week 3 and is not on the injury report today, meaning both backs are good to go for Week 4. Dobbins saw 17 carries versus the Rams compared to just two for Harvey, though the latter caught six passes. Dobbins caught one pass. The rushing advantage will keep Dobbins in the RB3 mix for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed 17 times for 49 yards in the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams, adding four yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins and the rest of the Denver offense have been subject to poor situational tendencies from first-time play caller Davis Webb’s offense through three weeks. Dobbins is the player arguably hit the hardest with poor play sequencing as the bulk of his work comes on early downs. Even so, Dobbins now has a higher share of the backfield opportunities following the placement of Jonah Coleman on IR Saturday. Dobbins is a shaky RB3 ahead of a Week 4 showdown with the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) is not on Denver’s final Week 3 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: He’ll form a committee with RJ Harvey, who was also cleared for Week 3, against the Rams. Dobbins is a low-end RB2 at best in this role against a tough Los Angeles defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: Broncos RB J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Hamstring cramps forced Dobbins to leave the Broncos’ Week 2 game against the Jaguars, but it appears as though his soft tissue is feeling better. A mid-week upgrade to full participation is a great sign for his Week 3 availability. He is an RB2 if active against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: Broncos RB J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Hamstring cramps forced Dobbins out of the Broncos’ Week 2 game against the Jaguars. Follow-up reports on the issue have been positive, and it sounds like he has a real chance to play in Week 3 against the Rams, potentially as the leader of a banged-up committee. Keep an eye on his practice participation this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jonah Coleman suffered a sprained ankle in Week 2 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: RJ Harvey missed Week 2 with a hamstring injury and J.K. Dobbins left the game early with what was eventually called leg cramps. It’s unclear if any of the three Denver backs will be available for Week 3. Dobbins appears most likely to suit up, though nothing is guaranteed. Tyler Badie could ultimately be the team’s starting running back on Sunday. He should be stashed in most fantasy leagues in case all three starting options ahead of him are ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 17-of-27 passes for 107 yards in the Broncos’ 17-14, Week 6 win over the Seahawks, adding two yards on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Broncos managed just 168 yards of total offense on a night their defense carried them to victory in overtime. Nine of the Broncos’ 11 possessions, excluding the two kneel downs to end each half, ended in punts on drives that lasted five plays or fewer. Two second quarter touchdown drives had the Broncos playing with a lead for much of the game but they were otherwise unable to move the football with any consistency. An overtime interception by nickel corner Ja’Quan McMillian allowed for a game-winning, 53-yard field goal from kicker Will Lutz after the Broncos again failed to gain a first down. The win sends Denver to 4-2 while averaging only 18.7 points per game through six weeks. The team gets a scheduling gift with the Cardinals on deck in Week 7, although Nix cannot be treated as a starter-worthy fantasy asset outside of the deepest leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 16-of-127 passes for 123 yards with a touchdown in the Broncos’ 23-17, Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix also added 10 yards on the ground on his four carries. He once again wasn’t able to get the ball downfield, with a long passing gain of 34 yards on a busted coverage. He was at least able to find Courtland Sutton for a short touchdown, but this was an ugly day for both signal-callers. Nix is no more than a QB2 for a matchup against the tough Seattle defense in Week 6, and it’s worth noting that game takes place Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 25-of-42 attempts for 214 yards and one touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding two rushes for ten yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix’s play — including missing easy intermediate throws in the first half — left Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb without answers, a common theme so far this season. His lone touchdown came on a garbage time score to Jaylen Waddle. Nix was in check-down mode throughout the game against the Niners, finishing with a 4.9 aDOT. He was 5 percent under his expected completion rate, targeting his running backs 12 times. Until Webb and Sean Payton figure out the offense, Nix will be a superflex-only fantasy option without much of a weekly ceiling. He gets the Chargers in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 17-of-34 passes for 186 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Broncos’ 30-26, Week 3 win over the Rams, adding seven yards and a touchdown on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Broncos were shut out in the first half amidst consistent struggles from Nix, who, for his part, turned in solid production in a third quarter that saw the Broncos knot the game at 16 through two touchdowns and successful two-point conversions. Nix and the Broncos would struggle to move the football again in the fourth quarter but a pick-six from safety Talanoa Hufanga gave them the lead with under five minutes to play. Stafford returned blows to send the Rams to a three-point lead before Nix’s game-winning score from one yard out. That final drive was aided by three key penalties to go against the Rams, the final of which was questionable, to put it kindly. Josh Wallace appeared to intercept Nix for the second time in the fourth quarter but a defensive pass interference penalty was called, giving the Broncos renewed life. Hufanga would intercept Stafford for a second time in the fourth quarter, this time in the end zone, to seal the victory for the Broncos as time expired. Nix and offensive coordinator Davis Webb have not looked good through three games despite the team’s 2-1 record, and will need to clean things up ahead of another NFC West showdown against the 49ers in Week 4. Nix is currently nothing more than a middling QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 22-of-31 attempts for 288 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Broncos’ Week 2 win against the Jaguars, adding five rushes for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was an uneven day for Nix, who missed some routine throws and threw a bad pick in the end zone while targeting Courtland Sutton. He targeted Jaylen Waddle heavily and connected with Waddle for a 49-yard gain in the first half, regularly attacking the Jaguars secondary downfield. After taking far too many sacks in Week 1 against the Chiefs, Nix was not sacked against a solid Jaguars pass rush on Sunday. Nix’s lack of early-season rushing success has dinged his fantasy prospects a bit. He’s a fine superflex option for Week 3 against the Rams, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix called the Broncos’ Week 1 offensive performance “pretty pitiful.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix during his postgame presser defended offensive play caller Davis Webb, who took over for head coach Sean Payton this offseason. “The players did not make it easy on [Webb] today,” said Nix, who completed 17-of-28 passes for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Monday night’s loss to Kansas City. “Pretty pitiful, actually.” Denver had the league’s second lowest drop back EPA of Week 1; only the Falcons were worse. Nix, meanwhile, ranked 28th out of 32 qualifying QBs in Week 1 accuracy. “We called exactly what we prepared for and what we wanted to get to and we just didn’t execute,” Nix said. “Then we were behind.” Webb and the Broncos will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a tough Jaguars defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 17-of-28 passes for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Broncos’ 31-10, Week 1 loss to the Chiefs, adding two yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix and the rest of the Denver offense struggled throughout against Steve Spagnuolo’s Kansas City defense, gaining fewer yards as a team (176) than opposing running back Kenneth Walker (191). Things seemed to be clicking early after the Broncos were able to knot the game at seven in the first quarter, but quickly fell apart under unrelenting pressure. The poor offensive showing is sure to draw criticism in the media considering it was the first game called by first-time offensive coordinator Davis Webb after head coach Sean Payton relinquished play calling duties this offseason. Whether that setup continues remains to be seen and we wouldn’t be shocked if Webb failed to make it through the first six weeks still calling plays. The Broncos hold the league’s most difficult schedule through the first six weeks, with games against Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks on the immediate horizon. Nix could regain form against the pass-funnel Jaguars in Week 2, where he will be a back-end QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos QB Bo Nix completed 6-of-9 passes for 76 yards and one touchdown in Friday’s preseason game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix looked mobile and eager to chuck it downfield. He even had a few overthrows, which we suppose is a good thing for a quarterback who spent the offseason rehabbing an ankle injury. The Broncos quarterback linked up with new WR Jaylen Waddle for a 35-yard gain down the seam and targeted WR Courtland Sutton a couple of times along the sideline. He found tonight’s starting RB RJ Harvey speeding down the right side of the field on a wheel route, and linked up with the second-year running back for a 21-yard touchdown to conclude the first drive. New OC Davis Webb regularly dialed up play action, which is great for fantasy purposes. Nix looks like a low-end QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos coach Sean Payton believes Bo Nix’s movement is “back to where it was” before his broken ankle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Payton said Nix’s health “looks really good.” Payton’s words come a week after Nix pledged to keep running this season despite his unfortunate injury. Considered something of a finished product upon being the No. 12 overall pick of the 2024 Draft, Nix took a decent sophomore step forward, and now has the best supporting cast of his career entering Year 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix has no plans to curtail his rushing despite last season’s broken ankle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: “Absolutely not,” was Nix’s response when asked if he planned to run less following his unfortunate Divisional Round injury. “I’m going to roll, and I’m going to be as athletic as I can be. Like the earlier question, it’s a strength of ours and we have to use our strengths. For me, that’s when I feel at my best and that’s when I feel free.” Nix went on for several more sentences. That’s about as clear as you could ever expect a player to be. Nix’s legs have been a big part of his low-end QB1 value and streamer success. Now with an enhanced supporting cast via the addition of Jaylen Waddle, the third-year starter could be set up for another “surprise” step forward in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 5-of-10 targets for 50 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp’s 10 targets finished second on the team behind alpha Jaxon Smith-Njigba but were largely a product of 51 Sam Darnold pass attempts in game that had all the ingredients for increased pass volume, including an inability to run the football, negative game script, and overtime. It continues to appear as if Kupp’s fantasy-relevant days are far behind him, with the veteran best left on the waiver wire ahead of a Week 7 showdown against the Chiefs on deck.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 4-of-5 targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp took advantage of the Commanders double-teaming Jaxon Smith-Njigba and walked into the end zone on the fourth touchdown throw from Sam Darnold. It’s his first score of the season, and it’s a season high in receiving yards for the former star. Kupp will try and build on this in Week 4 in a matchup against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp will be available for QB Sam Darnold (glute), who makes his return from his Week 1 injury. Kupp is a mild FLEX option, facing a soft Commanders’ coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp will not be fantasy-relevant in 12-team managed leagues this week, but he could be an option in single-game DFS tournaments. If QB Sam Darnold (glute) can play, he will appreciate having Kupp on the field with him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp also opened last week with a limited practice due to the back injury before getting in two full practices and playing in Week 2. His limited designation Wednesday is likely a continuation of veteran workload management for his back; fantasy managers should not be surprised to see the 33-year-old limited on Wednesdays this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp got involved on the Seahawks’ fifth and sixth drives, but was quiet outside of that. The 33-year-old wide receiver entered the game with a back injury, though he logged two full practice sessions, so it is unlikely to have meaningfully impacted him. He nabbed his second reception during the Seahawks’ two-minute drill at the end of the first half, but he was unable to get out of bounds, allowing precious seconds to tick away. Kupp is a WR5/FLEX against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) is not on the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp, 33, is good to go against the Cardinals. He was limited on Wednesday, but upgraded to full on Thursday and Friday. With QB Drew Lock under center, Kupp’s outlook is a little more volatile. He should be viewed as just a boom-bust FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) practiced in full on Thursday,
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: The 33-year-old wide receiver should play in Week 2 against the Cardinals, although he is just a boom-bust FLEX starter at this point. Kupp does not need to be in 12-team lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp popped up on the injury report with a back issue, though he was listed as a limited participant. The veteran 33-year-old may just be having his practice reps managed as he deals with a back ailment. Barring a change, Kupp is still trending to play Week 2 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 2-of-3 targets for 35 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 1 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp had one of the highlights of the night with a leaping, one-handed snag late in the third quarter. The 24-yard catch eventually resulted in a field goal and Seattle’s first points of the night. Kupp can still come up with the occasional clutch play, but his ability to earn targets is all but gone. With Drew Lock likely filling in for an injured Sam Darnold next week, Kupp is not on the fantasy radar ahead of Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 5-of-8 targets for 66 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos, adding two yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed’s eight targets were a product of 51 Sam Darnold pass attempts in a game the Seahawks could not find any room to run on the ground. He lost a fumble on a fluke play in the second quarter in which he rolled over the tackling defender, only for the defender’s knee to knock the football loose before Shaheed’s rear end touched the playing surface. he would fumble a punt return in the fourth quarter but easily had time to regain control before the ball was in real trouble. Shaheed remains the third option through the air for an offense typically not seeing this level of volume, making him a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option, for the time being. That doesn’t change ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Chiefs in Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 1-of-3 targets for 20 yards and rushed twice for 33 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 4 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: It wasn’t a ton of volume, but it was easily Shaheed’s biggest offensive day of the year. He took a pitch for a touchdown for his first score of 2026. He was once again not involved in the passing game, however, and he didn’t do much as a returner again, as well. Shaheed will be back in action — and should not be in lineups — against the 49ers in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Once again, Shaheed didn’t make an impact, with his biggest play being a drop that resulted in a first down because of a questionable personal foul after the play. The 28-year-old also hasn’t made an impact on special teams, and while his big-play ability is almost assuredly still there, fantasy managers can’t count on it right now. A chance to get going comes in Week 4 versus the Chargers at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 3-of-6 targets for 35 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals, adding one rush for four yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: The Seahawks tried to get Shaheed involved early on, but he largely made his presence felt on special teams, returning two kicks for 47 yards and three punts for 29 yards. Shaheed was unable to haul in his first target on the Seahawks’ second drive. He got open on a post route from the slot on the ensuing drive, and QB Drew Lock hit him for a 23-yard gain. He caught a four-yard pass in the flats immediately after that. Later, on the sixth drive, Lock fired a pass at Shaheed 34 yards downfield, but the coverage defender grazed the ball, altering the trajectory and leading to an incompletion that went off Shaheed’s fingertips. Shaheed also fumbled the second half’s opening kick return, but Seattle recovered it and advanced the ball 30 yards downfield. Shaheed remains a big-play-dependent FLEX against the Commanders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards in the Seahawks’ Week 1 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed caught multiple passes in 4-of-12 games as a Seahawk last year. He stayed the course in Week 1 with another single-catch outing. Shaheed simply can’t earn targets in an offense that revolves around getting Jaxon Smith-Njigba the ball at all levels. His versatility and elite skills on both punt and kick returns are valuable for the Seahawks in real life, but they don’t put fantasy points on the table. He is not on the FLEX menu headed into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: The Athletic’s Andrew Destin believes WR Rashid Shaheed “could very well usurp” WR Cooper Kupp as the No. 2 receiving option.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Destin echoes what ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler forecasted late in June. It’s nice to know that training camp performances have not altered expectations. Whether Shaheed can be more than a big-play-based FLEX option remains to be seen, but his ADP is hardly prohibitive. Stashing him on benches in Weeks 1-2 while monitoring his usage is a fairly low-risk move, though he is not a priority add.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said WR Tory Horton’s (undisclosed) “injury isn’t a long-term thing.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Frankly, it is tough to trust this statement. The Seahawks kept things quiet almost all offseason about Horton’s season-ending shin injury. They do not have to disclose anything until Week 1 practices begin. Were he to miss time in the regular season, WR Rashid Shaheed might be able to earn an extra target or two, operating as the team’s uncontested field stretcher.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: The News Tribune’s Gregg Bell reports that the Seahawks are ramping up WR Tory Horton (shin) after a successful offseason surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: The Seahawks shut Horton down after trading for WR Rashid Shaheed last year, citing a new shin injury. The trade came as a surprise. He and Shaheed possess similar skill sets, and Horton had already set two franchise records, so replacing him in the lineup due to poor play did not add up. Apparently, Horton played through discomfort in his shin for five games until the pain led to imaging, revealing a crack in his shin. Horton attempted to avoid surgery, but it was ultimately deemed necessary in February 2026, delaying his return. Bell adds that the coaching staff is “excited and curious to unleash” Horton and Shaheed in the same formations, “challenging the deep coverage of defenses.” Stressing the defense vertically should open up the short-to-intermediate areas of the field as well. Shaheed will likely be the more reliable boom-bust FLEX and could even ascend to WR3 status, but it is nice to know that the coaching staff still views Horton positively after the surprising in-season trade last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler believes Seahawks WR Rashid Shaheed “is going to be a big-time player” in 2026 after successfully taking on an expanded route tree this spring.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed reportedly had “major” performances throughout spring practices, hitting it off with QB Sam Darnold. Per Fowler, the Seahawks will continue to use WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba on PPR-friendly short and intermediate routes that helped him finish as the overall WR2 in total PPR scoring. But, rather than keeping Shaheed stuck in a field-stretching role, they plan to direct more short-to-intermediate stuff to Shaheed as well. Shaheed still has to go out and score more points this season, but this is the exact type of role change he needs to elevate above a frustratingly volatile fantasy profile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks team reporter John Boyle reports that the team is expecting more from WR Rashid Shaheed “when it comes to his role in the offense.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Good. Many of us expected Shaheed to hit the ground running after the Seahawks traded for him last season, reuniting him with former OC Klint Kubiak. He posted an 18/266/0 receiving line from Weeks 10 through Super Bowl LX, yet the Seahawks re-signed him to a three-year, $51 million contract this offseason. The Athletic’s Michael-Shawn Dugar said he believes Shaheed’s deal “suggests a demotion” for WR Cooper Kupp. Shaheed possesses big-play ability. Putting him in the WR2 role is logical. It will be interesting to see how the team splits up reps between the two of them in training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12-of-16 targets for 134 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba overcame a sluggish first half to extend his stranglehold on the overall WR1 in fantasy circles with a dominant second half and overtime period. While the 51 pass attempts from Sam Darnold were highly uncharacteristic of this Seattle offense, a complete inability to run the football paired with a negative script to form the perfect environment for Smith-Njigba to set a season high in targets and receptions. Smith-Njigba has now gone over 100 yards in five of six appearances to start the 2026 regular season and is in a good spot to continue that dominance when the Seahawks host the Chiefs in Week 7, where he remains a top-tier WR1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) has no injury designation ahead of the Seahawks’ Week 6 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba played through an ankle injury in Week 5 and was limited in practice this week before getting a full designation on Wednesday. Despite the short week ahead of a Thursday matchup against the Broncos, he is off the injury report and good to go. Smith-Njigba is once again a top-three wide receiver option for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was listed as a limited practice participant on Tuesday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba gets a second-straight “limited” practice designation. The Seahawks have technically not practiced yet this week but it is notably the 24-year-old receiver gets back-to-back limited designations. With a Thursday matchup against the Broncos on the horizon for Week 6, the Seahawks are leaving the door open for Smith-Njigba to play; he battled the ankle injury in Week 5 and the short week makes this a tougher evaluation. For now, we still expect Smith-Njigba to play against the Broncos on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Seahawks listed Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: With the Seahawks preparing to face the Broncos on a short week, it would be a bit more concerning if JSN were listed as a DNP. The team listing him as limited on the first day of the week is encouraging after he clearly battled through an ankle injury in Week 5’s loss to the 49ers. Smith-Njigba still topped 100 receiving yards for the fourth time this season and made several big plays despite being in visible pain. We’ll continue to update his practice status throughout the week, but as long as he’s active come Thursday, JSN should be in your fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 5-of-8 targets for 102 yards and one touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers, adding one rush for 16 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: JSN appeared to be playing through a bit of an ankle injury in this one, but he looked perfectly fine when he turned what would have been a short two-yard reception upfield for a 16-yard touchdown in the third quarter. In the fourth quarter, as the Seahawks were attempting a comeback, JSN hauled in a 35-yard reception, evading multiple defenders to get the Seahawks to the 50-yard line. A few plays later, he would drop a wide-open pass that may have set the Seahawks up for a game-winning field goal opportunity, but JSN did his part to keep the Seahawks in what proved to be a sloppy game for the offense as a whole. He’s gone for 100-plus yards in four of his first five games of the season and will look for his fifth 100-yard game on Thursday night when the Seahawks visit the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 5-of-6 targets for 78 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 4 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: For the first time this year, Smith-Njigba was held out of the end zone. It was a quiet day fore the star wideout, but if 78 yards is your worst day (so far), well, you’ve had a pretty good season. JSN and fantasy managers will hope for a return to the end zone and a little more volume against the 49ers in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 10-of-14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns in the Seahawks’ Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Goodness gracious. Smith-Njigba did have a drop, but it was yet another dominant effort for the 24-year-old. His first touchdown saw him fake a fade route only to comeback to the pylon for an easy six, and then he and Sam Darnold connected for a second time on a pass over the middle in the end zone. That’s already six touchdowns in three games for the 24-year-old, and he’s reached the century mark in all three contests. On top of that, he also completed a 14-yard pass. Asking for this kind of red-zone production every week is tough, but he’s more than capable of these kind of fireworks. Obviously. JSN will be a WR1 and then some for Week 4 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9-of-11 targets for 155 yards and three touchdowns in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: On the Seahawks’ second play from scrimmage, a Cardinals safety somehow failed to pick up Smith-Njigba, streaking down the right sideline, after he snuck right past CB Will Johnson. Seahawks QB Drew Lock noticed and fired a perfect pass to Smith-Njigba in stride, leading to the Seahawks’ wide receiver’s longest career gain. The rest of the day played out similarly, with Smith-Njigba routing up defenders right and left. He scored again on the Seahawks’ seventh drive, leaping past a diving cornerback to make the catch in the end zone. Lock linked up with him again for a third score in the back of the end zone, threading the ball past a linebacker in the end zone as Smith-Njigba broke left on a crosser, dusting Cardinals S Budda Baker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 8-of-11 targets for 122 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 1 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Sam Darnold went down with a hip injury on the first drive of the night. It took Drew Lock a couple of drives to dial in on JSN, but it was business as usual once he did. No Seahawk saw more than three targets aside from Smith-Njigba. He finished the night with a monstrous 41.7 percent target share. His highlight of the night wa sa 45-yard catch-and-run for Seattle’s only touchdown of the game. Even if Darnold misses time, JSN’s role is so fantasy-friendly that he will remain well inside the WR1 ranks for his Week 2 date with the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler believes Seahawks WR Rashid Shaheed “is going to be a big-time player” in 2026 after successfully taking on an expanded route tree this spring.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Shaheed reportedly had “major” performances throughout spring practices, hitting it off with QB Sam Darnold. Per Fowler, the Seahawks will continue to use WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba on PPR-friendly short and intermediate routes that helped him finish as the overall WR2 in total PPR scoring. But, rather than keeping Shaheed stuck in a field-stretching role, they plan to direct more short-to-intermediate stuff to Shaheed as well. Shaheed still has to go out and score more points this season, but this is the exact type of role change he needs to elevate above a frustratingly volatile fantasy profile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: George Holani rushed five times for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani split primary change of pace duties with recent practice squad call-up Velus Jones Jr, the latter of whom turned four carries into 20 yards while losing one yard on his lone reception. Both backs appear unlikely to return fantasy value as Zach Charbonnet nears a return from injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: George Holani rushed four times for seven yards in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers, adding four receptions for 24 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani put the ball on the turf twice in this one, but it was his fumble with 13 seconds left in the first half that proved to be one of the more costly mistakes of the game. With the Seahawks simply looking to get to halftime, Holani took a handoff from Sam Darnold for what should have been the final play of regulation. Instead, the third-year back had the ball knocked out and into his own end zone, which resulted in a Niners touchdown after it was recovered by DT Gracen Halton for the score. Holani hasn’t emerged as the late-round value fantasy managers hoped for this offseason and is fully off the fantasy radar for Week 6 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: George Holani is active for Week 5 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani is good to go for Sunday’s game after entering the weekend as questionable. Holani rushed seven times for 18 scoreless yards last week and shouldn’t be relied on in any fantasy format this week. While Holani is active, the Seahawks declared QB Jalen Milroe, RB Robert Henry Jr., LB Chazz Surratt, WR Montorie Foster Jr., and TE Nick Kallerup inactive for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks RB George Holani (ribs/knee) is questionable to play in Week 5 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani was nursing a ribs injury on Wednesday and Thursday, but he is now listed with a knee injury as well. This is concerning. He clearly picked up a new injury during the practice week. Velus Jones is the current RB3. Jones is not viable as a FLEX starter if Holani sits, but Emanuel Wilson should take on an RB2-worthy workload regardless.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks RB George Holani (ribs) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani should be good to go for the Seahawks’ Week 5 game against the 49ers, but he is certainly working through a decent little injury. The trusted passing game specialist should handle his normal workload, although he is only a touchdown-dependent PPR FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks RB George Holani (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Holani was listed as a limited practice participant due to a rib injury on Wednesday. The 26-year-old operated as a passing-down backup to Emanuel Wilson in Week 4 with Jadarian Price out. Unless he misses practice later this week, he is still on track to play in Week 5, though Holani does not have a large enough role to achieve fantasy relevance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: George Holani rushed seven times for 18 yards in the Seahawks Week 4 win over the Chargers, adding one reception for two additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: In the first week without Jadarian Price, Holani operated as a lightly used backup behind Emanuel Wilson, who rushed for 21-81-1, and added another 3-39-1 through the air on four targets. Any hope that Holani could see an increased workload sans Price needs to be put on hold for now. He can be left on fantasy benches in Week 5 when the Seahawks host the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Emanuel Wilson rushed 21 times for 81 yards and a touchdown while adding three catches for 39 yards and a score in the Seahawks’ Week 4 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Wilson picked up his first score on a screen pass from San Darnold. His second touchdown came on an untouched stroll from eight yards out. Wilson doesn’t have anything close to elite burst, but he’s tough to bring down and has good-enough vision to take advantage of the holes he receives. He was clearly the bellcow as George Holani received just seven carries for 18 yards and only one catch in the contest. He’ll be a RB2 for Week 5 against the Broncos and as long as Zack Charbonnet/Jadarian Price remain out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks rule out Jadarian Price (chest) for Week 4 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Price reportedly aggravated his chest injury on Wednesday. That is unfortunate. With Price out of the picture against the Chargers, and Zach Charbonnet (knee) still rehabbing, burly RB Emanuel Wilson and receiving specialist RB George Holani will split backfield reps. Wilson can be started as a volume-based RB2/FLEX while Holani is FLEX-viable in PPR formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks designated Zach Charbonnet (knee) to return from the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Charbonnet will return to practice this week. The team now has 21 days to officially activate him from the injured reserve. It’s unclear how much of that window they will use to get him up to full speed. He has to miss at least one more game while on the PUP list. Charbonnet tore his ACL in Seattle’s first playoff game last year. The team talked about his quick recovery throughout the offseason and that will be the case, even if he uses all three weeks of his practice window. Once he returns, Charbonnet will at least take over the roles of George Holani and Emanuel Wilson, who have been splitting the backfield with Jadarian Price so far. He could even work himself into the starting job if Price continues to struggle with fumbles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Emanuel Wilson rushed 14 times for 52 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: Wilson is now down to just 3.4 yards per carry while filling in for numerous key injuries in the Seattle backfield, with the team clearly waiting with bated breath for the return of Zach Charbonnet. Charbonnet continues to inch closer to a return from injured reserve and appears likely to bring an end to the Wilson experiment, relegating the latter to bench fodder in fantasy circles in the process. That could come a early a Week 7 when the Seahawks host the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Emanuel Wilson rushed 20 times for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers, adding two receptions for 11 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: Wilson again led the Seahawks in rushing sans Jadarian Price. He handled all but four of the team’s running back carries in this one and found the end zone on a two-yard plunge in the first quarter to tie the game at 7-7. Wilson coughed up a key fumble in the second quarter that gave the Niners the ball on Seattle’s 11-yard line. On the following play, the Seahawks would allow an 11-yard touchdown run to Christian McCaffrey to put the Niners back out in front. Assuming Zach Charbonnet (Achilles) is at least one more game away from returning, Wilson will be on the RB2 radar in Week 6 when the Seahawks take on the Broncos on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Seahawks RB George Holani (ribs/knee) is questionable to play in Week 5 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: Holani was nursing a ribs injury on Wednesday and Thursday, but he is now listed with a knee injury as well. This is concerning. He clearly picked up a new injury during the practice week. Velus Jones is the current RB3. Jones is not viable as a FLEX starter if Holani sits, but Emanuel Wilson should take on an RB2-worthy workload regardless.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.headline: Emanuel Wilson rushed 21 times for 81 yards and a touchdown while adding three catches for 39 yards and a score in the Seahawks’ Week 4 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emanuel-wi.analysis: Wilson picked up his first score on a screen pass from San Darnold. His second touchdown came on an untouched stroll from eight yards out. Wilson doesn’t have anything close to elite burst, but he’s tough to bring down and has good-enough vision to take advantage of the holes he receives. He was clearly the bellcow as George Holani received just seven carries for 18 yards and only one catch in the contest.
