Schefter confirmed that the NFL is still discussing potential discipline for Nacua and Rams LT Alaric Jackson. This probably isn’t something to be overly concerned about in fantasy drafts — we suspect any suspension for Nacua would be short-term — but Schefter believes it’s possible that Nacua is suspended for the Rams opener against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-jackson.headline: Rams OT Alaric Jackson was absent from training camp practice Wednesday due to treatment for blood clots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-jackson.analysis: Jackson has been dealing with this blood clot condition for the past year and Rams head coach Sean McVay said Jackson was absent Wednesday as he deals with the treatment for the condition. It doesn’t seem to be a major injury issue for now, but certainly one worth keeping an eye on. Jackson has also been dealing with off-the-field issues stemming this offseason but his practice absence seemed to be only related to his blood clot treatment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-jackson.headline: Rams OT Alaric Jackson will not face criminal charges after being arrested in June on suspicion of domestic violence.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-jackson.analysis: Prosecutors told The Athletic that Jackson will not be facing criminal charges as a result of a domestic violence arrest in June. The 28-year-old was arrested on a felony domestic battery charge after police responded to a call to his home. However, charges are not being filed against him. Jackson has started 45 regular-season games for the Rams over the last three seasons and was also facing legal issues after he was sued in November 2025 by “a woman who accused him of recording sexual acts with her without her consent.” This case is headed for pre-filing diversion, which may constitute a violation of the league’s Personal Conduct Policy and still lead to a suspension, pending league review.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-jackson.headline: Rams OT Alaric Jackson was arrested Monday on a felony domestic violence charge.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-jackson.analysis: The charge against Jackson, 27, who has been with the Rams since entering the NFL in 2021, was for “a person who willfully inflicts corporal injury,” according to the LAPD. Jackson, who has played in 45 regular season games for the Rams over the past three seasons, has a history of off-the-field issues, including a 2024 suspension for violating the NFL’s personal conduct policy. Jackson last November was sued “by a woman who alleged he recorded her without her consent during sex, repeatedly refused to delete the video and taunted her with it,” according to ESPN. Jackson is one of several Rams players facing legal issues this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-jackson.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said Alaric Jackson returned to practice on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-jackson.analysis: Jackson was diagnosed with blood clots in June, but has been trending toward being ready for Week 1. The fact that he was able to suit up for a Monday practice suggests he’s still trending in the right direction, and the team said the plan will be to start him in Week 1 against the Texans if all goes well this week. Jackson earned a PFF pass blocking grade of 79.5 last season, allowing just three sacks and 22 pressures on 502 dropbacks. If he is unable to start, D.J. Humphries looks like the most likely candidate to step up in Jackson’s absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-jackson.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said OT Alaric Jackson will progress to team drills next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-jackson.analysis: Jackson has been a massive question mark for the Rams this offseason after developing blood clots in June but avoided the PUP and NFI lists last month. The most recent update indicates he could be ready for the start of the regular season, which would be a significant boost to the protection of reeling veteran quarterback Matthew Stafford. Stafford has been dealing with back issues all offseason with the team recently stating the intent is to “keep him upright” in Week 1 against the Texans. Jackson could go a long way in accomplishing that goal. It’ll still be a “wait and see” approach with Jackson but he currently appears to be trending in the right direction.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-jackson.headline: The Athletic’s Jourdan Rodrigue reports that the Rams “aren’t worried” about Matthew Stafford’s (back) status for the coming season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-jackson.analysis: Due to Stafford’s lengthy injury history, the Rams had already “planned to put Stafford on a modified workout plan in training camp before the back issue popped up.” On the plus side, it sounds as if the Rams were prepared to occasionally run the offense sans Stafford in training camp. Stafford is also reportedly on schedule, following a plan that had been previously agreed upon by the Rams, Stafford and spine specialist Dr. Robert Watkins. Rodrigue does, however, note that the Rams’ starting left tackle Alaric Jackson (blood clots) and right guard Kevin Dotson (chest contusion) remain sidelined. Both Jackson’s and Dotson’s statuses are worth following. If Stafford’s Saturday workout goes well, he should resume practicing on Monday next week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Patriots place Mack Hollins on injured reserve with a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: The Patriots snuck Hollins onto the injured reserve list over the weekend. He will be eligible to return after sitting out for four games. The Patriots also placed FB Reggie Gilliam on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) will not play in New England’s Week 5 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: It sounds like Efton Chism, Kyle Williams, and Demario Douglas will all work more than usual next to Romeo Doubs in Week 5. Chism might be the most interesting FLEX play of the three after putting up 2/42/1 in relief of Hollins against the Patriots, though all of them have cases.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Normally a wind-sprinter and a blocking specialist, Hollins became shockingly important at work after A.J. Brown went on IR with an ankle injury. He currently leads the team in targets, tied with Romeo Doubs at 20 apiece. Hollins holds the lead outright in catches (15) and yards (209). His absence would free up downfield opportunities for Kyle Williams. Efton Chism and Demario Douglas would likely see an uptick in routes as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins injured his calf in Week 4 and was listed as questionable to return. He immediately went to the locker room and did not return. Hollins is unlikely to play in Week 5. Romeo Doubs finally broke out last week with six catches for 58 yards and two scores. He will be in line for another sizable role once Hollins is ruled out. Kyle Williams will take on a starting role, though he is only worth a stash in deeper fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Speaking Monday, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel did not have an update on Mack Hollins’ calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Vrabel said he’ll have more information on Hollins shortly, but added that Hollins may miss a few days of practice. Hollins exited Week 4’s game against the Bills with a non-contact injury, leaving the field with a 3-53-0 line on four targerts. Hollins has seen 13 targets over the last two weeks while running the third-most routes (45) of any receiver. We’ll likely know more about the severity of his injury soon, but he could be at risk of missing Week 5’s game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins is questionable to return with a calf injury
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins went down when he cut to the sideline on an out route. He had to hobble off the field and was immediately taken into the locker room. The Patriots have not ruled him out yet, but we’d be surprised if he returned today. Romeo Doubs should continue to see the vast majority of targets. Hollins had 53 yards receiving on 3-of-4 targets before getting hurt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins caught 6-of-9 targets for 87 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins looked the part of Drake Maye’s top option against Jacksonville, dominating air yards and easily leading all pass catchers in targets. Hollins manhandled much smaller Jaguars defensive backs throughout the game and nearly came down with a long play that would have put him over 100 yards on the day. Hollins, who had just two grabs last week against the Steelers, could have some flex viability in Week 4 against the Bills, especially if Maye and the Pats are once again chasing points in the second half.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss 6-8 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Schefter and other reporters previously called it a 4-6 week injury, which now seems unlikely. Schefter did add that Brown is moving “pretty well” and could come back on the faster side of his updated timeline. Still, it looks like Brown will miss at least half of the regular season. Romeo Doubs will operate as the team’s No. 1 receiver until he returns, though it will likely be a group effort to replace Browns’ production. Mack Hollins and Demario Douglas will also be more involved.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins caught 2-of-2 targets for 18 yards in the Patriots’ Week 2 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins quietly led Patriots wide receivers in snaps in the first game without A.J. Brown. He saw just two targets on the day, catching both for a total of 18 yards in a subpar offensive day. The Pats pass-catchers are a mix of low-ceiling fantasy viability as Maye spreads the wealth around the different receivers. Better offensive days are ahead for the Patriots but Hollins is a WR5 play at best for Week 3 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports A.J. Brown won’t require surgery on his injured ankle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Schefter added Brown will miss four to six weeks with the high ankle sprain he sustained on Wednesday night against the Seahawks. It could be much longer than that before Brown is back to full health and operating as the Patriots’ alpha WR1. For now, Mack Hollins will slide into three-receiver sets and Romeo Doubs — who didn’t catch any of his three targets against Seattle — will likely function as Drake Maye’s top option. Demario Douglas could be an interesting add in deeper formats after leading the team with seven targets in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) will be out for the Seahawks’ Week 6 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet was already expected to miss Week 6, so no surprise here. The Seahawks also ruled out LB Drake Thomas and LB Chazz Surratt. There are no other players with injury designations heading into Seattle’s Thursday showdown against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Zach Charbonnet (knee) has a “legitimate chance” to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet’s return from ACL surgery has been going well. He is currently practicing with his teammates, though the quick turnaround time for this week’s Thursday Night Football game against the Broncos is too short for Charbonnet to properly ramp up. The Seahawks need a reliable player in the backfield and Charbonnet has coach Mike Macdonald’s trust. He will likely get all he can handle whenever he retakes the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said he does not plan to play Zach Charbonnet (knee) in Week 6 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: The Seahawks face the Broncos in Week 6’s Thursday Night Football game. Late last week, Macdonald acknowledged that the short turnaround time would make it difficult to ramp up Charbonnet as planned. The Seahawks are set to scale back the intensity at practice this week, which runs counter to the rehab plan. The Seahawks face the Chiefs in Week 7’s Sunday Night Football game. That seems like a plausible return date at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Seattle’s Week 6 Thursday Night Football game against the Broncos makes Zach Charbonnet’s (knee) ramp-up “tricky.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet is on schedule in his rehab program and “will be ready to ramp up his work next week.” Unfortunately, the Seahawks will have scaled-down practices as they prepare for their Thursday Night Football game. It sounds like Charbonnet is close to returning, but team doctors might want to see how his knee responds to a full week or practicing before clearing him. A condensed practice week indeed makes that tricky. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks ruled out Zach Charbonnet (knee) for Week 5 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: We do not yet know Charbonnet’s Friday participation level, but he remained limited for the first two practices. The Seahawks are smartly bringing him along slowly despite mounting injuries at the position. He should be stashed in 12-team leagues, and could return to a sizable workload when healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks RB Zach Charbonnet (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet is starting to ramp up to a return from his torn ACL last season. The Seahawks opened up his practice window and he was limited on Wednesday. He is already ruled out for Week 5, but a Week 6 return is not out of the picture just yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Zach Charbonnet (knee) won’t play in Seattle’s Week 5 game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet’s practice window was opened this past week, and based on Macdonald saying this, it sounds like he’ll be using most of the 21-day window to practice before his return. Macdonald did say that Charbonnet will start receiving team reps in practice this week, perhaps opening a door for a Week 6 return. Emanuel Wilson will head the committee in Seattle until Charbonnet’s return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said the team is making sure Zach Charbonnet (knee) “feels great when the time comes for him to come back.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: The Seahawks opened Charbonnet’s practice window on Thursday, but he is not yet ready to return. Charbonnet’s left quad is noticeably thinner than his right quad, and Macdonald explained that there is “a process to get him physically and mentally ready to go.” That said, Macdonald also said the veteran running back “looks fantastic.” Stash him now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet is not guaranteed to play in Week 4 against the Chargers, but his return to practice is promising. Add him now. Seahawks rookie, Jadarian Price (chest), went from a limited session on Wednesday to sitting out on Thursday. Keep a close eye on this. Backup Emanuel Wilson would get the start if both Charbonnet and Price are sidelined, while George Holani handles passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks designated Zach Charbonnet (knee) to return from the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet will return to practice this week. The team now has 21 days to officially activate him from the injured reserve. It’s unclear how much of that window they will use to get him up to full speed. He has to miss at least one more game while on the PUP list. Charbonnet tore his ACL in Seattle’s first playoff game last year. The team talked about his quick recovery throughout the offseason and that will be the case, even if he uses all three weeks of his practice window. Once he returns, Charbonnet will at least take over the roles of George Holani and Emanuel Wilson, who have been splitting the backfield with Jadarian Price so far. He could even work himself into the starting job if Price continues to struggle with fumbles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.headline: Jonathan Greenard (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.analysis: Greenard missed Week 5 after he failed to practice due to an ankle injury last week. He is back at practice to open this week, getting in a limited session on Wednesday. Greenard has a chance to return for the Eagles’ Week 6 game against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.headline: Eagles declared EDGE Jonathan Greenard, WR Hollywood Brown, WR DeVonta Smith, RB Saquon Barkley, S Marcus Epps, and C Crew Kendall inactive for Week 5 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.analysis: Greenard was the only Eagle with a questionable tag headed into the weekend. The rest of their important players had already been ruled out. Greenard didn’t practice at all this week because of an ankle injury and could miss more time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.headline: Eagles EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle) is questionable for Philadelphia’s Week 5 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.analysis: He did not practice at any point this week, so it would be a little surprising if he gave it a go. At the very least, we have to imagine he’s on the pessimistic side of questionable. The Eagles also ruled out S Marcus Epps with a groin injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.headline: Eagles LB Zack Baun (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.analysis: This is Baun’s second limited practice this week. Fellow LB Jihaad Campbell (knee) resumed practicing in a limited capacity, but EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle) and S Marcus Epps (groin) remain sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.headline: Jonathan Greenard (ankle) was not seen at Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.analysis: Greenard is reportedly considered day-to-day after suffering an ankle injury in Week 4. A DNP would put him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5. Safety Marcus Epps was also absent from practice. He suffered a groin injury in practice last week and did not suit up on Sunday. He will likely miss this week’s contest as wel.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Eagles EDGE Jonathan Greenard is considered day-to-day with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.analysis: Greenard was downgraded from questionable return to doubtful during last week’s loss to the Rams, but it sounds like he’ll have a chance to suit up in Week 5 against the Jaguars if he’s able to log a few days of practice this week. Greenard missed the first two games of this season due to an oblique injury and has totaled just one tackle on the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.headline: Eagles EDGE Jonathan Greenard suffered an ankle in Philadelphia’s Week 4 game against the Rams and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.analysis: He was initially questionable before being downgraded to out. Free agent addition Greenard just made his Eagles debut in Week 3 after missing Weeks 1 and 2 with an oblique issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.headline: Eagles EDGE Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) is out for Week 2 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.analysis: Greenard will miss his second straight game to start his first season in Philadelphia. He managed a week of limited sessions, seemingly indicating he is inching closer to being available after being acquired this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.headline: Eagles DT Jalen Carter (wrist) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.analysis: Eagles CB Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) and OLB Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) joined Carter for a limited session. Eagles S Andrew Mukuba (knee) did not practice. Fortunately, the Eagles have a winnable game against the Titans this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.headline: Eagles EDGE Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-g.analysis: Greenard missed Week 1 against the Commanders after practicing in a limited fashion all of last week. He opens this week as a limited participant again, with room to ramp up throughout the week before the Eagles’ Week 2 matchup with the Titans. Greenard may need a full practice before he officially returns to playing in games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb (quad) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb played through a quad bruise last week but exacerbated the issue and left the game late in the fourth quarter. The injury is not believed to be serious and a full practice today means Lamb isn’t at risk of missing Week 6. Despite burning fantasy managers with two catches for nine yards last time around, Lamb remains one of the best fantasy football wideouts in play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports CeeDee Lamb’s quad injury is not believed to be serious after Week 5’s loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb was on the field for a few more plays in Thursday’s loss to the Buccaneers after his injury was announced. Rapoport reports that Lamb is believed to be dealing with a quad bruise, which is not believed to be serious. Lamb and the Cowboys now have over a week to rest up before facing the Packers on Sunday Night Football in Week 6. Barring an unexpected development, we would expect Lamb to be good to go for next week’s game against the Packers at Lambeau Field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb (quad) is questionable to return to Week 5 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb departed in the fourth quarter with a quad injury. He tried to return but managed one snap before making his way back to the sideline, coming back on the field later in the drive for a two-point attempt. He was shown on the sideline in visible discomfort following the additional two snaps. Lamb managed to catch just 2-of-5 targets for nine yards prior to departing. Fantasy managers will want to track his status in the coming week, although the additional recovery time could allow him to avoid any missed games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 17-of-21 targets for 189 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ Week 3 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: He simply could not be stopped the way the Texans were playing defense. Lamb feasted on the sideline and against zone coverages — his longest catch went just 30 yards — and he had the go-ahead touchdown with less than 30 seconds left that had FOX’s Greg Olsen wondering why any defense would play him that way when he’d been that productive over the course of the game. He’d never managed more than 17 targets in a game before today. Obviously he won’t do this again, but Lamb has delivered for those who lucked into him in the late first-round mix and will again be a plug-and-play alpha WR1 against the Bucs on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-8 targets for 112 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 3 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: That makes it back-to-back games of 100-plus yards for Lamb. Lamb didn’t officially find the end zone on this one, but he did come up with a catch on a two-point reception in the third quarter to cut the Ravens’ lead to 24-21. He came up with a few big plays in the fourth quarter, with his biggest being a 49-yard reception on a drive that ended with a KaVontae Turpin rushing touchdown to briefly give the Cowboys the lead. Despite being out-targeted 11 to 8 by George Pickens in this one, Lamb has looked like the unquestioned WR1 for the Cowboys through the first three weeks. He’s totaled 15 receptions for 265 yards and two touchdowns over the last two weeks and is a high-end WR1 in next week’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 8-of-9 targets for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 2 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb caught three passes on the Cowboys’ opening drive, picking up gains of 15 and 23 yards before connecting with Dak Prescott on a three-yard score. Lamb gave the Commanders fits all day, but strung together another massive drive late in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 35-yard pass from Prescott, who went right back to him five plays later for a 24-yard touchdown on a pass Lamb had to fight to come down with. Lamb has now scored in each of his first two games this season and will be firmly on the WR1 radar in next week’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 5-of-8 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 1 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Although he lead the team in both targets and receiving, Lamb got off to a slow start while committing an early drop. He would score from one yard out in the second quarter after a Javonte Williams touchdown was ruled short of the goal line and also draw a defensive pass interference penalty in the second half that would lead to a Williams score, but the Cowboys simply had problems creating the chunk plays that ruled the roost in 2025. Better days are likely ahead for the perennial WR1, which starts in a Week 2 home showdown against another divisional opponent in the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: ESPN’s Ben Solak believes Dak Prescott could throw for 5,000 yards in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Solak’s prediction was among his bold predictions for the 2026 NFL season. Prescott having a shot at 5,000 yards, Solak said, would hinge on the Cowboys remaining a fast-paced offense in 2026. Last season the Cowboys led the league in play clock remaining at the snap and offensive plays per game, leading to 600 passes for Dak — a career high. The wideout duo of George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb won’t hurt matters for Prescott, who has eclipsed 4,500 passing yards three times in his NFL career. Pickens’ downfield ability was reflected in Prescott finishing sixth in deep ball accuracy last season. “The volume will be there for Prescott to not just lead the league in passing in 2026 but to once again challenge for the 5,000-yard milestone,” Solak said. Quarterbacks have thrown for more than 5,000 yards just 14 times in league history.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: Cowboys will restructure contracts of QB Dak Prescott, WR CeeDee Lamb and OG Tyler Smith, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Restructuring the contracts of Prescott, Lamb and Smith will create $66 million in cap space. Schefter also passes along that Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said the Cowboys will rework the contracts of DTs Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams and Osa Odighizuwa, who are scheduled to count around $63 million against the cap. With the new cap set at $301.2 million, the Cowboys had negative-$56.1 million in cap space. These moves help Dallas become compliant and have money to work with this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught his only target for four yards in the Cowboys’ Week 18 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb started this game and wasn’t officially removed until the beginning of the second half, but he wasn’t much of a factor here as the Cowboys had nothing to play for. The 26-year-old will end the season with 75 catches on 117 targets for 1,077 yards and three touchdowns in 14 games. This is the fewest receiving yards Lamb has had since his rookie year and the fewest touchdowns he’s ever had in an NFL season. That’s a bit shocking considering that Dak Prescott is in a battle to lead the NFL in passing yards. Obviously, some of that is the three games Lamb missed due to injuries, but playing alongside a legitimate second wide receiver in red zone weapon George Pickens was also a factor. Pickens is set to enter free agency, so the Cowboys will need to decide if they want to, or can, pay to bring him back. If not, Lamb may go right back to being a threat for 1,500 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: A full practice today means Jones will play through the issue in Week 6, but it’s never a good sign to see a starting quarterback unexpectedly pop up on the injury report. Jones has also struggled mightily this year, so the last thing he needs is a lingering ankle issue, even if it’s a minor one. Needless to say, we aren’t itching to get Jones in our fantasy lineups in a low-scoring affair with the Titans. He is buried at the back of the QB2 ranks for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 24-of-44 passes for 267 yards in the Colts’ 34-22, Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: The 267 yards aren’t a terrible total for Jones, but the Colts’ offense was not effective for most of the game. They were stuffed inside the Steelers’ three-yard line at least four times during the game, and the only touchdown they scored was on a one-yard sneak to tight end Tyler Warren. Even on that play, Warren was stuffed short of the end zone and had to be pushed in from behind. Jones was unable to connect with any receivers down the field and overthrew a few deep shots on the day. The Steelers spent a lot of energy trying to corral Jonathan Taylor, and you’d assume other defenses will deploy the same strategy, which means Jones is going to need to start to make them pay. Things should get easier next week against the winless Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 19-of-34 passes for 143 yards and an interception in the Colts’ 30-13, Week 4 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones was disastrously inaccurate in the first half, making even routine catches absurdly difficult for his banged-up receiver room. He also began the game by losing the football after his left tackle was pushed into him, resulting in a fumble. He eventually got the grain on the tracks with back-to-back scoring drives to close the first half. Daniels settled in after the break, though the Colts mostly leaned on Jonathan Taylor, who scored twice, to salt away the game. Jones is averaging a dismal 188.5 yards per game with just three scores to his name. He is barely in the QB2 mix for Indy’s Week 5 game versus the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 24-of-36 passes for 235 yards, one touchdown and one interception in Indianapolis’ 19-17, Week 3 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: He added three fumbles, two of which were recovered by the Texans on Will Anderson Jr. strip sacks. It wasn’t pretty, and expectations should be held in check for the Colts passing game given the lack of relevant options, but Jones held on to help snap Indianapolis’ nine-game losing streak dating back to last season. His most impressive play was probably a middle-of-field ball to Laquon Treadwell that put the Colts in field-goal range for Spencer Shrader’s go-ahead kick with less than 30 seconds remaining. The Colts have a better matchup next week against the Commanders, but Jones would be tough to trust as more than a bottom-rung superflex QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 22-of-31 passes for 210 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Colts’ 33-30, Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, adding 10 yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones lost one of his top receivers at the end of the first quarter when Alec Pierce departed with a heel injury. He was largely unable to attack downfield following Pierce’s departure. That would all change on the team’s lone possession of overtime when Jones hit Laquon Treadwell for a 48-yard shot on the first play following a Chiefs field goal, but the team would be unable to punch their ticket to a win while settling for a field goal of their own. The team could be forced to play possession ball moving forward considering the short-area nature of the remaining pass-catchers, pending the status of Pierce. That spells trouble against the vaunted Houston defense in Week 3, where Jones will be a fringe QB2 while potentially down his field-stretching option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 19-of-31 passes for 166 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Colts’ 41-23, Week 1 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones and the Colts got off to a strong start in this one. The Colts came out of the gate attempting seven straight passes, with Jones going 5-for-7 on the drive for 59 yards. Jonathan Taylor would cap the opening drive with a one-yard touchdown to give the Colts an early lead, but Jones and company struggled to get things going after that. He would muster just 29 passing yards for the remainder of the first half and was baited by Ravens LB Roquan Smith into throwing an interception on the Colts’ second possession. Jones would orchestrate a scoring drive early in the fourth quarter, connecting on passes of 14 and 23 yards to Alec Pierce before eventually finding Tyler Warren for a nine-yard score. Things won’t get any easier for Jones and the Colts next week as they travel to Kansas City to take on the Chiefs. Jones shouldn’t be trusted as anything more than a mid to low-end QB2 in that matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Colts announced Anthony Richardson will start Thursday’s preseason game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Richardson and Riley Leonard will both play, while Daniel Jones will sit. Richardson’s trade request this offseason has gone nowhere, but the Colts appear to be giving him ample opportunity to showcase himself in the preseason as he will get the first half here and the second half next week against Atlanta, while Leonard picks up the other two halves. The Colts are likely hoping someone talks themselves into trading a low pick for Richardson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: The Indy Star’s Joel A. Erickson reports that QB Riley Leonard and QB Anthony Richardson will play in the Colts’ preseason Week 1 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Colts coach Shane Steichen did not indicate who will start the game, nor did he rule out QB Daniel Jones (Achilles). Per Erickson, holding Jones out would be unsurprising. Richardson was recently seen working with the third-team offense, so Leonard could have the inside track to start on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Colts Roundtable’s Jake Arthur reports Daniel Jones (Achiiles) appears to be “completely fine physically.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Arthur said Jones, coming off a December Achilles tear, looks “as if he’d never had major surgery, taking off on full-speed scrambles multiple times. He’s been efficient and accurate, kept the offense in rhythm, and spread the ball around.” This is in line with everything else coming out of Colts camp just eight months after Jones ruptured his Achilles — an injury that often requires a year of recovery. If Jones is able to scramble as much as he did before the injury, he could be one of the best late-round quarterback picks in fantasy this summer. Arthur said Jones has spread the ball around in camp, with Josh Downs and Tyler Warren seeing the bulk of the targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: ESPN’s Ben Solak reports Daniel Jones (Achilles) is “clearly in a good place” and looks “unimpeded.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Somehow, Daniel Jones returned. Both GM Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen “reported on the quality of his play with a little relief,” though he isn’t quite 100 percent yet. It does sound like he’s trending towards playing Week 1 and should be mobile enough to make the Colts offense work even if he’s not quite as fast as he was before tearing his Achilles. It’s good news for the Colts’ pass-catchers and Jonathan Taylor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.headline: Saints signed Jarquez Hunter, formerly of the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.analysis: Hunter, a 2025 fourth-round pick with the Rams, was traded to the Dolphins earlier this year. He was recently waived. The Saints need help in the backfield with Travis Etienne (hamstring) on injured reserve. Hunter has long odds of meaningfully contributing, though he was an intriguing prospect.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.headline: Dolphins signed RB Jarquez Hunter to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.analysis: Hunter was notably acquired for Tutu Atwell in the preseason but was released during final cuts. The Dolphins now bring him back as depth in the running back room. Also notably on the practice squad is former first-round defensive lineman Mazi Smith. The Dolphins rounded out the practice squad with RB Carlos Washington, WR Jalen Reagor, WR Will Sheppard, CB Ethan Bonner, DE Max Llewellyn, TE Tre Watson, OT Gottlieb Ayedze, DL Jordan Miller, EDGE Clelin Ferrell, EDGE Amari Gainer, EDGE Rodney McGraw, LB Liam Anderson, CB Jaylin Simpson, and S Major Burns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.headline: Dolphins waived RB Jarquez Hunter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.analysis: It’s a bit surprising after Hunter was acquired in a 1-for-1 swap for Tutu Atwell three days ago, but the Dolphins are undoubtedly hoping he will clear waivers and revert to the practice squad. The move was also a Miami money-saver, so it was not all for naught. Also waived/released by the Dolphins are OT Gottlieb Ayedze, CB Miles Battle, S Major Burns, TE Jeremiah Franklin, QB Mark Gronowski, WR Donaven McCulley, EDGE Rodney McGraw, CB Jai’Onte’ McMillan, QB Cam Miller, DL Fatorma Mulbah, LB Cam Riley, RB Carlos Washington Jr., DL Matthew Butler, LB Tyrel Dodson, EDGE Cameron Goode, OT Charlie Heck, S Lonnie Johnson Jr., WR Terrace Marshall Jr., EDGE David Ojabo, WR Jalen Reagor and CB Marco Wilson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.headline: Rams acquired WR Tutu Atwell from the Dolphins in exchange for RB Jarquez Hunter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.analysis: Back with his old team, Atwell is highly unlikely to warrant FLEX treatment this season, but he provides the Rams with a speed element that the offense was somewhat lacking. The move also indicates that TE Terrance Ferguson will not be asked to stretch the field as much as he did last year, freeing him up for a potential breakout campaign. Last week, The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported that Hunter has had a good training camp, showing “many of the rushing skills that had the Rams enamored enough to trade up and draft him in the fourth round last year.” He will likely compete for the No. 2 running back job in Miami.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Jarquez Hunter will retain “the same role” in 2026 that he had in the 2025 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.analysis: In other words, Hunter is simply waiting on Blake Corum or Kyren Williams to actually miss time. When neither of them did, he managed only five active games and zero offensive snaps. It’s early to cut bait with Hunter in dynasty leagues, but he certainly isn’t giving off any “must keep” vibes at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.headline: Rams RB Blake Corum (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.analysis: Corum is firmly on the wrong side of questionable at this point and the Rams have already secured a playoff spot. Starting RB Kyren Williams (ankle) is nursing an ankle injury. If both players are declared inactive, rookie RB Jarquez Hunter could get the start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.headline: Rams RB Kyren Williams (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.analysis: Williams’ backup, RB Blake Corum (ankle), has not yet practiced this week and the Rams are already headed to the playoffs. Rams rookie RB Jarquez Hunter could see live action this week against the Cardinals, if the coaching staff opts to preserve Williams’ health for the postseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.headline: Rams declared WR Davante Adams (hamstring) inactive for Week 16 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.analysis: Adams has been rehabbing this hamstring injury for weeks. He played through it without issue in Week 14 but suffered a re-injury in Week 15. Tonight’s absence was expected. It gives rookie WR Konata Mumpfield a chance to establish himself as a contributor, though expectations must be held in check. He should not be started in re-draft formats. The Rams also declared CB Ahkello Witherspoon, QB Stetson Bennett IV, RB Jarquez Hunter, OL Beaux Limmer and OLB Nick Hampton inactive in Week 16 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua (ankle) is active for Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.analysis: Nacua injured his ankle while attempting to secure an end zone target in Week 6. He sat out the Rams’ Week 7 game against the Jaguars, but fortunately for the Rams, they were on bye in Week 8, allowing him to miss just one game in two weeks. He should be started as a high-end WR1 against the Saints. The Rams declared QB Stetson Bennett IV, RB Jarquez Hunter, CB Darious Williams, OL Beaux Limmer, OL David Quessenberry and DE Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 9 against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.headline: Rams declared RB Jarquez Hunter, WR Puka Nacua, OG Beaux Limmer, RT Rob Havenstein, and DE Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 7 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jarquez-hunter.analysis: Nacua will get a Week 8 bye to rest up before eying a Week 9 return against the Saints. Hunter is back to being a healthy scratch after getting some work on special teams over the past month. He hasn’t earned a snap on offense this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: When asked if Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) could resume practicing for Week 6 against the Giants, Saints coach Kellen Moore said, “not right now.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson was officially a non-participant to begin the week, as expected. Moore adds that Tyson is “progressing well,” and New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett said there is “an expectation that he’ll return to practice soon.” Tyson should be rostered in 12-team formats, but fantasy managers must, unfortunately, remain patient.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is “weeks away from return.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: The Saints’ offense has managed just fine without Tyson, but it doesn’t sound like it will get a boost from the rookie first-rounder any time soon. According to Schefter, Tyson is “making progress and feeling good,” but the earliest we may see him is Week 7. That said, due to the Saints playing Week 7 in Paris, Schefter also notes that “the most logical” return date for Tyson could be Week 9 after the team’s bye week. Fantasy managers stashing Tyson will need to continue doing so for the next several weeks, and even when he’s active, it could take a few games for him to see a full assortment of snaps. We can expect Devaughn Vele to continue operating as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave until Tyson returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said that “at the moment,” he does not expect WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) to begin practicing next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson is currently on injured reserve and will be eligible to join his teammates on the practice field next week. Moore added, “but we shall see” at the end of his statement, making it at least possible for Tyson to resume practicing in Week 5. For now, Week 6 could be more likely. Once activated from injured reserve, Tyson will have a 21-day window to continue rehabbing, if need be.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints placed Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson has been dealing with hamstring issues since his senior season at Arizona State. The issue flared up during training camp and he is now expected to be sidelined for roughly two months, as of two weeks ago. With an international game in Week 7 and a bye the following week, a Week 9 return looks like the most likely outcome for the rookie. He could still put up strong fantasy numbers in the second half of the season, but it’s hard to justify holding him in leagues with shallow benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints WR Bryce Lance caught 2-of-4 targets for 28 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Lance could have the inside track for the Saints’ short-term No. 3 wide receiver job with WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) sidelined, though WR Barion Brown will almost assuredly make the roster as a receiver and returner. Lance nearly added a decent, leaping downfield gain to his box score, but QB Spencer Rattler’s pass grazed off his fingertips along the sideline. Brown was not involved as a receiver today, but rushed twice for 19 yards and one touchdown, including an eight-yard jet sweep that got him into the end zone. He also returned one punt for four yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett believes the Saints might not need to sign a short-term replacement for WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Triplett was apparently surprised to see reporters wondering whether the Saints should bring a veteran receiver aboard. According to him, the Saints had nine legitimate wide receiver candidates to make the final roster, with rookie WRs Bryce Lance and Barion Brown leading the charge. Per Triplett, Lance “is coming on faster than anyone else,” though Brown notably surged early in camp. Lance does not play on special teams, which could make him an ideal No. 3 wide receiver. Triplett also believes the Saints should design a package of plays for the speedy Brown, who WR Chris Olave said is “basically the same player” as former Saints WR Rashid Shaheed. For deep league fantasy managers, Lance could be worth a late-round dart throw. Both players should be rostered in dynasty.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is expected to miss roughly two months, reports NFL Insider Ian Rapoport.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson left practice last Thursday with a hamstring injury and sought opinions from multiple doctors over the weekend. Now he’s slated to miss roughly two months, according to Rapoport. It’s a tough blow for the 22-year-old receiver who also battled hamstring injuries during his college career. The Saints also drafted receivers Bryce Lance and Barion Brown, though Devaughn Vele could be first in line for additional targets while Tyson is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints HC Kellen Moore said the team is “still in collection mode” regarding Jordyn Tyson’s hamstring injury
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: This comes a day after we learned that Tyson is seeking multiple opinions on the hamstring injury he suffered on Thursday. At some point, the Saints will have collected enough information to feel comfortable telling us about Tyson’s injury, but for now, we will continue to wait. The longer this goes on, the worse the news will feel. Hopefully this is something that will only sideline Tyson for a few weeks, but given his history of hamstring injuries, which slowed him during the pre-draft process, it wouldn’t be surprising if his absence extended into the regular season. Hopefully we’ll have a clear answer on his status soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is seeking multiple opinions on his recent injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Garafolo captioned a report from ESPN’s Katherine Terrell regarding Tyson’s new injury, adding that Tyson’s “timeline to return is TBD but doesn’t seem it’ll be anytime soon.” Here’s what we know: Tyson injured his right hamstring yesterday. Multiple right hamstring injuries derailed his 2025 college season and kept him from participating in the pre-draft process. Saints coach Kellen Moore initially said the new injury is unrelated to Tyson’s prior injuries, but New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett noted today that Moore “changed his wording to say it wasn’t ‘necessarily’ related.” Moore also said that Tyson’s Week 1 availability may be impacted. Here’s hoping that Tyson’s decision to seek multiple opinions yields multiple positive reports. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints HC Kellen Moore said Jordyn Tyson is dealing with a right hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: According to Moore, this is not related to the previous hamstring injuries Tyson has dealt with, and the team is gathering more information before determining a recovery timeline. Moore also said the possibility of Tyson missing Week 1 can’t be ruled out. It’s not exactly encouraging news, but we’re holding out hope that, at worst, this is a short-term absence for Tyson, whose pre-draft process was hampered by hamstring injuries. Tyson profiles as a decent WR3 play in fantasy if/when he is on the field this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.headline: Keeanu Benton (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.analysis: Benton suffered the ankle injury in Week 5 against the Colts. The Steelers defensive tackle, who signed a four-year, $72 million contract extension in August, has had a quiet season statistically while being double-teamed at the highest rate of any defensive tackle in the NFL. Benton missing time would be another blow to a defensive line already playing without second-year defensive tackle Derrick Harmon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.headline: Steelers signed DL Keeanu Benton to a four-year, $72 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.analysis: The deal was first reported by NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Benton, who turned 25 in July, is entering his fourth season in the league after the Steelers selected him in the second-round of the 2023 NFL Draft. Coming off a career-best season that saw him record 5.5 sacks, Benton would’ve been set to hit free agency next offseason without a contract extension. Now Benton joins LB Nick Herbig, TE Darnell Washington and K Chris Boswell on the list of Steelers to receive extensions this offseason. With his $18 million per year contract, Benton is now the highest-paid defensive lineman in Steelers history.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.headline: Speaking on the Kaboly And Mack podcast, Mark Kaboly said Steelers DL Keeanu Benton could be “the odd man out” for an extension this summer.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.analysis: Kaboly and his co-host, Chris Mack, were wondering aloud why the Steelers have not yet signed CB Joey Porter to an extension this offseason when the conversation shifted to Benton. Both Kaboly and Mack were seemingly of the opinion that signing Benton, 24, to an extension does not appear to be a priority for the front office. Since joining the Steelers as a 2023 second-round pick, Benton ranks fifth on the team in sacks (nine) and quarterback pressures (75), 10th in solo tackles (82) and ties for sixth in TFLs (13). He is a capable defender, who should stick around in the league, but he may not earn a lucrative extension from team that drafted.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.headline: Steelers signed DL Keeanu Benton to his rookie contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.analysis: Benton, the 49th pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, signed a contract that includes guaranteed money in the third year -- an unprecedented deal, per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Benton performed well at the NFL Combine after serving as the anchor of Wisconsin’s defensive line, recording 60 tackles in his final two collegiate seasons. He should be a plus for a Steelers defense graded by PFF as 2022’s tenth best run-defending unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.headline: Steelers selected Wisconsin DL Keeanu Bentonwith the No. 49 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keeanu-ben.analysis: The Senior Bowl standout boosted his stock at every step of the pre-Draft process, also posting an 8.65 RAS at the Combine. His 3-cone time in the 91st-percentile reflects his lacrosse background, while the explosion indicated by his 85th-percentile Broad Jump is apparent in his play. While amassing 60 tackles in his final two seasons in Madison, Benton showed great ability to anchor in the middle of a stout Badger defense. He has a great punch that knocks many offensive linemen off their spots while his chops and rips have martial art precision. Despite not being put in a position to put up multiple sacks, he still ended up with six sacks in his junior and senior seasons, resulting in All-B1G honors. The biggest problem with Benton is his tendency to play with a high pad level thus losing his anchor. He’ll join a Steelers defense with a rush defense graded by PFF as last season’s tenth best.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (foot) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Theo Johnson has a neck injury and was limited in practice. Both tight ends should be able to suit up on Sunday. Coming off a career-high in targets (13), Likely is looking more like a top-five fantasy tight end every week. He should be in every fantasy lineup for his Week 6 date with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 11-of-13 targets for 94 yards and two touchdown in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely set a new career-high with 11 receptions in this one, and came up with two clutch touchdowns in the process. His first score came on a three-yard strike from Jameis Winston on a third-and-goal play that the Giants needed to stay in the game, cutting the Commanders’ lead to 19-13. Then, in the fourth quarter and with the Giants facing a fourth-and-eight, Likely turned an eight-yard reception upfield for a 17-yard touchdown that nearly looked like a fumble and turnover at the goal-line. Likely has been targeted 25 times in his last two games and has now gone for 66 or more yards in three of five games to start the season. He’s starting to show good chemistry with Jameis Winston and will be on the TE1 radar in next week’s game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 5 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: The Giants’ passing offense is tethered to Jameis Winston’s scattershot arm, but Likely has a favorable matchup against the Commanders’ defense this week. He can be started as a low-end TE1 in this divisional showdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely is on track to face the Commanders’ fantasy-friendly defense in Week 5. Ideally, we will see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. The Giants’ starting tight end warrants TE1 treatment thanks to his workload and plus matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely evidently got a little banged up while handling a second-high 12 targets last week. His early-week participation puts him on track to face the Commanders in Week 5, but new injuries are worth keeping an eye on. He is a TE1 if active this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 7-of-12 targets for 66 yards in the Giants’ Week 4 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely’s 12 targets were a new season high as fill-in QB Jameis Winston finally got a little something going through the air. That included two heinous interceptions, but we were beginning to wonder if Winston was ever going to complete another pass. That he did stabilizes Likely’s low-end TE1 value, though we have no doubt the giveaways will stick in the coaching staff’s mind. This is still an offense that is going to work to hide the quarterback and potentially start trade acquisition J.J. McCarthy at some point this fall. Those variables limit Likely’s upside even if the floor is now looking a little better heading into Week 5 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 2-of-5 targets for 13 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely’s yardage total came back to Earth last week with just 33 despite seeing 10 targets. It fell further today, as did the target total. On the plus side, he finished second on the team in receiving opportunities and finished with a 23 percent target share. Likely remains the team’s de facto No. 2 receiver behind Malik Nabers. That simply wasn’t worth much in terms of fantasy points today. He remains a solid TE1 bet for Week 4 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 5-of-10 targets for 33 yards in the Giants’ Week 2 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Although fantasy managers are thrilled with the team-leading 10 targets, the nature of those targets is cause for concern considering the uneven play from backup quarterback Jameis Winston. Starter Jaxson Dart was forced from the game with a knee injury on the team’s first possession and it would not be shocking to see him miss games considering the mechanism of his injury, leaving the offense in the hands of the inconsistent Winston. Even so, fantasy managers will be thrilled to start Likely in a plus matchup against the Titans in Week 3, particularly considering the multitude of injuries at the position throughout the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught all eight targets for 78 yards and two touchdowns in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Making his debut for a new team, Likely didn’t wait long to prove he can be a featured tight end for the Giants, scoring on the final possession of the first half and first possession after the break. His first score highlighted his athleticism as he escaped coverage to the corner of the end zone from 15 yards out while his second trip to paint was reminiscent of a Nagy design for Travis Kelce in which the veteran tight end shed a chip-block in the flat for an easy score from two yards. Likely looks every bit of a fantasy TE1 but gets a difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 2. Even so, you’re starting him if you got him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano believes Isaiah Likely could be a “breakout star” in the Giants offense this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Graziano affirmed what every fantasy manager believes: Likely will probably be the team’s WR2 behind Malik Nabers this season. New York coaches, according to Graziano, “love the way he has embraced and evolved his relationship with Jaxson Dart since he has been in New York. Likely is a regular visitor to the quarterback room, and the connection he has formed with Dart on and off the field could pay major dividends.” Graziano said Likely could be Dart’s top option if Nabers needs time to get back to full speed as he recovers from his 2025 ACL injury. Likely profiles as an easy click for fantasy drafters who forgo the game’s elite tight ends.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.headline: Taylor Moton (blood clots) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.analysis: Moton is tentatively on track to make his return from injured reserve this week. Meanwhile, RT Monroe Freeling (knee) sat out on Wednesday. Panthers DT Tershawn Wharton (neck) is practicing in full, while EDGE Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.headline: Panthers designated OT Taylor Moton (blood clots) for return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.analysis: Moton was placed on the reserve/non-football injury list entering camp after it was revealed that he was dealing with blood clots in his lungs. The 32-year-old tackle now has 21 days to be activated from IR or be ruled out for the season, but we would expect him to be activated in the coming weeks. Moton earned a PFF offensive grade of 80.5 last season and allowed just three sacks and 22 pressures. In addition to Moton, the Panthers also designated DL Tershawn Wharton (neck) for return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.headline: Panthers placed Ikem Ekwonu (knee) on the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.analysis: Ewkonu suffered a torn patellar tendon in the playoffs. He is expected to return “at some point” this year, though that does not rule out a lengthy absence for the veteran tackle. Fellow starting tackle Taylor Moton was placed on the reserve/NFI list because of a blood clot in his lung. He will also miss at least four weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.headline: Panthers placed RT Taylor Moton on the reserve/non-football injury list with blood clots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.analysis: He’s joined by CB Jaycee Horn, who cut his foot while running and required stitches. Horn’s injury is expected to be a minor one. Moton, on the other hand, is expected to miss the start of the season and the “belief” is he’ll play in 2026. The Panthers later clarified that Moton is hopeful to return from clotting in his lung at “mid-season.” Rookie first-round tackle Monroe Freeling figures to step in for Moton early.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.headline: Tetairoa McMillan (foot/ankle) will play in Week 16 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.analysis: McMillan was a DNP on Wednesday but was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday and Friday. The rookie receiver is officially off the injury report and good to go for Sunday’s pivotal Week 16 matchup against the Bucs. McMillan profiles as a low-end WR2 after failing to top 43 yards for three straight weeks. The Panthers also listed OG Damien Lewis, CB Jaycee Horn, and OT Taylor Moton as good to go for Sunday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.headline: Panthers listed OG Chandler Zavala (knee) as questionable for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.analysis: The Panthers didn’t open Zavala’s 21-day return window until this week, but the third-year guard was listed as a full participant in all three practices. Players who log a full week of practice tend to suit up come game day, so it’s possible this questionable designation is more cautious optimism than anything else. In addition to Zavala the Panthers also listed OG Damien Lewis (oblique), OT Taylor Moton (knee), S Nick Scott (groin), and LB Trevin Wallace (shoulder) as questionable for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.headline: Panthers RT Taylor Moton (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.analysis: Moton left the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Bills with the knee issue and did not return. A DNP to start the week puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Sunday’s game against the Packers. Yosh Nijman will take his spot in the lineup if he can’t suit up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.headline: Taylor Moton has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 8 against the Bills with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.analysis: Moton had previously missed games this season with an elbow injury. He is now on the sideline in street clothes, which is never a good sign. The Panthers are now without both of their starting offensive tackles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.headline: Panthers OT Taylor Moton (elbow) will not play in Week 6 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.analysis: The Panthers continue to take hits to their offensive line, with Moton being the latest starter to be sidelined following injuries to C Austin Corbett and RG Robert Hunt earlier this season. Moton has started all five games for the Panthers at right tackle this season, earning a PFF blocking grade of 73.7 while allowing 13 pressures and two sacks. Backup Yosh Nijman is listed behind Moton on the depth chart and will presumably draw the start on Sunday against the Cowboys. In addition to Moton, the Panthers have also ruled out CB Akayleb Evans (hamstring) and DT Tershawn Wharton (toe) for Sunday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.headline: Panthers signed RT Taylor Moton to a two-year, $44 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/taylor-mot.analysis: Moton is now under contract through the 2027 season. The veteran tackle has spent his entire eight-year career with the Panthers, starting every game he’s appeared in since 2018. Moton missed three games in 2024 due to a triceps injury and a knee injury, but hadn’t missed a game in his career prior to Week 6 of last season. A true Iron Man of the sport, Moton earned a PFF pass-blocking grade of 80.6 last season, allowing just 14 pressures and one sack on 538 pass blocking snaps. His new deal comes with $40 million in guaranteed money.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Abdul Carter (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Carter is doing well, so it doesn’t seem like he’s at much risk of missing Week 6. Rookie corner Colton Hood, on the other hand, is in concussion protocol and didn’t practice today. He will likely miss Week 6 while he works his way through the protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants HC John Harbaugh said Abdul Carter’s ankle injury doesn’t appear to be too serious.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Speaking after Monday’s minicamp, Harbaugh said Carter suffered a twisted ankle but downplayed any notion that it would be a serious injury. The Giants and their fans can breathe an early sigh of relief after the former No. 3 overall pick was seen limping off the field early in the first day of the team’s three-day minicamp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants beat writer Pat Leonard reports Abdul Carter suffered an apparent foot injury at Monday’s minicamp and could be seen limping to the sideline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: We’ll likely get an update on this soon, but it’s a concerning development for the second-year pass rusher who is hoping to build on a rookie season that included 43 tackles, four sacks, and seven TFLs. According to Leonard, Carter eventually made his way indoors and was seen leaving the field without his shoe. ESPN’s Jordan Raanan later reported that the “initial belief” is that Carter is okay, but we will provide an update when we receive one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants EDGE Abdul Carter (illness) is not on the injury report for Week 18 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Carter returned to practice on Friday, logging a limited session. Giants DL Dexter Lawrence (illness) was also removed from the injury report, though he did not resume practicing. We tentatively expect both players to be on the field for Week 18, but projecting their snap counts is tough. The Giants and Cowboys have both been eliminated from playoff contention.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants EDGE Abdul Carter (illness) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Carter’s absence is unsurprising. The coaching staff reportedly sent him and others home yesterday. The Athletic’s Dan Duggan noted DL Dexter Lawrence was also absent on Thursday. He believes Lawrence is “also in the illness category.” Both players have a chance to face the Cowboys this week, though the team notably kept TE Theo Johnson (illness) sidelined in Week 17, and he has not yet resumed practicing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants EDGE Abdul Carter (illness) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Three Giants players “were sent home or not at practice as they deal with illnesses.” Carter is, unfortunately, among them. The Giants’ stud rookie has been playing very well as of late. An absence would make life far easier on the Cowboys this week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Giants EDGE Abdul Carter “vehemently denied Tuesday that he slept through a walk-through practice last week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: The No. 3 overall pick was benched for a series on Sunday after reports surfaced that he slept through practice last week. Carter says the Giants changed their practice schedule and he was getting treatment while he was supposed to be at the walk-through. The young defender still owned up to his mistake but wanted to clear the air on exactly what happened. Between the Carter benching and a loss to the Packers in Week 11, it has been a rocky start for interim head coach Mike Kafka. Things won’t be getting any better in Week 12 when the Giants travel to Detroit to take on the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Giants EDGE Abdul Carter (hamstring) is a game-time decision for Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Carter was added to the injury report on Friday as a limited participant before being listed as questionable. That likely means he suffered the hamstring issue in practice. Per Rapoport, he will go through some work before inactives before the team makes a final decision on his status. The rookie has 24 pressures and .5 sacks this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants EDGE Abdul Carter (hamstring) is questionable for New York’s Week 7 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: He was a surprise limited participant in Friday’s practice, indicating he hurt it mid-session. Carter did talk to the media on Friday, which is usually a good sign, but he’s probably a true question mark heading into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants signed No. 3 overall pick EDGE Abdul Carter to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Per USA Today’s Art Stapleton, Carter’s fully guaranteed $45.255 million contract includes a $29.497 million signing bonus. Carter is officially the newest member of the Giants’ loaded pass rush. He is expected to contribute significantly in year one, lining up opposite veteran EDGE Brian Burns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.headline: Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.analysis: Eluemunor told reporters he felt his calf pop during Week 5 against the Commanders. He left the game and Marcus Mbow took his spot at right tackle. Head coach John Harbaugh called him day-to-day on Monday, so it’s at least not a long-term issue, though he still looks like a coin flip for Week 6. Left tackle Andrew Thomas did not practice, though that’s standard fare for him as he continues to play through a groin injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) is “day to day.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.analysis: It wouldn’t be surprising if he missed some practice time this week. Marcus Mbow would get snaps in Week 6 if Eluemunor were not able to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports Giants RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) is feeling better post-game, but the team will have to see how he feels as the week progresses.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.analysis: According to Raanan, Eluemunor felt his calf pop and left today’s game against the Commanders. Fortunately, he was able to walk around on his own, which is a good sign. The Giants went to Marcus Mbow at right tackle in Eluemunor’s absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.headline: Giants re-signed OT Jermaine Eluemunor to a three-year, $39 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.analysis: Eluemunor’s market did not generate quite as he hoped it would, and in the end he settles for the low end of Dan Duggan’s $13-18MM projection. It’s a good keep for the Giants, as Eluemunor has provided steady-if-not-spectacular line play over his two-year contract with them. Entering his age-32 season, the Giants will likely start trying to find succession plans in the next year or so.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan believes Giants RT Jermaine Eluemunor could make $13-$18 million a season on the open market.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.analysis: Duggan says he’d bet on the high end of that. Of New York’s three main free agents, Eluemunor is the one that they still seem to have some chance of retaining. Coming off a two-year, $14 million bargain contract, Eluemunor figures to strike it big in free agency as one of the few tackles of renown on the market.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.headline: Giants LT Jermaine Eluemunor (quad) is doubtful for Week 14 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.analysis: Right tackle Evan Neal is questionable with a hip issue. Head coach Brian Daboll called both week to week on Wednesday. It’s safe to assume Eluemunor won’t play through the doubtful tag while Neal appears to be on the wrong side fo questionable given Daboll’s comments. Drew Lock will be an easy target for the Saints’ pass-rush on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.headline: Giants RT Evan Neal (hip) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.analysis: Giants head coach Brian Daboll called Neal and left tackle Jermaine Eluemunor week to week with hip and quad injuries. Drew Lock will be behind backups at both tackle spots this week and possibly for the rest of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.headline: Giants signed OG Greg Van Roten, formerly of the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.analysis: Per ESPN’s Jordan Raanan, Jermaine Eluemunor is going to play right tackle with Van Roten at right guard. That means Evan Neal is the odd man out. The former top-10 pick is currently on the PUP list and doesn’t appear to have a role in the New York offense. Van Roten started all 17 games for the Raiders last year and is a solid addition for a team that fielded one of the league’s worst offensive lines in 2023.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.headline: Giants agreed to terms with OL Jermaine Eluemunor, formerly of the Raiders, on a two-year, $14 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.analysis: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport was first on the scoop. Eluemunor started 31 games for the Raiders over the past two years. The bulk of his work has come at right tackle, though he did see three starts at left tackle and one at right guard over that span. Eluemunor has additional experience at both positions from previous seasons. The move gives New York a versatile lineman who can fill any one of their many holes across the offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.headline: The Las Vegas Review-Journal’s Vincent Bonsignore reports “all options are on the table” for second-year RT Alex Leatherwood, including trading or cutting him.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jermaine-e.analysis: It would be quite the admission of defeat for the Raiders, dumping last year’s No. 17 overall pick, but the new Dave Ziegler-Josh McDaniels regime has no attachment to Leatherwood. There’s a chance he could also be moved inside to guard, but it’s clear this staff doesn’t view Leatherwood as a starter. A powerful run blocker, Leatherwood is horrid in pass protection. He’d probably be a better fit in a power run scheme. Veteran G/T Jermaine Eluemunor is viewed as the current favorite for right-tackle duties after following McDaniels over from New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker (quad) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Panthers coach Dave Canales told reporters earlier this week that Coker was returning from both quad and ankle injuries, though the team is only listing the quad issue.
