We take this as a good sign for his overall health. Coker can be treated as a WR2 in his first game back, facing an Eagles defense that struggles to cover opposing slot receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jalen Coker (quad) is “on track” to play in Carolina’s Week 6 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker was spotted practicing on Tuesday (there will be no injury report for this one) and seems like he’s well on track to return. He’ll be a fringe WR2/WR3 against the Eagles in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Panthers WR Jalen Coker (quadricep) is inactive for Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: This was though to be the most likely scenario after head coach Dave Canales told reporters Friday that the team would elevate Ja’Seem Reed if the belief was that Coker could not go on Sunday Night Football. Reed was, in fact, elevated Saturday and Coker was declared inactive. Brycen Tremaine appears to be in line for a featured role after playing 81 percent of the team’s offensive snaps a week ago. Expect John Metchie to also see additional snaps and opportunities, while David Moore could see package usage on the perimeter. Also inactive for the Panthers are TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, G Damien Lewis, OT Albert Reese, and DT Cam Jackson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jalen Coker (quad) is “unlikely to play” in Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker injured his quad in Week 3. He got in two limited practices this week before being listed as questionable. It doesn’t sound like a long-term injury, but the team is being cautious with a young wideout who has already suffered multiple lower-body injuries this year. With Xavier Legette on IR, Brycen Tremayne is Carolina’s WR2 for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Panthers elevated WR Ja’Seem Reed from the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: This is notable considering head coach Dave Canales previously said that the team would only elevated Reed if Coker couldn’t go in Week 4. Coker, listed as questionable, now appears on the worse side of the designation ahead of a Week 4 meeting with the Lions on Sunday Night Football. Fantasy managers are better off making contingent plans now considering the Panthers are the penultimate game of the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker (quad) is questionable for Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: After being a DNP on Wednesday, Coker logged back-to-back limited practices to close out the week. Coker played through an ankle injury in Weeks 2 and 3, and will likely play through his quad injury this week in a Sunday night matchup against the Lions. Hopefully we’ll get more clarity on his availability later in the weekend, but for now, we expect him to play. That said, managers would be wise to stash a Sunday/Monday night emergency option in the unlikely event Coker is ruled out when inactives are announced 90 minutes before kickoff.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Jalen Coker (quad) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker is currently going through drills, catching passes from Bryce Young. Yesterday, Panthers coach Dave Canales labeled Coker day-to-day. Today’s participation confirms that. The Panthers’ No. 2 wide receiver seemingly has a shot at playing in Week 4 against the Lions. We expect to see him listed as limited today, but we will circle back to provide an update if he ends up practicing in full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Panthers WR Jalen Coker (quad) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Panthers coach Dave Canales said WR Xavier Legette (knee) is week-to-week, while Coker “is more day-to-day.” Canales adds that the team “has to see Coker move around before he returns to action.” Coker remains firmly in the questionable camp at this time. He might have a chance to play in Week 4 against the Lions, but fantasy managers should make a serious backup plan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jalen Coker is considered questionable for Week 4 against the Lions after suffering a quad injury against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: Coker said after the game that he did not think his injury was too serious. He’s already been playing through an ankle injury, so we’ll assume he’ll be able to play through this based on his own estimation and the early reporting from Rapoport. Coker caught two passes for 18 yards in Sunday’s loss to the Browns, but will remain in the WR2 ranks for Week 4 if he’s able to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.headline: Panthers WR Jalen Coker (quad) said he does not think he suffered a “bad” injury in Week 3 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-coke.analysis: An official diagnosis has not yet been given, but Coker does not think his quad injury is “anything too crazy.” He spent time on short-term injured reserve with a quad injury last season, so adding another one to his injury history is a little concerning. We expect updates on the issue in the next 24-48 hours. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said Marvin Harrison Jr. will play in Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: It’s a slightly short turnaround for MHJ, who was traded to the Texans on Sunday, and a weird travel schedule with Houston flying to London to take on the Jags. On the other hand, a week is still more than enough time to get Harrison Jr. installed at least as a part-time player. He isn’t much of a fantasy option this week, but a week or two of practice reps could get him in the FLEX mix if Houston proves to be a better fit for the former No. 4 overall pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Texans acquired WR Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Cardinals in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison, 24, gets a fresh start partway through his third NFL season. The former first-round pick has averaged just 47.8 receiving yards per game in 33 career games. Adjusting to a new scheme on the fly could be challenging, and Harrison has not proven himself to be a reliable fantasy contributor. It could be tough sledding for fantasy managers, but if Harrison quickly adjusts to his new team, he has a clear runway to No. 2 wide receiver duties next to Nico Collins. He should be rostered in 12-team leagues. The Cardinals are also sending a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Texans in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Cardinals declared Marvin Harrison Jr., QB Carson Beck, CB Starling Thomas, Andrew Wingard and DL Andrew Billings inactive for Week 5 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Life continues to be rough for fantasy managers rostering Harrison. The soon-to-be ex-Cardinal will not participate in what should be a fantasy-friendly game against the porous Lions defense. Bummer. Still no definitive word on where he will end up next week. Trey McBride, Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne benefit from his absence. The Cardinals will be without Wingard, one of two starting safeties, but will have DT Walter Nolen (calf) available to them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Cardinals are finalizing a deal to trade WR Marvin Harrison Jr., reports ESPN’s Adam Schefter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: The Cardinals informed Harrison this morning that he will be inactive for Sunday’s game against the Lions as the details of the trade are finalized, according to Schefter. While it’s unclear where Harrison is headed, Schefter mentions the Houston Texans as one team known to have interest. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reported this morning that the Cardinals could be seeking a second-round pick and a mid-round pick in return. Harrison has just five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown in four games this year. According to Schefter, no Harrison trade will be completed until after Sunday’s games. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Cardinals would want a second-round pick and more to consider trading WR Marvin Harrison Jr., reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Pelissero says the Cardinals would want a second-pick and perhaps a mid-round pick in exchange for Harrison. The 24-year-old receiver was drafted fourth overall two years ago, but under new coach Matt LaFluer he has 85 yards in four games this year. Pelissero points to Harrison’s decision to hire an agent last month as evidence he could be preparing for a trade. While Harrison has obviously been a disappointment in fantasy this year, he should find his way into some starting lineups against the Lions secondary in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught a 12-yard touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 4 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison capped the Cardinals’ opening drive with a beautiful 12-yard end zone grab against Deonte Banks’ 1-on-1 coverage. It was the best possible start to the beleaguered wideout’s day. It would also prove to be a false start, as he caught zero other passes on three scattered targets. Admittedly, that does not include a late DPI that set the Cardinals up at the Giants’ four-yard line as they desperately sought a potential game-winning touchdown. Good, but nowhere close to enough for all involved. MHJ has now been out-targeted 30-9 by Michael Wilson over the past two weeks. That is to say nothing of Trey McBride. The Lions are a plus Week 5 matchup, but Harrison Jr. remains more waiver wire fodder than potential upside FLEX option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports teams are “doing their due diligence” on Marvin Harrison Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Schefter noted that the Cardinals aren’t “enthralled” with the idea of trading Harrison Jr. He also said point-blank that “it would not be a surprise” for MHJ to be traded. As much as the Cardinals may not want to admit it, this experiment needs to come to an end. The team has Michael Wilson and Trey McBride locked up on long-term contracts and MHJ has done nothing this year. He has four catches for 73 scoreless yards this year. At this point, it’s likely in the best interest of both sides for Harrison Jr. to find a new home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison finished the day with a modest 3/40 receiving line, though that represents a small share of the Cardinals’ offensive output on the day. His first target was a declined offensive pass interference on third down and his first reception came in the second quarter. Harrison did make a clutch catch on third-and-long in the fourth quarter but he ultimately saw just five targets on a day where Jacoby Brissett threw 52 passes. Michael Wilson looks like Brissett’s preferred wide receiver while the deep looks Harrison can excel at are not easily obtainable in this iteration of the Cardinals offense. Harrison is a low-end fantasy WR4 at best against the Giants next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: The Arizona Republic’s Theo Mackie reports Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur “met [the] idea” of manufacturing touches for Marvin Harrison “with skepticism.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: “I know it’s like, ‘Well, just get some easy completions to get going,’” LaFleur told Mackie. “And that’s fine. You also have Trey McBride, who’s one of the best underneath guys in the world. And there’s only about 60, 65 plays a game. And you’ve gotta run the ball. And you’ve got Kendrick, who works underneath pretty well too. So everyone’s kind of got their role.” In other words; don’t look for LaFleur to bail your Harrison fantasy pick out. If Harrison does get cooking this year it’ll be in the normal flow of their offense. So far that has yielded just four targets in two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said he “wouldn’t look into too much” about Marvin Harrison Jr.'s usage in Week 2 because “we didn’t throw the ball for crap anyway.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: “Schematically, it wasn’t good,” LaFleur added, presumably while giving himself a wedgie. Harrison only saw one official target — another was wiped away by penalty — and he played just 74 percent of the snaps. The real problem here is that when the Cardinals ran well on offense in Week 1, Harrison had just one catch for 33 yards on three targets. He’s going to be hard to trust in any given week until we see it “click” in some way with LaFleur’s offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles activated LG Landon Dickerson’s (knee) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: The Eagles desperately need offensive line health. Dickerson’s return cannot come soon enough. New Eagles C Drew Kendall (knee) was not seen practicing today, though Dickerson has officially resumed practicing in some capacity, which is great news. He was seen taking the field with his teammates this afternoon. The Eagles also opened DB Jakorian Bennett, TE Grant Calcaterra and TE Eli Stowers’ (hamstring/quad) practice windows.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles placed G Landon Dickerson (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: It’s about the worst-case scenario for an offense with no shortage of change in 2026, with new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion now hit with a substantial blow to his front five. The news comes on the heels of a close Week 1 victory over the divisional rival Commanders, a game that played much closer than expected. Time will tell if Dickerson makes it back to previous form in what could be his final professional season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles G Landon Dickerson told reporters he didn’t consider retiring this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: Dickerson, a second-round pick in the 2021 NFL Draft, denied reports that he considered retirement this offseason. “I’m not sure where you guys got that from,” he said. Dickerson, who turns 28 in September, said he’s not really concerned about the toll playing takes on his body. He also admitted he “probably shouldn’t have went out and played” last season after needing meniscus surgery so close to the start of Week 1. Dickerson’s rethinking his approach to pushing through injuries as he has in the past.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles and LG Landon Dickerson agreed to a reworked contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: Per ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, Dickerson was set to make $39 million over the next two seasons. That number is down to $36 million, though he can recoup the lost $3 million via 2027 incentives. Dickerson’s contract was previously set to expire in 2028. He is now only under contract through 2027. It’s a relatively minor pay cut for the veteran lineman, and hitting the open market a year earlier could ultimately work in his favor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo believes Landon Dickerson is “no certainty to return” to the Eagles in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: Dickerson is just 27, but struggled through a challenging season in 2025 with two missed games while struggling through several games with ankle and quad injuries. He didn’t look right from the jump. Lane Johnson is another retirement possibility for the Eagles, and The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane believes Johnson isn’t sure his body will hold up and he’s “not sure if he’s coming back or not.” The Eagles are set up for plenty of turnover on the offensive side of the ball this offseason and likely will need to target picks on the offensive line even if Dickerson and Johnson return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles declared LB Nakobe Dean, S Marcus Epps, OLB Jaelan Phillips, RT Lane Johnson, LG Landon Dickerson, TE Dallas Goedert, and DT Jalen Carter inactive for Week 18 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: The Eagles are resting several of their banged-up starters ahead of a Week 18 showdown against the Commanders. The Eagles have already won the division while the Commanders are already eliminated, so this game will see many reserves play snaps. Expect the bulk of the Eagles’ inactive starters to be back for the playoffs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles RT Lane Johnson (foot) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: Eagles LG Landon Dickerson (illness) was also not seen practicing. Dickerson played through his calf injury last week and should be good to go again for Sunday’s game. Johnson sat out, though he is expected to play in Week 17 against the Bills. Having both players on the field would be great for the Eagles’ offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles RT Lane Johnson (foot) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 16 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: The Eagles will at least get Landon Dickerson (calf/rest) off the injury report and up for this one, but it will be at least one more week off for Johnson, who has needed One More Week for about three weeks now. The Eagles don’t have much incentive to rush him with the NFC East all but sewn up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles RT Lane Johnson (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: Left guard Landon Dickerson (calf) was also held out of practices. That’s two DNPs to open the week for the pair of starting linemen. Both players can be considered on the wrong side of questionable for Week 16. With a winnable game versus Washington on tap, it could make sense for the Eagles to give their injured linemen the week off ahead of a Week 17 date with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles RT Lane Johnson (foot) did not practice in Tuesday’s walkthrough.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: In addition to Johnson, LG Landon Dickerson (calf) also was listed as DNP. Dickerson was at least able to play in Week 15, meaning the designation could just be out of precaution for Tuesday’s walkthrough ahead of a Saturday game. As for Johnson, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported last week he was going to practice this week, but he remains out to start Week 16. Johnson has a few more days to practice before the Eagles play the Commanders on Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.headline: Free agent Tyreek Hill’s player rep Drew Rosenhaus said he remains in talks with multiple NFL teams, but “nothing is imminent at this time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.analysis: Hill continues to rehab his surgically repaired knee, following a multi-ligament, season-ending injury in 2025, “with the goal of being on a team in the immediate future.” Earlier today, Hill was found “liable for two of 10 counts related to domestic violence and awarded his estranged wife $500,000 in compensatory damages.” He could face a suspension from the league if he signs with an NFL team. Chiefs players recently said they would be in favor of bringing Hill back to Kansas City.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.headline: The Athletic’s Adam Kilgore reports free agent Tyreek Hill could face NFL discipline under the league’s personal conduct policy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.analysis: A jury this week found Hill, 32, “liable for two of 10 counts related to domestic violence and awarded his estranged wife $500,000 in compensatory damages,” Kilgore reported. Hill, who has faced allegations of domestic violence in the past, was accused of several instances of harming his ex-wife. Hill denied the allegations. An NFL spokesperson told Kilgore that the league has been “monitoring developments in the matter which remains under review of the personal conduct policy.” That could mean Hill will face a suspension if he signs with a team in the coming weeks. Hill’s agent has reportedly reached out to the Chiefs — Hill’s former team — to gauge interest in the veteran wideout coming off a horrific knee injury in October 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.headline: NFL agent Drew Rosenhaus said Tyreek Hill (leg) is “close” to 100 percent recovered.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.analysis: Rosenhaus is shopping Hill to a contending team with “a good quarterback” about a year after Hill suffered a gruesome leg injury that ended his 2025 season with the Dolphins. Hill, who last week testified in his assault and battery court case, is a free agent. “I don’t know if he’s 100 percent today, but he’s close,” Rosenhaus said. “And he’ll get there really soon. But I think that’s probably something you’ll have to wait until he gets out in practices and gets with a team before saying he’s 100 percent.” There have been rumors of a potential Hill reunion with Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs, who recently lost Tyquan Thornton to a season-ending ankle injury and Rashee Rice to a hamstring issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.headline: Free agent WR Tyreek Hill testified in an assault and batter civil case in Miami on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.analysis: This trial stems from a 2025 case in which Hill was alleged to have physically abused his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro. At his hearing, Hill admitted to saying to her that he was “able to get people to hurt her,” but denied allegations that he “hit, scratched or shoved Vaccaro, pulled out her hair, spit in her face or punched toward her stomach while she was pregnant,” per ESPN’s Xuan Thai. Legally speaking, a jury will decide whether or not Hill’s actions warrant any kind of punishment, but the league will likely decide after the trial whether or not Hill’s actions warrant a suspension, which could be as high as six games. Hill’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, recently suggested the 32-year-old receiver could sign with a team in the very near future, but it wouldn’t be surprising if teams interested in him waited to see how this trial plays out. The trial is expected to continue on Friday, when Vaccaro’s attorney will have a chance to question Hill.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.headline: Agent Drew Rosenhaus said he “would anticipate Tyreek Hill potentially signing with a team over the next few days.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Rosenhaus will begin negotiating a deal for Hill with multiple teams. Among these teams is the Chiefs, who lost both Rashee Rice (hamstring) and Tyquan Thornton (ankle) in Week 4’s win over the Raiders. It was reported on Sunday night that the Chiefs have been in contact with Hill about a potential return. Now, it’s safe to say the Chiefs have a real need at the position that Hill could fill should the two reunite. It’s hard to know how soon Hill can contribute on the field, as he’s still working his way back from a brutal knee injury he suffered last season, but he’s posted videos of himself working out to his social media accounts to show he’s close to being ready to go. While other teams could emerge as suitors for Hill, the Chiefs feel like the most obvious landing spot right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.headline: The Athletic’s Mike Silver reports that the Chiefs have already reached out to Tyreek Hill’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.analysis: Less than an hour ago, Silver reported that he spoke to Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce and Chris Jones, among other Chiefs players. Everyone was reportedly into the idea of signing Hill whenever the veteran wide receiver who is currently eyeing a November return from his season-ending knee injury. With Rashee Rice (hamstring) and Tyquan Thornton (ankle) suffering injuries today, the Chiefs need help in the wide receiver corps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.headline: The Athletic’s Mike Silver expects the Chiefs to “have strong interest in a Tyreek Hill (knee) reunion when the free agent receiver is healthy enough to play.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.analysis: Silver said he spoke to Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce and Chris Jones, among others, in the locker room, and the group was “all for” signing Hill when he is ready to play. Per Silver, Hill is believed to be targeting a November return. Rashee Rice injured his hamstring today, and Tyquan Thornton suffered what is likely to be a season-ending ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.headline: Free agent WR Tyreek Hill posted to his account on X that it’s “almost time to get off the couch and get to work.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.analysis: Hill’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said earlier this month that the 32-year-old receiver was advised to postpone his return until “perhaps some time in October.” That makes Hill’s timing for his post a bit more interesting, as there could be a real chance he signs with a team in the coming weeks if he is able to pass a physical and prove he can contribute on the field. Given the injuries around the league, Hill could have a number of suitors if he’s fully recovered from the devastating knee injury he suffered last season, and could turn into a decent fantasy option in the second half of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.headline: Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus said Hill’s doctors recommended he postpone his comeback until “perhaps some time in October.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.analysis: Rosenhaus gushed about Hill’s recovery and how he looks right now. He also mentioned that multiple teams asked him when Hill would be available to sign. We’ll take these with a few grains of salt, given Rosenhaus’s financial ties to his client. Hill is still working his way back from the catastrophic knee injury he suffered in Week 4 of the 2025 season. Fantasy managers can leave Hill on the waiver wire for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.headline: Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, agent Drew Rosenhaus said he doesn’t expect free agent WR Tyreek Hill to sign before the start of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyreek-hil.analysis: Given the reports we’ve received on Hill this offseason, this news doesn’t come as much of a surprise. In May, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Hill might not be ready to play until closer to the midway point of the season, and in July, Hill himself said he had “no power” in his left leg. The 32-year-old receiver suffered a dislocated knee, torn ACL and LCL, along with other ligament damage in Week 4 last season, and could be a long shot to play this season. Rosenhaus did say that Hill “looked great” in a video of him running hills the other day; we won’t have a good sense of where Hill stands in his recovery until he gets a chance to showcase his recovery on a football field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Vikings “hope” to get Jordan Mason (thumb) back from injured reserve for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Late last week, Fowler’s colleague, Kevin Seifert, reported that Mason is expected to return in Week 7 as well. Add him if he is available. Mason is not involved much as a receiver, but his expected rushing workload makes him a reliable FLEX with RB2 upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Kevin Seifert reports Jordan Mason (thumb/IR) is expected to return for Minnesota’s Week 7 game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: The Vikings play the Saints this week, then go on bye in Week 6, so Aaron Jones has one more massive workload week ahead of him against New Orleans before the backfield heads back to a split. Mason looked good in the early going and, if he was cut loose in a shallow league, makes a worthwhile pickup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Vikings placed RB Jordan Mason on injured reserve with a thumb injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: That escalated quickly. On Monday, Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Mason’s “sore thumb” was being evaluated. Apparently, it had sustained a small fracture, which has now been “fixed,” ostensibly surgically, given O’Connell’s phrasing. Short-term injured reserve placement requires players to miss four games, but the Vikings are on bye in Week 6, so Mason will be eligible to return in Week 7. Mason led the backfield with 15 carries in Week 1, so his absence provides RB Aaron Jones with a touch-count boost. Veteran RB DeeJay Dallas operated as the RB3. Rookie RB Demond Claiborne was inactive last week, but should be active in Week 2 against the Lions. Speculatively stashing him could be worthwhile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said Jordan Mason has a sore thumb and is being evaluated.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason didn’t appear to have any issues in Week 1’s win, but adrenaline does carry athletes at times. We’ll likely get an update on this on Wednesday at the latest — we’d consider Mason likely to play in Week 2’s game against the Bears at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason rushed 15 times for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 1 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason led the team in carries but only rushed three more times than Aaron Jones, who also found the end zone. Both backs also ran nine routes each, though Jones was targeted once while Mason did not see a look in the passing game. Mason’s lack of a role through the air will limit his weekly ceiling, but a floor of double-digit carries isn’t half bad. He will sit in the RB3 ranks for his Week 2 date with the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Vikings OC Wes Phillips complimented RB Jordan Mason for losing weight this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason stands 5'11 and his weight is listed between 223-230 pounds depending on the source. He hits the latter figure on the Vikings’ website. That’s fairly hefty for a running back. The Vikings’ starter, RB Aaron Jones, is 31 years old and took a pay cut to stay with the team this offseason. Mason, 27, might have a chance to challenge for the primary rushing role this year, though Jones will likely remain the primary player on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis reports that Vikings RB Demond Claiborne is playing well, but his “short-term NFL impact will hinge on his ability to master the system and his reliability in pass protection.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Lewis believes that “in the long haul, the Vikings project a potentially game-breaking role.” Thus far, Claiborne’s new teammates have taken to addressing him by his childhood nickname, “Lightning.” And, Lewis, in an admittedly over-the-top manner, describes Claiborne’s lateral movements as “the closest thing you’ll find to real-life teleportation.” Hyperbole aside, beat reporters do not always take the time to write features on sixth-round rookies. Given Lewis’ short-term stipulations, it sounds as though Claiborne might be given the chance to compete for a role in the passing game this summer. Starting RB Aaron Jones is entering his age-31 season, and RB Jordan Mason, 27, is a one-dimensional rusher. The two veterans are ahead of Claiborne on the depth chart, no doubt, but this is not an elite one-two punch. Keep an eye on Claiborne this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Vikings restructured Aaron Jones’ contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: The running back takes a pay cut to a base salary of $5.5 million. This move quashes the fantasy value of Jordan Mason, who was looking like he’d head the committee in 2026 by a wide margin. Mason still may wind up leading the Vikings in carries given how often Jones gets hurt, but Jones will probably see at least half the snaps here after agreeing to stay. Jones is more of a high-end RB3 at this stage of his career, as entering his age-32 season he’s started to leave a concerning number of games with injuries and spent time on injured reserve last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason had 14 rushes for 94 yards in the Vikings’ Week 18 win against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason functioned as the team’s lead back with Aaron Jones inactive, seeing 14 of the Vikings’ 24 running back carries. It was the second highest rushing yardage total for Mason in 2025. He mostly served as Minnesota’s No. 2 back behind Jones, seeing more than ten touches in six games. He finishes the year with 770 rushing yards and six scores, catching 14 of 16 targets for 51 yards. Mason, 26, is signed through the 2026 season and could be the team’s lead back if Aaron Jones leaves town. Still, Mason’s lack of involvement as a pass catcher will limit his fantasy upside in any scenario.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Vikings declared RB Aaron Jones, WR Myles Price, QB John Wolford, CB Dwight McGlothern Jr., QB Brett Rypien Sr., T Walter Rouse, and TE T.J. Hockenson inactive for Week 18 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Facing defensive backups for the Packers, Jordan Mason will likely get a starter’s workload in the Minnesota backfield with Jones sidelined. JJ McCarthy, dealing with a hand injury, will start the regular season’s final game. Look for Justin Jefferson to be peppered with targets as QB-WR combo try to get on the same page ahead of an uncertain offseason for McCarthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.headline: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Dayo Odeyingbo (quad) will miss Week 6 against the Falcons but will not be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.analysis: It’s overall a good update for Odeyingbo, even if the veteran defensive end will miss at least one week. The fact that IR was even mentioned does suggest it could be a multi-week absence for him. Odeyingbo has three sacks and two pass breakups this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.headline: Bears agreed to terms with G Joe Thuney, DE Dayo Odeyingbo, and LB TJ Edwards on restructured contracts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.analysis: The moves create a solid $17 million in savings against the cap. The team found themselves right up against the salary cap before the restructures, now entering the regular season with about $22 million in space to maneuver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.headline: Bears EDGE Dayo Odeyingbo (Achilles) participated in full team drills on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.analysis: Odeyingbo tore his Achilles in early November, but it appears the recovery has gone well if he’s already getting full-team reps ahead of training camp. T.J. Edwards (shoulder) joined him in participating. With the Bears not adding much to their pass rush this offseason, they’ll be counting on a healthy Odeyingbo come September.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports EDGE Dayo Odeyingbo tore his Achilles and will miss the remainder of the 2025 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.analysis: Odeyingbo had just one sack this season, accomplished in Week 1, but had 21 tackles and four quarterback hits in his first year with the Bears after signing a big free-agent contract. The 26-year-old will probably be a candidate for the PUP list in training camp based on the timing of this injury. The Bears could conceivably get off his 2026 $20.5 million cap hit without much damage to their cap space. In year two of a three-year deal, the guess is that Odeyingbo will stick with the Bears this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.headline: Bears agreed to terms with Colts EDGE Dayo Odeyingbo on a three-year, $48 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.analysis: Odeyingbo had four sacks this past season, but 12 in 2023 when he took the jump to reliable pass rusher. Still entering his age-26 season, the Bears are likely forecasting some improvement here. He’ll step in across from Montez Sweat to give the Bears a pair of capable pass rushers at end. Odeyingbo had only started five games in his first three years with the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.headline: Colts second-round DE Dayo Odeyingbo (Achilles) expects to play this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.analysis: “The goal is to be back playing this year,” Odeyingbo said at this weekend’s rookie minicamp. “That’s what I’m working towards. I’m working hard to get back as fast as possible.” Odeyingbo tore his Achilles training for the Senior Bowl in January. He’s targeting an October return, but the Colts are likely to move him slowly. Odeyingbo is a candidate to open the season on the reserve/PUP list, sidelining him for at least the first six games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.headline: Colts signed No. 21 overall pick DE Kwity Paye to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.analysis: Second-round DE Dayo Odeyingbo, fifth-round S Shawn Davis, seventh-round WR Mike Strachan and seventh-round OG Will Fries have also signed their rookie pacts. As is the case with all first-rounders, Paye’s deal includes a fifth-year team option for 2025. If exercised, fifth-year options are now fully guaranteed. Paye (6'4/272) is a former high school running back who was a member of Bruce Feldman’s “Freak-List.” Paye has a thick frame that channels tremendous power into his bull rush. Vicious hands and natural athleticism help him shoot gaps on run plays. He’s difficult to dislodge once his base is established and will chase down plays from behind. He put on a show at his pro day workout, running a 4.52 40-yard dash, posting a 35 ½” vertical, 33” arms and a Herculean 36 bench reps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.headline: Colts selected Vanderbilt DE Dayo Odeyingbo with the No. 54 overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.analysis: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Odeyingbo, who injured his Achilles in preparation for the Senior Bowl, will be ready in September or October. Odeyingbo joins his older brother, Bengals IDL Dare, as Vanderbilt defensive linemen to make the jump to the NFL. The four-star prospect accrued 126 tackles, 12 sacks, 85 pressures, and 71 stops over his four year career. He was named second team All-SEC in 2020 and departs as the fifth leading player in Vandy history with 31 tackles for loss. He’s capable of challenging on the outside with a varied toolbox of pass rushing moves, or bulldozing his way through the B-gap. He fits the basketball-player-still-transitioning-to-the-gridiron mold and suffers from the usual array of developmental obstacles to climb. The Colts hope Odeyingbo can improve their pass rush, which was graded by PFF as the 13th worst in the NFL last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.headline: Vanderbilt senior DE Dayo Odeyingbo has opted out of the team’s final two games in order to begin preparing for the 2021 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.analysis: Odeyingbo (6'6/280) was one of the few bright spots for the Commodores this season, as the team remains winless with an 0-8 record. The senior defensive end, who has already accepted an invitation to play in the Reese’s Senior Bowl, has accounted for 3.5 sacks this season. Odeyingbo has been given a second-round grade by Pro Football Network draft analyst Tony Pauline, so playing on a bad team does not appear to have hurt his draft prospects.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.headline: Vanderbilt senior DE Dayo Odeyingbo has accepted an invite to the 2021 Reese’s Senior Bowl.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dayo-odeyi.analysis: The Vandy program does not have a whole lot to look forward to right now, but at least they will be sending a player to the Senior Bowl. Odeyingbo is a huge 6-foot-6, 280-pound defense end. His long, well-built frame makes him a perfect candidate as a strong-side defensive end who may be able to even kick inside on passing downs. So far in 2020, he has already reached his career-high 3.5 sacks. Odeyingbo is more of a run defender, though, as evidenced by his frame and 17 tackles for loss over the past two seasons. Odeyingbo is considered a UDFA right now, but a good showing down in Mobile could change things.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Talanoa Hufanga is expected to miss “about 2-3 weeks” with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: The former second-team All-Pro safety left last week’s game against the Chargers with the injury. Hufanga has been one of the biggest havoc creators in the league this year with one forced fumble and two interceptions, one of which was returned for a touchdown. His absence will be a big blow to the Broncos’ defense, which is already without Patrick Surtain II, Jonathon Cooper, and potentially Riley Moss for their Week 6 matchup against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Broncos CB Riley Moss (ribs) was listed as a limited practice participant on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Moss was ruled out of Week 5 against the Chargers but has a chance to play Week 6 against the Seahawks with back-to-back limited practice listings. Meanwhile, S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) was a DNP for the second straight day. With Patrick Surtain (ankle) still out in the short term, the Broncos’ banged-up secondary may have a tough time against Jaxon Smith-Njigba and company on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) did not practice on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: It was an estimated session, but one that probably bodes pretty prescient since Hufanga left Week 5’s game with the ankle injury and was ruled out. Riley Moss (ribs) was listed as limited and would appear to have a chance to come back after being ruled out for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: NFL Insider James Palmer reports Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga is “100% healthy and moving well.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Palmer dropped some quick-hitting notes on Monday’s camp practice, singling out Hufanga as fully healthy. Hufanga agreed to a three-year contract with the Broncos this offseason after coming off consecutive season-ending injuries in 2023 and 2024, the former of which was a torn ACL and the latter being a torn ligament in his wrist. He’ll look to regain his high-level play with the Broncos after earning first-team All-Pro honors in his last fully healthy season in 2022 while with the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Broncos agreed to terms with S Talanoa Hufanga, formerly of the 49ers, on a three-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: The deal is worth up to $45 million. Hufanga was a rising star coming out of his second NFL season. He started all 17 games in 2022 and totaled two sacks, nine pass breakups, and four interceptions, one of which was returned for a touchdown. Hufanga then tore his ACL 10 games into the 2023 season. His recovery lasted into the following season and he also missed time with a wrist injury, limiting him to just seven appearances. With a clean bill of health heading into 2025, Hufanga will look to get back on track as part of a Denver defense that ranked third in points allowed last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: 49ers activated S Talanoa Hufanga (wrist) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Hufanga bolsters an already sharp secondary, although the absence of DE Nick Bosa could place additional strain on the second level with a lessened ability to generate organic pressure up front. Expect Hufanga to step back into his starting safety role after missing all but two games this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: 49ers placed S Talanoa Hufanga on injured reserve with a wrist injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: This is a brutal two-year stretch for the 2022 first-team All-Pro. Hufanga tore his ACL in 2023 and is now sidelined at least four games due to the torn wrist ligament. The 49ers’ upcoming schedule consists of capable passing offenses, featuring the Seahawks, Chiefs, Cowboys and Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Talanoa Hufanga (wrist) tore ligaments in his wrist and will miss “a month or so.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: The team is still deciding whether to place Hufanga on injured reserve — we’d bet on that happening. Hufanga injured the wrist in the second quarter of Week 5’s game against the Cardinals. Rookie Malik Mustapha picked up most of Hufanga’s snaps and is line for more work going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: 49ers S Talanoa Hufanga suffered a wrist injury in Week 5 against the Cardinals and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Hufanga exited in the second quarter and went to the locker room shortly after leaving the field. The 2022 All-Pro saw his 2023 season cut short by a torn ACL and made his 2024 debut in Week 3 against the Rams. We hope this isn’t another serious setback for a player who has battled all offseason to return to the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: 49ers declared S Talanoa Hufanga, QB Joshua Dobbs, CB Darrell Luter Jr., WR Ronnie Bell and OL Ben Bartch inactive for Week 4 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Hufanga is now out with an ankle injury, one week after making his 2024 debut following his 2023 ACL reconstruction. The 49ers will fortunately have Williams (illness, toe) protecting Brock Purdy’s blindside though. Deebo Samuel Sr. is active as well. He remains a high-ceiling WR1, though the 49ers could opt to rest him late in the game if they establish a comfortable lead, as expected.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said he had a “cool conversation” with Cam Ward.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward’s head, per Saleh, is in a “good place” ahead of the Titans’ Week 6 game against the Colts. Ward has been dreadful through five weeks, ranking 24th in EPA per drop back and 27th in drop back success rate. Only five quarterbacks have a lower adjusted yards per attempt than Ward this season. Daniel Jones and Tyson Bagent are the only QBs who average fewer fantasy points per drop back. Saleh has defended his second-year QB at every turn and does not seem close to benching him in favor of journeyman backup Mitchell Trubisky.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 23-of-36 passes for 170 scoreless yards and an interception in Tennessee’s Week 5, 26-3 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans led off the day with a 58-yard field-goal drive that fell apart from a red zone first-and-5. They would not even flirt with crossing 30 yards in a drive for the rest of the game and crossed into Texans territory on only 11 more snaps all game, including just one inside the Houston 40. Ward took four sacks and avoided several others by turning Tyjae Spears into a PPR hero. The closest he came to actually putting points on the board was a double-covered bomb to Carnell Tate’s general area. It was, well, what you would have expected from both sides in the preseason. Ward remains a last gasp supeflex QB2 heading into Week 6’s game against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 20-of-31 passes for 222 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Titans’ 24-18, Week 4 loss to the Ravens, adding four carries for 27 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward’s second pass of the game resulted in an interception, but he would settle in to put together his most productive outing of the season. Ward linked up with rookie first-rounder Carnell Tate on multiple long gains and ended the day with four completions of 20-plus yards. The two would connect on a 33-yard pass late in the fourth quarter on a fourth-and-10, and on the next play, Ward would find Wan’Dale Robinson for a three-yard score to cut the Ravens’ lead to 24-18. Ward did a good job at evading pressure in this one. Despite being pressured on 11 dropbacks, per PFF, only one of those resulted in a sack. Ward has been sacked just once over the last two weeks, but will have a tough challenge ahead of him next week when the Titans play host to the Texans. Ward projects as a low-end QB2 next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Titans pass catchers and the team’s defense are to blame for Cam Ward’s sloppy footwork.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Asked about Ward’s continuing footwork disaster, Saleh said the second-year quarterback “usually starts off good then fades into old habits.” Titans beat writer Terry McCormick then asked Saleh “why if his footwork gets worse as the game goes on, why the offense has had such slow starts. [Saleh] said it has been dropped passes vs. Giants and defense not getting off field vs. Eagles.” Saleh has made a point to shield Ward from all criticism throughout the preseason and through three horrific regular season outings. Ward ranks 20th in accuracy and 29th in EPA per drop back this season. He’s fresh off throwing a game-deciding end zone interception against the lowly Giants in Week 3. Mitchell Trubisky will probably get a couple starts this season if Ward can’t turn things around.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said “no” when asked if he’d consider sitting QB Cam Ward.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward’s gotten off to a slow start in 2026, completing 62.5 percent of his passes for a meager 504 yards and two touchdowns in three games. He has improved his sack rate quite a bit, cutting it from 9.2 percent in 2025 to 5.38 percent so far this year. The Titans backup is Mitch Trubisky. It is probably too soon to give up on Ward, but it doesn’t bode well for his future that Saleh is already being asked the question. Ward will be one of the bottom five quarterbacks in the Week 4 fantasy rankings against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 23-of-36 passes for 181 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Titans’ 7-12, week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans’ offense looked dead on arrival with 34 yards on their six first-half drives. They opened the game with four consecutive three-and-outs and didn’t get on the board until late in the fourth quarter, when Ward tossed a short touchdown to Wan’Dale Robinson. It looked like Ward was getting in rhythm late in the game, but he ended the contest with a ghastly interception directly into the hands of Jevon Holland, who was standing in the end zone waiting for the ball. Ward took care of the ball until the game-ending throw, but this was a one step forward, two steps back showing from the young passer. That has unfortunately been the case for the better part of the last three weeks. Ward is not on the fantasy radar for Week 4 against the Ravens, and his poor play is making all of the team’s fantasy options largely irrelevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 13-of-20 passes for 183 yards in the Titans’ 24-20, Week 2 loss to the Eagles, adding four rushes for seven yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward’s two scores on the ground doubled his previous career total, though he is now sitting on one passing touchdown through eight quarters. He is at least not turning the ball over, and has taken “just” five sacks. He has been so far unable to heat up his connections with offseason additions Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson, but he found Elic Ayomanor for two critical gains vs. Philly. Cutting out the negative plays was an absolutely essential first step for Ward, but he has yet to supplement them with big gains or consistent chain-moving. That included botching a Hail Mary in the fourth quarter this afternoon. Ward won’t be much of a superflex option for next week’s road date with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 19-of-32 passes for 140 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ 23-10, Week 1 loss to the Jets, adding four rushes for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward also took three sacks for 13 yards. His touchdown was a too little, too late 11-yard strike to Elic Ayomanor with the Titans trailing 23-3 at the 2:42 mark of the fourth quarter. As was the case down the stretch last season, Ward did a good job of avoiding turnovers, but he struggled to generate positive plays of any kind. He was besieged by pressure, but he just wasn’t making anything happen. That could come in time — there’s a new experienced play-caller in Brian Daboll and several new weapons in the skill corps — but this was a highly discouraging start to the year at home vs. a not-exactly-amazing Jets defense. It was certainly confirmation that Ward is on the outside looking in of top-24 status in superflex leagues for the time being. The Eagles are a rough Week 2 matchup, even if the Titans are at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll said the team’s downfield passing attack has to improve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Cam Ward’s preseason has been as bad or even worse than his rookie campaign. Ward in last week’s preseason game against Seattle completed eight of his 12 attempts for 69 yards. His average depth of target on completed passes this preseason sits at a meager 1.2 . Carnell Tate, meanwhile, has been targeted five times on his 23 preseason routes and does not have a reception to show for it. Daboll has been somewhat defensive this month when asked about Ward’s immense struggles after working on basic fundamentals with the second-year QB in the offseason. Ward, one of the most inaccurate passers in recent NFL history, is unlikely to support more than one fantasy-viable pass catcher in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans QB Cam Ward completed 8-of-12 passes for 69 yards in Sunday’s preseason game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward would have cleared 100 yards in the box score had TE Gunnar Helm not stepped out of bounds while hauling in a downfield pass during a scramble drill. Ward’s ability to make ridiculous throws off-script remains a plus and a minus. It wasn’t a great game for his connection with rookie Carnell Tate. The duo went 0-of-2 out of five total pass attempts from Ward on the first drive this evening against Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: ArizonaCardinals.com’s Darren Urban believes Carson Beck won’t start in the “immediate future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Cardinals fans appear to be pining for the team to bench Jacoby Brissett and start the rookie in the coming weeks as another season circles the drain for Arizona. Beck so far has been the Cards’ emergency third quarterback. Urban said there remains a “chance Beck is made the backup this week or next and allow him to come on in relief if the situation presents itself. I don’t see Beck starting in the immediate future, but it does feel his time grows closer, and if the offense continues to sputter, that would be understandable.” Brissett this season ranks 15th in passing yards. He’s thrown nine touchdowns to five interceptions and ranks 30th out of 37 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt. He won’t be a viable fantasy play this week against a tough Rams coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals declared QB Carson Beck, S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson, OL Josh Fryar, DL Andrew Billings, and WR Reggie Virgil inactive for Week 3 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck continues to be the Cardinals’ third quarterback and will be a gameday inactive for Week 3 behind Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew. Dadrion “Rabbit” Taylor-Demerson (back) was scratched on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Team reporter Darren Urban reports that Cardinals QB Carson Beck (ribs) is unlikely to play in Friday’s preseason game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: This is unfortunate. Beck looked great before injuring his ribs in the Hall of Fame game. Per Urban, Beck has been a very limited participant in practice ever since, which is costing him valuable reps. Only starting QB Jacoby Brissett will take first-team practice reps once the regular season begins. Beck practiced the week after the injury, “struggling much of the time,” and has sat out since then. The Cardinals have an extremely difficult schedule, so a rough record could bring Beck back onto the field at some point this year. Ideally, he would have spent all of August refining his play, though. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team re-draft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said QB Carson Beck (rib) is unlikely to play in Saturday’s preseason game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck is scheduled to resume throwing after practice today, though, so the Cardinals’ rookie is indeed on the mend. Beck looked good in his prior preseason action. Hopefully, he has a chance to return in time for his team’s final preseason game against the Packers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur said he has ‘no concern’ over the rib injury that sidelined Carson Beck in Thursday’s preseason game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: LaFleur said Beck would have been well enough to throw if it were seven-on-seven drills, adding that the team “didn’t want to risk it” when it came to starting the rookie in Thursday’s preseason game. Beck already has some preseason experience under his belt. He threw for 188 yards and a touchdown in the Hall of Fame Game last week against the Panthers and will hopefully have a chance to suit up in next week’s preseason game against the Cowboys on Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals ruled out QB Carson Beck (rib) for the team’s preseason Week 1 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Beck suffered a rib injury in the Cardinals’ Hall of Fame game against the Panthers. Despite feeling “soreness,” he managed to practice this week. The Cardinals “decided to keep him out tonight as a precaution and to allow more time to heal.” This pours a little cold water on Beck’s moderate hype, but the reporting suggests that the injury is not overly concerning. Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett will start, and presumably be relieved by QB Kedon Slovis at some point. No word yet on QB Gardner Minshew’s potential involvement tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals QB Carson Beck completed 15-of-19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown in Thursday’s Hall-of-Fame Game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck played two-plus quarters. No offense to the Hall-of-Fame Game, but it’s not a contest we typically go into expecting highlights. The Cardinals’ No. 3 quarterback provided several of them, hitting Jalen Brooks for a 49-yard deep strike and Simi Fehoko for a five-yard end zone fade touchdown. In between were several smart in-rhythm completions, with Beck navigating the pocket well. 24-year-old Beck’s arm strength remains a massive question mark — even his Brooks completion drifted a bit toward the middle of the field — but his processing was on point against the Panthers’ second- and third-team defense. Although he was a highly polarizing pre-draft prospect, the fact that the rebuilding Cardinals were willing to use a Day 2 selection strongly suggests he will make late-season starts as the organization keeps an eye on the future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals announced QB Carson Beck will start Thursday’s Hall of Fame game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: It will be our first glimpse of Beck in an NFL uniform. Given the draft cost they paid for Beck, the 65th overall pick, it would behoove the Cardinals for him to be clearly better than everyone else out on the field Thursday and establish some sort of momentum to eventually get a starting role by the end of the season. We’ll see.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Cardinals and QB Jacoby Brissett “reached agreement today on a reworked contract.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Brissett was scheduled to make up to $4.88 this year, in the final year of his old deal. His new contract increases his compensation for this season, but he is still scheduled to hit free agency next offseason. The new deal includes a $15.5 million base salary. He can make up to $21 million via incentives. Things can always change in-season, but this appears to be clear-cut starter money — and it’s good news for Cardinals pass catchers. Although the Cardinals struggled to win games with Brissett under center last year, he was a very productive passer. Theoretically, he should be able to support TE Trey McBride and likely one of WR Marvin Harrison Jr. or WR Michael Wilson reliably. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur confirmed that the plan is for Brissett to start in Week 1 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals signed third-round rookie Carson Beck to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: The first pick of the third round, Beck’s deal is worth roughly $7.4 million over four years. Jacoby Brissett is also gunning for a new contract, though he is looking for a raise on his current salary and more guarantees. Brissett is penciled in as the Week 1 starter and is not even a highly paid backup. The two sides should come to an agreement soon, though the deal won’t guarantee Brissett a full season as the starter. If things don’t go well for Arizona this year, they will almost certainly take a look at Beck near the end of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.headline: Hearing officer James Thrash upheld 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw’s one-game suspension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.analysis: Greenlaw was suspended after he was ejected for headbutting Seahawks LB Ernest Jones during a sideline scuffle in the 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks. He appealed the suspension, but it has been upheld by hearing officer James Thrash. Greenlaw will miss Week 6 and is in line to return against the Falcons in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.headline: 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw has been suspended for one game after being ejected from Week 5’s game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.analysis: This was the exact outcome we expected after Greenlaw was ejected from Sunday’s game for headbutting Seahawks LB Ernest Jones on the sideline during a scuffle. Greenlaw, who was wearing a helmet, hit a helmet-less Jones and was immediately ejected and will now be suspended for one game without pay. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Greenlaw will appeal his suspension, but for now, he will miss Week 6’s game against the Commanders and be in line to return in Week 7 when the Niners visit the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.headline: Dre Greenlaw was ejected in the second quarter of the 49ers Week 5 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.analysis: A hit on Sam Darnold as he was scrambling toward the sidelines sparked a sideline scuffle between the Niners and Seahawks. In the middle of that scuffle were Greenlaw and Seahawks LB Ernest Jones. Jones, who was not wearing a helmet, was head-butted by Greenlaw, which immediately resulted in his ejection. This will certainly result in a hefty fine for Greenlaw, who could also be in danger of facing a suspension after the league has a chance to review the incident. Greenlaw has totaled 37 tackles and a forced fumble in the five games he has appeared in this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Dre Greenlaw (quad) is expected to play in Week 4 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.analysis: The 49ers are already banged up on defense with Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams ruled out on Friday. Greenlaw was listed as questionable after getting in a single limited practice. He has 22 combined tackles, 11 defensive stops, and one pressure this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.headline: 49ers LT Trent Williams (stinger) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.analysis: The 49ers will have their stud left tackle active on Sunday. 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw (quad bruise) is questionable to play. 49ers EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) and DL Mykel Williams (knee) have both been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.headline: 49ers LT Trent Williams (stinger) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.analysis: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said earlier this week that Williams was expected to resume practicing today. The fact that he is on track is a good sign for his Week 4 availability. 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw (bruised quad) is still sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.headline: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Trent Williams (stinger) “should be good to go by Thursday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.analysis: The 49ers don’t play until Sunday, so we’re assuming Shanahan is referencing when we should first expect Williams to take the practice field this week. Williams suffered what was classified as a stinger in Week 3’s win over the Cardinals, but appears to have avoided any serious injury. Shanahan said the team plans to manage he and LB Dre Greenlaw (quad) throughout the week, and didn’t rule out either player playing in Week 4 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said the team is still gathering information on WR Mike Evans’ (ribs/oblique) injuries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.analysis: According to ESPN’s Nick Wagoner, “it was unclear exactly what happened to Evans.” He got hit hard in the sternum on a catch over the middle, but remained in the game for a few plays before needing help from the training staff to get off the field. Shanahan said the team couldn’t tell if Evans broke a rib or injured his oblique, but he believes those questions will be answered tomorrow, indicating Evans will likely undergo imaging. He entered the game with a hip injury. Wagoner adds that LT Trent Williams (stinger) and LB Dre Greenlaw’s (quad) injuries “seemed less severe” than Evans’ injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.headline: 49ers listed RB Christian McCaffrey, OT Trent Williams, LB Dre Greenlaw, and EDGE Nick Bosa as resting non-participants for Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.analysis: McCaffrey and Williams were listed as DNP simply for rest, while Bosa had a rest/knee designation and Greenlaw had a rest/Achilles designation. This is notable as the 49ers have several key veterans who have dealt with injuries throughout their career and practice reps will be managed for these players, especially coming off a Week 1 in Australia. McCaffrey reportedly dealt with cramps in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams; though he is not injured, his experiences with Achilles tendinitis will certainly lend to rest days throughout the season. We expect the 49ers to continue to rest veterans in practice throughout the season in an effort to remain healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.headline: 49ers signed LB Dre Greenlaw, formerly of the Broncos, to a one-year, $7.5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dre-greenl.analysis: Greenlaw played in just eight games with the Broncos last season, dealing with a quad injury, a hamstring injury and a one-game suspension. He totaled 25 solo tackles, five TFLs, one interception, two quarterback pressures and one sack despite the bumpy year. Prior to 2025, he spent his whole career playing for the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) won’t have his 21-day practice window opened this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett went on injured reserve after Week 1 and is therefore eligible to have his 21-day practice window for activation off IR opened this week. However, McVay said the 30-year-old pass-rusher won’t have his window opened, indicating Garrett is not ready to practice yet and it will still be some time before we see him back on the field. His initial timeline after undergoing a knee scope was roughly six weeks. It’s been four weeks so far, but Garrett could still hit the six-week return timeline if his practice window is opened next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Myles Garrett “was given a timeline of roughly six weeks for his recovery from knee surgery.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett attempted to play through the knee issue in Week 1 but was clearly bothered by the balky knee. He underwent a knee scope shortly after the Rams’ opener and was placed on injured reserve. It was initially expected to be closer to a four-week absence for the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. Now he’ll miss a bit longer than that, and Rapoport added that the team will be cautious with his return, so he could be sidelined beyond even the six-week timeline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said he doesn’t have a timeline for when Myles Garrett (knee) will return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett will miss at least four games after going on injured reserve. The All-Pro pass-rusher is set to undergo arthroscopic surgery on his knee after struggling to play through the injury in Week 1. Garrett’s absence is a massive blow to the Rams’ defense, but they should have enough players in place to get through what they hope is a short time away.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Myles Garrett will undergo arthroscopic surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: According to Pelissero, Garrett had been dealing with lower leg pain and “wasn’t himself” in Week 1 against the 49ers. Garrett was routinely taken off the field and failed to record a single stat in the contest. Per Pelissero, the team hopes he will miss only a minimum of four weeks while on injured reserve. The impending return of Aaron Donald should help ease the loss of Garrett, but this is undoubtedly a massive blow to the Rams’ defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett said his goal ahead of Week 2’s game against the Giants is to “get healthy.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Coming off an underwhelming debut in which he failed to even record a tackle in Week 1’s loss against the 49ers, Garrett said he was “the worst version” of himself in Thursday’s game. The star pass rusher was dealing with a knee injury in the days leading up to the game, but was ultimately removed from the injury report on Wednesday. Speaking after the game, he said his knee didn’t feel 100 percent, but Garrett still managed to play on 40 snaps, per PFF. Unfortunately, he generated only three pressures and failed to get a hit on the quarterback. Hopefully, some extended time off before next Monday’s game against the Giants will be enough for Garrett to get right in the Rams’ official 2026 home debut.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: As expected, Garrett gets in a full practice ahead of the Rams’ Week 1 Australia matchup against the 49ers. He did not practice Tuesday but it was likely a load management day for the star pass-rusher’s knee. Expect more of these kinds of practice weeks from Garrett moving forward; he is good to go for Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) did not participate in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett was a non-participant in practice Tuesday, but it looks to be a load management day with other Rams players listed as DNP due to rest and head coach Sean McVay saying Tuesday he expects Garrett to play Week 1. Though the team will be without Aaron Donald for opening day, the Rams are still expecting to have Garrett good to go against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Myles Garrett (knee) will be ready to go for Week 1’s game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Heavily load-managed in the offseason, Garrett will enter his age-31 season fresh and ready to try to top last year’s 23-sack season in a new defense. We won’t be surprised if Garrett continues to be listed on the injury report going forward, but if he’s going to play through this there’s probably no need to be concerned about the report unless new concerns arise.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that Rams EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) and DT Aaron Donald will practice today.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett, 30, has been sidelined by swelling in his knee since late July. His return to practice puts him on track to play in Week 1 against the 49ers on Thursday. Donald’s status is tougher to decipher. The fact that he is practicing is a great sign, but the Rams could still slow-play his return to action. Rams coach Sean McVay said he will provide an update on their Week 1 statuses on Tuesday. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) did not participate in Monday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett continues to not practice while experiencing swelling in his knee. It sounds like this is more maintenance than anything else, as the Rams want the start pass-rusher to be ready to roll and at his best for the opener against the 49ers next week in Australia. Still, it’s something to keep an eye on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.headline: Chargers signed QB Jake Browning to the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.analysis: With Trey Lance hitting injured reserve, the Chargers worked out multiple quarterbacks Tuesday, eventually signing Browning. A former backup to Joe Burrow, Browning lost the Buccaneers’ backup job to Jalon Daniels this offseason. He now joins a Chargers team keen on adding some depth behind Justin Herbert with Lance out and DJ Uiagalelei on the 53-man roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.headline: Chargers worked out free agent WR JuJu Smith-Schuster on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.analysis: Smith-Schuster is touring wide receiver-needy teams, working out with the Chargers Monday after visiting the Vikings on Monday. Several other names also worked out for the Chargers, including former 49ers WR Ronnie Bell and quarterbacks Kyle Trask and Jake Browning. With Trey Lance on injured reserve and several Chargers receivers dealing with injuries, the Chargers are looking for reinforcements.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.headline: Buccaneers released QB Jake Browning.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.analysis: Jalon Daniels won the backup job in Tampa Bay. Browning was pretty unimpressive in 2025 and didn’t win a job over a rookie UDFA — it may not be easy for him to find a roster spot elsewhere.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.headline: Buccaneers signed QB Jake Browning, formerly of the Bengals, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.analysis: It’s easy to say “why?” and harder to say “why?” when the current backup quarterback on Tampa’s roster is 2025 UDFA Connor Bazelak. Browning has at least thrown well in NFL games before and is only entering his age-30 season. What he did last year wasn’t good enough, of course, but he’ll compete to hold the clipboard for the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Bengals will not tender restricted free agent QB Jake Browning.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.analysis: Browning split his first five years in the NFL between the Vikings and Bengals’ practice squads. He finally won the backup job in Cincy in 2023 and went on to throw for 1,936 yards, 12 touchdowns, and seven interceptions while making seven starts in place of an injured Joe Burrow. He signed a two-year deal with the Bengals after the season. Browning took over as the starter in 2025 after Burrow went down with a foot injury. Things did not go as smoothly this time around and he was eventually benched for Joe Flacco, whom the Bengals had to acquire via trade. Though the Bengals threw in the towel on Browning, another team will see his 2023 tape and give him a shot to win their QB2 job in camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.headline: Bengals declared QB Jake Browning, WR Charlie Jones, CB Josh Newton, S Daijahn Anthony, DE Joseph Ossai, TE Cam Grandy, and DT Jordan Jefferson inactive for Week 18 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.analysis: Browning took over for an injured Joe Burrow early in the year but was an utter disaster.
