The Bengals eventually had enough and traded for Joe Flacco, who remained the starter until Burrow returned from his turf toe injury. Browning is a restricted free agent at the end of the year, meaning the Bengals could keep him around on a team-friendly deal if they want to give him another shot at the QB2 gig.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.headline: Joe Flacco (shoulder) is active for Week 9 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.analysis: Flacco had been listed as questionable to face the Bears after sustaining a shoulder injury last week against the Jets. He’ll play through the injury against a soft Chicago defense, but presents a very real in-game injury risk. The fantasy prospects of every Bengals player rely on Flacco being under center for the pass-heavy Cincinnati offense. Bengals declared CB Marco Wilson, LB Logan Wilson, OL Dalton Risner, WR Jermaine Burton, TE Cam Grandy, and DE Trey Hendrickson (hip) inactive against Chicago. With Hendrickson out, the Bengals defense presents an even better matchup for Caleb Williams and the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.headline: Bengals QB Joe Flacco (shoulder) is questionable for Cincinnati’s Week 9 game against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.analysis: Flacco has talked a good game the last few days, leading us to believe the Bengals’ quarterback is on the optimistic side of questionable. But the Bengals also signed Sean Clifford to their active roster, leaving us to believe there’s still some question on if Flacco will indeed be ready to go. If Flacco is declared out, starting duties would likely fall to Jake Browning again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.headline: Joe Flacco (shoulder) said he is feeling good ahead of Week 9’s matchup against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.analysis: Flacco didn’t say if he expected to play in Sunday’s game, but that was clearly the vibe the veteran signal-caller was giving off on Friday when speaking with the media. Flacco and the Bengals plan to test his shoulder before ultimately deciding on his availability, but it sounds like he should be good to go in a plus matchup against the Bears barring any setbacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Joe Flacco’s (shoulder) Week 9 status is “up in the air.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-brown.analysis: Flacco is dealing with an AC joint sprain, per Rapoport. He sustained the injury late in the Bengals’ Week 8 loss against the Jets and could miss this week’s game against the Bears. That would force Jake Browning back under center for the Bengals, a huge hit to the fantasy prospects of every Cincy pass catcher, including Ja’Marr Chase. Fantasy managers should keep a close eye on Flacco’s Thursday and Friday practice status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.headline: Chargers worked out free agent WR JuJu Smith-Schuster on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.analysis: Smith-Schuster is touring wide receiver-needy teams, working out with the Chargers Monday after visiting the Vikings on Monday. Several other names also worked out for the Chargers, including former 49ers WR Ronnie Bell and quarterbacks Kyle Trask and Jake Browning. With Trey Lance on injured reserve and several Chargers receivers dealing with injuries, the Chargers are looking for reinforcements.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.headline: Vikings worked out WR JuJu Smith-Schuster on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.analysis: Smith-Schuster was released by the Giants in training camp, and last worked out for the Jets in September. The 29-year-old receiver caught 33 passes for 345 yards and one touchdown last season, but wouldn’t be anything more than a depth signing if he were to sign with the Vikings or another team this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.headline: Jets signed WR Tyler Johnson to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.analysis: They also tried out JuJu Smith-Schuster. The Jets clearly have some concern about Omar Cooper Jr.'s short-term prospects.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.headline: Giants released WR JuJu Smith-Schuster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.analysis: He wasn’t healthy for much of training camp and apparently wasn’t needed to help further teach the Matt Nagy offense to the Giants. Smith-Schuster is just veteran depth at this point of his career, he’ll try to catch on elsewhere before the season starts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.headline: Giants signed WR JuJu Smith-Schuster, formerly of the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.analysis: It’s been a busy Monday for the Giants, who have now added three receivers to the roster with the signing of Smith-Schuster. The 29-year-old pass-catcher has spent the last two seasons with the Chiefs as a role player, catching 51 passes for 576 yards and three touchdowns over that span. The receiver-needy Giants also added Braxton Berrios and Odell Beckham Jr. to give them what is quickly becoming one of the older wide receiver rooms in the league. Much like the other two players signed before him, there’s little reason to believe Smith-Schuster will make any sort of meaningful fantasy impact in 2026, if he makes the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports free agent WR Odell Beckham Jr. will work out for the Giants on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.analysis: The drumbeat continues to grow louder for an OBJ/Giants reunion. The star receiver was recently spotted at Brian Burns charity softball game over the weekend, and has remained in constant contact with the team this offseason. At 33 years old, it’s hard to imagine OBJ offering much upside in reality and in fantasy land. Beckham didn’t play in 2025 and had a forgettable 2024 season with the Dolphins, catching nine passes for 55 scoreless yards. In addition to Beckham, the Giants are also working out JuJu Smith-Schuster, Braxton Berrios, and Anthony Miller on Monday. Smith-Schuster caught 33 passes for 345 yards and one touchdown last season with the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.headline: JuJu Smith-Schuster caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 18 loss against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.analysis: The veteran had more than three receptions in just three games this season, totaling 34 catches for 334 yards and two a touchdown. Smith-Schuster operated mostly as a rotational receiver and an intermediate outlet for Patrick Mahomes. The 29-year-old wideout, with 51 catches over the past two seasons, will probably be with another team in 2026. He’s an unrestricted free agent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.headline: JuJu Smith-Schuster caught all three of his targets for 16 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 17 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.analysis: JuJu, Xavier Worthy, and Hollywood Brown all saw exactly three targets with Rashee Rice sidelined this week. Smith-Schuster somehow led the trio in catches and yards. He isn’t a fantasy option in his own right, but JuJu is preventing any other wideout from stepping up as the team’s No. 1 receiver. Fantasy managers can ignore all three players for their Week 18 showdown with Las Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.headline: Chiefs WR JuJu Smith-Schuster (knee) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.analysis: Smith-Schuster is barely on the FLEX radar, now thoroughly past his prime. He has totaled five targets in 3-of-4 games thus far, though, so losing him to an injury could hurt Patrick Mahomes’ scoring ability a tad. Fortunately, that will not be an issue here. Smith-Schuster should be good to go for Week 5 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.headline: JuJu Smith-Schuster caught 4-of-6 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 4 win against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juju-smith.analysis: Smith-Schuster logged a route on 37 of Patrick Mahomes’ 44 dropbacks and caught one of Mahomes’ four touchdowns in the easy win over a beat-up Baltimore defense. Smith-Schuster caught his touchdown — the first of his 2025 season — between two defenders from four yards out. An every-down player in the pass-heavy KC offense, Smith-Schuster — with 14 catches through Week 4 — should be rostered in deep fantasy leagues. He gets the Jaguars in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans S Jalen Pitre is week-to-week with an AC joint sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: Pitre suffered a left shoulder injury in Week 5, now revealed to be an AC joint sprain. The good news is he won’t require surgery or go on injured reserve, but the 27-year-old is considered “week-to-week.” Given the designation, Pitre seems unlikely to play Week 6 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed C.J. Stroud (concussion) cleared protocol and will start against the Colts on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: Jalen Pitre, too, cleared protocol and will take on the current AFC South leaders. Stroud will be on the QB2 line after a long layoff, but has done reasonably well against the Colts over his two NFL seasons to date. Indianapolis’ defense, while improved with the return of Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner, isn’t a bad matchup from a fantasy perspective.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans said C.J. Stroud’s (concussion) status for Week 12 against the Bills is uncertain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: Something similar was reported on Sunday morning, but speaking on Monday, Ryans confirmed that Stroud may not return this week. The Texans’ QB1 remains in the league’s concussion protocol, but the Texans playing on Thursday night only adds to the complications. Stroud has missed two straight games due to his concussion, but the Texans have managed to go 2-0 in his absence with Davis Mills under center. Mills has thrown for 566 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in his two starts this season, but shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a desperation play in 2QB/superflex leads if he draws the start. Ryans said S Jalen Pitre, who is also in the concussion protocol, is uncertain for Thursday night’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans EDGE Will Anderson (quad) is not on Houston’s final Week 10 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: He will be around to harass Trevor Lawrence on Sunday. Jalen Pitre (concussion) was ruled out, giving some extra space for Parker Washington to move around in the slot against Houston’s backup cornerbacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans signed CB/S Jalen Pitre to a three-year, $39 million extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports the deal has $29.156 million in guarantees. Pitre missed the back half of last season with a pectoral tear, but excelled in his new role as Texans nickel corner with a career-best 71.3 PFF coverage grade. This isn’t a needle-moving re-signing, but clearly Houston valued their slot corner highly to get this done ahead of the draft. Pitre was set to enter the final year of his rookie contract in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports Texans S Jalen Pitre (pectoral) will undergo season-ending surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: Pitre reportedly suffered a partially torn pectoral muscle and will undergo a repair that will sideline him for the remainder of the year. Pitre is technically a safety but primarily functions as the Texans’ slot DB, which is notable for fantasy purposes. Pitre finishes with a team-high 31 coverage tackles and six passes defended.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans DB Jalen Pitre (pectoral) is expected to miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: He partially tore the pec in Week 12’s loss against the Titans. His absence put Eric Murray on to the field as a deep safety and Jimmie Ward moved up to be the main nickel for Houston. Ward caught a pick-six in Pitre’s absence, so perhaps the drop-off won’t be stark, but Murray has never been a great defender. Pitre had been having the best season of his career with a 79.5 PFF run grade in 660 defensive snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Jalen Pitre (shoulder) left Houston’s Week 12 game against the Titans and was ruled out.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: Pitre initially was ruled questionable. He left in the second quarter without his helmet and was not spotted on the sidelines at the beginning of the second half. The Texans moved Jimmie Ward into the nickel safety spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans S Jalen Pitre (chest) officially returned to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: Pitre suffered a bruised lung in the Texans’ Week 1 game against the Ravens and has been out since. With CB Derek Stingley out, the Texans secondary is going to need Pitre back to boost the defense. A limited practice is good news for his Week 4 return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.headline: Texans beat writer Aaron Wilson says S Jalen Pitre is expected to return to practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-pitr.analysis: Pitre suffered a bruised lung in Week 1’s loss to the Ravens and has been sidelined ever since. The former second-round pick’s return will be a welcomed one by a Texans defense that ranks 21st in points allowed, but 16th in total yards allowed. We’ll see how Pitre fares in practice throughout the week, but it sounds like there’s a good chance he’ll play in Week 4 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: Saints owner Gayle Benson said in a speech that the team’s 1-4 record “is not acceptable to me.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: It appears that Kellen Moore and GM Mickey Loomis are on the hot seat after a surprisingly bad start and a no-show on the 20th anniversary of the return to the dome. We’d be a little surprised if Moore were fired in only the second year of his tenure, without even being given a chance to pick his own franchise quarterback. But most ownership groups would not say something like this out loud, so it’s worth noting.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore plans to call plays for the offense this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: This was expected to be the case, but Moore confirmed it at his introductory press conference on Thursday. The first-time head coach made a name for himself as an offensive play-caller and is fresh off leading the Eagles’ offense to 33 points in the team’s Super Bowl win over the Chiefs. Moore and the Eagles leaned heavily into the ground game last season, but during his 2023 campaign with the Chargers and his four-year run with the Cowboys (2019-2022), his offenses were ranked in the top-15 in early-down pass rate. How Moore decides to run his offense with the Saints could depend on how their off-season goes. While Alvin Kamara isn’t getting any younger, it’s hard to imagine any coach trusting Derek Carr to lead a high-volume passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Eagles quarterbacks coach Doug Nussmeier is a “strong candidate to have a big role” on the New Orleans offensive staff under Kellen Moore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: “Perhaps offensive coordinator,” Rapoport adds. Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni has made some noise about blocking assistants from leaving today but with an elevation, he’d have no way to block Nussmeier moving to the Saints. Nussmeier has been Moore’s quarterbacks coach with the Cowboys, Chargers, and Eagles. He has not been a candidate for any prominent external jobs that we’ve written about since interviewing for the Ravens offensive coordinator gig in 2023.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports 49ers assistant head coach Brandon Staley is a “leading candidate” to become Saints defensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: New Saints head coach Kellen Moore reportedly has strong interest in bringing in Staley as the team’s defensive coordinator. Staley flamed out as Chargers head coach after three seasons, going 24-24 and heading one of the NFL’s worst defenses. Staley spent the 2024 season as an assistant to Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan. As head of the Saints defense, Staley would take over a unit that last year ranked 19th in EPA allowed and 18th in offensive success rate allowed. The Saints pressured the passer at the 11th lowest rate in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: Saints hired Eagles offensive coordinator Kellen Moore as the team’s head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: Two days after Moore and the Eagles dominated the Chiefs in the Super Bowl, Moore, 36, gets his first crack at a head coaching gig. The Eagles reportedly expected Moore to be a short-term OC, especially if he had immediate success with Jalen Hurts and the Philly offense. He did just that in 2024: The Eagles were eighth in total yards and seventh in points, ranking sixth in EPA per play and first in rush EPA thanks to Saquon Barkley’s massive campaign. In New Orleans, Moore will have to figure out how to make it work with Derek Carr at the helm and an aging Alvin Kamara in the backfield. Moore’s ability to manipulate defenses and create space for his playmakers will be put to the test in 2025 and beyond.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: The Athletic’s Mike Silver “expects” Kellen Moore to have “strong interest” in Brandon Staley as a defensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: The Moore-Saints partnership is not actually, as an NFL national reporter would say, “officially official” yet. But all signs have been pointing that way for some time. Staley took on assistant head coach duties for the 49ers last year after washing out of Los Angeles in 2023. Given how poorly San Francisco’s defense played last year, he wouldn’t exactly be an inspiring defensiv coordinator hire for Moore. But Staley had a good track record on that side of the ball prior to 2023 and a Kliff Kingsbury-esque bounceback could definitely happen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: Speaking Sunday, Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie said “Unfortunately, we’re gonna have to wish (Kellen Moore) the very best with New Orleans.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: This comment came shortly after the team’s Super Bowl LIX victory over the Chiefs, when Lurie was asked if he expects the team to lose Moore to the Saints this week. Lurie simply responded with “I do” before proceeding to praise the coordinator who was fresh off leading the Eagles to their second championship in eight seasons. The ink has long felt dry on Moore’s contract with the Saints, even though nothing has been made official yet. We’d expect the official word to come down any day now, but Lurie’s recent comments are about as definite as it gets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter confirms Eagles OC Kellen Moore is expected to be named the Saints’ next head coach following Super Bowl LIX.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: The NFL’s worst kept secret keeps inching closer to becoming official. Moore’s hiring would be the Saints’ first leap outside the Sean Payton coaching tree in two decades, and would follow on the heels of an excellent “bounce-back campaign” for Moore after a trying 2023 with the Chargers. A methodical coaching riser who has overseen strong offenses most everywhere he’s been, Moore would address the Saints’ desperate need for fresh ideas when it comes to scoring points.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports the Saints plan to meet with Eagles OC Kellen Moore for their head coaching vacancy after the Super Bowl.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: Moore has already interviewed with the Saints twice. As Pelissero notes, a third meeting can’t happen until after the Super Bowl, hence the timing. The Super Bowl is also conveniently located in New Orleans, making an in-person visit a small ask for Moore. It’s been reported multiple times that Moore is the favorite to land the Saints opening. A third meeting all but confirms that. Dolphins DC Anthony Weaver and Giants OC Mike Kafka have both had multiple interviews with the Saints and are still in the mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Eagles OC Kellen Moore is in “a very strong position” with the Saints for their head coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: Moore interviewed with the Saints for a second time on Monday. He is still game-planning for the Super Bowl, so a potential hire would have to wait, but Rapoport reports Moore is in a strong position with the Saints. The Saints have also interviewed Dolphins DC Anthony Weaver and Giants OC Mike Kafka twice, while former Cowboys HC Mike McCarthy may still be in play. New Orleans is the last head coaching job available and Moore’s work with Dak Prescott when he was offensive coordinator with the Cowboys, along with his success with the Eagles this season, makes him a strong candidate to be a head coach.

https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.headline: Bears activated DL Shemar Turner (knee) off the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.analysis: Turner tore his ACL last October. He’ll likely work in a rotational role for the Bears early. The 23-year-old second-rounder will try to make up for lost time after spending all of camp and the first month of the season on the shelf.

https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.headline: Bears placed DB Kyler Gordon on the reserve/physically unable to perform list with a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.analysis: The Bears also placed LB Noah Sewell (Achilles) and DL Shemar Turner (knee) on the reserve/physically unable to perform list. All three players must miss at least four games to begin the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.headline: Bears coach Ben Johnson said DT Shemar Turner (knee) tore his ACL and will miss the remainder of the 2025 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.analysis: Turner ends his rookie year with six tackles, two TFLs, and a 34.4 PFF defensive grade. He was essentially being treated as a rotational player, maxing out at 23 snaps in Week 3. Depending on rehab, Turner may be ready for training camp in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.headline: Bears ruled out DT Shemar Turner (knee) for the remainder of Week 8’s game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.analysis: This looked like a minor injury when it first occurred. Turner went down in the first quarter, and was slow to get up before hobbling off the field under his own power. The rookie tackle, however, was later carted from the field and has now been ruled out for the game. The Bears drafted Turner in the second round of this year’s draft. He entered the day with six tackles and two TFLs in four games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.headline: Bears signed second-round pick OT Ozzy Trapilo to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.analysis: The Bears have now signed two of their three second-round picks, having kicked things off by signing DT Shemar Turner earlier today. Luther Burden remains the team’s only unsigned second-round pick. Trapilo will compete with incumbent OT Braxton Jones for the starting left tackle job. Jones has been recovering from ankle surgery and is expected to participate in the Bears’ training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.headline: Bears signed No. 62 overall pick DT Shemar Turner to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.analysis: The second-round rookies have largely been holding out as a group this year in search of fully guaranteed contracts. It’s unclear if Turner’s deal is fully guaranteed, but his signing, along with a few other contracts getting ironed out, should pave the way for more dominoes to fall. Chicago drafted Turner to be a versatile interior defender for their ascending defense. Turner totaled 10 sacks and three forced fumbles in four seasons at Texas A&M.

https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.headline: Bears selected Texas A&M DT Shemar Turner with the No. 62 overall pick of the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.analysis: Turner (6’3/290) served as a versatile chess piece who played all over the line, focusing mostly on edge for the first three years before moving to three tech in 2024. He was a major factor on the outside in 2023 creating 36 pressures, 6.0 sacks, a 15% pressure rate and an 80th percentile pass rush grade, earning Second Team All-SEC recognition. Turner suffered a stress fracture after bulking up for the move to defensive tackle, but played through it well enough to be graded positively on 24% of his run game snaps with 19 stops. His biggest issue was his tendency to abandon gap responsibilities and over run plays, leading to a sky-high 23.3% missed tackle rate and 31st percentile tackle grade. Somewhat undersized for an NFL three tech, Turner is at his best when parrying blockers’ hands to free himself up and pursue the play. A relentless competitor who prefers to slash his way into the backfield as opposed to bulldoze his way to it, Turner lacks the base necessary to defeat double teams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.headline: Texas A&M signed five-star 2021 DE Shemar Turner.
https://www.nbcsports.com/shemar-turner/.analysis: HC Jimbo Fisher keeps his house in order, staving off challenges from Alabama, Arizona State, Auburn, Florida, Georgia and a host of other prominent schools to land the DeSoto, TX native Turner (6'3/282). The five-star prospect is rated as the fourth best strong side defensive end and fifth overall recruit in Texas from the 2021 cycle. His impressive size means he could stay on the outside as a pass-rusher who can set the edge or move inside and beef up to the 300-pound range where his athleticism and sure-tackling ability would make him a nuisance. He faced elite competition in high school on a weekly basis and has the potential to become an all-conference caliber defensive lineman with early-round NFL potential down the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.headline: Dolphins claimed WR Jared Wayne off waivers from the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.analysis: The 26-year-old had four catches on 12 targets this year for the Texans as part of Nick Caley’s weird wideout platoon system. He’ll be tasked with watching Malik Willis throws land somewhere in his general vicinity for the next 11 weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.headline: Texans waived WR Jared Wayne.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.analysis: He had four catches on 12 targets and it felt worse than that. Wayne will likely resurface on the Texans practice squad upon clearing waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 2-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Houston’s Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.analysis: Boutte played 35-of-52 snaps, and if that sounds low, it actually lead the team in Nick Caley’s absolutely bizarre WR platoon situation where it seems like he is trying to find someone who he trusts. Boutte looks the best of the bunch, but we can’t recommend trying to eat these non-existent fantasy points. Jaylin Noel (2/17 on two targets) and Jared Wayne (1/20 on four targets including an inexcusable drop) continue to haunt the situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.headline: Jared Wayne caught 2-of-7 targets for 33 yards in Houston’s Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.analysis: Jaylin Noel outsnapped him 44-to-36 for the Texans No. 3 receiver role but Wayne beat Noel out by one catch, two yards, and two targets. “Man starts over again everyday, in spite of all he knows, against all he knows,” Emil Cioran once wrote. And these are the readings C.J. Stroud should get familiar with as he endures another week of this receiving corps in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Houston’s Week 1 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.analysis: Boutte managed just 36-of-79 snaps, third-most among Texans wideouts, as they ran weird platoons that had Jared Wayne, Jaylin Noel, and Xavier Hutchinson all on the field for at least 24 snaps. Until someone conclusively wins this job, or at least we start getting some juice that someone might win the job, it’ll be hard to start any of these receivers in fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.headline: Texans elevated WR Jared Wayne ahead of Week 1 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.analysis: Wayne’s standard elevation was expected following injuries to fellow wide receiver Christian Kirk and Braxton Berrios, leaving the team thin at the position. he could find himself active in the coming weeks as well pending the length of recovery for Kirk and Berrios.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.headline: Pitt wide receivers Jordan Allison and Jared Wayne have both been ruled out for Saturday’s game vs. Virginia Tech due to COVID-19 protocols.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.analysis: With Allison and Wayne both out, and Taysir Mack considered to be questionable due to injury, the Panthers will be shorthanded Saturday afternoon. DJ Turner and Shocky Jacques-Louis are among the wide receivers who are available to play, and they’ll be QB Kenny Pickett’s most trusted options in the passing game. In total at least eight players are out due to COVID-19 protocols alone.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.headline: Pitt wide receivers Jordan Addison (shoulder) and Jared Wayne (undisclosed) are taking part in warmups ahead of Saturday’s game at Boston College.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.analysis: The returns of Addison and Wayne will give the Panthers a welcome boost at the wide receiver position, with the former being able to play despite injuring his shoulder during last weekend’s loss to NC State. Addison, who’s only a freshman, has accounted for at least 55 yards and one touchdown reception in each of the Panthers’ last three games. Also taking part in pregame warmups is TE Kyi Wright, who will help fill the void left by the injured Lucas Krull.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.headline: Pitt sophomore WR Jared Wayne (undisclosed) is not playing today against NC State.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.analysis: Wayne (6'3/185) caught five passes for 59 yards and a touchdown in Pitt’s 21-10 victory over Syracuse two weeks ago, but did not record a reception in either of Pitt’s other two games as he battles nagging injuries. Taysir Mack should receive a full workload on the outside in Wayne’s absence and slot receiver Jordan Addison will likely see double-digit targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.headline: Pitt freshman WR Jared Wayne caught six passes for 100 yards in Saturday’s 26-19 loss to Boston College.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-wayn.analysis: Wayne (6'3/185) came into the contest having logged just 115 receiving yards on nine catches for the season. A nice effort, here. The freshman will see bowl action with the Panthers upcoming, after which he will look to take a developmental step forward this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Browns placed RB Raheim Sanders (hip) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: It’s unclear when he picked this injury up, but it does make the Audric Estime signing make some more sense. Sanders will miss at least four games. Assuming Quinshon Judkins (ankle) is good to go for Week 5, Jaleel McLaughlin and Estime will back him up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Quinshon Judkins is considered day-to-day with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: Monken was spotted in a walking boot after Sunday’s loss to the Jets, but Monken said his RB1 will have a chance to play in Week 6 against the Ravens. Judkins rushed 14 times for 44 yards last week and has a rushing line of 73-221-1 for the season, along with 18 receptions for 102 additional yards. Judkins’ practice status will be one to monitor throughout the week. If he’s not able to play, Raheim Sanders would likely handle the early-down work, with Jaleel McLaughlin mixing in as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Raheim Sanders rushed three times for 12 yards in the Browns’ Week 5 loss to the Jets, adding a one-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: Sanders also lost a few snaps to Jaleel McLaughlin. 4-5 touches have been Sanders’ weekly norm, but that could change for Week 6 against the Ravens after Quinshon Judkins was spotted with his right foot in a boot following today’s contest. There have not been any indications Judkins is dealing with something serious, but it’s a situation worth monitoring ahead of Tuesday evening’s waiver wire run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Browns signed RB Jaleel McLaughlin to their active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: He gets the elevation after the Browns place Dylan Sampson on injured reserve. McLaughlin and Raheim Sanders will be behind Quinshon Judkins in Week 2. McLaughlin’s career shows him as a more reliable pure runner than Sanders, but we’re unsure of how the split behind Judkins will go from here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Raheim Sanders rushed one time for one yard in the Browns’ Week 1 loss to the Jaguars, adding 3 receptions for 25 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: Sanders entered the game after Dylan Sampson (knee) was ruled out. The 24-year-old had a couple explosive kickoff returns, including a 74-yard return in the second half. He caught three passes filling the Brown’s receiving back role and showcased some burst by taking those receptions for 25 total yards. Sanders is an intriguing handcuff to pick up off waivers, pending Sampson’s status heading into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Browns RB Dylan Sampson (knee) is ruled out for Week 1 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: Sampson returned a kickoff and played on a third down play against the Jaguars before exiting in the first quarter. He left for the locker room with a knee injury and was promptly ruled out. Third-string running back Raheim Sanders will get more run with Sampson out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Raheim Sanders rushed five times for 26 yards in the Browns’ Week 18 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: Sanders signed with the Chargers after going undrafted in April. He didn’t make their final roster, but the Browns scooped him up and gave him some short-yardage work in Week 1 with Quinshon Judkins unavailable. He scored a short touchdown and didn’t touch the ball again until Week 16, after Judkins went down with a season-ending injury. Sanders split work with fellow rookie Dylan Sampson over the final three weeks of the year. Judkins is locked in as the high-volume runner in Cleveland and Sampson can be penciled in for most of the work on passing downs in 2026. That doesn’t leave much room for Sanders, but he has made progress toward earning a roster spot next year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Raheim Sanders rushed eight times for 21 yards in the Browns’ Week 17 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: Sanders drew the start in Sunday’s win over the Steelers, and handled six of his eight carries on the Browns’ first three possessions. His longest gain of the day came on a six-yard plunge on the first play of the game, and he also added a 10-yard reception in the fourth quarter. If Sanders finds himself in another split with Dylan Sampson next week, both backs will be hard to trust in Week 18 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Dylan Sampson (hand) is active for Week 17 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: With Sampson officially active, the rookie fourth-rounder has a chance to lead the Browns’ backfield with Quinshon Judkins (leg/ankle) sidelined. When Judkins was inactive for Week 1, Sampson stepped up to lead the Browns’ backfield with 20 total opportunities, and caught 8-of-8 targets for 64 yards. Playing in a rain-soaked Cleveland, Sampson should be a safe bet for double-digit touches and plenty of check downs from Shedeur Sanders, who has made a living off targeting his running backs this season. While Sampson is active, the Browns did declare QB Dillon Gabriel, CB Myles Harden, OL Kendrick Green, OT Jeremiah Byers, WR Jamari Thrash, TE David Njoku, and DT Sam Kamara inactive for Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.headline: Browns listed RB Dylan Sampson (hand) as questionable for Week 17 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/raheim-sanders.analysis: We still don’t know the specifics of Sampson’s hand injury that sidelined him for Weeks 15 and 16, but the rookie running back practiced every day this week and has a good chance of seeing a lead role for the Browns if he’s active. Sampson served as the Browns’ RB1 all the way back in Week 1, and wound up catching eight passes for 64 yards while adding another 12-29-0 on the ground. Sampson would have some appeal as an RB3/FLEX option if he’s available for this week’s fantasy championships. If Sampson is able to go, Raheim Sanders and Trayveon Williams would likely split backfield duties.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said James Cook needs to protect the ball or he’s going to get fewer carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: “At some point, there has to be consequences,” Brady said about his lead back, who has fumbled four times in five games this season, including twice on Monday night. Cook has played 67.3 percent of the team’s snaps, and this probably isn’t a threat to his lead back status, but it wouldn’t be surprising if he sat on the bench for a spell if he fumbled in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 25 times for 111 yards and two touchdowns in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams, adding seven yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook’s elite rushing line was overshadowed by two fumbles, the second of which was a lost fumble on the team’s first possession of overtime, placing the Rams in position to complete the comeback and steal away the victory. A blocked field goal on what would have been the game-winning kick breathed new life into the Bills, who demonstrated confidence in their lead back by throwing him right back out there on the following possession to eventually win the game. The 26 touches go down as a season high for the veteran back, who found paint for the fourth consecutive game in the thrilling overtime win. Cook remains a top-tier RB1 for fantasy purposes ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders in Las Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 12 times for 75 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: He added two catches for either yards. This game was never more than a one-score game, so it’s pretty shocking that Cook only had 14 touches. The Patriots did a good job containing him early in the game, apart from his touchdown run, but the Bills simply moved away from the running game too quickly. Cook was gaining huge chunk yards in the second half and should have been fed more carries during the game. With the Bills having their second straight mediocre offensive performance, you have to wonder if they will make it a point to lean on Cook more next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 24 times for 154 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook was the only running back to get a carry on the day, and he ripped off over six yards per rush. He got the Bills down inside the two-yard line twice but watched as Josh Allen ran it into the end zone each time. On the third trip deep into the red zone, Cook rushed it in from four yards out. With Ty Johnson back, Cook did cede some passing game work; however, Cook also played 42 of the team’s 62 snaps, compared to just 15 snaps for Johnson. The lack of receiving may prevent Cook from being a top-five running back, but he’s a clear RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions, adding four yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook jumped out to a scorching start on the ground, reaching the century mark in rushing before the half. Still, fantasy managers were left scratching their head as they watched Josh Allen account for three touchdowns from inside the five, two on the ground and one through the air. It wasn’t until a 22-yard carry that was down at the one late in the fourth quarter that the team rewarded Cook with a short-yardage touchdown, finally allowing fantasy managers their first taste of sweet touchdown copium from their first-round draft pick on the young season. Cook is likely to remain busy when the Bills host the Jets in Week 3, where he will remain a locked-in RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Bills “want to get that running game recharged” in Week 2 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Bills RB James Cook totaled 57 yards on just 13 rushing attempts last week, adding three catches for 12 yards. Per Fowler, the Bills plan to use him a lot more in primetime this evening. Cook can be treated as a locked-in RB1 in what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment on Thursday Night Football. The Bills notably elevated RB Frank Gore Jr. from the practice squad, which could indicate that RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) will be inactive tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 13 times for 57 yards in Buffalo’s Week 1 win over the Texans, adding three catches for 12 yards on four targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook had twenty yards on the game’s first drive, but the game eventually skewed pass-heavy for the Bills and Josh Allen had the game’s only two rushing touchdowns. Per PFF’s early charting data, Cook had 41 of the 57 snaps and almost all the work ahead of Ray Davis and Frank Gore Jr. Assuming Ty Johnson remains out on a short week against the Lions in Week 2, Cook will remain a touch-dominator on the RB1 line and will have a chance for a better touchdown runout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: Bills RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: It sure looks like the hamstring strain that Johnson suffered more than a month ago is going to keep him sidelined for the Bills’ season opener against the Texans. Starting RB James Cook was expected to play a larger role in the passing game this year. With Johnson sidelined, Cook could hog passing down snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: Bills RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) was not present during the portion of practice open to the media.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Johnson went down while running a route on August 9th. He resumed running roughly two weeks ago, but has not yet rejoined his teammates in drills. Although Johnson is not on the fantasy radar himself, he has hogged passing down snaps in recent seasons. Starting RB James Cook has been expected to take on a larger receiving role this season, and Johnson’s potential absence adds credence to that idea.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said the team will know more about RB Ty Johnson’s (leg) injury next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Johnson went down while running a route in practice on Saturday and immediately grabbed at the back of his right leg. He appeared to be grabbing at the lowest section of his hamstring, but both the back of his knee and the highest point of his calf are possible. Johnson logged a 65 percent third-down snap share and a 56 percent two-minute-drill snap share last season. Starting RB James Cook (19 percent and 31 percent) and fellow backup RB Ray Davis (16 percent and 13 percent) were also involved in both scenarios. If this is a serious injury that causes Johnson to miss time, it could meaningfully raise Cook’s fantasy-scoring ceiling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.headline: Patriots signed RB Hassan Haskins to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.analysis: It’s the second time he’s back; Haskins is a depth piece for the Patriots as they try to compensate for TreVeyon Henderson’s injury. Corey Kiner appears to be first up for a role behind Rhamondre Stevenson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is not present for the media-access portion of practice on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.analysis: The injury has sidelined Henderson since August 24. The Patriots face the Seahawks on Wednesday. At this point, Henderson must be considered questionable to play. Even if he were active, he would be slated for No. 2 duties behind starting RB Rhamondre Stevenson, and it is fair to wonder if the team would keep Henderson on a snap count. Reiss reported this morning that RB Lan Larison and/or RB Hassan Haskins would likely be elevated from the practice squad if Henderson cannot play, joining Stevenson and backup RB Corey Kiner on game day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.headline: Patriots signed Hassan Haskins, formerly of the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.analysis: Haskins appeared in a dozen games for the Chargers last year. He only saw 17 carries, which he turned into 45 yards, but did tally over 150 special teams snaps. That could ultimately be his path to a roster spot in New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.headline: Lions signed RB Raheem Blackshear.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.analysis: They also worked out Clyde Edwards-Helaire, Hassan Haskins and Kylin James and settled on Blackshear of the group. Blackshear has been a worthwhile return specialist and may have a chance to handle that role with the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.headline: Kimani Vidal rushed three times for 12 yards in the Chargers’ Week 18 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.analysis: Vidal also caught a screen pass on fourth down, but immediately received a hard hit from Broncos CB Pat Surtain, losing two yards on the play. Chargers RB Jaret Patterson led the backfield with eight rushes for 29 yards and caught 3-of-4 targets for eight yards. Fellow backup RB Hassan Haskins rushed once for three yards. Vidal should operate as RB Omarion Hampton’s primary backup next week against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.headline: Chargers RB Hassan Haskins (concussion) is active for Week 18 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.analysis: The Chargers have ruled out starting RB Omarion Hampton (ankle), among other impactful starters, as they prepare for the playoffs. Chargers No. 2 RB Kimani Vidal (neck) will likely get the start this week. While Haskins will rotate in, healthy RB Jaret Patterson will also be in play. It is a muddled situation against a tough Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.headline: Chargers RB Kimani Vidal (neck) is active for Week 18 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.analysis: Vidal injured his neck in Week 16 and was unable to play in Week 17. He practiced throughout Week 18, including two full sessions to close the week. Forecasting Vidal’s role is difficult, with the Chargers declaring QB Justin Herbert, S Derwin James Jr., RB Omarion Hampton (ankle), S Elijah Molden (hamstring), OLB Tuli Tuipulotu, OT Jamaree Salyer (hamstring) and C Bradley Bozeman (concussion) inactive for Week 18 against the Broncos. The team is clearly trying to preserve its health for the postseason and Vidal has meaningfully contributed to the offense this season. While we tentatively expect him to start, RB Hassan Haskins (concussion) and RB Jaret Patterson could also be regularly involved. Patterson is the backfield’s lone fully healthy player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.headline: Chargers RB Hassan Haskins (concussion) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 18 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.analysis: We’d be surprised if Haskins assumed a big role after suffering a concussion in Week 17. Kimani Vidal is likely to be the leader of the backfield in Week 18 for those of you searching for somebody to play in this game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.headline: Chargers RB Kimani Vidal (neck) practiced fully on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.analysis: Vidal could get the start this week with RB Omarion Hampton (ankle) sidelined by an ankle injury. The team could choose to preserve Vidal’s health for the postseason, though. Rotational RB Jaret Patterson is healthy and Hassan Haskins (concussion) remains limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.headline: Chargers RB Omarion Hampton (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hassan-has.analysis: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters earlier this week that getting his injured players healthy is his priority. With two absences to begin the week, Hampton seems unlikely to play this week. It is unclear whether rotational backup Jaret Patterson will get the start. Chargers No. 2 RB Kimani Vidal (neck) upgraded to full today while RB Hassan Haskins (concussion) remains limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.headline: The NFL suspended Bears EDGE Montez Sweat two games for violating the league’s Performance-Enhancing Substances Policy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.analysis: Assuming there’s not an appeal, Sweat will miss Week 6 and Week 7. Sweat has two sacks in five appearances so far this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.headline: The Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs reports that Bears LT Braxton Jones and EDGE Montez Sweat left practice early on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.analysis: Per Biggs, the Bears believe Jones did not suffer a “significant injury,” but it is unclear as to whether he will need time off. Reports on Sweat have been tougher to find. We do not yet know his status. Jones’ primary backup, OT Ozzy Trapilo, is expected to be sidelined “deep” into the season after rupturing a patellar tendon late last season. These injuries are worth watching.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.headline: Bears activated Montez Sweat from the active/NFI list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.analysis: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport called the issue a “short-term illness” when Sweat was first placed on the NFI list. It was indeed a short stay for Sweat, and he should be back at practice on Thursday. Sweat’s 10 sacks in 2025 were the second-best mark of his career. He nearly doubled his total from the previous season. He remains one of the biggest contributors on Chicago’s defense heading into his age-30 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.headline: Bears placed EDGE Montez Sweat on the active/NFI list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.analysis: Multiple reports have said that this won’t be a long stay. Sweat lead the team with 10 sacks last year. Assuming he is indeed activated soon, Sweat should have plenty of time to be ready for the start of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.headline: Bears EDGE Montez Sweat (ankle) is questionable for Week 11 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.analysis: Sweat missed Wednesday’s practice but returned on Thursday and was then upgraded to a full session before being listed as questionable. We fully expect him to play through the injury on Sunday. Sweat has 3.5 sacks, five TFLS, and a forced fumble this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.headline: Montez Sweat (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.analysis: Sweat dealt with an ankle injury in October before suffering a shin injury a few weeks later. Although the shin injury is now behind him, the team now lists him with an ankle issue. It is unclear as to whether this is a new injury or a continuation of the old one though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.headline: Bears EDGE Montez Sweat (shin) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.analysis: Kyler Gordon, who missed Week 9 with a hamstring issue, was also limited. Sweat bookended last week’s three practices with DNPs and was eventually made inactive on Sunday. A return to practice is a step in the right direction but doesn’t guarantee his availability for Week 10. The Bears were down multiple key defenders versus the Cardinals on Sunday and got rocked, giving up 29 points. It’s the first time Chicago has allowed more than 21 points in a game this season. Drake Maye’s fantasy outlook would receive a notable boost if Sweat or Gordon can’t play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.headline: Bears declared EDGE Montez Sweat (shin) inactive for Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.analysis: Sweat’s absence is significant for a Bears defense tasked with containing the highly mobile Kyler Murray. The secondary is also worryingly thin. S Jaquan Brisker, slot CB Kyler Gordon, DL Byron Cowart, RB Khalil Herbert, OL Kiran Amegadjie and OL Braxton Jones are also inactive for this one. Starting CB Tyrique Stevenson has also been demoted following his unfortunate Week 8 antics. He will not start this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.headline: Bears EDGE Montez Sweat (shin) is questionable for Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.analysis: Sweat missed Wednesday’s practice with the shin issue. He was upgraded to a limited session on Thursday but then returned to a DNP to close the week. That puts him on the wrong side of questionable heading into the weekend. Losing Sweat, who has 3.5 sacks and a forced fumble this year, would be a notable blow to Chicago’s top-notch pass-rush.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.headline: Bears EDGE Montez Sweat (shin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/montez-swe.analysis: The Bears held a walkthrough so Sweat’s status is only an estimation. We will learn more on Thursday’s injury report. Defensive backs Jaquan Brisker and Kyler Gordon, both of whom missed Week 8, were also held out of practice. A usually ironclad Bears defense could be down multiple starters for their Week 9 matchup with Arizona, giving Kyler Murray an easier matchup as he attempts to extend the Cardinals’ win streak to three.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Bengals OC Dan Pitcher said the team will “continually assess how that touch share between [Perine] and Chase Brown should play out.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Pitcher suggested that when they run the ball more from shotgun — as they did last week against the Dolphins — Perine’s a better fit for those kinds of plays. The Bengals spent a lot of time this offseason working on an under center run game to get Brown more explosives, but that has gone for naught early on in the season. We may indeed see more Perine in Cincinnati’s running game after they return from the bye week, lowering Brown into the RB2 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 13 times for 39 yards and a fumble in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins, adding 3 receptions for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown took a surprising backseat to Samaje Perine in the Bengals’ win over the Dolphins. He still out-snapped Perine 38-to-33, but a red zone fumble hurt his fantasy production while splitting backfield touches 50/50. There were a few snaps where Brown lined up as a receiver with Perine in the backfield; the Bengals used both backs heavily. Brown previously dominated all sorts of touches for the Bengals backfield, so this is a new development. Game script certainly played a factor but Brown’s ceiling as an RB1 may be considerably lessened if Perine’s usage sticks. He is a fantasy RB2 with a Week 7 matchup against the Ravens on the horizon after a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed nine times for 10 yards in the Bengals’ Week 4 loss to the Jaguars, adding 11 receptions for 71 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: It was a big pass-catching day for Brown, who saw 11-of-54 total Bengals targets on the day. After Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) exited, Brown and Tee Higgins saw massive upticks in usage. Brown saw 57 backfield snaps, catching a series of checkdowns and wheel routes despite just 10 rushing yards on the day. He worked ahead of Samaje Perine on passing downs, a good sign for his fantasy production moving forward. We don’t expect Brown to consistently see this many targets but a high backfield share gives him a consistent fantasy floor. Brown is a fringe RB1 for Week 5 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 13 times for 61 yards in the Bengals’ Week 3 loss to the Steelers, and two receptions for eight additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown was effective with the opportunities he received, but the Bengals did all of their damage through the air in this one, as Joe Burrow and the company aimed to keep pace with a surprisingly explosive Steelers offense. As far as the Bengals’ backfield is concerned, Brown continues to be the only game in town. He handled 71.4 percent of the Bengals’ running back opportunities in this one but has only one touchdown to show for his efforts this season. He’ll be a fringe RB1/RB2 in next week’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 20 times for 80 yards in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: He “added” three catches for two yards on five targets, getting absolutely exploded by Kamari Lassiter on one of them. He also had a 20-ish yard run called back for holding. Brown looked quick and able, but the Bengals ran just two plays inside the Texans red zone all game. He played on 42-of-60 snaps per PFF. Brown will be in the low-end RB1 ranks against the Steelers in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Bucs, adding five receptions for 22 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: It was neither an efficient nor prolific outing for the Bengals’ lead back, but he found the end zone and out-touched No. 2 Samaje Perine 21-8. It was a full “as expected” day in the Bengals’ backfield. Brown will remain in the RB10-14 range for Week 2 against the Texans. That’s a tough defensive matchup, albeit one the similarly offensive-minded Bills just handled with ease.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. said he “wouldn’t be surprised if the Bengals double last year’s” number of runs from under center on early downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Dehner has been covering the Bengals’ intent to increase the number of plays run from under center all summer. Last season, “the Bengals ran from under center 120 times on early downs. The league average was 210.” Per Dehner, it has become clear “over the weeks that the under-center offense would not be going away.” The Bengals are committed to changing their ways in pursuit of more explosive gains. Starting RB Chase Brown is a locked-in RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Bengals RB Chase Brown said coach Zac Taylor is calling “a lot” of play action and run plays from under center at training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Late in June, The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. reported that QB Joe Burrow had agreed to try out more under-center concepts in spring practices. The Bengals’ quarterback prefers to operate from shotgun, but the offense has struggled to generate explosive pass and run plays in recent seasons. Meanwhile, 2025 playoff teams notably thrived under center, prompting a potential schematic switch in Cincinnati this year. Dehner previously reported on Brown’s efficiency leaps when switching from shotgun to under center. Burrow and his wide receiver should, theoretically, receive an efficiency bump from the intended changes as well. This is exciting for fantasy football purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner, Jr. reports Chase Brown has been “at the center of unique twists” in the Bengals offense during training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown, according to Dehner, is “being used all over the formation,” similar to the way Ja’Marr Chase has been deployed in recent years. Brown lines up in the slot and runs a slant one play, then takes a jet sweep the next. He’s part of 20 personnel with two running backs, motions into the backfield, behind a fullback and almost any other spot imaginable.” The Bengals are preparing to use motion at a much higher rate than they have during the Joe Burrow era, especially when Burrow is under center. It’s led to some early camp struggles, per Dehner. “We all got to prepare a little bit more, at least I do, a lot for the motions and playing F and wherever they are putting me takes a little extra study time because I haven’t really done that before,” Brown said. “It’s cool they trust me doing that and believe in my skill set enough. It’s been fun.” Dehner said the team’s “pre-snap eye candy and under-center emphasis have helped establish a refreshed run game” ahead of the 2026 season. Brown’s pass game involvement should give him every chance to be a top-5 back in PPR formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. believes Chase Brown could be franchise-tagged in the 2027 offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown was reported to be discussing an extension with the Bengals in January, but nothing came of that. Dehner believes the $14.3 million franchise tag number for running backs “speaks the Bengals’ language as they continue to work on a potential longer deal for him.” Brown, entering his age-26 season, remains a fringe fantasy RB1 in Cincinnati’s wide-open offense. It doesn’t seem like there’s any danger of a holdout or anything of the sort here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Browns would like a third or fourth-round pick for WR Jerry Jeudy but he’s not sure they’ll be able to get it.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: We, too, would like to simply be given valuable things for no reason. Jeudy has fallen off the fantasy map enough that we’re now simply blurbing trade possibilities for him. The 27-year-old’s only real fantasy value at this point is hoping he gets traded somewhere where he can get involved again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jerry Jeudy “could be had” before the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: With Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion earning large roles right away, Jeudy has all but vanished from the box scores. He went two games without catching a single pass before bringing down three balls for 36 yards on Thursday night. Jeudy got pushed out of the Browns’ long-term plans on draft night and isn’t even part of the week-to-week game plan at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: KC Concepcion caught 5-of-8 targets for 64 yards in the Browns’ Week 4 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Concepcion continues to operate as the primary slot receiver for a Browns team clearly looking to their youth while phasing out veteran Jerry Jeudy, the latter of whom managed three receptions on three targets for 36 yards. Concepcion has yet to lead the team in receiving while working in a short area role, with this the first game thus far which he has gained more then 43 yards. He’ll be a difficult start in fantasy circles when the Browns take on the Jets in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jerry Jeudy did not catch his lone target in the Browns’ Week 2 win against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: After his two-catch performance in Week 1, Jeudy is off to a roaring start. Denzel Boston has established himself as Cleveland’s de facto No. 1 wideout while KC Concepcion is being force fed the ball on gadget plays near the line of scrimmage. With almost no avenue to fantasy relevance, Jeudy should remain on waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Browns WR Jerry Jeudy (wrist) is practicing in full for Week 2 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Jeudy is on track to play, but he is seemingly being phased out of the offense. Browns rookie WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion are establishing themselves as impactful starters, and their roles should only grow in the coming weeks. Jeudy should be left on waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Jerry Jeudy caught 2-of-4 targets for 26 yards in the Browns’ Week 1 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Jeudy felt like an afterthought behind the two rookie wideouts in the Browns’ passing game. He tied for second in targets and was a distant third in yards behind Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. The veteran is still involved as a starter on the outside, but Todd Monken made it a point to make Boston the deep target and Concepcion the primary offensive weapon. In a fantasy-unfriendly offense, Jeudy is best left off the fantasy radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Browns WR Jerry Jeudy (hamstring) did not practice at mandatory minicamp on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Cleveland’s Mary Kay Cabot reports that Jeudy “felt something in his hamstring today,” so he sat out. Coach Todd Monken made clear that he does not give veterans rest days right now, so if a player sits, it’s because they are being cautious with an injury. Today was the Browns’ final mandatory minicamp practice. They will now go on break until training camp begins in July. Early in May, Cabot reported that the team is hoping Jeudy reclaims his WR1 role this season. Browns rookie WRs KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston have been taking full rotations with both the No. 1 and No. 2 offensive groups. Yesterday, ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi reported Boston “has been one of the Browns’ standouts this summer.” Get well soon, Jeudy. The youngsters look promising.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Cleveland’s Mary Kay Cabot reports that the Browns hope WR Jerry Jeudy “can rebound from a down 2025 season and reclaim his role as the No. 1 receiver.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: Cabot later writes that “the Browns really need Jeudy to return to his Pro Bowl form, and are confident he will.” We think her initial, hopeful framing is closer to the truth. Last week, Browns general manager Andrew Berry said rookie WRs KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston’s presence has “zero impact” on Jeudy. There’s an awful lot of reassurance going on here. Jeudy posted a 92/1,229/4 receiving line in 2024 before cratering to a 50/602/2 receiving line in 2025. Jeudy is under contract through 2027, but the dead money and salary cap savings are nearly even if designated as a post-June 1 cut next year. Given the Browns’ pass-catching investments over the last two drafts, and Jeudy’s poor 2025 showing, he looks like a dicey pick in fantasy for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: Browns GM Andrew Berry said the drafting of KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston has “zero impact” on Jerry Jeudy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: The Browns selected two receivers in the top-40 of last week’s draft, taking KC Concepcion 24th overall and Denzel Boston 39th overall. While they clearly addressed a massive weakness on the roster, Berry said he doesn’t expect the addition to have an impact on Jeudy, adding that he prefers to build a receiver room “with different skillsets” and that doesn’t require one player to be a “ball dominant player.” In a somewhat contradictory statement, Berry also said he expects Jeudy, to be the “bell cow” receiver for the team. It’s hard to know what to make of this, but both Concepcion and Boston figure to see the field early as rookies. Even if Jeudy’s snaps don’t see a noticeable decrease, we probably shouldn’t expect him to see anything close to the 142 targets he had in 2024 when he broke out for 92-1,229-4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.headline: The Athletic’s Zac Jackson believes the Browns may attempt to “fix” the wide receiver position in next month’s draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jerry-jeud.analysis: It’s a situation he says “remains bad” as Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond appear to be the only two players guaranteed a role on next year’s team. The Browns struck out on their attempts to add to the room via trade early in free agency and prioritized their offensive line. Jeudy’s fantasy value is hanging on by a thread with Shedeur Sanders the likely starter in 2026. Any other impact rookie additions would likely push him into the WR5 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports the Cowboys are expected to re-sign RB Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: He’ll apparently get a 53-man roster spot after some roster machinations over the next few days. Demercado has lost the backup job to Tyler Goodson and doesn’t need to factor into any fantasy calculations at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: Cowboys waived RB Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Tyler Goodson has had the RB2 role for the past couple of weeks and is set to continue now that Demercado was waived to make room for Tyler Smith to come off injured reserve. Demercado has now been waived twice in two months, and though he may be claimed again, he could also wind up on a practice squad next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson reports the Cowboys are signing RB Tyler Goodson off the Falcons’ practice-squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Goodson will backfill the roster spot lost to placing Malik Davis on IR at the end of last week. It’s unclear whether Emari Demercado or Goodson would be the head of a committee if Javonte Williams were injured, as both of them showed up with the Cowboys after last cuts. Neither player is a must-roster as things stand.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports that Cowboys Malik Davis (hip) will have surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: It is unclear whether this is a season-ending injury or if Davis has a chance to return later in the year. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported earlier that the Cowboys were “bracing for an extended absence” and that a source told him, “it’s bad.” It sounds like Davis’ 2026 season may be over. Cowboys RB Emari Demercado now sits behind starting RB Javonte Williams, and RB Israel Abanikanda is on the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Cowboys “are bracing for an extended absence” after RB Malik Davis suffered a hip injury on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Regarding Davis’ injury, Fowler’s source said simply, “it’s bad.” The Cowboys’ No. 2 running back is undergoing further testing, but we expect them to place him on injured reserve before long. The Cowboys waived RB Jaydon Blue and RB Phil Mafah last month. Blue has since signed with the Eagles’ practice squad. The Cowboys have RB Emari Demercado on the active roster behind RB Javonte Williams. Currently, only RB Israel Abanikanda is on the practice squad in Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: DLLS Sports’ Clarence Hill Jr. reports Malik Davis was carted off the field on Friday with an injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Hill was quickly ruled out for Week 1. Dallas cut Phil Mafah and Jaydon Blue at the end of camp, briefly leaving Davis as the only backup running back on their roster. They eventually signed Emari Demercado after he was released by Kansas City. If the injury is serious, the Cowboys could bring either Mafah or Blue back, given their familiarity with the system. The Dallas Morning News’ Calvin Watkins reported shortly afterward that Davis has suffered a hip injury, though no further details were given.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: Cowboys claimed RB Emari Demercado off waivers from the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Demercado enters a wide open backfield depth chart behind starter Javonte Williams and primary backup Malik Davis, the two of whom were the only running backs to survive 53-man roster cuts Sunday. It does not appear the Cowboys are finished adding to their backfield, with most teams keeping four running backs on the active roster throughout the season. More to come.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: Chiefs waived RB Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Demercado’s departure leaves rookie RB Emmett Johnson and second-year RB Brashard Smith to back up starting RB Kenneth Walker. The Chiefs also waived DE Vincent Anthony, LB Kam Arnold, WR Andrew Armstrong, WR Wesley Bissainthe, DT Cole Brevard, WR Jason Brownlee, WR Jacob De Jesus, OT Ethan Driskell, WR Omari Evans, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, LB Cam Jones, WR Xavier Loyd, S Tanner McCalister, DT Amari McNeill, C Pete Nygra, RB Jaydn Ott, DT Damon Payne, CB D’Arco Perkins-McAllister, TE Mason Pline, S DeShon Singleton, CB Melvin Smith, EDGE Tyreke Smith, OG Josh Thompson, CB Zelmar Vedder, TE Tre Watson and WR Jeff Weimer. The Chiefs released LB Cole Christiansen, CB Kaiir Elam, CB Kader Kohou and EDGE Emmanuel Ogbah. The Chiefs placed DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) on the reserve/physically unable to play list and WR Jimmy Holiday on injured reserve. The Chiefs also waived OG C.J. Hanson, QB Chris Oladokun and RB EJ Smith with injury designations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: Emmet Johnson rushed seven times for 39 yards in the Chiefs’ preseason game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Johnson added two catches for 15 yards and had another chunk gain through the air called back because of a penalty. Kenneth Walker didn’t play in this contest, allowing Johnson to draw the start with some of KC’s first-team offense on the field. Johnson split reps with Emari Demercado over the team’s first three drives, then left the game for good. He looks like the team’s No. 2 back, though all three backs have been the next man up behind Walker at some point during the preseason. Johnson isn’t guaranteed the backup job, but he’s now the favorite, putting him in the mix as a late-round flyer in deeper fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Chiefs RB Emmett Johnson “is swiftly earning a role as an explosive, decisive runner.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emari-deme.analysis: Breer refers to RB Kenneth Walker as an “every-down” player, says RB Brashard Smith “has already shown he can be a weapon in space,” and notes RB Emari Demercado adds depth. Perhaps taking on a change-of-pace rushing role is in play for Johnson this season. The rookie back has pass-catching experience as well, but Smith and Demercado could offer more in that department at the moment. Johnson could be the next player up if Walker were to miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Commanders signed RB Devin Neal to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: He’ll replace Robert Henry, who signed to Seattle’s active roster, as Washington’s practice squad back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Vikings signed RB Devin Neal.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The 2025 sixth-rounder was waived from injured reserve with a settlement at last cuts. Still just 23, Neal has a non-zero shot of resurfacing for a real role here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints waived RB Devin Neal.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Saints placed Neal on injured reserve with a hamstring injury over the weekend, but did not designate him as a candidate to return. He received an injury settlement, and could potentially return to the Saints if he passes through waivers unclaimed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints placed RB Devin Neal on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, ending his season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Neal has hit I.R. without a return designation, so his sophomore season is over. Of course, he could later be released with an injury settlement. The 2025 sixth-rounder managed 74 touches for the Saints’ undermanned 2025 running back group, though he was not impressive in the process. He is still only 23 years old, so he could land on someone else’s practice squad if/when the Saints cut him loose.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Kendre Miller (back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
