https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Saints’ backup running back statuses continue to change. Veteran No. 2 RB Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to be sidelined for at least one month, and RB Audric Estime is now sidelined with an undisclosed injury. Miller and RB Devin Neal (hamstring) both returned this week, though. Beat reporter Jeff Nowak notes that Miller, Neal and RB Ty Chandler were all allowed to rotate in for first-team reps today, as coach Kellen Moore presumably seeks out a viable primary backup for starting RB Travis Etienne. Per Nowak, Miller “looks sharp despite the time missed.” This is worth tracking for short-term bench stash purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Devin Neal (hamstring) was seen working with trainers off to the side on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As of Thursday, Neal was taking advantage of RB Kendre Miller’s back injury by playing well at practice. Miller is still sidelined, but now Neal is too. The two backs, along with RBs Audric Estime, Ty Chandler and CJ Donaldson, are all competing for the RB3 job. The fact that Neal is working with the training staff out in the open is a good sign, but this is worth keeping an eye on because a hamstring injury ended his rookie season prematurely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Kendre Miller (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The good news is that Miller was not listed with a knee injury after suffering a season-ending ACL tear in Week 7 last year. The bad news is that he evidently has a new injury, and the Saints have a fairly deep running back room right now. RBs Devin Neal, Audric Estime, Ty Chandler and CJ Donaldson are all vying for roster spots. Per Underhill, Neal is taking advantage of the extra reps. He could have the inside track to the RB3 role right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Devin Neal (undisclosed) is rehabbing after suffering a “little injury” last week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: If the Saints cut bait on Alvin Kamara, Neal would probably be in the battle for the RB2 spot as things currently stand on the roster. This seems minor enough that we probably wouldn’t be concerned about it, but Neal was dinged up towards the end of last year and it’s worth keeping an eye on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett believes the Saints would “go shopping” for a No. 2 running back candidate if RB Alvin Kamara is not on the team this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Triplett and his colleague, Nick Underhill, joked about how RB Kendre Miller (knee) will likely once again dazzle at organized team activities, before things fizzle for him. It’s a brutal take on the 23-year-old Miller, who has dealt with ankle, hamstring and knee injuries, plus one concussion, in his short career. Miller is currently rehabbing a torn ACL suffered in October 2025, but it sounds like he is expected to participate next week. If Kamara is released, Miller should at least get a chance to compete for the No. 2 role. Triplett believes the team has one A-back in RB Travis Etienne, and two B-backs in Miller and, presumably, RB Devin Neal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints placed RB Devin Neal on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Bummer. His season is over. Neal was playing well in RB Alvin Kamara’s (ankle/knee) stead. Neal can be expected to contribute next year, though he may not have done enough to convince the coaching staff that he deserves to be the 2026 starter. The 22-year-old rookie rushed 57 times for 206 yards and two touchdowns, and caught 17-of-19 targets for 104 yards in his first season with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jauan Jennings “would be a name for me to keep an eye on” for the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings has been a major disappointment in Minnesota, falling behind Tai Felton on the depth chart. A small stakes trade could make sense for the 49ers, who are down to hoping Brandin Cooks can provide for Brock Purdy in a major rash of injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Tai Felton caught 2-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jordan Addison missed this game with an ankle injury and the Vikings deployed Felton as their WR2 over Jauan Jennings. Jennings ran fewer routes and failed to catch his only target. Felton wasn’t awfully productive either, but it’s good to see the former third-round pick picking up more work in his second season. He will return to a rotational role, assuming Addison is cleared to play after the Vikings’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings caught 1-of-1 targets for eight yards in the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings simply isn’t meaningfully involved in the Vikings’ game plan. That is unlikely to change in Week 5 against the Saints, especially with the Vikings’ offensive line getting banged up in Week 4. Jennings could be asked to contribute more as a run blocker next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings caught 1-of-2 targets for one yard in the Vikings’ Week 3 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings hasn’t been part of the Minnesota passing attack through three weeks. Against the Bucs Jennings ran the second most pass routes on the Vikings, behind only Jordan Addison. The low-volume Vikings passing offense likely can’t support more than one fantasy viable pass catcher per week. Jennings should remain on waivers for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Jauan Jennings (personal) is expected to return for Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings was targeted just once in Week 1. It could be argued that we’re not sure what his target count would look like in a normal Vikings game given how quickly Kyler Murray got hurt, but there’s never been a normal Vikings game anyway. Jennings is best monitored from the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Vikings WR Jauan Jennings (personal) is out for Week 2 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Head coach Kevin O’Connell ruled out veteran receiver Jauan Jennings, citing a death of a close family member. Jennings will step away from the team to mourn the passing, leaving Tai Felton as the player most likely to step into his vacated role when the Vikings take on the Bears. Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison should take on all the volume they can handle with the team also without Jordan Mason. Jefferson is a locked-in WR1 while Addison offers an intriguing upside-WR2 profile after putting up a dud in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings failed to catch his only target in the Vikings’ Week 1 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Things went off the rails in the first quarter when Kyler Murray left with a concussion, but one target is a bad omen no matter who is under center. Jennings was also a distant third on the team in routes behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. He is not on the fantasy radar headed into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports that Jordan Addison remains the Vikings’ No. 2 wide receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Pelissero affirmed Addison’s role as a guest on the Rich Eisen Show. He prefaced the remarks by saying that WR Jauan Jennings’ signing “immediately raises questions” about whether the Vikings planned to move on from Addison before saying that they, in fact, do not. Jennings was brought in on a “cut-rate,” one-year deal to play the No. 3 wide receiver role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports that Jauan Jennings will replace Jalen Nailor as the Vikings’ No. 3 wide receiver this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: We assumed this was the case, though Jennings’ size allows one to wonder if he might be valuable in heavy personnel packages. Nailor departed for the Raiders earlier this offseason. Vikings No. 2 WR Jordan Addison was suspended for Weeks 1-3 last season. From Week 4 on, Addison out-snapped Nailor 714-to-507. Expecting a similar split from Addison and Jennings this season is reasonable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Vikings signed WR Jauan Jennings, formerly of the 49ers, to a one-year, $13 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: The deal includes an $8 million base salary. Jennings can make an extra $5 million via incentives. This will be Jennings’ first time playing for a team other than the 49ers, who drafted him in the 2020 NFL Draft’s seventh round. Jennings, 28, caught 55 passes for 643 yards and a career-high nine touchdowns last year. He should start in three-wide receiver sets alongside Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. Jefferson will rarely leave the field, but one wonders if Jennings (6'3/212) might be able to steal snaps from Addison (5'11/175) in two-wide receiver sets, in part due to Jennings’ run-blocking ability. Addison, 24, is the more talented receiver, so we expect him to remain the No. 2 target earner, but this dynamic is worth keeping an eye on in training camp. For now, Jennings can be viewed as a WR4/FLEX, while Jefferson sits in the WR1 tier and Addison in the WR2/3 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyx-hunt.headline: Eagles DC Vic Fangio said it would take “something miraculous” for DE Jalyx Hunt (ankle) to play in Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyx-hunt.analysis: The Eagles defense is one of the better units in the NFL, but it has been quite banged up of late and losing Hunt here is not ideal. We’ll see if they can blot out Bryce Young’s strong start with the Panthers in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyx-hunt.headline: Jalyx Hunt is undergoing testing on his left leg after suffering an injury in the second quarter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyx-hunt.analysis: Hunt went down on the final play of the first half. The team initially brought out the cart for him, but he managed to limp off the field with the help of the medical staff. He doesn’t have an official injury status right now, but we’ll assume his day is over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyx-hunt.headline: Eagles selected Houston Christian EDGE Jalyx Hunt with the No. 94 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyx-hunt.analysis: Eagles defensive coaches were reportedly high on Hunt headed into the draft. After being utilized as a massive safety at Cornell during the 2019 and 2021 seasons, Hunt (6’4/252) made the switch to edge for his final two years after transferring to Houston Christian. He thrived in the new role, amassing a team leading 9.0 TFL and 6.5 sacks with an 83rd percentile overall grade, earning Southland Conference Defensive Player of the Year honors last year. The Senior Bowl invitee is an NFL caliber athlete who displayed good bend and flashes of having a pass rush bag, but was unable to land moves with much consistency. Hunt wins by bending the edge or playing with his food out in space, and using his superior athleticism to weave around blockers. His 90.2 PFF grade as a pass rusher in 2023 show that he was consistently able to win with his athleticism, but his lack of polish was not exposed against weaker competition.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Rams waived K Harrison Mevis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: Mevis, I told you six times before, you don’t work here no more. The Thiccer Kicker hit 12-of-13 for the Rams after coming in late last season and 39-of-39 extra points. He doesn’t quite have the distance of some of the league’s best kickers, but we expect him to continue to get chances at 24.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Rams signed K Blake Grupe off the Jets practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: Going 5-for-9 on the season will get you replaced in the modern NFL, as Thiccer Kicker Harrison Mevis is learning. It’s not totally fair, one of those was blocked, but clearly the Rams were not happy with how things were trending. Grupe is a worthwhile pickup in leagues that still use kickers. He went 11-for-11 for the Colts last year after being released by the Saints at midseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Rams tendered OL Justin Dedich, K Harrison Mevis, WR Xavier Smith.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: The team will maintain control of three players that surprised in 2025, including “thiccer kicker” Harrison Mevis. The tendering of exclusive rights free agents ties the three to the franchise through the 2026 season considering they are unable to negotiate with other teams. At least for now, it appears as if the Rams will continue forward with Mevis as their place kicker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Harrison Mevis made his only field-goal attempt in Los Angeles’ NFC Championship loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: Mevis finishes the year 12-of-13 on field goals — missing one against the Seahawks in Week 16 — and hit all 39 of his regular season extra point attempts. He was perfect in the playoffs on five field goals and nine extra-point attempts. The 23-year-old was a find for the Rams and should enter the starting kicker conversation in most fantasy leagues that use kickers in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Harrison Mevis made 2-of-2 field goals in the Rams’ Week 15 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: He hasn’t missed yet, going 5-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 27-of-27 on extra points. The Rams talked a big game about Joshua Karty eventually getting the job back when they waived him, but Mevis is not giving the former incumbent an inch of space to get active. The Thiccer Kicker will remain a low-end K1 against the Seahawks in Week 16.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Harrison Mevis converted his lone field goal attempt and all six of his extra point attempts in the Rams’ Week 14 win against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: Mevis has proven a fine weekly fantasy play thanks to the high-powered Rams offense and the positive game script it creates. He’s made all three of his field goals this season and has yet to miss an extra point. He should be in fantasy lineups next week against the Lions in what should be a high-scoring affair. The Lions have allowed 1.7 field goal tries per game this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Harrison Mevis will again be the team’s kicker in Week 11 against Seattle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: Mevis, the “Thiccer Kicker,” did not attempt a field goal against the 49ers, settling for six made extra points. Seattle will probably force some more attempts this week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Harrison Mevis will kick for the Rams in Week 10 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: He also said Joshua Karty’s roster spot is “not going anywhere” for whatever that’s worth. It sounds like Karty will be a healthy scratch for Week 10 while they try to work with him to get his confidence back. Mevis is worth a pickup in fantasy leagues with the Rams expected to pile up points on San Francisco’s banged-up defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Rams signed K Harrison Mevis, formerly of the Jets, to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: The former Birmingham Stallions kicker will provide some competition for Joshua Karty. Karty has struggled mightily this year, connecting on just 10-of-15 field goals and 23-of-26 PATs. Two of his field goal misses came on Sunday against the Saints. Mevis could take the job from Karty as soon as Week 10 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.headline: Jets waived K Anders Carlson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-m.analysis: New York parted ways with Carlson and signed K Harrison Mevis as they look for a starter headed into training camp. Carlson, who signed with the team last November and continued to struggle. He made eight of ten field goal tries and nine of 11 extra points over five games with the Jets in 2024. Carlson, who lost his starting job in Green Bay before coming to New York, will likely catch on with another team this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Rams signed K Blake Grupe off the Jets practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Going 5-for-9 on the season will get you replaced in the modern NFL, as Thiccer Kicker Harrison Mevis is learning. It’s not totally fair, one of those was blocked, but clearly the Rams were not happy with how things were trending. Grupe is a worthwhile pickup in leagues that still use kickers. He went 11-for-11 for the Colts last year after being released by the Saints at midseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Jets signed K Jason Sanders to their active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Sanders somehow won the kicking job over Blake Grupe despite Grupe being on the active roster and Sanders falling to the practice squad. Sure. Well, anyway, Grupe is being waived. Sanders will continue to kick for the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said Jason Sanders will serve as the team’s kicker in Week 1 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: This is notable because Sanders is currently on the Jets’ practice squad while veteran kicker Blake Grupe is on the 53-man roster. Fantasy managers expecting Grupe to contribute to their Week 1 lineups will want to make sure they find a replacement. Sanders certainly makes for a viable option after he converted 37-of-41 field goal attempts last season while going 12-of-14 from distances of 50-plus yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Jets claimed K Blake Grupe off waivers from the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Jason Sanders, who had won the Jets kicker competition, is instead released to make way for Grupe. As we wrote about Sanders a few days ago: Winning the Jets kicker competition is not an endorsement that provides many fantasy points. Grupe will probably be stuck in the 20s in weekly ranks in most of the Jets games this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Colts released K Blake Grupe.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Grupe, who had a “90% make rate in camp” per Mike Garafolo, has a chance to come aboard late and win a different kicking job. Spencer Shrader will kick for the Colts this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: The Indianapolis Star’s Nathan Brown reports Blake Grupe “has the clear statistical lead” in the Colts’ kicking competition.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Grupe is competing with Spencer Schrader for the Colts’ starting gig, and through a week of training camp, Grupe has been more accurate. Brown said the team is evaluating other factors as well, including ball flight and pre-practice kicks from Grupe and Schrader. The Colts in 2025 tied for tenth in team field goal attempts. That sort of opportunity will make Grupe or Schrader fantasy viable in 2026 as long as Daniel Jones is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Colts signed K Blake Grupe to a one-year, $1.4 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Grupe appeared in only five games for the Colts in 2025 but went a perfect 11-for-11 with the team. He was signed in December after making only 18 of 26 attempts with the Saints to start the year. His efforts to end the season earn him a chance to prove his worth on the modest deal. Spencer Shrader remains under team control, setting up a potential kicker battle in camp and preseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Blake Grupe converted all three of his field goal attempts in the Colts’ Week 15 loss against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Grupe, who was released by the Saints in early December after making just 18 of his 26 field goal tries, came through big time for Indy in their near-upset of the Seahawks. Grupe nailed a 60-yarder to take the lead in the fourth quarter — a kick that would have been good from at least 65 yards. Grupe will be a decent streaming option in Week 16 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Colts elevated K Blake Grupe from the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Grupe will be the kicker for the Colts in Week 14 against the Jaguars. The 27-year-old gets first crack at being the kicker for Indianapolis after the team released Michael Badgley following his missed extra point against the Texans in Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Colts signed K Blake Grupe to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: He’ll likely be elevated a few times as roster manipulation while the Colts figure out if he’s the answer. Grupe struggled this year for the Saints, hitting just 18-of-26 field goals, including two inside of 40 yards. He’ll be a worthwhile fantasy play if the Colts can get their offense back on track against the Jaguars in Week 14.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said the Chargers would not consider trading Justin Herbert.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Schefter reached out to the team after a league source told him the Chargers could get upwards of three first-round draft picks in exchange for Herbert. The Chargers source told Schefter the team has “never” discussed the idea of dealing Herbert, even as the Chargers start the season 0-5 and rank near the bottom in almost every offensive category. It would seem unlikely that the Chargers would consider trading Herbert even if they go all in on a rebuild following the 2026 season. Herbert, 28, who ranks 33rd out of 34 qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per drop back this year, is signed through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 14-of-24 passes for 121 yards with a touchdown and interception while rushing for 54 yards and losing a fumble in the Chargers’ 23-17, Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert was without his top wideouts, his top offensive lineman, and the fact he was able to put up even this type of statline is somewhat impressive, if you squint very hard. The 28-year-old quarterback was constantly under pressure, and was at his best when he was able to escape the pocket and use his underrated wheels. That being said, he could have had more turnovers than this, and his interception was an inexcusable throw right into the hands of the Broncos defender. Even if Herbert gets his weapons back, fantasy managers should be looking elsewhere in Week 6 in standard leagues with a tough matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Rashawn Slater suffered a high ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: The injury, sustained during the Bolts’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, will cost Slater between four and six weeks, Rapoport said. It’s yet another massive blow for the struggling Chargers offense. Through Week 4 the Chargers rank 30th in ESPN’s pass blocking win rate and fifth in run blocking win rate. Justin Herbert’s weekly prospects take a hit with the oft-injured Slate sidelined, as do the prospects of LA’s pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 19-of-31 passes for 189 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions in the Chargers’ 30-23, Week 4 loss to the Seahawks while adding 40 yards on the ground on six attempts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: It really wasn’t this close. Herbert and Sam Darnold became the first quarterbacks since 1991 to throw interceptions on their first throws of their game. Things didn’t get less weird, nor less shaky for the now 0-4 Chargers. He threw both his picks to linebackers, and outside of a 26-yard scramble, there just wasn’t much there from a quarterback who had (much) loftier expectations coming into the year. His only touchdown was a flip to Kimani Vidal that left Los Angeles down two scores. There’s a lot of football left, but this is ugly. Herbert will try and get going in Week 5, but the Broncos make for a tough team to get that ship righted.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Justin Herbert must “be better.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: It’s hard to write these quotes without sounding “clicky,” but Harbaugh was forthright at his Monday press conference when asked about Herbert’s decision-making. “Be better. Be better,” Harbaugh said before attempting to soften the blow. “And that drives Justin, that drives me, that drives his position coach, that drives (OC Mike [McDaniel). I mean, drives us all.” Harbaugh also said the team could look to simplify McDaniel’s complex scheme. “As far as the scheme going forward, all options are open,” Harbaugh claimed. When asked what that might entail, the coach responded “run, pass, up the middle, motion, no motion.” Alrighty then. It’s shocking to hear a coach talk this frankly — especially Harbaugh about Herbert — but the situation really is that dire in Los Angeles. Herbert is in the crossfire, but it could be McDaniel who is on something of a hot seat with his play-calling. Sitting at 0-3, the Chargers face the unwelcome prospect of a “must win” Week 4 contest against defending Super Bowl champion Seattle, itself coming off a rough loss. We will be benching Herbert in fantasy for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 20-of-34 passes for 226 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the Chargers’ 24-16, Week 3 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: On one hand, Herbert was under constant pressure in this game behind a beat-up offensive line and was able to evade pressure regularly and extend plays. On the other hand, he really wasn’t able to get anything going down the field. His one touchdown “pass” was on a handoff where he essentially let go of the ball and Keaton Mitchell took the “forward pass” into the end zone on a jet sweep. Herbert’s interception was a terrible pass in the end zone when the Chargers were up 13-10 and looking to put the game away. The Bills also dropped two other potential interceptions. Herbert looks pretty firmly like a QB2 here, and it’s hard to get overly excited about playing him next week against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 15-of-27 passes for 192 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Chargers’ 24-14, Week 2 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: The Chargers were an uncoordinated mess in this one. They committed loads of procedural penalties on offense, had several drops, and botched multiple handoffs or snaps. Their final penalty was holding in their own end zone, resulting in a safety. David Njoku handed Herbert’s first interception to a defender, but the second pick was all his fault. Herbert fired into a non-existent window on a deep shot and was easily intercepted by the Vegas secondary. Herbert also committed two fumbles, though both were recovered by the Chargers. Sitting at 0-2 with murderer’s row of opponents on deck, something has to change in a hurry for the Chargers. Herbert will shuffle into the QB2 ranks for his Week 3 date with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 17-of-27 pass attempts for 209 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Chargers’ Week 1 loss to the Cardinals, adding five rushes for 29 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert shredded the Arizona secondary in the Bolts’ first drive of the game. From there he struggled to complete even routine passes and got nothing going downfield. Ladd McConkey’s exit from the ballgame in the third quarter all but ended Herbert’s production for the day. Herbert, to his credit, tried to push the ball downfield, averaging 10.8 intended air yards per attempt, the fourth highest mark of Week 1. The Cards’ time of possession domination limited play volume for LA, torpedoing fantasy prospects across the board. Hopefully for Herbert, the Chargers will have McConkey back for Week 2 against the Raiders. Herbert will be a borderline top-12 option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said Justin Herbert has “exceeded expectations” in adapting to McDaniel’s offense.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: McDaniel said the team has worked diligently on the quick passing game during offseason practices and training camp. McDaniel said he knows Herbert can excel on the “long developing plays” but wants to create more easy drop backs with schemes that “nullify the pass rush” and allow Herbert to get the ball out quickly to his pass catchers. This should lead to plenty of easy-button targets for Ladd McConkey and the team’s tight ends as Quentin Johnston continues operating as Herbert’s primary deep ball guy. Under McDaniel, the Chargers will likely be run-first with a far more efficient passing attack than they had under former OC Greg Roman.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: ESPN’s Kris Rhim reports that when Chargers QB Justin Herbert threw in team drills during mandatory minicamp practices, “the results were uneven.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: New Chargers OC Mike McDaniel reduced Herbert’s throwing frequency in spring practices in an effort to keep Herbert’s arm fresh later in the season. Herbert is instead focused on adjusting his shotgun footwork according to McDaniel’s unorthodox, yet often successful preferences. According to Rhim, this led to Herbert and his receivers frequently being “just out of sync on timing” in team drills. That said, Rhim believes that this is " an expected part of implementing a new offense but something that will need to improve during training camp.” We agree. This is not overly concerning, but it will be worthwhile to follow up on Herbert’s connection with his pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.headline: Bengals TE Tanner Hudson (pec) is expected to miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.analysis: Hudson tore his pec in Week 5’s win over the Dolphins. The injury will likely keep him sidelined for the remainder of the regular season. Hudson had played 28 percent of the team’s offensive snaps and seen seven targets through five games, mostly functioning as a blocker. Drew Sample would see more snaps with Hudson sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.headline: Tanner Hudson caught 3-of-3 targets for 14 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.analysis: Hudson saw three targets on the day, catching a Joe Burrow touchdown pass towards the end of the first half. The Bengals used all of their tight ends against Miami; Hudson saw 19 snaps while Mike Gesicki saw 28 and Erick All and Drew Sample tied with 33 snaps. It was a run-heavy day for Cincy, but the four tight ends all combined for nine targets. All caught all three of his targets for 25 yards while Sample caught his only target for five yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.headline: Bengals signed TE Tanner Hudson to a one-year contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.analysis: Hudson, 31, was playing on an expiring deal this season but is now locked in for 2026. The veteran tight end played on 148 offensive snaps this season, per PFF, and has never been used as anything more than a backup since entering the league in 2019. He caught 19 passes for 168 yards and two touchdowns this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.headline: Tanner Hudson (concussion) is not on Cincinnati’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.analysis: He cleared concussion protocol and will return as a thorn in the side for Noah Fant-reliant fantasy managers in Week 8. Hudson has no standalone value, but he does leech off valuable snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.headline: Bengals TE Tanner Hudson (concussion) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.analysis: Hudson’s expected return bodes poorly for TE Noah Fant’s target-earning potential, though Fant should still run as the primary positional receiver. Hudson sat out in Week 7, allowing Fant to operate as a streaming TE1. Fant caught 4-of-4 targets for 44 yards and one touchdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.headline: Bengals declared EDGE Trey Hendrickson, CB Cam Taylor-Britt, C Matt Lee, WR Jermaine Burton, TE Tanner Hudson and DT McKinnley Jackson inactive for Week 7 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.analysis: Hendrickson is sidelined by a hip injury, though the Bengals fortunately get EDGE Shemar Stewart (ankle) back after a four-game absence. Taylor-Britt has evidently been benched in favor of CB Josh Newton this week. The Bengals’ offense lost two tight ends last week, with Hudson suffering a concussion and Mike Gesicki suffering a pectoral injury that landed him on injured reserve this week. Bengals TE Noah Fant is suddenly on the streaming TE1 radar as a result.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.headline: Bengals TE Tanner Hudson (concussion) will not play in Week 7 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.analysis: Mike Gesicki was placed on injured reserve earlier this week, meaning Noah Fant is now the only tight end of note available for the Bengals tomorrow. Expect Joe Flacco to lock on to his start receivers versus Pittsburgh, but Fant is at least in the TE2 mix as a player who could approach a 100 percent route rate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.headline: Bengals palced TE Mike Gesicki (pec) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.analysis: Gesicki will miss at least four games after sustaining a knee injury last week against the Packers. Noah Fant and Tanner HUdson split tight end routes after Gesicki exited the game; Hudson saw five targets while Fant saw four from Joe Flacco. Fant would be the slight favorite to be the team’s nominal TE1 going forward, as he’s been targeted on a strong 30 percent of his pass routes in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.headline: Bengals TE Tanner Hudson (concussion) did not practice Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.analysis: He’ll almost certainly be ruled out. Noah Fant has some TE2 and single-game slate upside on Thursday night with Mike Gesicki likely heading to injured reserve and Hudson not stealing snaps from him. That’ll leave just Fant and Drew Sample as oft-used cogs of the Bengals tight end room that are still healthy enough for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.headline: Tanner Hudson (concussion) did not practice on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-hud.analysis: It’s an estimated DNP, but we almost never see someone clear protocol ahead of a Thursday night game. With Mike Gesicki also likely out, it looks like Noah Fant may have some stream appeal as a TE2 as the Bengals are forced to rely heavily on him and Drew Sample in their well-stocked tight end platoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows believes Brandin Cooks is the “next man up” in the 49ers receivers room.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: With Deebo Samuel sustaining a serious hamstring injury in Week 5 against Seattle, Cooks stepped in and functioned as San Francisco’s No. 2 receiver behind Mike Evans. Cooks was targeted on 17 percent of his pass routes against the Seahawks and caught a touchdown on his only reception. Though Jacob Cowing could mix in with Samuel sidelined, Cooks should be in line for a few targets a game. The well-traveled veteran can be picked up in deeper fantasy formats this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: 49ers signed WR Brandin Cooks, formerly of the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Cooks is signing with the 49ers’ practice squad initially “to get up to speed for games.” Cooks, 32, posted a 24/279/0 receiving line in the regular season last year, before chipping in five catches for 78 yards in two playoff games. He is perhaps unlikely to be fantasy-relevant right away, but there is a real chance he could work his way into the 49ers’ wide receiver rotation, given their influx of injuries at the position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Free agent WR Brandin Cooks worked out for the Ravens on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: This is probably a bad sign regarding WR Zay Flowers’ (hamstring) Week 2 availability, though the Ravens also placed rookie WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) on short-term injured reserve this week. A signing seems likely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Bills GM Brandon Beane said he’s had conversations with Brandin Cooks and his agent.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks is probably a fallback plan for the Bills if they don’t draft someone. Even if he’s signed, the pecking order in targets in Buffalo has radically changed with DJ Moore in town and fantasy managers shouldn’t be expecting more than a WR5 role for Cooks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Brandin Cooks caught 2-of-6 targets for 20 yards in the Bills’ Divisional Round loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks made two spectacular almost catches. On one of them, he caught the ball while twisting on the sideline, and his knee came down in bounds, but his wrist landed a fraction of a second earlier and landed out of bounds. The other play was far more controversial. It seemed like Cooks had hauled in a 44-yard pass to set the Bills up for a game-winning field goal in overtime, but the ball was stripped away by a Broncos defender. The Bills believed Cooks was down by contact before the ball was stripped loose, but the call was not reviewed, and the Broncos would then drive for a game-winning field goal of their own. The 32-year-old came on down the stretch for the Bills, showing that he still has enough deep speed to make big plays. He finished the season with 24 catches on 36 targets for 279 yards and no touchdowns in 15 games with the Bills and Saints. Some team will sign him in free agency and give him a role as a deep threat.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Brandin Cooks caught 3-of-5 targets for 58 yards in the Bills’ Wild Card Round win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks came down with a 36-yard bomb from Josh Allen late in the fourth quarter that eventually set up a go-ahead score. He finished the day second on the team in catches, targets, and yards. With Josh Palmer on IR, there was already plenty of volume up for grabs in the receiver room. The Bills then lost Gabe Davis to a knee injury late in this game. His status for the Divisional Round is up in the air. Cooks will likely operate as the team’s No. 2 receiver next week, putting him squarely on the DFS radar as a salary relief option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Bills declared WR Brandin Cooks inactive for Week 18 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Every other player the Bills declared inactive is a key starter, like Dion Dawkins or Greg Rousseau, so this says a lot about how important Cooks is to the Buffalo offense despite only being on the roster for three games. The 32-year-old posted a 100-yard game last week and has emerged as the primary deep threat for Josh Allen and the offense. Expect Cooks to be a key contributor in the playoffs for as long as the Bills can keep winning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Brandin Cooks caught 4-of-6 passes for 101 yards in the Bills’ 13-12, Week 17 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks came into this game with just one catch and two drops in his two games with the Bills. However, Josh Allen kept firing deep shots to him and, in the first quarter, Cooks finally hauled in a huge 50-yard completion. Later in the game, on the Bills’ final offensive possession, Cooks converted on a key third-down catch and then made a ridiculous 36-yard grab with a defender draped all over him. At 32 years old, Cooks is not the receiver he used to be, but he can still make some plays down the field, and the Bills are clearly relying on him to do so. If Josh Allen plays in Week 18 against the Jets, we’d expect to see more deep shots to Cooks in an offense that is dying for big plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Brandin Cooks caught his only target for 13 yards in the Bills’ Week 13 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks was targeted on a third-down play on the Bills’ first drive of the game, and he converted a nice hitch route to move the chains. He was not targeted again. It’s obvious that he didn’t have a lot of time to learn the playbook, but it’s still surprising to see the Bills not try to use him more after that first drive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.headline: Bills signed WR Brandin Cooks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandin-co.analysis: Cooks has just 1,081 yards over his last 36 games and will need to prove to us that he’ll be a fantasy factor before we recommend adding him in anything but the deepest leagues. He did have a lower-rung role with the Saints early in the season, with 15 targets in his first four weeks, but his work eventually dwindled. It’s a big-name add, but not necessarily one that shakes up the fantasy landscape.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars OL Anton Harrison will undergo knee surgery and will miss at least 3-5 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Harrison, who sustained the injury in Week 5 against the Eagles, could miss the rest of the season once doctors determine the severity of his knee injury, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Harrison had protected Trevor Lawrence’s blindside before the injury. His absence could be a problem for a Jacksonville offensive line that has the league’s third worst pass blocking win rate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Anton Harrison was carted off the field with an apparent leg injury in the Jaguars’ Week 5 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Harrison went down with a non-contact injury in the third quarter. He rode the cart to the locker room. His day is likely over. Walker Little will take his spot at left tackle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars OT Cole Van Lanen (knee) was removed from the injury report for Week 1 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Van Lanen should at least be active, although he is not guaranteed to start. The veteran blocker broke out last year, playing all across the line before settling in at left tackle. He suffered a knee injury in Week 18, which forced the coaching staff to get OT Anton Harrison for left tackle duties while penciling Van Lanen in at right tackle. The team also has capable OT Walker Little at the ready. Unfortunately, Harrison appeared on the injury report with a foot injury and was unable to practice on Friday. Hopefully, his sidelining was a precaution and he is not seriously injured. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars exercised the fifth-year option for RT Anton Harrison.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Harrison was drafted with the No. 27 overall pick back in 2023 and has started all 48 games he’s appeared in since joining the team. He has spent his entire career at right tackle, allowing 10 sacks and 93 pressures in 48 regular-season games, and earned a PFF pass-blocking grade of 75.6 last season — his highest mark to date. Harrison will now be under contract with the Jaguars through the 2027 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars exercised RT Anton Harrison’s fifth-year option.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Over The Cap projects Harrison’s option at $19 million, but in announcing they’d pick it up, Jaguars GM James Gladstone said they’ll have “deeper conversations” on a long-term extension. Harrison, 24, had his best season yet in 2025, registering a career-high 75.6 PFF pass block grade while protecting Trevor Lawrence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars RT Anton Harrison (illness) is active for Jacksonville’s Week 17 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: He was questionable after being added to the report with an illness Sunday morning. The only other questionable Jaguars player was C Robert Hainsey (groin), who was scratched. Also inactive for the Jaguars are: CB Keith Taylor, RB Bhayshul Tuten (finger), OL Patrick Mekari (back), TE Hunter Long, DL Danny Striggow (ankle) and DT Maason Smith.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars RT Anton Harrison (illness) is questionable for Week 17 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Harrison was added to the injury report on Sunday morning, likely after falling ill over the weekend. Players tend to play through illnesses, so this shouldn’t be an issue for the Jags. Cole Van Lanen will take his spot in the lineup if Harrison can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars RT Anton Harrison (elbow) left Jacksonville’s Week 4 game against the 49ers and is questionable to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: He was injured in the second quarter and vacated the sideline quickly afterwards. Harrison was replaced by Chuma Edoga.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars T Anton Harrison (ankle) questionable to return against Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Harrison left in the second half of the Jaguars’ game against the Texans in Week 3 with an ankle injury. He is questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars signed first-round OT Anton Harrison to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: They also signed fifth-round DT Tyler Lacy. Harrison, a two-year starter at Oklahoma, should open the year at left tackle for the Jaguars with Cam Robinson facing a multi-game suspension, and projects to start on the right side when Robinson returns. With Harrison and Lacy under contract, Jacksonville has signed its entire 2023 draft class.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 5-of-7 targets for 51 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams cashed in on a corner fade from four yards out in the second quarter and ran a beautiful route on a double move slant from five yards out for his second score in the fourth quarter, proving that he remains an elite red zone weapon for an offense that has now attempted 51 or more passes in three straight games. Adams is back to modest target rates following the Week 4 return of Puka Nacua but remains a weekly WR2 due to his red zone acumen, which remains true ahead of a much more forgiving matchup against the Cardinals in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 4-of-9 targets for 32 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams was the victim of a bad Matthew Stafford ball or two in rainy Philadelphia conditions, but he sadly immediately reverted to clear No. 2 wideout status with Puka Nacua back in the lineup. Nacua went off for 9/125. Adams now has seven catches for 58 scoreless yards in two games with Nacua in the lineup compared to 15/332/2 in two games without. Hopefully that trend normalizes a bit for a potential Week 5 shootout with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 7-of-13 targets for 137 yards in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams’ 137 yards combine with the 195 yards he erupted for in Week 2 to set a new high in receiving yards in consecutive games during his remarkable career. Even more stunning was the fact that he did so against one of the top corners in the league in Pat Surtain, who shadowed Adams for all but a handful of his routes, proving his ability to get open against top competition even in the later stages of his career. Puka Nacua missed both Week 2 and Week 3 and his injury timeline remains convoluted, at best. Adams will remains a top-tier WR1 should Nacua miss more time, and would be solid WR2 should Nacua return for a Week 4 meeting with the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (groin) is “not making great progress.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: In a surprisingly candid interview with ESPN Los Angeles, McVay certainly did not sound optimistic that Nacua would play in Week 3. Nacua has already missed one practice this week and there’s been no indication that he will get back on the field over the next two days. Davante Adams racked up 195 yards and two scores with Nacua out in Week 2. It will be hard not to rank him as a WR1 once Nacua is ruled out. Terrance Ferguson operated as the team’s No. 2 receiver last week and will be in the TE1 mix without Nacua.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Rams WR Puka Nacua (groin) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Sean McVay was unsure if Nacua would be able to play in Week 3 when asked about it on Tuesday. A DNP today suggests Nacua will need at least one more week of rest before returning to the lineup. Terrance Ferguson finished second on the Rams in targets last week with nine. He caught six passes for 54 yards and a score. No receiver outside of Davante Adams was targeted more than two times. Adams was utterly dominant, turning his 10 targets into 195 yards and two scores. Those are the only two major beneficiaries of Nacua’s likely absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 8-of-10 targets for 195 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ Week 2 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams seamlessly stepped into the alpha role in the offense in the absence of Puka Nacua, routinely making absurd catches on the perimeter while also showcasing his adept route-running abilities in the open field. His first touchdown came on a deep post route following a double move, during which he strode beyond three defenders. He would cash in again from 11 yards out on a fade to the corner of the end zone. Adams remains a top-tier WR2 with WR1 upside when the Rams take on the Broncos in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 3-of-6 targets for 26 yards in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: There was plenty of talk about how great Adams looked in the precursor to the season, but it wasn’t on display in Week 1. The 33-year-old had a long gain of just 13 yards, and he and Matthew Stafford were unable to find many openings against the San Francisco secondary. Adams will get a chance to rebound in Week 2 in a Monday Night Football contest against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports Davante Adams was “uncoverable” in joint practices with the Cowboys and Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: “If there was concern over whether Adams still had it as a perimeter wide receiver at age 33, this camp has put a lot of those questions to rest,” Atkins said, adding Adams had retained his otherworldly connection with Matthew Stafford. “Adams looks fresh and explosive, and he was virtually uncoverable in the joint practices against the Dallas Cowboys and New Orleans Saints.” Atkins conceded that the Rams “might have to get creative again with load management at times” to ensure Adams can get through a whole season without injuries. A whole training camp with Stafford — something he didn’t have in 2025 — could make Adams one of the sneakier wideout selections outside the first couple rounds of fantasy drafts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said he’s “glad he’s a Ram” after confirming previous rumors about a trade of Davante Adams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: McVay said he was up front with Adams about the possibility of a trade earlier this offseason, but said the team ultimately decided that trading the 33-year-old receiver wouldn’t do much to benefit the team. Adams caught 60 passes for 789 yards in his first season with the Rams, playing second fiddle to Puka Nacua, but still managed to haul in a league-leading 14 touchdowns while operating as one of the premier end zone threats in the league. The veteran receiver is under contract through next season and should continue to thrive in the role he was in last season, putting him in the conversation as a fringe WR2/WR3 with plenty of touchdown upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports that the Rams explored trading away WR Davante Adams amid trade talks with the Eagles regarding WR A.J. Brown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Financial investments at the wide receiver position could have been the Rams’ primary motivating factor, though having three high-end wide receivers can hardly be viewed as a negative, albeit a pricey one. Nacua is entering the final year of his rookie contract and will presumably sign “a significant second contract” soon. Adams is due $24 million this season and Brown is set to make $29 million. Florio believes today might have been the Rams’ self-imposed deadline for trading Adams away because his $6 million roster bonus just became fully guaranteed. It appears as though Adams will remain a Ram for 2026, but anything is possible. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 5-of-6 targets for 83 yards in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Higbee continued to operate as the primary pass-catching tight end against the Bills, something that must please fantasy managers considering Colby Parkinson returned from a one-game absence. Furthermore, the team carried only three tight ends on the active game-day roster after being at either four or five through the first month of the 2026 season. Higbee is a middling TE2 in fantasy circles ahead of a juicy matchup against the divisional rival Cardinals in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Colby Parkinson (knee/shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson is unlikely to be startable as a TE1 if he plays on Monday night, but his return will likely reduce Tyler Higbee’s snap share. Higbee has been TE1-viable in each of the last two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Colby Parkinson (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson has a chance to return for the Rams’ Monday Night Football game against the Bills. If this is the case, he would hurt Tyler Higbee’s snap share, threatening the latter’s TE1 viability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 5-of-6 targets for 67 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 victory over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: One of only two healthy Rams tight ends, Higbee was the Rams’ clear-cut No. 3 passing-game weapon behind a returning Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. There’s a huge gulf between the Rams’ wideouts and Higbee, but he should be able to provide TE2 streamer value for the next several weeks, including Week 5 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) will likely miss Week 4 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Ferguson briefly departed after injuring his ankle in the team’s Sunday Night Football loss to the Broncos, returning for two snaps prior to departing again after his lone reception of the evening. The ankle injury now appears likely to cost the talented young tight end at least one game, with the potential for the absence to linger if the sprain is “more high than low.” McVay also relayed that fellow tight end Colby Parkinson suffered an AC sprain and is considered day-to-day. Veteran Tyler Higbee would be in line to operate as the primary receiving tight end after amassing 62 yards and a touchdown on eight receptions in Week 3, should both miss. Higbee should be added in all formats as a potential TE1 in the immediate future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 8-of-11 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Higbee’s first quarter touchdown got the scoring started for the Rams, but it wasn’t until Terrance Ferguson departed with an ankle injury that his volume truly took off. From that point forward, Higbee was one of the primary options through the air, finishing two targets behind Davante Adams for the team lead. Fantasy managers will want to monitor Ferguson’s status closely in the coming week as Higbee could become a legitimate waiver target should Ferguson miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught both of his targets for 12 yards in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Higbee ended up leading the Rams’ tight ends in targets and receptions, as Davis Allen had just one catch before exiting with a head injury, and Terrance Ferguson didn’t catch his only opportunity. Ferguson still seems like the tight end to roster going forward, but one could argue Higbee has the higher floor because he’ll see more snaps because of his blocking ability. That’s not a ringing endorsement, if it’s not obvious. The Rams will try and get it going against the Giants in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Terrance Ferguson “has some of the best breakout potential of current Rams players who haven’t done so yet.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Atkins added, “The ideal outcome for him is to lead their tight ends in catches and yards.” He noted that the coaching staff was focused on bringing Ferguson along incrementally in 2025. Now they will have the chance to move him into a more prominent role for his second season. Ferguson only caught 11 passes as a rookie, but he parlayed a seam-stretching role into 231 yards and three scores despite the low reception total. Atkins sees Ferguson as a de facto No. 3 receiver for the team, with Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee both fulfilling the role of a traditional inline tight end. Rookie Max Klare will also be in the mix for snaps, but will likely be brought along slowly as well. With an ADP that barely even registers in early best ball drafts, Ferguson is worth a look as a high-upside TE3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: ESPN’s Matt Bowen believes TE Kenyon Sadiq could be a “matchup player” in the Rams offense.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Sadiq out of Oregon is widely expected to be a first round pick after setting record at the NFL Combine. Bowen believes the hyper-athletic tight end could be a situation matchup player for Sean McVay, who used three tight end sets at the NFL’s highest rate in 2025. “With his frame and 4.39 speed, Sadiq could be a seam stretcher for quarterback Matthew Stafford. Plus, McVay could use Sadiq as a backside X receiver/power slot to draw favorable man matchups.” Sadiq, who had 80 receptions over three seasons at Oregon, could fit the LA offense “as a catch-and-run target on boot action concepts,” Bowen said. Stafford last season led the NFL with 75 pass attempts on designed rollouts. It’s a crowded tight end room in LA, with Colby Parikson, Tyler Higbee, Terrance Ferguson, and Davis Allen on the roster. Sadiq would likely function as a rotational player if he lands with the Rams, who have the 13th pick in the 2026 draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Rams signed TE Tyler Higbee to a two-year, $8 million contract extension through 2027.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: The deal prevents Higbee from entering free agency next week. The longtime Rams tight end spent time on injured reserve during the 2025 season, rehabbing an ankle injury. At 33 years old, he is best suited to a rotational role. Fortunately for him, the Rams employ a heavy tight end rotation while regularly calling plays out to 3TE sets. He caught 25-of-35 targets for 281 yards and three touchdowns last season. Higbee is not on the TE1 radar anymore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua caught 17-of-24 targets for 138 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills, adding nine yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua operated as the primary option through the air for a Rams team that attempted more than 50 passes for the third straight game. The veteran alpha was mostly confined to short-area work, something that could be attributed to the groin injury that continues to have his name on the injury report in practice, but that would not keep Nacua from returning another elite WR1 performance. Nacua was also inches away from padding his stat line further after failing to come down with what would have been a 51-yard touchdown reception on the final play of the first half. Nacua and the Rams fall to 2-3 ahead of a Week 6 divisional showdown against the Cardinals, where he will remain one of the top fantasy assets in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua caught 9-of-12 targets for 125 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles, adding a two-yard rushing touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua’s rushing score came on a second quarter end-around. Out there for the first time since Week 1, Nacua did what he always seems to do when active and post a dominant statline. We say “active” rather than “healthy,” as FOX’s Erin Andrews confirmed during the broadcast Nacua is dealing with some sort of sports-hernia situation. That could make him something of a week-to-week proposition but hopefully the superstar wideout has found some way to manage the pain for the rest of the season. He has a Week 5 smash spot in the Bills’ shootout-prone defense. He will also have an extra day to get healthy with the game taking place on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: FOX Sports’ Erin Andrews reports that Puka Nacua has been dealing with a “pre-hernia” injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Andrews broke the news while reporting from the sideline of the Rams’ Week 4 game against the Eagles. Signs have been pointing to this type of injury for a while now, with the Rams referring to Nacua’s nagging injury as both a hip and groin issue. Just over two minutes remain in the third quarter, and Nacua has only come off the field for a few plays thus far. It appears as though the team has handled the injury well, though one imagines re-injury risk is still a factor. That said, he is a WR1 whenever he is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Rams “do not intend to limit” Puka Nacua’s workload in Week 4 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Looks like we’ve got ourselves an old-fashioned source-off here. Schefter says Nacua won’t be limited, while The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero said over the weekend that Nacua may be on “a stricter snap count than usual.” Even if his snaps are cut back, Nacua is one of the best per-route receivers in the NFL. He will get by for fantasy managers in whatever role the Rams give him. He is, at worst, a low-end WR1 for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua (groin) may be on “stricter snap count than usual” in Week 4 against the Eagles, reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Rams HC Sean McVay said Nacua, who has been dealing with a groin injury, is good to go after getting a full practice in on Friday. The coach also noted that they’re still working through Nacua’s snap count and now Pelissero reports that it could be stricter than usual. Fantasy managers should still treat Nacua as a high-end WR1 even in a difficult matchup against the Eagles in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (groin) is “good to go” for Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua will return after getting in a Friday full practice and should be a WR1 play, even against the Eagles’ vaunted secondary. McVay noted that they are still working through how they will navigate his snap count, so Davante Adams should remain near the WR1 line this week as they reintegrate Nacua. But nobody is sitting Puka Nacua in a standard league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams OC Nate Scheelhaase said he expects Puka Nacua (groin) to practice in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Scheelhaase also said that Nacua “twisted” to catch a pass thrown behind him yesterday, which the offensive coordinator took as a good sign. Nacua is on track to face the Eagles in Week 4. As long as he gets through the practice week without suffering a setback, Nacua is an elite WR1 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said he expects WR Puka Nacua (groin) to play in Week 4 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: McVay also said that Nacua will be limited at today’s practice. Nacua has not played since injuring his groin in Week 1 against the 49ers. If active in Week 4, he will be a no-brainer WR1, though it would be great to see him log two full practice sessions over the next two days. The Rams’ pass-catching corps has dealt with an influx of injuries in recent weeks. Getting their star player back would be huge.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said he was “hopeful” WR Puka Nacua (groin) will be able to play in Week 4 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: We continue to get very little concrete news from McVay and the Rams regarding the injury, expected status, or recovery timeline for star wide receiver Puka Nacua. The most conclusive information given the previous two weeks is that the groin injury Nacua is dealing with is not related to the psoas injury he dealt with this offseason, although some have speculated that the verbiage used to describe the injury sounded like a sports hernia. Even that is pure speculation. Fantasy managers are left waiting in the holding pattern for more concrete news from their first-round fantasy selection. Davante Adams would clearly be in line to benefit from another absence after setting a career-high in receiving yards in consecutive games the previous two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua (groin) is inactive for Week 3 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua came into the weekend listed as doubtful but was seen working out before the game to see if he would be able to go. He’ll ultimately be held out for the second consecutive game as the Rams look to improve to 2-1. Davante Adams vaults into the top-tier WR1 range in Nacua’s absence. Also inactive for the Rams are DB Kam Kinchens, WR CJ Daniels, WR Tutu Atwell, QB Ty Simpson, S Maximus Pulley, and OL Bill Murray

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed five times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills, adding 53 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum provided a much needed spark in relief of lead back Kyren Williams, contributing three clutch receptions that kept drives alive in addition to a third quarter touchdown. That said, his modest volume continued while Williams turned in a third straight game with 20 or more opportunities, including 28 total targets in that stretch. Corum remains a top fantasy handcuff but is unlikely to return useful fantasy weeks for as long as Williams is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed five times for 14 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles, adding a seven-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was employed as a pure breather back this afternoon, as he got out-touched 26-6 by Kyren Williams. Four of Corum’s handles came on one first quarter series. With the 1-2 Rams staring down the barrel of 1-3 as they trailed by two scores for several quarters, they circled the wagons around their most established players, and that does not yet include Corum. The third-year pro will undoubtedly pop up for more 10-12 carry afternoons, but he’s fading from FLEX relevance as Williams gets re-established in the low-end RB1 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams need more from Blake Corum in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Atkins believes Puka Nacua’s (groin) impending return will lighten the box, in turn making life easier on the run game and preventing the opposition from blitzing as frequently as the Broncos did last week. Corum has not established himself as a reliable weekly contributor in fantasy. Perhaps positive impacts from Nacua’s return trickle down to the Rams’ No. 2 running back. Kyren Williams remains a locked-in starter. Keep Corum stashed for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 15 times for 88 yards in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos, adding 70 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Williams’ 70 yards through the air were a career-high mark in receiving for a single game, returning yet another RB1 fantasy performance despite sharing backfield work with Blake Corum. Corum managed only 15 yards on six carries and caught two passes for zero additional yards. Furthermore, Corum has still not seen a carry inside the red zone through three games of the 2026 season. Williams remains a surefire RB1 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Eagles in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed 12 times for 79 yards in the Rams’ Week 2 win over the Giants, adding 13 yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was kept out of the end zone for the second straight game to open the 2026 season but continues to display elite per-touch efficiency. The scoring woes could persist considering the robust red zone role of cohort Kyren Williams, the latter of whom found pay dirt for the second consecutive game to open the season. Corum continues to be a difficult weekly start outside of deeper leagues for as long as he is taken off the field where it matters most to fantasy production, and will remain a borderline FLEX start when the Rams face the Broncos in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed 10 times for 54 yards in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was unable to find the end zone while Kyren Williams did, but Corum was the more efficient tailback between the 20s with Williams only tallying 41 yards. He was also a non-factor in the passing game, but the Rams were basically a non-factor in the passing game with Matthew Stafford struggling to figure out the 49ers’ defense. Corum could see more touches in Week 2 against the Giants, but there’s no guarantee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Kyren Williams believes Blake Corum is “a lot leaner” heading into 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: “I would say he’s a lot leaner for sure, he looks a lot more explosive,” was Williams’ exact quote. The Rams’ in-house reporters claim “that explosiveness has been on display all camp.” A disappointing 2024 rookie, Corum successfully earned a 1B role as a sophomore and is pushing for more. It’s still difficult to believe he could crack the top 24 at running back in fantasy, but it is possible he continues to cut into Williams’ top-18 value. Williams and Corum’s workload split will be one of September’s most intriguing early-season storylines.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said Blake Corum will “be a big factor” in the offense this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum took a nice leap in his second season as a pro, posting a 145-746-6 rushing line over 17 games while competing with Kyren Williams for touches every step of the way. Like Corum, Williams was also healthy for 17 games, but that didn’t stop Corum from popping up for a few top-24 PPR finishes last season. Corum’s 9.4 opportunities per game weren’t enough to make him a reliable option in start/sit leagues, as he managed only one double-digit PPR performance from Weeks 1-12, but his production could pave the way for a more even split with Williams this season. It may take some time to determine whether or not we can view Corum as a player who has standalone value this season, but he remains one of the best handcuffs in fantasy playing in an elite offense that could feature him in a high-volume role should Williams ever miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Rams RB Blake Corum “could push for his first 1,000-yard rushing season this year.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Back on May 1st, Atkins predicted Rams coach Sean McVay would deploy starting RB Kyren Williams and Corum in a 50-50 split, with Williams operating as the “primary third-down back and between-the-tackles runner,” while Corum functions as “a change-of-pace option with explosive capabilities.” With spring workouts complete, Atkins is doubling down with minor clarifications. Corum has made strides as a pass protector and receiver, and could “earn more playing time in an offense that wants to blur the run and the pass,” but Williams still remains the superior passing game player and should out-snap Corum because of this. Williams’ “consistency and short-yardage skills” could also keep him on the field in goal-line situations. Williams posted a 259/1,252/10 rushing line while Corum went for 145/746/6. Atkins thinks the two backs could split carries almost 50-50, which would seemingly make a 1,000-yard season doable for Corum. However, Corum’s ceiling outcome is limited if Williams indeed remains the primary player on passing downs and in goal-line situations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins expects Rams RB Blake Corum to operate as “a change-of-pace option with explosive capabilities” in “more of a 50-50 split” this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Rams veteran RB Kyren Williams is expected to be the “primary third-down back and between-the-tackles runner,” which could get him most of the high-value touches. Atkins did not address whether Corum will get a chance to compete for the two-minute drill role, though. That would be big for him. If Corum does manage to take on half of the backfield touches, though, that should be enough to keep him in the low-end RB2, thanks in part to the Rams’ high-scoring offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 16 times for 49 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills, adding 27 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams has yet to see more than the 16 carries he saw against the Bills this season but the team’s recent pass-heavy nature has left the veteran lead back with six or more receptions in three straight games, including 27 total targets in that span. The elite-level aerial volume made it three consecutive games with 20 or more opportunities for Williams, who continues to return RB1 fantasy weeks while playing in one of the league’s top offenses. Williams remains a middling RB1 ahead of a Week 6 divisional showdown against the Cardinals at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 16 times for 80 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles, adding 10 receptions for 66 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams’ 10 receptions were a new career high, while his 26 touches were tied for his seventh most. This, as Blake Corum handled the ball only six times. With Matthew Stafford having trouble against a stout Eagles defense in the rain, he focused on Williams checkdowns, and the strategy actually paid off as the Rams erased a 20-10 halftime deficit. Williams now has 47 touches over the past two weeks after that number was 28 for Weeks 1 and 2. With the Rams off to a shaky start, it’s not surprising they’ve started concentrating touches on their most established weapons. Corum is going to hang around as a nuisance, but Williams has returned himself to the low-end RB1 mix ahead of a likely Week 5 shootout with the Bills.
