https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 12 times for 85 yards in the Rams’ Week 2 win over the Giants, adding 12 yards and a touchdown on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams has opened the season with touchdowns in consecutive games after hitting pay dirt 15 times or more the previous two seasons. The difference this season is that he’s doing it while Blake Corum has been much more involved in the weekly game plan. Williams continues forward with an elevated weekly floor due to his robust red zone role, albeit with a shakier ceiling than in recent years due to the presence of Corum. He remains a back-end RB2 when the Rams travel to Colorado to face the Bronco in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards with a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers while adding three catches for 24 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams’ day was salvaged with a short-yardage score. He finished with one more rushing attempt than Blake Corum, but Corum did look spryer with 54 yards on those attempts. The Rams’ offense just didn’t have it in the Australian showdown, and Williams should see a better box score in Week 2 against the Giants; even if Corum remains a fantasy adversary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Atkins still expects Williams to be the starter. Playing on third down and in the two-minute drill gives running backs an edge in PPR formats. Atkins did not specify which back will play in the latter scenario, but we imagine Williams will get the first crack at the gig. If Williams is also set to be the interior runner, it likely means he gets the first chance in the red zone. He out-snapped No. 2 RB Blake Corum in the red zone, 26-6, during the playoffs last year. That said, losing touches to the point of a 50-50 split hurts his upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 10 times for 39 yards in the Rams’ NFC Championship loss to the Seahawks, adding two catches for 22 yards and a touchdown on his only two targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: It was yet another game where the Rams struggled on the ground, but where Williams’ touchdown-catching prowess was enough to keep him in the scorebook as he got lost on a mesh concept near the end zone. Williams lost his volume back role this year as the Rams gradually started introducing more Blake Corum to the offense in October. He wound up playing 68 percent of the snaps on the season, but it was 63 percent after Week 6. He made up for it by scoring eight touchdowns down the stretch. With a long-term contract secured, there’s no reason Williams can’t be a reasonable RB2 in 2026 — just don’t draft him with the idea that he’s a true volume back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 40-of-54 passes for 383 yards and three touchdowns in the Rams’ 37-34, Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was the third consecutive game in which Stafford attempted 51 passes or more in what has become the most voluminous passing offense in the league. The two powerhouses felt each other out throughout the first half as only 20 combined points per scored before the break. Things would get aggressive for the final 30 minutes as seven combined touchdowns were scored on nine second half possessions, four of which were accounted for by the Rams. Stafford directed a whopping 24 targets toward alpha wide receiver Puka Nacua, who set a career high with 17 receptions in a short-area role. The reigning MVP returned an instant classic performance against the 2024 MVP, ultimately coming up short in overtime following a blocked field goal attempt from Harrison Mevis. The Rams fall to 2-3 ahead of a home matchup against the more forgiving Cardinals in Week 6. Stafford is once again a fantasy QB1 in that matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 32-of-51 passes for 316 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions in the Rams’ 24-20, Week 4 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford put the Rams behind the eight ball with a pair of first half interceptions but was better after the break as the Rams slowly erased a 20-10 deficit. Not that he was amazing, but with the Eagles finishing an inconceivable 0-12 on third down, Stafford needed to make just enough plays, and that’s what he did despite leaving some meat on the bone. It was forgivable on a rainy day in Philly, though Stafford now has at least one interception in all four of his starts. In fact, he has as many scores (six) as picks. Hopefully that trend reverses with Puka Nacua back in the lineup, though the schedule is not lightening up with the Rams hosting the Bills for Monday Night Football in Week 5. That should nevertheless be a fantasy football bonanza.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 30-of-55 passes for 390 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Rams’ 30-26, Week 3 loss to the Broncos, adding 13 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The Rams stormed out to a 16-0 lead they would take into the break but two unanswered scores and two-point conversions from the Broncos saw the game knotted at 16 heading into the fourth quarter, which is where the scoring really took off. Stafford and the Rams appeared to be in control of the game until a Talanoa Hufanga pick-six off Stafford, making 33 career pick-sixes thrown to give him a record he would otherwise not like to have on his ledger. Stafford answered on the following possession on a 48-yard strike to Konata Mumpfield, only for the Broncos to answer back with a Bo Nix rushing score with 47 seconds left to play. Stafford worked more magic to get the team into the red zone, marching the field with only one timeout with a chance to win on the final play of the game. Hufanga ultimately won the play with his second interception off Stafford, sending the Rams to a 1-2 record. Stafford also became the first quarterback in NFL history to throw for 20,000 yards for two different franchises in the loss. Stafford remains a locked-in QB1 in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 4 showdown with the Eagles on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said he’s “not sure” if Puka Nacua (groin) will play in Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: McVay said he’s “hopeful” Nacua, who missed Monday night’s game against the Giants, will be able to suit up against Denver next week. The Rams offense was fine without Nacua on Monday against an injury-ravaged Giants team. LA had the week’s fourth highest EPA per play on the way to a 28-6 win. Another game with Nacua sidelined will mean more target domination for Davante Adams and more involvement for Terrance Ferguson, who caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown against New York.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 22-of-31 passes for 327 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception in the Rams’ 28-6, Week 2 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was an inspiring effort from the 38-year-old quarterback while playing without his top option through the air in Puka Nacua. Stafford locked onto Davante Adams, the latter of whom turned 10 targets into eight receptions for 195 yards and two touchdowns, on his way to a 22nd career game with four touchdown passes. He also moved into sixth on the all-time passing touchdown leaderboard, overtaking Philip Rivers with the four-touchdown performance. The Rams shook off their travel woes in convincing fashion to move to 1-1 ahead of road meeting with the Broncos in Week 3, where Stafford will remain a locked-in QB1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 15-of-25 passes for 155 yards with an interception in the Rams’ 27-7, Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford didn’t get much time to enjoy Australia, and likely won’t leave this contest with fond memories. He completed just 4-of-11 passes in the first half and didn’t do much better in the final 30 minutes, and outside of a 41-yard connection with Puka Nacua, he just couldn’t get the ball downfield. He was also stuffed on a fourth-and-goal run at the goal line to cement the poor day. Credit the 49ers’ defense, but it’s fair to call this a disappointing season debut for the reigning MVP. Expect a rebound in Week 2 against the Giants in a Monday Night Football contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Rams QB Matthew Stafford said retiring from football will be a ‘year-to-year’ decision.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford discussed retirement rumors on Chris Long’s podcast, Green Light . He said a retirement decision would be “year-to-year...committing to more than that feels a little bit daunting and I think a little bit unfair to the team and myself.” The 38-year-old is looking only to the short-term, knowing he is “ready to play this year.” Stafford is not looking to make long-term decisions at this stage of his career without knowing how his body will feel after a season of play. The veteran also mentioned he has talked to Tom Brady and Drew Brees about playing into his 40s and is open to the prospect of doing so. However, Stafford is only focusing on the upcoming season for now; the Rams will be in Super Bowl contention between his return and the addition of Myles Garrett on defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that the Rams plan to manage QB Matthew Stafford’s training camp reps.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford’s degenerative back issue cost him almost all of training camp last year, yet he “returned and cast those fears aside with the best season of his life.” The Rams have reportedly realized how well the time off served Stafford, as a “critical form of load management,” and plan to do some of that again this year. Per Atkins, this has been the plan for some time, and it explains why the Rams tried to sign veteran QBs like Jimmy Garoppolo and Kirk Cousins, “and why they valued the backup role enough to help justify spending the No. 13 pick on QB Ty Simpson.” In other words, don’t be alarmed if we see Simpson taking a few first-team reps this summer. Stafford remains a locked-in QB1. However, we will, of course, track all of his notable offseason developments here at Rotoworld.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay revealed that the team almost placed QB Matthew Stafford (back) on short-term injured reserve to begin the 2025 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford aggravated a disc injury between the offseason workout program and training camp last year. He did not practice until August 18th. Reports on the injury ran the gamut. At one point, The Athletic’s Jourdan Rodrigue reported that the Rams “aren’t worried” about the injury, before later reporting that the back injury “is going to be a thing” all year. Ultimately, time spent in an Ammortal chamber outside the Rams’ facility helped Stafford get ready for an NFL MVP season. Injury risk is, of course, present. But Stafford remains one of the rare pocket passers capable of producing an elite QB1 season. Draft him accordingly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Rams signed QB Matthew Stafford to a one-year, $55 million extension through 2027.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the deal is worth up to $60 million with incentives. He can make up to $105 million over the next two seasons. Stafford, 38, is now the 11th quarterback currently averaging more than $50 million per year. Rams rookie QB Ty Simpson ostensibly now gets two seasons to learn from one of the game’s best pocket passers, while serving as Stafford’s primary backup. Stafford can once again be treated as a locked-in QB1 for fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: The Bills clearly came into this one intent on establishing the run, attempting 37 rushes to just 19 Josh Allen pass attempts in a game played without both DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer. Kincaid has now seen three or fewer targets in each of his last three games after erupting for 225 yards through the air in the first two weeks. The ceiling was never in question, but fantasy managers have to be reeling after three consecutive down performances for the enigmatic tight end. Kincaid remains an upside TE1 ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Bills head coach Joe Brady said he wants to find a way to get more targets for Dalton Kincaid.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid had just two targets in Sunday’s loss to the Patriots after seeing three looks last week against the Chargers. He’s cooled off considerably after a hot start to the 2026 season. “There’s no reason Dalton Kincaid should have two targets, especially with the flow of the game and how that goes,” a visibly frustrated Brady said after Buffalo’s Week 4 loss. “Gotta find a way to get the ball in his hands and do a better job of that.” Against the Patriots Kincaid was targeted on just 8 percent of his routes. He’ll look to bounce back next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: The Bills’ offense was struggling to move the ball during this game, and DJ Moore left early with a shoulder injury, so it’s almost inexcusable that Kincaid wasn’t used more often. Kincaid played one fewer snap than Dawson Knox but ran 22 routes to Knox’s 10. Still, Josh Allen dropped back to throw 40 times, and Khalil Shakir ran a route on 34 dropbacks, so there is no reason for Kincaid to run 12 fewer than that over the whole game. He ran fewer routes than Josh Palmer and only six more routes than Moore, who only played one and a half quarters. The Bills will need to find a way to get Kincaid back into their plans before Monday night’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 2-of-3 passes for 38 yards and a fumble in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid almost had another big catch over the middle of the field for another 15 or more yards, but he was lit up by a safety and dropped the ball at the end of the play. It was the type of hit where you’re just happy that he wound up healthy and able to stay in the game. The 26-year-old later made a nice catch and broke three tackles as he moved closer to the Chargers’ end zone, but the ball was poked out from behind by a chasing defender. Kincaid still ran the second-most routes of any receiver on the Bills and remains a TE1 in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 7-of-8 targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid truly did it all in this one, routinely in the middle of the blocking scrum on long James Cook runs in addition to his work through the air. His 95 yards handily paced the team, with his first touchdown of the young season coming from 16 yards out near the end of the second quarter. Kincaid remains one of the most efficient pass-catchers in the league on a per-route basis and has worked his way into the upper echelon of fantasy assets at the position. He remains a locked-in TE1 when the Bills host the Jets in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said there are no snap restrictions for Dalton Kincaid this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid, according to Fowler, “could be the real key to elevating Josh Allen and the Buffalo offense this season.” Fowler added “multiple people with the team told me Kincaid is healthier than he was this time last year and is on no snap restrictions.” This is further confirmation that Kincaid won’t see the highly restrictive usage of the Sean McDermott era in Buffalo. Head coach Joe Brady is keen on using Kincaid both as an intermediate threat and a downfield option. Kincaid in Week 1 against the Texans led all tight ends in air yards (94) and ran a route on nearly 70 percent of the Bills’ drop backs. He could be an elite every-week option going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 5-of-6 targets for 130 yards in Buffalo’s Week 1 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid was the recipient of many of Josh Allen’s biggest throws of the game, including a 35-yarder to put him over 100 yards on Buffalo’s final non-kneeldown drive. Kincaid played 42-of-57 snaps, a 73 percent rate he never came close to hitting in any game last year. It sure seems like there’s no reason for the Bills to not target him if he can stay healthy; so it will be hard to not recommend him as a TE1 against the Lions on TNF.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia believes Dalton Kincaid could become a “60 to 65 percent snap player” in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: The most efficient tight end in the NFL over the past two seasons, Kincaid ran a pass route on a meager 45 percent of Buffalo’s drop backs over 12 games in 2025, finishing the season with 49 targets while being targeted on a hefty 28 percent of his routes. Finally healthy, Kincaid has been talked up by Bills coaches over the past few months. Bills players and beat writers have even complimented Kincaid’s blocking, a point of concern for the fourth-year tight end. Buscaglia said if Kincaid can “be just competent enough in blocking to preserve the threat of play action when he’s on the field and continue to crush receiving efficiency metrics, he’ll become one of the most important pieces to the roster.” Kincaid is a high upside swing late in drafts for those who fade the game’s top tight ends.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia reports that the Bills TE Dalton Kincaid’s “health, summer usage, and ability are all trending toward an enhanced role in 2026.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid’s 2024 knee injury impacted his usage and availability through the 2025 season. That injury may finally be behind him. Per Buscaglia, Kincaid has been at practice every day, looks stronger and is “playing with more physicality in the blocking game.” That last part is critical for his overall snap share. Kincaid’s increased training camp usage has notably come even with TE Dawson Knox and TE Jackson Hawes fully healthy. Buscaglia adds that Kincaid might not be “on the precipice of playing 75 percent or more of the team’s offensive snaps,” but the 26-year-old tight end should take on a bigger, more fantasy-friendly role this year if all goes well. He’s a locked-in TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Bills TE Dalton Kincaid (knee) said, this is “probably the best” he has ever felt at this point in the year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Earlier this offseason, doctors reportedly advised against surgically repairing the PCL tear Kincaid suffered back in 2024. Instead, Kincaid was told to focus on “setting a good foundation for strength around the knee to support it.” Kincaid believes his failure to properly prepare his body for NFL rigors, and his uneasy feelings about the knee, led to compensatory hamstring issues in 2025, but Kincaid’s new preparations have drawn compliments from Bills coach Joe Brady and QB Josh Allen. Regarding potential load management in-season, Kincaid thinks he and the team can see how his participation this spring and summer goes, rather than preemptively assuming he needs a snap count. Kincaid warrants fringe TE1 treatment if the team keeps him in a limited role. If he can prove his health has turned a corner this summer, he could inch his way up into the mid-TE1 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was largely erased by the lockdown corner play of the Rams but had a receiving line also heavily influenced by a ground-heavy game plan from a Bills team that attempted only 19 passes in almost 70 minutes of football. It was quite the letdown fantasy performance for managers looking to take advantage of the absences of both DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer. Coleman is a borderline FLEX play in Week 6 against the Raiders, pending the status of Moore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Joshua Palmer (shoulder) was added to the injury report on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Palmer seemingly injured his shoulder in practice today. The Bills may already be without WR DJ Moore (shoulder) on Monday night. While Palmer is not relevant in 12-team leagues, his potential absence would improve Keon Coleman’s stock.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman should be good to go for the Bills’ Monday Night Football game against the Rams this week. He had a career day in Week 4, with a 6/116/1 receiving line. We have seen Coleman produce solid outings in the past, so caution is advised if one is to consider believing the hype. That said, he rose to the occasion last week and could do so again in what should be a high-scoring game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 6-of-7 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: This was the best game we’ve seen from Coleman in a long time. Not only did he show up in the box score, but two of his catches were unbelievable sideline grabs that showed the type of hands that made him an intriguing draft pick out of Florida State. He played on 46 of the team’s 59 snaps and ran a route on 31 of their 40 dropbacks. With D.J. Moore leaving this game with a shoulder injury, Coleman is a priority add on waiver wires before next week’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said WR Keon Coleman (ankle) “should be good to play” for Buffalo’s Week 4 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was limited on Thursday after a Wednesday DNP and apparently will avoid a questionable tag. He was questionable last week and played through the injury, though he doesn’t draw enough targets to be fantasy-relevant outside of the deepest leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman missed two practices last week before getting in a limited session on Friday. He still suited up and caught one of his two targets for a 37-yard gain. He will likely see a very limited number of reps in practice again this week. Coleman is not on the fantasy radar for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 1-of-2 targets for 37 yards in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was questionable to play with an ankle injury, but he was out there for 32 of the team’s 66 snaps, which was the third-most among wide receivers. His lone catch was a busted coverage down the sideline where a better throw from Josh Allen could have led to a touchdown. Coleman is playing better football this season, but he remains just an end-of-bench flyer if either DJ Moore or Khalil Shakir were to suffer an injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (ankle) is active for Week 3 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was iffy headed into the weekend with an ankle injury he sustained last week against the Lions. Last week Coleman caught all six of his targets for 63 yards with DJ Moore sidelined with a shoulder issue. Moore is active for Week 3, meaning Coleman should remain on fantasy benches for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Bills declared WR Skyler Bell, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL T.J. Sanders, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive for Week 3 against the Chargers
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Both DJ Moore (shoulder) and Keon Coleman (ankle) were listed as questionable on the final injury report, but both of them will suit up to play. There’s a chance that they could have their snap share managed as they play through injuries, but we’d have to assume they’re both relatively healthy if the Bills are going to put both of them on the field in an early-season matchup. You may just see a little more Khalil Shakir and Josh Palmer usage than normal. Moore remains the receiver with the most fantasy upside and could be a low-end WR2 with Shakir also being a solid WR3 in PPR formats given his role as a lower aDOT target-earner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports Keon Coleman (ankle) is expected to play in Week 3 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman returned to practice on Friday and was listed as questionable for today’s game. DJ Moore (shoulder) also looks likely to play through his questionable tag. Coleman stepped up last week with six catches for 63 yards on six targets. While he’s not on the fantasy radar as long as Moore suits up, Coleman could be a valuable role player for the Bills this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught all three targets for 80 yards in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir’s modest target total was primarily a product of a ground-heavy approach from the Bills, who were playing without both DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer. His quiet fantasy outing was quickly remedied through a 57-yard, catch-and-run reception on the team’s second possession of overtime to set up the game-winning, Tyler Bass field goal. Shakir remains a shaky fantasy bet ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 7-of-8 targets for 82 yards and a fumble in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir served as Josh Allen’s safety blanket for much of the first half, but he was quiet for much of the second half. Most of his production came on a 51-yard catch-and-run, where he broke a few tackles and got the Bills into the red zone. On another catch-and-run opportunity, he had the ball punched out by two Patriots defenders for a crucial fumble. Shakir and Allen were also not on the same page on a key third-down pass that led to a punt. The Bills are going to need more from Shakir if DJ Moore (Shoulder) misses any time, but Shakir did play the second-most snaps of any receiver and ran the most routes, so his role is still there.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 1-of-3 targets for six yards in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: The Bills’ offense was totally out of sorts in this game, and Shakir was hurt by their inability to get anything going through the air. Still, he played on 45 of their 62 snaps and ran a route on 23 of their 33 dropbacks, the second-most of any wide receiver. He’ll be in for a better game against the Patriots next week, but he remains just a desperation FLEX play right now unless the Bills are headed for a shootout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 3-of-6 targets for 38 yards in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir continued in a gadgety role for the Bills, primarily working the short areas of the field in addition to receiving snaps out of the backfield. That could change in the immediate future after lead receiver DJ Moore departed in the second quarter with what appeared to be a significant shoulder injury. Even so, Shakir is best left on the waiver wire in all but the deepest fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 4-of-6 targets for 50 yards in Buffalo’s Week 1 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: The good news is he was healthy enough to play after he was seemingly sidelined towards the end of training camp with something the Bills never disclosed. He played 30-of-57 snaps. The bad news is that if Dalton Kincaid is going to be this involved, it’s not likely that Shakir will be targeted enough to crack the WR3 ranks. A lot can change — and Kincaid isn’t known for his durability — but it was a “meh” debut for Shakir as he fell behind Kincaid and DJ Moore in the passing pecking order.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia reports that Bills WR Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) is on the practice field on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: This is good news. Shakir has been sidelined for multiple weeks, rehabbing an undisclosed injury. His return today puts him on track to play in Week 1 against the Texans’ top-tier defense. Whether Shakir can be a reliable FLEX with WR DJ Moore now in Buffalo and TE Dalton Kincaid reportedly set to take on a larger role remains to be seen. Getting back on the field is the first step, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports “there’s currently optimism” from the Bills that Khalil Shakir will play in Week 1 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir has been held out of practice for multiple weeks with an undisclosed injury. He has gotten some work off to the side, though it’s becoming more concerning with each day he fails to work in with the team. According to Zenitz, the team is simply being cautious with Shakir. We’ll learn more about his ailment when the first official injury report comes out next week. Like the Bills, fantasy managers should take a cautious approach with Shakir in the final week of drafts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Neither did Ty Johnson (knee), with both players still having plenty of time to get back before next Sunday’s Week 1 game against the Texans. It’s hard to tell how seriously to take these because Joe Brady has been a brick wall on injury questions, but we’ll get a better indication next week when injury reports start to hit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir has been sidelined from Bills practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir was sidelined from Tuesday’s special practice at Highmark Stadium and hasn’t suited up since. Coach Joe Brady did not divulge the nature of the injury. Like most ailments this time of year, it’s probably a minor issue where the team is opting for caution, but it’s good to “timestamp” these things, so to speak. Barely going in the WR5 range, 26-year-old Shakir could easily outproduce his ADP, though probably not to the extent he cracks the top 36.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: The Athletic Football Show’s Dave Helman believes Bills WR Skyler Bell could be “Ja’Marr Chase lite” in the NFL.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Taken by Buffalo with the 125th pick in the 2026 draft, Bell — a hyper-productive wideout at UConn — joins DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir, Josh Palmer, and Keon Coleman in an underwhelming receivers room. Bell, Helman said, enters the NFL with a multifaceted skill set that is highly valued among most NFL front offices. “This is probably the most reckless thing I’ll say on this show,” Helman said. “This is Ja’Marr Chase lite. He’s a freak athlete, he’s explosive, but he’s very powerful and strong. And watching him, I was just like, obviously, he’s not Ja’Marr Chase ... but he does all that type of stuff. He can take it to the house. He can just body people out of the way. He can high point the ball. If I was trying to get Ja’Marr Chase’s skillset on late day two or even into day three, I’m all the way in on this guy.” Helman wasn’t alone in his praise of Bell, who last season was second among all college wideouts in yards per route run. Ryan Fowler of NBC Sports Philadelphia said in March that Bell, 23, was close to a Round One prospect. The Bills took him late on the third day of the draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 12-of-19 passes for 210 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Bills’ 37-34, Week 5 win over the Rams, adding 121 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: The two teams mustered only 20 combined points in the first half as they felt each other out. There were only two punts after the break between the two sides, who combined for seven touchdowns on nine combined possessions including five straight touchdowns in the fourth quarter to send the game to overtime. Allen and the Bills took the ball first in the extra frame and quickly found themselves deep in enemy territory following a 57-yard, catch-and-run pass to Khalil Shakir. A James Cook fumble on the next play appeared to shatter Allen’s chances of earning his first career win in overtime, but a blocked 48-yard field goal attempt from Harrison Mevis gave the ball back to the Bills with a chance to win. Two Josh Allen scrambles set up a game-winning, 45-yard field goal for Tyler Bass. Allen ended with the second most yards on the ground of his career as the Bills moved to 4-1 with the wild win. Allen remains the top overall quarterback in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 23-of-33 passes for 253 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Bills’ 29-26 Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Allen did score a rushing touchdown, but he had just four rushing yards on five carries, making this the second straight game that he was contained as a rusher. Every time Allen rolled out, the Patriots had a defender in the lane, and Allen wasn’t able to make his usual big plays with his arm. Once D.J. Moore left the game with a shoulder injury, it felt like none of the Bills’ receivers were able to create space with their defenders, much like we saw for all of 2025. Allen’s interception was an egregious decision on the final drive of the game, where he made an impressive spin move to avoid a sack and then chucked an unnecessary Hail Mary into double coverage. You’re still starting Allen in fantasy leagues, but it’s a bit concerning that we’ve seen the Bills’ offense look scattered and out of sync for two straight games. It won’t get easier on Monday against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 16-of-26 passes for 204 yards and two interceptions in the Bills’ 24-16, Week 3 win over the Chargers, adding 22 yards rushing and two touchdowns on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Allen certainly wasn’t good in this one, but he wasn’t alone. The Bills turned the ball over five times, committed 10 penalties, and allowed four sacks and somehow won this game. His first interception was on a truly bad read over the middle of the field. The second was on a deep pass into coverage when Allen thought he had drawn an offside. The pass managed to hit the safety in the back and then land in his stomach when he rolled over after hitting the ground. Allen would also fumble on a sack later in the game. The Chargers did a good job of taking Allen’s scrambles away, and this entire Bills team was in disarray, so nobody was consistently open down the field. That being said, Allen’s two rushing touchdowns give him 85 for his career, which means he’s now tied with former Bill Marshawn Lynch for 17th on the NFL’s all-time list. The Bills and Allen will look to get things straightened out against the Patriots next week, and Allen will clearly be in your lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 20-of-31 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns in the Bills’ 41-31, Week 2 win over the Lions, adding 69 yard and two touchdowns on 14 carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Was it ever a doubt that Super Josh would make an appearance in the franchise’s first game in their new stadium? To the utter dismay of James Cook fantasy managers, Allen accounted for three touchdowns from inside the five against the Lions, two with his legs and one with his arm, extending his NFL-record for games with multiple rushing touchdowns and multiple passing touchdowns to 10 in the process. The unquestioned overall QB1 in fantasy circles continues to prove the doubters wrong as the Bills surge to 2-0 atop the AFC ahead of a home meeting with the Chargers in Week 3. Allen remains a top-tier fantasy asset until pigs fly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 20-of-29 passes for 334 yards and two touchdowns in the Bills’ 36-31, Week 1 win over the Texans, adding 23 yards and two touchdowns on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Some had suggested you might want to bench Josh Allen against the Texans defense this week. Instead, Allen absolutely decimated last year’s top defense with a game-winning stick throw to the post for Josh Palmer to take a late five-point lead. He did his typical witchcraft out of structure, the best of which was probably a floater in his own end zone with a man in his face that landed directly on Dalton Kincaid’s hands. He also owned the ground game in the red zone. It was the first Bills win in Houston since the JP Losman Era. Allen, as always, will be in the QB1 overall discussion against the Lions in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia said he would not be surprised if DJ Moore is “on the field constantly and for [Josh] Allen to default to looking his way.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Buscaglia called Moore, who was acquired from the Bears this spring, the “crown jewel of the offseason” for the Bills front office. “Moore’s contributions to the offense within training camp were immediate and obvious,” Buscaglia said. “Allen routinely pushed the ball downfield to Moore, making a concerted effort all summer to build on-field chemistry with the Bills’ new No. 1 receiver. ... The days of ‘everybody eats’ seem to be in the rearview mirror.” It’s a bullish report — one that could mean Moore is among the best values in redraft leagues this season even after being among the NFL’s most inefficient wideouts in 2025. Moore should be in all 12-team lineups for Week 1 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports Josh Allen and “most Bills starters” will sit for Saturday’s preseason game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: After a good week of joint practices against the Browns, the Bills are expected to sit most of their starters while giving their depth players a chance to show what they have. Veteran QB Kyle Allen will draw the start on Saturday, with backup Shane Buechele also expected to see work. The Bills’ decision to sit their starters should come as good news for Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson, who are still battling for the QB1 job, with Sanders in line to start with the first-team offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: The Athletic Football Show’s Dave Helman believes Bills WR Skyler Bell could be “Ja’Marr Chase lite” in the NFL.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Taken by Buffalo with the 125th pick in the 2026 draft, Bell — a hyper-productive wideout at UConn — joins DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir, Josh Palmer, and Keon Coleman in an underwhelming receivers room. He’s a freak athlete, he’s explosive, but he’s very powerful and strong. And watching him, I was just like, obviously, he’s not Ja’Marr Chase ... but he does all that type of stuff. He can take it to the house. He can just body people out of the way. He can high point the ball. If I was trying to get Ja’Marr Chase’s skillset on late day two or even into day three, I’m all the way in on this guy.” Helman wasn’t alone in his praise of Bell, who last season was second among all college wideouts in yards per route run. Ryan Fowler of NBC Sports Philadelphia said in March that Bell, 23, was close to a Round One prospect. The Bills took him late on the third day of the draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Bills HC Joe Brady said Josh Allen (foot) is “good to go” to participate in the team’s offseason program.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Allen underwent surgery to repair a broken bone in his foot, but two months post-op, the Bills’ QB1 appears to be in good shape. The Bills went out and traded for WR DJ Moore this offseason to give Allen a much-needed weapon in the passing game, and with Allen trending in the right direction, he should have plenty of time to build with Moore before training camp ramps up earlier this summer. Allen has finished as the QB1 in fantasy points per game in four of his last six seasons and projects as a high-end QB1 again this upcoming season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Bills restructured Josh Allen’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Per ESPN’s Field Yates, the move creates $40 million in cap space. As is the case with most elite quarterbacks, Allen’s contract being restructured has become an annual affair for Buffalo. This is essentially free cap space for the Bills. With the deadline to get cap compliant coming later today, Buffalo now has plenty of wiggle room to sign free agents or extend other players. Allen is under contract through the 2030 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.headline: Rams declared WR CJ Daniels, QB Ty Simpson, TE Max Klare, DE Larrell Murchison, and OL Bill Murray inactive for Week 5 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.analysis: Klare had been active from Week 2 through Week 4 but retreats to the inactives list with Colby Parkinson returning from a one-game absence. Puka Nacua’s absence Week 2 and Week 3 could have also played a role in Klare’s game-day status during that period, with the Rams now set to face the Bills with just three active tight ends after going through multiple games with either four or five active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.headline: Rams declared WR Tutu Atwell, WR CJ Daniels, OL Bill Murray, TE Max Klare and QB Ty Simpson inactive for Week 1 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.analysis: The Rams acquired Atwell via trade in August. Although he already knows the system, coach Sean McVay evidently feels that Atwell is unnecessary for this one. Incumbent QB Stetson Bennett has officially defeated Simpson for the QB2 job. Simpson is inactive, but has been labeled the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins thinks the Rams selected TE Max Klare “in the second round this year to get ahead of the learning curve” for a potential role in 2027.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.analysis: The Rams field a deep tight end room, and Atkins expects the personnel to undergo turnover in the next year or so. Second-year TE Terrance Ferguson could function as the de facto No. 3 wide receiver while TE Colby Parkinson continues “to be a focal point on third downs and in the red zone in this three-tight end offense” this season. He adds that Klare could get involved on “some yards-after-catch designs and wrinkles this season,” but it does not sound like Klare is due for a fantasy-friendly role in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Terrance Ferguson “has some of the best breakout potential of current Rams players who haven’t done so yet.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.analysis: Atkins added, “The ideal outcome for him is to lead their tight ends in catches and yards.” He noted that the coaching staff was focused on bringing Ferguson along incrementally in 2025. Now they will have the chance to move him into a more prominent role for his second season. Ferguson only caught 11 passes as a rookie, but he parlayed a seam-stretching role into 231 yards and three scores despite the low reception total. Atkins sees Ferguson as a de facto No. 3 receiver for the team, with Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee both fulfilling the role of a traditional inline tight end. Rookie Max Klare will also be in the mix for snaps, but will likely be brought along slowly as well. With an ADP that barely even registers in early best ball drafts, Ferguson is worth a look as a high-upside TE3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.headline: Rams selected Ohio State TE Max Klare with the No. 61 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.analysis: Klare (6’4/246) was a four-star recruit for Purdue and played a reserve role as a freshman. He only appeared in five games as a sophomore before an ankle injury ended his season. Klare finally broke out with a 51/685/4 receiving line in his third outing. As is often the case in the current college football landscape, Klare’s breakout made him a hot name in the transfer portal and the Buckeyes picked up the phone. Klare’s numbers tanked at Ohio State, though playing alongside at least two potential NFL stars in Carnell Tate and Jeremiah Smith is a reasonable alibi. He went for 448 yards and just two touchdowns. Despite the counting stats taking a hit, Klare likely improved his draft stock by bulking up for a more traditional tight end role. He increased his rate of inline routes and improved as a run-blocker. After rounding out his skill set at Ohio State, Klare looks ready to contribute on an NFL field out of the gates.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.headline: Ohio State TE Max Klare has made five top-30 visits ahead of the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.analysis: Per NBC Sports Houston’s Aaron Wilson, Klare has met “extensively” with the Texans, Buccaneers, Rams, Broncos and Panthers. Klare could be the second tight drafted next week, profiling as a potential every-down player. Although he performed better as a receiver at Purdue in 2024, he earned a respectable 71.6 PFF run-blocking grade at Ohio State last year. Klare could be a year one contributor, but he is not guaranteed to reach the TE1 ranks in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.headline: Ravens executive vice president and general manager Eric DeCosta thinks there is a “strong chance” his team selects two tight ends in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.analysis: Ravens team reporter Ryan Mink adds that although TE Mark Andrews posted a career-low 422 receiving yards last season, “the Ravens see a rebound in 2026.” DeCosta’s comments could indicate otherwise, though the team lost TEs Isaiah Likely and Charlie Kolar in free agency. Mink also notes that the Ravens have picked two tight ends in the same draft four times in franchise history: 2022, 2018, 2015 and 2010. DeCosta has been with the Ravens for his whole career, dating back to 1996, and the strategy has worked well for the organization. Mink believes replacing Likely with a receiving tight end could be viewed as a need in the short term. He lists 10 potential draftees, including Oregon TE Kenyon Sadiq, Ohio State TE Max Klare, Vanderbilt TE Eli Stowers, Baylor TE Michael Trigg and NC State TE Justin Joly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.headline: Broncos hosted Ohio State TE Max Klare for a top-30 visit.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/max-klare/.analysis: This is the second incoming rookie tight end the Broncos have brought in for a top-30 visit this week. The position remains an area of need despite head coach Sean Payton spending the last three years trying to find a Joker. In his final college season, Klare caught 41-of-53 targets for 420 yards and two touchdowns. Per 9News’ Mike Klis, Klare could potentially be the second tight end drafted this year and is “arguably the most well-rounded.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Browns signed RB Audric Estime from the Vikings’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Estime’s signing comes as Quinshon Judkins is dealing with an ankle injury he suffered in Week 5. Estime, who is only 23 years old, already feels like an NFL journeyman as he now heads to his fifth team in three seasons after brief stints with the Broncos, Eagles, Saints, and Vikings. The former fifth-round pick has rushed for 508 yards and three touchdowns in his career and rushed for 76-310-2 as a rookie with the Broncos. Estime could see snaps in Week 6 against the Ravens if Judkins is unable to play, but we wouldn’t expect to see anything close to a meaningful workload at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints placed Kelvin Banks (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The team signed long snapper Cal Adomitis and reached an injury settlement with running back Audric Estime in corresponding moves. Banks is undergoing surgery for a severe high-ankle sprain. He could return later this year, but the team will be without their starting left tackle for at least four games, and likely much longer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Alvin Kamara (knee) is questionable to play in Week 1 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kamara logged two limited sessions to begin the week, and New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill said he thinks Kamara will play, barring a setback. We do not yet know Kamara’s practice participation level on Friday, but he is traveling with the team, which is a good sign. Kamara would be a PPR FLEX if active. He is expected to play on passing downs while starting RB Travis Etienne leads the team in carries. Etienne is the best bet to handle the primary red zone role, but Kamara has been a prolific touchdown scorer over his career and could factor in. The Saints ruled out RB Audric Estime (thigh).

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Kendre Miller (back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Saints’ backup running back statuses continue to change. Veteran No. 2 RB Alvin Kamara (knee) is expected to be sidelined for at least one month, and RB Audric Estime is now sidelined with an undisclosed injury. Miller and RB Devin Neal (hamstring) both returned this week, though. Beat reporter Jeff Nowak notes that Miller, Neal and RB Ty Chandler were all allowed to rotate in for first-team reps today, as coach Kellen Moore presumably seeks out a viable primary backup for starting RB Travis Etienne. Per Nowak, Miller “looks sharp despite the time missed.” This is worth tracking for short-term bench stash purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Kendre Miller (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The good news is that Miller was not listed with a knee injury after suffering a season-ending ACL tear in Week 7 last year. The bad news is that he evidently has a new injury, and the Saints have a fairly deep running back room right now. RBs Devin Neal, Audric Estime, Ty Chandler and CJ Donaldson are all vying for roster spots. Per Underhill, Neal is taking advantage of the extra reps. He could have the inside track to the RB3 role right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Audric Estime rushed 21 times for 63 yards in the Saints’ Week 18 loss to the Falcons, adding five receptions for 43 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Playing out the string for the Saints’ injury-ruined backfield, Estime reached 100 yards from scrimmage for the first time in his career after posting 98 the week before. Not a bad end to the year for a player who spent the first half of the season on practice squads. Still only 22 years old, Estime is buying himself time to get established in the NFL, but he still probably mostly profiles as a special teamer if he’s going to make a 53-man roster out of camp. Considering the Saints’ issues at running back, it could very well be in New Orleans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Alvin Kamara (knee/ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The team opted not to place Kamara on injured reserve, though he has been sidelined since Week 12. Unless something drastic occurs, Saints RB Audric Estime will start in Kamara’s stead against the Falcons on Sunday. Both teams have been eliminated from the playoffs, but it still gives coaches a chance to evaluate key players one last time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints RB Alvin Kamara (knee/ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kamara has neither practiced nor played since spraining his MCL in Week 12. He was already dealing with an ankle injury at that time. We expect him to remain sidelined in Week 18 against the Falcons. Saints RB Audric Estime will again operate as the team’s starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Audric Estime rushed 14 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 17 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Estime ceded the first carry of the day to Taysom Hill. After Hill easily out-carried him last week, it looked like that would be the case again versus Tennessee. The Saints quickly threw in the towel on Hill and handed the backfield over to Estime. He punctuated a solid day with a 32-yard sprint into the end zone in the fourth quarter. The touchdown gave New Orleans an eight-point lead that Tennessee never erased. Estime should hold this role into Week 18, giving him some RB2 juice versus the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints ruled out RB Alvin Kamara (ankle/knee) for Week 17 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This leaves RB Audric Estime as the nominal starter, though TE Taysom Hill logged 16 touches to Estime’s eight last week. The Saints apparently wanted to feature Hill in Week 16, in what could be his final home game as a Saint. Projecting each player’s Week 17 role is difficult. Neither one should be considered a confident play, though the Titans’ defense is unimposing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Kirk Cousins is the starter “but if Fernando [Mendoza]'s number is called we have confidence in him.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: No real surprise after Mendoza’s mop-up appearance in Week 5. It doesn’t appear that he’s taken a major step towards unseating Cousins — who has played well — just yet. But it remains a reasonable bet to happen in the near future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Fernando Mendoza completed 6-of-8 passes for 48 yards in relief of Kirk Cousins in Las Vegas’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This doesn’t necessarily mean that Mendoza is going to take the reins this week; we expect Cousins to continue starting even if Raiders coach Klint Kubiak didn’t affirmatively get ahead of the situation in Sunday’s post-game. But Mendoza looked reasonable and this will obviously be something that will bubble up eventually. No. 1 overall picks don’t typically stay on benches too long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders named Kirk Cousins as the team’s Week 1 starter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: With input from Tom Brady, head coach Klint Kubiak will put the 38-year-old Cousins under center for the season opener against the Dolphins. Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, will serve as Cousins’ backup. How long this arrangement will last is anyone’s guess. A good start to the regular season could delay Mendoza’s first NFL start for a couple months but he’s almost certain to take over as the Vegas starter at some point in 2026. Mendoza should be stashed in most superflex formats and Cousins profiles as a decent QB2 in such formats for Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said he’s talking with Tom Brady “multiple times per week” about the team’s starting quarterback situation.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: An NFL head coach consulting with an NFL announcer on who his team should start under center is a brave new world for the league. It looks like the Raiders are set on Kirk Cousins to start Week 1 against the Dolphins after Fernando Mendoza’s spotty preseason play and struggles in training camp. Look for Cousins to target his short-area pass catchers relentlessly, like he did last year in Atlanta. It won’t be long before Mendoza gets a shot at starting duties. He should be rostered in most superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Raiders QB Kirk Cousins is expected to be named the starter eventually.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Appearing on NFL Live Friday afternoon, Fowler said that people inside the Raiders’ building and around the league still expect Cousins to be named the starter. Raiders HC Klint Kubiak declined to name a starting quarterback Friday morning. Following the loss of Thursday’s preseason game against the 49ers, Kubiak said rookie Fernando Mendoza needs another three preseason games before going as far as mentioning that Mendoza’s practice reps will decline once the regular season begins. While Kubiak continues to drag his feet when it comes to the official announcement, all signs still point to Cousins being named the starter at some point eventually.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Speaking after Thursday’s preseason game, Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said “I still don’t think we need to name anybody” when asked about who his starter will be in Week 1 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: That’s three straight weeks that Kubiak has declined to name his Week 1 starter despite the widely held belief that it will be Kirk Cousins getting the start in Week 1 against the Dolphins. Cousins has received the majority of first-team reps throughout the offseason and limited action in the preseason, while Fernando Mendoza has worked mostly with backups and played extensively in every preseason game. We’ll see just how long Kubiak is willing to stretch this decision out, but it would come as a surprise to almost everyone if Mendoza got the nod over Cousins in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders QB Kirk Cousins completed 8-of-11 passes for 51 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak declined to name a starting quarterback last week (and again this evening), but Cousins certainly received starter treatment this evening. He played two series, along with the Raiders’ other starters, before being subbed out for QB Fernando Mendoza. The rookie quarterback is playing well. He shares fault with WR Jalen Nailor for the interception. The throw was late, and Nailor tipped it to a 49ers defender. The 49ers’ pass rush also got home a few times against Mendoza as well. Cousins looks like the early-season starter at this time, but stashing Mendoza on benches in superflex leagues could eventually pay off.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak declined to name a starting QB after the team’s second preseason game against the Texans on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kirk Cousins didn’t play a snap in Thursday night’s game, but despite the decision not to dress his veteran QB, Kubiak opted not to commit to a starter just yet. Rookie Fernando Mendoza played the entire first half of yesterday’s game, completing 8-of-15 passes for 86 yards, with one of his incompletions resulting in an 80-yard pick-six. It’s long been believed that the Raiders’ plan entering this season was to go with Cousins as the starter before eventually making the move to Mendoza later in the year. While that may still end up being how things unfold, Kubiak’s decision not to name a starter on a night when several starters sat has raised questions ahead of the team’s third and final preseason game next week against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders RB Mike Washington rushed nine times for 56 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Texans, adding two receptions for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Washington looked good once again this week. His best play was an explosive gain on the Raiders’ first drive. Washington ran into the back of the line briefly but bounced off contact and took off downfield for a 33-yard gain. He was tackled by his shoestrings on the Texans’ 25-yard line. Unfortunately, the next play wasn’t great. Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza decided to check down to Washington on a play-action dropback, but the pass was intercepted and returned for an 80-yard touchdown. Texans LB Wade Woodaz made a great play on the ball. Washington possibly could have done a better job of maintaining spatial awareness and boxing Woodaz out, but the result of the play does not fall entirely on Washington’s shoulders. The rookie running back could offer standalone FLEX value this season. At worst, he is a high-upside stash.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Ryan McFadden reports Raiders coaches want Fernando Mendoza to improve his timing and anticipation.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This comes on the heels of Mendoza impressing Vegas coaches in his preseason debut, completing ten of his 16 attempts for 97 yards and a touchdown against Arizona. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said after the game that the team’s Week 1 starting gig was still Kirk Cousins’ to lose. It appears Mendoza, with another solid preseason performance, could challenge for that top spot. Kubiak will be watching the rookie’s anticipation closely when Vegas takes on the Texans on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Ben Skowronek (leg) has been ruled out for Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: We weren’t exactly worried about Skowronek siphoning many targets away, but with him out of the pecking order entirely Germie Bernard should be a wheels-up WR3 for Week 6 now that both Skowronek and Roman Wilson have been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek has been ruled out for Week 5 against the Colts with a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: There hasn’t been a lot of word on what happened to Skowronek. He went into the blue medical tent in the second quarter to have his leg looked at and then headed into the locker room. When the Steelers returned the kickoff to start the second half, Skowronek, who is a key special teamer, was not on the field. He was ruled out shortly after. With Michael Pittman Jr. already out, the Steelers are getting a little thin with their wide receiver depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek caught his only target for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 1 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: It was a play-action pass where Skowronek went against the flow of the defense and it almost operated like a screen, with Steelers receivers blocking downfield to create an easy crease for the 28-year-old receiver. Skowronek doesn’t need to be chased in fantasy leagues after only playing 10 of 53 snaps for the Steelers in this one. He’s operating more-or-less in a timeshare for Pittsburgh’s third receiver role with Roman Wilson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers re-signed WR Ben Skowronek to a two-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek caught five passes for 69 yards with the Steelers last season while playing in a very limited role. Skowronek’s 46 routes run and five targets marked the second fewest amongst any receiver on the team in 2024. A good blocker and willing special teamer, Skowronek probably has an inside track to a roster spot even if what he does isn’t worthy of fantasy interest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers WR Ben Skowronek (hip) is questionable to return to Week 16 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek was involved early, catching both targets for 25 yards, but departed early in the second quarter with a hip injury and was deemed questionable to return by the team. Already shorthanded at wide receiver due to the continued absence of George Pickens, it will be up to Calvin Austin, Van Jefferson, and Mike Williams to step up for a team fighting to clinch the AFC North against their great division rivals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers elevated WR Ben Skowronek for Week 2 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: The team also elevated Skowronek in Week 1, but he wasn’t a factor against the Falcons and shouldn’t be one this week either. If anything, it’s likely not a good sign for the chances that rookie WR Roman Wilson makes his NFL debut this weekend. Skowronek will have most of his value of special teams this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers elevated WR Ben Skowronek for Week 1 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek should fill a depth role on offense while contributing to special teams and is not in the fantasy discussion for Week 1 barring injury. The elevation likely has a lot to do with rookie Roman Wilson’s absence for Sunday for a team lacking in depth at the wide receiver position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers signed RB Boston Scott, formerly of the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Scott was let go by the Rams during final roster cutdowns and now lands with the Steelers. The veteran running back won’t be threatening for offensive snaps any time soon but could earn a look as a returner if somebody were to miss time with an injury. In addition to Scott, the Steelers also signed wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Brandon Johnson to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Texans released Ben Skowronek.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek signed with the Texans earlier this offseason after spending the first three years of his career with the Rams. The former seventh-round pick has caught 58 passes for 575 yards and one touchdown in his career and can be used both outside and in the slot. Skowronek also has valuable special teams experience and could find himself on another roster in the near future. The Texans also waived/released DT McTelvin Agim, LB Tarique Barnes, EDGE Solomon Byrd, WR Quintez Cephus, OG Dieter Eiselen, EDGE Malik Fisher, EDGE Ali Gaye, FB Troy Hairston, DT Marcus Harris, WR Johnny Johnson III, CB Troy Pride, RB J.J. Taylor, LB Max Tooley and OT Kilian Zierer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Texans acquired WR Ben Skowronek from the Rams in exchange for draft picks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: It was rumored earlier in the day that the Rams were planning to release Skowronek, who was a seventh-round pick from the 2021 class. Now, the Rams are set to deal Skowronek and a 2026 seventh-round pick to the Texans in exchange for a 2026 sixth-round pick. Skowronek, who has a receiving line of 58-575-1 through 45 career games, joins a crowded receiver room in Houston but can provide added depth both out wide and in the slot. He’s made 12 starts in his career but has surpassed 50 receiving yards just once in his career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore, asked directly if Tyler Shough’s non-throwing hand is broken, said “it got banged two weeks ago and he’s just wearing some protective layers there.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: So, probably, then. The hand hasn’t really been a contributing factor to New Orleans’ decline so much as the Saints offensive line has just been in the blender for two weeks against Atlanta and Minnesota’s fronts, but it sure looks like Shough is managing through something and we should probably break ties against him in the rankings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 16-of-25 passes for 96 yards and two interceptions in the Saints’ 23-13, Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough had been coasting on extreme play volume over the first month of the fantasy season. Brian Flores and the Vikings’ hyper-aggressive defense had no issues shutting down that approach. The Saints had five drives in the first half. Only one lasted longer than three plays. Of their four second-half drives, two ended with interceptions. A fumbled kickoff coming out of the break didn’t help the team’s play volume either. Shough has ultimately been a better fantasy quarterback than a real-life passer this year and the Vikings’ defense exposed that truth for the better part of four quarters. He will look to rebound against a far worse Giants unit in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough (hand) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As expected, he’ll start and be on the QB1/QB2 borderline against an extremely pesky and attacking Vikings defense that has held down quarterback scoring quite well so far this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough (hand) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As a right-handed quarterback, Shough should be fine despite his surprise appearance on the injury report. Even in a blowout loss on Monday, the second-year passer racked up 286 yards and a touchdown on 48 attempts. As long as the volume is there, Shough is good for low-end QB1 numbers. He will remain inside the top 12 at his position for Week 5 against Minnesota.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 30-of-48 passes for 286 yards and one touchdown in the Saints’ 45-24, Week 4 loss to the Falcons, adding five yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough and the Saints stayed true to recent form as they quickly fell into a 14-point hole in the first quarter, with the team now averaging an almost eight point deficit at the half since head coach Kellen Moore took over to start the 2025 season. The team was unable to reproduce the second half magic they so frequently muster behind an overmatched offensive line. Shough needed a late touchdown toss to Devaughn Vele with less than two minutes to play to give fantasy managers something of value. Moore and Shough have their work cut out for them with Brian Flores’ relentless defense coming to town in Week 5, where Shough will be on the QB1/2 border in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 29-of-42 passes for 255 yards, four touchdowns and one interception in the Saints’ 27-35, Week 3 loss to the Raiders, adding one rush for 36 yards and two lost fumbles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough funneled four touchdown passes to Saints TEs Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant, bringing the game’s total to six tight end touchdowns, which tied a league record. The Saints’ quarterback played well overall, though his interception was due to a poor throw. Both fumbles were caused by Raiders pass rushers, and Shough had a third fumble reversed by an illegal contact penalty on the Raiders. Regardless, he can be trusted to throw the ball voluminously while adding a little extra with his legs. He warrants low-end QB1 treatment against the Falcons next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 27-of-34 passes for 252 yards and one touchdown in the Saints’ 24-17, Week 2 win over the Ravens, adding nine carries for 23 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough played mistake-free football all afternoon, chipping away at the Ravens’ defense before leading his team to 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to secure the win. Shough repeatedly connected with Chris Olave all afternoon, and he found the star receiver uncontested in the end zone for his lone touchdown. Shough punched in a one-yard score on a QB sneak with 1:21 left to put the Saints up 24-17 and complete the upset of the Ravens on the road. It wasn’t an overly flashy outing by Shough, but he was efficient against a stout Ravens defense, which still managed three sacks on the day. He’s now strung together two strong fantasy performances and will be on the radar as a high-end QB2 next week against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 35-of-56 passes for 410 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Saints’ 30-31, Week 1 overtime loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough was nearly seeing ghosts in the first half. The Saints had zero points and their longest drive resulted in 36 yards with a punt. Then, in the second half, Shough turned the ball over on each of his first two drives. The game looked truly over at this point, but Shough battled back and got points on the board on each of his next four drives. Detroit played passively on defense and Shough routinely punished them with long throws to Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. Shough nearly won the game with a touchdown pass to Noah Fant in overtime. Kellen Moore went for two and Shough was unable to find his target in the back of the end zone. With the first-half rust hopefully shaken off, Shough will be a high-end QB2 versus the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill believes Saints WR Jordyn Tyson’s route running strengths fit well with QB Tyler Shough’s passing preferences.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Underhill compared Tyson’s best routes with Shough’s highest-targeted areas of the field and declared, “it’s the same diagram.” Coincidentally, Tyson’s route tree closely overlaps with that of No. 1 WR Chris Olave. Underhill believes that this dynamic will allow coach Kellen Moore to use Tyson and Olave interchangeably. They will both line up in the perimeter and in the slot. Underhill believes Olave will remain the team’s top pass catcher “for the near future,” but eventually both he and Tyson will work as two “top receivers.” Tyson missed most of spring practices with a hamstring injury, but Underhill said he will not worry about the issue unless Tyson misses training camp. Underhill closed the segment by saying a 55/700/5 receiving line on 90 targets is a “safe projection” for Tyson’s rookie season, though he believes Tyson is capable of doing more. The “safe” stat line equates to 155.0 PPR points and would have made him the WR40 last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill believes Saints QB Tyler Shough will finish among the top-12 quarterbacks in passing yards this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Underhill’s colleagues, Mike Triplett and John Hendrix, agree. Triplett was the most bearish of the bunch, saying he is not sure that Shough will be able to crack the position’s top 10. Underhill notes that Vegas sports books have Shough in a five-way tie for the sixth-best odds to lead the NFL in passing yards. He adds that he is “not sure” if he can get to sixth, but he knows for sure that he can’t get to 13th. Shough was the QB10 in per-game fantasy scoring from Weeks 8-18, and the upgraded offense is expected to take another step in Year 2 under head coach Kellen Moore. Shough’s top-12 passing potential seems legit, and he has a shot to finish in that range in fantasy as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Malik “is our quarterback.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: “Malik needs to be better, but that’s not the headline -- we all need to be better ... everything in the pass game has to be better.. It’s the receivers, it’s the tight ends, it’s the protection,” Hafley continued. Willis is by all statistical measures one of the weakest quarterbacks in the league with his arm, but at least he’s skimping some superflex QB2 value with his legs. There’s not much reason for the Dolphins to bench him either way, as they have nobody they pressingly need to evaluate. Willis should return after the Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 15-of-27 passes for 137 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions and a fumble in the Dolphins’ 31-24, Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding eight rushes for 74 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis had a poor passing day, finishing the first quarter completing 0-of-4 passes. He threw a pair of second quarter interceptions to Jordan Battle, the first coming off a tip and the second on a cross-body throw and poor decision. He also fumbled and recovered a snap in the two-minute drill while a potential third interception was dropped in the endzone in the second half. Willis recovered with a touchdown throw to Kevin Coleman in the fourth quarter but fumbled deep in the Dolphins’ own territory late in the game. He capped off his day with a quick goal-line rushing score at the end of the game but it was too little, too late.
