Between his decision-making and lack of ball security, Willis had a poor game but good fantasy production due to his rushing output. Willis is a fantasy QB2 heading into a Week 6 Dolphins bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 9-of-17 passes for 85 yards in the Dolphins’ 10-15, Week 4 loss to the Vikings, adding two rushes for 11 yards and one fumble lost.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis’ biggest plays of the day are the ones that didn’t count. Willis rolled out of the pocket, escaping pressure, on the Dolphins’ third drive and hit Chris Bell downfield for what could have been a 68-yard touchdown. Unfortunately, the officials determined that the tiniest edge of Bell’s right cleat grazed the sideline pre-catch, during the scramble drill, negating the play altogether. Heartbreaking. Willis also had a 10-yard scramble called back due to holding on the Dolphins’ fifth drive. He attempted a running fadeaway pass 25 yards downfield to Bell on 3rd-and-8 on the Dolphins’ ninth drive, but the catch was contested and ultimately fell incomplete. He is a QB2 against the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said increasing Malik Willis’ designed run rate will be discussed game by game, “when we need him to.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Hafley’s full quote is fairly non-committal. The first-year head coach was asked whether Willis could receive more designed rushes with De’Von Achane (knee) out for the year. Hafley said the game planning in that regard will “go game by game,” and be employed “situationally when we need him to.” For those hoping that Willis will consistently be involved in the run game, those outings could come, but the occurrences could be volatile. Willis remains a QB2 at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 20-of-36 passes for 210 yards and an interception in the Dolphins’ 24-10, Week 3 loss to the Dolphins, adding nine carries for 56 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis also lost a fumble late in the second quarter. Willis made some of his best throws of the season this afternoon, though the two turnovers were also his first of the year. He also missed impressive rookie Chris Bell on what could have been a pair long-ish touchdowns. He was at least running more after combining for just eight carries between Weeks 1 and 2. That is going to remain a must, especially now with De’Von Achane being waylaid with a serious knee injury. That will further change the face of this undermanned offense, and make things even harder for Willis in this no-win setup. Despite his intriguing young wideouts, he will be difficult to trust as a superflex option vs. the Vikings’ blitz-happy defense in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 14-of-23 passes for 197 yards and one touchdown in a 35-13, Week 2 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis was also held to just six yards on the ground as the 49ers’ defensive line was in his face all game long. 77 of Willis’ 197 passing yards came on one busted coverage pass to Ryan Miller in garbage time against defensive backups. There was a belief that Willis would provide fantasy value because of his talent as a runner, but the Dolphins offense has been so bad through two games that we’d find it hard to recommend playing Willis outside of the deepest two quarterback leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins Malik Willis (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis practiced in full all week, so his toe injury should not be an issue against the 49ers. The Dolphins’ quarterback told reporters this week that he is focused on taking fewer sacks moving forward. As his team fell farther behind on the scoreboard last week, Willis began holding onto the ball for far too long. Getting the ball out quickly or throwing on the run could help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins QB Malik Willis said he knows he must take fewer sacks in Week 2 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis stood in the pocket, holding onto the ball too long when trailing the Raiders in the second half last week. He is currently nursing a toe injury, though scrambling faster, or at least throwing on the run, might help him achieve his new goal. Checking down to explosive RB De’Von Achane would also be smart, but the South Florida Sun-Sentinel’s David Furones instead highlighted Willis’ strong connection with rookie WR Caleb Douglas in his article on the subject. Getting the ball out of his hands quickly to either player would be a smart move. Willis’ Dolphins will likely be trailing often in the second half. Developing go-to responses to this situation would help out all involved for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (toe) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis popped up on the Dolphins’ injury report with a toe injury, though he was a full practice participant. This indicates the issue is minor enough for the 27-year-old to keep practicing at full strength. Note down Willis’ toe issue, but expect him to be back out there for Week 2 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 15-of-27 passes for 220 yards and one interception in the Dolphins’ 13-27, Week 1 loss to the Raiders, adding six rushes for 39 yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis scrambled very effectively and was unafraid to test the Raiders’ defense deep. His pocket awareness seemingly waned as the Raiders extended their lead throughout the game, leading to two batted passes and three sacks taken in the fourth quarter, bringing his total to five on the day. Dolphins rookie WR Caleb Douglas looks like a hit, and RB De’Von Achane was his typically reliable self as a receiver. Willis should produce better box scores as the season progresses. He is a borderline QB1/2 against the 49ers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said “there’s a number you’d like to continue to give [Jaylen Warren],” even after Rico Dowdle (toe) returns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: “He’s produced, so it’s been heavy. It’d be great to get Rico back this week, too. ... Having him as a one-two punch was the vision of this offense, but Jaylen’s crushing it right now. He’s been awesome for us,” McCarthy continued. That’s a very telling “but.” Warren has to be regarded as the chair of a committee at this point rather than in a backfield split, and Dowdle probably doesn’t belong in the FLEX conversation coming off his injury until we see a good workload for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 15 times for 101 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts, adding six catches for 87 yards and another touchdown through the air.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren got the Steelers on the board with an 80-yard catch-and-run, where he simply beat the Colts defenders down the sideline. He also ripped off a 50-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. The Steelers only had one other play go for longer than 17 yards on the day. Since Rico Dowdle has been out with a toe injury, Warren has emerged as a true RB1 in fantasy football. Even when Dowdle returns, you have to think that the Steelers have seen enough that they need to give Warren the lion’s share of the work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Steelers declared RB Rico Dowdle, QB Will Howard, QB Drew Allar, CB Jamel Dean, RB Eli Heidenreich, CB Terell Smith, and DT Kevin Jobity Jr. inactive for Week 5 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: It was reported earlier in the day that Dowdle was unlikely to suit up due to his ongoing foot injury, so this doesn’t come as a major surprise. We could be looking at a big game for Jaylen Warren against an underperforming Colts defense. With Keenan Allen back for the Colts, the injury to Jamel Dean is a bit of a blow to this Pittsburgh secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Rico Dowdle is making progress in his attempt to return from a toe injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: McCarthy said he expects Dowdle and Jaylen Warren to be a “one-two punch” once Dowdle returns to the field. Warren has totaled 34 rushes over the last two weeks while rushing for 220 scoreless yards, but had a 21-89-0 line during the first two weeks of the season when Dowdle was active. Both backs will likely fall in the RB3/FLEX range if Dowdle suits up for Week 5’s game against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 17 times for 93 yards in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns, adding 33 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren’s six targets combine with his 17 carries to give him his second consecutive game with more than 20 opportunities in the absence of Rico Dowdle, seeing all but two running back opportunities in the process. More impressive was the fact that he once again maintained elite efficiency on the ground through the additional touches, averaging 5.5 yards per attempt against a solid Browns run defense. The veteran back appears likely to revert to a strict timeshare with Dowdle expected back for Week 5 after the long week, bringing him back to the RB3 range for a meeting with the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Steelers are going to use Jaylen Warren “a lot” while frequently utilizing two-tight end sets in Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: It sounds like Warren is belongs on the RB1/2 border with Rico Dowdle (toe) sidelined again this week. The Steelers will try to control the line of scrimmage by frequently deploying TEs Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington, both in the run game and as receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports there is a “pretty good chance” Rico Dowdle (toe) returns in Week 5 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Dowdle did not practice this week and was ruled out for Thursday’s game against the Browns. Rapoport called him day-to-day. The mini-bye between today’s game and Pittsburgh’s Week 5 date with Indy at home should be enough rest to get Dowdle back on the field. Jaylen Warren will see almost the entirety of the backfield tonight before returning to committee duties once Dowdle is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) will not play in Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Dowdle did not practice once this week before being ruled out for Thursday’s game against the Browns. The mini-bye ahead of Week 5 may help him get back on the field, but his status for next week’s contest is very much up in the air. Jaylen Warren will see the bulk of the backfield work versus Cleveland. he ran 17 times and caught three passes in Week 3. With an elite workload versus a middling Cleveland defense, Warren is a high-end RB2 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo believes Jaylen Warren will continue as a workhorse back in Week 4.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren operated as an every-down back in Week 3 against the Bengals, running for 127 yards on 17 carries and catching three passes for 49 yards in a victory. DeFabo suggested Warren had established himself as the team’s clear lead back option against the Bengals with Rico Dowdle (toe) sidelined. “I’ve always had respect for him, playing against him, and then being his teammate now for a little more than a season,” Aaron Rodgers said of Warren. “He is one of the toughest guys I’ve ever played with, and I just can’t say enough about his energy and the way he runs the football and the way he cares about his teammates.” Warren’s pass game involvement spiked in Week 3, as he ran a route on 70 percent of Pittsburgh’s drop backs. Dowdle, meanwhile, did not practice Monday ahead of the Steelers’ Thursday game against the Browns. Warren should remain in all lineups this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 17 times for 127 yards in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals, adding three receptions for 49 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren ripped off a 30-yard reception on the Steelers’ first play of the game and was reliable throughout while serving as the Steelers’ primary back. Warren gained 20 or more yards on three plays and would have found the end zone on a 26-yard run in the fourth quarter if not for tripping and falling in the open field. This was exactly the kind of performance fantasy managers were hoping for with Rico Dowdle (toe) sidelined, as Warren was on the field for 53 of 59 offensive snaps for Steelers RBs. The Steelers play the Browns on Thursday in Week 4; if Dowdle can’t heal up in time to play on the short week, Warren would again be a volume-based RB2 with plenty of upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.headline: Tom Kennedy (knee) suffered a significant MCL injury that is expected to require season-ending surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.analysis: The 30-year-old culture tonesetter has mostly only turned to fantasy relevancy when injuries piled up. The Lions had to use Amon-Ra St. Brown on returns after his injury and will likely seek a new returner off the practice circuit this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said LB Devin White “is probably going to need surgery” after fracturing his forearm in Week 5 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.analysis: The Lions’ backup linebacker is expected to miss some time. The Lions will also be without WR Tom Kennedy, who serves as the team’s top returner, for a while. Kennedy suffered a “sprain,” seemingly in his knee, during a return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.headline: Lions waived WR Tom Kennedy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.analysis: Kennedy, 26, had a big preseason for the Lions, posting 16 catches for 143 yards and a couple touchdowns. It still wasn’t enough for Kennedy to crack the Lions’ wideout room. Perhaps he’ll be brought back on the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.headline: Lions WR Tom Kennedy caught 5-of-7 targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns in Detroit’s preseason win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.analysis: Kennedy had eight catches for 104 yards on 13 targets in Detroit’s first preseason game, and has been getting plenty of praise from coach Dan Campbell. “That’s Tom Kennedy,” Campbell said earlier in the preseason. “He’s just dependable, that’s all he is just dependable. He’s just very dependable, that’s all he is.” We think that’s praise, anyway. Campbell is no threat to the upper crust of fantasy or anything but the 2019 UDFA could draw some league-wide interest if he doesn’t make Detroit’s final roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.headline: Lions re-signed WR Tom Kennedy to a one-year, $825,000 contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.analysis: Kennedy signed his tender with Detroit. You may remember Kennedy from the 75-yard touchdown pass he completed on his lone attempt of 2021. He also reeled in six catches for 54 yards in 12 games for Detroit. He profiles as a practice squad player for the Lions, barring a rash of wideout injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.headline: Lions declared DE Trey Flowers (shoulder/knee), LB Jamie Collins Sr., RB Jermar Jefferson, and WR Tom Kennedy inactive for Week 3 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.analysis: The Lions are among the healthiest teams in the NFL after two weeks, though they’ll go without Flowers and Collins against Baltimore’s run-heavy offense. Collins will miss the game while the Lions try to trade him. There was no way Detroit’s defense could stop Lamar Jackson and company, even with a fully healthy defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.headline: Lions signed WR Tom Kennedy, WR Victor Bolden, WR Jonathan Duhart, LS James Fisher, P Jack Fox, S A.J. Howard, OT Matt Nelson, DT Olive Sagapolu, LB Christian Sam, OG Casey Tucker and P Matt Wile to reserve/future contracts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.analysis: The Lions are adding their practice squad to their offseason 90-man roster. A 23-year-old UDFA out of small-school “Bryant,” Kennedy spent one game on the 53-man roster in 2019.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.headline: Lions promoted WR Tom Kennedy from their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tom-kenned.analysis: He’ll take the roster spot vacated by Travis Fulgham, who the Lions cut earlier this week. Kennedy’s promotion suggests Detroit expects to be without Danny Amendola (chest) Sunday against Kansas City.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.headline: Packers DT Javon Hargrave suffered a torn Achilles in Week 5’s win over the Bears, ending his season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.analysis: It was reported after Sunday’s game that the Packers believed Hargrave suffered a torn Achilles, so this news doesn’t come as a surprise. The 33-year-old lineman will now miss the remainder of the season and look to rehab in hopes of being back in time for training camp next season. Hargrave signed a two-year, $23 million contract with the Packers this offseason and has totaled six tackles in four games played.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Packers DT Javon Hargrave is believed to have suffered an Achilles tendon rupture in Week 5 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.analysis: He was injured in Week 5’s win over the Bears. Hargrave has one year remaining on his contract. He faces a tough recovery late in his career. This is the second Achilles tendon rupture for the Packers’ defense in as many weeks, with LB Edgerrin Cooper suffering the same injury in Week 4 against the Buccaneers. Hargrave will ultimately require surgery and be placed on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.headline: Packers NT Javon Hargrave (toe) is active for Week 5 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.analysis: It’s a mercifully quiet injury day for the Packers in this grudge match. Inactive for the Pack are OL Jacob Monk, OG Aaron Banks, OL Donovan Jennings and DT Anthony Campbell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.headline: Packers declared WR Jayden Reed, RT Zach Bako-Bewele, LG Aaron Banks, DT Warren Brinson and DT Anthony Campbell inactive for Week 3 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.analysis: Reed may not return in 2026, and Bako-Bewele suffered a season-ending knee injury. The Packers will also be without Banks, their starting left guard, though the Falcons are without both starting edge rushers right now due to suspension and injury. Packers DT Javon Hargrave (knee/concussion) is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.headline: Packers declared CB Benjamin St-Juste, OL John Williams, OL Travis Glover, DT Warren Brinson, and DT Javon Hargrave inactive for Week 2 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.analysis: That means that starting left guard Aaron Banks (knee) will be back on the field after missing Week 1 against the Vikings. In a game that figures to be played in constant rain, having a fully healthy offensive line will be a nice boost for Marshawn Lloyd and the Packers’ offense. Javon Hargrave (concussion) remains out for Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.headline: Packers agreed to terms with DT Javon Hargrave, formerly of the Vikings, on a two-year, $23 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.analysis: The deal includes $13 million in 2026, potentially giving Green Bay an early out if the 10-year veteran starts showing signs of aging following his age-33 season. The former two-time Pro Bowler played the 2025 season with the Vikings, registering only 3.5 sacks and 52 tackles in 16 appearances. He did prove healthy last year after playing only three games for the 49ers in 2024 and brings another capable body up front for the retooled Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.headline: Vikings released DT Javon Hargrave.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter previously reported that the Vikings would try to trade Hargrave before cutting. No takers were found and now Hargrave will be a free agent. Hargrave signed a two-year, $30 million contract with the Vikings amid their spending spree last offseaosn. He amassed 3.5 sacks and wasn’t particularly effective against the run, according to Pro Football Focus. Now a veteran of 10 years, Hargrave should be able to find a new home rather quickly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Vikings will release Aaron Jones if they can’t trade him before the start of the league year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.analysis: The Vikings have a lot of cap space to create and this was always the likely move based on that calculus. Jones probably won’t attract much interest on the trade market as he enters his age-32 season and has started to leave a concerning number of games with injuries, in addition to being placed on IR for a short stint early in the 2025 season. He’d likely only have head-of-committee ceiling heading into the 2026 offseason. Schefter added that the same trade-or-release ultimatum exists for DT Javon Hargrave.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Vikings have had trade talks with teams regarding DT Javon Hargrave.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.analysis: This is usually the first step towards a release, and The Athletic’s Alec Lewis called Hargrave’s release “a predictable offseason move” in December. Hargrave simply didn’t live up to expectations last year. Entering his age-33 season, we’d be surprised if the Vikings got anything more than a late-round swap for Hargrave.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.headline: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes it is a “predictable offseason move” for the Vikings to cut DT Javon Hargrave.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-harg.analysis: Hargrave can be cut for $11 million in cap savings. The veteran has been solid-but-unspectacular and turns 33 this offseason. He’d probably have a real market as a veteran plugger somewhere, but Hargrave has been a so-so run defender since leaving the Steelers and likely won’t command the same kind of salary in 2026 as he did last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.headline: Cardinals TE Teagan Quitoriano caught 2-of-2 targets for 15 yards and two touchdowns in Arizona’s Week 5 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.analysis: ( The Aristocrats voice ) The Lions defense! Quitoriano, Arizona’s No. 2 tight end, remains outside of the fantasy TE2 discussion. These were his first touchdowns since the 2022 season, doubling his career total to four.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.headline: Cardinals placed TE Hunter Long (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four weeks. Long had played 91 snaps in his first four weeks with the Cardinals and will cede blocking duties to promoted practice-squadder Teagan Quitoriano for those of you in points-per-blocked-players leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.headline: Cardinals signed TE Teagan Quitoriano, formerly of the Falcons, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.analysis: Quitoriano appeared in all 17 games for the Falcons last year but did not record any offensive statistics. The bulk of his offensive snaps came as a blocker. In total, he played primarily on special teams, logging 239 snaps on that side of the ball. Hen is likely in line for a similar role in Arizona.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.headline: Falcons signed TE Teagan Quitoriano, formerly of the Texans, to a contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.analysis: Quitoriano will settle into a backup role behind Kyle Pitts, Charlie Woerner and Feleipe Franks. The former Texan has dealt with knee, oblique, groin and calf issues in his short career but perhaps a change of scenery will be helpful. He did not earn any targets last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.headline: Texans placed TE Teagan Quitoriano on injured reserve with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.analysis: Quitoriano, 24 appeared in seven games, but has not received a single target in 2024. Myles Bryant was promoted to the active roster in the corresponding move.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.headline: Texans placed WR Nico Collins (hamstring) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.analysis: Collins went from being day-to-day to week-to-week to missing a minimum of four games in just a few days. It’s a tough blow for the Texans and the NFL’s leading receiver, as Collins won’t be eligible to return until Week 10 at the earliest. Collins has totaled a league-high 567 receiving yards this season, while his 17.7 YPR ranks third in the league amongst receivers who have seen at least 30 targets. His absence will create a target boon for both Stefon Diggs and Tank Dell, and will put Dell in the weekly conversation as a top-24 play in fantasy. In a corresponding move, the Texans have signed tight end Teagan Quitoriano from the Bears’ practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.headline: Texans signed TE Teagan Quitoriano off Chicago’s practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.analysis: Houston let Quitoriano go at last cuts with an injury settlement, so now that he’s healthy it’s not a surprise to see the two sides link up again. He was a 2022 fifth-round pick for Houston and played 481 snaps his first two seasons. He’ll mostly be a blocking tight end for Houston.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.headline: KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson reports Texans C Jarrett Patterson (ankle) was placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.analysis: Patterson was carted off in Week 8, leaving QB C.J. Stroud out a starter on the Texans’ offensive line. Backup Michael Dieter will likely take over at center. TE Teagan Quitoriano (groin) was also placed on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.headline: Texans activated TE Teagan Quitoriano from physically unable to perform list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.analysis: The second-year tight end provided the Texans with six starts in his rookie season and returns to a once again crowded tight end room. He spent time on injured reserve to start the 2022 season and began camp on the physically unable to perform list. Quitoriano is currently listed second on the team’s depth chart but the Texans also added three able bodies through free agency in presumed starter Dalton Schultz, Eric Tomlinson and Nick Vannett. The tight end depth chart remains murky, at best, leaving this a situation to largely stay away from outside of Schultz.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.headline: Teagan Quitoriano caught 3-of-4 targets for 83 yards in Houston’s Week 18 win over Indianapolis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/teagan-qui.analysis: In the process, he created 73 percent of his yardage on the season. Quitoriano caught a 52-yard seam ball to account for most of this, and also was wide open on the sideline for another long-ish catch. Quitoriano caught a pair of goal-line touchdowns this year but is more of a blocking tight end. The sixth-round pick may enter the offseason as Houston’s No. 1 tight end by default as his snap counts were trending up after a preseason IR stint. He’s not fantasy-useful at the moment, but he’s young enough to change that if the right structure is placed around him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden failed to haul in his only target in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden had another disappointing outing for the Chargers and his fantasy managers on Sunday. He’s now been held without a catch in two of his last three games and has yet to exceed 36 receiving yards in any game this season. Playing in one of the worst offenses in the league certainly doesn’t help things, but Gadsden can’t be trusted by fantasy managers at this point and won’t be on the fantasy radar in Week 6 when the Chargers visit the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught 5-of-8 targets for 36 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden did make a spectacular catch on fourth down to set up a touchdown, but oustide of that, the tight end — while finishing tied for the most catches on the day with Keaton Mitchell — was unable to find any room against the Seahawks’ defense. The 23-year-old was more involved than he has been in previous weeks, but that’s less compliment to this effort than insult to the first few. He’ll be back at it in Week 5 against another tough defense in the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: He did rejoin practice today, making it plausible he’ll be up for the Chargers’ Week 5 game against the Broncos. Second-year receiving TE Oronde Gadsden was unable to seize the moment with Kolar and TE David Njoku (knee) sidelined last week, catching 0-of-3 targets. The once-promising youngster must do something on Sunday if he wishes to remain re-draft-relevant in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden didn’t catch any of his three targets in a Week 3 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden’s first target of the day was on a third-down pass that hit off his hands and landed on the grass. Neither of his other two targets was particularly close to being caught. He did play on 39 of the team’s 69 snaps, more than any other tight end, and ran a route on 31 of their 43 dropbacks, which was the third-most of any player on the Chargers. We guess you can talk yourself into his role based on those numbers, but the results weren’t there, and the Chargers look discombobulated on offense. It’s hard to trust Gadsden in fantasy going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: ESPN’s Kris Rhim reports that Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) will not be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Kolar’s surgery earlier this week reportedly changed his prognosis. Kolar was expected to land on short-term injured reserve and miss at least four games. Apparently, the team expects him back sooner than that. Backup TE Oronde Gadsden is still set to start, given Kolar and TE David Njoku’s (knee) injuries, but Gadsden’s audition window has evidently shrunk. He remains a worthwhile add and can be started by TE-needy fantasy managers in what should be a productive game environment against the Bills this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden caught both of his targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 2 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: David Njoku left the game early with a knee injury and Charlie Kolar followed him to the locker room much later because of a forearm injury. As a result, Gadsden’s route rate jumped from 14 percent in Week 1 to 48 percent today. He still managed just two catches, but Gadsden at least found the end zone for the first time this year. The Chargers offense has looked defunct through two weeks, so even a full-time role for Gadsden could result in middling fantasy numbers. Still, he is worth a look off the waiver wire for teams in need of tight end production.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said the team plans on utilizing TE Oronde Gadsden’s skillset.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: McDaniel was asked why Gadsden only played eight snaps in Week 1. The Chargers’ offensive coordinator said he expected Gadsden to get more involved last week, but the game “didn’t play out” that way. McDaniel closed by saying he expects Gadsden “to be more involved outside of an unforeseen situation where the game and the parameters with which you’re playing change — and therein lies the problem. Gadsden is not a full-time player. Projecting his weekly usage will be challenging. He is currently not worth starting in 12-team leagues, though that could change if McDaniel decides to feature him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught both of his targets for 32 yards in the Chargers’ Week 1 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden hardly saw the field against Arizona. He ran just seven pass routes while David Njoku logged 17 routes and caught all five of his targets. Gadsden is clearly an afterthought in the Chargers passing offense for now. He should remain on waiver wires ahead of the Bolts’ Week 2 game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: The Chargers listed Charlie Kolar as the No. 1 tight end on their Week 1 depth chart.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Way back in late May, the Athletic’s Daniel Popper suggested Kolar, who signed a three-year, $24.3 million contract with the Bolts this spring, would enter the season as LA’s top tight end “because of his complete skill set.” Week 1 usage will tell us a lot about how offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will use his tight ends, but for now it seems Kolar will lead the group in Week 1 against the Cardinals. David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden II, however, could see more pass game involvement depending on how many routes they run in a given week, and whether the Chargers go run-heavy against an opponent. None of the Chargers’ tight ends are particularly appealing fantasy plays for Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Chargers TE Oronde Gadsden caught 2-of-3 targets for 21 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: The second-year incumbent tight end is seemingly behind the Chargers’ free agent signee veteran TEs Charlie Kolar and David Njoku. Neither Kolar nor Njoku suited up this evening. Gadsden can still be viewed as a TE2/3 in best ball formats, but his current role could be undesirable for re-draft purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 4-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews dropped a would-be touchdown on the team’s opening possession on a ball that went through his hands in the end zone. He would then fumble on the following possession, which Jessie Bates returned for a touchdown to force the Ravens into catch-up mode for the remainder of the game. Luckily for him, late heroics from Tyler Huntley and Derrick Henry had the team escaping with a victory. Andrews has not looked great to start the 2026 season, having not eclipsed 50 yards through five games. He’ll remain a shaky fantasy start in Week 6 when the Ravens host the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews practiced in full with the hand injury last week before posting a 5/27/1 receiving line. He should be good to go again this week, though he is a low-end TE1, with backup QB Tyler Huntley likely starting in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 5-of-6 targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 4 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews continues to see most of his work come in the short area of the field. He’s gone for less than 30 yards in each of his last two games, but did manage to haul in a three-yard score in the second quarter of Sunday’s win for his first touchdown of 2026. Lamar Jackson also missed Andrews in the end zone on a high throw earlier in the game, but he remains a very touchdown-dependent option as far as fantasy is concerned. He’s a boom-or-bust play in Week 5 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: The Ravens seemingly forgot about Andrews when they first posted their injury report, only noting his injury and status in a post 40 minutes after the initial run. In their defense, Andrews has been pretty forgettable this year, catching 13 passes for 122 scoreless yards. The hand injury shouldn’t be an issue this week, but he’s still stuck in the TE2 ranks versus Tennessee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 3-of-5 targets for 24 yards the Ravens’ Week 3 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews missed part of this game with a hand injury but returned to catch two passes for a total of 15 yards in the second half. Andrews has yet to find the end zone this season and hasn’t gone for more than 49 yards in a game. There’s not much for fantasy managers to rely on here heading into next week’s game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) returned in the third quarter of Week 3’s game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews returned to the field midway through the quarter. He saw three targets before leaving the game in the first half, but it seems unlikely he will see many more targets at this point. The Ravens have attempted just 11 passes through nearly three full quarters of play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) is questionable to return in Week 3 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: We’re not quite sure what happened here, but Andrews was not on the field for the Ravens’ fifth drive of the game, with the team announcing soon after that he would be questionable to return. The veteran tight end caught 1-of-3 targets for nine yards before exiting.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 6-of-7 yargets for 49 yards in the Ravens’ Week 2 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews was targeted four times on the Ravens’ first four possessions, with his biggest play coming on a 10-yard reception to start a drive that ended with a Derrick Henry touchdown. Andrews caught a 14-yard reception on the Ravens’ final drive of the game as they tried to mount a comeback, but the drive ended on an interception by Lamar Jackson three plays later. Andrews has caught 10 passes for 98 scoreless yards on 13 targets through his first two games. It’s decent production for a tight end, but he continues to look like a shell of the player he once was. He’ll be a boom-or-bust TE2 in Week 3 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) is doubtful to play in Week 2 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Flowers entered the season at the tail end of a rehab program for the hamstring strain he suffered on August 31st. He logged two full practice sessions before dominating the Colts early on in Week 1. Unfortunately, Flowers balled too hard, aggravating the hamstring injury in the process. He is unlikely to play this week, but his return to practice today is a great sign for his Week 3 availability. The Ravens placed WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) on injured reserve this week. This means WRs Rashod Bateman, Elijah Sarratt and Devontez Walker could be asked to step up, although TE Mark Andrews will probably serve as the team’s top pass-catching option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Early reports regarding Flowers’ health and Week 2 availability were positive, but two missed practices put him firmly in the questionable camp, with a lean toward sitting. Flowers and TE Mark Andrews banked six targets apiece last week and were the only Ravens who cleared three. With WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) on injured reserve, Andrews should handle another sizable workload. Ravens WRs Elijah Sarratt and Devontez Walker should both be active if Flowers sits.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 24 times for 102 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons, adding 18 yards and a touchdown on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry also tacked on a successful two-point conversion to further pad his counting stats. The King erupted for 59 yards in the first half before being largely held in check for the final two quarters with the Ravens playing from behind. He would watch from the sidelines for the duration of the team’s final possession in the two-minute drill but came on the field to tie the game with a two-point conversion on a direct snap. The Falcons were no match for Henry in the extra frame, with the bruising back tacking on an additional 32 yards on the ground on the team’s lone overtime possession. Henry continues to turn back the clock while notching his eighth touchdown in five appearances, having scored in every game to start the season. He remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 23 times for 73 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 4 win over the Titans, adding two receptions for six additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: This week marks the second straight game in which Henry averaged less than 4.0 YPC. Fortunately for fantasy managers, he did manage to find the end zone on a five-yard score on the Ravens’ first drive and was relied on heavily in the second half when Lamar Jackson exited the game with an ankle injury. This wasn’t a flashy game for Henry, who was held to three or fewer yards on 16 of his 23 rush attempts. That said, he continues to be the only Ravens RB of note and remains in the RB1 mix for next week’s game against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 26 times for 89 yards and two touchdowns in the Ravens’ Week 3 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Fantasy managers won’t balk at the production Henry provided their lineups in Sunday’s win over the Cowboys, but the Big Dog was largely bottled up against a suddenly stingy defensive front. Henry’s longest run came on a 29-yard burst in the third quarter that helped set up a Chris Moore receiving touchdown, but that run also accounted for 32.6 percent of Henry’s yards on the ground. He averaged a very underwhelming 2.4 YPC on his other 25 carries on the day and was tackled for a three-yard loss on a fourth-and-goal from the Cowboys’ one-yard line. The good news is Henry remains the unquestioned bell cow in the Ravens’ backfield, and he has a Week 4 revenge game against the Titans on tap. He’ll be a must start RB1 in what should be a plus matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 16 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 2 loss to the Saints, adding three receptions for 19 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry didn’t provide his signature explosive plays in this one, with his longest carry of the afternoon coming on an eight-yard run. On the Ravens’ second drive of the game, Henry turned seven touches into 45 yards from scrimmage, thanks in part to a screen pass he took for 19 yards, and capped the drive with a one-yard score to give the Ravens an early 7-0 lead. He averaged a respectable 4.3 YPC on the day, but the Saints were able to hold Henry in check for much of the afternoon. That said, fantasy managers won’t be mad at the production. He gets a plus matchup next week on the road against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns in the Ravens’ Week 1 win over the Colts, adding one reception for 19 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Age continues to be just a number for Henry. The 32-year-old bell cow handled 24 of the backfield’s 30 carries on Sunday, averaging an impressive 6.0 YPC while ripping off four gains of 10-plus yards. Henry did his part to keep the Ravens on schedule all afternoon, and wound up finding the end zone three times on Sunday. His first score, which came on a four-yard plunge in the first quarter, was followed by a 32-yard score in the second quarter, in which Henry shook off two tackles on his way into the end zone. He would add a third score early in the fourth quarter for good measure while pushing the Ravens’ lead to 38-16. It’s only one game, but Henry doesn’t look like he’s lost a step heading into his 11th season. He’ll be on the RB1 radar in Week 2 in a plus matchup against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Ravens RB Derrick Henry said he “would like to finish [his] playing career with [the] Ravens.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: In an appearance for the Up & Adams show, Henry said, “when I hang it up, Baltimore is the last place I want to be.” The 32-year-old later followed up on social media by saying he “would like” to finish his career with the Ravens, but clarifying he “never said anything about retiring.” Henry is still producing at a high level and is not headed for retirement just yet. However, when he does consider retirement, he hopes to close out his career with the Ravens. Henry has produced 3,516 rushing yards and 32 rushing touchdowns in two seasons with the Ravens and is currently under contract through 2027.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec believes the Ravens see Justice Hill “as a good complement to Derrick Henry and really value his ability out of the backfield and in blitz pickup.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Hill ended 2025 on injured reserve because of a neck issue. He was reportedly a cut candidate during the offseason and the team selected Clemson running back Adam Randall on Day Three of the draft. It seemed possible that the team planned on replacing Hill this year, but Zrebiec shot that idea down, at least for the start of the season. Zrebiec answered, “I can’t see that happening from the jump,” in reference to a question about Randall opening the season as Baltimore’s backup running back. Hill caught 21 passes for 169 yards and a touchdown in 10 games last year. He also punched in a pair of touchdowns on the ground despite running just 18 times. His ceiling is extremely limited, even in the event of a Henry injury, but Hill should have some standalone RB4 value in PPR leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 20 times for 126 yards in the Ravens’ Week 18 loss to the Steelers while not catching in lone target.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry got the party started with a 41-yard dash to open the game. Outside of that, there wasn’t a ton of room for the 32-year-old, but it’s another strong game for a running back who has defied aging. He finished 36 yards behind James Cook for the NFL lead. Regression will come for Tractorcito at some point, but nothing that happened in the 2025 campaign suggests it is coming soon. Even with little involvement in the passing game, it’s hard to imagine that he won’t be a fantasy RB1 again next year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 36 times for 216 yards and four touchdowns in the Ravens’ Week 17 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry now has more 200 yard rushing games (7) than any player in NFL history. He wasn’t targeted in the passing game, because why would you need to? Three of his touchdowns came in the first half, and he routinely ran over completely overmatched Green Bay defenders in yet another impressive effort for the 31-year-old. Keaton Mitchell was somehow able to get nine carries for 31 yards as his (beyond) clear backup on a day where Baltimore rushed for 307 total yards in Lambeau Field. Even if Lamar Jackson (back) returns for Week 18 against the Steelers, Henry is going to be the focal point of the Ravens’ offense for that contest. He has to be.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 18 times for 128 yards and two touchdowns in the Ravens’ Week 16 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry erupted in the second half following the departure of starting quarterback Lamar Jackson, quite literally putting the team on his back as the Ravens built an 11-point lead in the fourth quarter. The veteran bruiser overcame a lost fumble in the first quarter for his second consecutive 100-yard showing, sixth 100-yard outing, and fourth multi-touchdown game of the season. Henry was curiously mothballed in the fourth quarter after scoring his touchdown. The Ravens fall to 7-8 with the loss and no longer control their own destiny for a playoff berth. King Henry gets a difficult matchup against the Packers in Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Tyler Huntley completed 24-of-32 passes for 201 yards and two touchdowns in the Ravens’ 30-23, Week 5 win over the Falcons, adding 20 yards and a touchdown on six carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Huntley was in command of the offense throughout, showing poise and pocket presence in the face of one of the most stout defensive fronts in the league. The Ravens marched the field on the opening possession but a dropped touchdown from tight end Mark Andrews forced them to settle for a field goal. Their next possession resulted in a Mark Andrews fumble that was returned for a touchdown, forcing the Ravens to play from behind for the remainder of the game. Down by eight with just over two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, Huntley took the ball and led the team to a touchdown and successful two-point conversion to force overtime. He would then lead an opening possession touchdown drive in the extra frame, with the team escaping with an unlikely comeback victory on a game-sealing interception. Huntley could be tasked with another start in Week 6 against the Browns after late-week reports indicated that Lamar Jackson could be headed for another absence. Huntley will be a middling QB2, should he start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Tyler Huntley will start in Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Huntley figures to be a low-end superflex QB2 in Week 5, probably a bottom-five option for the week given how well the Falcons defense has played and how weak the Ravens skill position room looks. He led the team to zero points in the second half last week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) will not play in Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Many thanks to Minter for ruling Jackson out now rather than forcing fantasy managers to navigate a questionable designation all weekend. Jackson did not practice at all this week for the Ravens and felt like a near lock to miss this week’s game after it was reported on Tuesday that he had an “outside chance” to play on Sunday night against the Falcons. Minter said earlier in the week that he did not think Jackson’s injury would result in a “crazy long-term” absence, so we’ll see how things go for him next week when the Ravens prepare to face the AFC North-leading Browns in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Jackson did not practice this week, but head coach Jesse Minter said on Wednesday that his QB1 could still play even if he doesn’t practice. We’ve heard this one too many times when it comes to Jackson and nagging injuries, and it’s not often we see him suit up in these scenarios. His status will be one to keep an eye on when the team releases its final injury report, but even if Jackson is given the questionable tag, we would recommend stashing an emergency option at QB in the event he doesn’t start. Given that the Ravens play on Sunday night, Jackson’s backup, Tyler Huntley, and Falcons starter Michael Penix Jr. would be the most logical stashes as Matthew Stafford and Josh Allen, who play on Monday night, are rostered in nearly every league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lamar Jackson’s ankle sprain is “unconventional.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: The sprain Jackson sustained in Week 4 against the Titans, according to Rapoport, is neither low nor high. Rapoport said Monday that Jackson has an “outside” shot at suiting up in Week 5 against the Falcons and could miss multiple games with the unique ankle situation. Tyler Huntley will once again sub in for Jackson until he’s ready to return. Baltimore will likely be far more run heavy with Huntley under center, limiting targets for Zay Flowers and the rest of the Ravens pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lamar Jackson (ankle) has an “outside chance” of playing in Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Dealing with a sprained ankle he sustained last week against the Titans, Jackson will sit out at least one game and could miss multiple weeks, according to Rapoport. Tyler Huntley will make his annual start or two (or three) for the Ravens when they take on the Falcons defense, which is allowing the third lowest drop back success rate in the NFL. It’s a downgrade for Mark Andrews and Zay Flowers, though both should be played in 12-team leagues in Week 5. Huntley should be added in all superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Lamar Jackson will have an MRI on his ankle Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: It was reported after Sunday’s win over the Titans that Jackson was “believed to be day-to-day” after he left the game with what appeared to be a relatively minor ankle injury. Jackson was spotted in a walking boot, which has raised a bit more concern for his Week 5 availability, but hopefully the MRI doesn’t reveal anything too severe. Jackson and the Ravens are set to take on the Falcons on Sunday night, which could make for a difficult situation for fantasy managers. We’ll surely receive countless updates on his status throughout the week, but fantasy managers should have a backup plan in place in the event he enters the weekend with a questionable designation. If he’s unable to play, Tyler Huntley would draw his first start of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) is questionable to return in Week 4 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Lamar was sacked on the Ravens’ final play of the first half. His ankle got caught under Titans EDGE Jermaine Johnson on the play, and when the Ravens took the field in the third quarter, it was backup Tyler Huntley who was under center. With the Ravens holding a 24-7 lead, it wouldn’t be surprising if the Ravens opted to play it safe with Jackson and keep him out for the remainder of this one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Ravens signed QB Tyler Huntley to a two-year, $11 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Huntley has made 11 starts in five seasons with the Ravens, also starting five games for the Dolphins in 2024. He brings a level of familiarity with the system and allows the team added consistency should Lamar Jackson go down with injury due to his similar skill set, making the signing a no-brainer for both sides. A career 13-to-10 touchdown-to-interception ratio is less than sparkling, but his dual-threat abilities bring both upside and intrigue should he be forced into action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Tyler Huntley completed 16-of-20 passes for 107 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ 41-24, Week 17 win over the Ravens, adding eight rushes for 60 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Huntley got the start with Lamar Jackson’s back contusion keeping him from playing, and his main goal was handing the football to Derrick Henry (36/216/4) and getting out of the way. Mission accomplished. He did do a nice job connecting on his short-yardage passes, and was rewarded with a touchdown pass to Zay Flowers late in the contest. Huntley will be tasked with being a game manager in Week 18 against the Steelers if Jackson can’t go, and there’s a smidgen of upside because of his ability to make some plays as as a runner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 5-of-6 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts remained largely confined to short area work with his game-long reception going for only 13 yards. A second quarter touchdown from five yards out gave the veteran tight end his first trip to paint through five games and his five receptions doubled that of his previous four appearances. Pitts remains a difficult weekly start for as long as Drake London and Bijan Robinson remain healthy, which doesn’t change ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Bears in Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught all three targets for 47 yards in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts played just one snap on the team’s first two possessions before seeing modest usage the rest of the game. His counting stats were padded in the second half with a 28-yard, catch-and-run reception on a play action pass out of the flat. Pitts isn’t getting the snaps or route participation to return consistent fantasy production and is best left on fantasy benches for as long as Drake London remains healthy. That won’t change ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 1-of-2 targets for five yards in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts was the recipient of Michael Penix’s first completion of the 2026 season, with the latter making his season debut following ACL surgery. The return of his starting quarterback was not enough to give Pitts his first fantasy-relevant performance of the season as he watched blocking tight end Austin Hooper score the lone receiving touchdown of the evening from five yards out in the second quarter. Fantasy managers are stuck in the constant hype cycle with Pitts with very little to show for it through three games, making Pitts a difficult start on the road against the Saints in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 1-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Cooper Rush was a disaster once again, tanking the fantasy prospects of every Falcon. Pitts narrowly avoided his second straight bagel with a lone catch late in the second quarter. He failed to catch his only target last week. There’s not much to say about Pitts and the entire offense when Rush simply shuts down all production from the jump. Pitts will reclaim a spot in the TE1 ranks if Michael Penix is back for Week 3. He is not on the fantasy radar if Rush is under center once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowlers reports Michael Penix (knee) is “not yet ready for live game action.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Fowler said Penix, still recovering from his 2025 ACL injury, “wants to be fully confident before stepping onto the field. And my understanding is the Falcons are leaving the comfort level part of his recovery up to him.” “Penix is coming off his third ACL reconstruction, which is a lot of ACL reconstructions,” ESPN’s Dan Graziano added. “I believe it takes a lot of mental work to convince yourself it’s OK to go back out there and play. If Penix needs more time, I’m sure the Falcons will give it to him, though I believe we will see him on the field at some point this season.” That would leave Tua Tagovailoa as the team’s presumed starter if Tua can play through the oblique strain that sidelined him in Week 1 against the Steelers. If Tua can’t go, the Falcons could be forced to start Cooper Rush for another game or two. Rush, who had the lowest drop back EPA of any QB in Week 1, makes Drake London and Kyle Pitts iffy starts in 12-team fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts Sr. had no catches on one target in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts owes most of this to a poor performance by Cooper Rush under center. Pitts played on 39 of the team’s 61 snaps and ran a route on 22 of their 29 dropbacks. He simply wasn’t a factor with Rush struggling to move the ball down the field. We should note that the Falcons were very run-heavy with Rush at quarterback, and Charlie Woerner played 38 snaps and was on the field for 22 run-blocking snaps to just 16 for Pitts. If the Falcons are going to continue to be so focused on rushing the ball, that could cut into some of Pitts’ snaps and usage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Falcons TE Kyle Pitts caught 3-of-3 targets for 59 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts ripped off multiple double-digit gains, moved well and looked tough to bring down. He delivered a 37-yard catch on the Falcons’ first drive, securing the pass on a quick out route from bunch formation before taking off down the right sideline. He later had a 16-yard gain on a sort crossing route, where he again chewed up yards after the catch. Pitts is a mid-tier TE1 entering the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports “Falcons people on the ground” believe Kyle Pitts is moving better than he has in years.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Fowler settles on Pitts being a “certified first or second option in the passing game.” Pitts sets up as a potential high-end TE1 on an offense that loves to use the tight end, and the fact that he finished second in fantasy points among TEs last year is proof of concept that he was already playing better in 2025. With his contract taken care of, perhaps this will be the year Pitts ascends to the top of the tier, the writer said forgetting any of the last five years had happened.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Falcons signed TE Kyle Pitts to a three-year, $54 million extension with $36 million in guaranteed money.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: The Falcons had previously waffled a bit on potentially making Pitts available after “President Of Football” Matt Ryan took over, but must have liked what they saw in the early offseason. Pitts currently looks to be slated for the No. 2 receiver role in Atlanta behind Drake London and should be a fantasy-viable TE1 this year. (Words that have never come back to bite anyone.) Pitts settles for slightly below George Kittle’s $19.1 million per year and Trey McBride’s $19 million per year and will remain in Atlanta for the near future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Falcons TE Kyle Pitts said he will run “new routes” in head coach Kevin Stefanski’s offensive scheme this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Just yesterday, ESPN’s Dan Graziano opined that the Falcons might want to see how Pitts fits in their new offense before committing to a long-term contract. Today, his colleague Marc Raimondi published comments from Pitts, who described the tag as being “kind of like my fifth-year option, but it’s a sixth-year option.” Pitts believes that the new staff’s tag use shows that they see something in him and “trust” him. Tagged players sometimes hold out or argue for a long-term deal. Not Pitts. He is ready to play. Stefanski, a former tight ends coach, has helped deliver TE1 results over the years. Per PFF, flats and hitches were Pitts’ most run routes last year. Based on Stefanski’s 2025 play designs with the Browns, Pitts could run them even more this year, while also running more drags, curls and potentially, overs. Pitts is a TE1 this season, but his range of potential outcomes is still being decided. Hopefully, we learn more during training camp next month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 54 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson’s 54 yards finished second on the team behind alpha Drake London but his four targets finished behind London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson. His status as the starting wide receiver opposite London likely means little in the wake of modest volume games that continue to stack up. He can safely be left on, or returned to, the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-3 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson continues to operate as the team’s WR2 opposite Drake London but remains unlikely to return consistent fantasy production in an offense heavily concentrated on its top two options in London and Bijan Robinson. Dotson’s touchdown came in the fourth quarter with the team cruising, pushing the lead to 21 points with under 10 minutes to play. Fantasy managers can safely keep Dotson on the bench ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens in Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 11 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson saw four targets for the second week in a row. He went for 19 yards on one catch last week and didn’t look any different this time around. Dotson is the team’s No. 2 receiver by routes, but there aren’t enough targets to go around after Drake London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson all get theirs. Dotson is not on the fantasy radar for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 1-of-3 targets for 19 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson actually operated as the second receiver for the Falcons in this one, running a route on 20 of the team’s 29 dropbacks. He also played 38 snaps, while Olamide Zaccheaus played just 18. That didn’t amount to much, but it’s something for fantasy managers in deeper leagues to keep in mind when Michael Penix eventually gets back onto the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes Falcons WR Zachariah Branch could start the season as a “gadget guy,” before later earning a starting role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Branch was a screen game dominator in college, with speed to spare. Raimondi thinks the Falcons will attempt to replicate his Georgia game early on, but Branch has a chance to become “the No. 3 guy, maybe even the No. 2 guy at some point.” Falcons WRs Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus sit in those two spots. Branch is unlikely to contribute meaningfully in fantasy early in the year, but he is worth keeping an eye on in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes that if the Falcons make a “random offseason move,” it might come at wide receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The Atlanta depth chart at wideout is sparse even after we account for third-round pick Zachariah Branch in the draft. The No. 2 receiver right now might be Jahan Dotson. Olamide Zaccheaus is also in the picture. The Falcons still have $27 million in cap space but we’ve rarely heard them mentioned by national reporters as interested in the Stefon Diggs/Deebo Samuel/Keenan Allen best veteran free agent wideout tier. Those guys aren’t mentioned in this report either, but they do make plenty of sense from a roster standpoint.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes Jahan Dotson “may be” Atlanta’s No. 2 receiver this year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The Falcons released Darnell Mooney and KhaDarel Hodge, leaving them with a depth chart behind Mooney of Olamide Zaccheaus, Casey Washington and Deven Thompkins. The Falcons, who lost their first-round pick in the ill-fated James Pearce trade, also don’t have many draft picks this year and could be less likely than most teams to draft a wideout that could challenge Dotson for a role. We’re not quite at “sleeper” status here, but we’re at least late-round Best Ball curious.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Falcons signed WR Jahan Dotson, formerly of the Eagles, to a two-year contract worth $15 million.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson could see starter’s snaps in Atlanta after the Falcons parted ways with Darnell Mooney. Dotson was stuck behind DeVonta Smith and A.J. Brown over the past couple seasons in Philadelphia with no real way to see consistent routes or targets in the Eagles’ ultra run-heavy offense. Dotson managed just 37 catches and one touchdown over 34 regular season games with the Eagles. In Atlanta he will be a distant WR2 at best in Kevin Stefanski’s offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson was held without a catch in the Eagles’ Wild Card loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Finishing up his second year as the Eagles’ sparingly-used No. 3 wideout, Dotston was sporadically productive in a dysfunctional passing attack. Headed to free agency after Philly declined his fifth-year team option, Dotson could end up back with the Eagles on a non-guaranteed contract. The 2022 draft bust’s two years in the Eagles’ system probably make him worth more to Philly than anybody else. That being said, we doubt Dotson would be a candidate to ascend to No. 2 status if A.J. Brown is traded.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 3-of-8 targets for 40 yards in the Eagles’ Week 18 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson saw increased opportunity with the Eagles resting most of their starters in Week 18. He was able to convert eight targets into only 40 yards, including a miscommunication with Tanner McKee that led to a goal line interception in the second quarter. Dotson will only see an increase in routes if A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith are out. Heading into the playoffs, he is the No. 3 wide receiver in the Eagles offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 7-of-11 targets for 118 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London started slow along with the rest of an Atlanta offense that gained just 37 total yards on their first three possessions before a 78-yard scoring drive to end the half. He would add six receptions after the break to push his season average to 127 yards per game in games started by Michael Penix. Penix departed late in the fourth quarter with a ribs injury, suddenly making London’s fantasy managers skittish after the veteran receiver managed a meager 80 total yards in two games without Penix to begin the season. Fantasy managers will want to monitor Atlanta’s starting quarterback’s status in the coming days ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Bears, where London will be a WR1 with Penix or an upside WR3 in his absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 5-of-6 targets for 96 yards in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London turned in his second consecutive usable fantasy week with Michael Penix under center. The low volume can primarily be attributed to just 20 Penix pass attempts in a game Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson combined for 207 yards and five touchdowns on the ground on 33 carries. London could be tasked with more volume when the Falcons host the Ravens in Week 5, for which he will remain an unquestioned WR1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 9-of-10 targets for 194 yards in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: To make the stat line more impressive, London didn’t catch his first pass until three minutes into the second quarter following a 1-of-5 start from Michael Penix. He would catch his final nine targets on his way to a massive fantasy day, combining with Bijan Robinson to set the NFL record for a wide receiver and running back duo to both go over 150 yards in the same game with three such occurrences. London continues to excel with Penix under center and returns to the WR1 ranks in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 4 meeting with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 4-of-5 targets for 51 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London also had a 25-yard grab called back by penalty. As expected, the Falcons simply rolled out a dead-on-arrival offense with Cooper Rush under center. Rush turned the ball over three times before being benched in the third quarter. Things didn’t get any better with Jack Strand under center. He threw an immediate pick-six and the Falcons promptly pulled the bulk of their starters from the game. With Michael Penix expected to play next week, London should return to the WR2 ranks next time we see him. If Penix isn’t available once again, London will barely register as a WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowlers reports Michael Penix (knee) is “not yet ready for live game action.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: Fowler said Penix, still recovering from his 2025 ACL injury, “wants to be fully confident before stepping onto the field. And my understanding is the Falcons are leaving the comfort level part of his recovery up to him.” “Penix is coming off his third ACL reconstruction, which is a lot of ACL reconstructions,” ESPN’s Dan Graziano added. “I believe it takes a lot of mental work to convince yourself it’s OK to go back out there and play. If Penix needs more time, I’m sure the Falcons will give it to him, though I believe we will see him on the field at some point this season.” That would leave Tua Tagovailoa as the team’s presumed starter if Tua can play through the oblique strain that sidelined him in Week 1 against the Steelers. If Tua can’t go, the Falcons could be forced to start Cooper Rush for another game or two. Rush, who had the lowest drop back EPA of any QB in Week 1, makes Drake London and Kyle Pitts iffy starts in 12-team fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 2-of-4 targets for 29 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London also added six yards on one rush as the Falcons looked to do anything to get the ball in the hands of their best receiver. The 25-year-old was an absolute non-factor in this one, largely because Cooper Rush was highly inefficient and ineffective under center. The role is not in question though. London played 60 of the team’s 61 snaps and ran a route on 28 of their 29 dropbacks. However, he will be tough to trust with Cooper Rush (and probably even Tua Tagovailoa) under center. London has a much better matchup next week against the Panthers, but there is some fear that he’s more of a WR2 option until Michael Penix (knee) returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes Falcons WR Jahan Dotson will “probably” be the team’s No. 2 wide receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: Raimondi believes Dotson’s ability to stretch the field from the perimeter adds an element to the Falcons’ offense that they lacked in recent seasons. Although WR Drake London has been regularly deployed as a part-time slot weapon, Dotson’s presence helps reinforce London’s slot opportunities this season. Great news for all involved.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Falcons signed WR Drake London to a four-year, $141 million extension through 2030.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London can make up to $150 million on the new contract, which includes $100 million guaranteed. ESPN’s Adam Schefter notes that the deal “makes London the third-highest-paid receiver in the league with the highest average per year in Falcons franchise history.” Over the course of his four-year career, London has caught 309-of-473 targets for 3,961 yards and 22 touchdowns. A knee injury sidelined him in Weeks 12-15 last year, yet he still led the team with seven receiving touchdowns. London, 24, has not yet been named to a Pro Bowl, nor has he earned All-Pro honors, but it is reasonable to expect him to bring home a few accolades in the coming seasons. London is a WR1 for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Falcons GM Ian Cunningham said an extension for Drake London is “on top of mind.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London said the team remains focused on free agency and adds that an extension for London, along with RB Bijan Robinson, may not receive more focus until after the draft. London is in the final year of his rookie contract and caught 68 passes for 919 yards and seven touchdowns last season.
