https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: MarShawn Lloyd rushed six times for 20 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets, adding six yards receiving and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Perhaps more importantly, Lloyd lost a key fumble in the second half and then was barely on the field after that. The 25-year-old had plenty of trouble earning yards in the running game, but he was wide open on a well-designed screen pass in the first half for a touchdown catch. Lloyd played on just 16 of the Packers’ 53 snaps and handled seven of their 19 carries. This is a confusing committee that isn’t giving any running back real value, and Josh Jacobs could return at some point near the middle of the season. Fantasy managers in shallow leagues don’t need to hold onto Lloyd, and others could look to trade him away on the back of his receiving touchdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: MarShawn Lloyd rushed 13 times for 37 yards in the Packers’ Week 1 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Chris Brooks drew the start in this game and held a carries advantage over Lloyd for a while. Matt LaFleur eventually came to his senses and got Lloyd more involved, though it didn’t result in much production. He averaged a measly 2.8 yards per carry and didn’t catch his lone target. Lloyd will project for more carries than Brooks in Week 2, but he’s a committee back without a role in the passing game. Lloyd will shuffle to the back of the RB3 ranks versus the Jets next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Packers RB Josh Jacobs remains on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and that there is “no timetable” as to when he could be disciplined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: The NFL is “closely monitoring all developments in the matter, which remains under review of the personal conduct policy.” We expect Jacobs to receive a suspension, but the league can move at its own pace. Packers RB MarShawn Lloyd is expected to serve as the fill-in starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman reports Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Jacobs’ trial was initially slated to take place on November 17th. That date was recently moved up to today, signaling that Jacobs wanted to wrap up his legal proceedings quickly. He has been on the Commissioner’s Exempt List since the end of training camp. Roger Goodell could have kept him on the list indefinitely, especially with the trial previously scheduled multiple months into the season. With the legal matter now settled, Jacobs will likely serve a minor suspension as a result of the charges. MarShawn Lloyd is expected to handle the bulk of the carries until he returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said he expected Josh Jacobs to play for the team in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: “Asked if there’s a scenario in which the Packers release Jacobs, Gutekunst says he wants to let the process play out,” The Athletic’s Matt Schneidmann said. Jacobs on Sunday was placed on the Commissioners Exempt List while his legal situation plays out. Jacobs in May was arrested and booked on five charges, including felony strangulation. ESPN’s Adam Schefter said Monday that Jacobs’ time on the exempt list was, for now, indefinite, and hinged entirely on how his legal situation unfolds. If damning video evidence is released, Jacobs could miss most or all of the regular season. MarShawn Lloyd would start the year as Green Bay’s lead back and has a chance to be one of fantasy’s best running back values.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-5 targets for 16 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson had hovered around 50 yards in every game before today’s loss, but a shutdown Minnesota defense was more than enough to mute the production of every New Orleans pass-catcher. Things should improve for everyone when the Saints take on the Giants next week. Johnson will be a volume-based TE2 for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 6-of-8 targets for 59 yards in the Saints’ Week 4 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson saw a slight uptick in snaps and routes after Noah Fant was inactive with an abdominal injury but returned a modest receiving line while being kept out of the end zone. The towering veteran finished third on the team in targets behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele, the latter of whom scored the only receiving touchdown in a game that saw the two teams combine for seven rushing scores. Johnson remains a back-end TE1 for as long as rookie Jordyn Tyson remains sidelined, which appears likely to persist for another few weeks, at minimum. That holds true ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the vaunted Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 8-of-8 targets for 53 yards, two touchdowns and one lost fumble in the Saints’ Week 3 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was getting open at will on out routes and shallow crossers. He and Noah Fant, along with the two Raiders tight ends, combined for six touchdowns, tying an NFL positional record. Johnson fumbled while trying to make a big play for his team late in the game. He attempted to stiff-arm Nakobe Dean, who cleanly punched the ball out for Eric Stokes to recover. Tyler Shough threw a bad pass to Johnson earlier on, which CB Hezekiah Masses easily picked off and returned downfield. Johnson raced after him and successfully punched the ball out with a diving hammer-fist, but the Raiders ultimately recovered that fumble, leading to a turnover for the Saints. Johnson remains a reliable TE1 against the Falcons next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-4 targets for 66 yards in the Saints’ Week 2 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson was on the receiving end of two big plays in Sunday’s win over the Ravens. Johnson hauled in a short pass on a third-and-13 in the third quarter and turned it upfield for a 25-yard gain. In the fourth quarter, Johnson again picked up 25 yards on a short pass on third-and-eight, taking it to the Ravens’ five-yard line and setting the Saints up for a touchdown a few plays later. Johnson has caught seven passes in his first two games and is averaging an impressive 17.1 YPR on said catches. He’ll be on the TE2 radar for next week’s game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Saints TE Juwan Johnson (illness) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson posted a 3/54/1 receiving line last week and can be treated as a TE1 again in Week 2. Saints WR1 Chris Olave is nursing a hamstring strain, though the team is telling reporters that the injury is not concerning. Johnson could take on a slightly larger workload if Olave is at all limited, though we won’t know if that is the case until the dust settles and the game ends.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Saints TE Juwan Johnson (illness) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson is firmly on track to play. Illness-related absences are very rare, and the Saints’ No. 1 tight end is already back at it. The Saints face the Ravens this weekend, in what should be a high-scoring game environment. Johnson is a locked-in TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson (illness) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Players rarely miss games because of illnesses, especially when it crops up four days before kickoff. Johnson should be fine, but fantasy managers counting on him as a high-end TE2 will want to check in on Friday. Fellow tight end Oscar Delp was limited with a hamstring issue. He missed Week 1 because of the injury but has a shot at making his NFL debut versus the Ravens this Sunday. He will not be on the fantasy radar if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Juwan Johnson caught 3-of-7 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints’ Week 1 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Johnson didn’t catch his first pass of the game until the final minute, when Tyler Shough found him in the end zone for a game-tying score. He then racked up another 45 yards on a catch at the end of the fourth quarter and another in overtime. Johnson only finished fourth on the team in targets, which could be an issue when the team’s passing volume inevitably dips. He will be a mid-range TE2 for another potential shootout with the Ravens next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Saints TE Oscar Delp’s hamstring injury does not sound “like a serious deal.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Delp is dealing with a hamstring injury, missing the Saints’ practice on Tuesday. With Jordan Tyson (hamstring) slated to miss at least the next couple months, NFL Network’s Steve Wyche and Garafolo believe the Saints will lean on their tight ends. The rookie Delp is behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant on the depth chart. Based on Garafolo’s report, he won’t miss too much time with his hamstring strain; he has upside as a Dynasty stash but Juwan Johnson should be the top tight end as a low-end fantasy TE1 heading into the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.headline: Louisiana Sports’ Ross Jackson believes Oscar Delp “won’t see such a limited role in head coach Kellen Moore’s offense.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/juwan-john.analysis: Jackson noted that the rookie tight end was “the top target for the team’s offense” during the team’s first day of minicamp. Most rookie tight ends don’t bring much fantasy value to the table in their first season, but Delp could be the latest exception to that rule, especially if Moore plans to follow the trend of 12 and even 13 personnel sweeping the league. Delp wasn’t awfully productive at Georgia, peaking at just 284 yards as a sophomore, but he is a solid YAC creator and isn’t afraid to put his hand in the dirt to block. Delp should at least be on the radar in all dynasty formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed six times for 11 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright entered the day questionable with a foot injury and wound up playing nine offensive snaps with special teams mixed in. The 23-year-old is the clear backup to Ollie Gordon for now, he is best left off fantasy rosters.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) is active for Week 5 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright had back-to-back limited practices to close out the week after seemingly reaggravating a foot injury. He is active against the Bengals and will backup Ollie Gordon for Week 5. The Dolphins declared WR Caleb Douglas (ankle), RB Kaytron Allen, CB Reese Taylor, EDGE Rob Beal Jr., G DJ Campbell, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, and TE Justin Joly inactive for Week 5 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) is questionable for Miami’s Week 5 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright was limited on Thursday and Friday after seemingly reinjuring his foot. He feels like a true wild card for Sunday. Ollie Gordon-reliant managers would benefit if Wright were ruled out, as it appears Kaytron Allen, who was just claimed on waivers today, would be the backup if Wright can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: It’s unclear if this was related to the foot that was giving Wright problems earlier this year, but a mid-week downgrade is never great news for a player. Wright has a real chance to miss Week 5. We’ll probably have a better sign of how likely it is that he plays Friday morning if no national reporters pick up the story earlier than that.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed five times for seven yards in the Dolphins’ Week 4 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: The best thing we can say about Wright’s day is that he got the start. The Dolphins kept him out there for the first drive, giving him a chance to keep his position, but he was unable to do so. Ollie Gordon outplayed him as the game progressed, rushing nine times for 100 yards and one touchdown, while Wright was relegated to unproductive offensive snaps and five kick returns for 97 yards. Wright is a zero-floor FLEX against the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: The South Florida Sun Sentinel’s David Furones reports that Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright is lining up with the first-team offense during pre-game warmups.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Dolphins RB Ollie Gordon is rotating in behind Wright, confirming Wright is the team’s current starter. That said, the Dolphins could still split the backfield workload almost evenly. We won’t know what the plan is until the game is underway. For now, Wright should be viewed as the slightly safer FLEX, though both running backs could get bottled up by the Vikings’ defense today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright sits atop the Dolphins’ depth chart with De’Von Achane (knee) done for the year. He will likely split touches with new No. 2 running back Ollie Gordon in a very difficult matchup against the Vikings this week. Both players are worth rostering, but they are shaky FLEX starters this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said Jaylen Wright (foot) should be good to go for Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright was a full participant in Thursday’s and Friday’s practices, which is a good sign for his Week 4 availability. If he doesn’t draw a questionable tag later in the day, we’ll go ahead and assume that the third-year back will be on the field when the Dolphins visit the Vikings. Wright should be in line for a decent day as far as volume is concerned, but it’s hard to invest much hope in him or Ollie Gordon, who will split work with De’Von Achane (knee) out for the remainder of the season. It’s hard to know how the touches could be distributed here, but fantasy managers shouldn’t be rushing to put either back in their lineups against a stout Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright should be rostered in 12-team leagues. He is now on track to play in Week 4 against the Vikings and is still listed ahead of RB Ollie Gordon on the Dolphins’ depth chart. The Vikings’ defense could bottle up this running back, but things might get a tad easier in Week 5 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) said he was “very close” to playing in Week 3 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright and RB Ollie Gordon are expected to split backfield touches moving forward, though this could be a fluid situation if one running back simply outplays the other. Gordon profiles as a burly grinder, while Wright may offer more big-play potential. It sounds like Wright has a strong chance of playing in Week 4 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson rushed four times for 13 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings, adding one catch for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Alvin Kamara entered this game with a back injury and played just eight snaps in the second half, freeing up some extra work for Donaldson. He led the team in snaps, but Kendre Miller was the top option between the tackles, seeing 10 carries, one of which went for a touchdown. Even if Kamara remains on the injury report for Week 6, Donaldson won’t crack the FLEX rankings versus the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Kamara briefly left the Saints’ Week 4 game against the Falcons to deal with a knee injury. Today, he is sidelined by a back injury. It’s perhaps unsurprising for a 31-year-old player who has clearly lost a step at this point in his career. He is backed up by Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson. Either player can be stashed in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Saints placed Travis Etienne on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: This is a tough break. The Saints’ high-priced free agent signee will be sidelined for at least four games. Their Week 8 bye makes him eligible to return in Week 9. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara is the next man up, followed by RB Kendre Miller. Both should be rostered in 12-team leagues. Kamara will likely get the first crack at the starting job, but he has struggled to play efficiently this season, and coach Kellen Moore gave RB CJ Donaldson the backfield’s first green zone touch last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne exited Week 3 against the Raiders after suffering an apparent hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Etienne entered the game with a hamstring injury and appears to have aggravated it on an explosive run. The Saints’ starting running back broke off a 16-yard gain in the third quarter, setting up a Saints passing touchdown on the following play. Etienne could be seen grabbing at his left hamstring at the end of the run. He had mostly been limited to modest single-digit gains before that, rushing 13 times for 57 yards and catching 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards on the day. He seems highly unlikely to return. Etienne and the other veteran running backs notably ceded the first backfield touch inside the green zone to RB CJ Donaldson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Saints RB Kendre Miller (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The good news is that Miller was not listed with a knee injury after suffering a season-ending ACL tear in Week 7 last year. The bad news is that he evidently has a new injury, and the Saints have a fairly deep running back room right now. RBs Devin Neal, Audric Estime, Ty Chandler and CJ Donaldson are all vying for roster spots. Per Underhill, Neal is taking advantage of the extra reps. He could have the inside track to the RB3 role right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Saints signed Ohio State RB CJ Donaldson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson (6’2”/230) burst on the scene as a true freshman at West Virginia, rushing for 87-526-6 in seven games before a leg injury ended his season. Donaldson was recruited as a three-star tight end before moving to RB during training camp and quickly cemented himself as the starter for the Mountaineers. He rushed for 421-2,058-30 in three seasons before transferring to Ohio State last season. With the Buckeyes, Donaldson managed just 96 carries in 13 games, rushing for 361 yards and 10 scores while averaging a paltry 3.8 YPC. Despite his prowess as a former tight end, Donaldson has never been much of a factor in the passing game, catching just 47 passes for 286 yards in four seasons. Despite his size, Donaldson struggled mightily after contact, posting a 2.99 yards after contact per attempt for his career, and averaging 2.92 YCO/ATT or less in each of his final three seasons. He totaled just 24 carries of 15 or more yards in his career, and may not have much to offer outside of a short-yardage/goal-line role. His larger body of work leaves much to be desired. He’ll need a strong camp if he hopes to stick on the end of a roster. The Saints also signed DT Keeshawn Silver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 18 times for 88 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon continued to operate as the Dolphins’ No. 1 running back, scoring a touchdown for the second straight week. He took all of Miami’s red zone backfield touches and was tackled at the one yard line in the third quarter, coming close to his second touchdown of the day. He lost two yards the next play and the Dolphins did not convert. Gordon saw 42 snaps on the day and will be a low-end fantasy RB2 for Week 7 against the Jets after a Week 6 bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed nine times for 100 yards and one touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon entered the game on the Dolphins’ second drive, generating one yard and two receptions on three touches during that possession. Things improved from there. After letting nominal starting RB Jaylen Wright and Gordon each play their own drives, the Dolphins eventually began rotating them in and out until Gordon separated on the first drive after halftime. Gordon notched three carries in a row, breaking off a 53-yarder on the second one by navigating traffic and making his way to the left sideline, shedding a jersey grab along the way. On the seventh drive, he had what could have been a breakaway touchdown run blown dead by officials, who thought Gordon was down by contact as he stumbled through the box. It was a close call. He then touched the ball on two-of-four plays on the ensuing drive, including a touchdown run up the middle from 12 yards out, in which Gordon acrobatically vaulted over a downed lineman. Tentatively expect Gordon to be the Dolphins’ starter in Week 5 against the Bengals and treat him as an RB2/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) was limited during practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Wright was inactive with his foot injury last week against Kansas City. De’Von Achane went down with a season-ending ACL injury and Ollie Gordon took over as the team’s workhorse with no other running back on the active roster. Dolphins coaches have implied that both Gordon and Wright will get work in the Miami backfield with Achane out. An even backfield split would make both Wright and Gordon nothing more than deep-league flex plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said all running backs on the roster are “going to have their roles.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: In other words, expect a committee. Ollie Gordon remains the most likely back to chair the committee in the short-term as he’s actually healthy while Jaylen Wright missed last week’s game and has just seven snaps this year in two games while active to Gordon’s 15 in the first two weeks. This all feels a little desperate given how poor the Dolphins have looked, but volume at running back is volume at running back in a year where many RB2 stabs have disappointed early.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: De’Von Achane suffered a torn ACL in the Dolphins’ Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, ending his season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: It felt like things were trending in this direction when head coach Jeff Hafley said after the game that he was not “optimistic” about Achane’s injury, but now the worst has confirmed. The 0-3 Dolphins will now be without their best playmaker for the remainder of the season, creating yet another challenge for an offense that ranks 31st in points per game (12.0 PPG) and 26th in yards per game (290.7 YPG) through the first three weeks of the season. Ollie Gordon will become a priority add off of waivers this week after he rushed for 17-41-1 in place of Achane, but his upside will be limited in what is one of the worst offenses in the league. Third-year vet Jaylen Wright could also be worth a stash. Wright missed Week 3’s game with a stringer/foot injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 11-of-20 targets for 121 yards and one touchdown in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers saw 15 of his targets come in the second half after the Giants opted to abandon a mostly useless ground game in a game they trailed for most of the afternoon. Nabers came up with multiple big plays as the Giants mounted their comeback attempt, with his biggest coming on a leaping 17-yard touchdown in the end zone to tie the game at 27-27 with under two minutes to go in the game. Nabers had a key drop on a screen pass in overtime that had a chance to set up a big gain, but he made up for it later in the game with a 28-yard gain as the Giants were trying to position themselves for a potential game-winning field goal attempt. Nabers has now gone for 100-plus yards in back-to-back weeks and has found the end zone in both of those games. He seems to finally be hitting his stride after a slow start to the season, and will profile as a high-end WR2 in next week’s game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Malik Nabers (knee) will be “ready to play” on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: It was presumed that Nabers would play after sitting out Wednesday with soreness in his surgically repaired knee. Though this is just our speculation, the Giants may take it easier on their star receiver this week after he hauled in 6/112/1 against the Cardinals in Week 4. He remains on the WR2 line in what has been (when not facing the Cardinals) a rough offense with Jameis Winston under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers is currently going through route running drills with his position group, putting him on track to play in Week 5 against the Commanders. Nabers sat out yesterday, citing extra soreness in his surgically repaired knee, but told ESPN’s Jordan Raanan that he usually feels better as the week progresses. A WR1 finish is in play this week, assuming he is active. He was later listed as limited on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Earlier today, The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reported that Nabers sat in the rehab section, speaking with the team’s head trainer during individual drills before seemingly going through some sort of rehab routine. ESPN’s Jordan Raanan then reported that Nabers said he was feeling “more sore than usual,” and “did as much as he could at practice.” When asked whether this could affect his ability to play in Week 5 against the Commanders, Nabers said, “we’ll see,” adding that it usually gets better as the week progresses. We tentatively expect Nabers to play, though this is worth monitoring closely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 6-of-7 targets for 112 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 4 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers’ first 100-yard game of the season almost didn’t happen after he re-injured his shoulder on a soaring first quarter reception, his first catch of the afternoon. He thankfully shook it off and went on to score his first touchdown, as well, a 25-yarder in the second quarter. He got matched up 1-on-1 with LB Mack Wilson, and Jameis Winston did not miss. It was a desperately needed outing for fantasy managers who were beginning to wonder if Nabers would even produce WR2 returns, let alone WR1. The top 12 is probably still a little far fetched, but this was an encouraging outing heading into next week’s road date with the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 5-of-6 targets for 26 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: The good news is that Nabers didn’t appear bothered by his shoulder injury and led the Giants with a 27 percent target share. The bad news is everything else. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants took the air out of the ball and ran 33 times compared to just 22 pass attempts. Winston also stuck mostly to check-down duties, taking any chance of a big play for Nabers off the table. The Giants should be forced to throw more next week, but this isn’t going to be an exciting offense without Jaxson Dart under center. Nabers is likely stuck in the WR2 ranks for Week 4 versus the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers is not on New York’s final Week 3 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: It sure didn’t seem like he had great chemistry with Jameis Winston on Monday night, leaving Nabers feeling more like a mid-range WR2 than someone you’d really want to count on to carry you to victory in what will be a windy Week 3 game against the Titans. Still, he’s fully healthy and got in full practices in each of the last two days of the week to clear the injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (shoulder) said his shoulder feels good and x-rays came back with positive results.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers speaking to the media is likely also good news for his availability on Sunday. The 23-year-old wideout is practicing and upgraded to full today, so he’s likely to be good to go and has a chance at avoiding a questionable tag on Friday altogether.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Giants WR Malik Nabers (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers hurt his shoulder in the Giants’ Week 2 loss to the Rams, staying in the game and catching zero passes after the injury. The Giants had a walkthrough practice on Wednesday, listing Nabers as limited. When asked if the 23-year-old had X-rays done, head coach John Harbaugh gave his usual vague answer, saying, “I don’t know.” A limited practice listing indicates Nabers is not dealing with a major issue, but his practice status is worth monitoring leading up to Week 3 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 1-of-4 targets for one yard in the Giants’ Week 2 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers departed the game at the end of the first quarter with a shoulder injury but was able to return after missing only one drive. His putrid box score can largely be attributed to uneven quarterback play from backup Jameis Winston, whom came on in relief of the injured Jaxson Dart after the team’s first possession. Beyond the fact that fantasy managers were left with a near goose egg from their third round selection, Nabers could be forced to contend with backup-level quarterback play in the coming weeks considering the mechanism of Dart’s knee injury. Even so, it will be difficult to sit Nabers in a cake matchup with the Titans in Week 3, making him a classic hold-your-breath start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 6-of-8 targets for 143 yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson’s 143-yard outburst was the third highest receiving total of his career, joining a Week 11 2024 effort and his 6/147/2 broadside against the Vikings this Week 1. Rather amazingly, the two-score effort was his seventh. This one came in true Watson fashion, as he found the end zone from 42 and 53 yards out. For the 42-yarder he ran right by the defense. For the 53-yarder, he high-pointed the ball off the defender’s helmet in the end zone. It was just that kind of day for the Packers, and it’s been just that kind of season for a wideout in Watson who continues to break out. Now firmly in the weekly WR1 mix, Watson has a potential Week 6 smash spot in the sorry Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught all three of his targets for 47 yards in the Packers’ Week 4 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: After scoring four touchdowns over the first three weeks, Watson finally cooled off with his first quiet game of the year. Jordan Love couldn’t get the deep ball going in this game and funneled the short targets to Tucker Kraft and Matthew Golden, leaving Watson without much to do. For a player known for having a low floor, 47 yards is a stunningly reasonable floor game. Watson is simply too good at picking up chunk gains to have the bottom truly fall out. He remains a boom/bust WR2 for his Week 5 date with the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 7-of-10 targets for 96 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson now has four touchdowns through three games while ranking one target behind Matthew Golden for the team lead at 29. Even better news for fantasy managers is the fact that we’re likely to see this sudden spike in pass volume continue forward given the current state of the Green Bay backfield and offensive line, meaning fantasy managers can continue to start Watson as a legitimate WR1 ahead of a road meeting with the pass-funnel Buccaneers in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 4-of-11 targets for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: It was not a pretty game for Watson or the Packers’ offense, which struggled to move the ball against the Jets in a light drizzle all game. While Watson and Jordan Love were inefficient in their connection, they did link up for some big catches, including a short fourth-quarter touchdown. Watson led the team in targets while running one fewer route than Matthew Golden. There is some concern that losing Jayden Reed (neck) to an injury may put even more attention on Watson, but this felt like an off-day for the offense. The ceiling remains really high for Watson this season, especially next week against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 6-of-8 targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers’ Week 1 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson got on the board early with an 81-yard bomb for a touchdown in the first quarter. He continued to gash the Vikings for big plays throughout the contest and even got in the end zone a second time on a short toss from Jordan Love just before halftime. Watson slowed down in the second half, but the damage was already done, at least for fantasy purposes. He won’t hit a career-long score every week, but the well-paid wideout certainly looked like a focal point of the Packers’ passing attack today. He will be in the WR2 mix when the Packers take on the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said the team needs Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden “out there for as many plays as humanly possible.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Prior reports indicated that the Packers’ coaching staff realized that their frequent wide receiver rotation was rubbing their stars the wrong way, prompting a positional personnel churn this offseason. LaFleur’s comments confirm the Packers’ starting wide receiver trio is going to play a lot, and fantasy managers should take note. Watson played extremely well in his recent from an ACL tear last year. If that play carries over, he is a shoo-in WR2 with substantial upside. Golden could be in for a Year 2 leap, and Reed could reliably return FLEX value, or better, if his snap share is high enough.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Packers WR Jayden Reed and WR Christian Watson took first-team reps in two-wide receiver sets on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: We know this is getting into the weeds, but Reed’s weekly range of outcomes will be somewhat dependent on his access to heavy personnel packages. Through three NFL seasons, Reed has taken just 31 snaps in 12 personnel, so even a mild increase would boost his target-earning opportunities. Packers QB Jordan Love confirmed that second-year WR Matthew Golden is replacing WR Romeo Doubs as the X-receiver when speaking with the media today, so Golden and Watson (Z-receiver) will likely take the majority of 12 personnel reps this season. If Reed can at least send Golden to the sideline for a decent share of those opportunities, his fantasy managers would stand to benefit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Packers signed WR Christian Watson to a four-year, $110.5 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The extension was first reported by ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The deal includes a $31 million signing bonus. The Packers have stocked their receiver room for years now. Green Bay let Romeo Doubs walk in free agency this offseason, but signed Watson and Jayden Reed to extensions this offseason after drafting Matthew Golden last year. Watson appeared in only 48 games in four seasons with the Packers. He appeared in just 10 games last year, but arguably had his best season and that was enough for Green Bay to lock him in as their top wideout for years to come.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Eagles acquired WR Dontayvion Wicks from the Packers in exchange for a 2026 fifth-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter breaks the news, adding that Wicks will now sign a one-year, $12.5 million extension with the Eagles. Over the last four weeks, they also signed WR Hollywood Brown and WR Elijah Moore as well. Schefter reminds us that if the Eagles were to trade away WR A.J. Brown, that would probably happen after June 1st, “when the cap burden would be more manageable for the Eagles.” As things currently stand, Wicks will likely compete for WR3 duties. The trade also leaves Packers WR Christian Watson, WR Jayden Reed and WR Matthew Golden as the team’s top-three options after allowing WR Romeo Doubs to sign with the Patriots last month. The Eagles tacked on an additional year to Wicks’ contract after the deal, tying him to the franchise through the 2027 season. The extension includes $12.5 million in maximum money with $9 million guaranteed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Packers WR Christian Watson said he wants to sign a “long-term” contract extension to remain in Green Bay.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson remains under contract through 2026, having signed a one-year extension in September 2025. The 26-year-old wide receiver suffered a season-ending ACL tear in 2024 and retook the field for the first time in Week 8, 2025. He impressively averaged a career-high 2.28 yards per route run despite coming off a significant knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 7-of-11 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: The 100-yard effort was Wilson’s second in three weeks. It was no easy feat on a rainy afternoon in Jersey where Geno Smith completed only 17 passes. Wilson’s score was a 32-yarder where he spun out of a tackle for a catch-and-run house call. In addition to the 100-yard efforts, Wilson now has a score in three of his past four appearances. It’s like Wilson’s lost 2025 never happened, which is exactly what the Jets and fantasy managers were hoping for. A weekly fixture in the low-end WR1 ranks, Wilson has a Week 6 date with the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 3-of-4 targets for 27 yards in the Jets’ Week 4 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: No one on the Jets offense got home for fantasy purposes as the Bears held on to the ball for several long drives in the second half. The Jets possessed the ball for just 17 minutes on the day. Wilson’s four targets led the New York offense, as Geno Smith was limited to a mere 15 pass attempts. Wilson continues to dominate air yards and targets in the Jets offense and should remain in all lineups next week against Cleveland.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Garrett Wilson was evaluated for a concussion and was cleared to return in the Jets’ Week 3 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson took a hard hit late in the fourth quarter and was slow to get up. The Jets turned the ball over on the next play, so we never got to see Wilson return, but it sounds like he would have been back on the field had the game gone to overtime. Wilson ended the day with 10 catches for 107 yards and a touchdown on 13 targets. He found the end zone on an incredible circus catch late in the fourth quarter to tie the game up. As expected, Wilson was the focal point of the Jets’ passing attack with Adonai Mitchell sidelined. Even if Mitchell returns next week versus the Bears, Wilson will be moving up the WR2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 5-of-7 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 2 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson saw five fewer targets than Adonai Mitchell, but played more snaps and ran more routes. Mitchell simply sees more quick-hitter looks close to the line of scrimmage, while Wilson is used more over the middle of the field. The Packers also frequently sent safety help over to Wilson’s side, but the 26-year-old was still able to make a few big catches when they mattered. He should be in for a bigger day against the Lions next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 6-of-7 targets for 79 yards in the Jets’ Week 1 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: With the Jets in the unusual position of dominating a game from whistle to whistle, new QB Geno Smith dropped back just 24 times. Translation, Wilson coming away with seven targets was actually a pretty good outcome. The Jets’ blocking appeared much improved, but this was not a true test, even if it came on the road. That will come in Week 2 for the Jets’ home opener against the Packers. Wilson will remain a solid WR2 whose high floor will hopefully be accompanied by more ceiling efforts this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich said he’s been “so impressed” with Geno Smith’s play.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Reich has reportedly added wrinkles to the offense he deployed as head coach of the Colts and Panthers. At both of those stops his offenses were near the bottom of the league in most basic offensive metrics. Smith, meanwhile, has looked sharp as the team’s starting quarterback throughout training camp and in limited preseason snaps. He’ll look to bounce back from a nightmarish statistical 2025 season in Vegas. Jets players, including Garrett Wilson, told The Athletic that they have enjoyed the “player empowerment” that comes along with Reich’s coaching style and his offensive scheming, which leaves room for improvisation. The Jets offense could be functional as long as Smith, 35, is healthy and upright.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson said his knee has felt “great” at practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson’s knee injury cost him 10 games last season, but the star receiver is in a good spot this offseason. Wilson is participating in OTAs and also had praise for his quarterback, Geno Smith, who he said throws a “friendly ball.” It’s an encouraging sign for the 25-year-old receiver who posted three-straight 1,000-yard seasons to start his career before his 2025 season was derailed. He’s the unquestioned WR1 on the Jets’ depth chart and is surrounded by unproven talent in Adonai Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. Wilson will have high-end WR2 upside this season with a chance to crack the top-12 at his position in fantasy in a new-look offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes reports the Jets are “open to dealing & listening.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: The reports comes off the heels of New York swapping Jermaine Johnson for T’Vondre Sweat. Hughes made it clear the Jets aren’t having a fire sale, though it’s hard to see this as anything else. They sent most of their big names packing at the trade deadline last year, with Sauce Gardner, Quinnen Williams, and Michael Carter all traded. At this point, the Jets are running out of players to deal, even if they want to keep making moves. Justin Fields is expected to be released, but a team looking to sign him could guarantee his services by trading for him. Garrett Wilson was also the subject of trade rumors last year, though the Jets just inked him to a long-term deal and didn’t seem interested in moving him at the deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said Garrett Wilson (knee) will not return this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Glenn had been reluctant to say in recent weeks whether Wilson would return this season, but he has finally confirmed that his WR1 will be shut down for the remainder of the season. Wilson suffered a knee sprain in Week 6 against the Broncos and re-aggravated that same injury in Week 11. The Week 11 injury landed Wilson on injured reserve, meaning he wouldn’t be eligible to return until Week 15. With the Jets in the final weeks of another lost season, there was little reason to force Wilson back on the field and risk another injury. Wilson caught 36 passes for 395 yards and four touchdowns in the seven games he appeared in this season while averaging 8.4 targets per game. This will mark the first time in his four-year career that Wilson failed to go for 1,000 yards, but there’s little reason to believe he won’t be ready to bounce back next season. The Jets have a lot to figure out this offseason, especially at the quarterback position following the failed Justin Fields experiment. Despite the question marks in the team’s QB room, Wilson should profile as a high-upside WR2 in fantasy next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said he did not have an update on Garrett Wilson (knee) possibly returning from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson is eligible to be activated off injured reserve this week, but Glenn declined to comment on whether or not that would happen. The Jets’ head coach said any decision to activate Wilson would be a medical decision that’s made by Wilson and the team doctors. The Jets are 3-10 and in the process of wrapping up another lost season. Given the nature of his knee injury and the fact that it was a re-aggravation that landed him on injured reserve, it would seem there’s little reason for the Jets to risk the health of their top receiver at this point in the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 1-of-2 targets for 4 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: The Bengals utilized all of their tight ends against the Dolphins, with Gesicki catching just one pass on the day. His sole reception was a touchdown on the Bengals’ opening drive, totaling four on the season and salvaging some fantasy value for those who streamed him at tight end this week. Gesicki’s value is lowered when Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are active; his red zone utilization makes Gesicki a low-end fantasy TE2 heading into the Bengals’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Bengals’ Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki caught a third quarter touchdown against the Jaguars, his third score of the year. He saw just five targets on a day where Joe Burrow threw 54 passes and Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) exited early. However, Gesicki has a clear red zone role and he led all Bengals tight ends in snaps on the day. If Chase and Tee Higgins (adductor) miss any time, Gesicki is a tight end streaming option for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 3-of-3 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 3 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: After going without a target last week, Gesicki made the most of his three targets in this one. His most notable reception came in the fourth quarter on a fourth-and-two when he broke free across the middle of the field for a wide-open 25-yard touchdown to put the Bengals up 27-24. Gesicki has now scored in two of his first three games this season, but is averaging just 3.3 targets per game. Fantasy managers should be rushing to add him to their lineups for next week’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki was not targeted in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: The rollercoaster ride that is “tertiary target in a Tee Higgins/Ja’Marr Chase-centric offense.” Erick All (2/5 on three targets) lead Bengals tight ends in receptions. Drew Sample (36 of 60) led Bengals tight ends in snaps. Starting Gesicki will pay off at times, but this wasn’t one of them. He’s a TE2 in Week 3 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 5-of-7 targets for 78 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki led the Bengals in catches, targets and yards and was the only pass catcher to score on an afternoon where the Bucs’ defense was funneling Joe Burrow to the middle of the field. Gesicki’s score was a two-yarder where he rolled in to the end zone in the first quarter. Gesicki’s yardage total would have been his second highest of 2025. He’s a valuable real-life contributor, but he is going to have trouble cracking the top 18 tight ends on a regular basis with Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown all usage monsters for the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: ESPN’s Ben Baby reports that Bengals rookie WR Colbie Young is competing for OC Dan Pitcher’s “passing target No. 3" role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Baby’s practice notes indicate that incumbent No. 3 WR Andrei Iosivas and No. 1 TE Mike Gesicki are the other two competitors for the role, and both players “had productive springs.” Pitcher also said RB Chase Brown “can sometimes be viewed as a slot receiver,” but those types of comments are common in the summer and rarely pan out in the fall. Iosivas and Gesicki have been helpful contributors, but the fact that the team is searching for an answer at the No. 3 receiving role is indicative of their ceilings. Pitcher believes Young is “going to fight and battle” this summer, and thinks there are things Young “can do quickly and help us.” If he can actually become the team’s third-most voluminous target earner, he could pay off as a late-round best ball pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Bengals’ Week 18 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Hot off a rebound 2024 season, Gesicki inked a three-year, $25.5 million contract to stay in Cincinnati in the offseason. It became apparent early in the year that Gesicki would not be giving Bengals fans an encore in 2025. He was held under 20 receiving yards in each of his first six games before a pec injury sent him to injured reserve. Gesicki started to turn things around after coming off IR, totaling 35 yards on four grabs in Week 12. At the time, it was his best game of the year. He eventually popped for a few other meaningful games, though he ultimately topped 50 yards just once on the year. He posted a 28/307/2 receiving line in total. The Bengals could save $3.3 million in cap space with a $4.3 million dead cap hit if they move on from him after the year. Either way, we don’t expect him to be on the fantasy radar in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 2-of-2 targets for 47 yards in the Bengals’ Week 17 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: This is close to Gesicki’s standard statline when the Bengals’ offense is at full strength, which it is at the current moment. They have a rough Week 18 matchup in the Browns, meaning Gesicki probably won’t be much of a DFS play even with the usual final Sunday chicanery primed to be more insane than ever this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 3-of-4 targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 16 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: This was only the fourth time all season Gesicki caught at least three passes, though the score was his second in three weeks. Good for him, but there’s still no reason to rank Gesicki in the top 20 for Week 17 against the Cardinals. Even in that plus matchup, you need to do better for the fantasy finals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Tee Higgins is back in concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Taylor told reporters that Higgins — who was checked multiple times after a couple major hits on Sunday — reported symptoms after the game. Given the quick turnaround from his last concussion, it would be surprising if Higgins managed to play this week. It looks like Andrei Iosivas and Mitchell Tinsley, as well as Mike Gesicki, will be solidly on the 12-team radar for Week 15.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Laquon Treadwell caught 2-of-8 targets for 34 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Treadwell was third on the team in targets, but he’s seeing most of his work on deep passes down the field, which Daniel Jones has had a hard time connecting on. Treadwell did play only three fewer snaps than Josh Downs and ran 39 routes on 47 dropbacks. We should note that Keenan Allen (groin) was not playing a full snap share in his first week back from injury, so Treadwell could see his role slip a bit next week. Even so, he’s a downfield threat on a team that has struggled to pass the ball, which makes it hard to roster him outside of the deepest formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Laquon Treadwell caught 5-of-6 targets for 42 yards in the Colts’ Week 4 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Treadwell has taken over Alec Pierce’s role with the latter now on IR. Though he isn’t as productive as Pierce, Treadwell is still capable of moving the chains every now and then. He somehow led the Colts in targets this week, which may ultimately be a sign of the dysfunction in their passing game. Even after the solid performance, fantasy managers shouldn’t be looking to play Treadwell in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Colts placed Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Pierce will be sidelined for at least four weeks after suffering the injury in Week 2 against Kansas City. Pierce had seen 19 percent of the Colts’ targets and 53 percent of the team’s air yards in Week 1 against the Ravens, resuming his role as a strictly-downfield pass catcher. With Pierce out, Josh Downs should have every chance to operate as the Colts’ No. 1 wideout while Tyler Warren sees a bump in targets. Laquon Treadwell is likely to take over as the team’s lone deep threat. Treadwell can be picked up in 14-team fantasy formats ahead of the Colts’ Week 3 matchup with the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Colts waived/released DE Genard Avery, CB Chris Lammons, WR D.J. Montgomery, TE Eric Tomlinson, WR Laquon Treadwell, CB Micah Abraham, LB Austin Ajiake, LB Liam Anderson, QB Jason Bean, DE Levi Bell, S Marce Dabo, RB Demetric Felton, OG Arlington Hambright, RB Evan Hull, DT Eric Johnson, DT Jonah Laulu, DE Titus Leo, TE Jordan Murray, C Mike Panasiuk, RB Zavier Scott, CB Jaylin Simpson, CB Ameer Speed, S Michael Tutsie, OT Jake Witt, LB Craig Young.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Treadwell caught 10-of-11 targets for 121 yards and one touchdown this preseason. The former first-round pick played a handful of snaps on offense for the Ravens last season but hasn’t done anything of note since 2021, when he went for 33-434-1 with the Jaguars. At 29 years old, Treadwell could still garner some interest as a practice squad body, but he’s unlikely to stick on a 53-man roster this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Colts signed WR Laquon Treadwell, formerly of the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Indy waived WR Xavier White in a corresponding move. Treadwell bounced between the Ravens’ practice squad and active roster throughout the 2023 season. He appeared in five games and caught one pass for 16 yards. The former first-round pick will be a depth option for the Colts if he makes their 53-man roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Ravens signed WR Laquon Treadwell to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Treadwell had been on Baltimore’s practice squad for much of the season, catching just one pass for 16 yards in five games. He was released on Monday to make room for Dalvin Cook. Now, just two days later, the Ravens have added Treadwell back to the practice squad and released Tarik Black to make room.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Ravens waived WR Laquon Treadwell.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: Treadwell caught just one pass for 16 yards in five games with the Ravens this season. The former first-round pick has struggled to find a home in the league since being drafted by the Vikings in 2016 and will likely be playing for his fifth team in as many seasons if he catches on elsewhere in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: Ravens signed WR Laquon Treadwell, formerly of the Seahawks, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: The Ravens continue to bolster their wide receiver corps heading into this season, but Treadwell is little more than added depth on a roster that boasts Odell Beckham Jr., Rashod Bateman, Laquon Treadwell, and Nelson Agholor. After being released by the Jaguars last August, Treadwell caught on with the Seahawks last December, appearing in six games while catching six passes for 42 yards. He’ll compete with Devin Duvernay, James Proche, and a slew of players hoping to crack the 53-man roster at the conclusion of training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: 49ers hosted free agent WR Chris Conley for a visit.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: The team also brought in Laquon Treadwell for a visit. Conley re-signed with Texans last offseason. He was cut, re-signed, and cut again before the start of the season. He had a cup of coffee with the Chiefs and then closed out the year by bouncing between the Titans’ practice squad, free agency, and their active roster. Conley is nothing more than a depth option at this point in his career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports free agent WR Laquon Treadwell is visiting with the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/laquon-tre.analysis: After a 2021 season in which he went for 33-434-1 with the Jaguars, Treadwell caught just six passes for the Seahawks in 2022. The former first-round draft pick has bounced around the league since being released by the Vikings after the 2019 season, but just 27 years old. While the 49ers receiving corps is firmly entrenched at the top, Treadwell could battle for a backup role in camp if the team were to sign him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: Tai Felton caught 2-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Jordan Addison missed this game with an ankle injury and the Vikings deployed Felton as their WR2 over Jauan Jennings. Jennings ran fewer routes and failed to catch his only target. Felton wasn’t awfully productive either, but it’s good to see the former third-round pick picking up more work in his second season. He will return to a rotational role, assuming Addison is cleared to play after the Vikings’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: ESPN’s Kevin Seifert reports Vikings WRs Jordan Addison and Tai Felton will have “no issues going forward” after suffering arm injuries in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Seifert earlier reported that Addison and Felton had left with “what looked like hand/arm injuries.” Neither resumed practicing for Wednesday, but seem to be fine moving forward, according to Seifert. The Vikings avoid a major injury with Addison, but he is still set to miss the first three games of the season. Felton is the team’s third-round rookie and in line to compete with Jalen Nailor for the WR3 role this season. Both are still on track for Week 1, but with Nailor (hand) currently week-to-week, the Vikings may still look to acquire a veteran receiver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: Vikings WRs Jordan Addison and Tai Felton left practice early on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: We don’t have confirmed status updates from the team yet, but The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes Addison jammed “something” and that Felton “looked like he dinged his arm.” Felton, per ESPN’s Kevin Seifert, walked off the field with a wrap on his left hand. If there’s one thing that would accelerate trade talks for wideouts ahead of last cuts, it’s more injuries to this room. The Vikings should update Addison’s (and Felton’s) status in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: Vikings WR Jalen Nailor will undergo further evaluation after suffering a hand injury on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Nailor was expected to function as the Vikings’ fill-in No. 2 wide receiver with Jordan Addison suspended for the first three games of the season. Justin Jefferson is sidelined by a hamstring injury and Rondale Moore recently suffered a season-ending knee injury. The Nailor news leaves the wide receiver corps worryingly thin, and early-July reports on dynasty darling, rookie WR Tai Felton, indicated he may be best suited to special teams work in year one. The Vikings could make a move to acquire a proven, if unexciting, veteran to the mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes Vikings WR Tai Felton’s rookie season will be “spent mostly on special teams.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Lewis notes that Felton could see some snaps on offense if Jordan Addison is suspended in relation to his pending DUI trial. Otherwise, it sounds like Jalen Nailor will be back as the team’s third receiver. Nailor didn’t earn many targets in the WR3 role last year but did cash in with six touchdowns and 414 yards on 28 grabs. Nailor is on the menu as a dart throw in deep best ball formats while the third-round rookie is only intriguing as a dynasty stash.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: Vikings signed third-round pick WR Tai Felton to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Felton is quietly in play to challenge Vikings No. 3 WR Jalen Nailor in training camp. Nailor (5'11/190) caught 28-of-42 targets for 414 yards and six touchdowns in his first season as a starter last year, with the latter category buoying his fantasy productivity. Felton (6'1/183), meanwhile, caught 96-of-143 targets for 1,119 yards and nine touchdowns while averaging 2.32 yards per route run in his final college season. Fantasy managers should monitor Felton’s training camp reports this summer, as he could have a matchup-based WR5 role if everything falls into place.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.headline: Vikings selected Maryland WR Tai Felton with the No. 102 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tai-felton.analysis: Felton’s production steadily rose over four years at Maryland, culminating in a 96/1124/9 receiving line in his senior season. He’s a svelte outside receiver (6'1/183) who won after the catch and racked up 590 YAC in his final season and forced 26 missed tackles; the fifth-most among wide receivers last year. Unsurprisingly, Felton didn’t have the frame to win contested targets in college, bringing down 7-of-18 contested looks in his final season. Felton showed off his speed and burst at the combine with a 4.37 Forty followed by broad and vertical jumps above the 90th percentile. He left Indianapolis with a 9.2 RAS. Felton has the production of a potential NFL starter, but he may need to bulk up to be anything more than a volatile WR3 in the pros.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen rushed 24 times for 116 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen surprisingly added just one catch for zero yards on four targets. Not ideal, though Allen’s rushing output nearly doubled his previous career high of 59. It was exactly what the Jets and fantasy managers needed during Breece Hall’s second straight absence with a quad injury. Allen contributed runs of 10, 17, 11 and 22 yards, with that final rush finding the end zone. He also had a 13-yarder called back by holding. In other words, he was both grinding out tough yards and providing longer gains. Isaiah Davis mixed in for only cursory breather back work. With Hall yet to resume practicing, Allen should have another plug-and-play RB2 setup in Week 6 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Braelon Allen will once again be in line to lead the Jets’ backfield with Hall sidelined for a second consecutive week. Hall did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday and will presumably be a DNP again on Friday, now that he has been ruled out ahead of practice. Allen saw 100 percent of the Jets’ running back opportunities last week, rushing 14 times for 59 scoreless yards while adding two receptions for an additional eight yards on two targets. He’ll be a fringe RB1/RB2 in what should be another high-volume day for the third-year back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) is still “week to week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: It doesn’t look like Hall will practice this week as he recovers from the injury he sustained in Week 3. That would mean Braelon Allen, who saw all 14 running back rushes for New York in Week 4, will again function as the team’s workhorse in Week 5 against the Browns. Allen should still be considered a top-24 option despite the Jets’ immense offensive struggles last week against Chicago. The Browns’ defense is allowing the sixth-highest EPA per rush this season. Hall was officially a non-participant on Wednesday’s injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen had 14 rushes for 59 yards in the Jets’ Week 4 loss to the Bears, adding two catches for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen accounted for every running back rushing attempt for New York with Breece Hall (quad) sidelined. He also ran a route on 14 of the team’s 19 drop backs on a low-volume day for the Jets offense. It’s fantastic usage, even if it didn’t amount to much in the lopsided affair. Allen should remain in lineups next week against the Browns if Hall remains out. His pass game involvement could give Allen plenty of weekly upside for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Hall was initially mentioned as being week-to-week when he was diagnosed with his quad injury, so he was never really considered a candidate to play in Week 4 despite the team waiting until the end of the week to rule him out. With Hall out, the Jets will look to Braelon Allen to handle most of the backfield duties. Allen will profile as a solid RB2 candidate with a chance for more upside in what could be a high-volume day against the Bears. In addition to Hall, the Jets also ruled out OG Dylan Parham (knee), TE Mason Taylor (thumb), and LB Kiko Mauigoa (quad) for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall (quad) did not practice Wednsday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Hall went down with a quad injury on Sunday against the Lions and did not return to the game. Braelon Allen took over as the Jets’ lead back, a role he’ll likely continue to occupy in Week 4 against the Bears’ gettable rush defense if Hall is sidelined. Allen should be rostered in all leagues and could be a top-20 option in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Breece Hall is considered week-to-week with a quad injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: According to Rapoport, Hall received “good news after the MRI” he received after he suffered a thigh injury in the Jets’ Week 3 loss to the Lions. It doesn’t sound like Hall will be in line to suit up for Week 4’s game against the Bears, but he could avoid being placed on IR if the Jets believe he can return in less than four weeks. Braelon Allen will presumably take over as the Jets’ lead back during Hall’s absence, while Isaiah Davis could also see some work on offense after playing primarily on special teams through the first three weeks of the season. Allen has rushed 19 times for 61 yards and a touchdown this season while also tallying four receptions for 11 yards. He will border on the RB2/RB3 range in Week 4 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said he will not have an update on Breece Hall (thigh) until Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Hall exited in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s loss to the Lions and did not return to the field after being ruled out quickly. Braelon Allen went on to handle backfield duties for the remainder of the game and will be a top waiver wire add this week if Hall were to miss any time. Hall has gotten off to a bit of a slow start this season, rushing for 51-163-1 (3.2 YPC), but has caught all 10 of his targets for 102 scoreless yards. Allen would be a fringe RB2/RB3 in Week 4 against the Bears if Hall is held out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen rushed four times for 14 yards in the Jets’ Week 3 loss to the Lions, adding three catches for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Breece Hall suffered a thigh injury late in this game and did not return, leaving Allen as the lead back for the Jets’ final two drives. He touched the ball six times on the pair of drives. Fellow backup Isaiah Davis did not touch the ball once. His role would likely grow if Hall misses time, but Allen is the clear target in his backfield on waivers. Allen would push for an RB2 ranking if Hall is sidelined for Week 4 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen rushed 10 times for 40 yards in the Jets’ Week 1 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: The only Jets back to touch the ball behind Breece Hall — Isaiah Davis was not heard from — Allen was mixed in throughout the game as a true breather back. As in, he did not rack up a disproportionate amount of his touches with the Jets looking to kill the clock late in a sleepy victory. Allen actually notched a nifty 23-yard touchdown run in the third quarter, but it was called back by holding. Although Allen would undoubtedly form a committee with Davis in the event of a Hall injury, it is clear he would be the strong-side. He’s a high-upside contingency back heading in to Week 2 against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.headline: Dohnte Meyers caught 2-of-2 targets for 12 yards in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.analysis: With both Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins active, Meyers saw just 19 offensive snaps. He caught both of his targets but his biggest play was an 81-yard kickoff return to start things off in the first quarter. As long as Chase and Higgins are playing, Meyers is best left on fantasy benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.headline: Tee Higgins (adductor/neck) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.analysis: Head coach Zac Taylor told reporters before practice that Higgins would be listed as limited. Not only did he not practice, but the team listed him with a neck injury on top of his adductor issue. He went down with the adductor injury late in Cincy’s Week 4 loss to the Jags. It’s unclear when the neck issue cropped up. With multiple injuries holding him out of practice, Higgins looks unlikely to play in Week 5. With Ja’Marr Chase potentially out as well, Dohnte Meyers could be Joe Burrow No. 1 receiver this week. He should be added in all fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.headline: Dohnte Meyers caught 7-of-9 targets for 82 yards in the Bengals’ Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.analysis: Meyers entered the pass-catching fray with Andrei Iosivas and Colbie Young both out. Add in Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) leaving early and Tee Higgins (adductor) getting hurt at the end of the game and Meyers is suddenly a waiver wire option this week. The 26-year-old former CFL player caught 7 passes, seeing designed screens and downfield targets as he led Bengals wideouts in snaps. He made a juggling catch to set the Bengals up near the red zone on their final drive, capping off a productive day where he mostly operated as the team’s No. 2 receiver. Also involved was Mitchell Tinsley, who caught 3-of-7 targets for 49 yards. As we await Higgins’ and Chase’s statuses for next week, Meyers is the best wide receiver option to add as a potential FLEX play for Week 5 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.headline: Bengals ruled out WR Colbie Young (knee) for Week 4 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.analysis: With WR Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve, WR Dohnte Meyers should operate as the Bengals’ No. 3 wide receiver this week. He is not reliable enough to warrant FLEX consideration in 12-team leagues, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.headline: Andrei Iosivas caught his only target for seven yards in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.analysis: He played 32-of-60 snaps as the Bengals have spread the ball around, letting Colvie Young (1/7 on one target) and Dohnte Meyers (0/0 on one target) also get involved against the Texans. Iosivas looks like a poor FLEX risk in Week 3 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.headline: Bengals WR Dohnte Meyers caught 3-of-3 targets for 51 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.analysis: Meyers seemingly has the No. 4 wide receiver job locked up. On the first drive, he hauled in three passes. He bagged a nine-yard pass on an in-breaking route from the slot on the first, a 17-yard pass via a corner route from the slot and a 25-yard gain on the following play. The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. labeled Meyers a “roster lock,” saying at first a special teams returner role seemed to be Meyers’ ticket to a roster spot, but “the consistency of his playmaking at every turn of camp and the preseason made him undeniable.” He ran with the first-team offense in practice this week, and Bengals wide receivers coach Troy Walters said, “he can play all three positions.” File Meyers’ name away for down the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner Jr. reports that WR Colbie Young and WR Andrei Iosivas are still competing for the Bengals’ WR3 role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dohnte-mey.analysis: Young, the rookie, “has seemingly stacked at least one impressive catch per day.” Iosivas has had “a few notable drops,” but he reportedly “appears as polished and athletic as ever at getting open.” Both players could be worth late-round picks in best ball formats, but neither one is likely to return FLEX value in re-draft without WR1 Ja’Marr Chase or WR2 Tee Higgins missing time. Iosivas is entering a contract year, and the team just spent a fourth-round pick on Young. An in-season breakout from the rookie would make things easier from a salary cap perspective. Dehner also notes that former CFL WR Dohnte Meyers “has been a talk of camp” thus far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 17-of-30 passes for 182 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ 17-12, Week 5 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith “added” five carries for seven yards. He also lost a fumble. Coming off a generationally bad Week 4 clunker against the Bears, Smith was hardly outstanding in rainy MetLife Stadium conditions, though he was superior to Deshaun Watson. Not that you would have noticed in real time. Smith fumbled “just” once compared to Watson’s four, also taking “only” four sacks to Watson’s staggering eight. Like Watson, Smith also lost a key pass catcher to a concussion, with Kenyon Sadiq going down in the third quarter.
