He’ll presumably log another limited practice on Friday, which could put him in line to return for Week 5’s game against the Giants, but it will be Marcus Mariota drawing the start on Sunday morning when the Commanders take on the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 6-of-7 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson didn’t miss a beat after returning from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury. He made several spectacular grabs in this game, the most amazing of which was a toe-tapping catch in the back of the end zone with three defenders covering him. Even at less than full strength, Jefferson is simply one of the best receivers in the league. He will remain near the top of the WR1 ranks when the Vikings face the Colts after their bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is active for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jordan Addison is out. Jefferson would normally see plenty of targets anyway, but the absence of Addison all but guarantees that he will see one of the highest target shares in the league. Jefferson remains a top-end WR1 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: ESPN’s Jeff Darlington reports Justin Jefferson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jordan Addison, on the other hand, is not expected to suit up because of a hamstring issue. Even at less than full strength, Jefferson will dominate the targets for Minnesota, especially with Addison on ice. Barring a setback in warmups, Jefferson remains a top-half WR1 play for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Justin Jefferson will work out pregame to determine his status for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: The same is true of Jordan Addison. Both Minnesota wideouts are currently listed as questionable for Week 5. Jefferson is from Louisiana and has already told reporters he plans to play in the homecoming game. We expect him to suit up, but fantasy managers should have a backup plan for him and Addison to be safe.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Justin Jefferson (ankle) plans to play in Week 5 against the Saints, but the team “has to see how he feels on Saturday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: This is great news. We will not have to wait for the dreaded game-time decision call with Jefferson this time around. If active, Jefferson should be started as a WR1 against the Saints. He remained limited in practice all week. We will provide an update on the matter as soon as possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is questionable for Minnesota’s Week 5 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson practiced on Friday after limited sessions on Thursday and Wednesday. He also insisted that he plans to play when asked earlier this week. We think he’s on the optimistic side of questionable as he returns as close to LSU as he can in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: The Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver is on track to play in Week 5 against the Saints, but it would be really nice to see him practice in full tomorrow. Ideally, the full participation upgrade would have come today. Regardless, Jefferson is the type of veteran who does not need to practice fully in order to play. He is a WR1 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) said he plans to play in Week 5 against the Saints, but the final decision has not yet been made.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: According to ESPN’s Kevin Seifert, Jefferson said, “the plan is definitely to play Sunday, but who knows?” Overall, we take this as a net positive, but the Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver is still clearly rehabbing his ankle injury. For now, we tentatively expect him to be active this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Justin Jefferson (ankle) will be limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: This is a good sign. Jefferson is tentatively on track to play in Week 5 against the Saints. Ideally, he will upgrade to full participation tomorrow, though. O’Connell told reporters last week that his No. 1 wide receiver had made “great progress” in his rehab program. That indeed appears to be the case. He will be a WR1 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said he does not know if Justin Jefferson (ankle) will play in Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson made “great progress” this week, according to O’Connell, but it is still too early to say whether the Vikings’ star wide receiver will be good to go. Jefferson did not practice at all in Week 4. Hopefully, he is feeling well enough to resume practicing by Wednesday. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner had six rushes for 52 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding one catch for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner’s seven touches came after TreVeyon Henderson went down with what could be a serious ankle injury in the second quarter. While much of his work came in garbage time, Kiner could work as the Patriots’ No. 2 back behind Rhamondre Stevenson if Henderson is sidelined in Week 6. Kiner is worth a look on waiver wires this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed six times for 11 yards in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner served as Rhamondre Stevenson’s backup with TreVeyon Henderson out this week. He was the only other Pats running back to see a carry in this game, though practice squad call-up Lan Larison was targeted twice, both of which he caught. Kiner did not see a look through the air. As a backup running back without any pass-catching value, Kiner is not on the fantasy radar heading into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is not present for the media-access portion of practice on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The injury has sidelined Henderson since August 24. The Patriots face the Seahawks on Wednesday. At this point, Henderson must be considered questionable to play. Even if he were active, he would be slated for No. 2 duties behind starting RB Rhamondre Stevenson, and it is fair to wonder if the team would keep Henderson on a snap count. Reiss reported this morning that RB Lan Larison and/or RB Hassan Haskins would likely be elevated from the practice squad if Henderson cannot play, joining Stevenson and backup RB Corey Kiner on game day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots acquired RB Corey Kiner from the Cardinals in exchange for a seventh-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The trade was first reported by ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The draft pick going to the Cardinals is a seventh-round pick in 2028. Kiner was buried on the depth in Arizona, but should immediately step in as the RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson with the Patriots. A former UDFA who appeared in four games with the Cardinals last year, Kiner is only worth a stash in deeper formats and has no standalone fantasy value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Emari Demercado rushed five times for 30 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 16 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Demercado failed to snag his only target and he was out-touched 6-to-5 by fellow backup RB Corey Kiner. Cardinals RB Michael Carter is the clear-cut starter and Kiner’s presence reduces Demercado’s bench-stash value. This looks like a three-player committee with one FLEX-viable player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cardinals signed RB Corey Kiner off the Vikings’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Cardinals released RB Jermar Jefferson in a related move. We’d love to say this doesn’t matter, but sadly, all Cardinals running back news is real news. Kiner spent time with the 49ers in training camp before getting hurt, he was a priority UDFA signing this offseason. It’s possible he may be fantasy-relevant at some point given how banged up the Cardinals RB room is.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan said RB Patrick Taylor (shoulder) will miss a couple of weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Taylor exited Saturday’s preseason game against the Raiders with the injury and did not return to the field. Rookie UDFA Corey Kiner also exited with a high-ankle sprain and is expected to miss a couple of weeks. The 49ers are already dealing with injuries to Isaac Guerendo (shoulder) and rookie Jordan James (knee). Behind Christian McCaffrey is journeyman Ke’Shawn Vaughn and the recently re-signed Jeff Wilson, who rushed for 8-16-1 against the Raiders while adding another catch for 16 yards. Both Vaughn and Wilson could spell McCaffrey in Week 1 against the Seahawks if Guerendo, James, and Taylor are all sidelined. That said, none of these players carry much fantasy upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers RB Corey Kiner was carted from the field in Saturday’s preseason game due to an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner is a UDFA from Cincinnati who has been impressing in Niners camp. The rookie broke off a 19-yard run in the second quarter and remained down after the play, only to later be carted from the field. While he’d typically be considered a long shot to make the roster, Kiner may have had an opening given the current state of the 49ers’ backfield. We’ll hopefully know more on his injury soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers signed RB Corey Kiner.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Though he played his freshman year at LSU, Kiner (5’9/209) made a name for himself with back-to-back 1,000-yard rushing seasons at Cincinnati. A steady runner, Kiner consistently moved the chains. The Athletic’s Dane Brugler describes Kiner as having “high-level contact balance” and notes he shows “better short-area quickness than true burst.” Kiner can fight through contact and finish runs, though he is less of a receiving back or home-run threat. He profiles as an early-down back who can contribute in a committee role at the NFL level if he secures a roster spot. He’ll have an uphill climb for a spot on the 53 as he chases fifth-rounder Jordan James and veteran Patrick Taylor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: LSU sophomore RB Corey Kiner transferred to Cincinnati.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner (5'9"/217) was LSU’s second leading rusher last year behind Tyrion Davis-Price. He racked up 324 yards on 79 carries and scored two touchdowns. He was a four-star recruit in the 2021 class out of Cincinnati, Ohio, so it’s a homecoming for Kiner. He is described as a bruiser, a compact runner that will burst through the hole and won’t get taken down by arm tackles. He’ll be a worthy replacement for Jerome Ford and Cincinnati gets a great RB that they would struggle to get in actual recruiting

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 14 times for 68 yards in the Bengals’ Week 5 loss to the Dolphins, adding 2 receptions for 10 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine was involved heavily against the Dolphins, a surprising development given his lack of touches to open the season. He trailed Chase Brown by just five snaps on the day, getting involved in short-yardage situations and seeing an increase in red zone snaps after Brown’s red zone fumble in the second quarter. He caught a touchdown running a route out of the backfield and finished with 78 total yards. We don’t expect Perine to consistently see this kind of usage, but he is back on the radar as a deep-league FLEX value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed three times for seven yards in the Bengals’ Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine only saw three touches on the day, though he had a rushing touchdown called back for holding in the second quarter. He has generally held a pass-catching role throughout his career but ceded all the backfield pass-catching opportunities to Chase Brown on the day. Perine remains a handcuff in the event of a Brown injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed two times for six yards in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: He added 16 yards on his only catch, making him the third-leading receiver for the game. Perine has 42 snaps in the first two games of the season and looks like a decent stash in case of a Chase Brown injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed eight times for 42 yards in the Bengals’ Week 18 loss to the Browns, adding three catches for 10 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine returned to Cincinnati on a two-year deal in the offseason. He easily took the RB2 gig over rookie Tahj Brooks and eventually parlayed that into a committee role. Perine didn’t log a single carry over the first two weeks but was stacking 10-touch games by November. He finished the year with 84 carries for 382 yards and three scores while adding 17 grabs for 87 yards. Perine was a staple of the RB4 ranks over the final two months of the year. He will likely keep his No. 2 role with the Bengals into the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed seven times for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 16 win over the Dolphins, adding two receptions for 16 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine got the Bengals’ backfield scoring started with a four-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, but then Chase Brown got the next three. Wild. Brown ended up out-touching his veteran backfield mate 16-9. Perine has been much more involved of late, but it’s not creating standalone fantasy value, and it’s somehow not affecting Brown’s. Brown has a plus Week 17 matchup in the Cardinals while Perine remains off the radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 14 times for 42 yards in the Bengals’ Week 15 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine saw one more carry than Chase Brown, but averaged just three yards per carry on the day with his longest gain coming on an eight-yard pickup. Perine briefly left the game in the fourth quarter due to a knee injury, and was carted to the locker room at one point. Despite all of this, he returned to finish out the day and should be good to go for Week 16 against the Dolphins. Even if he is active, fantasy managers can avoid him next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine returned in the fourth quarter of Week 15’s game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: It’s not often we see a player carted to the locker room only to return later in the game. That said, Perine did exactly that in the fourth quarter after exiting earlier with a knee injury. Perine didn’t even miss a drive despite the injury, and returned to take more carries from Chase Brown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine (knee) exited in the fourth quarter of Week 15’s game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine remained down on the field after a third down carry and appeared to be grabbing at his knee. He was eventually helped off by trainers, but later carted from the field. This will spell the end of the day for Perine, who was splitting work with Chase Brown all afternoon and exits with a rushing line of 9-31-0. He also caught one pass for one yard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 14 times for 39 yards in the Bengals’ Week 13 win over the Ravens, adding two catches for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine missed the previous two games with an ankle injury but was cleared to play early this week. The Bengals immediately split their backfield in two, giving Perine just one fewer carry than Chase Brown. The latter, of course, was far more efficient, running for 5.2 yards per carry compared to 2.8 for Perine. Perine also coughed up a red zone fumble late in the game. He still saw carries on the next drive, meaning his coaches weren’t deterred by the mistake. Perine doesn’t hold much fantasy value heading into Week 14, but he will be a thorn in the side of fantasy managers hoping for a better workload from Brown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Bengals RB Samaje Perine (ankle) practiced in full on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: It’s an estimation, but it’s a rapid recovery from Perine after being doubtful for Week 12. Perine left Week 9 against the Bears with a high-ankle sprain and has not played since. His return would prevent Chase Brown from hogging the whole workload pie against the Ravens, much to the chagrin of Brown-reliant managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm failed to catch his only target in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: 45 snaps, one target. Helm has somehow grown less relevant than his 4/28 Week 1 showing would have even suggested. He can be dropped in most leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm continued to split reps with Daniel Bellinger, who also caught two passes today. Helm hasn’t topped 30 yards in a game this year and his four catches in Week 1 remain a high-water mark. He isn’t even in the TE2 mix for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is now sitting on a scoreless 6/41 through the Titans’ first two contests. Helm is an intriguing second-year pro, but there’s not going to be much intrigue in the Titans’ offense for the time being. 24-year-old Helm is best left on 12-team league waiver wires head of Week 3 vs. the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 4-of-5 targets for 28 yards in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm gobbled up snaps as he tied Carnell Tate for the second most Titans receptions on an afternoon where Cam Ward completed just 19 passes. Helm is looking heavily involved in the offense, it’s just unclear if that will even amount to anything in this situation. Week 2 is going to be tough against the Eagles before a slightly more forgiving Week 3 date with the Giants. For now, Helm is not a recommended TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) will not play in Tennessee’s Week 18 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm finishes a successful rookie season with a 44/357/2 slash line, and looked to be making a climb up Tennessee’s target pecking order before injuries largely derailed his final month. It’s hard to rely on anything in Tennessee’s offense until we see exactly what happens with the coaching staff, but there are offseason runouts that will put Helm as a high-end TE2 with Chig Oknokwo slated for free agency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is now on the wrong side of questionable, which benefits TE Chig Okonkwo, who has scored a touchdown in consecutive weeks. Okonkwo is scheduled to enter free agency at the end of the season and has a chance to earn a decent payday with another strong showing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 17 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is good to go, which is nice for QB Cam Ward. The promising rookie tight end has made good on his fourth-round draft capital, though the Titans’ distributive offense makes him too dicey a start for Week 17. Helm is up to 52 targets on the year, while averaging 1.58 yards per route run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans have been distributing the ball across the skill position corps in recent weeks, and we see no reason for that to change in Week 17 against the Saints. Helm is a touchdown-dependent fantasy-starter in re-draft formats. His rookie season showings have been encouraging overall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-3 targets for nine yards in the Titans’ Week 16 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm’s missed connection was a fourth down grab where he couldn’t quite get both feet in bounds. It wasn’t the best awareness from the rookie tight end, but a rare notable mistake for a player who has been looking lively down the stretch, even if it’s not always reflected in the box score. Despite that intrigue, Helm will not be a top-24 option for the fantasy finals against the Saints. The Titans don’t generate enough pass attempts, and spread the ball around too much on the targets they do disperse.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm (toe) is active for Week 16 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As is Van Jefferson (back). It means this undermanned Titans skill corps is at least at full strength as it tries to steal a victory vs. the dazed and confused Chiefs. Inactive for the Titans are OL Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, OL Garrett Dellinger, OL Drew Moss, DL Cam Horsley, LB Cedric Gray and S Erick Hallett.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley caught 2-of-3 targets for 33 yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Is this doing anything for anybody? Ridley had a 23-yarder to open the game and vanished thereafter. He has not cracked more than two catches or three targets all year and does not need to be in fantasy consideration in the vast, vast majority of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley failed to catch his only target in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley has been held without a catch in 2-of-3 games this year. He’s losing routes to Elic Ayomanor and not earning targets when on the field. He can be cut even in the deepest of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley caught 2-of-2 targets for 35 yards in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: The grabs were Ridley’s first two of the season. He also cost the Titans with a 15-yard personal foul penalty. Although it’s good to see Ridley’s Week 1 doughnut was something of an aberration, it’s not like he can be counted on for high-volume days going forward as the Titans sort out the rotation in their revamped skill corps. Despite his pedigree, Ridley can be safely left on 12-team league waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley was not targeted in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley’s 25 routes run were good for third-most among Titans receivers in Sunday’s loss, but the 31-year-old receiver went without a target despite his team trailing the entire game. Any hope that Ridley would improve on last year’s 17-303-0 performance will need to be put on hold for now, as Ridley and the Titans offense as a whole struggled mightily in the season opener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll said the team’s downfield passing attack has to improve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Cam Ward’s preseason has been as bad or even worse than his rookie campaign. Ward in last week’s preseason game against Seattle completed eight of his 12 attempts for 69 yards. His average depth of target on completed passes this preseason sits at a meager 1.2 . Carnell Tate, meanwhile, has been targeted five times on his 23 preseason routes and does not have a reception to show for it. Daboll has been somewhat defensive this month when asked about Ward’s immense struggles after working on basic fundamentals with the second-year QB in the offseason. Ward, one of the most inaccurate passers in recent NFL history, is unlikely to support more than one fantasy-viable pass catcher in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: ESPN’s Turron Davenport reports that Titans OC Brian Daboll’s intent to improve on third down was a “key reason” for signing WR Wan’Dale Robinson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Davenport penned a lengthy piece detailing how OC Brian Daboll is focused on developing QB Cam Ward’s play on third down, in the red zone and in the two-minute drill. This is pretty straightforward. Those are all high-leverage situations, so harping on Ward’s performance there makes sense. Robinson played on all three drives in the Titans’ first preseason game while veteran Calvin Ridley was on the field for one. Rookie WR Carnell Tate was on the field for the first and third drives. A featured role on third downs could help Robinson return FLEX value — he’s certainly being paid like he is going to be featured.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said Calvin Ridley (leg) will participate in 7-on-7 drills on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley suffered a broken fibula in Week 11 of the 2025 season and missed the remainder of the year. He hadn’t participated in any 7-on-7 or team drills up until this point, making today’s participation a major step in the right direction. Ridley agreed to a restructured deal to stay in Tennessee this offseason. He will tumble to third in the pecking order for targets now that Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson are both in the fold. That should still allow for the occasional splash play, but fantasy managers should look elsewhere for FLEX options.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll praised WR Calvin Ridley as a “good player.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley in March restructured his contract with the Titans to remain in Tennessee for at least one more season following a terrible 2025 campaign in which he totaled 303 yards over seven games before a season-ending ankle injury. Ridley played under Daboll at Alabama before being drafted by the Falcons in 2018. “Rid is Rid,” Daboll said. “I’ve got a long-standing relationship with Rid back to 2017. He means a lot to me as a player. He was a good player for us when I was at Alabama. But as a person, we’ve developed a good relationship. It’s good to have him here. We’ve changed some stuff as we’ve went, but he’s smart. He’s a good player. He’s a good teammate. I’ve got a lot of appreciation and love for Rid.” Ridley will have to compete for WR3 duties in the new-look Tennessee offense this season with Wan’Dale Robinson and first-round rookie WR Carnell Tate shaping up as the team’s top two pass-catching options.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Titans agreed to terms on a restructured contract with WR Calvin Ridley.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: The details of the restructure were not immediately made available, but it sounds like the two sides did not address the maturation of the contract, meaning Ridley is still under team control through the 2027 season after signing a four-year contract with the team prior to the 2024 season. Ridley missed the second half of 2025 due to a broken fibula suffered in the middle of November. Rumors swirled throughout the offseason of the team potentially releasing Ridley, but he remains in Tennessee... at least for the immediate future. The reworked contract reportedly saves the Titans $11 million against the cap in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: ESPN’s Turron Davenport believes “it isn’t out of the realm” for the Titans to keep Calvin Ridley and add Wan’Dale Robinson in free agency.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: The Titans already have $100 million in cap space, so releasing Ridley wouldn’t exactly free them up to go anywhere they couldn’t already go. (Davenport admits it could still happen.) Robinson, a former Giant, would obviously be a worthwhile fit with his old head coach Brian Daboll calling plays in Tennessee. It’s very obvious that Cam Ward didn’t have enough weapons to work with last year, and while we’d stop short of calling Robinson a game changer for the Titans, he could at least help them figure out more about Ward in his second season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 26-of-34 attempts for 374 yards and four touchdowns in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding seven rushes for 25 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye had all day to operate in the pocket against a Raiders front seven that entered Week 5 with the league’s ninth highest pressure rate and fourth highest quick pressure rate. He attacked the Vegas secondary downfield from start to finish, hitting Kyle Williams and Pop Douglas for long touchdowns, and Williams for another long gain that put the Pats inside the five yard line. Maye’s rushing score came on a green scramble in the third quarter. Fully emerged from his early-season struggles, Maye is once again carving up opposing coverage units and causing fits with his scrambling ability. Maye, with eight total touchdowns over his past two outings, should be locked into lineups next week against a middling Jets secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 22-of-37 passes for 269 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in a 29-26, Week 4 win over the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye also added 53 yards rushing on eight carries. This was easily the best game of Maye’s season. The Bills had pressure in his face often, but Maye was frequently able to evade pass rushers and pick up chunk gains with his legs. When he did have time to throw, he ripped off big passes downfield and could have even had a bigger day after a potential 40+ yard pass slipped through Romeo Doubs’ hands in the fourth quarter. Maye did wince and grab his right shoulder on one hit, so that will be something to watch during practice this week, but we don’t expect him to miss any time. The bad news is that Maye figures to be without Mack Hollins (calf) in Week 5, and A.J. Brown (ankle) is not yet ready to return, so Maye will play with limited options next week against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Bills declared CB Christian Benford, WR Skyler Bell, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL T.J. Sanders, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive for Week 4 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: No real surprises here. Benford was listed as questionable heading into the day, but he didn’t practice at all this week so he was never likely to play. Rookie Davison Igbinosun is likely to step into his spot opposite Maxwell Hairston, which makes the Bills young and inexperienced on the boundary. Perhaps Drake Maye could finally take advantage of that on the way to his first truly good fantasy game of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye (right shoulder) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: We are happy to see that the Patriots’ quarterback is practicing fully, but this is a new injury for Maye. He notably dealt with a throwing shoulder injury during the Patriots’ playoff run last season. His listing raises questions as to whether there might be a lingering issue. We expect a follow-up report on this in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: The Athletic’s Chad Graff believes Drake Maye’s confidence is “shot.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye, after another meltdown in Week 3 against the Jaguars, has now posted a negative drop back EPA in six dtraight outings dating back to last season. Against Jacksonville on Sunday he posted a meager 40 percent drop back success rate, the fifth lowest of the week. “What’s fallen apart with Maye looks like it’s between the ears as much as anything physical,” Graff said. “He looks like a quarterback whose confidence is shot.” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said this week that Maye needs to calm down if things are going to turn around. “We need to stop trying to choke the life out of every single play,” Vrabel said during his Monday radio appearance. “We need to relax.” Maye through Week 3 ranks 32nd in fantasy points per drop back, below the likes of Daniel Jones and Cam Ward. It will be tough to start Maye in Week 4 against Buffalo if there are other viable QB options on the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 14-of-29 attempts for 199 yards and two interceptions in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars, adding four rushes for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: He fumbled twice, losing one to the Jags defense. Maye was under duress and missing routine throws for most of this game. He also had a long touchdown throw and a rushing touchdown called back on penalties. Without A.J. Brown (ankle) in the lineup the Patriots have no one to threaten secondaries, allowing opposing defenses to stack the box, shut down the run game, and leave the Pats a one-dimensional offense. Though Maye’s rushing could keep him afloat as a top-12 quarterback in Week 4 against the Bills, he should be considered a shaky option for now. New England’s offensive line might be able to hold up against a Buffalo front seven that has struggled to pressure the passer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 14-of-22 passes for 208 yards and an interception in the Patriots’ 20-3, Week 2 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: It was a defensive slugfest for the Patriots and Steelers in Week 2, with neither team passing for a touchdown on the day. Maye added 17 rushing yards on four carries but took three sacks, including one in the red zone in the second quarter. His interception was a floater in Steelers territory in the third quarter, tossed right to Patrick Queen to end a drive. He ends the day with 44-percent of his passing yards coming on two third-quarter chunk plays to Romeo Doubs. Maye has had a rough start to the season, following up a three-interception Week 1 with a scoreless, one-interception Week 2. He faces another solid defense in the Jaguars for Week 3; Maye’s rushing upside keeps him in the low-end QB1 territory for next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 23-of-33 passes for 178 yards, a touchdown, and three interceptions in the Patriots’ 13-10, Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye once again struggled with Seattle’s ironclad defense, routinely making poor decisions when attempting to push the ball downfield. His third, and worst, interception of the night came when he lobbed a pass off his back foot at Mack Hollins with under 30 seconds left. The throw fell well short of his target and Josh Jobe made a toe-tapping pick in the end zone. Maye only threw multiple interceptions once last year, including the postseason. That came in his Super Bowl loss to the Seahawks. His multi-pick total is already at one this year, again at the hands of Seattle. It’s a long season, but Maye did nothing to silence the “schedule merchant” claims tonight. He will look to rebound as a mid-range QB1 versus the Steelers next week. That could be without A.J. Brown, who left this game with an ankle injury and did not return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Patriots OC Josh McDaniels said he plans to “push the tempo” offensively this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: PFF charts the Patriots’ use of tempo at just 2.4 percent last season, tying for dead last in the NFL. The league average was 6.27 percent and the Saints led the league at 19.2 percent. The Patriots averaged 64.6 offensive plays per game, just 0.28 above average. Playing faster leads to more plays, and more plays lead to more opportunities to score fantasy points. Hopefully, McDaniels’ preseason play-calling confirms his intended offensive change is being implemented.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that Patriots WR A.J. Brown’s “connection with QB Drake Maye has been immediate.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye and Brown have already begun generating highlight plays together against Patriots defenders. Coaches and players from both sides of the ball are highly complimentary of the new receiver, and Brown has taken on a leadership role within the offense. It sounds like things are coming together for Brown and the Patriots. Treat him as a WR2 with upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught 6-of-9 targets for 80 yards in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Michael Pittman (foot) was ruled out earlier in the week, and then Roman Wilson dislocated his finger during the game, so there wasn’t a lot of competition for Bernard and DK Metcalf. The rookie from Alabama played the same number of snaps as Metcalf and ran a route on 35 of the team’s 38 dropbacks. This isn’t an explosive passing attack, but Bernard looks like the WR2 in Pittsburgh now and is more of an intermediate and short-area target than DK Metcalf, which could lead to decent fantasy value over the next few weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Roman Wilson has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 5 against the Colts with a dislocated finger.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Wilson had just one target in the first half. He pinned the reception to his hip, but the ball was ripped loose by a defender, which not only made the pass incomplete but also seemed to dislocate Wilson’s finger. With Michael Pittman Jr. also hurt, we should continue to see a lot of Germie Bernard in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Michael Pittman re-aggravated his foot injury and will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: McCarthy told reporters the team is evaluating Pittman’s roster spot, meaning they could place him on injured reserve. He would miss at least four weeks while on IR. Pittman tried to play through the foot injury but only made it two weeks before aggravating the issue. He was spotted using a scooter to support his foot in the locker room on Wednesday. We suspect the Steelers will place him on IR to give Pittman enough time to fully recover. Germie Bernard will now operate as the team’s permanent WR3, with Roman Wilson taking on more work as the clear No. 2 receiver. Both players will be decent FLEX options for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 3 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: He was limited in practice all three days this week with a foot injury that kept him out of Week 2. We’d say Pittman is on the optimistic side of questionable based on his participation status. If he’s out again, it would likely be Germie Bernard picking up the slack, as he did in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Pittman didn’t practice once last week, so a limited session today is a big step in the right direction. Germie Bernard took his spot in the lineup on Sunday and caught four passes for 35 yards, but he also coughed up a drop that was then intercepted by New England. The mistake all but guarantees his return to the bench once Pittman is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught 4-of-8 targets for 35 yards in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Bernard saw increased opportunity with Michael Pittman ruled out for Week 2. He caught all four of his receptions on one drive in the second quarter but ended as the second-most targeted receiver on the team. Bernard seemed to lose much of the trust he earned with a rough bobble on an Aaron Rodgers screen pass that led to an interception in the fourth quarter. The rookie second-round pick will find fantasy relevance while Pittman is out, but is no more than a fantasy WR5 for Week 3 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Steelers WR Germie Bernard caught 1-of-2 targets for 13 yards and one touchdown in Thursday’s preseason game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Bernard started alongside other Steelers backups this evening, indicating he has not yet earned a starting role in three-wide receiver sets. That said, he looked good. Bernard found the end zone via a screen pass on the Steelers’ second drive, shaking a defender immediately after the catch before muscling past another as he crossed the plane. He nearly scored again on the following drive, but QB Will Howard overthrew him in the end zone. The Steelers’ top-two WRs, DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman, are just getting over injuries, and No. 3 WR Roman Wilson should not be considered insurmountable in-house competition. Bernard could work his way into the lineup early in the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: ESPN’s Benjamin Solak reports Germie Bernard “ran almost exclusively with the second-stringers” during 11-on-11s and “struggled with some of the finer details of the playbook.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Not a glowing review. Combine Bernard’s struggles with the idea that the Steelers might remain run-heavy this year (also espoused by Solak) and it feels like Bernard might just be a deep-league bench option this year. It should be noted that the overwhelming majority of the drumbeat about Bernard this offseason has been positive, so perhaps this was just an off-day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo says Germie Bernard “probably will carve out his niche as a big slot” receiver this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: The rookie second-rounder joins an offense that includes established veterans on the outside in D.K. Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr., so a slot role may be his best path to early playing time. DeFabo is already on record as saying that he believes Bernard “has a good shot” at early playing time this season, a point he reiterated in his latest article. It’s hard to imagine Bernard having much fantasy upside this season given the veteran presence in the receiver room, but for those holding Bernard in dynasty leagues, it sounds like the rookie has gotten off to a good start ahead of his first NFL training camp, which is set to kick off next month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo believes second-round WR Germie Bernard “has a good shot” to work his way into the rotation at receiver in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: DeFabo calls Roman Wilson the WR3 “at this exact moment,” which isn’t exactly a qualifier that lends to us believing that Wilson will be there at the end of training camp after his first few lost seasons. Bernard “has a really high floor” per DeFabo’s looks at OTAs and we wouldn’t be surprised if he had a role in his first season. It’s hard to see how it would be more than mildly fantasy interesting behind DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman, but perhaps Bernard can establish himself for a bigger 2027.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate caught 1-of-5 targets for six yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Well, at least last week was good. He did have a 40-plus yarder pulled off the board because of a holding penalty. Next week offers a more welcoming Colts defense and Tate should have a path to low-end WR3 numbers there.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (back) is active for Tennessee’s Week 5 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: The Titans had named him questionable despite Robert Saleh saying he’d play on Friday, so this outcome was no surprise. Inactive for the Titans are: RB Nick Singleton, RB Michael Carter, S Amani Hooker (concussion), CB Jaylon Jones, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE David Martin-Robinson (hamstring) and DT Jackie Marshall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (back) is good to go for Week 5 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: He was officially listed as questionable with two limited sessions on Thursday and Friday. Tate popped up on Thursday’s injury report with a back injury, but Titans coach Robert Saleh said it was just some random tightness that isn’t expected to slow him in Week 5. Tate has seen 21 targets over the last two weeks and has posted a 15-203-0 line over that span. He has some solid WR3/FLEX appeal against a Texans defense that has struggled against the pass early in the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate (back) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate was limited today, suggesting he suffered a back injury in practice. That is not good. He, of course, still has a chance to play, but we will have to monitor this situation closely. For now, Tate must be viewed as questionable to play in Week 5 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate caught 9-of-12 targets for 145 yards in the Titans’ Week 4 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate was targeted early and often in this one. The rookie first-rounder would lead the Titans in targets and found himself at the end of multiple big plays. Tate’s first reception resulted in a 22-yard gain, and he later popped up for a 35-yard catch in the second quarter, only to lose a fumble on the play moments later. Tate hauled in a clutch 33-yard reception on a fourth-and-10 play late in the fourth quarter as the Titans tried to mount a comeback, setting up a three-yard touchdown pass to Wan’Dale Robinson on the next play. Tate has been targeted 21 times over the last two weeks and will be a risky WR3/WR4 against the Texans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate caught 6-of-9 targets for 58 yards in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: The first-round rookie posted new high-water marks in every receiving category, though he did so while seeing fewer targets than Wan’Dale Robinson. Tate got going with a few chunk plays late in the game, setting up a Robinson touchdown and another scoring opportunity that was squandered by Cam Ward. Tate might be making incremental progress with this box score, but he’s still at the fringes of the WR4 discussion for Week 4 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate caught 3-of-5 targets for 27 yards in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate led the Titans’ receiver corps in snaps, catches and targets, but both Elic Ayomanor and Calvin Ridley churned up more yardage. No one had a useful day in fantasy football. Tate’s usage has been excellent through his first two NFL contests, but this severely-limited offense is predictably limiting his fantasy upside. He’s a WR4 heading into next week’s Giants road trip.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Carnell Tate caught 4-of-6 targets for 38 yards in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Tate tied for the team lead in receiving yards, but as you can see, that amounted to 38 in this dismal Titans attack. He also tied for the team lead in targets, though Wan’Dale Robinson edged him 5-4 in receptions. Today was an extremely ominous Cam Ward performance against a far-from-stellar Jets defense, but there is nothing to quibble with in Tate’s usage. He was out there for 44-of-50 snaps and had healthy “shares” of everything from targets to air yards. Now we just need to see if Ward can get his career on track in Year 2 before we commit to Tate as a WR3. The Eagles are a rough Week 2 matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said Carnell Tate is “working out some stiffness” and did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: This is, to be a broken record, probably not much to be concerned about just yet. The 21-year-old Tate is in a weird spot as a clear high-volume target on a passing offense that has not looked good all preseason and probably should be eyed skeptically heading into 2026. Nevertheless, Tate has the goods to be a fantasy producer this year if the offense around him is good enough to let that happen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.headline: Titans team reporter Jim Wyatt reports that Thursday’s joint practice against the Bears was “arguably” WR Carnell Tate’s “best day of camp.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carnell-ta.analysis: Wyatt notes that Tate “had been quiet in recent practices, and he still doesn’t have a catch in two preseason games.” Today’s standout showing comes at the right time. The end of the preseason is fast approaching and the first-round rookie will be asked to contribute right away this season, especially with WR Wan’Dale Robinson currently undergoing evaluation for a concussion. The Titans’ offense is still a work in progress, so producing as a WR3 could be Tate’s ceiling for quite some time. Still, today’s report is nice to read.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 23-of-32 passes for 190 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 31-24, Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: The Bengals offense mostly had a smooth-sailing day against the lackadaisical Dolphins defense. After a high-volume Week 4, Burrow threw 32 passes, tossing touchdowns to Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, and Tanner Hudson in the first half. He just missed Ja’Marr Chase for a 70-yard score in the second half, but later connected with Chase for a 45-yard score in the third quarter. Burrow was hardly under pressure and had plenty of time to make accurate throws and take deep shots against Miami. He is a fantasy QB1 heading into the Bengals’ bye and gets a middling defense in the Ravens for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 39-of-54 passes for 428 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Bengals’ 22-17, Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: The Bengals offense struggled to finish drives for much of this game, with Burrow throwing his first touchdown to Mike Gesicki in the third quarter. He also added a rushing touchdown on a fourth-quarter quarterback sneak. Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) leaving early didn’t help as Burrow threw two interceptions and nearly had a third. He threw one to Travis Hunter in the first quarter, though it was nullified by a roughing the passer penalty. He later threw one with under two minutes left in the first half, leading to a Jaguars score the other way. The final interception came in the fourth quarter in the red zone, ending a promising drive. Burrow made great plays under pressure, often finding Tee Higgins downfield. However, the interceptions proved to be back-breaking and the Bengals’ comeback attempt ultimately fell short. Burrow is a low-end fantasy QB1 for Week 5 against a soft Dolphins defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 28-of-37 passes for 281 yards and three touchdowns in the Bengals’ 30-27, Week 3 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow came out hot in this one, completing his first 14 passes while throwing a three-yard touchdown to Ja’Marr Chase on the Bengals’ opening drive. Burrow would throw his second touchdown of the day late in the second half when he connected with Tee Higgins for a 28-yard score and found Mike Gesicki 25 yards downfield on a fourth-and-two for his third touchdown of the day. Burrow led his offense on multiple long drives in this one, but with his team trailing 30-27 and driving late in the fourth quarter, he would cough up the ball on a strip-sack, which was recovered by Pittsburgh to seal the win for the Steelers. Burrow has attempted 30-plus passes in every game this season while throwing for six touchdowns to just one interception. He’ll be on the QB1 radar for next week’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow completed 20-of-31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns in Cincinnati’s 20-6, Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow was under pressure quite a bit in this one, as he took five sacks, but the Bengals were able to establish enough of a lead on a few incredible out-of-structure plays by Burrow that they took the air out of the ball in the middle of the third quarter. Both touchdown passes were to Ja’Marr Chase, the second as Burrow drifted out of his pocket to the right. It’s full-steam ahead in the QB1 tiers as Burrow heads to Pittsburgh in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow (back) is active for Cincinnati’s Week 2 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: It never seemed like there was a real chance Burrow would miss this game, even after Josh Johnson was elevated from the practice squad yesterday. Burrow will be on the QB1 line against a Texans defense looking to rebound. Inactive for the Bengals are: Johnson, WR Ke’Shawn Williams, CB Josh Newton, C Connor Lew, OL Myles Hinton, DT B.J. Hill (Achilles), and DT Landon Robinson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Joe Burrow (back) will play in Week 2 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: The Bengals called up Josh Johnson from the practice squad over the weekend, raising some eyebrows regarding Burrow’s health. The move, however, was purely a precaution. Burrow has already said he is playing this week. He remains near the top of the QB1 ranks despite a tough matchup with the Houston defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Bengals QB Joe Burrow (back) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: This listing is effectively a formality. Burrow laughed off the idea of missing the Bengals’ game against the Texans earlier this week, and today, coach Zac Taylor said Burrow is “good to go” after practicing in full. Burrow’s status is, of course, worth following, but we do expect him to play. Treat him as a QB1, per usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Joe Burrow (back tightness) will play in Week 2 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow was upgraded to a full participant in Friday’s practice and is good to go for Sunday’s game, per head coach Zac Taylor. Burrow was limited in the first two practices of the week due to back tightness, but that was likely more out of precaution than it was due to anything serious. Burrow profiles as a high-end QB1 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Bengals expect Joe Burrow (back tightness) to play in Week 2 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: Burrow has been limited in each of the team’s first two practices, likely because the Bengals are exercising caution with their QB1. With one more practice to go before the Bengals release their final injury report, it sounds like there is no real concern about Burrow’s availability for Week 2 against a Texans defense looking to rebound from a tough season opener in which they allowed 36 points to the Bills. We will be sure to provide a final status for Burrow once the team announces it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.headline: Bengals QB Joe Burrow (back tightness) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-burrow.analysis: We knew Burrow was practicing, but we did not know whether he would upgrade to full participation. He remains limited, but beat reporters note that Burrow did far more today than he did yesterday. The Bengals’ quarterback skipped stretches before doing some light throwing on Wednesday. Today, he was suited up in pads and appeared to do everything up through individual drills. He likely sat out team drills, but that is not overly concerning. Burrow should be good to go as a QB1 this week. Hopefully, he upgrades to full participation tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.headline: Tyson Bagent completed 12-of-21 passes for 87 scoreless yards and two interceptions before being benched in the fourth quarter of the Bears’ 31-7, Week 5 loss to the Packers.
ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Bears QB Tyson Bagent will “most likely” start in Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.analysis: Caleb Williams (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity today, and the Bears ended up listing him as questionable to play. Consider him highly questionable. Rushing their star quarterback back onto the field when Bagent and Case Keenum have both played well is unnecessary. Regardless, keep an eye on this situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.analysis: Bears coach Ben Johnson told reporters on Monday that Tyson Bagent will start against the Packers this week. Fast forward a few days and the odds have changed slightly. Williams did a little throwing, practicing in a limited capacity today, and is progressing through his rehab plan. That said, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Bagent will “most likely” get the start. We expect that to be the case. Regardless, make sure Williams is rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.headline: Bears head coach Ben Johnson said Tyson Bagent will start in Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.analysis: We assumed this was where things were heading after Bagent turned in a solid outing in his first start against the Jets. Bagent has been the QB2 on the Bears’ depth chart throughout the season and only missed Week 3’s start against the Eagles because he spent most of the week in the league’s concussion protocol. Bagent threw for 268 yards and one interception in Sunday’s win over the Jets and will have some appeal in 2QB/Superflex leagues, especially with the Chiefs and Panthers both on byes in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.headline: Tyson Bagent completed 25-of-34 attempts for 268 yards and one interception in the Bears’ Week 4 win against the Jets, adding four rushes for one yard.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.analysis: Getting the start after Case Keenum led the Bears to victory in Week 3 against the Eagles, Bagent successfully managed the run-heavy Bears offense. He was inaccurate for stretches of the game, throwing at least two balls that should have been intercepted by the New York secondary. On the day he was 8 percent over his expected completion rate. Bagent targeted Rom Odunze a team-high nine times. He connected with Colston Loveland and Luther Burden III a handful of times on well-times throws to the middle of the field. Bagent will get another start in Week 5 against the Packers with Caleb Williams sidelined. He’ll have some superflex appeal in that matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.headline: Bears QB Tyson Bagent will start in Week 4 against the Jets, reports Dan Wiederer of the Athletic.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.analysis: Bagent came in after Caleb Williams suffered a hamstring strain in Week 2, but missed Week 3 as he was in concussion protocol with Case Keenum getting the start. With Williams still out, Bagent will be back under center against the Jets. With Ben Johnson calling plays, Bagent is a super-flex option in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that QB Tyson Bagent is expected to start for the Bears in Week 4 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.analysis: Bagent signed a two-year, $10 million contract extension in August 2025 to serve as the Bears’ No. 2 quarterback. He took the majority of first-team reps this week despite QB3 Case Keenum’s Week 3 heroics. Bagent can be started in Superflex leagues against the Jets, assuming he is officially named the starter this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) will not play in Week 4 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.analysis: Williams was never believed to have a real shot at playing, but the Bears officially ruled him out on Friday. Tyson Bagent has reportedly taken all of the first-team snaps in practice this week, but Ben Johnson may wait until kickoff to reveal who his starter will be on Sunday, with both Bagent and Case Keenum expected to be active. We’ll see if Williams’ status improves for Week 5’s game against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.headline: ProFootballTalk’s Mike Florio reports “as we hear it, Tyson Bagent has gotten the first-team reps so far this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.analysis: While head coach Ben Johnson will do his best to keep his QB1 for Week 4’s game against the Jets under wraps, it’s hard to slip things past all the reporters who are present during the media portion of practice. With reports that Bagent, who is listed as the Bears’ QB2 on the depth chart, is taking first-team reps, it’s safe to assume things are trending toward him making the start this week. We may not get a clear answer from the team on who the starter will be until kickoff, which makes both Bagent and Case Keenum hard to trust for fantasy managers who may have been considering them in 2QB/Superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.headline: Bears QB Caleb Williams (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyson-bage.analysis: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Williams will not participate in today’s walkthrough, but noted that Williams is “getting better every single day.” He also said he has not decided which quarterback will start in Week 4 against the Jets. Week 3 starter QB Case Keenum was victorious over the Eagles on Monday Night Football and nominal No. 2 QB Tyson Bagent has cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.headline: Dylan Laube had four rushes for nine yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots, adding three receptions for 16 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.analysis: Laube functioned as the team’s No. 2 back behind Ashton Jeanty, who battled through foot and ankle issues on his way to 77 scoreless yards against New England. Mike Washington, meanwhile, had one rushing attempt and did not catch a pass. If Jeanty misses time this season it might be Laube who leads the Vegas backfield in touches. He can be stashed in deeper formats headed into Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.headline: Mike Washington rushed six times for 63 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.analysis: The rookie fourth-rounder wound up leading the Raiders in both rush attempts and rushing yards on Thursday, with his most notable run coming on a 53-yard burst that saw him evade multiple defenders on the play. Washington is competing for the Raiders’ RB2 spot behind Ashton Jeanty and should have the inside edge over third-year back Dylan Laube, who totaled 11 yards on five carries in Thursday’s loss.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.headline: Raiders declared RB Raheem Mostert (knee/ankle) inactive for Week 17 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.analysis: Mostert entered Week 17 questionable to play due to knee and ankle injuries. He is not fantasy-relevant on his own. His absence could result in a few late-game touches for RB Zamir White and RB Dylan Laube. Neither player should be anywhere near fantasy lineups, though. Starting RB Ashton Jeanty could feasibly handle all backfield touches against the Giants today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.headline: Dylan Laube did not record a touch in the Raiders’ Week 18 loss to the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.analysis: Laube’s first offensive snaps in the NFL came in Week 6. He got two reps on offense, fumbled his first carry, and was never heard from again. The Raiders put him in timeout as a healthy scratch for a few weeks before bringing him back in the fold as a high-volume special teams player. Laube did not log any more snaps on offense after Week 6, let alone touches. Having been exiled from the offense entirely, it’s fair to wonder how Laube fits on the team’s roster in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.headline: Dylan Laube did not record a touch in the Raiders’ Week 12 loss against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.analysis: Outside of a 59-yard kickoff return, Laube was invisible. Alexander Mattison and Zamir White were sidelined, leaving Ameer Abdullah and Sincere McCormick — who had never had a regular season carry before Sunday — to split the Vegas backfield work. Laube did not run a pass route against Denver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.headline: Alexander Mattison (ankle) is doubtful for Week 12 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.analysis: Zamir White is also doubtful, meaning Ameer Abdullah should draw the start. Abdullah hasn’t seen double-digit carries since 2017, so we should get plenty of Dylan Laube touches as well. As underdogs to a stout Denver defense, this isn’t a great spot for either running back, but there are touches up for grabs. Abdullah enters the weekend as a low-end RB3 while Laube is a dart-throw RB4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.headline: Raiders beat writer Vincent Bonsignore writes Dylan Laube “is expected to be a big part of the game plan” in Week 12 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.analysis: Injuries to Zamir White (quad) and Alexander Mattison (ankle) will shoehorn Laube into Sunday’s rotation. The rookie sixth-round pick hasn’t been active since losing a fumble on his first career touch back in Week 6 against the Steelers, but it sounds like he and Ameer Abdullah could be slated for busy days against one of the league’s top defenses. Laube could offer some upside as a pass-catcher in Sunday’s AFC West showdown, but fantasy managers shouldn’t be flocking to put him in their starting lineups. If the matchup wasn’t challenging enough as is, the Raiders have been one of the worst rushing teams in the league all season. Pro Football Focus has them graded as the fifth-worst run-blocking team in all of football. Laube is better used as a stash rather than a start in Week 12, even with a tough week of byes on tap.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.headline: Zamir White suffered a quad injury in Week 11 against the Dolphins and did not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.analysis: White went down in the second half with a quad issue. Though he was listed as questionable to return, the young back never got back on the field, leaving Ameer Abdullah as the team’s only active running back. Dylan Laube was a healthy scratch for this game but will likely get some run down the stretch with both White and Alexander Mattison (ankle) banged up. Abdullah and Laube are worth adding off the waiver wire in all formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.headline: Raiders RB Zamir White (quad) is active for Week 9 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.analysis: Raiders declared RB Dylan Laube, CB Sam Webb, S Trey Taylor, C Andre James, and DE Janarius Robinson inactive for Week 9 against the Bengals. With White ready to go against the Bengals, Laube was deemed inactive as Alexander Mattison and White will continue to be the Raiders’ top backs. Andre James (ankle) is the Raiders’ major injury inactive as the center will miss his first game of the season. EDGE Maxx Crosby (ankle) and LB Robert Spillane (knee) both did not practice Friday but are good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.headline: Zamir White (quad) didn’t practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-laub.analysis: White was a limited participant during Wednesday’s session, and the 6-foot, 215-pound tailback was unable to go Thursday. This could be load management, but it’s not being listed as such. White’s absence would set up potentially more touches for Ameer Abdullah or Dylan Laube.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 14 times for 52 yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard looks like he could be a legitimate NFL running back somewhere, but it sure can’t happen on this offense. He’s cleared 14 carries and 48 yards in each of his last four games and has just one touchdown to show for it. It’s fringe low-end RB2 land for Pollard, as usual, against the Colts next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (foot) is not on Tennessee’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard will take on the 0-4 Texans, who have had some trouble handling the run, and should be a viable low-end RB2 this week. He continues to get Wednesday vet days while dealing with this foot injury, but doesn’t seem to be in any real danger of missing time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (foot) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: During Weeks 3-4, Pollard took Wednesdays off, rehabbing an ankle injury. He would resume practicing on Thursday and suit up on Sunday. Now, with his new foot issue, he appears to be on the same practice plan. Expect him to play in Week 5 against the Texans. Pollard was a full participant on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: The Titans have given Pollard Wednesday off in back-to-back weeks. He was removed from the injury report entirely on Friday both times. This week should be no different. Pollard has 39 touches over the past two weeks. Even on a struggling Titans offense, that’s enough work to put him on the RB2/3 border for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 16 times for 48 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 4 loss to the Ravens, adding two catches for two additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard was wildly inefficient in this one, but saved his fantasy day when he scored a three-yard touchdown in the first quarter to give the Titans their first points of the day. It was the first touchdown of the season for Pollard, who continues to serve as the Titans’ primary back, but there’s not much fantasy upside to be had here. Pollard will be a boom-or-bust RB3 next week against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes Tony Pollard “fits the profile” of a player who could be traded ahead of the deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Schefter didn’t cite any sources telling him that Pollard could be on the move, but he did connect a few key dots. Pollard is in the final year of his contract and the Titans are going nowhere fast. If they don’t plan on re-signing him next offseason, they might as well get something in return for him in the middle of another lost season. His departure would also clear the way for rookie Nick Singleton to see more work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (ankle) is not on the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: With Titans RB2 Tyjae Spears (ankle) questionable to play, Pollard could end up handling a big workload. Unfortunately, the Titans field an unproductive offense and face the Ravens this week. He can only be viewed as a moderate FLEX starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: The full practice keeps him as a potential RB2/FLEX option against the Ravens for Week 4. Pollard dominated reps in Week 3 with Tyjae Spears active as a game-time decision. Spears looks to be a little better this week, but Pollard should be at the head of the committee still in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Neither did Tyjae Spears, who is also dealing with an ankle issue. Both backs played through their injuries last week and head coach Robert Saleh said today that he isn’t concerned about either of them missing Week 4. The Titans held them out of last Wednesday’s practice as well, so this seems to be the new norm for the backfield tandem. Pollard remains a volume-based RB3 after seeing 21 touches last week. Spears is nothing more than a backup right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 17 times for 74 yards in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants, adding four catches for 22 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard handled all but three of the running back carries in this contest and was the only Titans running back to earn a target. Tyjae Spears was a game-time decision because of an ankle injury and was likely on some sort of pitch count, shifting the bulk of the touches to Pollard. The role was great, but the fantasy production was lacking. That has been a theme for Titans players over the past few years. Pollard is capable of earning an RB2 workload but will ultimately project for RB3 fantasy numbers when the Titans take on the Ravens next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray completed 24-of-30 passes for 229 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ 23-13, Week 5 win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Murray was extremely active on the ground, addnig 51 yards on 10 rush attempts. His deep ball, on the other hand, remains a work in progress. His lone touchdown of the day came on a dime to Justin Jefferson on the back of the end zone. He was hesitant to even pull the trigger on deep shots at other times, even when his receiver was wide open. Murray is largely a game-manager right now, but that’s enough to win football games when the Minnesota defense is simply shutting down every opponent they face. Murray will be a mid-range QB2 when he returns to take on the Colts after a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray completed 27-of-37 passes for 247 yards in the Vikings’ 15-10, Week 4 win over the Dolphins, adding six rushes for 16 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: The Dolphins’ pass rush made life tougher than expected for the Vikings’ signal caller. Murray managed to turn a few extended plays into successful scrambles, but he also took four sacks, at times simply holding the ball too long. As the game progressed, Murray locked in on T.J. Hockenson when the pass rush was closing in, linking up with him 13 times for 119 yards. The duo should have shared a late touchdown, but Hockenson smartly downed himself at the Dolphins’ five-yard line, so Murray could kneel out the clock from there. Murray will be a high-end QB2 against the Saints next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray completed 15-of-29 attempts for 168 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Vikings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs, adding two rushes for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: In his first action since sustaining a concussion in Week 1, Murray wasn’t asked to do much in this one. He was about four percent below his expected pass rate on the day with an average depth of target of 9.4 yards. Murray targeted Jordan Addison heavily after Justin Jefferson left the game with an ankle injury, connecting with Addison on a 41-yard score and narrowly missing the speedy downfield wideout for another touchdown. Murray took three sacks and avoided a handful of other sacks against a Tampa front seven missing key players. Murray likely won’t be a 12-team starting play in Week 4 against the Dolphins even if Jefferson suits up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Kyler Murray has cleared concussion protocol and will start in Week 3 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: The 2-0 Vikings will hopefully get their first full look at Murray, who exited in Week 1 after just 11 snaps.
