https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: Texans and QB C.J. Stroud will pause contract discussion until after the 2026 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: The two sides worked diligently to get a deal done before the start of the regular season but will now pause discussions until after the year. Stroud was reportedly offered a substantial deal earlier in the offseason but turned it down, now forced to “bet on himself” as he plays out the final year of his rookie deal, minus the fifth-year option. Stroud has been unable to rekindle his rookie year magic while playing under two different offensive coordinators, something he’s looking to remedy in his second season under Nick Caley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Texans are “prepared to put CJ Stroud in what it feels is a strong place among the 12 quarterbacks in the $50 million club.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: Houston GM Nick Caserio recently said the team would not negotiate a new deal with Stroud once the regular season begins, putting a hard and fast deadline on Stroud’s ability to secure a longer-term contract with the team that drafted him. His immense and nationally-televised struggles down the stretch last season — including his playoff meltdown against the Patriots — could factor into the team’s decision to go all in on him as a long-term franchise quarterback. Fowler said Stroud “can let an exploding quarterback market do the work for him if he waits an additional six to eight months” and explore free agency in 2027. Stroud over the past three seasons ranks 22nd out of 40 qualifying QBs in adjusted EPA per drop back, alongside Bo Nix and Trevor Lawrence. He ranks 24th in drop back success rate, just behind Mac Jones.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: Texans GM Nick Caserio said there were “productive talks” on a contract extension for QB C.J. Stroud and that if a deal isn’t done before the start of the season, they’ll pick it up next offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: There’s really no reason for Stroud to want to negotiate off last year’s end-of-season performance, so we’re not stunned that there’s been no extension. It does sound like the Texans are at least laying the groundwork for next offseason. The general NFL expectation has been that Stroud will go into the year without an extension. The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan Alexander reported that league sources believe the Texans and Stroud’s camp “are not far off on what they think Stroud’s contract terms should look like and how much he should be paid per year.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Texans QB C.J. Stroud has “been steadier and more consistent this offseason.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: Stroud is currently eligible for a contract extension, and Breer believes Stroud is conducting himself “with a seriousness that underlies the big year he has in front of him.” Citing good health and a growing relationship with OC Nick Caley, Breer adds that Stroud has also taken “more command of the offense” this summer. The Texans might not need Stroud to be a prolific passer every week, given their elite defense, but it sounds like Stroud is taking the necessary steps to deliver more reliable results when called upon. Hopefully, he indeed rises to the occasion when the regular season arrives.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 2-of-3 targets for 37 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has been held to two and three catches over his past two games. It’s probably not a coincidence that Brenton Strange leads the team with 14 catches during Meyers’ two-game slump. Meyers is still operating as the Jags’ WR2, but his role will come down to matchup nuances on a week-to-week basis. He is sliding back into the WR5 fantasy ranks ahead of his Week 6 matchup with the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 3-of-4 targets for 33 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers continues to see the most snaps among all Jaguars wide receivers as Liam Coen utilizes him as both an outside target and willing blocker. He was second in targets against the Bengals as Trevor Lawrence threw just 23 passes on the day. Meyers now seems to be ahead of Brian Thomas Jr. on the wide receiver pecking order and is WR3 fantasy play for a London game against the Eagles in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: He should be trusted as a low-end WR3/FLEX play against the Bengals. Meyers has cleared the injury report with this thumb listing three times in three weeks, though he was questionable in Week 2. It clearly isn’t bothering him enough to impact his play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: No real surprises here; Meyers has played through this thumb listing in two consecutive weeks and will likely be removed from the injury report on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has been playing through the thumb issue all year and that won’t change in Week 4. With Brian Thomas Jr.'s role disappearing, Meyers has quietly emerged as the No. 2 receiver on one of the league’s best offenses. He remains a solid FLEX play for his Week 4 date with the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 7-of-8 targets for 64 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers made the most of his opportunities in a revenge game against his former team. After totaling three catches for 68 yards in his first two games of the season, Meyers led the Jaguars in targets and grabs against New England, catching one of Trevor Lawrence’s three touchdown throws. Meyers entered the game with a meager six percent target share and a 11 percent air yards share. He could have some flex viability in Week 4 against a middling Bengals secondary that gave up a big day to Steelers pass catchers in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) is active for Week 3 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers was able to practice late in the week and will suit up as the team’s WR3 against a tough New England coverage unit. It’s a revenge game for Meyers, who through Week 2 has a 6 percent target share and a 12 percent air yards share while running a route on 76 percent of the Jaguars’ drop backs. Jaguars declared WR CJ Williams, S Jalen Huskey, LB Jack Kiser, OL Daniel Faalele, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis inactive against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) isn’t on Jacksonville’s final injury report for Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: He will play against the Patriots. Meyers got in his first full practice since suffering the thumb injury and should be a reasonable FLEX play against New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) remained limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers played through this thumb listing last week and was limited in back-to-back sessions to start the week; he should be considered likely to play against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught his lone target for 28 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers, who came into the game with a lingering thumb injury, led the Jaguars in pass routes but only saw one look from Trevor Lawrence, who had a meager 189 yards on the day. Through two games Meyers has 68 yards and a touchdown in what should be a productive Jacksonville offense. He will be flex-viable next week against New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 7-of-8 targets for 68 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: After a quiet three games to start the year, Strange has heated up over the past two weeks. He led the team with seven catches last week and did so again today in London. Strange had seven catches in his first three games combined. He can’t be expected to pace the Jags in receiving, but Strange is back on the TE1/2 border for his Week 6 date with Houston.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 7-of-8 targets for 95 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange was Trevor Lawrence’s primary target against a Bengals defense that has struggled against tight ends. Many of his targets were middle-of-the-field intermediate passes as he tallied 95 total receiving yards on the day. The Jaguars offense has a variety of pass-catchers that can find success based on defensive matchup. The game environment aligned perfectly for Strange, who rarely came off the field with 53 total snaps. The Eagles are a tougher matchup for tight ends, but Strange is a good streamer option in the high-end TE2 territory for a Week 5 matchup in London.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 3-of-5 targets for 32 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers dominated looks from Trevor Lawrence on a low-volume day for the Jacksonville offense. Strange played his usual role as a check down option for Lawrence, rumbling for yards after the catch on two of his three grabs. Strange, with seven catches on the year, could be a streaming play in Week 4 against the Bengals if the game turns into a shootout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught both of his targets for 17 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange ran a pass route on 30 of the team’s 36 drop backs but was invisible for most of the game. For now Strange can be treated as a desperation streamer in 12-team formats ahead of the Jags’ Week 3 matchup against the Patriots. He should remain on waiver wires in 10-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 2-of-3 targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange operated as the Jaguars’ primary receiving tight end, seeing three targets on the day. In a loaded passing attack, he still found opportunity in what was a very fantasy-friendly offense. Strange caught a 14-yard touchdown in the second quarter and was mostly quiet in a second half where the Jaguars were already up by four scores. The Jaguars wide receivers will take much of Lawrence’s targets but Strange has a role over the middle of the field; he profiles as TE2 for Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Jaguars signed Brenton Strange to a three-year contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the deal is worth “up to” $48 million. A chunk of that figure is presumably based on incentives. The contract includes $25 million guaranteed. Strange posted a minor breakout in 2024 with 411 yards on 40 grabs. He upped the ante in 2025 to 46 catches for 540 yards despite missing five games. Strange was heading into the final year of his rookie deal before this extension and the team spent multiple draft picks on tight ends, making it look like they were considering letting him walk next offseason. Instead, Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol will primarily see the field for heavy offensive looks, something the team talked about after the draft. Strange will sit on the TE1/2 border in early fantasy drafts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes Brenton Strange will be a “key piece of everything the Jaguars do on offense” in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Shipley said the Jaguars drafting Texas A&M TE Nate Boerkircher and Houston TE Tanner Koziol in the 2026 draft does not mean the Jaguars coaching staff has a smaller role planned for Strange, who last season 46 catches, 540 yards, and three touchdowns as the team’s TE1. Shipley expected Strange’s pass game involvement to grow as the Jaguars deploy more tight end-heavy offensive sets. The Jaguars, Shipley said, are “clearly hoping that injecting the [tight end] room with talent should allow Strange to produce at an even higher level than before.” Last season Strange was targeted on 21 percent of his routes, which ranked 25th out of 58 qualifying tight ends. Though he’ll likely be the team’s third or fourth option in the passing game, Strange should be a viable fantasy option in 12 and 14-team leagues this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: ESPN’s Michael DiRocco reports the Jaguars have had preliminary discussions about extensions for WR Parker Washington, TE Brenton Strange, and EDGE Travon Walker.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: It was pointed out by John Shipley a few days ago that Wan’Dale Robinson’s free agent contract might be a starting point for the Washington extension. Walker is entering his final season under his rookie contract’s fifth-year option. Strange and Washington are both on the final year of their rookie contracts. The Jaguars have been uncharacteristically (and probably smartly, given their success last year) quiet in free agency, so perhaps they’re just focusing on locking up their core.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes the Jaguars could target a tight end in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Shipley refers to Jaguars starting TE Brenton Strange as “maybe the most underrated tight end in the entire NFL” and says the team knows “just how important he is to everything they do.” Sounds like Strange’s role is safe. Shipley believes TE Quintin Morris could have true TE2 potential, but Morris caught just 6-of-7 targets for 55 yards and one touchdown after signing with the Jaguars in free agency last year. His position on the depth chart sounds less secure. Strange can be viewed as a low-end TE1 candidate at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 2-of-5 targets for nine yards in the Jaguars’ Wild Card Round loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: A hip injury early in the year suppressed Strange’s numbers in what would have easily been a breakout season for the third-year tight end. He was placed on injured reserve and missed five games. Despite that, Strange’s 46 catches, 540 yards, and three touchdowns were all career-highs. He finished the year as a mid-range TE2 on a per-game basis. The Jags run four deep at receiver when everyone is healthy. Liam Coen dials up designed targets for his running backs a few times a week. That makes it hard for Strange to be a consistent target-earner, but he is a solid streaming option when bye weeks roll in. He will be stuck in the TE2 range in 2026 drafts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed two times for five yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez was all but phased out of the rotation in this game. His most notable touch was a goal line carry which he was stuffed on and then fumbled the ball away. He was called down on the field. Even though replay clearly showed him losing the ball, there was no clear recovery and the refs didn’t bother overturning the non-fumble. Rodriguez may still be the occasional touchdown vulture, but his role has been reduced to the point where fantasy managers can safely cut ties with him on the next run of waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed six times for 35 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez entered the game frequently when the Jaguars entered Bengals territory. He has a hold on short-yardage opportunities while also getting some red zone looks, but Bhayshul Tuten is the clear lead back. Rodriguez was out-snapped 36-to-15 but salvaged his fantasy day with a 25-yard rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter. He is a handcuff for fantasy purposes heading into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez had eight rushes for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez remained the second option in the Jaguars backfield behind Bhayshul Tuten, but stole a short score from Tuten in the blowout victory. Through three games Rodriguez has been a between the tackles option who has next to no involvement in the passing game. He would only be fantasy viable if Tuten misses time this season. For now C-Rod is a decent stash as a contingency option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said he “fully anticipates” more snaps for LeQuin Allen on third down.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Allen played on just one offensive snap in last week’s win over the Browns, but led the Jaguars in third-down snaps (146) last season. Despite all the snaps he saw on third down as a rookie, Allen never materialized into a viable fantasy option. Whether or not that changes this season is to be determined, but any additional snaps he receives on third down would come at the expense of Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, after Rodriguez led the way with five third-down snaps last week. While Allen seeing additional work in these situations could be problematic for fantasy managers, they shouldn’t let that deter them from starting Tuten in Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez Jr. rushed six times for 23 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez was the Jaguars’ second running back in the game, but equaled Bhayshul Tuten’s touches on the first drive. He was used both in the red zone and short-yardage situations early on; Rodriguez tied for the lead in backfield snaps in the first half. The game was out of reach in the second half, with Ameer Abdullah taking on garbage time carries and Rodriguez finishing the game second in backfield snaps. Fantasy managers will like the high-leverage utilization but a lack of receiving upside caps Rodriguez’ ceiling. He is firmly in the RB4 range for Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said RB LeQuint Allen (hip) is a game-time decision for Week 1 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: As expected, Allen did not practice Wednesday. It’s not that fantasy managers were eager to start Allen this week, but his absence would open up more routes and potential targets for Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, who are listed as co-starters on Jacksonville’s Week 1 depth chart. Both C-Rod and Tuten would be slightly better options if Allen is sidelined this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes neither Bhayshul Tuten nor Chris Rodriguez will emerge as the lead back in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Shipley hedges a bit by noting that there’s a chance that one back simply carries the momentum early in the season forward and never lets up, but ultimately falls on the idea that neither back is likely to hit 1,000 rushing yards in 2026. “I think there is a more likely chance we see both running backs hit 750+ yards than one of them hit 1,000,” Shipley writes. Such a split would probably lean towards Rodriguez at the goal line, making him slightly more fantasy-valuable on a weekly basis barring big plays from Tuten. If this prediction comes true, both backs might have trouble cracking the weekly RB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said he would be “pleasantly surprised” if LeQuint Allen Jr. (soft tissue) played in Week 1 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Coen talked up Ameer Abdullah as a potential replacement for Allen’s duties in pass protection. He also singled out Chris Rodriguez’s abilities in pass pro. Pass protection duties aren’t a direct source of fantasy value, but it usually means that player will be on the field for the two-minute drill, which can generate plenty of receptions for running backs. Bhayshul Tuten not getting those reps would be a notable ding to his fantasy outlook. Allen himself isn’t on the fantasy radar, healthy or not.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Jaguars RB LeQuint Allen (soft tissue) will miss the rest of training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Allen suffered a soft tissue injury during Monday’s practice and the Jaguars announced Tuesday morning that he’ll miss the rest of training camp. It’s unclear if he’ll be ready for the start of the regular season. While Allen doesn’t have standalone fantasy value, he seemed destined for a legitimate role as the primary receiving back in this offense. If Allen misses time in the regular season, it would boost receiving opportunities for Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said the team’s running back usage “is going to have to be a little bit more by committee” this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Coen discussed both RB Bhayshul Tuten and RB Chris Rodriguez during his presser. Regarding Tuten, Coen said the second-year back has shown that he has “bought in” over the past year, and complimented his ability to take “hard coaching” while noting his 4.28-second 40 speed. Coen adds that Tuten has to continue working on making his reads and not overthinking things. Regarding Rodriguez, Coen complimented his recent downhill running and blitz pickups. Coen loves consistency at the running back position. This looks like it will be a committee to start the year. That said, if one player separates, things can change quickly. Tuten remains the high-upside pick, although Rodriguez can be productive in his own right.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 22 times for 72 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles, adding two catches for 24 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: The Jags’ offense struggled to execute at a basic level in this game, and Tuten may have been hurt the most by errors. Their first goal line sequence of the day started with a Chris Rodriguez near-fumble. After two incomplete passes, Liam Coen dialed up a jet sweep for Tuten that was blown up for a loss of six yards. The Jags’ next goal line sequence featured a pair of delay of game penalties followed by an incomplete pass on fourth down. Tuten got the full workhorse treatment in this game, ceding just two carries and one catch to his backups. He unfortunately could not make much of the touches. Tuten will be a high-end RB2 if this role persists into his Week 6 matchup versus the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 17 times for 73 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals, adding two receptions for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten continued to operate as the Jaguars’ lead back, ripping off a 15-yard carry to open the game. He found success running to the outside edges of the Bengals defense, tallying 91 total yards on the day. However, fantasy managers will be frustrated with the results as Tuten had touchdowns of 44 yards and three yards get called back due to holding penalties while Chris Rodriguez scored late in the game. The good news is Tuten out-snapped Rodriguez 36-to-15 on the day. He is still the lead back, though he cedes short-yardage and clear passing-down opportunities to Rodriguez and LeQuint Allen. Tuten gets enough opportunities to be squarely in the fantasy RB2 range on a weekly basis, he is a top-20 play for Week 5 against the Eagles in London.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Chris Rodriguez had eight rushes for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Rodriguez remained the second option in the Jaguars backfield behind Bhayshul Tuten, but stole a short score from Tuten in the blowout victory. Through three games Rodriguez has been a between the tackles option who has next to no involvement in the passing game. He would only be fantasy viable if Tuten misses time this season. For now C-Rod is a decent stash as a contingency option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten had 15 rushes for 73 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots, adding two catches for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten has taken control of the Jaguars backfield over the past couple weeks. Against the Patriots he out-carried Chris Rodriguez 15 to eight, with much of Rodriguez’s opportunity coming after the game had been decided. Tuten split pass-catching duties with LeQuint Allen, who also had two grabs on the day. Tuten probably won’t be a 20-touch back most weeks, but he should be a solid RB2 option going forward, including in Week 4 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten had 13 rushes for 65 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss against the Broncos, adding two catches for -3 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten more than doubled the workload of Chris Rodriguez, who had six rushes for 13 yards and did not record a reception. Tuten looked like the far more explosive backfield option for the Jags. He nearly broke a couple big runs and had one long carry called back on a penalty. Last week Tuten had 88 total yards against the Browns. The second-year back is looking more reliable as a fantasy option in what was regarded as a shaky situation ahead of the season. He should be seen as a top-24 play in Week 3 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said he “fully anticipates” more snaps for LeQuin Allen on third down.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Allen played on just one offensive snap in last week’s win over the Browns, but led the Jaguars in third-down snaps (146) last season. Despite all the snaps he saw on third down as a rookie, Allen never materialized into a viable fantasy option. Whether or not that changes this season is to be determined, but any additional snaps he receives on third down would come at the expense of Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, after Rodriguez led the way with five third-down snaps last week. While Allen seeing additional work in these situations could be problematic for fantasy managers, they shouldn’t let that deter them from starting Tuten in Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 15 times for 66 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns, adding one reception for 22 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten started the game for the Jaguars, getting the first two carries of the game. His utilization was mixed, tying Chris Rodriguez for snaps in the first half. Tuten was rotated out for early red zone and short-yardage snaps, though he saw some of those opportunities later in the game. He held up well in pass-protection and took a screen pass 22 yards for his first reception. With the game out of hand in the second half, Tuten ultimately saw the highest snaps out of the backfield, tallying 28 on the day. He showed good burst and the ability to fight through contact, but Rodriguez will continue to be a thorn in his side for utilization. Tuten profiles as a high-end RB3 for Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said RB LeQuint Allen (hip) is a game-time decision for Week 1 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: As expected, Allen did not practice Wednesday. It’s not that fantasy managers were eager to start Allen this week, but his absence would open up more routes and potential targets for Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, who are listed as co-starters on Jacksonville’s Week 1 depth chart. Both C-Rod and Tuten would be slightly better options if Allen is sidelined this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes neither Bhayshul Tuten nor Chris Rodriguez will emerge as the lead back in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Shipley hedges a bit by noting that there’s a chance that one back simply carries the momentum early in the season forward and never lets up, but ultimately falls on the idea that neither back is likely to hit 1,000 rushing yards in 2026. “I think there is a more likely chance we see both running backs hit 750+ yards than one of them hit 1,000,” Shipley writes. Such a split would probably lean towards Rodriguez at the goal line, making him slightly more fantasy-valuable on a weekly basis barring big plays from Tuten. If this prediction comes true, both backs might have trouble cracking the weekly RB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said he would be “pleasantly surprised” if LeQuint Allen Jr. (soft tissue) played in Week 1 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Coen talked up Ameer Abdullah as a potential replacement for Allen’s duties in pass protection. He also singled out Chris Rodriguez’s abilities in pass pro. Pass protection duties aren’t a direct source of fantasy value, but it usually means that player will be on the field for the two-minute drill, which can generate plenty of receptions for running backs. Bhayshul Tuten not getting those reps would be a notable ding to his fantasy outlook. Allen himself isn’t on the fantasy radar, healthy or not.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-sava.headline: Dolphins OL Jonah Savaiinaea is questionable to return Week 5 against the Bengals with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-sava.analysis: Savaiinaea hurt his ankle at some point in the second quarter and was declared questionable to return. He stood on the sidelines for some time but Jarrett Kingston is in at right guard for the 22-year-old second-year lineman.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.headline: Mykel Williams is active for Week 5 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.analysis: Williams entered the weekend as questionable after being limited in practice all week. Now, the Niners DT will officially be active for a pivotal NFC West showdown against the 3-1 Seahawks. While Williams is active, the Niners did declare DL James Thompson Jr., LB Tatum Bethune, DL Nick Bosa, OL Enrique Cruz Jr., QB Kurtis Rourke, FB Kyle Juszczyk, and S Marques Sigle inactive for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.headline: 49ers DL Mykel Williams (knee) is questionable for Week 5 against the Seahawks
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.analysis: Williams is officially listed as questionable, though he is expected to take the field for the first time since tearing his ACL in Week 9, during this 2025 rookie season. His return could not have come soon enough. The 49ers’ defensive line has been hit hard by injuries this year. The 49ers correspondingly released DL Ogbo Okoronkwo to make room on the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said he hopes to activate EDGE Mykel Williams (knee) for San Francisco’s Week 5 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.analysis: Williams wasn’t eligible to return in Week 4 because of reserve/PUP list rules. It appears that he’ll have a real chance to go against Seattle in what figures to be a drag-out battle between two of the NFC West’s best.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.headline: 49ers LT Trent Williams (stinger) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.analysis: The 49ers will have their stud left tackle active on Sunday. 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw (quad bruise) is questionable to play. 49ers EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) and DL Mykel Williams (knee) have both been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.headline: 49ers activated DL Mykel Williams (knee) from the reserve/physically unable to perform list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.analysis: Williams tore an ACL during his rookie season last year. He will resume practicing for the first time today. Before suffering the injury, he totaled 19 quarterback pressures, 13 tackles and one sack. He will be eligible to play in Week 5 against the Seahawks at the earliest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.headline: 49ers placed DL Mykel Williams (knee) on the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.analysis: Williams is still recovering from an ACL tear from last November. The 49ers will start him out on the reserve/physically unable to perform list, meaning the second-year pass rusher will miss at least the first four games of the season. Without the 2025 first-round pick in the pass-rush rotation to start the year, the 49ers will rely on Keion White to try and fill the void.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said DL Mykel Williams (knee) will likely sit out in Week 1 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.analysis: This is unfortunate. The second-year pass rusher seemingly had a chance to play right away, but the team is apparently adjusting its expectations. Williams, 22, suffered a season-ending ACL tear in November. Whenever he makes it back, he will provide a decent boost to the 49ers’ defensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.headline: The Athletic’s Vic Tafur reports “the expectation is that (Mykel Williams) will be ready to return to the field very early at camp, if not for the beginning.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.analysis: Williams suffered a torn ACL in Week 9 last season and was seen doing resistance bands workouts at the team’s facilities last month. The second-year pass rusher totaled 11 tackles, four TFLs, and one sack in his rookie season before going down, and is one of a handful of players the Niners are hoping to have back on the defensive side of the ball. Veteran pass rusher Nick Bosa (knee), who also suffered a torn ACL last season, is also working his way back to the field and said he is “pretty far along” in his recovery. If either player is unable to go by the start of camp, they will likely be added to the PUP list with a chance to be activated when they clear all medical and conditioning tests.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.headline: The California Post’s Vincent Bonsignore reports that the 49ers’ 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick and EDGE Mykel Williams form the “framework for a suitable offer” in a potential trade for Raiders EDGE Maxx Crosby.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.analysis: Multiple league sources tell Bonsignore that the Raiders would revisit the idea of trading Crosby away “if the right offer was made.” According to Bonsignore’s sources, the 49ers could make a play for him if they so desire. The Raiders nearly traded Crosby to the Ravens earlier this offseason, but the Ravens cancelled the deal due to concerns over a “degenerative issue” in his knee. Per Bonsignore, if Crosby “returns to terrorizing Raiders’ practices during training camp, he’ll put all concerns to rest,” and “the Raiders will be flooded with calls from interested teams.” The 49ers hope to make a Super Bowl run this season. Adding Crosby to their pass rush makes sense. Williams, the 49ers’ EDGE in reference, is currently recovering from a torn ACL and it is unclear whether he will be able to play in Week 1. At 22 years old, he is more of a long-term option anyway, and the Raiders are currently rebuilding. This framework is interesting and could work well for both sides. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.headline: 49ers GM John Lynch said it’s “too soon to say” whether Mykel Williams (knee) will be ready to play in San Francisco’s Week 1 game against the Rams in Melbourne.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mykel-will.analysis: Fellow EDGE Nick Bosa (also knee, also ACL), who suffered his injury six weeks earlier, is expected back for Week 1. It sounds like Williams is in more doubt. Based on that, it’s certainly possible the second-year EDGE player starts training camp on the PUP list. 49ers beats saw Williams doing side-to-side movements and working with resistance bands at rookie minicamp, so he’s certainly active, but he still has several hurdles to clear in his rehab before a return is on the table.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 6-of-9 targets for 38 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert returned to the lineup after missing three games with a knee injury. Already without Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith, Goedert was immediately thrust into a high-usage role. He led the team in targets and catches, though much of his looks were simply check-downs. Even if that’s his role going forward, Goedert should catch enough passes to sustain borderline TE1 numbers until DeVonta Smith returns. He gets a date with the Panthers in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert got in a full session on Friday and is cleared. With DeVonta Smith down, he has some TE1 potential against the Jaguars on volume. He’s always been one of Jalen Hurts’ favorite red zone targets, and Saquon Barkley being down may lead the Eagles to throw more once the field condenses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert’s return cannot come soon enough. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Hollywood Brown (ankle) remain sidelined, and Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) got hurt in today’s practice. If Goedert can play this week, he will vault right back into the TE1 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: It’s Goedert’s first practice since going down with a knee injury in Week 2. Even a limited session today puts him on track to suit up for Philly’s Week 5 game against the Jags. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) unlikely to play, Goedert could be in line for a large role right away. He will be on the TE1/2 border for Week 5 if he is cleared for action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 4 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and will again be replaced by the combination of Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt in Week 4. Neither of those players are particularly appealing options, though Ertz has enough of a history of success and the Eagles are bereft enough of targets to make him a viable TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) remained sidelined at Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: That leaves Goedert extremely likely to miss his second consecutive contest when the Eagles host the Rams this Sunday. Zach Ertz was Goedert’s feel-good Week 3 fill-in, but Ertz’s 38 percent snap share ended up producing one catch on two targets. With this entire offense looking rather sluggish at the moment, Ertz does not have TE2 streamer appeal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Eagles declared TE Dallas Goedert, QB Tanner McKee, WR Hollywood Brown, QB Cole Payton, DL A.J. Epenesa, and T Fred Johnson inactive for Week 3 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: No real surprises here after Goedert was ruled out earlier in the week. The team elevated veteran Zach Ertz to the active roster from the practice squad, although he remains unlikely to see a full workload after joining the team this week in the midst of recovering from a torn ACL suffered in 2025. Tanner McKee will serve as the emergency quarterback. EDGE Jonathan Greenard will make his season debut after missing the team’s first two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Dallas Goedert is expected to miss a few weeks with a sprained MCL.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert avoided a serious injury, but the veteran tight end will still be sidelined for a few weeks. It’s a blow to an Eagles passing game that has struggled coming out of the gate, as Goedert has already tallied five receptions for 81 yards and two touchdowns in the first six quarters of football he has played this season. Veteran TE Johnny Mundt should be the favorite to replace Goedert going forward; he stepped in to play 49 snaps against the Titans. Mundt has 76 career receptions in 116 games and shouldn’t be viewed as an option to replace Goedert in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Dallas Goedert will have an MRI on his knee after Week 2’s win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert exited in the second quarter of Sunday’s game and did not return to the field. The 31-year-old tight end will undergo an MRI to confirm the severity of his injury, but it sounds like he could be at risk of missing some time. With rookie tight end Eli Stowers (quad) already on injured reserve, veteran Johnny Mundt would be in line to see an increased role after leading all Eagles tight ends in snaps (49) and routes run (20) against the Titans. Mundt caught just two passes for eight yards and will not be on the fantasy radar for Week 3 against the Bears even if he does draw the start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert suffered a right knee injury in the Eagles’ Week 2 game against the Titans and is questionable to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert got roughed up run blocking early in the second quarter. He was then absent for the following drive, earning the questionable tag. It’s not a good development for someone with Goedert’s injury history, though to the naked eye, it did not have the looks of a season-ending injury. Goedert had a four-yard catch on two targets before departing. Johnny Mundt is the next man up at tight end. Second-round rookie Eli Stowers (quad, hamstring) is currently on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 5-of-7 targets for 43 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: The good news is that Lemon set new season highs in targets, catches, and yards. The bad news: All of that resulted in a measly 9.3 PPR points. Lemon will hopefully continue to earn more opportunities as the season progresses, but DeVonta Smith’s return could just as easily stall the rookie’s progress. Lemon will be a WR4/5 if Smith remains out for Week 6 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Wicks was listed as a limited participant today, indicating that he strained his hamstring during Thursday’s practice. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) still sidelined, rookie WR Makai Lemon could be the de facto top receiver, though the team has struggled to use him effectively thus far. Hollywood Brown (ankle) also remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-6 targets for 27 yards in the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon moved up a spot in the targets pecking order with DeVonta Smith sidelined, but it resulted in the same quiet box score he posted the first three weeks of his career. The No. 20 overall pick is now sitting on 10 receptions for a scoreless 65 yards through his first four NFL appearances. There has yet to be any light at the tunnel with regards to either his usage or the Eagles’ overall offensive environment. Even with byes beginning and injuries mounting, Lemon is not a recommended WR4 heading into Week 5 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-4 targets for 29 yards in the Eagles’ Week 3 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon was the target on the team’s first play from scrimmage, gaining a first down on a first down play for the Eagles for the first time all season. The offense would sputter throughout the game on their way to only 47 offensive plays run from scrimmage, capping the fantasy upside of all involved in the process. Lemon has yet to live up to his lofty draft capital through the first three games of his professional career, but he could be called on for heavier work with tight end Dallas Goedert nursing an MCL sprain. Things don’t get any easier with a matchup against the Rams on deck for Week 4, where Lemon can safely be left on fantasy benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught a 14-yard pass in the Eagles’ Week 2 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon also “added” a -5 yard rush. Lemon’s first quarter catch ended up going down as his only target of the afternoon. He’s now stuck on four catches for nine yards through his first two NFL contests, and is getting soundly out-targeted by Dontayvion Wicks. That’s with Darius Cooper mixing in. The Eagles are calling plays like Lemon has to be manufactured his touches. Two games is not a large sample size, but it is enough to know we can’t rely on Lemon as a WR4 for Week 3 in Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-4 targets for negative -5 yards in the Eagles’ Week 1 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: It’s possible things could’ve gone worse for Lemon in his debut, but not much worse. The rookie first-rounder saw two of his four targets come at/behind the line of scrimmage, with his longest target coming eight yards downfield. Lemon’s 28 routes run were good for third-most among Eagles receivers in this one, but we would expect him to see a little more work downfield going forward. Lemon remains a bench stash heading into Week 2’s game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: ESPN’s Tim McManus believes “expectations should be tempered early” for Eagles WR Makai Lemon.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: It’s a reasonable assessment for a rookie who missed valuable spring and summer practice reps due to a recurring hamstring strain. Lemon reportedly admitted that he should have been “more professional off the field” regarding the injury, and Eagles WR coach Aaron Moorehead eventually told him to do “whatever” WR DeVonta Smith did during his own hamstring rehab program. Per McManus, “coaches say Lemon attacked the mental part of the game with high intensity as he waited to get healthy.” McManus believes Lemon should get playing time right away, but Smith and WR Dontayvion Wicks will “receive the bulk of targets while the rookie gets his footing.” Lemon must be safely stashed on benches at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Eagles WR Makai Lemon caught 3-of-5 targets for three yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon had a rough night, but tonight’s outcome does not make him any less of a top-tier prospect. The first-round rookie was sidelined by a recurring hamstring injury for much of the spring and summer, so a rusty first showing is understandable. Lemon took the blame, on the field, for QB Tanner McKee’s interception, although it is fair to note that McKee’s pass arrived late. Lemon had broken inward, off his stem, and an open window was available to the Eagles’ backup quarterback. Unfortunately, Lemon was forced to slow down and leap for the pass, accidentally batting it backward as he attempted to high-point it. Bengals CB Tacario Davis snagged it and that was that. Davis also broke up a pass intended for Lemon on a corner route 20 yards downfield earlier in the game. He had a good night. Lemon may need to ramp up for another couple of weeks, but he remains a smart draft pick in 12-team leagues. Lemon later went back into the game to field a punt, but went nowhere with it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Eagles WR Makai Lemon said he believes he will be ready to play in Week 1 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon returned to practice last week and was seen running with the first-team offense on Monday. Speaking with the media after Monday’s practice, Lemon confirmed that the hamstring injury he had been dealing with was in the same leg that had given him problems earlier this offseason. He’s missed a lot of time, but the rookie first-rounder has just under three weeks to get up to speed and be ready for the season opener, so we’ll see if he can get there. Lemon is worth a late-round pick in fantasy drafts, but shouldn’t be put in lineups until we see how he’s used in game situations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Eagles WR Makai Lemon (hamstring) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon was back at practice for the first time in weeks. The first-round receiver missed most of minicamp and training camp up to this point with a hamstring injury. While Lemon is playing from behind, there’s plenty of time for him to work his way into the offensive game plan ahead of the Eagles’ Week 1 matchup against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. failed to catch any of his three targets in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: This game started with Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr. getting ejected on the opening kickoff. He would go on to catch as many passes as his wide receiver doppelganger. BTJ nearly saved face with a late touchdown, but he failed to drag his back foot and stepped out of bounds for an incompletion. Josh Cameron, the team’s WR4, saw six targets. Thomas Jr. simply doesn’t have much of a role in this offense anymore. He will be the subject of trade speculation in the coming weeks. That seems to be his only path to meaningful fantasy production.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. caught 2-of-2 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.

Despite the score, Thomas’ lesser role relegates him to the WR3 spot in the Jaguars offense as he tied for fourth in targets against the Bengals. Thomas is a touchdown-dependent fantasy play and should be in the WR5 range for Week 5 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Brian Thomas Jr. played only 23 snaps in Week 3 because the Jaguars “were playing in a little bit more 12 and also some of the things that we had Josh [Cameron] on specifically were things that we felt good about him doing within a role that he has.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes that Cameron’s usage (23 snaps) could make it “stand[s] to reason Thomas could quickly become the fourth option instead” in a column that says he believes a “new start would be best for both parties.” It sounds like there’s a non-zero chance that Thomas is on the trade block at the deadline, as weird as that seems given how good the Jaguars have been on offense. Thomas isn’t necessarily someone who has to be rostered in shallow leagues given how things are trending.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Brian Thomas, Jr. caught his lone target for eight yards in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: After back-to-back 40-yard outings as the Jaguars’ No. 2 receiver, Thomas bottomed out on a low-volume day for the Jacksonville offense. Thomas’ usage has been spotty even in two-receiver sets so far this season. That leaves him as an iffy flex play week to week. He could benefit from a potentially high-scoring game in Week 4 against the Bengals. In shallower leagues he should stay on the bench for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. caught 3-of-8 targets for 40 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Thomas had a couple drops in this one and once again seemed not to be on the same page as Trevor Lawrence. Parker Washington led the Jaguars with a dozen targets and was clearly Lawrence’s preferred target. The highlight of Thomas’ day came on a 22-yard grab. BTJ’s downfield role in the Jacksonville offense means he will be a high variance weekly play in 12-team leagues. He some some flex appeal for Week 3 against a tough New England secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Jaguars WR Brian Thomas (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Thomas missed a little time in Week 1 after landing on his injured shoulder, but was able to return. The Jaguars’ X-receiver could face Broncos CB Pat Surtain on the perimeter this week, but he should get a few chances to make big plays downfield. He remains a FLEX starter in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Jaguars WR Brian Thomas (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: The Jaguars are seemingly just managing Thomas’ reps after their X-receiver aggravated his shoulder injury in Week 1 against the Browns. Thomas remains a volatile WR3/FLEX playing in a productive, if crowded, offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.

It’s believed to be a reaggravation of the shoulder injury he dealt with during training camp. Thomas Jr. will be stuck at the back of the WR3 ranks for his date with the Broncos on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said he expects Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) to play in Week 2 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Thomas exited Week 1 after reaggravating a shoulder injury he dealt with in the days leading up to Sunday’s game. https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. caught 3-of-3 targets for 40 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Thomas got off to a fast start, making a toe-tap catch on the Jaguars’ first drive and catching all three of his targets in the first quarter.
