https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Dameon Pierce rushed 11 times for 14 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Pierce “added” two catches for -2 yards. He took over as the Eagles’ lead back after Will Shipley went down with a foot injury in the first half. Carson Steele did not see the field for a single offensive snap. Pierce would presumably in line for a workhorse role in Week 6 if Shipley and Saquon Barkley are both out, but his efficiency today speaks for itself. This isn’t an offense capable of opening running lanes, nor is Pierce a back who can make a lot out of a little. Pierce is a low-priority waiver wire add for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Will Shipley (foot) will not return to the Eagles’ Week 5 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Shipley suffered the foot injury in the second quarter and was initially listed as questionable to return. He will now miss the remainder of the contest. Dameon Pierce is the only other running back on the roster with a touch today. Carson Steele is also active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Will Shipley (foot) is questionable to return in Week 5 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Shipley got stuffed on a carry in the second quarter and was checked out by trainers after the play. He went to the locker room after a brief trip to the blue medical tent. Dameon Pierce will be the next man up if Shipley’s day is over. Carson Steele is the only other back on the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Barkley will likely be listed as a non-participant on today’s official injury report. He is unlikely to play in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Aside from Barkley, the Eagles have RBs Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce on the active roster. Shipley will probably lead the backfield in touches this week, but it could be a messy workload split.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Eagles activated RB Dameon Pierce to the team’s active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Pierce will probably operate as the team’s No. 2 back behind Will Shipley this week against the Jaguars, one of the league’s best rush defenses. Tank Bigsby and Saquon Barkley are sidelined, leaving the Eagles scraping bottom for backfield depth. Look for Pierce to get some early-down work against the Jaguars. Shipley, who had six carries for 23 yards last week, is the only viable fantasy option of the two, though head coach Nick Sirianni heaped praise on Pierce Wednesday. “He’s an NFL starting running back,” Sirriani said of Pierce. “Maybe wouldn’t have said that when he was on our practice squad publicly, because of the fear of losing him. But he’s an NFL starting running back.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tank Bigsby will have core muscle surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Rapoport reports there are hopes that Bigsby will be back “in six weeks or shorter.” The 24-year-old back will be required to miss at least four games now that he’s headed for an IR stint. With Saquon Barkley (hamstring) also at risk of missing at least one game, third-string RB Will Shipley could be in line for a busy day in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Shipley rushed six times for 23 yards in Sunday’s loss to the Rams, but could be a sneaky option in PPR leagues given his pass-catching profile during his days at Clemson, when he caught 85 passes over three seasons. It also wouldn’t be surprising if Dameon Pierce or Jaydon Blue were promoted off the practice squad and saw early down touches while Shipley serves in more of a third-down role. There’s a lot to figure out here over the next few days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Eagles signed RB Dameon Pierce to the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: The news was first reported by ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. Pierce was released by the Eagles on Sunday with the team keeping Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley to backup Saquon Barkley. Pierce will head to the practice squad and be the next running back up if an injury arises.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Eagles released RB Dameon Pierce.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Per Aaron Wilson, the Eagles want Pierce back on the practice squad. We’ll see how that goes. Pierce is a good returner so he does have some special-teams versatility.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Eagles signed Dameon Pierce, formerly of the Chiefs, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Pierce most recently played for the Chiefs, appearing in four games for them last year after the Texans cut him midseason. The former fourth-round pick broke out as a rookie, running for 939 yards and four scores on 220 attempts in 2022. His role then declined drastically in back-to-back seasons before the team pulled the plug entirely. Pierce will be competing with Tank Bigsby for the RB3 and kick returner roles this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Chiefs declared RB Dameon Pierce, CB Melvin Smith, DE Ethan Downs, DE Tyreke Smith, OL C.J. Hanson, OL Jaylon Moore and DT Derrick Nnandi inactive for Week 17 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Pierce was promoted to the active roster last week, but he won’t be active for the Christmas showdown against Denver as Kansas City looks to play out the string.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 2-of-3 passes for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Cooper has been a touchdown magnet this year, scoring three times on five catches before today’s explosion. He broke loose against the Jags in the second quarter with a 62-yard grab. Cooper beat his man deep and his adjustment to the throw, which was thrown back toward the center of the field, put him in open space with a full head of steam. He ran untouched into the end zone. Cooper’s absurd touchdown efficiency can’t be sustained, but he is developing into a meaningful deep threat for a struggling Philly passing attack. He will at least warrant some FLEX consideration if DeVonta Smith remains out for Week 6 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 3-of-7 targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Doing his best Isaac TesLaa impression, Cooper is now up to three touchdowns on only five catches this season. His first score today was a fluke 18-yarder where he turned a Jalen Hurts end zone interception into six after he wrestled the ball away from Quentin Lake. His second was a 10-yarder where the Rams somewhat understandably simply stopped covering him in the painted area. Cooper is one of the only Birds stepping up right now, but his paltry targets total through four appearances — 10 — means he’s not about to push for WR4 status even with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) on the shelf.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: The Philly Voice’s Jimmy Kempski reports that Eagles WR Johnny Wilson had a “better” spring than WR Darius Cooper and could challenge for a roster spot.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Wilson’s first two years in the NFL were riddled with injuries. A summer concussion and in-season hamstring injury slowed his rookie season development, and he was robbed of his second season after being rolled up on in an August practice. He underwent season-ending ankle and knee injuries and was replaced in the lineup by Cooper, who uninspiringly caught nine passes for 92 yards all year. Wilson, an oversized slot receiver, is unlikely to be fantasy-relevant, but it sounds like he has a chance to at least contribute this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: The Athletic’s Zach Berman reports Darius Cooper “raised eyebrows” and “even pushed Jahan Dotson last year to be the No. 3 receiver.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: In trying to figure out how the Eagles could look if A.J. Brown gets traded, it’s possible Cooper pushes for a role in a three-wide set with Johnny Wilson also in the conversation. Cooper did manage a five-target, 33-yard game in meaningless Week 18 action with Tanner McKee starting. He’s on the deep dynasty radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Darius Cooper caught 3-of-5 targets for 33 yards in the Eagles’ Week 18 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Cooper, an undrafted free agent rookie from Tarleton State, had six targets on the season heading into Week 18. He made a few chunk plays running the most routes he had all season with the Eagles resting starters. Also splitting WR4 looks for the Eagles was Britain Covey, who caught 2-of-4 targets for 20 yards. Neither Cooper nor Covey are relevant on offense when the Eagles are playing starters, which they will be doing in the Wild Card round against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.headline: Eagles placed OLB Nolan Smith on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darius-coo.analysis: Smith reportedly re-injured the triceps muscle that he tore during Super Bowl LIX. He underwent surgery to repair the torn tissue this offseason. The Eagles believe Smith will not require surgery and hope to have him back “around” their Week 9 bye. Players placed on injured reserve are eligible to return after missing four games. The Eagles also placed CB Jakorian Bennett and WR Darius Cooper on injured reserve with undisclosed injuries. Both players are likewise expected to avoid surgery and are expected to return around Week 9. The Eagles signed S Marcus Epps, TE Cameron Latu, and CB Parry Nickerson to the active roster, and LB Lance Dixon, DB Eli Ricks, and WR Quez Watkins to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 24-of-39 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Jaguars’ 19-17, Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: Lawrence gave fantasy managers what they needed with a solid box score, but he was not the reason the Jags won this game. Lawrence struggled under pressure, throwing one ugly interception while putting the ball on the ground twice via sack-fumbles. Both were recovered by the Jags. The offense was also a catastrophe in the red zone, though a series of penalties and bizarre play calls are largely to blame there. Down by one with eight seconds left, it looked like the team’s struggles on offense would be too much to overcome. Instead, Ameer Abdullah returned a kickoff 53 yards to set up a walkoff field goal from Cam Little. If the Jags can clean things up after an uncharacteristically sloppy game, Lawrence will remain a mid-range QB1 for Week 6 versus the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown in the Jaguars’ 22-17, Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: The Jaguars offensive operation was far from clean against the Bengals; the team as a whole tallied 10 penalties for 100 yards by halftime. Lawrence was sacked four times behind a struggling offensive line but still put together an efficient game. He found Brian Thomas Jr. for the game’s first touchdown as time wound down in the first half and found tight end Brenton Strange for seven of his 18 completions. Despite a relatively pedestrian showing, Lawrence comes away with zero turnovers and the win. He will be a top-12 fantasy option for Week 5 against the Eagles in London.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 19-of-29 attempts for 182 yards and three touchdowns in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots, adding four rushes for 25 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: Lawrence’s big statistical day could have been bigger if he hadn’t inexplicably taken a knee at the one yard line on a QB rush with about eight minutes left in the fourth quarter. Bhayshul Tuten would go on to score a rushing touchdown a few plays later. Lawrence picked apart of the New England secondary with very little pressure in his face, targeting former Patriots WR Jakobi Meyers heavily and connecting with three different pass catchers for touchdowns — including Parker Washington, who had another score called back. Lawrence, with one of the highest weekly floors in the game, will again be a top-12 QB option in Week 4 against Bengals in what should be a high-scoring game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 17-of-29 attempts for 189 yards and one interception in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss against the Broncos, adding two rushes for six yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: The Jaguars were relatively run-heavy against Denver a week after the Broncos were shredded by Ken Walker and the Chiefs. Lawrence mostly checked down in this one, targeting Parker Washington a team-high 12 times. Brian Thomas, Jr., meanwhile, had two untimely drops, one that appeared to frustrate Lawrence. Lawrence’s interception came on a poor throw to Washington near the sideline. He’ll look to bounce back next week against a stingy New England secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns in the Jaguars’ 34-10, Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: It was a monstrous offensive showing from the Jaguars, led by Lawrence and his four passing touchdowns. He opened scoring with a 30-yard touchdown throw to Parker Washington in the first quarter, tossing two more scores in the first half. Lawrence flexed his mobility with a lob on the run to Jakobi Meyers for a 32-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With a comfortable lead, Lawrence rested in the fourth quarter, finishing with a whopping 0.72 EPA per play. Nick Mullens tallied three kneel-downs in relief. Liam Coen’s offense will generate many fantasy opportunities across the board, especially when operating as efficiently as it did Week 1. Lawrence built upon his solid 2025 season with an all-star showing Week 1 against the Browns and should be a low-end fantasy QB1 for Week 2 against a tougher Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence said he is more confident in his “progressions, adjustments, when to kill a play and what to call instead.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: According to ESPN’s Michael DiRocco, Lawrence’s offseason “was about gaining a graduate-level understanding” of coach Liam Coen’s offense. Last season, Lawrence was rehabbing an injury while attempting to change his footwork and adjust to a new play caller. He is now calmer and “can play more freely the way he did in the second half of last season.” Lawrence was the overall QB1 in total scoring from Weeks 9-18. If Lawrence and his pass catchers can carry the momentum into 2026, Lawrence can once again finish as an elite QB1, this time from Week 1 onward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said he is “trending toward” playing the starters in Friday’s preseason game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: The Jaguars didn’t play any starters in last week’s preseason game against the Saints, but Coen said that because they couldn’t do a padded practice on Monday with the Panthers, he may consider playing his starters a bit on Friday in order to get some “good (players) on good (players)” facing one another. If the Jaguars do play their starters this week, it will be their only taste of preseason action, as Coen has already said he won’t be playing them in the third preseason game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said he is “pleased” with QB Trevor Lawrence’s performance in spring practices.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: Specifically, Coen said Lawrence “did a really nice job taking care of the football,” perhaps throwing fewer than five interceptions across organized team activities and mandatory minicamp. Lawrence also performed well when “running the whole operation, managing the protections and some of the concepts on the field.” With a year of experience in Coen’s system now under his belt, Lawrence said he feels more confident going through his progressions and is doing “a lot less thinking” as plays are unfolding. Jaguars OC Grant Udinski has been impressed with Lawrence’s recall and his ability to guide teammates through concepts that the team hasn’t practiced in quite a while. Positive reports on the Jaguars’ offense continue to roll in. Lawrence warrants QB1 treatment in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes the chemistry between QB Trevor Lawrence and WR Jakobi Meyers “has taken a leap” this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: The Jaguars acquired Meyers via trade in Week 10 last year. He then led the Jaguars in targets (63) and receptions (43) until their season came to a close with a Wild Card Round loss to the Bills. Fellow Jaguars WRs Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. have generated buzz in recent weeks, but Meyers should not be overlooked. He still has a chance to repeat as the team’s target leader this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said he is focused on improving the deep passing game, particularly the chemistry between QB Trevor Lawrence and WR Brian Thomas.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: Lawrence found his groove after the team’s Week 8 bye, totaling 20 passing touchdowns, seven rushing touchdowns and seven interceptions. Coincidentally, Coen notes, their “average depth of target went up towards the second half of the season.” Coen wants to “keep pushing that envelope a little bit -– especially with [Lawrence] and BT.” Lawrence and Thomas have put a lot of work into trying to get their timing down this offseason, and Lawrence said, “it’s starting to pay off.” He feels like the two of them are “clicking more and more every day.” That’s great to hear. Thomas’ play dropped off significantly after an explosive rookie season, and trade rumors have swirled around him prior to the 2026 NFL Draft. If he can return to rookie season form, Thomas can smash his ADP this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 6-of-9 targets for 124 yards and two touchdowns in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Coming off a pair of quiet weeks, Washington paid off for fantasy managers early with a 51-yard score in the first quarter. It was somehow nowhere close to his best play of the day. Washington scored his second touchdown on a falling, one-handed grab in the end zone from 27 yards out near the end of the game. The grab was reminiscent of Odell Beckham’s famous touchdown catch. Washington remains the most talented and most involved receiver on the Jags. He will be a high-end WR2 versus the Texans next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 1-of-3 targets for 7 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington also added three yards with one carry on the ground. After a hot start to the season, Washington was relatively quiet against the Bengals. The Jaguars receivers combined for just 11 of Trevor Lawrence’s 23 targets and Washington saw three of those. His first reception came in the fourth quarter on a 40-yard catch-and-run that would have sealed the game, but was called back after replay showed he stepped out of bounds after seven yards. Game script and the Bengals’ tight end weaknesses played a factor in this game, with Brenton Strange the primary target on the day. Washington should still be the Jaguars’ No. 1 receiver and is a fantasy WR2 for Week 5 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: It’s Washington’s second touchdown in the Jags’ first three games of the season. Washington caught his touchdown against the Patriots after having an acrobatic touchdown grab called back on a penalty. Having established himself as the team’s clear-cut WR1 — well ahead of Brian Thomas, who had one target in Week 3 — Washington will have a rock solid weekly floor with ceiling to spare in shootout game scripts. Washington should remain in all lineups next week against a middling Bengals defense, in what could be a high-scoring affair between two potent offenses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 8-of-12 targets for 98 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Trevor Lawrence, as always, targeted Washington heavily, as no other Jacksonville pass catcher saw more than eight targets on the day. Washington came within half a yard of a touchdown in the first half after scoring in Week 1 against the Browns. Clearly the team’s No. 1 wideout, Washington should have a rock-solid weekly floor with upside to spare, especially when the Jaguars have to operate a more pass-heavy offense. Washington will be a top-15 play next week against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 5-of-6 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington saw elite usage in the first half, making the first Jacksonville catch of the game and ending the Jaguars’ first drive with a diving 30-yard touchdown reception. He followed it up with a one-handed sideline catch on the second drive and tallied five receptions in the first half. His usage was that of a legitimate No. 1 wide receiver for the Jaguars’ fantasy-friendly offense. The game was out of hand in the second half, leading to no more receptions the rest of the day, but fantasy managers will be happy with Washington’s utilization and production as he adds to his elite box scores from the end of last season. Washington is a fantasy WR2 heading into Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports the Jaguars are “unlikely” to extend Parker Washington before Week 1.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Per Wolfe, the Jags explored a deal similar to that of Michael Wilson, who just landed a three-year, $75 million extension. The two sides couldn’t agree to terms, and Washington will now start his contract year. It’s a highly risky move for a largely unheralded player who caught lightning in a bottle at the end of last year. Washington caught 29 passes for 507 yards and three touchdowns in his final five games, including one postseason appearance. If he repeats anything close to those numbers over a full season this year, Washington will make far more than Wilson as a free agent next offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said Parker Washington will “absolutely” be the team’s punt returner to start the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Coen also noted that Washington is “the guy right now,” suggesting that his role as the returner could change at some point in the year. Washington returned 25 punts for the Jaguars last season and racked up 341 return yards and two touchdowns on those returns. Coen said the Jaguars will hope to get Travis Hunter involved as the punt returner at some point, but Washington will start the season in the role. Washington profiles as a solid WR2 to start the fantasy season after going for 58-847-5 last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington said his contract talks with the Jaguars “are continuing.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Jags GM James Gladstone said last week that the team was open to an in-season extension with Washington, who is set to hit free agency next offseason. Both sides want to get a deal done, but they are clearly still at odds over the details of the contract. Even if it takes longer than expected, it does look like Washington will sign an extension before he gets to test the waters of free agency. Coming off an outstanding training camp, Washington should be treated as a fantasy WR2 for the Jags’ Week 1 date with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said the team would be open to negotiating an extension with WR Parker Washington in-season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington, 24, is entering a contract year, coming off the best season of his career. He is reportedly expected to be the team’s No. 1 wide receiver. If Washington plays up to that standard, he will unquestionably be able to raise his asking price. Signing him to a deal right now could save the team money in the long term, but the front office evidently wants to see how he fares early in the year. Although this route could be costly, having a true No. 1 wide receiver affirm his financial value with top-tier play is a good problem to have.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington (undisclosed) returned to practice on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: After missing last week due to an undisclosed issue, Washington was back on the field Sunday, participating in drills and working in seven-on-sevens. Whatever he was dealing with doesn’t appear to be anything too serious, which is a good sign for the fourth-year receiver who is looking to build on last year’s breakout campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson suffered a concussion in Week 5 against the Saints and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson was slammed into the ground on his first catch of the day. He got up slowly and was immediately checked out by the medical staff. Hockenson was eventually evaluated for a concussion and ruled out. With a bye week on deck for Week 6, Hockenson should be able to return for the team’s next game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 13-of-13 targets for 119 yards in the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: With just over two minutes left in the game, Hockenson took a knee at the Dolphins’ five-yard line, allowing Kyler Murray to seal the game with a trio of kneel-downs after that. Although Hockenson surrendered the touchdown, he still delivered a TE1-worthy stat line on the day. The veteran tight end served as Murray’s go-to receiver, regularly nabbing passes on short-to-intermediate slants and curls. Hockenson mostly dove forward for a couple of extra yards after catching passes, but he did manage to drag a defender on a 14-yard gain early in the fourth quarter. The Dolphins’ pass rush was very effective today, and Murray seemed to hone in on Hockenson as his primary pressure fix as the game progressed. Hockenson will be a borderline TE1/2 against the Saints in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 2-of-4 targets for 11 yards in the Vikings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Running a route on 29 of the team’s 37 drop backs, Hockenson was uninvolved in the offense even after Justin Jefferson exited the game with an ankle injury in the first half. Hockenson, who has nine grabs over the Vikings’ first three games, profiles as a low-floor weekly option in a Minnesota offense that has not passed at its usual volume early in the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 3-of-4 targets for 29 yards in the Vikings’ Week 2 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson more or less repeated his Week 1 statline, only this time on far less passing volume for the Vikings’ offense. Carson Wentz attempted just 20 throws as the Vikes went “survive and advance” mode in weather-addled Chicago. With Kyler Murray expected to return from his concussion in Week 3 in Tampa, perhaps Hockenson can post a higher-end TE2 statline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 4-of-5 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 1 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson finished second on the team in targets, though his 17 percent target share isn’t much to write home about. He found paydirt late in the third quarter on a red zone strike from Carson Wentz over the middle of the field. Wentz was filling in for a concussed Kyler Murray, who will likely miss Week 2. Hockenson is more of a TE2 than a true TE1, but his strong Week 1 outing at least puts him on the border versus the Bears next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: Vikings restructured the contract of TE T.J. Hockenson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: The move saves $5 million against the cap for the Vikings in 2026, a franchise that is now scrambling to get under the salary cap following numerous high profile moves made the year prior. Hockenson is coming off the worst statistical season of his career following a devastating knee injury suffered in 2024. Now two years removed from the injury and playing with something to prove, the fantasy needle could be pointing up should he find more consistent quarterback play moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: Vikings TE T.J. Hockenson (shoulder) won’t play in Minnesota’s Week 18 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: With Jordan Addison taking a major leap in 2024, Hockenson has slid into an uninteresting low-end TE1 stab over the past two years, generating 41/455/0 in 2024 and 51/438/3 in 2025. Cutting Hockenson would free up over $8.9 million in cap space for a team that’s currently up against it to get cap-compliant and The Athletic’s Alec Lewis pointed to Hockenson as one contract that could be reworked this offseason. His future with the Vikings is in some question entering 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: Vikings TE T.J. Hockenson (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson sat out in Week 17 against the Lions and he appears likely to sit out this week as well. Hockenson’s backup, TE Josh Oliver, should not be in re-draft lineups against the Packers even if Hockenson cannot play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson missed Week 17 with the shoulder issue and looks likely to sit out of Minnesota’s season finale. Josh Oliver and Ben Sims each caught exactly one pass in his absence last week. There isn’t a fantasy tight end of note on the team if Hockenson is out for Week 18.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (shoulder) will not play in Week 17 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson got banged up versus the Giants last week and was unable to practice once before being ruled out for Week 17. With one week left to go, it’s possible his season is over. Max Brosmer is under center for the Vikings this week. We don’t expect him to make any of the Vikings’ backup tight ends relevant for fantasy purposes tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.headline: Tyler Steen (shoulder) returned to the Eagles’ Week 5 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.analysis: Steen left with the shoulder issue earlier in the game and was listed as questionable to return. Fred Johnson took his spot at right guard for a few drives. While the Eagles are still down several key names due to injury, Steen is no longer among them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.headline: Michael Carter suffered an abdominal injury in Week 5 against the Jaguars and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.analysis: Right guard Tyler Steen is questionable to return with a shoulder injury. Philly came into this game without several key players because of injuries. Now they will be without even more players on both sides of the ball.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.headline: Mekhi Becton (right leg) was seen “limping for much of [Eagles] practice” before leaving early.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.analysis: The report comes from ESPN’s Tim McManus. The fact that Becton was allowed to continue practicing for some time despite the evident limp could indicate the team is managing a known issue but it’s a negative development overall. Becton projects to start in place of injured OG Tyler Steen (ankle) at least in the short term. Becton plays with a brace on his right knee, stemming from a pair of kneecap injuries. He suffered cartilage damage following a 2021 kneecap dislocation. The same kneecap then suffered an avulsion fracture one year later. The issues could provide grounds for routine soreness moving forward but we will monitor the situation for updates.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.headline: Eagles HC Nick Sirianni said OG Tyler Steen will miss some time with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.analysis: Steen is projected to start at right guard for the Eagles this season. The second-year player reportedly injured his ankle at Saturday’s practice and will miss a few days with the injury. Former No. 11 overall pick Mekhi Becton, who is hoping to break camp with the Eagles this offseason, is expected to see some work in place of Steen, which could go a long way in determining whether or not he lands on the 53-man roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.headline: The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reports Eagles rookie Tyler Steen is working with the starters at right guard.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.analysis: The Eagles selected Steen with the No. 65 pick in last year’s draft. He played sparingly last season, appearing on just 71 offensive snaps over four games. Steen started every game at left tackle during his final season at Alabama, but with both tackle positions currently solidified in Philly, Steen has a chance to move to the interior and win a starting job heading into his second season with Sua Opeta now in Tampa Bay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.headline: Eagles selected Alabama OL Tyler Steen with the No. 65 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.analysis: Steen (6’6/321) was a 3-star recruit, and the 112th-ranked offensive tackle in the 2018 recruiting class, from Miami, Florida, according to 247 Sports. A converted defensive lineman, Steen is a large immovable force in the run game. Once he gets rumbling, little remains standing in his wake. An experienced tackle with 36 starts in the SEC, Steen has enjoyed good durability and position flex. Due to his lack of athleticism, pass blocking can be an issue when he can’t simply overpower an opponent. Although he put on 20 pounds when he transferred to Alabama, he may benefit from dropping at least some of that weight to combat his heavy feet. However, for a team with a run focus and a scheme that values play in a phone booth, Steen will be a fit and a developmental piece.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.headline: Former Vanderbilt junior LT Tyler Steen has several high-profile visits lined up in coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-stee.analysis: Steen (6'5/315) entered the transfer portal in mid-January, and has quickly become a hot commodity over the last several weeks. His father shared with 247Sports.com that Steen has visits setup with Alabama, NC State, LSU and Penn State and that UCLA, USC and Kentucky may also be in the future. Steen is a native of Ft. Lauderdale, Florida and was a three-star recruit from the 2018 class. He has come a long way since joining Vanderbilt, playing on over 2,200 snaps since 2019 per Pro Football Focus while allowing just 34 quarterback pressures and 11 sacks on 1,262 passing down snaps. Steen appears to be heading to a top program somewhere in 2022, now we will wait to see which one he lands with.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.headline: Michael Carter suffered an abdominal injury in Week 5 against the Jaguars and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.analysis: Right guard Tyler Steen is questionable to return with a shoulder injury. Philly came into this game without several key players because of injuries. Now they will be without even more players on both sides of the ball.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.headline: Jets acquired WR John Metchie and a 2027 sixth-round pick from the Eagles in exchange for CB Michael Carter and a 2027 seventh-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.analysis: Metchie provides the Jets with much-needed depth in the pass-catching corps, and there is a chance he starts in Week 10, post-bye. Jets No. 1 WR Garrett Wilson has been sidelined by a knee injury, forcing the team to rely on wide receivers like Allen Lazard, Arian Smith, Josh Reynolds and Tyler Johnson. Metchie would be tough to trust as a FLEX option right away, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano report that they expect the Jets to “consider dealing veterans to acquire draft capital” and “probably will be active sellers.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.analysis: In a linked article, Fowler identifies the Chargers, Chiefs and Texans as the best fits for Jets RB Breece Hall and puts Hall’s odds of being traded at 35.0 percent, for what that’s worth. The 24-year-old running back is scheduled to enter free agency at the end of the year, and the Jets currently have RB Braelon Allen (knee, injured reserve) and RB Isaiah Davis under contract through 2027. Davis can be stashed, speculatively, at this time. Acquiring draft picks in exchange for Hall makes sense from a team-building perspective. Should he land with the Chargers or Chiefs, Hall’s fantasy-scoring ceiling could rise considerably, operating as a featured player in a high-scoring offense. Things could become complicated upon Chargers RB Omarion Hampton’s (ankle) return from injured reserve in the former scenario. Hall would undoubtedly become the Texans’ lead running back but the positional rotation gets a bit murkier. The ESPN reporters also list EDGE Jermaine Johnson and CB Michael Carter II also potential trade candidates.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.headline: Jets declared CB Michael Carter, WR Allen Lazard, RB Khalil Herbert, OT Esa Pole, TE Jelani Woods, DL Tyler Baron, and DL Leonard Taylor inactive for Week 6 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.analysis: Carter remains out with a concussion. He did not practice at all this week and was ruled out on Friday. Per usual, the Jets are a great matchup for opposing passers. Bo Nix will look to take advantage this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.headline: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said Michael Carter (concussion) will miss Week 5 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.analysis: Backup nickel Isaiah Oliver will presumably take over in Carter’s absence. Carter, who was a DNP all week, was unable to clear concussion protocol in time for Sunday’s Week 5 matchup and will now eye a Week 6 game against the Broncos for his targeted return date. While Carter is sidelined this weekend, Glenn said RB/KR Kene Nwangwu (hamstring) could be a game-time decision.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.headline: Jets CB D.J. Reed (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.analysis: Fellow cornerback Michael Carter (back) also missed Wednesday’s practice. Both players look likely to miss Week 7, though the Steelers don’t have a deep cast of receivers to worry about. George Pickens will see plenty of Sauce Gardner on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.headline: Jets CB D.J. Reed (sore knee) did not participate in team drills on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.analysis: HC Robert Saleh told reporters yesterday that he expects Reed to play on Sunday, though Reed was able to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday. We’ll wait to see Thursday’s official injury report but it appears as though Thursday may be a step in the wrong direction. Regardless, he will likely need to log a limited participant designation on Friday for him to suit up this week. Slot CB Michael Carter II (ankle) was a limited participant on Wednesday as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.headline: Jets signed DB Michael Carter II to a three-year, $30.75 million extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.analysis: The Jets lock up their slot corner with a three-year extension that can be worth up to $33 million and includes over $19 million in guarantees. The deal makes Carter the highest-paid slot corner in the NFL. Initially a fifth-round pick in the 2021 NFL Draft, Carter has started 20 games in three seasons for the Jets. He has 23 passes defended, two interceptions, and 185 tackles throughout his career. Now locked up for the foreseeable future, Carter reinforces a scary Jets secondary with Sauce Gardner and D.J. Reed playing the outside corner positions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.headline: Jets DB Michael Carter II left Week 13’s game against the Vikings and did not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.analysis: He came back to test the ankle for a play, then immediately headed out again. Brandon Echols replaced Carter for the Jets. Carter’s status was not updated by the team after the loss.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.headline: Jets DB Michael Carter II (chest) left Week 11’s game against the Patriots and did not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ca.analysis: He was carted off following time in the medical tent after suffering the injury. Brandin Echols replaced Carter. Carter had a 76.3 PFF coverage grade entering today, so he’s a real loss for the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants declared S Jason Pinnock, RB Devin Singletary, CB Nikko Reed, DT Bobby Jamison-Travis, OT J.C. Davis, and QB Jake Haener inactive for Week 5 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Singletary is once again a healthy scratch as the Giants will roll with Cam Skattebo, Najee Harris, and Tyrone Tracy as their top three backs. J.J. McCarthy will serve as the QB2 behind Jameis Winston in what figures to be a messy game in the elements in Washington this afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants declared RB Devin Singletary, S Ar’Darius Washington, CB Nikko Reed, DL Jihad Ward, OL J.C. Davis, TE Thomas Fidone, and DT Bobby Jamison-Travis as inactive for Week 4 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: This is the second-straight week that Singletary has been made a healthy scratch for the Giants. Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy will serve as the backups to Cam Skattebo. It’s also worth noting that QB J.J. McCarthy, who was acquired from the Vikings earlier this week, is active for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants declared RB Devin Singletary, TE Thomas Fidone II, OL J.C. Davis, DL Josh Tupou, DL Bobby Jamison-Travis, CB Deonte Banks, and S Tyler Nubin inactive for Week 3 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Singletary is a healthy scratch this week. Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy are the backup running backs for New York. Singletary had nine carries and four catches in the first two weeks of the year. His absence could be a slight boost to Cam Skattebo, though Singletary’s touches may just be distributed to the other backups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Although Skattebo was not targeted in the pass game, his 18 carries handily led the team. Furthermore, presumed backup Tyrone Tracy lost a fumble on one of his two carries, resulting in Devin Singletary taking over primary backup duties for the remainder of the game. Those two variables should keep Skattebo’s weekly volume high after showing no ill effects of the devastating ankle injury suffered in 2025. His touchdown now gives him eight total scores in nine professional appearances despite only six of those being starts, a rate that will keep Skattebo in the weekly borderline RB1 discussion moving forward. Tracy managed just two snaps to Singletary’s 25, leaving Singletary as the primary backup for the moment. It’s possible Najee Harris gets into this discussion after being a healthy scratch in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Tyrone Tracy Jr., Najee Harris and Devin Singletary are all listed as co-No. 2 backs on New York’s unofficial Week 1 depth chart.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: We can’t endorse relying on anyone in this backfield as a surefire bellcow in the event that Cam Skattebo gets hurt or is ineffective enough to lose playing time. It seems like it will be hard to rely on Tracy to have a major role this year with Harris in town.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan says Najee Harris “was brought in under the premise that he’s going to be a significant contributor” for the Giants this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: It’s worth noting that Cam Skattebo continues to be the first running back up in practice, but it sounds like the Giants could have a vision for Harris, who signed with the team on a one-year, minimum-salary deal, per Raanan. Harris is returning from a torn Achilles that ended his 2025 season in Week 3, but there’s plenty of room for him to earn snaps behind Skattebo once he gets up to speed. A blown pass-blocking assignment by Tyrone Tracy in the team’s first preseason game against the Vikings raised immediate questions about whether or not the Giants will trust Tracy in pass-blocking situations this season, and Harris has proven to be a capable pass-blocker in the past. At this point, it’s hard to imagine Harris having any standalone fantasy value in a healthy Giants backfield, but he could be worth a handcuff to Skattebo in deeper leagues based on these latest reports.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes said it’s “clear Cam Skattebo is the top back” for the Giants in training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: According to Hughes, Skattebo is “the first up in almost every running drill,” and he has also handled the majority of carries in practice. While it’s certainly an encouraging sign for Skattebo’s usage, Hughes also notes that the preferred options in the passing game are Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary. If the Giants were to dial back Skattebo’s role in the receiving game, it could deal a bit of a blow to his fantasy stock. He was on a 17-game pace to catch 51 passes last season, and his work in the passing game made up 43.7 percent of his fantasy scoring in PPR leagues last year. Skattebo’s role as an early-down grinder and goal-line back should be more than enough to satisfy fantasy managers this season, but a reduced role in the passing game would put a bit of a cap on his ceiling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants restructured RB Devin Singletary’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Singletary’s job with the Giants is safe, for now. The 28-year-old back has been relegated to backup duty in each of his last two seasons with the Giants, totaling 874 yards and nine touchdowns on 232 carries while appearing in 232 games. The Giants are reportedly going to be big players in the running back market once free agency kicks off next week, and could also eye a high-end rookie in the draft. Any major additions could put Singletary’s spot on the 53-man roster in jeopardy, especially if Cam Skattebo is healthy for the start of next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Devin Singletary rushed nine times for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 18 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: The 28-year-old will finish the season with 119 carries for 436 yards and five touchdowns in 17 games. He also added 18 catches on 19 targets for 151 yards and served primarily as the red zone option whenever either of Tyrone Tracy Jr. or Cam Skattebo was injured. Singletary is under contract for $5 million next season, but the Giants could opt out of that deal and take on a $1.25 million dead cap. Whomever they hire as head coach will likely play a big role in deciding that.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Devin Singletary rushed eight times for 45 yards and one touchdown in the Giants’ Week 17 win over the Raiders, adding four receptions for 25 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: The Giants allowed RB Tyrone Tracy to handle 10 of the team’s first 11 snaps. Singletary caught a five-yard checkdown pass at the end of the first drive and then bided his time until the Giants’ third drive. He accounted for 38-of-44 scrimmage yards and one touchdown on that drive, keyed by a 29-yard toss play that set up his one-yard scoring plunge. He operated as a frequent change-of-pace player after that. Singletary warrants FLEX consideration against the Cowboys next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: Texans declared TE Marlin Klein, CB Collin Wright, DE Chris Braswell, LB Aiden Fisher, OG Febechi Nwaiwu and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Houston’s Week 5 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: The Texans had five questionable players, including three offensive linemen with illnesses. All three of those linemen will play, and Kayden McDonald and M.J. Stewart were activated off injured reserve to make their season debuts as well as the Texans try to avoid an 0-5 start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M. Alexander reports that Texans TE Marlin Klein “will have some sort of role” this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: Alexander also lists Klein behind TE1 Dalton Schultz and apparent TE2 Foster Moreau, so this isn’t exactly a ringing endorsement. Klein has efficiently caught 4-of-5 targets for 62 yards thus far in the preseason, and OC Nick Caley unpromptedly complimented Klein’s run blocking. The latter aspect is likely Klein’s ticket to game-day snaps this season. Schultz is a trusted veteran. Klein will likely be a non-factor in fantasy this year, but perhaps he can gain some ground in-season and force the Texans to get him involved late in the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M. Alexander believes the Texans “will likely utilize a lot more 12 personnel packages in 2026 than they did last season.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: Injuries thinned the Texans’ tight end depth last season. This offseason, the front office signed TE Foster Moreau and drafted TE Marlin Klein, who is currently sidelined by a hamstring injury. Starting TE Dalton Schultz should continue to play a lot of snaps, though he is likely just a high-end TE2. Increasing 12 personnel sets decreases the number of snaps available to the wide receiver position, which could be a problem if the coaching staff decides to employ a rotation at the WR2 spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: Texans TE Marlin Klein was sidelined this week after injuring his hamstring at organized team activities.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: Klein’s hamstring injury is not expected to be a long-term issue. The athletic second-round rookie caught 37 passes for 351 yards and one touchdown over his final two college seasons. The Texans have a decent group of backup tight ends, though many of the veterans have fairly extensive injury histories. Klein may have a chance to earn the TE2 role this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: Texans signed No. 59 overall pick TE Marlin Klein to a four-year, $8.184 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: An elite athlete at the position, Klein didn’t begin playing football until high school, but totaled 37 passes for 371 yards and one touchdown in his last two seasons at Michigan. While he should still see plenty of playing time in his rookie season, we wouldn’t expect him to contribute much from a fantasy perspective with Dalton Schultz still with the team. Klein is an interesting stash in dynasty leagues but he can be left on the waiver wire in redraft leagues for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: Texans selected Michigan TE Marlin Klein with the No. 59 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: Klein began playing football in Germany before moving to the United States in high school. Because he was late to football, his numbers at Michigan aren’t much to write home about. Over Klein’s last two seasons, he caught 37 passes for 351 yards and one touchdown. He stands 6’6/248 and ran a 4.61-second 40 at the NFL Scouting Combine. Add in strong burst numbers and he left Indy with a 9.05 RAS. Klein is also a strong blocker despite his lack of reps. His receiving game needs work, but the athletic profile gives him a considerable ceiling. He will get to learn behind Dalton Schultz for a year before potentially taking over in 2027, when Schultz becomes a free agent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: Michigan received a verbal commitment from three-star 2022 TE Marlin Klein.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: Klein (6'6/215) became Michigan’s third verbal commitment in the Class of 2022 Tuesday morning, joining DT Alex VanSumeren and LB Tyler Martin. While he’s been used at both wide receiver and tight end at the high school level, Klein has been projected as a tight end once he arrives on campus. Currently attending Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School in Rabun Gap, Georgia, the three-star recruit is actually a native of Germany. Klein’s recruitment picked up during the summer as Power 5 programs such as Boston College, Florida State, Georgia, Louisville and Virginia Tech all tendered offers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets EDGE Will McDonald (calf) is active for New York’s Week 5 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: He popped up on the Friday injury report with a calf, but will try to play through it. Inactive for the Jets are RB Breece Hall (quad), LB Kiko Mauigoa (quad), OL Dylan Parham (knee), WR Adonai Mitchell (finger), EDGE Nate Lynn and CB Nahshon Wright. The four with injury statuses were ruled out on Friday, the other two are healthy scratches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Will McDonald (calf) is questionable for New York’s Week 5 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: He popped up on the injury report on Friday, never a great sign. McDonald has a 68.4 PFF pass rush grade on 69 pass rushes and the Jets would lose something on defense without him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets declared CB D’Angelo Ponds, S Minkah Fitzpatrick, RB Kene Nwangwu, ED Joseph Ossai, LB Trevin Wallace, and K Blake Grupe inactive for Week 2 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: We knew Fitzpatrick had already been ruled out with a groin injury. D’Angelo Pounds had practiced all week, and Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that he was healthy enough to play, but apparently there is no room for him in the secondary at the moment. The good news for the Jets is that Will McDonald (ankle) is active and will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said Will McDonald will play in Week 2 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: McDonald popped up on Thursday’s injury report with an ankle injury, but speaking with the media on Friday, Glenn said the fourth-year pass rusher will be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Packers. Rookie CB D’Angelo Ponds, who missed last week with an ankle injury, is also expected to make his NFL debut this week, giving the Jets additional help in the secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets EDGE Will McDonald (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: The midweek downgrade is never a promising sign, and the Jets were definitely hoping to have a full complement of pass-rushers against a beleaguered Packers offensive line in Week 2. Assuming this wasn’t a practice injury that spirals into an extended absence, we’d expect McDonald to be listed as questionable tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes said “there is a lot of smoke” to the Jets drafting Ohio State LB Arvell Reese with the 2026 NFL Draft’s No. 2 overall pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: There is “an internal debate” in the Jets’ organization between drafting Reese or Texas Tech EDGE David Bailey. Bailey, 22, is generally regarded as the draft’s top pass rusher and is knocked for his run defense. Reese is a complete player and is currently just 20 years old. Hughes notes that current Jets EDGE Will McDonald is a great pass rusher, but can be a liability in run defense. McDonald and Bailey would form a potent pass rush duo, but could be a suboptimal tandem against the run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets general manager Darren Mougey said the team plans to exercise EDGE Will McDonald’s fifth-year option.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: McDonald was taken No. 15 overall in the 2023 draft and is now eligible to have his fifth-year option picked up. In three seasons, McDonald has tallied 21.5 sacks, including back-to-back seasons of at least eight sacks. His option is expected to be around $14 million, making his contract for 2027 relatively light for a productive edge rusher. McDonald will head into year four with the Jets likely exploring extension talks to keep him long-term.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets placed EDGE Will McDonald IV (knee) on season-ending injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: McDonald marked eight sacks in 15 games this year and continues to look like a solid building block pass rusher. The Jets will face a decision on whether they want to pick up his fifth-year option this offseason. With the season over in all but name, the Jets also sent LB Kiko Mauigoa (neck) and DL Jay Tufele (foot) to the injured reserve list.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets ruled out TE Mason Taylor (neck) for Week 17 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: Taylor has now missed three straight games as a result of his neck injury. The rookie tight end, who has caught 44 passes for 369 yards and one touchdown this season, will have one more chance to suit up for Week 18’s season finale against the Bills, but after missing three-straight weeks of practice, he could be a long shot for next week. In addition to Taylor the Jets also ruled out EDGE Will McDonald (knee), DL Jay Tufele (foot), and LB Kiko Mauigoa (neck) for Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters that EDGE Will McDonald IV gained 15 pounds this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/will-mcdon.analysis: Glenn did not provide McDonald’s current weight, but he is likely close to 260 pounds. He was listed at 245 pounds on the team website and tipped the scales at 239 pounds at the 2023 NFL Scouting Combine. Per ESPN’s Rich Cimini, Jets coaches “believe it will make him a stronger edge setter against the run.” McDonald recorded team highs in both quarterback pressures (60) and sacks (10), but notched just 12 tackles in run defense, only one of which went for a loss or no gain.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Vikings declared Jordan Addison (hamstring) inactive for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison seemingly gave it a go this morning but wasn’t quite ready to play. The Vikings get a Week 6 bye, so Addison should be ready to go when they return to face the Colts in two weeks. Also inactive for the Vikings are OT Christian Darrisaw, S Jakobe Thomas, WR Odell Beckham, CB Chuck Demmings, DT Elijah Williams, and QB Max Brosmer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: ESPN’s Jeff Darlington reports Jordan Addison (hamstring) “isn’t likely to be active” for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison got in two limited practices this week before being listed as questionable. He was considered a game-time decision as of this morning, but it sounds like the team is going to hold him out for at least one week. Justin Jefferson, on the other hand, is expected to suit up. The offense will run through him, per usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Justin Jefferson will work out pregame to determine his status for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: The same is true of Jordan Addison. Both Minnesota wideouts are currently listed as questionable for Week 5. Jefferson is from Louisiana and has already told reporters he plans to play in the homecoming game. We expect him to suit up, but fantasy managers should have a backup plan for him and Addison to be safe.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (hamstring) is questionable for Minnesota’s Week 5 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison practiced on Thursday and Friday after taking Wednesday off. We’d consider him on the optimistic side of questionable for Sunday’s game against New Orleans, but he will probably only be a WR3/FLEX play if Justin Jefferson (ankle) also returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (hamstring) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: The Vikings’ No. 2 wide receiver sat out on Wednesday due to “a little hamstring soreness.” If he can get through today and tomorrow without aggravating the sore muscle, he should be able to play in Week 5 against the Saints. His WR3/FLEX viability is subject to Justin Jefferson’s (ankle) status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Jordan Addison (hamstring) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: According to O’Connell, Addison has “a little hamstring soreness,” though it is “considered minor.” Keep an eye on this. Hamstring injuries can quickly become problematic at the wide receiver position. If active and practicing fully by the end of the week, Addison will be a WR3/FLEX against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison caught 4-of-6 targets for 52 yards in the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison’s box score could have looked a little bit better, had his 21-yard gain on a curl route during the Vikings’ third drive not been erased by a penalty. Regardless, he played sidekick to T.J. Hockenson in this one. For his part, Addison maximized his opportunity, delivering the longest play of the game via a 27-yard catch on a crosser in which he barreled through multiple Dolphins defenders to generate extra yardage. The Vikings also gave him the ball on a jet sweep, but he lost one yard on it. Addison will be a WR3 against the Saints next week if Justin Jefferson (ankle) is still sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison caught 5-of-9 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison dominated air yards and targets with Justin Jefferson sidelined with an ankle injury he sustained in the second quarter. His 41-yard touchdown grab from Kyler Murray was one of three downfield looks he got on the day; he nearly converted the other two as well. A non-factor in the Vikings’ first two games of the season, Addison should be locked into lineups if Jefferson misses any time with the ankle issue. If Jefferson returns for Week 4 against the Dolphins, Addison would figure to be flex-viable as long as Murray is under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison caught 2-of-5 targets for 21 yards in the Vikings’ Week 2 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: It’s another disappointing statline for a wideout held without a catch in Week 1, though it was yet another game where we didn’t get to see the Vikings’ “real” offense. With Kyler Murray out with a concussion, Carson Wentz was fed to the wolves at rainy Soldier Field. Murray is expected back for Week 3 in Tampa, and with him, hopefully finally a useable statline for the Vikes’ talented No. 2 receiver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Vikings WR Jauan Jennings (personal) is out for Week 2 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Head coach Kevin O’Connell ruled out veteran receiver Jauan Jennings, citing a death of a close family member. Jennings will step away from the team to mourn the passing, leaving Tai Felton as the player most likely to step into his vacated role when the Vikings take on the Bears. Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison should take on all the volume they can handle with the team also without Jordan Mason. Jefferson is a locked-in WR1 while Addison offers an intriguing upside-WR2 profile after putting up a dud in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.headline: Browns declared WR Tylan Wallace (knee), QB Taylen Green (third qb), TE Carsen Ryan (calf), DT Mike Hall Jr. (ankle), G Parker Brailsford, G Teven Jenkins (back) and DT Mason Graham (knee) inactive for Cleveland’s Week 5 game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.analysis: Congrats to Parker Brailsford on being the only healthy scratch. No surprises here; everyone else but Green was ruled out on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.headline: Browns signed WR Tylan Wallace, formerly of the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.analysis: Wallace was a valued special teams contributor and pass-catching depth piece for the Ravens since being drafted in the fourth round of the 2021 NFL Draft. The 26-year-old has one touchdown reception each of the last two seasons and a punt return for a touchdown in 2023. He reunites with Todd Monken in Cleveland, where he will compete for special teams snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.headline: Ravens declared WR Tylan Wallace, QB Cooper Rush, G Ben Cleveland, T Carson Vinson, and OLB David Ojabo inactive for Week 13 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.analysis: There are no real surprises here as the Ravens enter Week 13 as one of the healthier teams in the league. They hunt for their sixth consecutive victory against their division rivals on Thanksgiving as they continue their bid for a late-season push towards the postseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.headline: Ravens re-signed WR Tylan Wallace to a one-year, $2.25 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.analysis: Wallace returns to the Ravens after a productive season as a blocking receiver and special teamer. The highlight of his season was an 84-yard catch-and-run touchdown against the Bengals in Week 10. He will rotate into the offense behind Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman, and DeAndre Hopkins, primarily playing special teams for the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.headline: Tylan Wallace caught 3-of-3 targets for 115 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 10 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.analysis: Tonight was the first time role-player Wallace ever caught three passes or scored a receiving touchdown. His winding, 84-yard scoring grab in the fourth quarter was a third down dump-off that featured comically inept tackling from the Bengals. A huge play, but not something that will be repeated moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.headline: Ravens placed WR Devin Duvernay (back) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.analysis: Duvernay, the Ravens’ primary kick returner, suffered a back injury this month and will miss at least four weeks. The team believes he will return in the postseason. Until then, Tylan Wallace — who had a game-winning punt return touchdown in Week 14 — will take over for Duvernay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.headline: Odell Beckham (shoulder) was removed from the Week 8 injury report and will play against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.analysis: Beckham was added to the injury report on Thursday as a limited participant in practice but got back to a full session on Friday. The Ravens have limited his routes since he returned from the ankle injury he suffered earlier in the year. That will make it hard for Beckham to surpass WR4 status versus the Cardinals. Fellow skill position players Keaton Mitchell and Tylan Wallace were listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.headline: Ravens designated WR Tylan Wallace to return from IR.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.analysis: The 2021 fourth-round pick is also back at practice as the Ravens now have 21 days to activate him off the IR. Wallace has just six catches on 13 targets in his first two seasons but was a productive receiver at Oklahoma State where he had at least 900 yards and six touchdowns in each of his last three seasons. He could emerge as a solid addition to the Ravens receiving corps but is unlikely to see enough snaps and targets to matter for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.headline: Ravens WR James Proche will miss a “week or two” after suffering a soft-tissue injury in practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.analysis: The diagnosis came straight from coach John Harbaugh in his post-game press conference. Proche has reportedly been in the lead for No. 2 duties opposite Rashod Bateman, which says more about this wideout group than Proche. Harbaugh also said second-year pro Tylan Wallace is dealing with a “minor” knee sprain but might not miss any time. Although neither injury sounds like a long-term concern, it further highlights just how thin and unproven this receiver corps really is. The Ravens probably need to get on the receiver workout circuit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.headline: Ravens second-year WR Tylan Wallace suffered a sprained knee in the preseason opener Thursday night.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tylan-wall.analysis: Coach John Harbaugh said it’s a “minor” sprain for Wallace, but it’s unclear how long he’ll be out. Both Wallace and James Proche are injured, and Proche is expected to miss a couple weeks with his soft-tissue issue. Both are competing for snaps behind Rashod Bateman and even Devin Duvernay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-matth.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jake Matthews (groin) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-matth.analysis: The Falcons’ left tackle has started 199 consecutive games in his career. His streak appeared to be in jeopardy early in the week, but the iron-man tackle practiced in full on Friday, putting him on the right side of questionable for today’s game. He should be good to go for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marlon-hum.analysis: Humphrey logged one limited practice this week before being listed as questionable for Week 5. He’s one of several key defenders dealing with an injury heading into Sunday Night Football. EDGE Trey Hendrickson has already been ruled out, while S Kyle Hamilton is questionable with a groin injury. Even with some missing names, this defense still looks like a true test for Michael Penix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.headline: Jaguars declared S Eric Murray, WR CJ Williams, CB Alijah Huzzie, CB Jaylon Jones, OL Daniel Faalele, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis inactive for Week 5 against the Eagles.

Murray has started all four games this year, though we don’t think his absence will spark a revival of the Eagles’ passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Packers placed RB Chris Brooks (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks had been the most consistent contributor to a Green Bay backfield working to find their way in the absence of Josh Jacobs. The team appears likely to utilize journeyman Pierre Strong as the preferred passing down specialist, likely keeping the backfield in a maddening timeshare without Brooks. None are worthy of legitimate fantasy interest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Steelers placed WR Michael Pittman (foot) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman aggravated the foot injury that cost him Week 2 last week and will now miss four games, at minimum, while on injured reserve. Roman Wilson appears to be the primary beneficiary of Pittman’s absence and has seen six targets in each game this season while mostly playing a situational role. Wilson is a priority waiver addition over rookie Germie Bernard.

ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reports that Michael Pittman (foot) was in “the locker room with his left foot propped up on a scooter.”

Michael Pittman caught 2-of-5 targets for 16 yards in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals.
Michael Pittman (foot) is active for Week 3 against the Bengals.
ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Michael Pittman (foot) is expected to play in Week 3 against the Bengals.
